greenhouse_4232626009.title: Leasing Consultant
greenhouse_4232626009.rewritten_description:
Leasing is a skills game. The people who do it well aren't just friendly. They read a prospect quickly, adjust their pitch without being manipulative, handle a "I need to think about it" without desperation, and still find time to follow up on six other leads before lunch. That's the core of what Hawthorne Residential Partners is hiring for at their Atlanta community.

The Skills This Role Runs On

Every day, you're using a short stack of skills repeatedly: active listening, objection handling, written communication, and basic sales discipline. Conducting personalized tours is less about memorizing floor plans and more about figuring out what matters to the person standing in front of you. Is it the commute? The closet space? The dog-friendliness? You ask, you listen, and you connect the dots out loud for them.

Beyond tours, you're processing leasing applications, completing move-in paperwork accurately, and tracking your own follow-up pipeline. The paperwork isn't glamorous, but a missed step during move-in creates problems that ripple into the resident's entire tenure. Precision matters here, not just personality.

You'll also help coordinate resident events and community engagement efforts. These aren't optional extras. They're how a property builds the kind of retention that keeps occupancy healthy without relying entirely on new traffic and concessions.

What Separates a Good Leasing Consultant from a Great One

The honest answer is follow-up discipline. Most prospects don't lease on the first visit. The consultants who convert at a high rate are the ones with a consistent, non-annoying system for staying in touch after a tour. They're also the ones who actually know the competing properties in the submarket, because a prospect asking "how does this compare to the place down the street?" deserves a real answer, not a deflection.

One more thing worth knowing: this schedule includes Saturdays, and resident events can occasionally push into evenings. That's the nature of leasing. If your weekends are completely off-limits, this role will create friction. If you're flexible and like the trade-off of a weekday off during the week, it tends to work well.

Building a Career Here

Hawthorne has a formal career path program, and the Leasing Consultant role is a recognized entry point into property management leadership. The natural next step is Assistant Community Manager, where the skills shift toward operations, financials, and team coordination. The leasing experience you build here, particularly around occupancy management and resident relations, translates directly into that next level.

  • High school diploma or GED required; one year of customer service or sales experience preferred
  • Valid driver's license required
  • CALP certification is a plus but not required on day one
  • Total target compensation around $55,000, including hourly pay plus monthly leasing and renewal commissions
  • Benefits include medical, dental, vision, 401k match, paid time off, pet insurance, and paid parental leave

Hawthorne is one of the larger Southeast-rooted multifamily operators in the country. If you want a company with enough structure to support your growth but enough regional identity to actually feel like something, that combination is harder to find than it sounds.

greenhouse_4232201009.location: Retreat at Knoxville - 10600 Castlepointe Way - Knoxville, TN - 37932
greenhouse_4232201009.rewritten_description:
Multi-site leasing roles aren't for everyone. You're covering more than one community, which means your schedule shifts, your product knowledge has to be sharp across multiple floor plans and rent ranges, and your follow-up game has to be tighter than average. If that sounds like a grind, it probably is. If it sounds like a challenge worth taking on, keep reading.

Hawthorne Residential Partners is one of the larger Southeast-based operators in the country, consistently ranking among the top 50 multifamily management companies nationally. This position is based at Retreat at Knoxville in the 37932 zip code, a growing corridor on the west side of the city that has seen consistent rental demand. The role itself is a leasing consultant position, but because it spans multiple sites, you're essentially running a tighter version of the full leasing cycle on repeat: handle traffic, tour prospects, convert leads, process paperwork, support renewals, and then do it again at the next property.

Day to day, you're the first person a prospective resident talks to, whether that's a walk-in, a phone call, or an email inquiry from an ILS. You're conducting tours, managing follow-up, and building enough rapport that someone chooses your community over the three others they toured that week. You'll also help coordinate resident events and keep an eye on what competitors are doing in the local market. It's a sales role with a service wrapper around it, and the best people in these seats understand that difference instinctively.

What actually separates strong candidates from average ones here isn't just personality. It's consistency. Anyone can have a great tour on a good day. The people who move up in leasing careers are the ones who follow up on the cold leads, who close on a Saturday afternoon when foot traffic has slowed, and who treat the 30th inquiry of the week with the same energy as the first. Hawthorne's own career path program recognizes this: leasing consultant to assistant community manager is a well-worn track in this industry, and operators like Hawthorne tend to promote from within when they see someone who can perform under volume.

What You'll Need

  • High school diploma or GED
  • At least one year in customer service, sales, or apartment leasing (preferred, not required)
  • Valid driver's license (required given the multi-site nature of this role)
  • CALP certification is a plus if you have it
  • Comfortable working Saturdays and occasional evenings for resident events

Compensation includes an hourly base plus monthly leasing and renewal commissions, which is standard for the role. Benefits include medical, dental, vision, 401k with match, paid time off, pet insurance, and paid parental leave options. The office runs Monday through Friday, 9 to 6, and Saturdays, 10 to 4, with one weekday off each week to keep the schedule at 40 hours.

If you're early in your property management career and want to build leasing fundamentals fast, multi-site exposure does that more quickly than a single-property seat. You'll see different resident profiles, different pricing strategies, and more situations in a shorter period of time. That experience compounds.

greenhouse_4232198009.title: Maintenance Supervisor - Multi-Site
greenhouse_4232198009.rewritten_description:
Multi-site maintenance supervision is a different animal than running a single property. You're not just fixing things. You're managing schedules across communities, tracking vendor timelines on multiple make-readies simultaneously, keeping your team accountable when you're not physically on-site, and still finding time to put hands on equipment when the situation calls for it. Hawthorne Residential Partners is hiring for exactly that kind of role in Atlanta.

The day-to-day here spans the full maintenance lifecycle. Unit turns need to be inspected and signed off before move-in, preventative maintenance programs need to run on a quarterly cadence, and capital improvement projects need bids sourced, schedules built, and execution managed. On any given week you might be walking a punch list on a vacant unit in the morning, meeting with a vendor about an ongoing capex project at noon, and coaching a technician through a proper HVAC repair in the afternoon. The variety is real, and so is the accountability.

Budget monitoring and inventory management fall under this role too. That means you need to understand what things cost, catch waste before it compounds, and make sure your team isn't sitting idle waiting on parts that should have been stocked. Grounds, amenities, and common areas also stay on your radar because curb appeal directly affects traffic and, ultimately, occupancy.

What separates a strong candidate here isn't just technical range, though you do need solid working knowledge across HVAC, plumbing, and electrical. It's the ability to keep multiple communities moving without letting any single one slip. Supervisors who thrive in multi-site roles tend to build tight vendor relationships early, because when a turn is sitting incomplete, a reliable contractor you can call on short notice is worth more than almost anything else.

On-call rotation is part of the job. After-hours emergencies happen, and Hawthorne expects you to respond. That's worth knowing going in.

What Hawthorne Is Looking For

  • High school diploma or GED
  • At least 3 years in apartment maintenance or a skilled trade (HVAC, plumbing, electrical)
  • Prior supervisory or lead tech experience strongly preferred
  • Valid driver's license required
  • EPA certification required
  • CPO certification highly preferred (required in some states)

Compensation includes hourly pay plus a monthly renewal bonus, quarterly performance bonuses, and quarterly resident satisfaction bonuses. Hawthorne also offers a career path program with genuine development structure, education reimbursement for maintenance skills, and a benefits package that includes medical, dental, vision, 401k match, paid parental leave, and pet insurance, among other things.

If you've been running maintenance at a single property and want the complexity and career growth that comes with multi-site responsibility, this is a logical next step. Multi-site supervisors who build strong operational track records often move into regional or director-level maintenance roles, and Hawthorne's internal development program is structured to support that trajectory.

greenhouse_4979411008.title: Regional Property Manager
greenhouse_4979411008.rewritten_description:
This role lives or dies on two skills: reading a financial statement fast and reading people even faster. The Regional Property Manager position at Hillpointe asks you to do both simultaneously, across a Sun Belt portfolio of workforce housing communities in and around Atlanta.

What This Role Actually Demands

Hillpointe isn't a third-party fee management shop. They develop, build, and operate their own product. That matters because when you're the Regional here, you're not translating an owner's vision through layers of bureaucracy. You're sitting close to the source. Budget variance conversations happen with people who built the asset. That's a different dynamic than most regionals experience.

The financial side is real. You're building annual budgets, managing pricing and renewal strategies inside Entrata, and digging into performance gaps before they show up as NOI problems on the T-12. If you can't spot a delinquency trend early or explain why T-3 occupancy is trending down before your owner asks, this isn't the right seat for you.

But the job posting says "Sales, Sales, Sales" three times, and that's not an accident. Workforce housing in the Sun Belt is competitive. You're competing on price, reputation, and leasing execution. A regional who can only manage expenses but can't drive traffic and close occupancy gaps is only doing half the job. The expectation here is that you build teams who sell, and you model that culture from the top down.

The People Side of the Portfolio

Identifying talent and developing site-level teams is where the leverage is in this role. You can have the best pricing strategy in the market and still lose ground if your on-site managers aren't executing. Hillpointe wants someone who can hire right, train with purpose, and hold teams accountable to leasing goals and deadlines without micromanaging every punch list item.

Regular travel across the portfolio is expected. Site inspections, team check-ins, market surveys. If you're the type who prefers to manage by spreadsheet from a home office, this one isn't for you.

What Separates Strong Candidates Here

  • Entrata fluency, or at minimum, the ability to get up to speed fast on a new platform without hand-holding
  • Proven experience managing lease-up or stabilization across multiple communities at once
  • A real track record in workforce or Class B/C garden-style product, not just Class A high-rise
  • The ability to develop marketing plans that actually move the needle on online leads and tours, not just repost listings
  • A real estate license, or a clear path to obtaining one in the Georgia market
  • Comfort communicating with stakeholders across legal, financial, and HR contexts

Regionals who come up through the ranks at integrated developer-operators tend to have an edge here. They understand that every operational decision connects back to asset value, and they don't need to be reminded of it. If your background includes ownership-side thinking alongside your management experience, that's the profile Hillpointe is building toward.

greenhouse_5981531004.title: Customer Experience Specialist (Leasing/Customer Service)
greenhouse_5981531004.rewritten_description:
Leasing roles get mislabeled constantly. This one sits at the intersection of sales, customer service, and light operations, and Cottonwood Residential is calling it what it actually is: a customer experience position. That framing matters, because if you think this job is just showing apartments and collecting applications, you'll underperform here.

Park Avenue Apartments in Salt Lake City needs someone who treats every interaction, whether it's a prospect walking in cold, a resident calling about a package, or a vendor dropping off supplies, as worth full attention. You'll be the first voice people hear on the phone and the first face they see at the door. That's not a small thing. First impressions in leasing move the needle on traffic conversion more than most people realize.

Day to day, you're keeping vacant units show-ready, walking the tour path, staying sharp on current pricing and availability, and responding to inquiries across phone, email, and text without letting anything fall through the cracks. You're also helping coordinate community events and supporting social media marketing efforts, which is increasingly part of the leasing consultant role whether it's listed in the job title or not. Package room organization is in the mix too. Not glamorous, but residents notice when it's a mess.

Cottonwood was early to self-guided tours, and that's shaped how they think about the customer journey. They're not looking for someone who just unlocks a door and steps aside. They want someone who can design an experience even when they're not physically in the room.

The schedule is full-time and includes weekends and evenings. That's the job. Leasing doesn't close when the office does, and the candidates who thrive here are the ones who don't resent that reality.

What strong candidates bring

  • Genuine comfort with phone sales and the ability to convert inquiries, not just answer questions
  • Attention to detail on unit readiness and the move-in experience, because a botched make-ready kills a first impression fast
  • Composure when a frustrated resident walks in and the leasing office is the closest target
  • Curiosity about the industry. This role has a stated path toward management, and Cottonwood seems to mean it
  • Comfort with digital communication across multiple channels simultaneously

If you're early in your property management career and want a role that builds real leasing fundamentals at a company that's been willing to rethink how the customer experience works, this is a reasonable place to start. The quarterly bonus structure means your effort has a direct return, which is how it should work in leasing.

Most leasing teams succeed or struggle based on who's running the floor when the General Manager isn't there. That's the real weight of an Assistant General Manager role, and it's why Bozzuto takes the hire seriously. This isn't a stepping stone for someone waiting around for a promotion. It's a position that demands genuine leadership, sales instincts, and the ability to hold a team accountable with patience rather than pressure.

Based in Stamford, CT, this role sits inside one of the more active rental markets in the Northeast. Stamford draws a mix of commuters, young professionals, and corporate relocations, which means your prospect pool is varied. Residents have real expectations. They compare your community to other Class A options in the area, and they'll notice quickly if the experience doesn't match the price point. That context matters when you're conducting tours, handling service concerns, or coaching a leasing consultant through a tough follow-up conversation.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Day to day, you're moving between leasing, operations, and people management. You'll conduct personalized community tours that convert, not just inform. You'll manage delinquency, post rent receipts, and keep an eye on occupancy numbers. When the GM is out, you step into that decision-making seat without waiting to be told. The team looks to you, and you need to already know what you're doing when that moment comes.

Weekends are part of the schedule. Prospective residents shop on Saturdays and Sundays, so you'll work one to two weekends per month with corresponding weekdays off. That's not a small thing, and it's worth naming directly. If weekend availability is a real conflict, this role will create friction fast.

  • 2+ years in property management, hospitality, or retail
  • Familiarity with rent collection, delinquency management, and basic budget concepts
  • Experience with Yardi or comparable property management software preferred
  • Comfort creating and posting content across social media platforms like Instagram and Facebook
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Real estate license required or must be obtained within 90 days of hire where applicable
  • Four-year degree or equivalent hands-on experience

What Separates Strong Candidates Here

The candidates who thrive in this role aren't just organized. They read people well. Bozzuto's brand is built on the resident experience, which means your instincts for conversation, empathy, and follow-through carry as much weight as your leasing numbers. Someone who can close a lease but leaves residents feeling processed rather than heard won't last long here.

This role also tends to lead somewhere. AGMs at well-run companies like Bozzuto who demonstrate consistent financial performance and team development often move into General Manager seats within a few years. The exposure you get here, including budget accountability, delinquency management, and team oversight, builds a resume that translates directly into site leadership.

Compensation for this position ranges from $67,362 to $70,000, with additional bonus opportunities. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, 20 days of paid time off plus holidays, a 401(k) with company match, and tuition reimbursement.

greenhouse_5197325008.rewritten_description:
What You'll Actually Do

This is a full property management role at a Bozzuto community in Abingdon, MD. You're running the operation: occupancy, NOI, team performance, client reporting, and resident experience. All of it lands on your desk. You'll own the financial performance of the property, which means you're reading your T-12, watching your T-3, managing delinquency, and presenting accurate operational and financial reports to clients on a consistent schedule. Bozzuto is a fee management company with a strong client-service orientation, so that client relationship piece isn't a footnote. It's core to this role.

On the leasing and marketing side, you're not just monitoring traffic numbers. You're partnering with the consumer marketing team to execute strategy, staying sharp on competitive intel, and making sure your concessions and pricing decisions are grounded in what the local market is actually doing. You'll also work one weekend per month, which is standard for a role where prospective residents are most active on Saturdays and Sundays.

The team leadership component here is real. Bozzuto puts genuine weight on coaching and developing the people under you. Rolling up your sleeves when the situation calls for it isn't optional, it's expected. If a make-ready needs hands on it or the leasing office is slammed, you're in it.

What You Bring

  • A four-year degree or equivalent experience that demonstrates you've earned it the hard way
  • Five or more years in property management, hospitality, or retail, with a track record that shows you can lead people and manage a P&L
  • Real budget experience. You know what variance analysis looks like and you're not intimidated by it
  • Proficiency with Yardi or a comparable platform
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, specifically the kind that work with both residents and clients
  • A professional presence that matches a Bozzuto community's positioning

Context Worth Knowing

Bozzuto operates across the mid-Atlantic and Northeast, and their properties tend to skew Class A with a service culture that's closer to hospitality than traditional multifamily. That's not a bad thing, but it does mean expectations around resident experience and community presentation are high. If you've come up in a high-volume lease-up environment or a more transactional operation, the adjustment is real. The upside is that Bozzuto invests in its people at a level you don't see at every management company, and the brand carries weight if you're thinking about where this role takes your career.

Strong candidates for this type of role typically separate themselves not on the leasing or financial side, but on team retention and client communication. Those two things are where average property managers lose the job and strong ones build a reputation. Worth keeping in mind when you're putting your application together.

greenhouse_4227832009.title: Groundskeeper - Cortland at Fredericksburg - San Antonio, TX
greenhouse_4227832009.rewritten_description:
What This Job Actually Looks Like Day to Day

The Groundskeeper role at Cortland at Fredericksburg in San Antonio is physical, outdoor-heavy work. Most of your shift starts before residents notice anything is wrong, which is exactly the point. You're walking the property, picking up litter, cleaning common areas inside and out, and making sure the grounds look sharp before the first person heads out to their car in the morning. San Antonio summers are brutal, and you'll be working through them.

Beyond the daily trash and debris rounds, you'll handle seasonal deep-cleaning tasks, flag safety hazards to the maintenance team, and occasionally pitch in on resident events or community functions. You're not a maintenance tech, but you're close enough to the operation that your eyes matter. Spotting a broken light, a drainage issue, or a safety concern before it becomes a work order or a liability is part of the value you bring.

The maintenance team may pull you in to support service requests when volume gets heavy. That's not overstepping the role. It's how well-run communities actually function.

What You Bring

  • Prior groundskeeping, landscaping, custodial, or general labor experience is preferred, but not a hard requirement if you're reliable and willing to learn
  • Physical stamina for lifting, bending, and working outdoors in variable weather conditions
  • Attention to detail that goes beyond "good enough." You notice when something looks off
  • Punctuality and the ability to work independently without someone checking on you every hour
  • Basic familiarity with cleaning tools and safe material handling, or a genuine willingness to get up to speed quickly
  • Clear, respectful communication with residents and teammates when issues come up

A Realistic Lens on This Role

Curb appeal is not a small thing in multifamily. A well-kept exterior directly affects how prospective residents feel when they walk a property during a tour. It affects renewal decisions more than most people admit. The Groundskeeper is one of the first and most consistent impressions a community makes, which means this work carries real weight even if it doesn't always get recognized as such.

What separates strong candidates from average ones here isn't experience. It's consistency. Showing up every day, covering the full property, and not letting the small stuff slide, even on a 100-degree Tuesday in August, is what actually moves the needle. Cortland operates as a top-10 multifamily owner and operator nationally, and their properties are expected to reflect that. The standard is real, and this role is part of holding it.

greenhouse_4227816009.title: Leasing & Sales Consultant - Cortland at Fredericksburg - San Antonio, TX
greenhouse_4227816009.rewritten_description:
Leasing is one of those roles where the job title undersells the actual work. At a community like Cortland at Fredericksburg, the leasing consultant isn't just processing applications. They're the first and most important impression a prospective resident gets, and they're directly responsible for occupancy, revenue, and the lived experience of the people who choose to call that community home.

What This Role Actually Requires

Cortland is looking for someone who treats leasing like a sales craft, not a hospitality gig. That distinction matters. You'll be managing a pipeline: following up on leads, tracking conversion rates, keeping your CRM current, and hitting KPIs that leadership will hold you to. The consultative side of the work means you're not reciting floor plan prices. You're listening for what a prospect actually needs, then matching that to a solution and closing with confidence.

You'll also own the resident experience side of things. That includes planning community events, managing the social media presence for your property, and handling objections without losing composure. Turning a hesitant prospect into a signed lease is a skill. So is keeping current residents engaged enough to renew instead of shop around.

  • At least 6 months of sales, customer-facing, or performance-driven experience (leasing experience is not required, but a track record of meeting goals is)
  • Comfort being measured: traffic, conversion, and occupancy numbers will reflect your work directly
  • CRM fluency, or the willingness to get there fast
  • Polished communication and personal presentation that fits a premium brand standard
  • Coachable. Cortland has a defined sales methodology, and the expectation is that you implement feedback quickly, not eventually

What This Role Builds

Leasing consultant is one of the most direct paths into property management leadership in the multifamily industry, and companies like Cortland tend to promote from within when they find someone who produces. The skills you develop here, specifically pipeline management, objection handling, and resident relationship-building, transfer cleanly into an Assistant Manager role where you'd add financial responsibilities like delinquency tracking and lease administration. From there, the path to Community Manager becomes much shorter.

One honest note: this role lives and dies on follow-up discipline. The difference between a strong leasing consultant and an average one usually isn't charisma. It's the person who sends the follow-up text two hours after a tour, logs it in the CRM, and calls again on day three. Cortland operates with metrics visibility, which means your conversion numbers are visible to your manager. That accountability is motivating for the right person and uncomfortable for the wrong one.

If you're someone who genuinely enjoys the close, takes pride in a well-managed pipeline, and wants to build a career in multifamily with a company that has real infrastructure behind it, this role at Cortland's Fredericksburg community in San Antonio is worth a serious look.

greenhouse_7857812.title: Property Manager in Training
greenhouse_7857812.rewritten_description:
Most property management companies hire experienced managers and hand them a set of keys. Weinstein Properties does something different. This training role exists specifically to bring in sharp people from adjacent fields, customer service, hospitality, retail, sales, and develop them into site leaders with real operational ownership. It's a deliberate pipeline, not a gap-filler.

This position is based at Kings Crossing, a Weinstein-managed community in the Henrico/West End corridor of Richmond. You'll train alongside an existing manager, learning the day-to-day rhythm of the property before eventually stepping into your own site. The timeline for that transition varies, so if you need a guaranteed promotion date, this probably isn't the right fit. If you're comfortable building skills first and earning that step forward, there's a clear path here.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Your days will split between leasing activity and operational support. You'll handle internet leads and phone inquiries, schedule tours, walk prospects through the community, and process applications through to signed leases. On the resident side, you're the person helping someone understand their renewal options, process a notice to vacate, add a pet to their lease, or get clarity on their account balance. That part of the job requires patience and consistency. Not every interaction is easy.

You'll also work closely with maintenance. That means walking make-ready apartments to confirm punch list items are complete, following up on open work orders, and keeping an eye on the overall condition of the property. Rent posting, delinquency follow-up, move-out processing, and security deposit dispositions round out the administrative side. And because this is a leadership track, you'll be expected to help coach the team and contribute to community events, not just execute tasks assigned to you.

  • Prior management or team leadership experience is required (1 to 3 years)
  • Property management background is a plus but not a dealbreaker
  • Strong administrative skills and comfort managing competing priorities
  • Clear, confident communication with residents, prospects, and team members
  • Self-directed work style. You won't be micromanaged, but you will be expected to stay busy
  • Schedule includes weekday and rotating Saturday coverage (Sundays off)

What Separates Strong Candidates Here

Weinstein has been family-owned for over 70 years and manages more than 60 communities across five states. That scale means real career mobility, but the culture still runs on a hands-on, people-first approach. The candidates who thrive in this program aren't just organized and friendly. They take genuine ownership of their property's condition, their team's performance, and the resident experience. They notice things. They follow through without being reminded. They treat the property like it's theirs.

If your background is in hotel front desk management, retail leadership, or a high-volume customer service environment, the translation to property management is more direct than you might think. Leasing is sales. Resident relations is hospitality. The operational side adds a layer, but the core skills carry over well. This role pays starting at $25 per hour with quarterly bonuses and a sign-on bonus discussed at the interview stage.
greenhouse_7857812.description_text: We have a fantastic Property Manager In Training opportunity available! $2,000 Sign On Bonus* Weinstein Properties, headquartered in Richmond, Virginia owns and manages over 60 apartment communities in Virginia, North Carolina, Texas, Tennessee, and Georgia. Some previous property management experience is a plus, but not needed if you have strong management experience from customer service, sales, hospitality or retail environments. We offer training and coaching on how to master the necessary skill sets, and direction for professional development. Prior management experience is a must. greenhouse_4233227009.rewritten_description:
Leasing is one of the few roles in property management where you can enter with a customer service background and, within a year or two, be running the front office of a multifamily community. At Hawthorne Residential Partners, that path is built into the job description rather than left to chance. The company's internal career progression puts the Leasing Consultant role directly below Assistant Community Manager, and their Learning and Development program exists specifically to close that gap.

The position is based at Hawthorne at Hixson, a community in Hixson, TN, where you'd be the first voice prospects hear and the first face they see. Your days will center on touring apartments, converting leads to signed leases, and keeping the resident experience warm after move-in. That means following up on web and phone inquiries, completing leasing paperwork accurately, supporting renewal goals, and helping organize resident events that build a genuine sense of community. The office runs Monday through Friday, 9 to 6, and Saturdays from 10 to 4, with one weekday off each week to keep you at 40 hours. Occasional evenings may come up around community events.

Compensation here is structured to reward performance. Beyond an hourly base, you're eligible for monthly leasing commissions and renewal bonuses, which means your income grows directly with your ability to close and retain residents. That commission structure is a good early lesson in how NOI thinking works at the property level, and it's the kind of context that makes the jump to a management role feel natural rather than abstract.

What the Role Asks Of You

  • High school diploma or GED equivalent
  • Valid driver's license
  • A CALP designation is a plus if you already have it
  • Comfort communicating across phone, email, and in-person conversations

What separates strong leasing consultants from average ones isn't usually the ability to give a tour. It's the follow-up. Most prospects visit two or three communities before deciding. The ones who choose Hawthorne do so because someone followed up with them thoughtfully, remembered a detail from the conversation, and answered their specific question rather than giving a scripted response. If that kind of relationship-building comes naturally to you, this role builds real, transferable skills in sales, resident retention, and community operations that carry value well beyond this particular job.

Hawthorne is one of the 50 largest multifamily operators in the country, with a concentration in the Southeast. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401k match, paid time off (including your birthday), pet insurance, and paid parental and adoption leave. Telehealth access and company-paid life insurance round out the package.

greenhouse_4232670009.title: Maintenance Supervisor
greenhouse_4232670009.location: Hawthorne at Bear Creek - 110 Bear Creek Lane - Asheville, NC - 28806
greenhouse_4232670009.rewritten_description:
Most apartment communities don't fail because of bad leasing. They fail because the physical asset deteriorates faster than the team can respond. The Maintenance Supervisor role exists to prevent exactly that, sitting at the intersection of technical skill, team leadership, and resident experience.

Hawthorne Residential Partners is hiring a Maintenance Supervisor at Hawthorne at Bear Creek, a community in Asheville, NC. This isn't a wrench-turning role dressed up with a title. You're running a maintenance operation: scheduling your team, managing the budget, overseeing unit turns, coordinating vendors, and keeping a preventative maintenance program alive quarter after quarter.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

On a typical day, you're walking the property before the office opens, triaging overnight service requests, and confirming your team has clear assignments before 8 AM. By mid-morning, you might be inspecting a vacant unit before it goes on the make-ready schedule, catching a punch list item that would've delayed move-in. By afternoon, you're following up with a vendor on a capital project or reviewing inventory to make sure supplies don't run short during a heavy turn cycle. On-call rotation is part of the deal, and Asheville's weather means after-hours calls aren't hypothetical.

The role requires at least three years of apartment maintenance or skilled trade experience, with HVAC, plumbing, or electrical work in the background. EPA certification is required. CPO certification is strongly preferred. Prior supervisory or lead technician experience matters here because you'll be mentoring techs, not just working alongside them.

Qualifications Worth Having

  • Minimum 3 years of apartment maintenance or skilled trade experience (HVAC, plumbing, or electrical)
  • Supervisory or lead technician experience, strongly preferred
  • Valid driver's license
  • EPA certification (required)
  • CPO certification (highly preferred, may be required depending on state)
  • High school diploma or GED

Hawthorne offers a bonus structure that includes monthly renewal incentives, quarterly performance bonuses, and quarterly resident satisfaction bonuses on top of hourly pay. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, 401k with match, paid time off (including your birthday), paid parental leave, pet insurance, telehealth access, and company-paid life insurance. There's also an education reimbursement program and a formal career path program for employees who want to grow within the company.

Here's the career angle worth knowing: Maintenance Supervisors who build strong vendor relationships, keep turns tight, and develop their teams tend to move into Regional Maintenance Director roles or transition into facilities and capex-focused positions as companies scale their portfolios. The skills compound quickly. Managing a preventative maintenance program teaches asset thinking. Running a team teaches operational leadership. Both open doors well beyond any single property.

What separates strong candidates from average ones in this role is usually vendor management and turn discipline. Anyone can fix things. The supervisors who advance are the ones who keep the make-ready schedule from slipping, catch problems before residents report them, and build a team that doesn't need to be micromanaged on routine work.

What You'll Actually Do

This is an evening porter position covering common areas at a Comstock-managed office property in Reston, Virginia. The shift runs Monday through Friday, 6PM to 10PM, which means you're working after the building empties out. That's actually a real advantage: fewer interruptions, a clear checklist, and the satisfaction of leaving a space genuinely clean before the next workday starts.

Your daily work covers lobbies, restrooms, sidewalks, and public spaces. You'll follow cleaning schedules and checklists assigned by the Senior Operations Manager, track supply inventory, and keep the janitorial closet organized and hazard-free. Pressure washing is part of the rotation. When events happen at the property, you'll help with setup and breakdown. If something looks broken, unsafe, or damaged, you document it and report it. Simple accountability, consistently applied.

At the end of each shift, you complete the required documentation and hand off properly to whoever follows you. That handoff discipline matters more than most people realize. A missed note about a wet floor or a low supply stock creates problems for the next shift and reflects on the whole team.

What You Bring

  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • Valid driver's license with no major violations
  • Ability to lift, push, or pull up to 50 pounds and stay on your feet for extended periods
  • Flexibility to occasionally work weekends or outside your regular hours during high-traffic events
  • Strong time management and the ability to work independently with minimal supervision
  • A professional, courteous manner with property staff, tenants, and visitors
  • Comfort working around cleaning chemicals and following safety protocols correctly

Context Worth Knowing

Comstock is a significant player in the Reston Town Center corridor, which has grown into one of Northern Virginia's denser mixed-use nodes. Office properties here serve a mix of tech, government contracting, and professional services tenants who have real expectations about building presentation. A porter who takes visible pride in clean lobbies and well-maintained exteriors directly supports how those tenants experience the property every single day.

Porter and groundskeeper roles at well-managed commercial and mixed-use properties are often a starting point for people who grow into facilities technician or building operations positions. If you're reliable, attentive, and show initiative, those paths are real. The skills you build here, chemical safety, equipment care, maintenance documentation, shift handoffs, transfer directly into maintenance technician work and beyond.

Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, 401(k) matching, life insurance, free parking with EV charging, parental leave, and an annual professional development fund. For a part-time evening shift, that's a meaningful package.

This is a leasing-forward, operations-grounded position at what Bozzuto operates as a premium residential community. You're not just covering the front desk when the GM is out. You're driving occupancy through personalized tours, managing delinquency, posting receipts, and coaching your team through the small moments that add up to resident retention. Fort Lauderdale's rental market is competitive, with strong demand from young professionals and a steady churn of residents who have real options. That means your leasing instincts matter. A tour that feels scripted won't close.

What the Role Actually Looks Like

On a typical day, you might start by reviewing delinquency and following up on outstanding balances, then shift to walking the property to make sure the curb appeal and common areas meet Bozzuto's standard before afternoon traffic picks up. You'll take tours yourself, not just delegate them. When the GM is off-site, the team looks to you. That means vendor conversations, resident escalations, and coaching a leasing consultant through a difficult interaction all fall in your lap, sometimes in the same hour.

Weekend availability is part of the role. One to two weekends per month, with corresponding weekdays off. That's the honest reality of leasing-driven property management, and it's worth knowing upfront.

What Bozzuto Is Looking For

  • A four-year degree or equivalent hands-on experience in property management, hospitality, or retail
  • At least two years working in one of those industries, with real exposure to rent collection, accounts receivable, and basic budget awareness
  • Comfort with Yardi or comparable property management software
  • Genuine ability to connect with people in conversation, not just on paper
  • Active presence on social media platforms, with the instinct to create content that actually represents a community well
  • A current real estate license, or the willingness to obtain one within 90 days of hire where required
  • A polished, professional appearance that reflects the brand

The salary range sits between $60,000 and $66,000, with bonus eligibility on top of that. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, 20 days of paid time off plus holidays, a 401(k) with company match, and tuition reimbursement.

Strong candidates for this role typically have one quality that separates them from the rest: they're equally comfortable closing a lease and having a hard conversation with a resident about a late payment. Both require trust-building, and both happen on the same shift. If you lean heavily toward one and avoid the other, this role will feel unbalanced quickly.

For someone who performs well here, the natural next step is a General Manager or Property Manager role, either within Bozzuto's portfolio or across the broader multifamily industry. The AGM seat is genuinely one of the best training grounds in the business.

greenhouse_5201959008.title: Assistant Maintenance Manager
greenhouse_5201959008.rewritten_description:
It's 7:15 on a Saturday morning and a resident has no heat. Your phone buzzes, you run through the likely culprits in your head before you've even had coffee, and by 9 a.m. the issue is resolved and documented. That's the job, and if that scenario sounds more energizing than exhausting, keep reading.

What This Role Actually Involves

Bozzuto is looking for an Assistant Maintenance Manager at one of their Alexandria, VA communities. The title says "assistant," but the scope is real. You're co-running the maintenance operation: turns, preventative maintenance, emergency response, and the day-to-day service ticket queue. You'll work hands-on with HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and appliance repair while also keeping an eye on the broader team's performance and professionalism.

The make-ready process is a significant part of this. Turns need to come back clean, complete, and on schedule so leasing can do its job. A slow or sloppy punch list shows up in occupancy numbers fast. You'll own that cycle alongside the maintenance manager and be expected to hold the team to a consistent standard without the leasing office having to chase you for updates.

Preventative maintenance isn't optional here. Bozzuto operates well-maintained, higher-end communities, and asset preservation is taken seriously. If you're comfortable with complex mechanical systems like central plant, boilers, or chillers, that background will be useful. It's not required, but it separates candidates who can grow into a senior role from those who top out early.

Weekend availability and participation in the on-call rotation are real expectations. Worth saying plainly: this role does not have clean 9-to-5 edges.

What You Need to Bring

  • At least 5 years in the trades, facilities, or residential building maintenance
  • HVAC, EPA, and/or NAPE certification
  • Working knowledge of plumbing, electrical, and appliance repair
  • Basic carpentry, drywall, and paint skills for make-ready work
  • Familiarity with OSHA standards, risk management, and MSDS protocols
  • Some supervisory experience or a demonstrated ability to lead a small crew
  • Comfort with technology platforms and basic Microsoft Office proficiency
  • Physical ability to handle the demands: lifting, ladders, stairs, and outdoor work in all weather

The salary range sits between $66,000 and $69,000, with bonus eligibility on top of that. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, 20 days of paid time off plus holidays, a 401k with company match, and tuition reimbursement.

One thing worth noting about Bozzuto specifically: they promote from within more consistently than most operators we've seen at their scale. An Assistant Maintenance Manager who performs well here has a credible path to Maintenance Manager and eventually to a Regional Facilities role. The company tracks certifications and development, so if you're willing to keep building your credentials, the trajectory is there.

greenhouse_5200337008.rewritten_description:
Strong technical skills drive this role. So does the ability to lead a team, manage a punch list, and keep a property running without cutting corners. The Assistant Maintenance Manager position at Bozzuto in Brandywine, MD puts both to work every day.

The Skills This Role Runs On

HVAC is the backbone. You need real hands-on experience with split systems, boilers, chillers, and central plant equipment, not just a passing familiarity. EPA certification matters here. So does working knowledge of plumbing, electrical, and appliance repair. Bozzuto is looking for someone who can diagnose a problem, fix it correctly, and close the ticket without a second trip.

Beyond the technical side, this is a supervisory role. You're not just doing the work. You're modeling how the work gets done. That means coaching your team on safety standards, OSHA compliance, and MSDS handling while keeping the operation accident-free. A safety mindset isn't optional here. It's the baseline.

The make-ready process is another core skill area. Managing turns efficiently, keeping units on schedule, and getting apartments rent-ready without sacrificing quality directly affects the property's occupancy. Delays in turns mean delayed move-ins. That pressure is real, and you'll own it.

What You'll Actually Be Doing

Day to day, you're splitting time between resident service tickets and broader asset preservation. A resident's AC goes down, you handle it. The preventative maintenance schedule needs to run on time, you make sure it does. Snow removal, grounds upkeep, and general cleanliness fall under your watch too. None of it is glamorous, but all of it matters for the property's condition and resident satisfaction.

You'll also be in the on-call rotation and available for weekend work. That's a real commitment. If you've worked in residential property maintenance before, this won't surprise you. But it's worth stating plainly: this role doesn't clock out at 5.

  • 5 or more years in the trades, facilities, or residential building maintenance
  • HVAC, EPA, and/or NAPE certification required or strongly preferred
  • Supervisory or lead experience is a plus
  • Comfort with Microsoft Office and property maintenance software platforms
  • Ability to lift 25 to 50 pounds frequently, climb ladders, and work in varying weather
  • Basic carpentry, drywall, and painting skills

What Sets Strong Candidates Apart

The technicians who stand out in this kind of role aren't just skilled with tools. They think about the building the way an owner would. Bozzuto uses the phrase "know it like you built it," and that's the right mental frame. The best candidates have an instinct for catching problems before they become work orders, and they communicate clearly enough that residents trust them and team members follow their lead.

Bozzuto is a well-regarded operator with a reputation for high standards across its portfolio. Coming in as an Assistant Maintenance Manager here gives you exposure to professional systems and processes that translate directly if you move toward a Maintenance Manager or Chief Engineer role down the road. The salary range for this position is $61,000 to $65,000, with bonus eligibility, benefits including medical, dental, and vision coverage, 20 days of paid time off, a 401k with company match, and tuition reimbursement.

greenhouse_5198596008.title: Assistant Property Manager
greenhouse_5198596008.rewritten_description:
Bozzuto runs some of the better-managed communities in the country, and their Assistant Property Manager role reflects that. This isn't a leasing-only position with a fancy title. You're genuinely second in command, expected to own the financial side, support the team, and step into the Property Manager seat when needed.

What This Role Actually Covers

The financial responsibilities here are real. You'll handle rent collection, manage delinquency, and maintain awareness of the community's P&L. If you've only ever done leasing and toured prospects around, this role will stretch you. That's not a bad thing, but go in with clear eyes.

On the leasing side, you're conducting tours and converting traffic into signed leases. Bozzuto expects those tours to feel personalized, not scripted. You're also responsible for maintaining the physical presentation of the community, inside and out, and making sure the team projects the same level of professionalism. Social media content creation is part of the job too, specifically Instagram and Facebook, so comfort with that is genuinely expected, not just a checkbox.

Weekend availability is part of the deal. One to two weekends per month, with compensating days off during the week. That's standard for most communities doing any real leasing volume, and Kirkland is an active submarket.

What You'll Need

  • A four-year degree or equivalent experience in property management, hospitality, or retail
  • At least two years in a relevant customer-facing or operations role
  • Some exposure to budgets, revenue tracking, or P&L management
  • Proficiency with Yardi or similar property management software
  • Solid written and verbal communication skills
  • Real sales ability, not just friendliness

Worth Knowing Before You Apply

The APM role is one of the cleaner paths to a Property Manager title in this industry. You're building the exact skill set required: financial oversight, team leadership, leasing performance, and operations. At a company like Bozzuto, that progression is more structured than you'd find at a smaller owner-operator. The salary range sits between $54,080 and $58,240, with bonus eligibility on top of that. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, 20 days of PTO plus holidays, a 401k with company match, and tuition reimbursement.

If you've been doing leasing for a couple of years and you're ready to stop handing off the hard conversations to someone else, this is the step up that actually teaches you the business.

greenhouse_5197373008.title: Evening Concierge
greenhouse_5197373008.rewritten_description:
What You'll Actually Do

This role runs Monday through Friday, 11am to 8pm, which means you're the face of the building during the hours residents actually use it. You're not managing a back-office inbox. You're greeting people coming home from work, handling the wave of packages that stacks up every afternoon, and solving whatever comes up before the evening shift ends. Small stuff and not-so-small stuff, back to back.

Bozzuto operates a portfolio of high-quality residential communities, and at this San Francisco property the concierge desk functions as the heartbeat of the resident experience. You'll plan and execute community events that actually get people to show up, not just calendar invites that get ignored. You'll manage front desk logs, coordinate club room and freight elevator reservations, and keep the package room from descending into chaos. You'll also help build the community's online reputation by encouraging satisfied residents to share their experiences on review platforms.

The social media piece is real work here. Bozzuto communities use social channels to generate leasing interest and keep current residents engaged, and you'll contribute to that effort with content that reflects the energy of the property.

What You Bring

  • At least two years working in hospitality, hotel, retail, or travel, where reading people quickly and responding gracefully was part of the job
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including comfort with digital tools, apps, and property software
  • A professional presence and genuine attention to detail
  • The ability to anticipate what someone needs before they ask for it
  • Physical ability to lift up to 25 pounds (package volume gets real during the holidays)

Context Worth Knowing

San Francisco's luxury residential market is competitive, and residents in Class A buildings have high expectations baked in from day one. The concierge role at this level isn't just about being friendly. It's about consistency. Residents notice when the experience slips, and they notice when it's excellent. Your ability to remember names, preferences, and even pets by name is the kind of detail that drives renewal decisions and five-star reviews more than any amenity upgrade can.

The 11am to 8pm window is worth thinking about honestly. You'll catch the tail end of move-ins, the full afternoon delivery surge, and the early evening resident return. It's a high-touch shift. People are tired after work and want things handled quickly and warmly. If you've thrived in a hotel front desk or concierge role where the afternoon-to-evening transition is the busiest stretch, that experience maps directly here.

The salary range for this position is $55,000 to $58,000, with bonus eligibility, benefits including medical, dental and vision coverage, 20 days of paid time off plus holidays, a 401k with company match, and tuition reimbursement.

greenhouse_5198386008.rewritten_description:
It's 6pm on a Thursday. A resident walks through the lobby after a long commute, carrying groceries and looking frazzled. You greet them by name, hand them the package that arrived that afternoon, and mention that the rooftop event this Saturday starts at 7. They leave the lobby smiling. That's the job, distilled.

What This Role Actually Involves

Bozzuto is hiring an Evening Concierge for a residential community in Hackensack, NJ. The shift runs Tuesday through Saturday, 3pm to 11pm, which means you own the building's most active hours: commuter arrivals, package rushes, evening amenity use, and weekend energy. You're the face residents see most often.

The responsibilities span a wider range than most people expect from a concierge title. Yes, there's front desk work: managing logs, coordinating freight elevator reservations, keeping the package room organized (especially during the holidays, when volume spikes hard). But there's also genuine community-building work. You'll plan and execute resident events, manage social media presence to build visibility, and actively encourage satisfied residents to share their experiences online. The role blends hospitality, light marketing, and operational detail into a single position.

Bozzuto describes its culture around four values: concern, creativity, passion, and the pursuit of perfection. Those aren't just wall art. A company that builds, manages, and maintains its own communities tends to have more internal consistency than a third-party operator juggling dozens of unrelated clients. That matters for a concierge role because brand standards stay stable.

What You Bring

  • At least two years working in hospitality, retail, hotel, or travel environments
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Comfort with software, apps, and property-related computer systems
  • A detail-oriented mindset and a habit of anticipating needs before they're voiced
  • Professional appearance and a genuine interest in people
  • Ability to lift up to 25 pounds for package handling

The salary range is $48,000 to $50,000 annually, with bonus eligibility on top of that. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, 20 days of paid time off plus holidays, a 401k with company match, and tuition reimbursement.

One thing worth knowing: concierge roles at well-run residential communities are legitimate entry points into property management careers. The skills you build here, reading residents, managing competing priorities under time pressure, executing events, maintaining a brand standard consistently, translate directly into leasing consultant and assistant manager roles. If you're thinking about where this leads, the path is real and well-worn at companies like Bozzuto that promote from within.

greenhouse_5198826008.title: Executive Concierge
greenhouse_5198826008.rewritten_description:
Luxury residential communities live and die by the quality of their front-of-house experience. When a prospect walks through the lobby at a Bozzuto property in Cambridge, the Executive Concierge is often the first human impression they get. That moment either converts or it doesn't. This role exists to make sure it converts, and then keeps residents happy enough to renew.

Bozzuto is hiring an Executive Concierge at their Cambridge, MA community. The base salary runs $55,000 to $58,000, with additional bonus opportunities on top of that. This is not a pure front desk job. You're part operator, part hospitality lead, and part team coach. When the property manager or assistant PM isn't on site, you step into that leadership gap without being asked.

What the Day Actually Looks Like

Your shift might open with a package room that needs organizing before the morning rush, a follow-up call to a resident whose maintenance request went sideways, and a quick check on the club room reservation log before a weekend event. By mid-morning you're greeting prospects by name if you've met them before, and working to learn new names fast if you haven't. Resident retention is a real KPI here. The relationship you build with a resident in month two is what influences whether they renew in month eleven.

Bozzuto takes resident events seriously as a retention tool, and you'll plan and execute them. You'll also manage the property's social media presence, including encouraging happy residents to post reviews publicly. Those reviews feed traffic. Traffic feeds occupancy. It all connects.

Weekends and evenings are part of the rotation, depending on your assigned shift. That's worth knowing upfront.

What Bozzuto Needs From You

  • At least 2 years in hospitality, retail, hotel, or a similarly service-intensive environment
  • Genuine comfort with social media content creation on platforms like Instagram and Facebook
  • Strong written and verbal communication, and a professional appearance that matches a luxury building
  • Comfort with software, apps, and property management tools
  • Ability to lift up to 25 pounds (package volume gets real during the holidays)
  • An instinct for anticipating what someone needs before they ask

What separates a strong candidate from an average one here isn't just friendliness. It's the ability to hold relationship detail in your head. Knowing a resident's dog's name, remembering that another one travels every other week and needs packages held, noticing when a prospect seems hesitant and knowing how to reopen that conversation naturally. That kind of attentiveness doesn't come from a checklist. It has to be genuine.

Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, 20 days of paid time off plus holidays, a 401k with company match, and tuition reimbursement. Bozzuto also offers employee resource groups and invests meaningfully in internal career development, which matters if you're thinking about where this role leads. Executive Concierge experience at a well-run Bozzuto community is a real stepping stone toward leasing consultant or assistant property manager positions for people who want to grow in residential management.

greenhouse_5198537008.title: Floating Maintenance Technician
greenhouse_5198537008.rewritten_description:
The Role in Context

Floating maintenance roles are operationally demanding in a specific way. Instead of owning one community's punch list, you're moving across multiple properties, picking up wherever the gap is. That means your diagnostic speed matters. You don't have weeks to learn a building's quirks. You need to walk in, assess, and execute.

Bozzuto operates across a portfolio of residential communities, and this technician position supports that network from a Chapel Hill base. The work spans the full maintenance spectrum: service ticket resolution, make-ready turns, preventative maintenance, and after-hours emergency response when something breaks at 11pm and a resident is waiting.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Day to day, you're resolving maintenance issues across HVAC, electrical, plumbing, and appliance repair. Beginner to intermediate proficiency covers the baseline. You're also contributing to turns, which means prepping vacant units for move-in through repairs and improvements that directly affect lease-up readiness and resident satisfaction scores. Grounds upkeep, snow removal, and general building cleanliness round out the scope.

  • HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and appliance repair at a beginner to intermediate level
  • Turn and make-ready work on vacant units
  • Preventative maintenance and general upkeep
  • On-call rotation for after-hours emergencies
  • Weekend and evening availability as needed
  • Physical capability to frequently move 25 to 50 pounds
  • Personal, reliable transportation (required for on-call response)
  • Comfort with software and mobile apps used for work orders

Strong candidates here aren't necessarily the most experienced technicians in the room. What separates them is response reliability and communication. A resident-facing maintenance role lives or dies on follow-through. If you close a ticket cleanly, communicate clearly, and show up on call without drama, you'll stand out fast.

Growth and Compensation

The base salary is $48,000, with additional bonus opportunities on top of that. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, 20 days of paid time off plus holidays, a 401k with company match, and tuition reimbursement. One specific perk worth noting: after your 12-month anniversary, Bozzuto covers your EPA 608 Universal Refrigerant Certification in full. For anyone looking to sharpen their HVAC credentials without paying out of pocket, that's a real tangible benefit.

From a career trajectory standpoint, floating technician roles build something most single-property positions don't: cross-portfolio exposure. You see how different communities are operated, where processes break down, and how maintenance coordinators and property managers interact with maintenance under pressure. That breadth is often what accelerates a move into a lead technician or maintenance supervisor role down the line.

Bozzuto is hiring a Leasing Consultant at their Bayonne, NJ community. You'll spend a meaningful portion of your week on follow-up. Converting initial leads into scheduled tours requires persistence without being pushy, and that's a real skill. Strong written communication matters just as much as verbal here because a lot of those touchpoints happen over email, text, or social media before a prospect ever walks through the door.

Social media fluency is genuinely part of the job description, not a soft add-on. greenhouse_5192611008.title: Maintenance Manager
greenhouse_5192611008.rewritten_description:
The Skills This Role Lives On

Maintenance management at Bozzuto is fundamentally a leadership role that happens to require deep technical fluency. You're not just fixing things. You're teaching others how to fix things, building the systems that prevent things from breaking, and making judgment calls that protect both the resident experience and the asset value of the property.

The technical foundation matters a great deal here. Advanced HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and appliance repair aren't nice-to-haves; they're the credibility that earns a team's respect and allows you to diagnose problems quickly, assign work intelligently, and know when a vendor is padding scope. Exposure to complex mechanical systems like boilers, chillers, and central plant equipment is a genuine differentiator for this position. If you've worked in garden-style communities your whole career, the systems complexity here may be a stretch worth acknowledging honestly.

Equally important is the supervisory craft. With 3+ years of team leadership expected, Bozzuto is looking for someone who has already made the mental shift from individual technician to multiplier. That means you've hired people you're proud of, coached techs through difficult repairs rather than just handling them yourself, and built a team culture where accountability is normal rather than punitive.

What You'll Be Building and Protecting

Day to day, this role operates across several distinct functions. The make-ready and turnover process demands attention to both speed and quality. Every day a unit sits vacant is lost revenue, so your ability to manage a punch list efficiently and keep turns on schedule directly affects NOI. Preventative maintenance programs protect the long-term value of the asset. Vendor management keeps capital improvement projects on budget. And emergency on-call coverage means the role doesn't fully clock out at 5pm, which is an honest reality worth understanding upfront.

  • 7+ years of facilities or residential building maintenance experience
  • 3+ years leading maintenance teams, including hiring and development
  • HVAC, EPA, and/or NAPE certification
  • Working knowledge of OSHA, risk management, and MSDS standards
  • Comfort with Microsoft Office and property operations technology platforms
  • Physical ability to lift 25 to 50 pounds frequently and work in varying weather conditions
  • Availability for emergency response and on-call rotation

What Strong Candidates Bring That Average Candidates Don't

The people who thrive in this role tend to think like owners. They track recurring work orders and ask why a repair keeps coming back. They build vendor relationships before they need them urgently. They treat a resident's service ticket as a promise, not a task in a queue. Bozzuto uses the phrase "know it like you built it," and that mentality is genuinely useful here because the best maintenance managers develop an almost institutional knowledge of their property's quirks, histories, and vulnerabilities.

This role also builds skills that transfer well across the industry. Managing capital projects sharpens budgeting instincts. Leading a team through a high-volume turn season develops operational planning skills. Both are directly relevant if your long-term interest is facilities director or regional maintenance oversight. Bozzuto's investment in tuition reimbursement and career development reflects a company that takes that trajectory seriously.

The compensation for this position is $72,800, paired with bonus eligibility, health, dental, and vision coverage, 20 days of paid time off plus holidays, and a 401k with company match.

greenhouse_5200030008.title: Maintenance Technician
greenhouse_5200030008.rewritten_description:
Skills This Role Runs On

This Maintenance Technician position at Bozzuto's Sunnyvale, CA community puts four skill sets to work every single day: HVAC troubleshooting, plumbing, electrical repair, and appliance work. You don't need to be a master of all four on day one. Beginner to intermediate proficiency gets you in the door. What matters is that you're comfortable diagnosing problems, completing repairs correctly, and moving on to the next ticket without a lot of hand-holding.

The schedule runs Sunday through Thursday, so Friday and Saturday are your weekend. That's worth knowing upfront because it shapes your life outside work as much as it shapes your shifts.

What You're Actually Doing Day to Day

Service ticket resolution is the core of the job. Residents submit requests, you resolve them. HVAC calls, leaky faucets, tripped breakers, broken appliances. You work through the queue, document your work, and keep residents informed. That last part matters more than people expect. A repair done right but communicated poorly still creates a bad experience.

Beyond tickets, you're turning vacant units for move-in. Make-ready work: punch list repairs, touch-ups, getting the apartment into showing condition. It's detail-oriented work that directly affects how quickly a unit can be leased.

You're also part of an on-call rotation for after-hours emergencies. That's a real commitment. Reliable personal transportation isn't just a preference here, it's a hard requirement so you can respond when something breaks at 11pm.

Grounds upkeep and general building cleanliness round out the role. The physical demands are real too. Expect to lift and carry between 25 and 50 pounds regularly throughout a shift.

What Separates Strong Candidates Here

Bozzuto operates Class A communities and holds service quality to a high standard. The technicians who do well here aren't just mechanically competent. They communicate clearly with residents, show up looking professional, and treat every interaction as part of the resident experience, not a distraction from the repair work.

One practical upside worth knowing: after your 12-month anniversary, Bozzuto covers the cost of your EPA 608 Universal Refrigerant Certification. For someone early in their HVAC career, that's a meaningful credential paid for by the company rather than out of your own pocket. It also signals something about how this employer approaches technician development.

  • Experience in building maintenance or a trades education background
  • Beginner to intermediate HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and appliance repair skills
  • Availability for on-call emergency response, including weekends and evenings
  • Reliable personal vehicle
  • Strong written and verbal communication
  • Basic computer skills for work order software and apps
  • Ability to lift 25 to 50 pounds frequently

Compensation for this role sits between $54,110 and $58,000 annually, with bonus eligibility on top of base pay. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, 20 days of paid time off plus holidays, a 401k with company match, and tuition reimbursement.

Maintenance tech work at a Bozzuto community in Lake Worth comes down to a specific combination of technical range and people skills. You're not a specialist here. You're handling HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and appliance repair across a single property, which means your value is in breadth. Beginner-to-intermediate proficiency across those trades is the baseline. What separates a good tech from a great one is the ability to triage quickly, communicate clearly with residents, and keep the punch list moving without constant supervision.

Turns matter here too. Preparing vacant units for move-in is a real part of the job, and how efficiently you move through make-ready work affects the property's ability to lease. A tech who treats turns as an afterthought tends to create bottlenecks at exactly the wrong time.

What the Day Actually Looks Like

You'll work through a service ticket queue, handle preventative maintenance tasks, support grounds upkeep, and jump into turns when units come available. Bozzuto properties are known for a higher standard of presentation, so general cleanliness and building aesthetics are part of your responsibility, not just an occasional ask. This is South Florida, so HVAC calls aren't seasonal. They're year-round, and resident tolerance for a down A/C unit is low. You should expect that reality.

On-call rotation is part of the deal. After-hours emergencies happen, and you'll need reliable personal transportation to respond. That's not unique to Bozzuto, but it's worth saying plainly: this isn't a strictly 9-to-5 position.

greenhouse_5200104008.rewritten_description:
It's 7 a.m. on a Monday. A resident submitted a ticket over the weekend: no hot water. You're the first person they see, and how you handle the next 30 minutes sets the tone for their entire week.

Bozzuto is hiring a Maintenance Technician for their community in Burke, VA. This is a hands-on, full-cycle maintenance role covering everything from daily service requests to unit turns and grounds upkeep.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Most of your day runs on service tickets. HVAC, plumbing, electrical, appliance repair. You diagnose the problem, fix it correctly, and close it out. Residents notice when you do it fast and when you do it right. Both matter here.

Unit turns are a regular part of the job. When a resident moves out, you go in, assess the punch list, and get the apartment ready for the next move-in. You're not just patching walls. You're resetting the unit to a standard that justifies the rent.

General upkeep rounds out the role: building cleanliness, grounds maintenance, and snow removal when the season calls for it. You'll also rotate on-call for after-hours emergencies. That part's non-negotiable, and it's worth understanding upfront before you apply.

What You Need to Bring

  • Hands-on experience in building maintenance or a trades education background
  • Beginner to intermediate skills across HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and appliance repair
  • Ability to lift and carry 25 to 50 pounds frequently as part of daily work
  • Reliable personal transportation for commuting and on-call response
  • Basic computer skills for work order systems and communication
  • Strong communication, a professional appearance, and a genuine service mindset

You don't need to be a master of every trade on day one. Bozzuto is looking for someone with solid fundamentals and the willingness to keep learning. After your 12-month anniversary, they'll cover the cost of your EPA 608 Universal Refrigerant Certification. That's a real credential that transfers anywhere in this industry.

The salary for this role is $50,000, with bonus opportunities on top of that. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, 20 days of paid time off plus holidays, a 401k with company match, and tuition reimbursement.

One thing worth noting for anyone thinking about career trajectory: technicians who build strong diagnostic skills and a reliable on-call track record tend to move into Lead Tech or Service Manager roles faster than those who only handle routine tickets. If that path interests you, this is a reasonable starting point with a company that has the portfolio size to promote from within.
