greenhouse_5146892007.rewritten_description:
The Skills That Drive This Role

Maintenance supervision at a mid-size multifamily community runs on diagnostic thinking, trade breadth, and the ability to move between hands-on work and team coordination without losing momentum on either. At 4400 Syracuse Apartments in Denver, MG Properties is looking for a Maintenance Supervisor who can do both. You're not just executing repairs. You're triaging incoming service requests, assessing what your team can handle versus what needs outside coordination, and keeping the physical asset in the kind of condition that supports occupancy and resident retention.

Denver's multifamily market has seen sustained demand across its urban corridors, and properties along the I-25 spine have stayed competitive partly on the strength of their upkeep. A well-run maintenance operation directly supports a community's ability to hold occupancy and minimize costly turns. That connection between maintenance quality and NOI isn't abstract here. It shows up in resident renewals, in punch list efficiency on vacant units, and in how quickly a make-ready moves from notice-to-vacate to rent-ready.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Day to day, you'll diagnose and perform routine repairs across all trade areas, or delegate them to your team and inspect the completed work. You'll manage the service request pipeline, schedule maintenance personnel in coordination with the property manager, and run regular safety meetings to keep your team sharp and compliant. Preventive maintenance tracking and accurate record-keeping for expenditures are part of the job. So is equipment maintenance oversight.

The qualification floor here reflects the scope: at least two years in a supervisory maintenance role and experience on properties of 150 units or more. Multi-trade competency is required. If you've only worked in one trade, this role will stretch you in ways you may not be ready for.

  • 2+ years of maintenance supervisor experience preferred
  • Experience managing maintenance at a community of 150+ units
  • Demonstrated competency across multiple trade areas
  • Valid driver's license and reliable transportation required
  • Strong customer service orientation and team-first mindset

What MG Properties Offers and What Sets Them Apart

Compensation ranges from $36 to $38.35 per hour depending on experience, with monthly bonuses and company profit sharing on top of base pay. The benefits package includes medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401(k) with employer match, life insurance, FSA and dependent care spending accounts, paid sick time, holidays, personal days, and rental discounts. PTO accrues from day one.

MG Properties has been acquiring, developing, and managing apartment communities across the Western U.S. for over 30 years. That kind of institutional continuity matters in maintenance leadership. It means you're working within established systems rather than building them from scratch, and that there's genuine organizational depth behind decisions about capital expenditures, vendor relationships, and team development. Strong candidates here tend to be supervisors who take preventive maintenance seriously rather than running purely reactive, and who treat accurate record-keeping as a professional standard rather than an afterthought. This position is anticipated to be filled in June 2026.

Multifamily operators have learned that lease renewals and resident satisfaction don't happen by accident. They happen because someone is consistently showing up, communicating clearly, and making residents feel like the property actually cares about them. That's the gap this role fills.

MG Properties, a Western U.S. owner-operator with over three decades of apartment acquisition, development, and management behind them, is hiring a Part Time Resident Services Coordinator at Shift Apartments in San Diego. This isn't a traditional leasing role, though you'll assist with leasing when needed. The core of the job is communication and community: handling resident correspondence around lease questions and service requests, planning and running resident events, producing the monthly newsletter and events calendar, and keeping the overall resident experience feeling intentional rather than reactive.

What the Day-to-Day Actually Looks Like

On a typical shift, you might start by working through the communication queue, responding to email inquiries, logging service requests, and following up on anything outstanding. From there, you could be finalizing details for an upcoming resident event, coordinating with vendors or staff, and checking that the amenity spaces are operating properly and policies are being followed. There's also a competitive awareness component: you'll stay current on what nearby communities are offering so the team can respond to market shifts. When leasing needs an extra hand, you step in.

It's a role with real variety, which means you need to be genuinely organized. Dropping the ball on event logistics or letting communication pile up affects residents directly, and residents notice.

Who Tends to Do Well Here

  • Strong written communicators who can shift tone between a friendly event announcement and a policy reminder without sounding robotic
  • People who take initiative on follow-through rather than waiting to be reminded
  • Customer service backgrounds that include handling complaints or escalations calmly
  • Basic computer proficiency and comfort with property management or communication platforms
  • Valid driver's license and flexibility for occasional travel off-site

What separates strong candidates from average ones in this specific role is the ability to build genuine rapport with residents over time. Anyone can answer an email. The people who thrive here are the ones residents actually recognize, trust, and come to with concerns before those concerns become problems. That kind of relationship doesn't come from a script; it comes from consistent, honest communication and follow-through.

This is a part-time position compensated at $23/hour, with monthly bonuses and company profit sharing included. MG Properties also offers paid time off accrual and paid sick time for part-time team members, which is worth noting in a market where part-time benefits are often minimal.

greenhouse_8565409002.rewritten_description:
A Leasing Role Built Around Relationships, Not Just Renewals

Student housing operates on a rhythm that's unlike any other segment of property management. Leases turn on an academic calendar, traffic spikes around housing fairs and move-in weekends, and your residents are navigating a major life transition while they're also deciding whether to re-sign. The Experience Team Member role at Lark Chapel Hill sits right at the center of that dynamic, and it requires someone who genuinely connects with people, not just someone who can recite floor plan pricing.

Scion has built its brand around the student living experience, and this position reflects that. It's part leasing consultant, part community ambassador, part administrative coordinator. On any given day, you might be giving a tour to a prospective resident and their parents in the morning, helping coordinate a resident engagement event in the afternoon, and fielding a package pickup or lockout call in the evening. The variety is real, and so is the pace.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Your core focus is customer interaction: tours, follow-ups, fielding objections, and communicating what makes the community worth choosing. You'll also contribute to local marketing efforts and assist with social media content, which means you need to understand both the sales side and the storytelling side of leasing. Beyond the front-facing work, there's property administration involved: maintaining office organization, logging and retrieving packages, scheduling maintenance requests, and supporting the overall presentation of the clubhouse and common areas. Turn periods, which in student housing can mean hundreds of move-ins in a single week, are a critical part of the calendar, and availability during those stretches is a genuine requirement.

  • Conduct community and amenity tours for prospective residents
  • Support social media and resident engagement initiatives
  • Handle package management and general office upkeep
  • Follow up on maintenance requests and communicate status to residents
  • Participate in after-hours on-call rotation, including lockout assistance
  • Relay sales barriers and resident feedback to the management team

Who Tends to Thrive Here

The candidates who stand out in this role aren't necessarily the ones with the most leasing experience. They're the ones who stay composed when three things need attention at once, who communicate clearly with an eighteen-year-old first-year student and their parent in the same conversation, and who take pride in how a space looks and feels. Reliability matters more than polish here. The on-call rotation and Turn availability requirements aren't optional, and the team depends on everyone pulling their weight during the high-demand stretches.

This kind of role also builds a strong foundation for growth in property management. Leasing consultants who develop a feel for traffic patterns, objection handling, and resident relations often move into assistant manager roles, and student housing specifically gives you exposure to lease-up pressure and high-volume operations that translate well across property types. Chapel Hill's market, anchored by UNC, keeps demand active and the leasing environment genuinely competitive, which means the skills you build here are real ones.

Scion offers health, dental, and vision coverage, 401k matching, paid parental and maternal leave, PTO, and learning reimbursement. A discretionary annual bonus is also part of the package. Work authorization is required; visa sponsorship is not available.

greenhouse_8565382002.rewritten_description:
What You'll Actually Do

The Experience Team Member role at The Magnolia at Auburn sits at the intersection of leasing, marketing, and resident relations. On any given day, you might be touring a prospective resident through the community, responding to a social media inquiry, logging packages, and following up on a maintenance request before your shift ends. That range isn't accidental. Scion builds this role to cover the full front-facing operation of a student housing community, which means you're rarely doing the same thing twice.

Touring is central. You'll walk prospects through amenities, handle objections in real time, and report sales barriers back to the management team so pricing strategy and messaging can adjust accordingly. You'll also support local marketing efforts, assist with resident engagement events, and help maintain the kind of community presence that keeps occupancy strong through the competitive student leasing cycle.

Property administration rounds out the role. Package management, office upkeep, maintenance request coordination, and after-hours lockout coverage are all part of the job. These aren't glamorous tasks, but they're where residents form their strongest impressions of a community's management.

What You Bring

  • Genuine comfort talking to a wide range of people, including prospective residents, parents, and current residents with complaints
  • Reliability during high-stakes periods: summer, holidays, and Turn (the concentrated move-in/move-out cycle that defines student housing operations)
  • Self-discipline to handle an on-call rotation without needing constant supervision
  • Flexibility when priorities shift mid-shift, because they will
  • Basic comfort with social media platforms used for community communication and marketing

What This Role Builds

Student housing leasing sharpens skills that transfer directly into conventional multifamily. You'll develop the ability to read traffic patterns, respond to seasonal leasing pressure, and communicate concessions and incentives clearly without overselling. The Turn period in student housing is one of the most operationally demanding experiences in residential property management. Executing it well, even in a supporting role, demonstrates a level of operational awareness that carries real weight on a resume.

Strong candidates here aren't necessarily the most extroverted people in the room. They're the ones who follow through consistently, stay professional when residents are frustrated, and treat the administrative side of the job with the same care they give the sales side. The two are inseparable in student housing, and the candidates who understand that early tend to advance quickly.

greenhouse_4258976009.title: Leasing Consultant
greenhouse_4258976009.location: Hawthorne at Hixson - 5883 Verdant Way - Hixson, TN - 37343
greenhouse_4258976009.rewritten_description:
Leasing consultants at garden-style communities in suburban markets like Hixson carry a specific kind of weight. Chattanooga's north shore corridor has seen steady residential growth, and properties in the Hixson submarket compete on experience as much as price. That means the person handling tours, follow-up calls, and move-in paperwork isn't just processing leads. They're often the deciding factor in whether a prospect signs or keeps shopping.

What the Role Actually Covers

Hawthorne Residential Partners calls this position a Leasing and Live It Specialist, which signals something about how the company thinks about front-line leasing. The work spans the full leasing cycle: greeting walk-ins, conducting personalized tours, working phone and email inquiries, completing applications and move-in paperwork accurately, and contributing to occupancy and renewal goals. You'll also support resident retention through event coordination and community engagement, help maintain a clean and welcoming office environment, and stay current on competing properties and local market conditions.

The schedule runs Monday through Friday, 9 to 6, and Saturdays from 10 to 4, with one weekday off each week to keep the total at 40 hours. Occasional evenings may come up around resident events, so some schedule flexibility is realistic to expect.

What Sets Strong Candidates Apart

One year of customer service, sales, or leasing experience is preferred but not required. What actually separates people who thrive in this role from those who struggle is the combination of genuine follow-through and the ability to read a prospect's priorities quickly. A lot of applicants can give a decent tour. Fewer stay organized across 20 or 30 active leads, remember what each prospect said they cared about, and follow up in a way that feels personal rather than scripted. A CALP accreditation is a plus if you have it, and a valid driver's license is required.

Compensation includes an hourly base plus monthly leasing and renewal commissions, along with leasing incentive programs. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401k with company match, paid time off (including your birthday), paid parental and adoption leave, pet insurance, company-paid life insurance, and 24/7 telehealth access.

Where This Role Can Go

Hawthorne has a defined career path program, and leasing consultant is a common entry point into assistant community manager roles. The skills built here, specifically traffic management, lease conversion, renewal conversations, and resident communication, transfer directly into that next step. For someone who wants to move into property operations, this role builds the foundation.

  • High School diploma or GED required
  • One year of customer service, sales, or leasing experience preferred
  • Valid driver's license required
  • CALP accreditation is a plus
  • Comfortable with Saturday availability and occasional evenings

Leasing Consultant roles at garden-style apartment communities like Lakeside Village are front-line sales and service positions. You're the first person a prospect meets, and often the last one they talk to before signing. At Paragon Properties in Clinton Township, this role covers the full leasing cycle: traffic, tours, applications, move-ins, and renewals.

What the Job Actually Involves

Most of your day splits between incoming leads and on-site activity. You'll take calls, respond to inquiries, schedule and conduct tours, and follow up with prospects who didn't convert on the first visit. When someone is ready to move forward, you process the application and paperwork for manager review. You also walk vacant units and models regularly to make sure they're showing-ready. Move-in follow-up and work order check-ins keep current residents from going quiet before renewal time.

Marketing and outreach are part of the job too. That includes helping plan and execute local advertising efforts and resident events, not just tracking them on a spreadsheet.

What Paragon Is Looking For

  • At least one year in a customer-facing sales or service role; six-plus months of on-site leasing experience is preferred
  • High school diploma required; some college coursework preferred
  • Solid computer skills including MS Office (Word, Excel, Outlook); Yardi experience is a plus
  • Familiarity with Fair Housing regulations is preferred
  • Strong attention to detail and genuine sales ability

Pre-employment background check, drug screening, and physical are required. The workplace is drug-free.

Compensation and Benefits

Starting pay is $18.50 per hour, negotiable based on prior experience. The position is guaranteed full-time at 40 hours per week. Benefits include paid time off, nine paid holidays, a leasing move-in bonus, rent discount, 401(k) with employer contribution, and medical, dental, and vision coverage with a short waiting period. Company-paid life and disability insurance is also included.

Paragon has a structured training program and an internal advancement track. Consultants who consistently hit occupancy and traffic goals tend to move into assistant manager or property manager roles over time. If you want a clear path upward in property management, this is a reasonable place to start building it.

greenhouse_5230656008.title: Community Manager
greenhouse_5230656008.rewritten_description:
It's a Tuesday morning and your delinquency report is open on one screen while a prospective resident waits at the leasing desk. Your maintenance supervisor is texting about a delayed turn on Unit 204, and your Regional Manager wants updated occupancy numbers by noon. This is the pace of a Community Manager role at Ackermann Group, and it rewards people who can triage, delegate, and still close a lease before lunch.

The Role

Ackermann Group has been operating in the Midwest since 1938, and their Lexington presence reflects that same long-view approach to property management. As Community Manager, you'll carry full operational responsibility for your site. That means owning the budget, keeping occupancy healthy, leading a combined leasing and maintenance team, and functioning as the primary decision-maker when residents or prospects bring concerns to the door.

Day-to-day, you'll work closely with your Maintenance Supervisor to keep turns moving, grounds maintained, preventative maintenance on schedule, and service requests closed out efficiently. On the financial side, you'll use Yardi Voyager and associated reporting tools to track property-level performance and flag anything that's drifting from plan. Capex projects at the site level fall under your ownership as well, coordinated with leadership. Marketing strategy is a collaborative effort with the regional team, but execution lives with you.

People management is a real part of this job. You'll partner with a recruiter and your Regional Manager to hire leasing and maintenance staff, set performance goals, and build the kind of internal communication cadence that keeps a team aligned without constant hand-holding.

What Ackermann Is Looking For

  • At least two years of residential property management experience, or comparable leadership in operations or performance management
  • Demonstrated ability to meet a community's financial goals, not just track them
  • Proficiency in property management software, specifically Yardi Voyager, Rent Cafe CRM, EliseAI, and AIRM are all mentioned as preferred
  • Solid working knowledge of Fair Housing laws
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • High school diploma required; bachelor's degree preferred
  • CAM certification preferred
  • Availability Monday through Friday, 9am to 6pm, plus at least one Saturday per month

Lexington's multifamily market has seen steady absorption over the past few years, with newer Class A product applying real pressure on older communities to compete on service and retention rather than just amenities. A Community Manager here who understands how to minimize MTM exposure and keep renewal traffic strong will have a measurable advantage. Ackermann's emphasis on a personal, community-focused culture suggests their properties lean into resident relationships as a differentiator, which makes soft skills genuinely matter alongside the financial acumen.

One thing that separates strong candidates in this type of role: the ability to read a T-12 and connect what they see there to specific operational decisions they've already made. Hiring managers at well-established owners like Ackermann tend to probe for that connection in interviews. Candidates who can speak to a time they improved NOI or reduced delinquency through a concrete operational change will stand out from those who can only describe their responsibilities.

Compensation includes a base salary with quarterly bonus potential and commission on new and renewed leases. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401k with company match, paid time off, a birthday holiday, an employee rent discount at any Ackermann community, and access to career coaching and development resources.

greenhouse_5231218008.title: Maintenance Supervisor
greenhouse_5231218008.rewritten_description:
Maintenance Supervisors at the apartment level wear a lot of hats, but the ones who excel understand the difference between fixing things and managing a maintenance operation. This role at Ackermann Group's Lexington community leans heavily on both.

The Skills This Role Requires on Day One

You'll need hands-on trade proficiency across plumbing, electrical, carpentry, HVAC, appliance repair, and painting. Specialist-level troubleshooting isn't something you'll grow into here; it's what you'll be expected to bring. EPA Type I and II Certification is required before you start, and experience with Aquatherm systems is a genuine plus given the mechanical demands of maintaining a residential campus.

Beyond the tools, this role demands real organizational discipline. You'll manage a maintenance budget, control parts inventory, negotiate rates with vendors, and coordinate contractor services. Those aren't tasks you hand off; they're responsibilities you own. Familiarity with Microsoft Office and whatever property management software Ackermann runs is necessary for documenting work orders, tracking spend, and reporting to the Community Manager.

The make-ready process sits at the center of your daily rhythm. Keeping the unit turn schedule on track, ensuring vacant units are market ready, and making sure amenities stay in showing condition are all non-negotiable. Delinquency in any of those areas shows up fast in occupancy numbers.

What This Role Builds

If you're a strong technician stepping into supervision for the first time, or an experienced supervisor refining your leadership approach, this position develops a specific set of skills that carry significant weight in property management careers. Running meaningful team meetings, participating in hiring, and coordinating capital improvement projects alongside the Community Manager gives you exposure to the operational and financial side of running a community that purely technical roles don't offer. Supervisors who get comfortable with capex planning and vendor negotiation often move into regional or facilities director tracks over time.

The on-call rotation is honest work. After-hours emergency calls are part of this role, and candidates who thrive here tend to be the ones who treat that responsibility as part of the job rather than an inconvenience. Ackermann has been operating in the Midwest since 1938, and that kind of organizational tenure usually means established systems and a maintenance culture that values doing things right over doing things fast.

What Separates Strong Candidates Here

  • Three or more years of broad maintenance experience, with supervisory time on record
  • EPA Type I and II Certification (required, not preferred)
  • CPO and CAMT certifications (preferred and genuinely valued)
  • Comfort managing a preventive maintenance plan end to end, not just responding to reactive requests
  • A valid driver's license and reliable transportation
  • High school diploma or equivalent

The candidates who stand out in roles like this aren't just technically sharp. They communicate clearly with residents, hold their team accountable without micromanaging, and treat the budget like it's their own. Ackermann's stated emphasis on a personal, community-focused approach means the soft skills matter as much as the certifications.

greenhouse_7957683.title: Leasing Consultant (Village on the Lake Apartments)
greenhouse_7957683.rewritten_description:
Leasing is often described as a sales role, and it is. But the consultants who actually build strong occupancy and earn renewals understand that the sales part is the easy half. The harder skill is relationship management: knowing your residents, following up without being pushy, and turning a complaint about a slow service request into a reason someone signs another lease. Van Metre is hiring a Leasing Consultant for Village on the Lake, a residential apartment community in Spring Lake, NC, and this role develops both sides of that equation.

Day to day, you'll be the first person a prospective resident meets, whether they walk in off the street, call ahead, or find the property online. You'll conduct tours, follow up by phone and email, process applications, and work toward occupancy goals through grassroots marketing efforts in the local area. That's the sales side. On the relationship side, you'll check in with current residents, coordinate with the service team on open maintenance requests, help plan resident events, and process lease renewals. You'll also do three exterior inspections each week and flag anything that needs attention, from landscaping to visible property damage, and inspect vacant units to confirm they're ready to show or report what's needed to get them there.

What separates a strong leasing consultant from an average one in a role like this is follow-through. Traffic matters, but unconverted leads and ignored service concerns quietly erode both occupancy and retention. The candidates who thrive here are organized enough to manage follow-up consistently and self-aware enough to know when a resident interaction needs more than a scripted response.

Prior leasing or property management experience is preferred but not required. Van Metre genuinely recruits from hospitality, retail, and customer-facing sales backgrounds, and those environments build skills that transfer well: handling volume, reading people quickly, and staying composed when someone is frustrated. Bilingual candidates are preferred. Weekend availability is required, which is standard for leasing roles where Saturday and Sunday often drive the highest tour traffic.

What you'll bring

  • Experience in customer service, sales, hospitality, or a related field
  • Comfort conducting property inspections indoors and outdoors in varying weather
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills
  • Ability to manage time across competing tasks without losing the personal touch
  • Familiarity with social media as a leasing and marketing tool
  • Bilingual ability (preferred)

Compensation ranges from $18 to $20 per hour depending on experience, with up to $5,000 in annual bonus potential plus leasing and renewal commissions. Van Metre also offers a benefits package that includes medical, dental, and vision coverage, a company-matched 401(k), tuition reimbursement, paid certifications, mentorship programs, and a wellness reimbursement of up to $900 annually. For someone entering property management, the professional development structure here is worth noting: this is a company that treats the leasing consultant role as a starting point, not a ceiling.

greenhouse_6005948004.title: Part-Time Customer Experience Specialist
greenhouse_6005948004.rewritten_description:
It's a Saturday afternoon. You've got three prospective residents touring back-to-back, two resident emails waiting on responses, and a package room that looks like it absorbed a small shipping warehouse. That's a normal shift here, and if that description makes you lean in rather than lean away, keep reading.

What This Role Actually Involves

Cottonwood Residential is hiring a part-time Customer Experience Specialist at Alkire Glen Apartments in Columbus, Ohio. The work centers on two things: helping prospective residents figure out whether this community is the right fit for them, and making sure current residents feel taken care of once they're home. That means you're on the phone, on email, on text, and in person, often switching between all of them within the same hour.

The schedule requires flexibility, including weekends and evenings. That's not a footnote. It's core to the role, so if your availability doesn't stretch that far, this one isn't the right match.

Day-to-day, you'll walk the property regularly, checking vacant units, the tour path, amenities, and anything that needs attention before a prospect or a new move-in sees it. You'll know the current availability cold, including pricing, so you can answer questions without fumbling. You'll help coordinate community events and contribute to social media efforts. You'll keep the package room organized as deliveries come in, which sounds minor until you've worked a community where it isn't managed well.

Cottonwood was an early adopter of Self-Guided Tours, which shifted how prospects interact with the property before they ever talk to a leasing team member. You'll support that experience and help refine it over time.

What Strong Candidates Bring

  • Genuine comfort talking to people who are stressed, excited, or both at once (apartment hunting is often all three)
  • Clear, prompt written communication across phone, email, and text
  • Attention to the physical condition of the property, not just the office experience
  • Weekend and evening availability, consistently
  • Some interest in growing into a management track over time

What separates a good candidate from an average one here is composure when the desk gets busy and the instinct to follow through without being reminded. Plenty of people can be friendly at the front desk. Fewer can handle a full Saturday, stay organized, and still make the last prospect of the day feel like the first one.

This is a part-time role, but Cottonwood has signaled it as a real entry point into property management. Leasing experience translates directly into assistant manager and eventually property manager positions, especially at companies that promote from within. If you're early in your PM career and looking for a place to build the foundation, the customer-facing side of leasing is where it starts.

greenhouse_8564600002.title: Leasing Consultant
greenhouse_8564600002.rewritten_description:
Leasing Consultant roles tend to get undersold. On paper they look like sales jobs with a property management coat of paint, but the reality is more interesting. A good leasing consultant is the first real impression a community makes, the person who converts curiosity into a signed lease, and the connective tissue between the marketing funnel and actual occupancy numbers. At Waypoint Management Services in Davenport, FL, that's exactly what this position is built around.

Day to day, you're managing the full leasing cycle: fielding inquiries, scheduling and conducting tours, handling applicant qualification, preparing lease files, calculating prorations, and coordinating move-ins. You'll track prospect traffic, maintain leasing records, and keep your pipeline organized in Yardi or a CRM. You'll also monitor competitor pricing and community features closely enough to answer the "why here?" question with real confidence rather than rehearsed talking points. Weekend availability is part of the deal, since that's when traffic peaks.

What separates strong candidates here isn't just closing ability. It's follow-through. The consultants who consistently hit occupancy targets are the ones who treat every unanswered inquiry as an open loop, who know their waitlist, and who understand that a lease renewal saved is just as valuable as a new lease signed. Bilingual Spanish speakers have a meaningful advantage in the Davenport market, where a significant portion of prospective residents are more comfortable conducting the leasing conversation in Spanish.

The career trajectory from this role is worth thinking about. Leasing Consultant is one of the cleaner on-ramps into property management because you build skills that compound quickly: Fair Housing compliance, financial literacy around rent calculations and concessions, CRM discipline, and the ability to read a prospect's objection and respond without losing momentum. From here, the natural next step is Assistant Manager, where that leasing foundation gets paired with delinquency management, reporting, and owner communications. Some consultants move into regional leasing or training roles if they develop a strong sense of what makes a leasing process work across multiple properties.

What You'll Bring

  • At least two years of experience in leasing, sales, or hospitality
  • Solid communication skills and a genuine comfort with the sales process
  • Familiarity with Yardi or similar property management software is a plus
  • Working knowledge of Fair Housing regulations
  • Bilingual English/Spanish preferred
  • Availability for weekend rotation
  • Valid driver's license
  • High school diploma or equivalent required

Waypoint offers monthly leasing and renewal bonuses, a leaser-of-the-month monetary reward, an employee housing discount, medical, dental, and vision coverage starting on day one, 401k with company match, 120 hours of PTO in year one, two floating days, and professional development support. The compensation structure is set up to reward performance directly, which matters more in leasing than in most property management roles.

greenhouse_4259362009.title: Leasing Consultant
greenhouse_4259362009.rewritten_description:
Leasing Consultant roles are often treated as entry points, and technically they are. But the ones who treat this position as a craft rather than a stepping stone tend to move fast. A strong leasing consultant at a well-run property builds a skill set that transfers directly into assistant manager, then manager, then regional work. The foundation gets laid here: closing technique, traffic conversion, market awareness, and the resident experience habits that drive renewals and NOI long after the initial lease is signed.

Berkshire Residential Investments operates as both owner and manager, which matters more than it might seem. When the same company owns the asset and runs the day-to-day, there's less friction between leasing goals and operational reality. You're not navigating the gap between a third-party management contract and an ownership group with different priorities. That alignment tends to produce cleaner processes, clearer expectations, and a team culture that takes performance seriously without the dysfunction that sometimes comes with fee management arrangements.

The Edison is looking for a leasing consultant who can hold a 20% or better closing ratio, which is a real benchmark. That number forces you to think about every step of the leasing process: how you qualify traffic, how you conduct a tour, how you follow up, and how you read a prospect's objections and respond to them. Customer service experience translates well here, especially if you've worked in roles where you had to convert interest into a committed decision under some pressure.

Day to day, you're the first impression. Tour routes and model units need to stay in show-ready condition, the leasing office atmosphere sets the tone for every prospect who walks in, and your written and verbal communication with residents reflects the property's brand. You'll also stay current on local market conditions, which over time sharpens your ability to advise a prospective resident honestly rather than just pitch them, and that shift from salesperson to trusted advisor is exactly what separates consultants who get promoted from those who plateau.

What you'll bring

  • At least two years of customer service or sales experience in any industry
  • Comfort with technology and the ability to pick up new platforms without a long ramp
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Attention to detail on administrative tasks, leasing paperwork included
  • A genuine interest in working with a wide range of people and personalities

Berkshire offers three weeks of vacation, a 25% rent discount, personal development plans, and solid insurance coverage. More relevant to someone thinking about career trajectory: the company has a stated commitment to internal growth, and the structure here, owning and managing their own assets, means there are real rungs above this role if you perform.

greenhouse_4257132009.title: Leasing Consultant (Summer Intern)
greenhouse_4257132009.rewritten_description:
Berkshire Residential Investments is running a summer internship for a Leasing Consultant at Tribeca Apartments, and it's worth understanding what that actually means before you apply. This isn't a fetch-coffee-and-file-things internship. You'd be working the leasing office as a functioning member of the sales team, handling traffic, conducting tours, and closing applications. Berkshire holds interns to a closing ratio of at least 20%, which is the same standard applied to permanent staff. That's a real benchmark.

The day-to-day is pretty straightforward: greet prospective residents, walk tour routes and models, keep the leasing office presentable, and follow up with leads. You'd also be expected to stay current on local market conditions and bring ideas to the property manager on marketing and resident satisfaction. The administrative side matters too. Lease files and prospect tracking require accuracy, and sloppy paperwork creates problems downstream that someone else has to clean up.

What separates the interns who get something real out of this from the ones who don't is comfort with rejection and a genuine ability to read people. Leasing is a sales role. You'll have days where traffic is light, your closing rate drops, and you're not entirely sure why. The candidates who push through that, ask questions, and adjust their approach are the ones who tend to get offers or strong references out of it. Two years of customer-facing experience in any industry translates here. Hospitality, retail, food service. If you've handled difficult people under pressure and still delivered, that background carries weight.

What Berkshire is Looking For

  • At least two years of customer service or transferable experience
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills

lever_03b70c48-6ab5-4162-a7aa-c6a66e0826.title: Experienced Field Maintenance Technician (3+ Years Required)
lever_03b70c48-6ab5-4162-a7aa-c6a66e0826.rewritten_description:
The work order hits your queue at 7:45 a.m.: a water intrusion issue flagged at a single-family rental in North Port. By 8:30, you've assessed the source, documented it properly, and already know what parts you need. That's the pace and the standard Lessen operates at.

What Lessen Does and Where You Fit

Lessen sits at the intersection of technology and field operations, managing maintenance across a portfolio that spans more than one million properties and processes upward of 3.5 million work orders per year. The company operates a vetted vendor network and a tech platform built around data and work order management. What that means for a field tech in North Port is straightforward: you're not waiting on direction from a slow-moving maintenance queue. You own your work orders, you manage your materials budget, and you're accountable for the quality of every job you close out.

This isn't a role where quantity is the metric. Lessen specifically prioritizes quality of service, which means a thorough punch list approach matters more than rushing through volume. Clients notice when a make-ready is done right the first time, and that's what drives retention in fee management at this scale.

Role Requirements and Compensation

Lessen requires a minimum of three years of verifiable, hands-on experience in property maintenance or a closely related trade. The pay range starts between $23 and $27 per hour, determined by your actual skill level, relevant competencies, and work history.

  • At least 3 years of hands-on maintenance experience in property management or a related trade
  • Ability to manage work orders independently, including materials and budget oversight
  • Solution-oriented approach to diagnosing and resolving maintenance issues across a dispersed portfolio
  • Willingness to complete OSHA training provided by the company

The compensation package includes a sign-on bonus opportunity, a quarterly discretionary bonus of up to 5% of quarterly earnings, a company fleet vehicle with a fuel card, a $50 monthly tool and equipment allowance, and a $50 monthly cell phone allowance. There is no on-call requirement, and the schedule runs weekdays.

For technicians who want a path forward, Lessen has defined growth into Lead Technician and Field Maintenance Manager roles as the company expands nationally. If you're someone who already thinks in terms of scope, cost, and quality rather than just task completion, that trajectory is realistic here.

One thing worth knowing about the North Port market: Southwest Florida's rapid residential growth means dispersed single-family and scattered-site portfolios are common. Technicians who are comfortable working independently across multiple property types, rather than in a single centralized building, tend to perform best in this kind of setup.

greenhouse_5233022008.title: Assistant Property Manager
greenhouse_5233022008.rewritten_description:
The Role in Context

Bozzuto's Assistant Property Manager position at their Wellington, FL community sits at the intersection of leasing performance and day-to-day operations. This isn't a pure leasing role, and it isn't a back-office admin job either. You're the person who closes tours, monitors delinquency, coaches the team, and holds down the property when the manager is out. At a company like Bozzuto, which manages a significant portfolio of Class A communities, the APM role carries real operational weight.

What the Day-to-Day Actually Looks Like

Mornings might mean pulling a delinquency report and flagging accounts before they age past 30 days. Midday, you're walking a prospective resident through the community, personalizing the tour based on what you learned in the first two minutes of conversation. Afternoons could involve coaching a leasing consultant on follow-up technique or reviewing the exterior with fresh eyes before a regional visit. On weekends (one to two per month, with weekday days off in exchange), traffic tends to spike, and you're the one converting that traffic into signed leases.

Specific responsibilities include:

  • Managing rent collection and keeping delinquency in check
  • Conducting tours that lead to new leases, not just good impressions
  • Maintaining the community's physical presentation, inside and out
  • Using social media platforms including Facebook and Instagram to create content that supports leasing and brand awareness
  • Stepping into the property manager's seat when needed, handling decisions with confidence
  • Coaching and developing team members with a consistent, values-driven approach

Yardi experience is preferred. A real estate license is either required or expected within 90 days of hire, depending on applicable state rules. The salary range runs $56,000 to $64,000, with bonus eligibility on top of base. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, 20 days of PTO plus holidays, a 401k with company match, and tuition reimbursement.

What Separates Strong Candidates Here

The APM who succeeds at Bozzuto isn't just good with people. They're comfortable reading a P&L, spotting a delinquency trend before it becomes a collections problem, and translating that financial awareness into daily team behavior. Two or more years in property management, hospitality, or retail is the baseline. What pushes a candidate from average to strong is the ability to sell, coach, and manage financial outcomes simultaneously without dropping any of the three. A four-year degree or equivalent experience rounds out the profile, but the operational instincts matter more than the credential.

This role is a natural stepping stone toward a Property Manager position, particularly for candidates who use the APM seat to build budget fluency and team leadership experience alongside their leasing skills.

greenhouse_4259998009.title: Community Manager-3700M
greenhouse_4259998009.rewritten_description:
It's a Tuesday afternoon. A prospective resident is touring while your leasing team handles a spike in renewal calls, maintenance has flagged a vendor issue on the punch list, and your regional director wants the month-end variance report by end of day. As Community Manager at Cortland's 3700M community in Dallas, you'll be steering all of that at once without losing composure or quality.

Cortland operates as a vertically integrated multifamily firm, meaning design, construction, and management stay in-house. That structure gives Community Managers more operational context than you'd typically get at a third-party management shop, but it also means you're accountable to a layered set of internal stakeholders alongside your onsite team and residents. The autonomy is real. So is the expectation.

What This Role Actually Covers

This is a full-scope community leadership position. You'll own NOI performance for a multimillion-dollar multifamily asset, which means budgeting, expense control, and revenue generation all sit with you. On the leasing side, you'll set occupancy and revenue targets, coach your team on conversion and pipeline discipline, and work with Cortland's marketing partners to keep traffic healthy and brand presence sharp. Operationally, you'll manage vendor relationships, conduct property inspections, keep the community in compliance with Fair Housing and OSHA standards, and ensure day-to-day execution stays tight.

Resident experience runs through everything. Cortland positions its communities at a premium level, so the expectation isn't just resolving complaints professionally. It's creating an environment where residents genuinely want to stay and renew. You'll handle escalated concerns directly and set the tone your team follows.

Who Fits This Role Well

  • At least two years leading a sales-driven team in a high-velocity environment: multifamily, hospitality, luxury retail, or a comparable field where short-cycle closing and follow-up discipline matter
  • Demonstrated ability to hit and exceed occupancy and NOI targets, with the financial fluency to explain variance and adjust course
  • Comfortable working across corporate partners, centralized support teams, and onsite staff without losing clarity on priorities
  • Proficient in property management software, CRM tools, and Microsoft Office; at ease using social platforms for community marketing and brand storytelling
  • High school diploma required; bachelor's degree preferred

One thing that separates strong candidates here from average ones: financial acumen paired with people instincts. Plenty of managers can read a T-12 or coach a leasing consultant in isolation. Fewer can do both well while keeping delinquency low, maintaining curb appeal, and holding a team accountable without burning them out. Cortland's model rewards managers who treat those as connected, not competing, priorities.

Dallas remains one of the more competitive multifamily markets in the country, with sustained new supply putting pressure on concessions and occupancy across Class A assets. If you've managed through a lease-up or held strong occupancy during a softening rent cycle, that experience will translate directly here.

greenhouse_5147510007.title: Maintenance Technician
greenhouse_5147510007.rewritten_description:
Commercial facilities don't run on good intentions. They run on work orders closed, equipment inspected on schedule, and tenants who notice nothing because everything just works. That's the operational reality this role exists to support. Lincoln Property Company manages north of 680 million square feet of commercial space across the U.S. and internationally, and the Maintenance Technician position in Chantilly, VA sits at the ground level of keeping that portfolio performing.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

This is a hands-on, boots-on-the-floor role working under the direction of a Chief Engineer or Assistant Chief Engineer. Day to day, you're handling the kind of tasks that keep a commercial building running: restroom repairs (toilets, soap dispensers, drain clearing), lamp replacements, air filter swaps, ceiling tile work, fire extinguisher checks, door hardware, minor furniture repairs, and basic painting in equipment rooms. You'll also run to suppliers using a company vehicle when parts are needed, so a clean driving record matters. Mechanical spaces need regular cleaning and inspection, and debris removal is part of the rotation too.

Tenant interaction is real in this role. You'll be communicating with building occupants, contractors, and engineers while work is in progress, so professionalism and clear communication aren't soft skills here, they're operational requirements. Safety compliance is non-negotiable: PPE use, OSHA standards, NEC, NFPA, and fire/life safety protocols are part of every shift.

What You Bring

  • High school diploma or GED
  • Technical or vocational training, or 1 to 2 years of hands-on experience in HVAC, electrical, mechanical, plumbing, or process controls
  • Familiarity with blueprints and local code requirements
  • Comfort with work order systems and basic tools including Microsoft Outlook
  • Any engineering or trade licenses required by local, state, or national regulation
  • Physical ability to lift up to 50 pounds, climb ladders, and work in positions that require stooping, crouching, or kneeling
  • Availability for after-hours, weekends, holidays, and emergency response when the building needs it

Pay for this position runs $26 to $28 per hour. This is a fully on-site role in Chantilly with no remote option.

One thing that separates strong candidates in commercial maintenance from average ones: the ability to prioritize independently when three things need attention at once, communicate clearly with a tenant who's frustrated about a repair timeline, and still close out your work orders accurately by end of shift. Technical skills get you in the door. Judgment and communication are what get you trusted with more complex systems over time. For someone with solid fundamentals who wants exposure to large-scale commercial building operations, this role offers genuine breadth across multiple trade disciplines under experienced engineering leadership.

greenhouse_7749312003.title: Business Manager - Cielo
greenhouse_7749312003.rewritten_description:
What You'll Actually Do

As Business Manager at Cielo, you're running the full operation of a luxury Charlotte community. That means your week spans budget reviews, lease renewal strategy, vendor negotiations, maintenance oversight, and resident relationship management, sometimes all before noon on a Tuesday. You'll own the financial performance of the asset: analyzing monthly numbers, building annual business plans, and sitting down with your Regional Manager and Regional VP to talk through what the T-12 is telling you and where you can tighten NOI. You're not just reporting on performance. You're expected to have a point of view on it.

You'll lead a mixed team of office and maintenance staff, which means your day has real range. One hour you're coaching a leasing consultant on how to convert traffic. The next you're walking a unit punch list with a maintenance tech or reviewing a vendor bid on a one-time capital project. Keeping occupancy strong, delinquency low, and the property in market-ready condition are the core metrics your leadership will measure you against. The role is full-time Monday through Friday with schedule flexibility built in for resident events and the occasional after-hours situation, because that's the nature of managing a Class A community.

What You Bring

  • At least two years of direct property manager experience in multifamily, with Class A luxury experience strongly preferred
  • Comfort reading and interpreting financial statements, budget variances, and monthly performance reports
  • Hands-on experience with RealPage, Knock, or Onesite (a real plus here, not just a nice-to-have)
  • A track record of developing onsite staff, not just directing them
  • Experience bidding and negotiating vendor contracts, both recurring service agreements and project-based work
  • The kind of communication style that works equally well with a frustrated resident, a skeptical investor, and a maintenance tech who needs clear direction

The Honest Picture

Olympus has earned recognition as a top employer in the National Apartment Association for three consecutive years, and a lot of that comes down to how they treat the people doing the actual work. greenhouse_7962132.title: Groundskeeper
greenhouse_7962132.rewritten_description:
Every apartment community makes its first impression before a prospective resident ever steps inside a unit. The condition of the grounds, the cleanliness of the breezeways, the state of the pet waste stations , these details shape how people feel about a place before they've spoken to a single leasing agent. The Groundskeeper role exists because that first impression requires real, consistent, daily effort from someone who actually cares about it.

Weinstein Properties has operated for more than 70 years as a family-owned company, managing over 60 apartment communities across Virginia, North Carolina, Texas, Tennessee, and Georgia. They're not a faceless REIT. They take a hands-on approach to operations, and that philosophy extends to how they invest in their on-site teams. This opening is at Bexley 3Five, a community in South Austin.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Honest answer: this job has some unglamorous parts. Picking up pet waste, trashing out vacant apartments, cleaning up after other people , those tasks are daily and recurring. If you need variety to stay motivated, you'll want to think carefully. But if you're someone who takes satisfaction in leaving a space noticeably better than you found it, that repetition becomes its own rhythm.

Beyond the daily rounds, you'll operate equipment including backpack blowers and power washers, handle light planting and weeding, assist with make-ready support when the maintenance team needs an extra set of hands, and occasionally take on light painting or housekeeping tasks. You'll work Monday through Friday, 8am to 5pm, outdoors year-round. Austin summers are genuinely hot, and this role requires working through that, along with cold snaps, rain, and humidity. Physical stamina matters here: expect prolonged walking and standing, frequent lifting up to 50 pounds, and a lot of bending and stooping.

Who Fits Well Here

The traits Weinstein calls out are worth taking seriously. Reliability isn't a soft quality in this role , if the grounds don't get walked in the morning, nobody else covers it. Self-motivation matters because you'll often be working independently without someone checking in. And a collaborative spirit helps too, because you'll be part of a broader on-site team that includes maintenance techs and leasing staff, all of whom are easier to work with when the person keeping the community presentable communicates well and pitches in without being asked.

  • Reliable and punctual , consistent attendance is foundational to this role
  • Comfortable with physically demanding, outdoor work in all weather
  • Self-directed enough to manage daily tasks without close supervision
  • Willing to take on varied work including light maintenance support
  • Open to learning and growing toward a maintenance technician role over time

The pay starts at $19/hour with quarterly bonuses, and there's a stay-on bonus available after 90 days in good standing (your recruiter can walk through the specifics). Benefits include rent discount, health, dental and vision coverage, a 401k with company match, paid holidays, vacation and sick time, and birthday time off.

One thing worth noting for anyone thinking longer term: Groundskeeper roles at companies that promote from within, as Weinstein explicitly does, are a real entry point into maintenance tech work. You're building familiarity with the physical plant of a property, earning trust with a team, and developing habits that translate directly into a more technical role. It's not a guaranteed path, but it's a genuine one.

What You'll Actually Do

Every morning at Bexley at Anderson Mill, the property's first impression gets set before most residents leave for work. As a Groundskeeper, that first impression is yours to own. You'll walk the community daily, picking up trash and pet waste, clearing debris, and keeping the common areas looking sharp. Blowing off walkways, pressure washing surfaces, pulling weeds, touching up landscaping, helping trash out a vacant unit before a make-ready gets started. These are the rhythms of the role, and they repeat. That's not a warning so much as a reality check: if you take genuine satisfaction in maintaining a standard rather than just completing a checklist, this kind of work is actually fulfilling.

You'll also support the maintenance team when needed, whether that means light painting, housekeeping tasks in common areas, or pitching in on jobs that don't fit neatly into one category. The leasing team notices when the property looks good. Residents notice. Prospective renters notice. Your work shows up in occupancy and in how people feel about where they live.

Weinstein Properties is a family-owned company that's been operating apartment communities for over 70 years, with a portfolio of more than 60 properties across Virginia, North Carolina, Texas, Tennessee, and Georgia. greenhouse_5148140007.title: General Manager - Gresham, OR
greenhouse_5148140007.rewritten_description:
What You'll Actually Do

This is a full-scope General Manager role at a residential apartment community in Gresham, OR. You're not inheriting a finished product and coasting. You're building and leading the on-site team, owning the budget top to bottom, and driving the operational metrics that keep NOI healthy. That means you're accountable for occupancy, delinquency, renewals, and every line item between gross potential rent and net income. Marketing the property, managing turns, approving make-ready costs, and keeping traffic converting to signed leases all fall on your desk.

Day to day, you're splitting time between people management and operational oversight. In the morning that might mean reviewing a delinquency report and coordinating with your team on notices. By afternoon you're approving a vendor invoice, reviewing a lease application, or working through a budget variance with your regional. The role demands someone who can read a T-12, spot where the property is bleeding, and actually fix it.

MG Properties has been acquiring, developing, and managing apartment communities across the Western U.S. for over 30 years. This isn't a startup operation. There's infrastructure behind you, including company profit sharing that connects your site's performance directly to your compensation.

What You Bring

  • Recent hands-on experience managing a multifamily apartment community (not just assistant-level exposure)
  • Supervisory experience: you've hired, trained, and managed on-site staff
  • Demonstrated budget management skills: you can build, read, and defend a property budget
  • Sales and marketing fluency: traffic generation, closing ratios, concession strategy
  • Yardi experience is preferred, not optional in spirit
  • Valid driver's license with proof of insurance

The Operational Reality

General Managers at this level typically sit at the intersection of people leadership and financial accountability in a way that Assistant Managers and Leasing Consultants simply don't. If you perform here, the career path typically opens toward Regional Manager or Director of Operations roles, especially within a company that promotes from within and has a growing Western U.S. portfolio.

The Gresham submarket sits east of Portland, a Class B and C heavy corridor where operational discipline matters more than luxury amenity packages. Residents are price-sensitive. Delinquency management, retention strategy, and controlled turn costs tend to separate the strong GMs from the average ones here more than flashy marketing ever will. If you've kept occupancy above 95% and held delinquency under 2% at a comparable community, that track record will carry serious weight in this search.

Compensation ranges from $85,000 to $95,000 annually depending on experience, with monthly and performance-based incentive bonuses layered on top. The full benefits package includes medical, dental, vision, 401k with employer match, profit sharing, and rental discounts.

It's 10 a.m. on a Saturday and three prospects are lined up to tour a two-bedroom. You've already qualified two of them by phone, pulled their files, and coordinated with maintenance to make sure the unit is show-ready. That's the rhythm of leasing.

The Role

MG Properties is hiring a Leasing Consultant for an apartment community in Gresham, OR. With more than 30 years operating across the Western U.S., MG Properties manages a portfolio built on acquisition, development, and rehabilitation. This isn't a passive administrative role. You're the front line of occupancy, and the metrics reflect it directly.

Day to day, you're converting traffic into signed leases. That means greeting and qualifying applicants, preparing lease documents, and walking new residents through a smooth move-in by staying in close contact with the maintenance team. When a unit turns, you're part of the chain that gets it leased back up quickly. You'll also keep rental files current and accurate, enter data into property management software, and help close out monthly administrative tasks so the property's paperwork stays clean.

Resident relations are part of the job too. When a resident has a maintenance concern or a billing question, you handle it professionally and follow through. Delinquency doesn't fix itself, and neither does a frustrated resident who never heard back. Consistent communication keeps renewals strong and occupancy stable.

What Strong Candidates Bring

  • At least one year of property management or leasing experience (preferred)
  • Genuine sales ability, not just friendliness. You close.
  • Comfort with leasing software and accurate data entry habits
  • Professional communication with both prospects and current residents
  • A team-oriented mindset. Leasing doesn't happen in a silo.

The candidates who stand out in leasing roles aren't just personable. They track their own numbers. They know their closing ratio, they notice when traffic is up but applications are lagging, and they adjust their pitch accordingly. If you've ever looked at a T-3 occupancy trend and thought about what it means for your month, you're already thinking like the right person for this role.

Compensation runs $20 to $22 per hour depending on experience, with monthly bonuses and company profit sharing on top of base pay. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401(k) with employer match, paid holidays, sick time, and a rental discount program.

This role is a real launching pad within MG Properties. The company promotes from within, and leasing is where most property management careers begin. Strong performers here typically move into assistant manager roles, where NOI accountability and full-site operations come into focus.

greenhouse_8567024002.rewritten_description:
Student housing leasing runs on a different clock than conventional multifamily. The academic calendar drives everything: fall turn periods compress a staggering volume of move-ins into a matter of days, summer is peak leasing season rather than a slow stretch, and your residents are 18 to 22 years old with parents often involved in the decision. If you've worked conventional residential leasing and want to try student housing, that context matters before you apply.

What the Role Actually Covers

The Scion Group calls this position an Experience Team Member, and the title reflects the scope honestly. You're not just pulling traffic and closing leases. The role blends leasing, light marketing, customer service, and property administration into one position. On a given day you might be running a community tour for a prospective resident and their parents in the morning, logging and distributing packages in the afternoon, following up on open maintenance requests before close, and jumping on an after-hours lockout call that evening. The on-call rotation is real. It's listed in the requirements, not buried in fine print.

On the sales side, you'll give tours of the community and amenities, work through objections with prospects, and contribute ideas on local marketing and outreach. Scion operates in collegiate markets, so building relationships with campus organizations, local businesses, and student groups is part of the outreach picture. You'll also help manage the community's social media presence and assist in planning resident engagement events.

Property administration is a consistent part of the workload too: keeping the office and common areas clean and organized, scheduling maintenance follow-ups, and handling general operational tasks that keep the property running smoothly day to day.

What the Job Requires

  • Genuine comfort working with a diverse, mostly college-age population and their families
  • Strong verbal communication and the ability to read a room during a tour or a tense conversation
  • Flexibility to work weekends, holidays, and during turn periods when the schedule gets demanding
  • Reliability and self-direction. Managers can't babysit a leasing floor
  • Eligibility to work in the United States (Scion does not sponsor visas)

Where This Role Can Take You

For someone early in a property management career, a student housing leasing role builds a specific and transferable skill set. Turn coordination alone teaches you more about logistics and resident communication than months of conventional leasing. The sales, marketing, and administrative blend here also maps well onto an Assistant Manager or Leasing Manager path, either within student housing or at a conventional Class A or B property. Scion operates communities across multiple university markets, so internal movement is a realistic option for strong performers. The work isn't always easy, but the foundation it builds is solid.

Running a multifamily community at the manager level means wearing several hats at once: financial steward, team coach, leasing driver, and resident advocate. At Hawthorne Residential Partners, one of the top 50 largest multifamily management companies in the country and a company with deep Southeast roots, the Community Manager role at Landmark Apartments in Murfreesboro, TN carries all of that weight and then some.

What This Role Actually Demands

The financial side of this position is real and consequential. You'll own the community's budget, monitor delinquency, oversee deposit accounting, and produce reporting through Yardi. That means reading a T-12 with fluency, not just skimming it. You'll set and adjust pricing strategy to protect occupancy, manage concessions carefully, and partner with ownership on performance expectations. Compliance with fair housing standards and company policy runs underneath all of it.

On the operational side, you'll coordinate with maintenance on work orders and preventative care, manage vendor relationships, and conduct regular property inspections to keep curb appeal and common areas sharp. The leasing function doesn't disappear at this level either. You'll guide your team through traffic, renewals, and lead response, and you'll step in on tours yourself when the situation calls for it.

Team leadership here is hands-on. You'll hire, train, and coach both office and maintenance staff, run weekly alignment meetings, and handle the harder conversations that come with accountability. Escalated resident concerns land on your desk, and how you resolve them shapes the community's reputation, including what shows up in online reviews.

What You'll Need Coming In

  • At least two years of property management experience, ideally progressing through Leasing Consultant and Assistant Community Manager roles
  • Six months of direct community manager experience in multifamily, strongly preferred
  • Working knowledge of Yardi and Knock, preferred
  • A valid driver's license; CAM, CAPS, or a real estate license is a plus
  • High school diploma or GED equivalent required

greenhouse_4260561009.location: 1287 Shoals Apartments - 1287 Cedar Shoals Drive - Athens, GA - 30605
greenhouse_4260561009.rewritten_description:
Hawthorne Residential Partners runs one of the more intentional cultures in Southeast multifamily, and the Leasing Consultant role at their 1287 Shoals community in Athens reflects that. This isn't a post-and-pray leasing job where you sit behind a desk waiting for walk-ins. The expectation is that you're the first and most lasting impression a prospect has of the property, and you carry that responsibility through every tour, every follow-up call, and every renewal conversation.

Athens is a college town with a rental market that moves in cycles tied closely to the academic calendar. That means traffic can spike hard at certain points in the year, and the ability to work a lead list with genuine follow-through, not just reactive inbox management, separates consultants who hit their occupancy targets from those who don't. Strong leasing consultants here understand that a prospect who toured on a Saturday and went quiet isn't a dead lead. They know how to re-engage without being pushy.

Day to day, you'll handle inbound inquiries across phone, email, and web, conduct personalized tours, process applications and move-in paperwork, and contribute to resident events and community programming. You'll also spend time on market surveys and social media outreach to keep the property visible and competitive. The schedule runs Monday through Friday, 9 to 6, and Saturdays from 10 to 4, with one weekday off each week to keep the hours at 40. Some evening availability may come up for resident events.

What Hawthorne Is Looking For

  • High school diploma or GED
  • At least one year of customer service, sales, or leasing experience (preferred, not required)
  • Valid driver's license
  • CALP certification is a plus
  • Genuine comfort communicating in person, by phone, and in writing
  • Ability to handle objections and guide prospects toward a decision without pressure tactics

On the compensation side, the hourly rate is supplemented by monthly leasing and renewal commissions, which means your effort has a direct line to your paycheck. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401k match, paid time off (including your birthday), pet insurance, and paid parental and adoption leave options.

Hawthorne also runs a formal career path program, and this role has a clear next step: Assistant Community Manager. If you want to move toward property operations and eventually run a community, this is a reasonable place to start building that foundation. The leasing role gives you early exposure to occupancy metrics, resident retention, and the administrative side of property management, all of which matter when you step into a management track.

greenhouse_4260123009.title: Leasing Consultant
greenhouse_4260123009.rewritten_description:
Leasing consultant roles at established New England operators tend to be high-touch, relationship-driven positions. At Babcock Towers, a John M. Corcoran property in Boston, that holds true. JMC has been in the business since 1951, and the company still runs with the kind of hands-on culture where a leasing consultant's work is visible and valued.

What the Job Looks Like

Most of your week centers on converting traffic into signed leases. You'll show apartments, walk prospective residents through pricing and lease terms, and process applications. When someone decides to move in, you build the lease package and manage the move-in process so it goes smoothly from start to finish.

You're also responsible for keeping the property's occupancy pipeline active. That means setting your own sales goals and working toward them through online advertising, social media, and local networking. This isn't a role where marketing gets handed off to someone else. You own it at the property level.

Beyond leasing, you'll stay in contact with current residents throughout their tenancy and conduct property inspections to keep curb appeal sharp. The schedule runs Tuesday through Saturday, 9 AM to 5 PM.

What JMC Is Looking For

  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Comfort with computers and standard leasing software
  • Organized, with solid time management habits
  • A genuine, positive presence with prospective and current residents

No prior leasing experience is required. JMC states openly that they want someone eager to learn the business, which means this role is a real entry point, not just a title for someone who already has three years of experience.

Compensation and Benefits

The pay range runs from $24 to $27.50 per hour, plus a $2,500 sign-on bonus. Benefits include medical, dental, vision, and life insurance, paid time off and holidays, and a 401(k) with a company match.

One thing worth noting for candidates new to leasing: this role builds a skill set that transfers directly into assistant manager and property manager positions. The combination of sales, lease administration, resident relations, and basic marketing exposure is exactly what operators look for when promoting from within. JMC has a track record of long-tenured employees, which suggests those paths are real here, not just recruiting language.

greenhouse_4260100009.title: Market Maintenance Manager II
greenhouse_4260100009.rewritten_description:
Maintenance Manager roles at residential communities tend to attract two kinds of candidates: those who want to stay hands-on forever, and those who see the position as a platform. At John M. Corcoran & Company, the structure genuinely supports the second group. JMC has been operating in New England since 1951, and the kind of institutional knowledge that accumulates over that span shapes how their maintenance teams are built and how they're led.

This opening is for a Market Maintenance Manager II based at Union 346 I & II in Somerville, a market where multifamily demand runs high and residents expect responsive, professional service. You'd be responsible for the full physical operation of the community: daily work orders, unit turns and make-readies, preventive maintenance scheduling, inspections, vendor coordination, and budget adherence on supplies and equipment. You'd also supervise maintenance, janitorial, and grounds staff, which means your day includes as much people management as it does building systems.

The on-call rotation is real, and worth naming plainly. After-hours emergencies are part of the job, and candidates who thrive here tend to be the ones who've already made peace with that reality. The upside is that participating in an on-call structure at a company like JMC builds the kind of operational judgment that's hard to learn any other way. When you're the person who responds, troubleshoots, and resolves, you develop a systems fluency that translates directly to Regional Facilities Director and Director of Maintenance roles down the line.

What separates strong candidates here

Technical range matters, but it's not the whole picture. JMC is looking for someone who can keep accurate records, track purchase orders, and communicate clearly with the management team so that unit availability is never a mystery. In a community where occupancy and turn timelines affect NOI, a Maintenance Manager who treats documentation as a core function, not an afterthought, is genuinely more valuable than one who's simply a skilled tradesperson. If you've ever had a leasing team thank you for a punch list that was actually complete, you already understand the dynamic.

  • High school diploma or equivalent; relevant experience considered
  • At least 3 years in trade or general building maintenance
  • Working knowledge of electrical, mechanical, and building systems
  • Demonstrated ability to supervise a team and manage vendor relationships
  • Comfort with safety procedures, compliance expectations, and budget guidelines

The schedule runs Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., with on-call rotation included. Compensation is competitive and includes a $2,500 sign-on bonus, medical, dental, vision, and life insurance, paid time off and holidays, and a 401(k) with company match.

For someone who wants to grow in property maintenance leadership, a company with JMC's tenure and portfolio depth in New England is a credible next step. The skills you build managing a community of this profile compound quickly, especially when you're working inside an organization that has promoted from within for decades.
