greenhouse_4266012009.title: Maintenance Technician - 219
greenhouse_4266012009.rewritten_description:
High-rise and mid-rise maintenance in urban infill markets runs at a different pace than garden-style suburban work. Resident density is higher, service request volume is compressed into vertical space, and curb appeal extends to lobbies, elevators, and rooftop amenities. The Maintenance Technician role at The Grid Soma sits squarely in that environment, supporting Berkshire Residential Investments' in-house management model at a property where physical upkeep directly shapes resident retention and the overall living experience.

What This Role Actually Involves

Berkshire owns and manages its own assets, which means maintenance staff work within a direct chain of accountability rather than through a third-party management layer. That distinction matters: decisions about standards, vendor relationships, and capital priorities stay closer to the people doing the day-to-day work. As a technician here, you'll take ownership of the property's physical condition across plumbing, electrical, appliances, carpentry, and general building systems. You'll assist with inventory control, shop organization, and key security, and you'll serve as an inspector for curb appeal and common area presentation. Safety enforcement is part of the role, not an afterthought.

Resident interaction is constant. Service requests come from people who live where they work and socialize, so responsiveness and attitude carry real weight. Strong technicians in this type of role treat each completed work order as a touchpoint, not just a task.

What Berkshire Looks For

  • At least one year of hands-on maintenance experience in a residential community setting
  • Working knowledge across plumbing, electrical, appliances, carpentry, and general building maintenance
  • Comfort with computers and related applications for work order management
  • Strong written and verbal communication in English
  • A self-directed approach to quality and follow-through on punch list items without being told twice

What separates solid candidates from average ones at a property like this is the combination of technical range and people skills. A technician who can diagnose a plumbing issue quickly and leave the resident feeling genuinely taken care of is rare. Berkshire's in-house model creates room for that kind of professional to grow into lead technician or facilities supervisor roles over time, particularly within a portfolio that spans multiple markets.

Berkshire offers three weeks of vacation, a 25% rent discount, personal development planning, and a full benefits package. The SoMa location puts you in one of San Francisco's denser residential corridors, where building systems tend to be older and more complex, making the technical learning curve real and the skill-building genuine.

greenhouse_5234474008.title: Assistant Maintenance Manager
greenhouse_5234474008.rewritten_description:
Skills That Drive This Role

This position sits at the intersection of hands-on technical work and front-line supervision. The skills it draws on most heavily are trade proficiency across HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and appliance repair, combined with the organizational discipline to manage a make-ready schedule and the interpersonal range to hold a maintenance team accountable without micromanaging. If you've spent years as a technician and you're ready to carry more responsibility for how a building runs, this is the natural next step.

Bozzuto manages a portfolio that skews toward higher-finish, amenity-rich communities, and Arlington is one of their core markets. Properties in the 22202 zip code tend to be mid-rise or high-rise buildings with more complex mechanical systems than you'd find at a garden-style lease-up. Comfort with central plant equipment, split systems, boilers, and chillers is listed as desired here, and in practice it's the kind of experience that separates candidates who can handle the full scope of the role from those who'll need significant ramp-up time.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Day to day, you're splitting time between completing service tickets yourself and making sure your team completes theirs correctly and on time. You're tracking the turn schedule so apartments are punch-listed, made ready, and handed off to leasing before move-in dates slip. You're running preventative maintenance rounds so the building's systems stay ahead of failures rather than chasing them. You're also the person who shows up for the emergency on-call rotation, which means nights and weekends are part of the job. That's worth being clear-eyed about before you apply.

The role carries a "preserve and protect" framing that reflects something real about how Bozzuto approaches asset management. Preventative maintenance programs, safety code adherence, grounds upkeep, and general cleanliness all fall within your scope. The detail orientation required here isn't just about fixing things correctly; it's about catching problems early and keeping the physical asset in the condition that justifies the rents the building commands.

What Bozzuto Brings to the Relationship

The posted salary range runs $63,000 to $65,000, with bonus eligibility on top of that. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, 20 days of paid time off plus holidays, a 401k with company match, and tuition reimbursement. That last item is worth noting: for someone who wants to move from assistant manager to maintenance manager or eventually into a facilities or regional operations role, having tuition support available is a meaningful advantage.

Certifications that matter for this role include EPA 608 for refrigerant handling and HVAC credentials. If you have those plus a genuine supervisory track record, you're in a strong position. If your certifications are current but your leadership experience is thin, be ready to speak concretely about times you've trained or directed other technicians, because that supervisory dimension is central to what Bozzuto is hiring for here.

  • 5 or more years in the trades, facilities, or residential building maintenance
  • HVAC, EPA, and/or NAPE certification
  • Working knowledge of OSHA standards and risk management practices
  • Experience with complex mechanical systems (central plant, boilers, chillers) preferred
  • Supervisory or leadership experience, formal or informal
  • Availability for on-call emergency response and weekend coverage
  • Ability to lift 25 to 50 pounds frequently and work in varying weather conditions

greenhouse_4265681009.title: Bilingual Screening & Applications Specialist - Sandy Springs, GA
greenhouse_4265681009.rewritten_description:
Skills That Drive This Role

This position lives at the intersection of two demanding skill sets: sharp document review and genuinely warm human communication. Cortland's centralized contact center handles application volume across a large multifamily portfolio, which means the person in this seat needs to hold both of those things at once, often in the same conversation. You're reading through an application with compliance in mind while also reassuring a nervous prospective resident that their paperwork is in good hands. Bilingual fluency (English and Spanish) isn't a nice-to-have here. It's the point. Many applicants moving through this pipeline communicate primarily in Spanish, and your ability to guide them clearly through one of the more stressful housing decisions they'll make carries real weight.

Strong candidates in this role tend to be precise without being cold. They catch a missing document before it causes a delay, update multiple applicants simultaneously without letting anyone feel like a number, and de-escalate a frustrated caller without losing the thread of the task they were working on before the phone rang. That combination, accuracy under volume and interpersonal steadiness, is harder to find than it sounds.

What You'll Be Doing Day to Day

Your work sits in the application-to-move-in window of the leasing process. You'll review and process rental applications, collect and verify supporting documentation, and maintain compliance with Fair Housing standards and company policy throughout. A good portion of your time goes to inbound communication: calls, emails, and chat inquiries from applicants who are somewhere in the process and need an update, a clarification, or a next step. Cortland uses platforms including Funnel, OneSite, and RealPage, so comfort with property management software matters, as does a willingness to adapt when systems or workflows shift.

  • Process and review applications accurately, keeping pace with a high-volume queue
  • Collect, verify, and track applicant documentation with discretion and attention to detail
  • Respond to inbound calls, emails, and chat in both English and Spanish
  • Communicate proactively with multiple applicants at various stages of the process
  • Handle escalated or sensitive situations with patience and a practical focus on resolution
  • Uphold Fair Housing compliance in every interaction without exception

Weekend availability and occasional extended hours come with the territory. Application volume doesn't always follow a Monday-through-Friday schedule, and this team is expected to flex with it.

What's Distinctive About This Role at Cortland

Cortland operates with a vertically integrated model, meaning design, construction, and property management all sit under one roof. For someone in a contact center role, that structure has a practical upside: there's real organizational depth behind you. When a process question surfaces or a policy needs clarification, you're not waiting on a third-party management company to respond. You're working inside a system built to move.

This role also offers a clear window into how centralized leasing operations function at scale, which is increasingly the direction the multifamily industry is heading. Contact center leasing models are growing across large operators, and experience managing the full application-to-move-in cycle in a centralized environment transfers well to leasing management, compliance coordination, or operations roles down the line. If you're precise, people-oriented, and genuinely bilingual, this is a position where those qualities get used every single day.

greenhouse_4265678009.title: Bilingual Screening & Applications Specialist - Sandy Springs, GA
greenhouse_4265678009.rewritten_description:
Centralized leasing operations have reshaped how large multifamily portfolios handle application volume. Instead of each property running its own leasing office, companies like Cortland route prospective residents through a contact center staffed by specialists who process applications, verify documents, and keep applicants informed from submission to move-in. It's efficient for the portfolio and, done well, a genuinely better experience for applicants than waiting on a busy on-site team.

This role sits at the center of that model. Cortland is hiring a bilingual Screening and Applications Specialist for its centralized contact center in Sandy Springs. The position handles incoming calls, emails, and chat inquiries from prospective residents, reviews rental applications for accuracy and compliance, collects and verifies supporting documentation, and keeps multiple applicants updated simultaneously throughout the leasing process. Fair Housing compliance is non-negotiable here, and the volume is real. This isn't a one-application-at-a-time environment.

What the Day Actually Looks Like

On a busy morning, you might have a dozen open application files at different stages, two applicants asking for status updates via chat, and a phone queue with callers who have questions about income requirements or missing documents. Some callers are patient. Some aren't. De-escalation is a regular part of the job, not an occasional one. The bilingual requirement exists because a meaningful portion of applicants communicate primarily in Spanish, and clear communication at this stage matters. A misunderstood document request or a confusing denial process creates real problems for applicants and for compliance.

You'll work across platforms including Funnel, OneSite, and RealPage, along with CRM tools standard to contact center operations. Cortland expects you to manage competing priorities without dropping accuracy on the compliance side. Rental application review carries regulatory weight, and errors here aren't just inconvenient.

What Cortland Is Looking For

  • Two or more years of customer service experience, with preference for high-volume contact center or multifamily backgrounds
  • Fluency in both English and Spanish (written and verbal)
  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • Demonstrated comfort handling confidential applicant information with discretion
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite and familiarity with property management platforms
  • Strong organizational skills and the ability to maintain accuracy under pressure
  • Availability to work weekends and extended hours when business needs require it

Candidates who stand out tend to have experience in both customer-facing communication and document review, not just one or the other. If you've worked leasing at a property level and understand what makes an application file complete, that background translates directly here. The centralized model means you're rarely meeting applicants in person, so your written and verbal communication carries more weight than it might in an on-site role. Bilingual fluency isn't a checkbox in this position. It's a core function.

Cortland is a vertically integrated multifamily owner and operator founded in 2005, ranked among the top ten in the country by portfolio size. The Sandy Springs location puts this role within the company's Atlanta-area operations hub.

greenhouse_8575775002.title: General Manager
greenhouse_8575775002.rewritten_description:
It's mid-August, and the academic year starts in two weeks. Hundreds of incoming residents are scheduled to move in across a compressed window of days, your turn board in Turnable shows three units behind schedule, and a vendor just called to say their crew is short-staffed. This is the week a General Manager at 44 North earns their stripes.

What This Role Actually Manages

The Scion Group operates in student housing, a segment that runs on a fundamentally different calendar than conventional multifamily. The annual turn isn't just a busy season; it's the operational centerpiece of the year. As General Manager, you own the full cycle: forecasting turn costs, coordinating vendors, conducting move-out inspections, and getting hands-on when needed, whether that means helping move furniture or walking punch lists with your facilities team to confirm units are genuinely move-in ready. The rest of the year, you're responsible for NOI performance, expense management, leasing velocity, concessions strategy, and reputation management across internal survey platforms and public review channels.

Staff development is a genuine part of the job description here, not a footnote. You'll partner with HR and Learning and Development to hire through Greenhouse, build training plans, and actively work toward keeping your team on a growth track within Scion's structure. You're also the primary on-call responder for after-hours situations, which is worth understanding clearly before you apply.

On the financial side, you'll prepare annual operating and capital budgets, manage variance reporting, and identify capex needs at the property level before escalating to your Regional Manager for approval. Vendor bid management and contract oversight run through your desk, with Legal as a resource for more complex matters.

What You Bring vs. What You'll Build

This role requires at least three years managing a residential community and leading a team of three or more people. Comfort with property management systems is expected, and Entrata experience is preferred. You'll also work across a fairly wide tech stack: Vena for budgeting, ADP for payroll and scheduling, ClickUp for project management, Qualtrics for experience data, and Lattice for performance management. If you haven't used all of these, adaptability matters more than a perfect checklist.

What separates strong candidates from capable ones in this specific role is the ability to shift registers quickly. Student housing demands a customer-facing, community-building presence one hour and a financially disciplined, variance-explaining operator the next. Managers who treat those as separate skill sets tend to struggle here. The ones who thrive understand that resident experience and NOI are connected, not competing priorities.

  • 3+ years managing residential communities with direct team oversight
  • Demonstrated financial acumen: budgeting, forecasting, expense control
  • Experience owning a turn process from planning through completion
  • Strong conflict resolution skills, including resident escalations
  • Proficiency in Entrata or comparable property management platform
  • Availability for on-call response and non-traditional hours during peak periods
  • Eligibility to work in the United States (visa sponsorship is not available)

The General Manager role in student housing is one of the better training grounds in multifamily for operators who eventually want to move into regional or portfolio-level positions. The compressed leasing cycles, high resident turnover, and budget complexity give you reps that conventional lease-up or stabilized Class A management simply doesn't replicate at the same pace.

greenhouse_4265606009.title: Assistant Community Manager of Permanent Supportive Housing (Donner Lofts)
greenhouse_4265606009.rewritten_description:
Permanent supportive housing operates at a different frequency than conventional multifamily. The residents at Donner Lofts aren't just renters. Many have experienced chronic homelessness, mental health crises, or substance use challenges, and stable housing is often the first foothold they've had in years. That context shapes every operational decision in this role, from how you handle a delinquency conversation to how you respond to an incident report at 7 a.m.

MidPen Housing has been developing and managing affordable housing across Northern California since 1970. With more than 130 properties and roughly 20,000 residents in their portfolio, they run a serious operation, one that integrates property management directly with onsite resident services. For an assistant manager, that integration is felt daily. You're not just tracking rent collections and occupancy. You're coordinating with social service providers, supporting residents through complex situations, and maintaining a property environment that has to be both operationally sound and genuinely welcoming.

The day-to-day work covers the full range of assistant manager responsibilities: supporting rent collection and delinquency management, maintaining compliance with HUD, TCAC, and Fair Housing requirements, conducting property inspections, and stepping into the Community Manager's seat when they're out. The compliance piece carries real weight in affordable housing. Tax credit and HUD regulatory requirements don't leave much room for error, and the expectation is that you'll either hold a Tax Credit Specialist or Certified Occupancy Specialist certification already, or earn one within six months of starting.

What separates strong candidates in this specific role isn't just affordable housing experience, though that matters. It's the ability to hold two things at once: genuine empathy for residents navigating serious hardship, and clear, consistent professional boundaries. Trauma-informed doesn't mean boundaryless. The best operators in supportive housing know how to de-escalate a tense situation in the hallway and then document it accurately and completely in an incident report an hour later. RealPage proficiency and solid written communication aren't nice-to-haves here. They're the scaffolding that keeps operations clean when the human dynamics get complicated.

What MidPen is looking for

  • One to two years of multifamily residential management experience, with at least one year in affordable housing
  • At least one year of supervisory experience
  • Tax Credit Specialist or Certified Occupancy Specialist certification, or the ability to obtain within six months
  • Fair Housing knowledge and completion of FHA certification within the first 60 days
  • Experience in supportive housing preferred
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite and property management software, ideally RealPage
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to interpret and apply regulatory guidelines

The pay range for this role runs from $23.27 to $26.18 per hour, based on experience and qualifications. MidPen's benefits package includes health, dental, vision, life and disability insurance, a 403(b) retirement plan, paid parental leave, FSA options, an employee education reimbursement program, EAP access, pet insurance, paid time off, company holidays, and wellness days.

This role is based in San Jose at Donner Lofts. MidPen is an equal opportunity employer committed to an inclusive and accessible hiring process.
greenhouse_4265606009.description_text: About MidPen At MidPen, we build communities that change lives. Since 1970, we have been committed to our mission: to provide safe, affordable housing of high quality to those in need; establish stability and opportunity in the lives of residents; and foster diverse communities that allow people from all ethnic, social, and economic backgrounds to live in dignity, harmony, and mutual respect. We develop affordable housing, provide professional property management for all our communities, and coordinate robust onsite support programs that help residents thrive. greenhouse_4265122009.rewritten_description:
Most multifamily markets in Florida have seen sustained demand pressure over the past few years, and Palm Coast is no exception. The area's growth along the I-95 and US-1 corridors has brought a wave of new residents who expect professional management from day one. At a community like Integra Woods, the Assistant Community Manager sits at the center of that expectation: part leasing agent, part financial administrator, part team anchor when the Community Manager is out.

Hawthorne Residential Partners, a top-50 multifamily operator rooted in the Southeast, is hiring for this role at their Integra Woods property. Hawthorne runs their communities under a "Live It" culture that puts resident experience and team development at the front of daily operations. This isn't a role where you wait for direction. You're expected to carry real operational weight.

What the Day-to-Day Actually Looks Like

On any given morning, you might be reviewing delinquency reports and making follow-up calls before the leasing office opens, then shifting into tours and lease execution by mid-morning. Afternoons can bring ledger reviews, renewal conversations with current residents, or a quick check on common area presentation before a prospect walks in. You'll handle rent collection and payment posting, monitor accounts for billing accuracy, and coordinate with the Community Manager on financial reporting for regional leadership. When the Community Manager is away, you step into that seat and keep things moving without missing a beat.

Hawthorne also expects you to manage the community's social media presence, which means thinking about resident events and community engagement as part of your ongoing responsibilities, not as an afterthought.

What Hawthorne Is Looking For

  • Two years of property management experience, with at least six months in an assistant manager capacity preferred
  • Comfort reading financial reports and making decisions within budget parameters
  • Proven ability to handle delinquency follow-up and, when necessary, coordinate eviction procedures professionally
  • Strong leasing skills: lead response, touring, objection handling, and closing
  • High school diploma or GED required; a CALP designation is a plus
  • Valid driver's license

The schedule runs Monday through Friday, 9 AM to 6 PM, and Saturdays from 10 AM to 4 PM, with one weekday off to keep the week at 40 hours. Some evening and weekend availability may be needed for resident events.

What separates strong candidates here is financial fluency paired with people instincts. Plenty of leasing professionals can run a tour. Fewer can also catch a posting error on a ledger, de-escalate a frustrated resident, and then lead a team meeting in the same afternoon. If you've been the person your Community Manager leans on when things get complicated, this role fits where you already are.

Hawthorne offers monthly leasing and renewal commissions, quarterly performance bonuses on top of hourly pay, and a formal Career Path Program designed to move Assistant Managers into Community Manager roles. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401k match, paid time off including your birthday, pet insurance, paid parental and adoption leave, and company-paid life insurance.

greenhouse_5239431008.title: Maintenance Technician
greenhouse_5239431008.rewritten_description:
What You'll Actually Do

This role sits at the operational core of a Hillpointe workforce housing community in Fort Pierce. On any given day, that means working through a queue of resident work orders, running preventive maintenance on HVAC units, plumbing fixtures, and appliances, and turning vacant units so they're ready for incoming residents. Make-readies are a big part of the rhythm here. A tight punch list, a clean unit, a fast turn. That cycle directly affects occupancy, and occupancy drives NOI. You'll feel that connection every week.

Beyond the unit-level work, you'll handle grounds and common area upkeep, conduct inspections, manage parts inventory, and coordinate with vendors when the scope goes beyond in-house capacity. Documentation matters too. Work order records, incident reports, materials used. That paper trail supports cost tracking and helps the property team make smart capex decisions over time.

The on-call rotation is real. Evenings, weekends, early mornings. Maintenance tech roles at lease-up and stabilized communities alike carry after-hours responsibility, and this position is no different. If that schedule works for you, the tradeoff is meaningful: you're working for a vertically integrated developer that controls everything from land acquisition through asset management, which means fewer bureaucratic bottlenecks when you need parts approved or a vendor scheduled.

What You Bring

  • Hands-on mechanical ability: HVAC, plumbing, electrical, appliances. You can diagnose before you repair.
  • EPA Type I and II or Universal certification for refrigerant handling, or a genuine willingness to obtain it quickly
  • Valid driver's license (required for golf cart operation on property)
  • High school diploma or GED, plus relevant trade experience or training
  • Comfort reading technical manuals, schematics, and blueprints
  • Physical readiness: lifting up to 50 lbs regularly, working at heights, bending and kneeling throughout the day, and operating in outdoor Florida heat
  • Familiarity with OSHA standards and a genuine habit of using PPE correctly
  • Clear communication with residents, management, and contractors. You don't need to be chatty, but you do need to be reliable and clear.

Why This Role Is Worth Your Attention

Hillpointe focuses on market-rate workforce housing across the Sun Belt, a segment that's seen sustained demand and continued development activity. Fort Pierce fits that profile. Working for a developer that handles construction and asset management in-house means the maintenance team operates closer to the decision-making layer than at a typical third-party managed property. That's a different kind of environment than a scattered-site portfolio or a legacy Class C asset with deferred capex. For a tech who wants to sharpen skills across multiple systems and eventually move toward a lead or facilities manager role, the exposure here is broad and the feedback loop is short.

greenhouse_6011486004.title: Groundskeeper
greenhouse_6011486004.rewritten_description:
Groundskeeping work is physical, repetitive, and visible. Every resident who walks the property notices whether the grounds look sharp or neglected. This role at Stonebriar of Frisco Apartments requires someone who takes that visibility seriously and shows up consistently to maintain it.

Skills This Role Uses Daily

The core of this job is physical competence and attention to detail. You'll spend most of your time on your feet, covering the property grounds on foot, scanning for trash, debris, and anything that makes the community look less than its best. Pressure washing, sweeping, basic gardening, window cleaning, and wiping down common area furniture are all regular tasks. You'll also handle general maintenance work tied to the grounds and exterior buildings.

Physical stamina matters here. You need to lift up to 50 lbs., climb ladders and stairs, work in varied terrain, and stay productive through long stretches of standing and walking. Heat is a real factor in Frisco summers, so the ability to pace yourself and stay focused in outdoor conditions is part of the job.

What the Schedule Looks Like

This position includes on-call availability for nights, weekends, and company events. That's standard for grounds roles at apartment communities. If consistent weekday-only hours are a priority, this may not be the right fit. If you're comfortable with some flexibility in your schedule, the role offers steady, predictable work the rest of the time.

Working at Cottonwood Residential

Cottonwood manages its own communities rather than operating as a third-party management company. That structure tends to mean clearer accountability and more consistent standards across properties. They've been early adopters of Self-Guided Tours, which means the physical presentation of the community carries even more weight since prospects are often walking the property without a leasing agent alongside them. A clean, well-kept exterior is part of the leasing experience, not separate from it.

Benefits start within the first 30 days and include full health, vision, dental, life, and disability coverage. The company offers a 401k with a match, HSA matching, 10.5 paid holidays, and three weeks of paid time off in the first year.

  • Trash and litter removal across property grounds
  • Sweeping and pressure washing pathways and building exteriors
  • Basic gardening and weed control
  • Cleaning windows and common area furniture
  • General exterior and grounds maintenance tasks
  • On-call availability for nights, weekends, and events

Strong candidates for this role take pride in what a property looks like and don't need someone checking behind them to stay on task. If you can spot a problem before it becomes a complaint and you work well without constant supervision, that's the profile Cottonwood is looking for.

greenhouse_4264425009.title: Leasing Consultant
greenhouse_4264425009.rewritten_description:
Leasing is a skill set, not just a job title. At Skyline Towers, Berkshire Residential Investments is looking for someone who treats traffic conversion like a craft. A 20% closing ratio is the stated floor here, which means you're expected to track your own numbers, read the funnel, and adjust your approach when something isn't working.

The Skills This Role Runs On

Sales instinct sits at the center of this position. You're not just answering questions and handing out floor plans. You're reading a prospect in the first five minutes, identifying what matters to them, and building a tour experience around that. The model and tour route are your sales floor. They need to look sharp every single day, not just when corporate visits.

Market awareness matters just as much. Knowing your comp set, understanding what concessions are moving the needle down the street, and flagging shifts in traffic patterns gives your Property Manager real intelligence to act on. You're a source of ground-level data, not just a front-desk presence.

Administrative precision rounds out the skill profile. Lease paperwork, prospect follow-up logs, resident communications. Errors in this part of the job create downstream problems that stretch from the leasing office to accounting. Attention to detail here isn't a soft skill. It's operational.

What the Day Actually Looks Like

A busy Saturday might mean three tours before noon, two follow-up calls from yesterday's traffic, a walk of the model to fix anything that drifted overnight, and a quick conversation with your manager about a prospect who went cold. The role moves fast when occupancy is under pressure and slows into relationship-building mode when the property is stabilized. Both modes require different energy, and strong consultants know how to shift between them.

Berkshire owns and manages its own properties, which means decisions don't travel through a third-party management layer before they reach the asset. That structure tends to make the leasing team's feedback more actionable. When you flag a marketing idea or a resident satisfaction issue, it's more likely to get traction.

What Separates Strong Candidates Here

  • At least two years of customer-facing experience, ideally in a role where closing or conversion was tracked
  • Comfort with leasing software and a willingness to pick up new platforms quickly
  • Clear written and verbal communication skills, since resident relations live and die on follow-through
  • The ability to hold a professional tone under pressure without losing warmth

The consultants who tend to move up in this environment are the ones who treat closing ratio as personal data, not just a company metric. If you've ever looked at your own numbers and figured out why a week went sideways, that mindset fits here. Berkshire offers a 25% rent discount, three weeks of vacation, and personal development plans, so there's real investment in keeping good people and growing them.

greenhouse_5242215008.title: Assistant Maintenance Manager
greenhouse_5242215008.rewritten_description:
Mid-rise and high-rise apartment communities in the greater Seattle area carry mechanical complexity that garden-style properties simply don't. Central plant systems, boilers, and sophisticated HVAC infrastructure mean that keeping a building performing at a high level requires someone who thinks like a technician and leads like a manager. This role exists at that intersection.

Bozzuto is hiring an Assistant Maintenance Manager at their Mountlake Terrace community, and the scope here goes well beyond turning units and handling service requests. This is a hands-on leadership position where you'll work alongside the maintenance team, set the standard for workmanship, and carry real responsibility for the long-term condition of the asset.

What This Role Actually Covers

Day-to-day, you're splitting your time between direct technical work and team oversight. You'll diagnose and repair across HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and appliances, while also managing the make-ready process to keep turns moving on schedule so leasing has inventory to work with. Preventative maintenance programs fall under your watch, and executing those consistently is what separates a building that holds its value from one that doesn't.

You'll also carry after-hours responsibility through an on-call rotation and weekend availability. That's a real part of the job, not a footnote. Emergency calls for a community with complex mechanical systems can range from a boiler issue in January to a plumbing failure mid-week. Candidates who've handled that kind of unpredictability in a residential setting will have an easier adjustment.

Additional responsibilities include:

  • Responding to resident service tickets with timely follow-through and documented completion
  • Maintaining compliance with applicable building codes, OSHA standards, and safety protocols
  • Overseeing grounds upkeep, snow removal, and common area cleanliness
  • Keeping all building systems running at peak efficiency

What Bozzuto Is Looking For

Five or more years working in the trades, facilities, or residential building maintenance is the baseline. HVAC, EPA, or NAPE certification is expected. Supervisory experience is preferred, and given the leadership component of this role, candidates who've coached less experienced technicians or overseen a crew will have a clear advantage over those with deep technical skills but no management exposure.

Familiarity with complex mechanical systems, including split systems, central plant, chillers, and boilers, is a genuine differentiator here. Many applicants will have solid apartment maintenance backgrounds. The ones who stand out will also understand how those larger systems behave, how to troubleshoot them, and how to build a PM schedule around them.

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Comfort with property management software, apps, and the Microsoft Office suite
  • Basic carpentry, drywall, and painting capability
  • Physical ability to lift 25 to 50 pounds frequently and work in varying weather conditions
  • A detail-oriented, safety-first approach to every task

greenhouse_5151963007.title: Lease Administrator
greenhouse_5151963007.rewritten_description:
Lease administration is detail work at its core. If you thrive on accuracy, catch errors others miss, and find satisfaction in keeping complex records clean and current, this role at Lincoln Property Company in Nashville puts those skills to daily use. It's not a glamorous position, but for someone who genuinely enjoys the data and documentation side of commercial real estate, it's substantive and stable work.

Where Your Skills Actually Get Used

The majority of your time goes toward lease abstracts and database integrity. You'll prepare and edit abstracts, verify data pulled from paper and electronic sources, and make sure lease files meet institutional-quality standards. That last phrase matters here. Lincoln manages commercial portfolios on behalf of institutional clients, which means the accuracy bar is high and the paper trail has to be clean. A miskeyed commencement date or a missed amendment can create real downstream problems for accounting and legal teams.

You'll also handle monthly production and tracking reports, maintain a daily lease document tracker, and process client-specific reporting. The work requires you to read and interpret actual legal documents, including lease agreements, amendments, subordination agreements, and title commitments. You don't need to be an attorney, but you need to be comfortable with legal language and know when something looks off.

This is a fully in-office role in Nashville. No hybrid, no remote option. Standard business hours, desk-based work, with occasional cross-functional communication with property managers, accounting personnel, area managers, clients, and outside legal counsel.

What the Role Requires

  • High school diploma or GED required; associate degree or higher preferred
  • At least two years of database administration or commercial real estate experience
  • Experience with Yardi, MRI, or Visual Lease is a real advantage
  • Strong Excel and Word skills, plus comfort learning new lease administration software
  • Ability to read and interpret lease documents and legal agreements
  • Property management or real estate accounting background preferred
  • Solid math comprehension for tracking and reporting functions
  • Background check required prior to start

What Separates Strong Candidates Here

The difference between someone who does this job adequately and someone who does it well usually comes down to two things: proofing instincts and communication. You're going to be the person catching data discrepancies before they reach a client report. That requires a genuine habit of double-checking your own work, not just a line on a resume about attention to detail. The communication piece matters too because you'll interact across disciplines, including legal counsel and clients, not just internal staff. Being clear and professional in writing without over-explaining is a real skill in this context.

Lincoln's commercial portfolio spans more than 680 million square feet across multiple asset types and geographies. Working inside that infrastructure gives you exposure to how institutional-grade lease administration actually functions at scale, which is a meaningful credential if you're building a career in commercial real estate operations or real estate accounting.

greenhouse_6012299004.title: Centralized Collections Associate
greenhouse_6012299004.rewritten_description:
Collections work in property management doesn't always get framed as a career builder, but it should. The Centralized Collections Associate role at Asset Living sits at the intersection of financial operations, resident relations, and legal compliance. For someone who's spent time on-site as a leasing agent or assistant manager, this position takes what you already know about ledgers, delinquency, and resident communication and puts it to work at scale across a student housing portfolio, all without the commute.

Asset Living is one of the larger third-party management companies in the country, ranked in the NMHC top 50 and operating across multifamily, student housing, build-to-rent, affordable, and active adult assets. The centralized collections function is remote, meaning you're not tied to a single property. You're managing accounts receivable across multiple sites, which means you'll develop a sharper eye for ledger discrepancies, a faster hand with move-out reconciliations, and a more systematic approach to the eviction process than most site-level roles ever require.

Student housing adds its own complexity here. Guarantor relationships are common, lease timelines are compressed around academic calendars, and the delinquency window before turnover is short. If you've worked student housing before, you know the pace. If you haven't, this role will teach you quickly, and that knowledge transfers cleanly to conventional multifamily, affordable, and build-to-rent portfolios later in your career.

Day to day, you're monitoring accounts across assigned properties, posting payments and charges accurately, issuing notices, coordinating with legal teams on filings, and keeping records audit-ready through monthly close. You're also the point of contact for residents and guarantors navigating balances and payment plans, which means you need to hold a firm line on policy while communicating with real empathy. That balance is harder than it sounds, and people who do it well tend to move into property manager or regional roles faster than peers who only have leasing or maintenance coordination experience.

What separates strong candidates here isn't just the ability to work independently (though that matters in a fully remote role). It's ledger fluency. Candidates who can read an account, spot a misapplied payment, and trace a discrepancy back to its source before it becomes a reporting problem are the ones who add the most value in centralized operations.

What the role requires

  • At least one year of site-level property management experience, leasing or assistant/community manager level; student housing background is a strong plus
  • Working knowledge of general ledger functions and account reconciliation
  • Familiarity with county and state eviction procedures and Fair Housing compliance
  • Comfort with property management software and the ability to manage tasks independently in a remote setting
  • High school diploma required; a bachelor's degree is preferred

No travel is required. This is a fully remote position with Asset Living's centralized operations team.

greenhouse_7762404003.title: Business Manager - Preserve at Henderson Beach
greenhouse_7762404003.rewritten_description:
Destin's residential market sits in one of Florida's most competitive coastal corridors, where Class A communities compete hard on lifestyle, amenity quality, and resident experience. The Business Manager role at Preserve at Henderson Beach puts you at the center of all of it: financials, people, physical asset, and culture. That's a lot of plates to keep spinning, and that's exactly why this role builds the kind of operator that regional and VP-level leadership is made of.

Olympus Property, a three-time National Apartment Association Top Employer (2023, 2024, and 2025), is looking for a proven multifamily property manager to lead this community. The title says Business Manager, but the scope is full asset leadership. You'll own the financial performance, which means tracking NOI, managing occupancy and delinquency, building annual business plans, and running budget projections in close collaboration with your Regional Manager and Regional VP. You'll also lead the on-site team, covering both office and maintenance staff, with real responsibility for training, counseling, and performance development.

On any given day, you might be reviewing a T-12 in the morning, walking a make-ready punch list before noon, negotiating a vendor contract after lunch, and hosting a resident event in the evening. That variety is genuinely what this role demands. Olympus is transparent about the expectation for schedule flexibility, including after-hours coverage for events and emergencies, which is honest and worth factoring in.

What separates strong candidates here isn't just experience with the operational checklist. It's the ability to hold a luxury resident experience standard while simultaneously running a tight financial operation. Coastal Class A communities carry real expectations around amenity presentation, unit condition, and service responsiveness. Managers who treat those as competing priorities tend to struggle. The ones who thrive understand that a market-ready asset and a satisfied resident base are the same goal approached from different angles.

RealPage, Knock, and Onesite experience will help you hit the ground running, as Olympus prefers candidates already comfortable in that software environment. Minimum two years of multifamily property management experience is required, with luxury background preferred.

What Olympus is looking for

  • At least two years of direct property management experience in multifamily, with Class A exposure strongly preferred
  • Demonstrated ability to manage budgets, read financials, and drive NOI performance
  • Experience supervising both office and maintenance teams
  • Comfort with RealPage, Knock, or Onesite platforms
  • Full-time availability Monday through Friday, with flexibility for after-hours resident events and emergencies

The compensation structure includes monthly commissions alongside quarterly and annual bonuses, which means your financial upside is tied directly to how the asset performs. Olympus also offers a benefits package that includes medical, dental, and vision coverage, 401(k) with employer matching, tuition reimbursement, apartment rental allowance, and a sabbatical program. Career pathing and leadership conferences round out an employer that's clearly invested in retention and internal promotion, which matters if your goal is to move into a regional or multi-site role over time. This kind of full-scope property management seat is often the last stop before that transition happens.

greenhouse_7763082003.title: Maintenance Technician - Olympus at Three Springs
greenhouse_7763082003.rewritten_description:
Maintenance technician roles at apartment communities tend to attract two types of candidates: those who can fix things, and those who can fix things while keeping residents satisfied, tracking their work in software, and jumping on an emergency at 9 PM without too much grumbling. Olympus Property is clearly looking for the second type.

Olympus at Three Springs is a residential community in Durango, CO, and this full-time technician position sits within the service team reporting up through a Lead Maintenance Technician. The schedule runs Monday through Friday, 9 AM to 6 PM, with emergency availability built in. That's a relatively standard structure for a managed apartment community, and it means your weeks have shape to them, even if the occasional off-hours call does not.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Day to day, you're moving through a work order queue that covers the usual range: plumbing repairs, appliance troubleshooting, electrical fixture swaps, lock changes, HVAC filter replacements, and coil cleaning. You'll handle minor to moderate plumbing and electrical, which in practice means sink and toilet fixture replacements, switch and outlet repairs, and knowing when something needs to escalate. Make-readies will pull you toward unit turns as needed, and grounds and common area upkeep are part of the rotation. The shop stays organized on your watch, and work orders get logged in the system, not just completed and forgotten.

HVAC knowledge is a real requirement here. An EPA or HVAC certification is a plus, and preventative maintenance on HVAC units is a regular part of the job, not a once-a-year thing. If that's not your strongest area yet, it's worth being honest about that in your application. Two years of residential, commercial, or apartment maintenance experience is the baseline.

What Separates Strong Candidates

Technicians who do well in this kind of role tend to be self-managed on their route. The Lead sets priorities, but a good tech doesn't need hand-holding on a standard work order. They also communicate clearly with office staff, because residents expect updates and the leasing team needs to know when a unit is actually ready. If you've worked in apartment maintenance specifically, you already know that the difference between a good tech and a great one often comes down to how you interact with residents while you're in their home. The technical skills get you hired. The people skills keep residents renewing.

Olympus has been recognized as a top employer by the National Apartment Association three consecutive years (2023, 2024, 2025), which in our industry carries some weight. The compensation range is $17 to $22 per hour depending on experience and location, with monthly and quarterly bonus eligibility on top of that. Benefits include medical, dental, vision, 401(k) with employer matching, and an apartment rental allowance, which is a practical perk if you're looking to live closer to where you work in a market like Durango.

greenhouse_7979574.title: Leasing Consultant
greenhouse_7979574.rewritten_description:
Skills This Role Uses From Day One

Leasing is a craft that sits at the intersection of sales, service, and operations. At Bexley Stockyards in Nashville's Germantown neighborhood, you'll use interpersonal communication constantly: reading what a prospect actually needs, adjusting your pitch accordingly, and knowing when to listen instead of talk. You'll also exercise organizational skills every shift, balancing incoming traffic, follow-up calls, administrative tasks, and resident concerns without letting anything slip. Weinstein Properties is direct about this: the role isn't a desk job. Expect to walk units, inspect homes, and stay engaged with the physical property alongside the people in it.

You don't need prior leasing experience to start. Weinstein explicitly builds from the ground up, which means the company has structured its training around people who bring the right mindset rather than a pre-loaded resume. What they need on arrival: genuine warmth with strangers, the ability to stay organized when priorities shift mid-morning, and enough drive to care about quarterly results. The sales skills, the lease documentation process, the fair housing fundamentals , those get taught.

What the Role Actually Builds

A few months in, you'll have developed a working fluency in the full leasing cycle: generating and qualifying traffic, conducting tours, following up with prospects, handling objections, and converting applications. These are transferable skills. Consultants who master this at a well-run community often move into assistant manager roles, where the same instincts get applied to delinquency management, renewals, and NOI-level thinking. Weinstein has a stated history of promoting from leasing into leadership, both on-site and at the corporate level.

The administrative side of the role builds a different kind of discipline. You'll handle tasks that don't belong neatly to any one job description: helping with property appearance, supporting resident events, and occasionally working outside the standard weekday or Saturday schedule during weather events or community programming. That adaptability is exactly what separates consultants who grow quickly from those who plateau.

What's Distinctive About This Particular Opportunity

Weinstein Properties has operated for over 70 years and remains family-owned, which tends to produce a different management culture than institutional ownership. Decisions move closer to the property level, and the hands-on philosophy the company describes isn't marketing language at this scale. Bexley Stockyards sits in Germantown, one of Nashville's more established urban neighborhoods, which means the leasing experience here will involve a resident profile that expects quality service and genuine community engagement.

The starting rate of $21 per hour, plus quarterly bonuses and a rent discount, reflects a real commitment to retaining good people early in their careers. If you're willing to put in the learning curve, this role offers both a structured entry point into property management and a clear path forward within a company that's been building that path for its people for decades.

  • Starting pay at $21/hour with quarterly bonus eligibility
  • Benefits include health, dental, vision, 401k with company match, and paid birthday time off
  • Schedule runs weekdays 9-6 and rotating Saturdays 9-5

What You'll Actually Do

At Abbington West End in Henrico, you'll split your time between leading the service team and working alongside them. That means some days you're pulling a work order and diagnosing an HVAC issue yourself. Other days you're coordinating vendor schedules, walking a make-ready punch list, or reviewing turn status to keep occupancy on track. The Assistant Supervisor role at Weinstein sits right at the intersection of hands-on trade work and team accountability, and candidates who thrive here are genuinely comfortable in both modes.

The scope covers the full range: HVAC repair and diagnostics, electrical, plumbing, appliances, carpentry, drywall, pool maintenance, and exterior structural work. You'll supervise in-house staff and outside vendors, assign and track work orders through business software, and share on-call rotation with your teammates. A $150 weekly on-call bonus applies regardless of call volume, with an additional $150 for holidays.

Weinstein Properties owns and manages its portfolio in-house rather than operating under third-party management, which matters practically. Decisions move faster, capital repair approvals aren't filtered through a distant asset manager, and there's real continuity in how properties are maintained year over year. For a maintenance professional, that structure typically means less friction when you need to get something done right.

What You Bring

  • At least 4 years of trade experience across electrical, plumbing, HVAC, and general building systems
  • A minimum of 1 year in a lead, assistant supervisor, or supervisory role in apartment maintenance
  • EPA/CFC certification (Type I and II, or Universal) plus hands-on HVAC repair experience
  • Comfort using property management software to manage work orders, schedule turns, and order supplies
  • Valid driver's license, reliable transportation, and your own tools
  • Willingness to participate in shared on-call rotation

Compensation and Context

The role starts at $26 per hour depending on experience, with a $1,500 sign-on bonus (details covered during the interview), a quarterly performance bonus of up to $1,110, and a rent discount for those interested in living on-site or nearby. Benefits include paid holidays, birthday PTO, health, dental and vision coverage, an Employee Assistance Program, and a 401(k) with company match.

One thing worth noting for candidates considering this step: the Assistant Supervisor position is a natural bridge toward a full Maintenance Supervisor or Service Manager role. If your trade skills are sharp but your supervisory experience is still developing, this is the kind of role where you can build that credibility with a stable, vertically integrated owner-operator. Weinstein's in-house model means the growth path is real rather than theoretical.

greenhouse_5152931007.title: Part-Time Leasing Consultant- Hearth Apartments
greenhouse_5152931007.rewritten_description:
Leasing is the front line of any multifamily operation. Occupancy doesn't maintain itself, and the leasing consultant is usually the first real human interaction a prospective resident has with a community. Get that interaction wrong and no amount of amenities or curb appeal recovers it. MG Properties has been acquiring, developing, and managing apartment communities across the Western U.S. for over three decades, and they're adding a part-time leasing consultant at Hearth Apartments in Vancouver, WA.

What This Role Actually Involves

The core of the job is converting traffic into signed leases while keeping current residents reasonably happy. You'll greet prospective residents, walk them through units, qualify applicants, and shepherd new residents through move-in. That last part requires real coordination with maintenance to make sure make-readies are actually ready when a new resident shows up with a moving truck. You'll prepare leases, manage the signing process, and keep rental files current and accurate. Data entry is part of the job, not an afterthought.

On the resident-facing side, you'll handle complaints, route maintenance issues, and follow up on rent collection. None of that is particularly glamorous, but it's where good leasing consultants separate themselves from average ones. The person who handles a frustrated resident with patience and actually follows through gets renewals. The one who brushes it off doesn't.

Monthly administrative tasks round out the workload. Property paperwork has to be organized and complete. If you're someone who lets files pile up or finds data entry tedious, this role will frustrate you quickly.

Who Fits Well Here

  • At least one year of property management or leasing experience (preferred, not required)
  • Genuine sales ability, not just a friendly personality
  • Customer service skills that hold up under pressure, not just in easy interactions
  • Comfort working within a team and coordinating across departments like maintenance
  • Professional communication in person, over the phone, and in writing
  • Willingness to work within a drug-free workplace; background check and drug screen required upon offer

Pay runs $20 to $23 per hour depending on experience, with monthly and quarterly bonuses, company profit sharing, accrued PTO, and paid sick time. MG Properties promotes from within, so this part-time role can realistically grow into a full-time leasing or assistant manager position for someone who performs. That's a real career path in this industry, not a talking point.

One honest note: leasing is a sales job, and slow traffic periods can feel unproductive. Vancouver's rental market has grown alongside the broader Portland metro, which means competition for qualified renters is real. Strong candidates know how to stay sharp during quiet stretches and close when traffic picks up.

greenhouse_8576513002.title: Assistant Community Manager
greenhouse_8576513002.location: Alight West Tenn, Tallahassee, Florida, United States
greenhouse_8576513002.rewritten_description:
Student housing runs on a different clock than conventional multifamily. Lease-up happens once a year, turnover is compressed into a matter of weeks, and your residents are 18-to-22-year-olds who may have never signed a lease before. The Assistant Community Manager role at Alight West Tenn in Tallahassee exists precisely because that operational complexity needs more than one set of hands to manage well.

What the Role Actually Involves

Scion is one of the larger student housing operators in North America, and this position sits directly below the General Manager, which means you're expected to run the property when the GM isn't there. That's not a footnote. It shapes everything about how you'll need to show up. On a given week you might be reviewing delinquency reports and enforcing collection policy, coordinating move-in room assignments, pulling inspection punch lists on vacant bed spaces, and handling an escalated resident situation that came in after hours. The paperwork load is real. Resident accounts, utility billing, accounts receivable, month-end reconciliation, final billing at move-out. Keeping delinquency below 2% by month end is a stated expectation, not a soft goal.

There's a sales component here too. You'll run weekly market surveys, manage concessions within budget, track KPIs, and direct the team toward occupancy and revenue targets. Student housing traffic tends to spike in predictable windows, but those windows are intense. The annual turn process, where hundreds of residents move out and a new group moves in within days, is the defining event of the student housing calendar. You'll help plan and execute it.

Staff development is part of the job as well. You'll coach leasing and maintenance staff, help with hiring, and make sure everyone on site is current on Fair Housing compliance and safety protocols. After-hours on-call is part of the schedule rotation.

What Separates Strong Candidates Here

The gap between a decent candidate and a strong one usually comes down to two things in student housing. First, comfort with the pace of a single annual leasing cycle. Unlike conventional properties where you're absorbing new residents throughout the year, here the stakes concentrate. Missing the leasing season has consequences that don't reset for twelve months. Candidates who've worked lease-ups or annual turn processes in student or conventional housing understand that rhythm. Second, account management discipline. The billing side of this role, damage charges from quarterly inspections, NSF fees, move-out final statements, utility reconciliation, is detailed and unforgiving. Candidates who treat the financial side as secondary to the customer-facing side tend to struggle.

  • At least one year of experience in property management or residential living communities
  • Proficiency in a property management system, with Entrata preferred
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Ability to work non-traditional hours during peak periods and respond to emergencies
  • Work authorization in the United States (visa sponsorship is not available)

Benefits include health, dental, and vision insurance, 401k matching, paid time off, paid parental and maternal leave, a discretionary annual bonus, and learning reimbursement. The position is based on-site at Alight West Tenn in Tallahassee, with periodic travel possible.

Leasing roles at apartment communities often get reduced to traffic logs and application processing. At Prometheus, the expectation runs deeper than that, which is probably why they gave the position a different name entirely.

Prometheus Real Estate Group has been in the Bay Area since 1965 and has built one of the largest privately held apartment portfolios in the region, now over 13,000 units across Silicon Valley, Portland, and Seattle. They're vertically integrated, handling acquisitions, development, value-add renovations, and operations all in-house. That structure matters for anyone in a leasing role because it means the company is genuinely invested in the long-term performance of each asset, not just hitting occupancy numbers for a third-party client.

What the Role Actually Involves

Prometheus calls this position a Neighbor Ambassador rather than a Leasing Consultant, and the distinction reflects how they think about the work. You're handling the full leasing cycle: qualifying prospects, guiding tours, walking people through rental agreements, and converting leads into signed leases. But the job doesn't stop at the signature. You're also the ongoing point of contact for residents, which means your customer service instincts get tested just as much as your sales ability.

On the administrative side, you'll run market surveys, prepare Neighborhood reports, and manage apartment advertising. For someone early in their PM career, this is actually useful exposure. Knowing how to read a comp set and understand your position in the local market is a skill that pays dividends when you move into an Assistant Manager or Property Manager role later.

Weekend availability is required. That's not a footnote. Saturdays and Sundays are peak traffic days at most communities, and Prometheus schedules accordingly, with weekday time off in exchange.

What You Bring

  • Comfort working in a customer-facing, sales-oriented environment
  • Strong communication skills, both written and in person
  • Ability to work independently and take initiative without waiting to be told what to do next
  • A genuine interest in people, not just a tolerance for them

Prometheus is explicit that they hire from outside property management. If you've come from retail, hospitality, or another service-heavy field, your background is considered relevant here. What they're evaluating is how you think and how you treat people, not whether you already know Yardi.

The Skills That Drive This Role

This position sits at the intersection of financial fluency, people leadership, and operational hustle. Prometheus calls the role a Neighborhood Director rather than a Property Manager, and that distinction matters. You're not just maintaining occupancy and processing renewals. You're running a lease-up, which means you're building a community from the ground up, setting the cultural tone before a single resident has moved in, and making real-time decisions that directly shape the property's financial trajectory from day one.

The financial side of this role gets real attention. You'll work with operating budgets, track variances, interpret market dynamics, and stay current on local rental ordinances, which in the Bay Area and Silicon Valley means navigating some of the most closely watched and frequently updated housing regulations in the country. California rent law, just cause eviction rules, and local tenant protections aren't background noise here. They're part of your weekly operating reality.

On the people side, you'll lead a team that includes leasing, experience, and maintenance functions. Coaching matters more than directing. Your team will look to you for clarity during the chaotic early weeks of a lease-up, when traffic is high, processes aren't yet second nature, and resident expectations are being set for the first time. Your ability to stay steady and keep your team motivated through that stretch is genuinely what separates strong candidates from average ones in this kind of role.

What You'll Actually Be Doing

During lease-up, no two days look the same. Early on, you're likely reviewing punch lists, coordinating with maintenance on make-ready timelines, and training your leasing team while simultaneously fielding calls from prospective residents. As units fill, your focus shifts toward building the resident experience, managing delinquency, tracking concessions, and keeping NOI on target. You'll report on occupancy, leasing velocity, and budget performance to leadership while staying close enough to daily operations to pitch in on tours or answer phones when volume spikes.

Being on-call is a real part of the job. Prometheus is transparent about this. Maintenance emergencies and urgent resident situations don't follow a 9-to-5 schedule. That said, the company also builds in meaningful time off, including your birthday and anniversary vacation banks at tenure milestones. The expectation is genuine availability, not burnout.

  • Multi-site experience is preferred
  • Working knowledge of California housing law and local rental ordinances
  • ARM, CPM, or CAM designation preferred
  • Bachelor's degree preferred

What's Distinctive About Doing This at Prometheus

Prometheus has operated in the Bay Area since 1965 and holds more than 13,000 apartments across Silicon Valley, Portland, and Seattle. As a privately held company, they take a long-term view on their properties, which means capital investment decisions tend to be made with the asset's full lifecycle in mind rather than short-term yield optimization. That context affects how you operate as a Neighborhood Director. You're not squeezing short-term metrics at the expense of resident experience. You're building something meant to last.

The company carries a Certified B Corporation designation, which signals a genuine commitment to using business as a positive force. That's not just marketing language here. It tends to attract Prometheans who care about how the work gets done, not just the numbers it produces. If you've worked in environments where culture was an afterthought, this will feel different. Whether that difference suits you is worth thinking about honestly before you apply.

Compensation ranges from roughly $90,000 to $103,000 annually, with per-lease incentives, a semi-annual discretionary bonus, and additional bonuses tied to lease-up performance specifically. Benefits include fully company-paid medical, dental, and vision plans, 401(k) with employer matching, and a behavioral health program available around the clock.

greenhouse_4272646009.title: Community Manager
greenhouse_4272646009.location: Grove at Park Place - 2640 Latrobe Avenue - Fayetteville, NC - 28304
greenhouse_4272646009.rewritten_description:
Community Manager roles in multifamily carry real operational weight, and at a company like Hawthorne Residential Partners, the expectation is that the person in this seat runs the property like a business owner. Grove at Park Place in Fayetteville, NC is one of their managed communities, and Hawthorne's Southeast footprint means this role connects to a broader network of regional support, benchmarking, and career infrastructure that smaller operators can't match.

What This Role Actually Covers

You're accountable for the full picture: financial performance, occupancy, team development, and resident experience. That means reading your T-12, managing delinquency, and making budget-informed decisions, not just passing reports up the chain. On the leasing side, you'll stay close to traffic and conversion, guide your team through renewals, and adjust pricing strategy to protect occupancy. Yardi and Knock are the primary platforms, so comfort with both matters from day one.

Day-to-day, you're splitting time between the office and the property itself. Inspections keep curb appeal and make-ready quality where they need to be. Vendor relationships require active oversight, not passive check-ins. And when a resident issue escalates past your leasing staff, it lands with you. Fayetteville's rental market has a meaningful military-connected renter base, which means move-out cycles can be faster and less predictable than in purely civilian markets. Managers who build strong retention habits and respond quickly to resident needs tend to outperform here.

The schedule runs Monday through Friday with Saturday hours, and one weekday off each week keeps the schedule at 40 hours. Resident events and community needs can occasionally push beyond standard hours.

Who Fits This Role Well

  • At least two years of multifamily experience, including time as a leasing consultant and assistant manager
  • Six months of community manager experience in multifamily is strongly preferred
  • Working knowledge of Yardi, Knock, and Microsoft Office
  • CAM, CAPS, real estate license, or property management license preferred
  • Valid driver's license required
  • High school diploma or GED

The candidates who genuinely stand out in this kind of role are the ones who can hold both sides of the job at once: the financial discipline to manage a budget and the people instincts to keep a team motivated and a resident base satisfied. Leaning too far into either side creates problems. Strong community managers treat NOI and team culture as equally important metrics, because over time they are.

Growth and Compensation

Hawthorne runs a formal career path program, and Community Manager to Regional Manager is a real trajectory within the company, not just a recruiting line. Monthly leasing and renewal commissions plus quarterly performance bonuses supplement base salary. Benefits include dental coverage at no cost, medical and vision options, a 401k match, paid parental and adoption leave, pet insurance, and paid time off that includes your birthday.

For someone who wants to grow inside a structured, regionally grounded multifamily company rather than job-hop for the next title, this is a legitimate opportunity to build toward a regional role with a company that has the size and infrastructure to support that path.

greenhouse_5247340008.title: Floating Leasing Specialist
greenhouse_5247340008.rewritten_description:
A floating leasing role is fundamentally different from a site-based position. Where a traditional leasing consultant builds relationships over months at a single community, a floating specialist has to establish credibility fast, read a new property's strengths quickly, and close traffic without the benefit of familiarity. Hillpointe, a Sun Belt workforce housing developer ranked among NMHC's top builders, uses this position to shore up leasing momentum across its portfolio wherever the need is sharpest.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Your assignments will shift based on where Hillpointe needs coverage most. That could mean stepping into a lease-up community during its first high-traffic weeks, filling in during a team transition at an established property, or supporting a new community launch before a full leasing team is in place. Each assignment asks you to get up to speed on a different unit mix, a different amenity package, and a different prospect profile. You'll conduct tours, follow up on inquiries by phone, text, and email, and keep tour paths and model units presentation-ready. The role requires weekend availability and genuine comfort with travel between properties, including the possibility of temporary or permanent relocation when operational needs call for it. Hillpointe provides free rent at an assigned community, which reflects the mobile nature of the position.

Strong candidates come in knowing how to ask qualifying questions on a tour without making a prospect feel like they're filling out a form. They connect specific unit features to what a prospect actually said they need. Average candidates walk people through a floor plan. Strong ones close a lease.

Skills Required vs. Skills You'll Build

The role requires a customer service or sales foundation, strong interpersonal communication across diverse populations, a valid driver's license, and schedule flexibility including evenings and weekends. Fair housing compliance is non-negotiable from day one.

What the role builds is less obvious but genuinely valuable. Floating across multiple communities gives you exposure to different lease-up strategies, pricing environments, and traffic volumes that a site-based consultant rarely sees. You'll develop an instinct for reading a community's competitive position quickly and adjusting your pitch accordingly. You'll also build the kind of operational adaptability that property management leadership looks for when promoting from leasing into assistant manager or property manager roles.

Who Fits This Role

  • Previous experience in leasing, hospitality, or sales (customer service backgrounds translate well)
  • Comfort working independently in unfamiliar environments without a long ramp-up period
  • Willingness to travel frequently and relocate if the portfolio requires it
  • Flexible availability, including weekends and occasional evenings
  • High school diploma or equivalent; valid driver's license
  • Physical ability to tour indoor and outdoor areas, walk stairs, and lift up to 25 pounds

Workforce housing communities across the Sun Belt tend to run at high occupancy demand, which means traffic can move fast and prospects don't always wait for a follow-up. If you're someone who follows up the same day and closes with genuine enthusiasm rather than scripted pressure, this position puts those habits to work across a portfolio that's actively growing.

Position requires extended periods of computer use. May involve outdoor work while conducting property tours in varying weather conditions. Fast paced, customer focused environment requiring professional demeanor and problem solving skills. Occasional exposure to noise, interruptions, and multiple concurrent tasks.
