greenhouse_5255250008.title: Asset Management Field Technician
greenhouse_5255250008.rewritten_description:
Hillpointe builds and owns workforce housing across the Sun Belt, and unlike most property management companies, they control everything in-house: land, construction, procurement, and asset management. This field technician role sits inside that asset management function, supporting newly opening and operating properties across multiple states.

What the Work Looks Like

This is a traveling maintenance role, not a site-based one. You'll move between Hillpointe properties in Georgia, North Carolina, Tennessee, Florida, South Carolina, and Colorado, spending roughly 75% of your time on the road with overnight travel expected. Each stop has a checklist: open work orders pulled from Smartsheets, HVAC filter checks and replacements, electronic deadbolt verification, key documentation, unit status reporting, and photo uploads to OneDrive. You're the boots on the ground when a property needs eyes and hands before or after a lease-up.

Communication matters as much as the physical work. You report directly to the Asset Management Lead and flag anything beyond your scope, whether that's a warranty item or a repair that needs a subcontractor. You keep the work vehicle stocked, the documentation accurate, and the timelines moving. The job requires lifting up to 150 lbs and working in whatever conditions the property presents.

What Hillpointe Is Looking For

  • High school diploma or equivalent preferred
  • Prior maintenance experience is a plus, not a hard requirement
  • Ability to travel up to 75%, including overnight stays
  • Comfortable with Microsoft Office basics (Word, Excel)
  • Strong attention to detail, especially with documentation and photo reporting
  • Able to work independently and manage your own schedule across sites
  • Physically capable of standing, bending, and lifting throughout the workday

Why This Role Is Worth Considering

Candidates who do well here tend to have a self-starter mindset. You're often working without a supervisor physically present, so the ability to follow protocols, document correctly, and communicate proactively carries more weight than raw technical skill. Experience with work order platforms or property management software is a real advantage, even if it's not listed as required.

The exposure across multiple properties and markets also builds practical knowledge fast. Technicians who come through multi-site roles like this often move into site-level maintenance lead positions or regional maintenance roles, since they've seen more property types and operational setups than someone who spent the same time at a single community.

greenhouse_4688736006.title: Maintenance Helper A - Local 1 (Temp to Permanent Position)
greenhouse_4688736006.rewritten_description:
Entry-level maintenance roles at Chicago multifamily properties tend to be either purely custodial or purely mechanical. This one sits at the intersection of both, which is exactly what makes it useful for someone building toward a Building Engineer or full Maintenance Technician position.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Reside Living is hiring a Maintenance Helper A under Local 1 union classification, reporting directly to the Building Engineer on a Tuesday through Saturday schedule (8 AM to 4:30 PM). The position starts as temp-to-hire, with the real possibility of converting to permanent. Pay is set at the union rate of $28.23 per hour, with benefits flowing through Local 1.

Day to day, you're working alongside the Building Engineer on service requests, preventive maintenance tasks (HVAC filter replacements, sewer rodding, mechanical system checks), and apartment turns during make-ready cycles. Exterior upkeep is part of the scope too, including snow removal during Chicago winters. You'll coordinate vendor access, flag water infiltration or mold immediately, and handle custodial work when the property needs it. The role uses a mobile app for documenting completed work orders and inspections, so comfort with a smartphone matters practically, not just administratively.

You'll also be on-call for after-hours emergencies on your scheduled rotation, which is worth knowing upfront. That's standard for building maintenance in multifamily, but it's not always spelled out clearly in postings.

What Reside Is Looking For

  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • At least one year of maintenance experience, or a related trade background
  • EPA certification (or willingness to obtain it within 90 days)
  • Familiarity with plumbing, electrical, HVAC, and mechanical systems is preferred
  • Comfortable with hand tools, power tools, and basic mechanical equipment (voltmeters, pressure gauges, augers)
  • Valid driver's license and personal vehicle required
  • Personal smartphone required (iPhone or Android); a $50 monthly stipend offsets that cost

Additional perks include a student loan repayment contribution of $100 per month and a 25% apartment discount after 90 days.

Where This Role Leads

Maintenance Helper A is a recognized union classification, and that matters for career trajectory. The skills you build here, reading mechanical systems, managing preventive maintenance schedules, handling resident-facing service calls, are the same ones evaluated when engineers and supervisors move up. Working under a Building Engineer gives you direct exposure to building systems at a level most maintenance roles don't offer this early. If you're targeting a Maintenance Technician B or C classification, or eventually a Building Engineer role yourself, a stint like this inside a union shop builds credentials that transfer across Chicago's multifamily market. Candidates who get EPA certified quickly and show initiative on the punch list side of turns tend to stand out and convert to permanent faster.

greenhouse_6018545004.title: Maintenance Supervisor
greenhouse_6018545004.rewritten_description:
Cottonwood Residential is hiring a Maintenance Supervisor for Cottonwood Clermont Apartments in Clermont, FL. This is a hands-on leadership role covering the full scope of property maintenance: service requests, make-readies, preventive maintenance, grounds, and around-the-clock emergency coverage for the community.

The day-to-day splits between wrench-turning and team management, and you need to be comfortable in both modes. You'll carry your own work order load, particularly on HVAC, electrical, plumbing, and appliance repair, while also keeping your techs and community care associates moving efficiently. The turn process is a big part of this job. Getting units through punch list, make-ready, and back to leasable condition on schedule directly affects occupancy, so someone who treats the turnover calendar as optional won't last long here.

Beyond the technical side, you're also the person building the team. That means hiring, scheduling 24/7 coverage, running on-the-job training, and setting the standard for how maintenance work gets done on the property. The expectation is that your crew reflects your habits, for better or worse.

What Cottonwood is looking for

  • EPA certification Type II or Universal (required)
  • Significant hands-on HVAC troubleshooting experience
  • Valid driver's license
  • Demonstrated experience leading a maintenance team, not just working alongside one
  • Comfort with building, county, and safety code compliance
  • Strong follow-through on resident service tickets and communication

Benefits include full medical, dental, vision, life, and disability coverage available within the first 30 days, a 401k with company match, HSA match, three weeks of PTO in the first year, and 10.5 paid holidays. There's also a bonus structure tied to the role.

One honest note on the role: maintenance supervision in a residential community means after-hours calls happen. Emergency coverage is a real expectation, not a footnote. The candidates who thrive here are the ones who've already made peace with that reality and built systems to manage it well, because scrambling through on-call without a plan wears a team down fast. If you've got the HVAC background, the leadership track record, and the organizational discipline to keep a make-ready schedule tight, this is a straightforward role with solid support behind it.

greenhouse_4282662009.title: Full-Time Concierge (Mon-Fri 4pm-12am)
greenhouse_4282662009.rewritten_description:
The 4pm to midnight shift at a residential community has its own rhythm. The leasing office is closed, the management team has gone home, and residents returning from long days expect the front desk to handle whatever they walk in with: a package question, a noise complaint, a guest they need cleared, a loading dock reservation they forgot to book. The concierge on this shift is the community's operational anchor for eight hours, and that's exactly what makes the role worth taking seriously.

Comstock is filling a full-time concierge position at their Rockville, MD property, Monday through Friday, 4pm to midnight. The schedule alone tells you something about what this role demands. Evening coverage at a Class A residential building means you're dealing with peak resident traffic, not the quiet mid-morning hours. You'll greet residents and guests, manage access control, coordinate amenity and loading dock reservations, and keep the lobby environment polished and presentable. Building walks are part of the routine, which means you're also acting as an early alert system for maintenance items the daytime team may have missed.

The skills this role requires are interpersonal above all else. You need a genuine ability to connect with people across backgrounds, handle complaints without escalating them, and stay composed when several things demand your attention at once. One year of concierge or high-end customer service experience is preferred, and Microsoft Office proficiency (particularly Outlook) matters because coordination tasks like reservation management and communication with the property team happen in writing.

What the role builds is equally worth naming. Evening concierge work sharpens your ability to operate independently and make judgment calls without a supervisor nearby. You develop a working knowledge of how a residential building actually functions after hours, which is valuable context if you eventually move toward a leasing, assistant manager, or property operations role. Concierge positions at Class A properties are a legitimate entry point into residential property management, particularly for candidates who want to understand the resident experience from the ground up before stepping into a leasing or administrative track.

Qualifications

  • High school diploma or GED required
  • At least one year of concierge or high-end customer service experience preferred
  • Proficient in Microsoft Office, particularly Outlook, Word, and Excel
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Ability to work holidays and pick up additional shifts when needed
  • Self-directed with strong problem-solving instincts and attention to detail
  • High integrity and accountability in all interactions

Comstock offers a competitive hourly wage in the $18 to $22 range, along with medical, dental, vision, 401(k) match, life insurance, a housing discount, commuter benefits, free parking with EV charging, parental leave, and annual professional development funds. Benefits vary by role.

greenhouse_4283868009.title: Multisite Maintenance Supervisor
greenhouse_4283868009.rewritten_description:
BAM Companies has been managing multifamily communities since 2010, and this Multisite Maintenance Supervisor role sits at the center of how those properties actually perform. You're not tied to a single building. You move across the portfolio, leading a maintenance crew and keeping HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and general systems running the way residents expect them to.

The multisite piece matters here. Des Moines has seen steady apartment development over the past decade, and managing maintenance across several communities means your day rarely looks the same twice. You might be coordinating a preventative maintenance schedule at one property in the morning, running a punch list inspection at another in the afternoon, and coaching a technician through a repair before the day ends. The role rewards people who can prioritize on the fly and still hold their team to consistent standards across every site.

Team development is a real part of this position. You're expected to train, coach, and give ongoing feedback to the people working under you. That means your communication skills matter as much as your mechanical ones. A supervisor who can explain the right way to do something, and then follow up to make sure it sticks, is going to get more out of a crew than one who just fixes things themselves.

BAM also expects you to manage costs. That includes purchasing supplies, tracking spend, and making sure maintenance operations stay efficient. If you've worked in property maintenance but always handed budget questions up the chain, this role will push you to own that side of things directly.

What the role requires

  • 2 to 3 years of property maintenance experience, with supervisory experience preferred
  • EPA Type 2 or Universal Certification for refrigerants
  • Valid driver's license and a reliable vehicle for travel between sites
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills

Pay ranges from $25 to $30 per hour depending on experience and other factors. Benefits include medical, dental, vision, and life insurance, paid time off starting after 90 days, and a rent discount if you choose to live at a BAM property.

Multisite maintenance supervisors who perform well in portfolio settings often move into regional or director-level maintenance roles over time. Managing across properties builds a breadth of operational experience that single-site positions rarely offer at the same pace.

greenhouse_7771758003.rewritten_description:
Olympus Property has earned the National Apartment Association's Top Employer designation three years running (2023, 2024, 2025), and their Floating Leasing Consultant position gives you a clear look at why. This role covers properties across Albuquerque and Santa Fe, so you're not anchored to one address or one lease-up cycle. You're moving between communities, reading traffic patterns at each, and closing deals across different product types and price points.

The core of the job is conversion. You're greeting prospects, walking units, explaining floor plan differences, and turning that interest into signed leases. You'll also prep move-in paperwork, get keys ready, and enter resident data into the system. On the marketing side, you'll work outreach with locators and local businesses to build traffic, and you'll help plan and run resident events that support retention. Renewal bonuses are on the table alongside leasing commissions, so your compensation has a direct line to both occupancy and resident satisfaction.

Starting pay runs $20 to $23 per hour depending on experience and location, with monthly leasing commissions and renewal bonuses layered on top. Mileage is reimbursed given the travel between sites. The schedule is full-time Monday through Friday with required Saturdays and occasional after-hours resident events each month.

  • Ability to work a rotating weekday schedule (9 AM to 6 PM, hours may vary) plus Saturdays
  • Availability for monthly after-hours resident events
  • Reliable transportation for travel between Albuquerque and Santa Fe communities
  • Comfort with leasing software and resident database entry

Candidates who tend to perform well in floating roles have sharper product knowledge than their peers. When you're covering multiple properties, you can't fake familiarity with unit layouts, concession structures, or what's sitting vacant and why. The consultants who hit their numbers consistently are the ones who review occupancy and traffic data before they show up at a site, not after. If you've worked a lease-up or covered a sister property during a staffing gap, that experience translates directly here.

Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401(k) with employer matching, educational assistance and tuition reimbursement, pet insurance, short and long-term disability, life and AD&D insurance, paid time off, an apartment rental allowance, and a sabbatical program. Olympus also offers defined career pathing, which matters in a floating role because your exposure to multiple communities and management styles tends to accelerate the path toward assistant manager or property manager faster than staying fixed at a single site.

greenhouse_8002641.title: Assistant Property Manager
greenhouse_8002641.rewritten_description:
What You'll Actually Do

This role at Bexley at Anderson Mill in Cedar Park covers a lot of ground, and that's not a complaint, it's just the reality of the job. On a given day you might be following up on internet leads in the morning, touring a prospect through the community before lunch, then sitting down with a current resident to walk through their renewal options or handle a notice to vacate. Afternoons might involve coordinating with maintenance, walking a unit on punch list to confirm it's ready before a new resident moves in, or posting rent and chasing down a balance.

The leasing side is real work: fielding calls, scheduling appointments, processing applications, pulling together lease paperwork, collecting security deposits, and getting signatures. The resident services side is equally active: move-ins, move-outs, security deposit dispositions, transfer requests, pet addendums, work order follow-ups. You'll also help plan and host resident events, and you'll support the property manager with training and team goals as your confidence grows.

Saturdays are part of the schedule on a rotating basis with the team. Hours are 9 to 6 weekdays and 9 to 5 Saturdays. Some situations, like resident events or weather-related issues, will pull you outside normal hours occasionally.

What You Bring

  • Strong communication skills, both written and in person, including the ability to handle tense conversations calmly
  • Comfort working directly with people all day, including prospects, residents, and maintenance staff
  • Organization and attention to detail, especially when handling leasing documents and financial transactions
  • Prior property management experience is a plus, but Weinstein will train candidates who come from customer service, sales, or hospitality backgrounds
  • A genuine team-first approach, including the willingness to help outside your immediate lane when the situation calls for it

Context Worth Knowing

Weinstein Properties is a family-owned company that's been operating for over 70 years, managing more than 60 apartment communities across Virginia, North Carolina, Texas, Tennessee, and Georgia. That kind of longevity in the industry usually means the internal processes are well-developed, and in this case there's a structured training program designed to get people up to speed even without prior property management experience. The pay starts at $23 per hour, increases with experience, and includes quarterly bonuses plus a sign-on bonus (details discussed during the interview).

One honest note about the role: the assistant property manager position tends to be the busiest seat on a site team. You're the connective tissue between leasing traffic, resident concerns, maintenance coordination, and administrative follow-through. People who do well here typically move into property manager roles or take on larger communities over time. The ones who struggle usually underestimate the volume of concurrent tasks on any given day. If you've handled a high-contact, detail-heavy job before and kept your composure, this work will feel familiar.

greenhouse_5162686007.title: Floating Leasing Consultant - Phoenix Region
greenhouse_5162686007.rewritten_description:
A Leasing Role Built for Adaptability

Floating leasing consultants carry a different kind of pressure than their site-based counterparts. You're not just learning one property, one team, one lease-up story. You're stepping into communities mid-stream, reading the room quickly, and producing results without the luxury of a long warm-up period. MG Properties, a Western U.S. owner-operator with more than three decades of acquisition, development, and management experience, is looking for someone who genuinely thrives in that kind of environment across their Phoenix region portfolio.

The day-to-day centers on what good leasing has always required: greeting prospects warmly, qualifying applicants thoroughly, and moving people through the process with care and efficiency. You'll prepare leases, walk new residents through signings, and coordinate with maintenance staff so move-ins go smoothly rather than chaotically. Keeping rental files accurate and current, entering data correctly, and supporting monthly administrative tasks are all part of the rhythm. When residents have concerns, whether about a maintenance issue or a billing question, you're often the person they talk to first. That means your communication style and composure matter as much as your closing rate.

What Makes This Role Work Well

Strong candidates here tend to share a specific combination: they're genuinely good with people under pressure, and they're organized enough to handle unfamiliar systems and processes without dropping details. When you're floating between properties, you don't always have a colleague next to you who knows where everything lives. The people who do well in this kind of role are the ones who ask smart questions early, take notes, and build rapport with site teams quickly rather than waiting for a formal handoff.

  • At least one year of property management experience, preferably in leasing
  • Strong sales instincts paired with genuine customer service orientation
  • Comfort working across multiple locations and team environments
  • Professional communication, written and verbal
  • Attention to detail in file management and data entry

Growth and Culture

MG Properties has a stated commitment to promoting from within, and floating roles often accelerate that path faster than single-site positions. Exposure to multiple communities, management styles, and occupancy challenges builds a kind of institutional breadth that's hard to get otherwise. Consultants who perform well in a floating capacity tend to move into assistant manager or property manager roles with a broader frame of reference than peers who spent the same time at one address.

The company offers a compensation structure that includes both monthly and quarterly bonuses alongside a profit-sharing program, which signals that they want staff invested in outcomes, not just activity. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401(k) with employer match, paid holidays, personal days, sick time, and a rental discount. The work environment is team-oriented, and the expectation is that you bring professional etiquette to every interaction, with residents, prospects, and colleagues alike.

greenhouse_4281851009.title: Asset Management Analyst (Foster City)
greenhouse_4281851009.rewritten_description:
Affordable housing asset management operates at the intersection of financial compliance and mission-driven stewardship. At MidPen Housing, that intersection is especially consequential: the organization manages more than 130 properties across 12 Northern California counties, serving roughly 20,000 residents. This analyst role sits inside that operation, supporting a senior Asset Manager and carrying real responsibility for the financial and regulatory health of an assigned portfolio slice.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

A significant portion of this role centers on reporting. You'll prepare monthly, quarterly, and annual packages for investors, lenders, and regulatory agencies, which means your output lands in front of external stakeholders who scrutinize it closely. Audited financials, budgets, and required compliance reports all need to go out on time and in good shape. Beyond the calendar-driven deliverables, you'll analyze property financials and portfolio performance, research partnership agreements and financing documents, and help monitor the legal and financial requirements embedded in those agreements.

You'll also support reserve draws and capital projects, contribute to annual budgeting cycles, and build proforma models as needed. Coordinating communications with lenders, agencies, and partners is part of the day-to-day, so you'll need to manage competing requests without letting things fall through the cracks. Database accuracy matters here too: the department's reporting depends on clean, reliable data.

What MidPen Is Looking For

  • Bachelor's degree in Finance, Business Administration, Accounting, or a related field, plus two years of relevant experience (or an equivalent combination)
  • Strong Excel skills and comfort producing financial analysis and written reports
  • Ability to read and interpret legal documents, including financing agreements and regulatory requirements
  • Clear written and verbal communication, since you'll be a point of contact for external partners
  • A master's degree or prior experience in real estate, low-income housing, accounting, or asset management is preferred
  • Valid California driver's license with reliable transportation and current auto insurance

Why This Role Builds Real Expertise

Low-income housing tax credit (LIHTC) portfolios carry a compliance and reporting load that most market-rate asset management roles don't. Learning to read partnership agreements, track regulatory requirements, and manage investor and lender relationships in that context builds a very specific skill set. Analysts who come through this kind of shop tend to move into full asset management positions, portfolio director roles, or development finance work, because they understand how affordable deals are structured from the inside out. The Bay Area's regulatory environment and land costs make affordable development exceptionally complex, which means the institutional knowledge you'd build at MidPen is genuinely hard to replicate elsewhere.

The salary range is $70,304 to $76,500, based on experience and qualifications. MidPen carries a Great Place to Work certification for 2025, and the benefits package includes health, dental, vision, a 403(b) retirement plan, tuition reimbursement, paid parental leave, and several flexible spending account options.

greenhouse_7771881003.title: Maintenance Supervisor (Cliffside)
greenhouse_7771881003.rewritten_description:
What You'll Actually Do

This role sits at the center of everything physical at Cliffside, a Prometheus property in Gig Harbor, Washington. You're responsible for the condition of the building, the performance of your maintenance team, and the budget that funds both. That means hiring and training technicians, managing vendors and contractors, overseeing capital projects, and keeping inventory in order. When safety training needs to happen, you run it. When a contractor needs direction, that's you. When something breaks down at 11pm, you're the one your team calls.

On-call is real here. Prometheus lists standby pay and on-call premium pay in the compensation package, which tells you something: after-hours situations are frequent enough that they built a structure around compensating for them. If you've led a maintenance team before, you already know what that means in practice.

The budget side of this job carries real weight. You'll manage maintenance costs with an eye toward preserving NOI, which means making smart calls on repairs versus replacements, keeping capex projects on track, and not letting deferred work pile up into bigger problems. You're expected to know your numbers and own your decisions.

What You Bring

  • At least five years of apartment maintenance experience, with a minimum of two years in a supervisory role
  • Three or more certificates from recognized programs such as BOMA, IREM, or vocational maintenance courses
  • Working knowledge of federal, state, and local safety regulations, including the ability to read and apply operating manuals and safety documentation
  • The physical ability to stand, walk, and lift up to 50 lbs. occasionally
  • High school diploma or GED
  • Comfort communicating clearly with residents, staff, vendors, and management

Compensation and Context

The hourly range runs from $32.75 to $38.00, with a discretionary semi-annual bonus on top. Prometheus also offers standby and on-call premium pay, referral bonuses, renovation bonuses, and lease-up bonuses where applicable. The benefits package includes fully company-paid medical, vision, and dental plans with buy-up options, 401(k) with employer matching, 12 paid holidays including your birthday, paid volunteer time, and tenure-based housing discounts. Educational assistance and tuition reimbursement are available too.

What separates strong candidates in this role is the combination of technical depth and team accountability. Plenty of experienced technicians can fix things. Fewer can build a team culture where work orders get closed on time, make-readies stay on schedule, and residents trust that maintenance actually follows through. If you've managed that balance before, Gig Harbor is a solid market to do it in again.

greenhouse_4284100009.title: Affordable Assistant Property Manager II
greenhouse_4284100009.rewritten_description:
A prospective resident calls with questions about income limits and unit availability. You pull up the file, walk them through the eligibility requirements, and schedule a showing. By noon, you've also followed up on two late accounts, signed off on a move-in checklist, and touched base with maintenance about an open work order. That's a representative morning at Saugus Commons.

The Role

John M. Corcoran and Company is hiring an Affordable Assistant Property Manager II at Saugus Commons in Saugus, MA. JMC has operated in New England since 1951 and manages properties with a hands-on, team-oriented approach. This position supports the day-to-day operations of an affordable housing community, working closely with the property manager on leasing, compliance, resident relations, and administrative functions.

Day to day, you'll lease apartments, review and approve rental applications, and help keep occupancy on target. You'll handle resident inquiries and concerns directly, coordinate move-ins and move-outs, and track maintenance activity to make sure things don't fall through the cracks. Rent collection and delinquency follow-up are part of the job, as is keeping resident files accurate and preparing required reports. You'll also coordinate resident activities and work with community partners when needed.

Affordable housing compliance is a real part of this role. You need to know Fair Housing regulations and understand how income qualification and program requirements shape leasing decisions. Candidates without affordable housing experience will find the learning curve steep.

What You Bring

  • High school diploma or equivalent; relevant experience considered
  • At least 3 years of property management experience
  • Direct experience with affordable housing programs and Fair Housing compliance
  • Strong organizational skills and comfort managing multiple priorities at once
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office and Yardi

greenhouse_6019115004.title: Part-Time Customer Experience Specialist (Leasing/Customer Service)
greenhouse_6019115004.rewritten_description:
Park at Oak Ridge Apartments in Greensboro is hiring a part-time Customer Experience Specialist. The role sits at the front end of the leasing cycle: greeting prospects, fielding calls and messages, showing available homes, and making sure residents feel taken care of after they move in.

Day-to-day, you're the first voice people hear when they call the office and the first face they see when they walk in. You'll walk the tour path, amenity areas, and vacant apartments daily to confirm everything looks right before a prospect arrives or a new resident moves in. Package organization, community event planning, and some social media support round out the week.

Cottonwood operates self-guided tours across their portfolio, which means prospects may already be mid-tour when they reach you with questions. Knowing how to pick up that conversation, answer accurately, and keep the experience smooth is a real part of this job.

The schedule is part-time, up to 24 hours per week, with evening and weekend availability required. This is a customer-facing role, so the hours reflect when prospects and residents actually need you.

What they're looking for

What You'll Actually Do

This role puts you at the center of daily operations at a high-end luxury apartment community in Daytona Beach. You'll coordinate with contractors on unit turns, confirm make-ready conditions are met before move-in, and hold a 24-hour resolution standard on priority work orders. Plumbing repairs, carpentry, grounds upkeep, pool service, trash compactor maintenance, and security gate functionality all fall within your scope. On-call availability is part of the position, which means you'll need to be comfortable responding when residents need you most.

EPA Section 608 Types I and II certification is required before you start. A CPO certification is a bonus. You'll work within OSHA standards and company safety policies, and you're expected to stay current on both.

What You Bring

  • Hands-on experience repairing building systems and equipment across multiple trade areas
  • Working knowledge of service supplies, materials, and equipment used in residential maintenance
  • EPA Section 608 Types I and II certification (required)
  • Solid understanding of OSHA standards and safe work practices
  • Availability for on-call rotation
  • A service-first attitude and the energy to match a high-expectation community
  • High school diploma or equivalent, plus relevant trade experience or training

Where This Role Takes You

Waypoint Management Services operates a growing portfolio, and technicians who demonstrate strong diagnostic skills, reliable follow-through on turns, and a sharp eye for detail tend to move into lead technician and maintenance supervisor roles over time. The craft skills you build here, reading T-12 maintenance cost patterns, managing vendor relationships on make-readies, and keeping HVAC systems running efficiently, translate directly to those next-level positions.

Working on a luxury community sharpens your standards. Residents at this tier notice everything, which means your attention to detail and resident-facing communication skills develop faster than they would at a Class B or C property. That experience carries real weight on a resume as you grow your career in property maintenance.

The position pays between $23 and $25 per hour and comes with medical, dental, and vision benefits starting on day one, a 401k with matching, an onsite housing discount, and both referral and recognition programs.

greenhouse_5255477008.title: Assistant Property Manager
greenhouse_5255477008.rewritten_description:
The Assistant Property Manager role exists in a specific tension: you're not the top of the org chart at the property, but you're often the one holding it together. Delinquency follow-up, leasing traffic, team coverage when the PM is out, resident escalations that need someone with actual authority to resolve them. Bozzuto is hiring for this position at their Tampa community, and the salary band sits at $58,000 to $60,000 with bonus eligibility on top.

What the Role Actually Covers

Financially, you own rent collection and delinquency management. That means you're not just sending notices; you're tracking aging, making judgment calls on payment plans, and keeping the ledger clean enough that it reflects well on the T-12. On the leasing side, you're conducting tours and converting traffic into signed leases, which at a Bozzuto community means the presentation standard is high. They're not a C-class operator, and the expectation on both physical curb appeal and the professionalism of the team reflects that.

When the Property Manager is absent, you run the property. That's not a ceremonial title. You're making operational decisions, coaching the team, and keeping the day-to-day from sliding. Weekend availability is part of the deal: one to two weekends per month, with compensating days off during the week. If weekend work genuinely doesn't fit your life right now, this one probably isn't the right fit.

What Bozzuto Is Looking For

  • A four-year degree or equivalent experience in property management, hospitality, or retail
  • At least two years in a customer-facing or operations role, ideally with some exposure to P&L or budget management
  • Comfort in Yardi or comparable property management software
  • Working knowledge of social media platforms for community marketing purposes
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, which matter more in this role than most people expect

The candidates who tend to stand out at this level aren't necessarily the ones with the most years on a resume. They're the ones who can read a delinquency report, handle a difficult resident conversation, and then turn around and give a polished tour to a prospect, all in the same afternoon, without either task suffering. That range is harder to find than it sounds.

Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, 20 days of PTO plus holidays, a 401k with company match, and tuition reimbursement. The APM seat at a well-regarded regional operator like Bozzuto is a credible stepping stone toward a Property Manager role, and Tampa's multifamily market has enough activity that the experience you build here travels well.

greenhouse_4282154009.title: Maintenance Technician - Cortland at Valley Ranch
greenhouse_4282154009.rewritten_description:
The Skills This Role Runs On

This position draws on a specific combination of technical trades knowledge and independent problem-solving. You're diagnosing systems, not just replacing parts. Electrical, plumbing, HVAC, appliance repair, and general building systems all fall within your scope. Strong candidates already know how to read a situation, identify the root cause, and fix it correctly the first time. EPA certification (Type I, II, or Universal) is required before you start.

Attention to detail matters here as much as technical skill. Preventative maintenance only works when someone actually tracks equipment condition, catches small issues early, and documents what was done. If you treat work orders as a checklist to close rather than a record of the property's health, things slip through.

What You'll Be Doing Day to Day

Most of your time goes toward completing work orders across apartment and building systems. That includes HVAC servicing, plumbing repairs, electrical fixes, appliance troubleshooting, and addressing anything that creates a safety hazard on the grounds or inside units. You'll also run scheduled preventative maintenance on HVAC equipment and building systems to reduce downtime and extend asset life.

Part of the job is keeping an eye on building infrastructure: automatic doors, security cameras, exterior lighting, gates. You report condition issues up the chain before they become expensive problems. You'll manage your own parts inventory to keep work orders moving without unnecessary delays.

On-call rotation is part of the role. Emergency maintenance requests happen outside business hours, and you'll be expected to respond when it's your turn.

  • 1 to 3 or more years in maintenance, facilities, or multifamily housing
  • EPA certification required (Type I, II, or Universal)
  • Hands-on experience with electrical, plumbing, HVAC, and appliance repair
  • Comfortable with physical work: lifting, ladder use, indoor and outdoor conditions
  • Organized enough to manage multiple open work orders without losing track
  • Clear communicator with residents and teammates

Doing This Role at Cortland

Cortland operates a vertically integrated model, meaning design, construction, and property management stay in-house. For a maintenance tech, that structure matters. You're working within a system that has direct lines to capital resources and operational support, which typically means faster approvals on repairs and access to better tooling than you'd find at a smaller operator. The Irving property sits within a large national portfolio, so there's real room to grow within the company if you perform well and want to move up toward lead tech or maintenance supervisor over time.

What separates strong candidates here: technicians who communicate clearly with residents, document their work consistently, and handle on-call situations without needing hand-holding tend to stand out quickly on a team like this.

greenhouse_5163805007.rewritten_description:
It's 8 a.m. on a Tuesday. You're reviewing last night's delinquency report, a vendor is waiting on your signature for a make-ready, and two leasing consultants have questions before the office opens. That's the job. If you can hold all of that without losing your footing, read on.

The Role

MG Properties is hiring a Community Manager for a property in Portland, OR. The company has been acquiring, developing, and managing apartment communities across the Western U.S. for over 30 years. This is a full operational leadership position: you run the site, you build the team, and you own the results.

Day to day, you'll oversee leasing activity and occupancy targets, manage the property budget, direct marketing efforts, and keep operations running across every department on site. You'll also be responsible for hiring, training, and developing your team. Strong candidates treat team-building as a core part of the job, not a side task.

Yardi is the platform in use here. Comfort with it matters, though the company lists it as preferred rather than required.

A manager who understands how to protect occupancy without over-relying on concessions, and who reads a budget with enough depth to spot problems early, will be better positioned here than someone whose experience is mostly leasing-side.

MG Properties offers a compensation package that includes monthly and performance-based incentive bonuses, company profit sharing, a 401(k) with employer match, and medical, dental, and vision coverage. greenhouse_8590192002.location: Varsity House Gainesville, Gainesville, Florida, United States
greenhouse_8590192002.rewritten_description:
A prospective resident stops by at 5:45 PM, fifteen minutes before close, wanting to tour a two-bedroom. You grab your keys and take them through the amenities with the same energy you had at 9 AM. That's the baseline expectation here.

Varsity House Gainesville is a student housing community managed by The Scion Group, a company that specializes in collegiate living. This leasing consultant role (called an Experience Team Member internally) sits at the intersection of sales, marketing, and day-to-day operations. You're the first person prospects meet, the one who handles package retrieval, maintenance follow-ups, office upkeep, and after-hours lockout calls when your rotation comes around.

What the Job Covers

On the leasing side, you'll run tours, respond to inquiries across multiple platforms, assist with social media content, and report back to management on what objections you're hearing from prospects. You'll also help plan and execute resident engagement events and support local marketing outreach.

On the operations side, expect to keep the office and common areas presentable, log and manage resident packages, schedule maintenance requests and track resolutions, and assist with opening and closing procedures. After-hours on-call rotation is part of the job.

Availability during summer, holidays, and the annual turn period is required. Student housing turns are compressed and high-volume. If you haven't worked one before, expect a few intense weeks each year when a large portion of the community turns over in a short window.

What Scion Is Looking For

  • Strong communication skills with a diverse, student-age population
  • Comfort with a schedule that shifts based on leasing season and community needs
  • Self-discipline and reliability without close supervision
  • A customer-first approach that holds up under pressure

The role comes with health, dental, and vision insurance, a 401k match, paid time off, paid parental leave, a discretionary annual bonus, and learning reimbursement opportunities.

greenhouse_4285450009.rewritten_description:
Skills at the Center of This Role

The Assistant Community Manager position at Hawthorne Residential Partners draws on a specific combination of skills that don't always appear together in property management: financial literacy, leasing ability, and the kind of interpersonal range it takes to deescalate a frustrated resident one hour and close a lease the next. If you've been building those skills in a leasing or administrative role and you're ready to carry more operational weight, this is the next logical step.

The property is The Whitby, located in Birmingham's 35242 zip code, a competitive suburban submarket where resident expectations skew higher. Keeping occupancy strong here means your leasing instincts matter, but so does your ability to retain the residents already in place. Renewals, relationship management, and follow-through on maintenance or billing concerns all factor into how the community performs.

What You'll Be Doing Day to Day

On the financial side, you'll handle rent collection, payment posting, ledger reviews, and delinquency follow-up. That last item deserves a clear-eyed look: weekly calls to delinquent residents and coordinating eviction procedures when necessary is real work that requires both firmness and professionalism. You'll also assist with financial reporting that goes up to regional leadership, so accuracy and attention to detail in your administrative work directly affects how the community is evaluated.

On the leasing side, you'll conduct tours, respond to leads, guide prospects through the application process, and manage renewals. You'll also handle social media content for the community, which increasingly connects to traffic generation at the property level. This breadth is what makes the ACM role valuable: you're touching both the revenue side (leasing, renewals, delinquency) and the operations side (team coverage, resident relations, daily workflow) at the same time.

When the Community Manager is out, you step into that seat. That's not a formality. It's the part of this role that builds the judgment and confidence that separates a strong ACM from one who stays in the role for years without advancing.

Where This Role Leads

Hawthorne runs a formal Career Path Program specifically designed to move Assistant Community Managers into Community Manager roles. That's worth taking seriously. The ACM position is where most property managers develop the financial fluency, leasing track record, and team leadership experience they need to run a community independently. The skills you build here, reading a T-12, managing delinquency, supporting a leasing team through a slow traffic month, carry directly into a CM role and compound over time.

Candidates who stand out in this role tend to already have a feel for the numbers side of property management, not just the leasing side. Two years of property management experience is preferred, along with at least six months in an ACM capacity. A CALP designation is a plus and signals that you've invested in the leasing fundamentals. The schedule runs Monday through Saturday with one weekday off, and some evening or weekend availability comes with the territory for resident events.

  • High school diploma or GED required
  • Two years of property management experience preferred
  • Six months of prior ACM experience preferred
  • Valid driver's license required
  • CALP accreditation is a plus

Compensation includes hourly pay plus monthly leasing and renewal commissions and quarterly performance bonuses. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401k match, paid time off (including your birthday), paid parental and adoption leave, pet insurance, and company-paid life insurance.

greenhouse_6018634004.title: Maintenance Technician
greenhouse_6018634004.rewritten_description:
Maintenance Technician roles at apartment communities touch every system in the building. Plumbing, electrical, carpentry, grounds, and unit turns all fall within scope, which makes this kind of position one of the most skill-dense in residential property management. Cottonwood Residential is adding a Maintenance Technician at Antero Apartments in Colorado Springs, and the role reflects that full range of hands-on work.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Day to day, you'll handle repairs across plumbing, electrical, and general carpentry for both individual units and common areas. Make-readies and punch list work are a natural part of the rhythm at any residential community, so attention to detail on unit condition matters as much as technical ability. You'll also be part of the on-call rotation, providing after-hours emergency service with support from the Service Manager. That after-hours expectation is worth understanding clearly before you apply: it's a real part of this job, and the best technicians treat it as part of the craft rather than an inconvenience.

The physical demands here are genuine. Lifting up to 50 lbs, extended periods of standing and walking, working on ladders and scaffolding, and accessing confined spaces are regular parts of the role. A valid driver's license is required. EPA Type II or Universal certification and CPO certification aren't required but will strengthen your candidacy.

Skills This Role Requires vs. Skills It Builds

You need to bring working knowledge of residential repair trades, basic English literacy for safety documentation and work orders, and the physical capability the job demands. What this role builds is something different: diagnostic instincts sharpened by variety. Because you're not siloed into one trade, you develop the ability to triage problems quickly across systems, which is the foundation of a strong Service Manager skill set down the road. Technicians who come through full-scope community maintenance roles tend to advance faster than those who specialize too early, because they understand how all the systems interact.

Compensation and Benefits

  • Competitive pay
  • Full health, vision, dental, life, and disability benefits available within 1 to 30 days of hire
  • Generous 401k and HSA company match
  • Three weeks (120 hours) of paid time off available in the first year
  • 10.5 paid holidays

Cottonwood Residential built a reputation partly by introducing Self-Guided Tours early in the industry, which reflects a company culture that takes the resident experience seriously. The maintenance team is a direct extension of that experience. How a work order gets handled, how quickly a unit turns, and how a technician responds to an after-hours call all shape whether a resident feels at home. That connection between craft and customer experience is what separates strong candidates at a company like this from those who treat maintenance as purely transactional.

The delinquency report hits your inbox at 8 a.m. By 8:30, a resident's at the leasing desk with a question about their renewal. That rhythm, administrative and relational at the same time, is the core of this role.

The Position

Waypoint Management Services is hiring an Assistant Community Manager for their multifamily community in Davenport, FL. This is a hands-on operational role that sits directly alongside the Community Manager, with real responsibility across leasing performance, financial oversight, and resident relations. You're not shadowing someone. You're running alongside them.

On the leasing side, you'll support the team's daily performance, help execute sales and marketing strategies, and track traffic and occupancy trends. You'll conduct market surveys and recommend pricing adjustments when occupancy goals or competitive conditions call for it. On the financial side, you'll assist with rent collection, monitor delinquency, help manage the eviction process when necessary, and contribute to reporting that keeps the Community Manager and ownership informed. You'll also maintain accurate records across lease files, rent rolls, and make-ready schedules, so nothing slips through during turns or renewal cycles.

Weekend availability is required for this role, including a rotating weekend schedule. That's standard for multifamily at this level, and it's worth knowing going in.

  • Solid computer skills, including Microsoft Office and comfort with social media platforms
  • Experience with Yardi or a comparable property management platform (Yardi preferred)

  • Strong written and verbal communication; residents and ownership both need clear information

Candidates who stand out at this level typically bring some exposure to delinquency management or renewal strategy, not just front-desk leasing. If you've helped a team close out a month-end or worked through a lease-up push, that experience translates directly here.

Davenport sits in the Polk County corridor between Orlando and Tampa, a market that has absorbed significant multifamily supply over the past several years as Central Florida's growth has extended well past the I-4 spine. Communities here compete actively on renewals and concessions, which makes market awareness and pricing discipline genuinely important skills for anyone in this seat.

greenhouse_6026659004.title: Operations Specialist - Remote
greenhouse_6026659004.rewritten_description:
Third-party management firms like Asset Living operate across enormous portfolios spanning multifamily, affordable housing, student housing, and build-to-rent communities. Keeping that kind of operation running cleanly requires people who can sit between senior leadership and the properties, translating data into decisions and keeping reporting on track. That's the core function of this Operations Specialist role.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

This is a remote, corporate-level support position. You're not on-site turning units or walking punch lists. You're working with senior portfolio managers, pulling together financial and operational data, and making sure the right information gets to clients and internal stakeholders on time. That means collecting and reviewing historical income and expense data on apartment buildings, preparing weekly, monthly, and quarterly property reports, and gathering rent comparables and market trend information from both internal tools and third-party sources.

You'll also handle some tasks that feel more administrative. Coordinating travel, fielding resident calls that come in at the corporate level, and managing internal projects are all part of the job. The scope shifts depending on what the portfolio needs at any given time. A background in finance, real estate, or economics helps you make sense of the numbers faster, and fluency in Excel is essentially a baseline requirement. Experience with property management software like MRI or One-Site is useful, though not required.

The salary range is $60,000 to $65,000 annually, and the position is fully remote with roughly 10% travel for property visits or internal meetings.

Who Does Well in This Role

Strong candidates tend to have a genuine feel for financial data. If you can look at a T-12, spot a variance worth flagging, and explain it clearly to a client, that's the kind of analytical instinct this role rewards. Attention to detail matters here more than speed. Reports that go out with errors erode trust with clients, and in third-party management, client relationships are everything.

A few honest notes worth considering:

  • The scope is deliberately broad. "Other duties as assigned" is real here, not filler.
  • Multiple deadlines running in parallel is the normal state, not the exception.
  • Answering resident calls at the corporate level occasionally means handling frustrated residents whose property-level team hasn't resolved something. It requires patience and a calm, professional tone.

For someone early in a property management career who wants exposure to portfolio-level operations, this role builds a useful foundation. The combination of financial analysis, client communication, and cross-functional project work maps well onto future roles in regional management, asset management, or corporate operations.

greenhouse_7771959003.title: Lead Maintenance Technician - Capital Crest at Godley Station
greenhouse_7771959003.rewritten_description:
Capital Crest at Godley Station is a residential community in Savannah, GA, and Olympus Property is looking for a Lead Maintenance Technician to run the day-to-day maintenance operation there. This is effectively a working supervisor role: you're on the tools when needed, but your primary output is a well-organized team, a tight work order queue, and units that are ready to lease.

What You'll Actually Do

The bulk of your week lives in scheduling and execution. You'll assign daily, weekly, and monthly workloads to your maintenance team, manage vendor relationships when outside contractors are on site, and keep service request volume moving at a pace that protects occupancy. Turn operations are a core responsibility here. When a unit vacates, you're coordinating the make-ready sequence: punch list, repairs, inspections, and final sign-off before the unit hits the leasing floor. Delays in turns cost the property real rent dollars, so your ability to keep that cycle tight matters directly to NOI.

Beyond turns, you'll run the preventative maintenance calendar: HVAC systems, appliances, irrigation, pools, and structural elements across the community. You'll conduct monthly, quarterly, and annual property inspections, keep the shop organized and properly stocked, and stay current on state, federal, and local compliance requirements. You'll also work closely with the Business Manager and office staff to make sure show units are show-ready and move-in units are complete before a new resident takes possession.

What You Bring

  • At least 3 years of experience in residential, commercial, or apartment maintenance, with some time in a supervisor or lead capacity
  • EPA/HVAC certification (required)
  • Comfort using software platforms to track work orders, inventory, and inspection records
  • Ability to work a Monday through Friday schedule with on-call availability as needed
  • Experience coordinating with third-party vendors and holding contractors accountable to scope and timeline

The Operational Reality

A strong Lead Tech at a property like this knows that the service team's output is visible everywhere: in resident satisfaction scores, in delinquency patterns tied to habitability concerns, in the speed at which vacants flip to rent-ready. The candidates who stand out aren't just technically skilled. They track their own metrics. They notice when work order volume is climbing in a specific building and investigate before it becomes a capital problem. They treat the shop and inventory like a business within the business, because surprise supply shortages are a tax on your team's time.

Olympus Property has been recognized as a National Apartment Association Top Employer for 2023, 2024, and 2025. The starting salary for this role is $56,160 annually, with monthly and quarterly bonus eligibility. greenhouse_5255797008.title: Assistant Maintenance Manager
greenhouse_5255797008.rewritten_description:
What You'll Actually Do

This role sits between the wrench and the whiteboard. You're hands-on enough to diagnose a failing compressor or track down a plumbing issue at 7 a.m., but you're also the person making sure the rest of the maintenance team is executing turns on time and keeping the punch list honest. Bozzuto runs well-maintained communities, and the Assistant Maintenance Manager is a big reason why that holds up day to day.

The make-ready process will own a meaningful chunk of your attention. Units need to turn clean, complete, and on schedule so leasing can do its job. Beyond turns, you're running preventative maintenance programs, keeping mechanical systems operating efficiently, and making sure the property stays safe and presentable. In Portland, that includes grounds maintenance through the rainy season, which is most of the year. Snow removal is listed, though Portland's relationship with snow is complicated.

You'll carry a spot in the emergency on-call rotation and work some weekends. That's standard at any well-run residential community. If that's new information, this probably isn't the right fit.

The systems exposure here matters. Bozzuto mentions central plant, boilers, chillers, and split systems as desirable knowledge. If you've worked in a mid-rise or high-rise setting with complex mechanical infrastructure, that background translates directly. Garden-style experience alone may leave some gaps.

What You Bring

  • At least 5 years in the trades, facilities, or residential building maintenance
  • Working proficiency in HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and appliance repair
  • EPA certification; HVAC or NAPE certification strongly preferred
  • Familiarity with OSHA standards, risk management, and MSDS
  • Basic carpentry, drywall, and paint skills for unit turns and common area upkeep
  • Some supervisory experience, or a clear track record of leading peers informally
  • Comfort with work order platforms and basic Microsoft Office tools
  • Physical ability to handle frequent lifting in the 25 to 50 pound range, ladder work, and outdoor conditions

Context Worth Knowing

Bozzuto operates as a fee management company with a portfolio that skews toward higher-quality residential communities. That means asset preservation carries real weight internally. The "know it like you built it" language in their posting isn't just a slogan. Managers here are expected to understand why systems work the way they do, not just react when they don't.

greenhouse_4285309009.title: Leasing Hub Associate - Sandy Springs, GA
greenhouse_4285309009.rewritten_description:
Cortland's Leasing Hub Associate role sits in a corner of multifamily that most people outside the industry don't fully understand. This position operates centralized, off-site from any individual community. Instead of walking a prospect through a model unit, you're working a lead queue, handling inbound and outbound calls, emails, and texts, and converting that traffic into appointments for Cortland's on-site leasing teams. It's a volume role with a sales spine.

On a typical day, you're working through 40 to 50 leads sourced from RealPage's OneSite platform, qualifying prospects, matching them to the right community based on their needs, and generating scheduled tours. You carry deep knowledge of multiple Cortland properties at once, which means understanding pricing, concessions, amenities, and availability across a portfolio rather than a single address. That breadth is what makes this role a genuinely different kind of leasing experience.

The skill set that compounds here is worth naming directly. High-volume outbound sales sharpens your ability to qualify quickly and communicate value under pressure. Working across multiple communities builds portfolio fluency that traditional single-site leasing rarely develops. And because you're feeding the on-site teams, you develop a clear-eyed view of how traffic converts, where leads stall, and what messaging actually moves prospects to tour. Those are the instincts that translate well into leasing manager roles, regional marketing positions, or even revenue management support work down the road.

Cortland is a vertically integrated operator, one of the ten largest multifamily owners and managers in the country, with in-house design, construction, and operations. That structure means internal mobility is real, and the exposure you get to how a large portfolio runs from a centralized function tends to open doors that a single-community leasing role doesn't.

The strongest candidates for this role tend to have genuine comfort with outbound volume. Customer service experience alone isn't enough if it's been mostly reactive. What separates a good fit from a great one is someone who can hold a conversation with a prospect, read what they actually need, and connect that need to a specific community with enough conviction to get a commitment on the calendar.

What Cortland is looking for:
  • Two or more years of customer service experience, with a preference for direct sales
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills in English; bilingual fluency is a plus
  • Comfort with high outbound contact volume in a structured, metrics-driven environment
  • Proficiency in OneSite (RealPage); familiarity with L2L is preferred
  • Solid typing and computer skills to manage simultaneous lead channels efficiently

This role is based in Sandy Springs, GA, which puts you close to Cortland's Atlanta headquarters. For someone who wants to grow inside a large, professionally managed organization, that proximity matters.

greenhouse_8007634.title: Maintenance Supervisor
greenhouse_8007634.rewritten_description:
Weinstein Properties has operated its own communities for over 70 years, and Bexley Chamblee in the Atlanta metro fits that same model: owned, managed, and maintained in-house. For a Maintenance Supervisor, that structure matters. There's no third-party management layer between you and decisions, which means less friction when you need to move on a repair, a vendor call, or a turn.

What the Work Looks Like Day to Day

This is a working supervisor role. You'll lead a service team while staying hands-on across HVAC, plumbing, electrical, appliance repair, carpentry, drywall, and pool maintenance. Scheduling turns, managing work orders through business software, coordinating vendors, and running punch lists are all part of the job. You'll share on-call rotation with teammates, with a bonus paid for those on-call periods.

The Chamblee submarket sits in a busy corridor northeast of Atlanta, with a mix of garden-style communities and newer mid-rise product. Resident expectations in this area trend toward responsive, professional service, so the customer-facing side of this role carries real weight. How quickly and cleanly your team closes work orders directly affects occupancy and renewal rates.

What Weinstein Is Looking For

  • Minimum 4 years of trade experience across building maintenance disciplines
  • At least 1 year as a lead, assistant supervisor, or supervisor in apartment maintenance
  • EPA/CFC certification required (Type I and II, or Universal)
  • Comfortable using software to manage work orders, schedule turns, and communicate with the team
  • Valid driver's license, reliable transportation, and personal tools
  • Background and DMV check required

Candidates who stand out in this type of role typically bring more than technical breadth. The ability to prioritize competing work orders under pressure, coach junior technicians without slowing down production, and communicate clearly with residents separates strong supervisors from average ones. HVAC diagnostic confidence is especially useful given Georgia's climate demands on cooling systems.

Stability and Growth

Weinstein promotes from within and provides training for technicians who want to move up. For someone currently working as a lead tech or assistant supervisor, this role is a natural step toward a service director or regional maintenance position. Because Weinstein owns all of its communities across Virginia, North Carolina, Texas, Tennessee, and Georgia, internal mobility is a real option rather than a talking point.

The position includes a $2,500 sign-on bonus (details discussed during the interview), competitive base pay tied to experience, quarterly and annual bonus opportunities, rent discount, birthday time off, PTO, paid holidays, health, dental and vision coverage, an Employee Assistance Program, and a 401k with company match. Hours are Monday through Friday, 8 AM to 5 PM, with shared on-call rotation after hours.

greenhouse_5164936007.title: Lead Maintenance Technician- The Retreat
greenhouse_5164936007.rewritten_description:
Lead maintenance roles at apartment communities ask you to carry two jobs at once: hands-on technician and working supervisor. At MG Properties, a regional owner-operator with more than three decades of acquisition, rehabilitation, and management experience across the Western U.S., the Lead Maintenance Technician at The Retreat in Phoenix is exactly that kind of dual-function position. You'll turn wrenches and you'll direct a team.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Your day pulls in multiple directions. A service request queue needs triage. A make-ready punch list needs sign-off before a turn can close. A technician needs guidance on an HVAC diagnosis. Grounds need a walk. That's a representative morning at a property this size, and the ability to sequence those competing priorities without letting any one of them slide is the core skill this role exercises daily.

On the technical side, you'll handle diagnostics and repairs across all trades, including plumbing, electrical, and HVAC, and you'll be expected to hold HVAC Universal certification and CPO certification. Appliance repair, lock changes, appliance transfers, and painting are all part of the make-ready cycle here. You'll also manage preventive maintenance scheduling, track service requests through Yardi on an iPhone-based workflow, maintain SDS documentation, and keep accurate records on expenditures and work-in-progress.

The supervisory layer includes running safety meetings, maintaining HAZCOM standards, scheduling technicians in coordination with the property manager, and coaching your team on both technical execution and safety discipline. Emergency coverage is part of the job. A 200-plus unit community doesn't stop needing maintenance at 5 p.m.

Skills This Role Requires vs. Skills It Builds

MG Properties expects you to arrive with multi-trade competency and at least two years of apartment maintenance experience, ideally on a property of comparable size. HVAC Universal and CPO certifications are required, not preferred. You need to know how to read utility shut-off maps, manage parts inventory to avoid downtime, and keep a make-ready schedule moving. A valid driver's license with current liability insurance is also required.

What the role develops is the supervisory muscle. Scheduling a team to cover preventive maintenance, emergency response, and routine service simultaneously is a skill you sharpen through repetition. So is vendor coordination, budget awareness through PayScan, and the kind of documentation discipline that protects both the property and the owner's investment. Technicians who grow into this role and do it well often move into Maintenance Supervisor positions, where they own those responsibilities fully rather than sharing them with a supervisor above them.

What Separates Strong Candidates

Phoenix's heat puts HVAC demand on a different level than most markets. Summers here mean a compressed, high-volume service window where response time and diagnostic accuracy matter more than usual. Candidates who have managed that seasonal spike, kept delinquent work orders from stacking, and maintained resident satisfaction through it tend to stand out. The other differentiator is attitude toward documentation. Strong leads treat accurate records as part of the job, not a burden on top of it, because those records protect the team, the property, and the NOI.

  • Minimum two years of apartment maintenance experience, preferably on a 200-plus unit property
  • Demonstrated competency across plumbing, electrical, and HVAC trades
  • HVAC Universal certification and CPO certification required
  • Proficiency with Yardi maintenance systems
  • Valid driver's license with proof of current liability insurance
  • Ability to lift 50 pounds; comfort working indoors and outdoors with required safety attire
  • High school diploma or equivalent, or five years of maintenance experience in lieu of diploma

greenhouse_8590605002.rewritten_description:
Roofstock's short-term rental division is hiring a Hospitality Coordinator to work on the ground in the Isle of Palms market, keeping a portfolio of vacation homes ready for every guest arrival. At $22.50 an hour with a $135 monthly car allowance and $100 toward tools and equipment, this is a field-based, full-time position that requires real availability: weekends, holidays, early mornings, evenings. Two days off each week, but the schedule rotates around guest traffic, not a standard Monday through Friday calendar.

The work itself sits at the intersection of property care and hospitality operations. You'll run pre- and post-stay inspections, restock consumables, handle light maintenance (bulb swaps, TV resets, minor repairs), support turnovers, and respond when something goes wrong mid-stay. Think of it as a blend of property caretaker, runner, and front-desk coverage. You'll document everything through task management software and flag homes that show unusual supply burn or recurring issues. Occasionally you'll handle inbound and outbound calls with guests and owners, and assist Hospitality Managers with dispatching during off-peak hours.

Success in this role gets measured concretely: guest review scores averaging above 4.8, inspection completion rates, task accuracy, and how consistently your assigned homes meet what the team calls FCS readiness (functional, clean, stocked). Market leadership verifies this. There's real accountability built into the structure.

What Roofstock Is Looking For

  • At least one year in hospitality, property care, vacation rentals, or a closely related field
  • Comfort following checklists and brand standards with consistency
  • Physical capability: walking and standing throughout shifts, lifting up to 50 lbs
  • Reliable vehicle and valid driver's license (frequent driving between properties is a daily reality)
  • Proficiency with mobile apps and task tracking tools
  • Availability for weekends, holidays, and on-call rotations

Isle of Palms is a barrier island market where short-term rental demand is seasonal and compressed. Summers and holiday weekends create genuine surge periods, and the gap between a 4.7 and a 5.0 review score often comes down to whether the home felt cared for when the guest walked in. That's the standard this role is held to.

From a career trajectory standpoint, roles like this one build a specific and transferable skill set. You'll develop fluency in STR operations at a company that has been actively acquiring and expanding in this space, including its 2025 stake in Casago. People who perform well in coordinator roles within growing STR organizations often move into Team Lead positions, market operations, or vendor coordination. The operational discipline you build here, running inspections systematically, tracking inventory patterns, managing urgent issues calmly, translates directly into property management roles across both short-term and long-term rental platforms. Roofstock's broader platform spans SFR investment, asset management software, and tenant screening, which means internal mobility is a realistic path for someone who builds credibility on the ground.
