greenhouse_8628421002.title: Assistant Community Manager
greenhouse_8628421002.location: The Village at Muller Park, Bloomington, Indiana, United States
greenhouse_8628421002.rewritten_description:
Student housing runs on a different clock than conventional multifamily. Lease-up happens once a year, turn happens in a compressed window, and the resident base cycles out whether you're ready or not. The Assistant Community Manager role at The Scion Group's Village at Muller Park in Bloomington, Indiana sits right inside all of that. It's a real operational seat, not a stepping stone with a vague title.

What the Role Actually Covers

You'll work alongside the General Manager and step into that seat when they're out. That means you need to understand every layer of the property, not just the parts that fall under your usual responsibilities. Day-to-day, you're managing resident accounts, coordinating utility billing, keeping delinquency below 2% at month end, and handling the paperwork that comes with move-ins, transfers, and move-outs. You'll also stay close to the leasing side: running market surveys, tracking KPIs, managing concessions within budget, and helping the team hit revenue goals.

Facilities don't take care of themselves either. You'll conduct monthly inspections of vacant units and bed spaces, walk common areas and grounds, and coordinate work orders with staff or vendors. When something goes wrong after hours, you're on the on-call rotation. That's worth knowing before you apply.

Annual turn is a significant part of this job. Student housing communities typically execute a large-scale turnover in a short window between lease cycles. You'll help plan it, lead parts of it, and make sure the team executes it on time.

On the people side, you'll help hire, train, and coach onsite staff. Fair Housing compliance and safety training fall under your watch. A disorganized team creates resident experience problems fast in student housing, so keeping staff accountable to the schedule matters.

What Scion Is Looking For

  • At least one year of experience in property management or a residential living community
  • Comfort working inside a property management system (Entrata experience is a plus)
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Attention to detail, especially around accounts receivable and resident billing
  • A customer-focused approach that holds up under pressure
  • Ability to prioritize when several things demand attention at once

Honest Context for This Role

Student housing is operationally intense in ways that conventional Class A or B multifamily isn't. Residents are often living independently for the first time, which shapes the nature of escalated concerns and the volume of account issues you'll handle. Bloomington is a Big Ten college town, and occupancy pressure is real around IU's academic calendar. Strong candidates for this role tend to have sharp instincts around delinquency management and aren't rattled by the pace of turn season. The AGM title is a genuine path toward a General Manager role, and Scion promotes from within regularly across their portfolio.

Benefits include health, dental, and vision coverage, a 401k with matching, paid maternity leave, PTO, and a discretionary annual bonus. This is a full-time, exempt position based on-site at The Village at Muller Park. Visa sponsorship is not available.

greenhouse_4310236009.title: Senior Community Manager of Permanent Supportive Housing (Donner Lofts)
greenhouse_4310236009.rewritten_description:
Donner Lofts is a permanent supportive housing community in San Jose, and this role sits at the center of everything that keeps it functioning. MidPen Housing has operated affordable communities across Northern California since 1970, and this Senior Community Manager position reflects the complexity that comes with that track record. The population here includes residents experiencing housing instability and other significant challenges, so the work requires more than standard property management competency.

Day to day, you're overseeing rent collection, HUD compliance, certifications, and inspections while also supervising on-site staff and coordinating with service partners who provide resident support programs. Vendor management, invoicing, budget tracking, and variance reporting are steady parts of the job. So are tenant relations, lease enforcement, and the occasional eviction process handled with care and documentation. When emergencies arise, you respond and you lead.

What separates strong candidates here from average ones isn't just affordable housing experience, though that matters. It's the ability to hold both accountability and compassion at once. Residents in permanent supportive housing often have complex histories. A manager who defaults to pure compliance thinking will struggle. So will one who avoids difficult conversations. The people who do well in this environment understand trauma-informed approaches without abandoning the operational standards the property requires.

Yardi proficiency and familiarity with HUD regulatory requirements are expected. ARM or COS certifications are preferred and will be weighted in the review process. A valid California Real Estate license and a reliable insured vehicle are required for this role.

What You Bring

  • High school diploma or GED; two or more years of continuous property management experience, preferably in affordable or supportive housing
  • Working knowledge of HUD, ADA, and DFEH compliance requirements
  • Experience supervising staff and managing performance across a site team
  • Budget management skills including variance reporting and invoice processing
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office and Yardi
  • ARM or COS certification (preferred)
  • Valid California Real Estate license and insurable driving record

Pay runs between $36.81 and $41.41 per hour depending on experience. MidPen offers a full benefits package including health, dental, vision, a 403(b) retirement plan, paid parental leave, education reimbursement, and an EAP program, among others.

This role is based on-site at Donner Lofts in San Jose. MidPen has been recognized as a Great Place to Work in 2025, and their portfolio of more than 130 properties reflects an organization that has stayed active and stable in the affordable housing space for over five decades.

greenhouse_7798932003.title: Leasing Consultant (Alderwood)
greenhouse_7798932003.rewritten_description:
Leasing sits at the front door of every apartment operation, and the skills you build there compound fast. A strong leasing consultant learns to read traffic patterns, understand concessions strategy, and close leases in competitive markets. Those fundamentals carry directly into assistant manager roles, then property management, then regional oversight. Prometheus, the largest privately held apartment owner in the Bay Area with more than 13,000 units across Silicon Valley, Portland, and Seattle, is hiring a Leasing Consultant for their Alderwood community in Santa Clara.

What This Role Actually Involves

Prometheus calls this position a Neighbor Ambassador, and the title reflects a real operational philosophy rather than marketing language. You're handling three distinct functions simultaneously: guiding prospective residents through the leasing process from first inquiry to signed agreement, maintaining the administrative backbone of the community (market surveys, occupancy reports, rental postings, lease paperwork), and keeping current residents genuinely satisfied with where they live. That's a broader scope than a pure leasing role at many companies, and it's worth taking seriously as a credential builder.

Weekend availability is required. Saturday and Sunday are peak traffic days for apartment communities, so your regular days off will fall during the week. If you're coming from retail, hospitality, or food service, this schedule will feel familiar. If you're not, it's worth factoring in before you apply.

Qualifications and Compensation

Prometheus hires across industries and doesn't require prior property management experience. What they're looking for:

  • Genuine comfort in customer-facing, sales-oriented environments
  • Strong communication skills and the ability to self-manage day-to-day priorities
  • An entrepreneurial, problem-solving mindset
  • Alignment with a team-oriented culture that takes its B Corporation status seriously

The base pay runs $25.00 to $26.25 per hour, with a $200 per-lease incentive, a discretionary semi-annual bonus, and weekend shift premium pay layered on top. Additional bonuses exist for referrals, lease-up assignments, renovation projects, and training coaching. The benefits package is unusually strong for this level: Prometheus covers 100% of medical, vision, and dental premiums for eligible employees and dependents, offers 401(k) with employer matching, and includes tenure-based housing discounts that become more meaningful as you stay.

One thing that separates strong candidates from average ones at this level: the ability to treat administrative work with the same care as a guest interaction. Leasing consultants who let paperwork slide create delinquency exposure and compliance gaps that follow a property for months. The candidates who advance treat the back-office side of leasing as seriously as the front-door side.

greenhouse_4309017009.title: Assistant Community Manager
greenhouse_4309017009.rewritten_description:
Pooler sits in one of the more active growth corridors in coastal Georgia, and Hawthorne Residential Partners has built a footprint across the Southeast that puts them consistently in the top 50 multifamily operators nationally. That context matters for this role, because an ACM at a well-run regional company isn't just processing payments and answering phones. You're being groomed, whether you realize it yet or not.

The day-to-day here splits roughly into two lanes: leasing activity and financial administration. On the leasing side, you're working leads, conducting tours, closing applications, and keeping a close eye on renewal timelines. On the financial side, you're posting payments, monitoring delinquency, running ledger audits, and making the weekly collection calls that nobody loves but everybody needs. The community manager leans on the ACM to keep both lanes moving, and when the CM is out, you hold the wheel.

Hawthorne is looking for someone with at least two years in property management, preferably with some prior ACM experience. A CALP designation is a plus, though not a hard requirement. A valid driver's license is.

  • Two years of property management experience preferred
  • Six months of prior ACM-level experience preferred
  • High school diploma or GED required
  • Valid driver's license required
  • CALP accreditation a plus

The schedule runs Monday through Friday with Saturday hours (10 to 4), and one weekday off per week to keep you at 40 hours. Evening and weekend availability may come up around resident events. That's standard for this industry. If it surprises you, the role will be a rough fit.

Compensation includes hourly pay plus monthly leasing and renewal commissions and quarterly performance bonuses. The benefits package covers medical, dental, vision, 401k match, paid leave including parental leave, pet insurance, and a few things you don't always see at this level, like company-paid life insurance and telehealth access.

What separates a strong ACM from an average one at a company like Hawthorne is usually the financial piece. Leasing skills are teachable. Reading a ledger, catching a misapplied payment before it becomes a problem, understanding where delinquency is trending before the regional asks about it. That's where the real value shows up. Hawthorne's internal career path program is designed to move people from ACM to Community Manager, and the ones who get there fastest tend to be the ones who already think in terms of NOI and occupancy, not just traffic and leases.

greenhouse_8624537002.title: Leasing Consultant
greenhouse_8624537002.rewritten_description:
Jeffersonville sits just across the Ohio River from Louisville, and that positioning matters more than it might seem. Southern Indiana's rental market draws residents priced out of Louisville proper, people relocating for work in the river corridor, and long-term locals who want suburban stability without suburban isolation. A leasing consultant working this market needs to know how to sell that story, not just recite square footage and rent rates.

Waypoint Management Services is hiring a Leasing Consultant to join the team at their Jeffersonville community. The core of the job is converting interest into signed leases: answering calls and emails quickly, conducting tours that actually move people, following up with prospects who haven't committed, and guiding applicants through the full leasing process from qualification to move-in. You'll manage the paperwork side too, including lease preparation, prorations, and keeping traffic and application records accurate in the system. Yardi experience is a plus, though not required.

Beyond the transactional work, you'll contribute to occupancy through renewals and waitlist management, help with outreach and lead generation, and keep the leasing office, model, and amenity spaces tour-ready at all times. Fair Housing compliance isn't optional here, and comfort with lease documents and landlord-tenant basics is expected.

Bilingual candidates (English/Spanish) are preferred, which reflects the actual resident mix in many Southern Indiana communities. Weekend availability is required, as that's typically when traffic peaks.

What separates a strong candidate here from someone who's technically qualified: the ability to read where a prospect is in their decision and adjust the conversation accordingly. Objection handling in leasing isn't about overcoming resistance with scripts. It's about understanding what's actually holding someone back, whether that's timing, pricing, or uncertainty about the neighborhood, and responding with real information. Candidates who've come from hospitality or retail sales often develop this instinct faster than those with leasing experience alone, because they've learned to work with people under pressure without losing the relationship.

What Waypoint is offering

  • Monthly leasing and renewal bonuses, plus a Leaser of the Month monetary reward
  • Competitive base wage with an employee housing discount program
  • 120 hours of PTO in year one, increasing with tenure, plus two floating days
  • Medical, dental, and vision benefits subsidized and active on day one
  • 401(k) with company match
  • Commuter benefits, employee referral program, and professional development training

A minimum of two years in leasing, sales, or hospitality is preferred. A high school diploma or equivalent and a valid driver's license are required. If you're building a career in multifamily and want a role where your leasing numbers are actually recognized and rewarded, this is worth a close look.

greenhouse_5322881008.title: Community Care Associate
greenhouse_5322881008.rewritten_description:
Bozzuto has built a reputation in multifamily management for caring about the physical condition of its communities the same way it cares about the people who live in them. A Community Care Associate is the person who makes that visible every single day, keeping shared spaces clean, safe, and welcoming before most residents even notice anything needed attention.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

This is a hands-on, outdoor-and-indoor role that covers a lot of ground. Daily trash pickup and cleaning the trash area sets the tone first thing each morning. From there, the work shifts across the property: pulling weeds, raking, watering grounds, sweeping halls and curbs, checking and cleaning handrails, and making sure the pool is vacuumed and the clubhouse is tidy. You'll check hall lighting once a week and remove bandit signs daily. Monthly and seasonal tasks include hosing out hallways, power washing stairwells twice a year, and assisting with snow removal when needed. You'll also help deliver newsletters and community fliers to residents by early afternoon and pitch in with the maintenance team on light tasks and painting when they need an extra set of hands.

The role requires reliable personal transportation, the physical ability to lift 50 pounds, and comfort with sustained pushing, pulling, and climbing throughout a shift. Prior experience cleaning in a multifamily or commercial property setting is a plus, though not required.

Who Tends to Thrive Here

The candidates who do well in this role are the ones who take genuine ownership of their section of the property. They notice the thing that needs attention before someone else points it out. They're comfortable working independently through a routine but can pivot when the maintenance team needs backup or a resident interaction requires a moment of patience and courtesy. The job puts you in contact with residents regularly, whether it's a friendly nod in the hallway or fielding a quick question while you're working. A warm, professional presence matters.

This position also serves as a real entry point into property operations. Associates who build familiarity with how a community runs at the ground level, how maintenance workflows, how common areas affect resident satisfaction, often find themselves well-positioned to move into maintenance tech roles or porter lead positions over time. Bozzuto's investment in career development, including tuition reimbursement and internal growth programs, makes that trajectory more accessible than it is at many other operators.

Compensation and Benefits

  • Annual salary of $41,600, plus eligibility for additional bonus opportunities
  • Medical, dental, and vision coverage
  • 20 days of paid time off plus holidays
  • 401(k) with company match
  • Tuition reimbursement
  • Access to employee resource groups and a workplace that takes inclusion seriously

If you want to work for a company that treats the physical environment of its communities as a reflection of its values, and where your day-to-day work directly shapes how residents feel about where they live, this role in Saint Petersburg is worth a close look.

greenhouse_7800072003.title: Maintenance Technician (HVAC Required) - Riata
greenhouse_7800072003.rewritten_description:
Multifamily maintenance techs with real HVAC skills are in short supply. Olympus Property is staffing Riata, their Austin community, with a technician who can handle the full range of unit and building repairs and also own HVAC diagnostics without hand-holding.

What the Work Looks Like

This is a full-time, Monday through Friday position (9 AM to 6 AM, with some schedule flexibility) at a residential apartment community. You'll work alongside the lead maintenance technician and the broader service team, moving through daily work orders that span plumbing, electrical, appliance repair, carpentry, painting, and lock systems. HVAC is a core part of the job: preventative maintenance, diagnostics, filter replacements, and coil cleaning on residential units. You'll also cover minor to moderate plumbing work, fixture replacements, and common area upkeep including grounds and pool areas.

Work orders are tracked through property management software, so comfort logging and closing tickets is expected. Emergency availability is part of the role, though the primary schedule is standard weekday hours.

A typical day might start with a handful of open service requests from residents, a scheduled HVAC filter rotation on a block of units, and a punch list item from a recent turn. Priorities shift based on what the lead sets each morning, so being organized and communicative matters as much as technical skill.

What Olympus Needs from You

  • At least 2 years of maintenance experience in commercial, residential, or apartment settings
  • Working knowledge of HVAC systems; EPA certification or HVAC license required
  • Hands-on experience with plumbing, electrical, appliance repair, and general carpentry
  • Comfortable using software to track and close service requests
  • Available for emergency calls as needed outside regular hours

Pay runs $23 to $26 per hour depending on experience and location, with monthly and quarterly bonuses on top of base pay. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401(k) with employer matching, paid time off, an apartment rental allowance, tuition reimbursement, and pet insurance, among others.

Olympus has been recognized as a top employer by the National Apartment Association three consecutive years (2023, 2024, 2025), which reflects something real: technicians here tend to stay and grow. For a maintenance tech looking to move toward lead or service manager roles, Olympus has a stated career pathing program, which is worth asking about in the interview.

greenhouse_7801361003.title: Leasing Consultant (Crystal Springs Terrace)
greenhouse_7801361003.rewritten_description:
What You'll Actually Do

Crystal Springs Terrace is a Prometheus-managed community in San Bruno, and the Leasing Consultant role here sits at the intersection of sales, customer experience, and property operations. Prometheus calls this position "Neighbor Ambassador," and that framing reflects how the work actually runs day to day. You're guiding prospective residents through the leasing process, following up on traffic, and closing applications, but you're also the person current residents come to when something feels off about their experience. That dual accountability is real, and it shapes how you'll spend your time.

On the administrative side, you'll prepare rental agreements, run market surveys, build out neighborhood reports, and manage apartment listings. These tasks are where newer leasing professionals often underestimate the learning curve. Getting comfortable with lease documentation and occupancy tracking takes deliberate attention, and this role gives you the repetitions to build that fluency.

Weekend availability is required. Saturdays and Sundays are peak traffic days at any residential community, and your regular days off will fall Monday through Friday. If you've worked retail, hospitality, or any customer-facing role with weekend schedules, you already know what that rhythm looks like.

What You Bring

  • A background in customer service, sales, or marketing (property management experience is not required)
  • Comfort working through objections and guiding people toward a decision without pressure
  • Strong written and verbal communication for follow-up, resident correspondence, and reporting
  • Self-direction on routine tasks: market surveys, ad postings, and lease prep don't always come with someone checking behind you
  • Weekend availability as a consistent part of your schedule

The Bigger Picture

Prometheus is the largest privately held apartment owner in the Bay Area, with more than 13,000 units across Silicon Valley, Portland, and Seattle. They operate as a vertically integrated company, handling acquisitions, development, value-add renovations, and property management under one roof. For someone starting in leasing, that structure matters: there are visible career paths into leasing management, assistant management, and eventually property management within the same organization, without needing to jump to a different company to find the next level.

Compensation runs $25.00 to $26.25 per hour, with a $200 per-lease incentive, a discretionary semi-annual bonus, and weekend shift premium pay. Medical, dental, and vision coverage is 100% company-paid, and the benefits package includes a 401(k) with employer matching, tuition reimbursement, and tenure-based housing discounts. Prometheus also holds B Corporation certification, which reflects a specific set of commitments around how the company operates. Whether that matters to you is a personal question, but it's not marketing language. B Corp status carries third-party accountability.

The skill set you develop here, specifically closing leases, managing resident relationships, and learning the administrative backbone of a residential community, transfers cleanly into assistant management and beyond. Leasing is where most strong property managers started, and the reps you get on a busy Bay Area community will move you along that path faster than most entry points would.

greenhouse_4313610009.title: Regional Maintenance Floater
greenhouse_4313610009.rewritten_description:
Monday morning: three work orders already queued, a contractor arriving at one property at 9, and a call just came in about a door that won't latch at a building two towns over. That's a pretty normal start for this role.

John M. Corcoran and Company has operated across New England since 1951, and they've built a reputation that holds up under scrutiny. This opening sits south of Boston, covering multiple residential properties as a regional floater. The float structure means your week rarely looks the same twice. You're dispatched based on where the need is greatest, which gives you exposure to a wider range of physical plant conditions and unit types than a single-site technician typically sees.

What the Work Looks Like Day to Day

Daily maintenance requests form the core of the job. You'll handle the technical side of things: appliances, smoke detector installations, light fixtures, electrical and mechanical systems. You'll also keep the cosmetic side of properties sharp, painting, swapping screens, replacing windows, fixing doors, locks, tiles, and handrails. JMC properties are maintained to a standard that reflects the company's standing in the market, so attention to detail in make-ready and routine upkeep genuinely matters here.

Contractor oversight is part of the picture too. You'll coordinate with outside vendors on-site, track paperwork, and manage invoices tied to your work orders. When emergencies hit, including floods or back-to-back move-ins that compress your schedule, you're expected to stay composed and prioritize effectively. The on-call rotation means occasional after-hours availability comes with the territory.

What JMC Is Looking For

  • At least six months of hands-on trade or building maintenance experience
  • Working knowledge of electrical and mechanical systems at the property level
  • Ability to identify safety concerns and address them without waiting to be told
  • Comfort managing your own workflow across multiple sites
  • Specialized trade background in plumbing, electrical, HVAC, or roofing is a meaningful advantage

The pay range runs from $26.75 to $32.00 per hour, with a $2,500 sign-on bonus. The schedule is Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., with on-call rotation. Benefits include medical, dental, vision, life insurance, paid time off, holidays, and a 401(k) with company match.

From a career development standpoint, the float model here is genuinely useful. Technicians who work across multiple properties build pattern recognition faster than those who stay fixed at one site. You see more unit configurations, more contractor relationships, and more varied capex and repair scenarios. That breadth tends to accelerate the path toward a lead maintenance or maintenance supervisor role, where managing a team and a full property's physical plant becomes the job. If that's the direction you're heading, this kind of regional exposure builds the foundation faster than most single-site positions will.

greenhouse_5308655008.title: Leasing Agent
greenhouse_5308655008.rewritten_description:
Leasing is a skill set, and Birgo is looking for someone who's genuinely good at it. The work here centers on two core abilities: building quick, genuine rapport with strangers, and following through with the kind of organized, detail-oriented execution that turns a first phone call into a signed lease and a smooth move-in. Both matter equally. One without the other leaves gaps.

What This Role Actually Looks Like

You'd be covering roughly 700 units spread across Lockport, North Tonawanda, Hamburg, and Buffalo. These are vintage, market-rate properties, ranging from small 12-unit buildings to a 191-unit community. The heaviest concentration sits in Lockport and North Tonawanda, where you'd have dedicated leasing offices at Maplewood East Apartments and Roosevelt on Main. That local footprint matters: you'll get to know these neighborhoods well, and prospective residents will often be choosing between Birgo properties, which means your product knowledge needs to be real, not scripted.

Day to day, you're responding to inquiries, scheduling and conducting tours, processing applications accurately, and shepherding new residents through move-in. That last piece involves coordinating with property management and maintenance to make sure units are inspected, documented, and ready. You'll also keep an eye on listing ads and occupancy trends, and support the property manager with tenant care when needed. The role reports directly to the Western New York Regional Manager.

Weekends (Saturdays especially) are part of the schedule. Prospective residents shop for apartments on their days off, so availability on those days is a real requirement, not a footnote. You'll also need a reliable insured vehicle, since covering multiple WNY locations means you're driving between properties regularly. Occasional trips to Pittsburgh come up as well.

Skills That Will Carry You Here

Birgo says one year of leasing experience is preferred, but they're genuinely open to candidates coming from sales, customer service, or hospitality backgrounds. The underlying skills transfer well: reading people quickly, handling objections without getting defensive, staying organized under competing demands, and caring about the details that make a resident's first week feel smooth rather than chaotic.

Fair Housing knowledge is a real plus. If you haven't had formal training, it's worth getting familiar before you apply. Leasing software experience also helps, though it's learnable on the job.

What separates strong candidates here isn't just charisma. It's the combination of people skills and follow-through. Leasing agents who close well but let applications stall, or who charm prospects but miss documentation steps during move-in, create downstream headaches for the whole team. The candidates who thrive tend to be self-managing, genuinely curious about people, and comfortable holding themselves accountable without a lot of hand-holding.

Working at Birgo

Birgo describes itself as a growth-oriented company with an entrepreneurial culture, and the compensation structure reflects that. On-target earnings range from $46,000 to $71,000, combining an hourly base with performance-driven commissions. The spread is wide, which means your results directly shape your income. Benefits include medical, vision, dental, pet, and life insurance with a company contribution, a 401(k) with employer match, paid time off, mental health days, a profit-sharing program, a professional development stipend, and a healthy lifestyle reimbursement. Discounted rates at Birgo properties are also available for team members.

One thing worth knowing upfront: because this role involves managing Birgo's rental properties, team members can't hold concurrent outside real estate sales, leasing, or property management positions. If you're actively working in those areas elsewhere, that's a conflict you'd need to resolve before starting.

Birgo emphasizes team diversity and invests in the kind of culture where people actually know each other, through team outings and volunteer events alongside the professional development pieces. It's a real workplace with real dynamics, and they seem to know that retention starts with treating people like whole humans rather than just headcount.

greenhouse_4313257009.title: Maintenance Technician, Littleton, CO
greenhouse_4313257009.rewritten_description:
What You'll Actually Do

Maintenance work at a residential community covers a lot of ground, and that's exactly what makes it worth doing well. At Dakota Ridge in Littleton, you'll handle the day-to-day service requests that keep residents comfortable: appliance repairs, plumbing fixes, electrical troubleshooting, carpentry, and general building upkeep. You'll also support the broader physical condition of the property, which means walking the grounds with a sharp eye for curb appeal, flagging issues before they become bigger problems, and keeping the shop organized with tools accounted for and inventory tracked. Key control is part of the job, and so is making sure safety standards stay consistent across the community.

This role puts you in regular contact with residents. How you show up during a service call, whether it's a straightforward fix or a more involved repair, shapes how residents feel about where they live. That relationship piece matters here as much as the technical work.

What You Bring

  • At least one year of hands-on maintenance experience in a residential or commercial setting
  • Working knowledge across the core trades: appliances, plumbing, electrical, carpentry, and general building systems
  • Comfort using computers and related applications for work orders or communication
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills in English
  • A methodical approach to inspections and follow-through on punch list items

Where This Role Takes You

Technicians who build a broad skill set across trades and develop consistent, professional habits with residents tend to move into lead maintenance or maintenance supervisor roles over time. The ability to diagnose problems accurately, prioritize work orders efficiently, and manage make-ready turns well are the skills that property managers notice and that open doors to higher responsibility. What You'll Actually Do

This leasing consultant role at Bozzuto's New Rochelle community puts you at the center of the resident acquisition cycle. Your day runs from prospect to lease: fielding inbound inquiries, following up with leads before they go cold, and converting that interest into scheduled tours. The tours themselves matter here. Bozzuto operates communities where the in-person experience is a real differentiator, so your ability to read a prospect and personalize the walk-through carries genuine weight on your closing rate.

Beyond the floor plan conversation, you're responsible for building the community's social presence. That means creating content on platforms like Instagram and Facebook that generates organic interest, not just reposting corporate graphics. Residents and prospects increasingly discover communities through social before they ever contact the leasing office, so this piece of the job is tied directly to traffic and occupancy. You'll also work three weekends per month, with two weekdays off in exchange. That's the reality of leasing: peak prospect traffic happens on Saturdays and Sundays, and the schedule reflects it.

What You Bring

  • Strong verbal and written communication, comfortable shifting tone from a quick text follow-up to a detailed email about lease terms
  • Genuine comfort with social media content creation, specifically Facebook and Instagram
  • Sales instinct and the ability to read where a prospect is in their decision process
  • Proficiency with software and property management platforms (or the aptitude to learn them quickly)
  • A sharp, professional presentation for in-person tours and community events
  • A New York real estate license, or the commitment to obtain one within 90 days of hire

Context Worth Knowing

New Rochelle has seen meaningful multifamily development activity over the past several years, with the downtown rezoning attracting new Class A product. That means the rental market there carries real competitive pressure. Prospects often tour multiple communities in a single afternoon, so the quality of your interaction and follow-up cadence matters more than it would in a less saturated submarket. Consultants who stand out in this environment tend to be the ones who remember details from a prospect's first call and reference them during the tour. That kind of specificity builds trust faster than any scripted pitch.

Bozzuto reports a salary range of $56,732 to $58,000 for this position, with additional bonus opportunities. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, 20 days of paid time off plus holidays, a 401(k) with company match, and tuition reimbursement.

greenhouse_4308279009.title: Front Door Waste Technician - North Fort Worth, TX
greenhouse_4308279009.rewritten_description:
Valet trash has become a standard amenity at Class A and many Class B multifamily communities across the Dallas-Fort Worth metro, and keeping that service running well requires someone who's consistent, physically capable, and takes resident-facing work seriously. Cortland operates a large portfolio of apartment communities in DFW, and this role supports one of their North Fort Worth properties.

What the Work Actually Involves

Each shift, you'll walk a set route through the community, collecting bagged waste from resident doorsteps and moving it through leak-proof carts to onsite compactors or containers. The route includes stairs, outdoor walkways, parking areas, pool decks, dog waste stations, and mail kiosks. You'll also clear debris, clean spills, and keep the compactor area clear and safe. All of this gets logged through a mobile app, including timestamps and photos, so documentation habits matter as much as the physical work itself.

Cortland expects its site teams to follow EPA and OSHA standards for waste handling, and this role is no exception. You'll need to recognize prohibited or improperly bagged waste and respond appropriately, and you'll interact with residents and staff throughout your shift. A professional, courteous presence is part of the job, not an afterthought.

What Cortland Is Looking For

  • High school diploma or equivalent, preferred
  • At least one year in waste services or a customer-facing role
  • Working knowledge of EPA and OSHA regulations around waste handling
  • Physical ability to climb stairs, walk extended distances, and lift up to 50 lbs
  • Comfort working outdoors in varying Texas weather conditions, including summer heat
  • Valid Class E driver's license for local driving as needed
  • Personal smartphone (Android 2.2+ or iPhone iOS 4.3+) with an active data plan for app-based reporting
  • Bilingual ability is a plus, though not required

One thing that separates reliable candidates in this role from those who wash out quickly: route discipline. The job looks straightforward, but completing a full property route efficiently every shift, in summer heat that regularly pushes past 100 degrees in North Fort Worth, while keeping documentation clean and resident interactions professional, takes real consistency. If you've held a route-based service job and take pride in finishing what you started, that background translates directly here.

Cortland is a vertically integrated multifamily owner-operator founded in 2005, currently ranked among the top 10 multifamily owners in the country. Their DFW presence is significant, which means this role sits inside a company with genuine infrastructure and defined career paths for people who perform well at the site level.

greenhouse_7947387.title: Leasing Consultant
greenhouse_7947387.rewritten_description:
Leasing consultant roles at family-owned, multi-state operators tend to look different from those at institutional REITs. The training is more hands-on, the culture tends to be less siloed, and the people who rise fast are usually the ones who treat the job as a craft rather than a stepping stone. That's the environment Weinstein Properties has built over 70 years of continuous family ownership, and their opening at Bexley Westshore in Cumming, GA reflects that philosophy.

What the Role Actually Involves

This position covers the full leasing cycle: greeting prospects, conducting tours, following up on leads, and converting traffic into signed leases. But it also extends into the day-to-day work that keeps a community running well. You'll handle administrative tasks, respond to resident concerns, help maintain the appearance of the property, and assist with resident events when they come up. Weinstein is direct about this: everyone does a bit of everything. If you're someone who counts tasks and guards job descriptions, this probably isn't the right fit. If you like variety and want to understand how a property actually operates, it's a solid environment to learn in.

The schedule is worth understanding clearly. This is an alternate schedule position, working Saturdays and one weekday off each week. Hours run 9am to 6pm on weekdays and 9am to 5pm on Saturdays. Sundays are always off. Weinstein pays an additional $80 per pay period bonus for this schedule, which compounds meaningfully over a year on top of the base hourly rate starting at $20. If you have flexibility on which weekday you take off, that can also be accommodated.

What Weinstein Is Looking For

Prior leasing experience isn't required. Weinstein trains from the ground up, and they're direct about preferring attitude and drive over a polished resume. That said, the candidates who tend to thrive here share a few specific traits:

  • Strong verbal and written communication, especially the ability to listen well before responding
  • Genuine comfort with customer-facing work, including difficult conversations with residents
  • The organizational discipline to manage administrative tasks alongside a busy leasing floor
  • Physical readiness for a role that keeps you moving: walking units, inspecting make-ready homes, and staying engaged throughout the day
  • A team orientation where pitching in outside your lane is the norm, not the exception

Where This Role Leads

Leasing consultant is one of the best entry points in property management because the skills compound quickly. You develop sales instincts, customer service depth, and operational awareness simultaneously. At Weinstein specifically, many current managers and corporate team members started in leasing. The path from consultant to assistant manager to property manager is well-worn here, and the company has enough geographic scale across Virginia, North Carolina, Texas, Tennessee, and Georgia to support lateral moves and promotions without having to leave the organization. If your goal is eventually managing a community's full NOI performance, understanding leasing fundamentals first makes you a sharper operator later.

Benefits include health, dental and vision insurance, a 401k with company match, rent discount, paid holidays, birthday time off, vacation and sick time, and an Employee Assistance Program. Quarterly bonuses are also part of the compensation structure beyond the hourly rate.

What You'll Actually Do

This is a grounds and make-ready support role at Somerfield at Lakeside Apartments, a residential community in Elk Grove, CA managed by MG Properties. Your day starts outside. You're picking up litter, clearing pet droppings, pulling abandoned furniture and trash, and keeping every exterior area presentable. That's the core of it.

greenhouse_4313918009.location: 1287 Shoals Apartments - 1287 Cedar Shoals Drive - Athens, GA - 30605
greenhouse_4313918009.rewritten_description:
Community Manager roles at mid-size multifamily operators tend to sit at an interesting intersection: you're close enough to daily operations to feel the pulse of the property, but accountable enough to ownership that your financial decisions actually matter. At Hawthorne Residential Partners, a Southeast-rooted company that ranks among the top 50 largest multifamily managers in the country, that dynamic is very much in play at 1287 Shoals Apartments in Athens, GA.

What the Role Actually Covers

This is a full-scope community manager position. You'll own the financial side: budgets, rent collection, delinquency tracking, deposit accounting, and reporting through Yardi. On the leasing side, you're not just supervising the process, you're participating in it. Conducting tours, responding to leads, guiding renewals, and managing occupancy through both traffic conversion and resident retention are all part of the job. You'll also handle vendor relationships, property inspections, maintenance coordination, and online reputation management.

The team leadership piece carries real weight here. You'll hire, train, and coach both office and maintenance staff, run weekly team meetings, and serve as the primary point of escalation for resident concerns. Hawthorne emphasizes their "Live It" culture, which in practical terms means they expect their community managers to model the service standards they want the whole team to deliver.

What Hawthorne Is Looking For

  • At least two years of property management experience, with time in both leasing consultant and assistant community manager roles
  • Six months of direct community manager experience in multifamily, strongly preferred
  • Familiarity with Yardi and Knock preferred
  • CAM, CAPS, a real estate license, or a property management license is a plus
  • Valid driver's license required
  • High school diploma or GED equivalent

The schedule runs Monday through Friday, 9 AM to 6 PM, with Saturdays from 10 AM to 4 PM. One weekday off is provided to keep the week at 40 hours. Some evening and weekend availability may come up for resident events or community needs.

Where This Role Can Take You

Hawthorne explicitly names the path: Community Manager to Regional Manager. That trajectory is realistic in multifamily, and the skills you build here are the exact ones regional roles demand. Reading a T-12, managing NOI under budget pressure, developing leasing staff, handling ownership communication, keeping occupancy steady through a slow lease-up season. All of it compounds. Community managers who can demonstrate clean financials, low delinquency, and a team that retains strong performers are the ones regional operators promote.

Athens is a college market, which adds its own rhythm. Seasonal traffic spikes, a high MTM exposure near the academic calendar, and turnover patterns that differ from a typical suburban garden-style community. If you've worked a university-adjacent property before, that experience transfers directly. If you haven't, it's a genuine learning curve worth acknowledging.

Compensation includes a base salary plus monthly leasing and renewal commissions and quarterly performance bonuses. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401k match, paid parental and adoption leave, pet insurance, and paid time off that includes your birthday.

greenhouse_5326124008.title: Maintenance Technician
greenhouse_5326124008.rewritten_description:
Hillpointe builds and operates market-rate workforce housing across the Sun Belt, and this Maintenance Technician role sits at the center of keeping those assets performing. Based in Lakeland, FL, you'll work across buildings, grounds, common areas, and amenities, handling the full range of day-to-day maintenance that keeps a residential property running.

The work is hands-on and varied. On any given day that might mean diagnosing an HVAC issue in the morning, closing out work orders from resident requests midday, and walking a vacant unit through make-ready punch list items before the afternoon ends. You'll also handle preventive maintenance, assist with grounds upkeep, manage inventory, and coordinate with vendors and contractors when outside work is needed. Documentation matters here, including tracking materials used and keeping records current.

This position runs on a rotating on-call schedule. Evening, morning, and weekend availability is required. That's a real part of the job, and worth factoring in before you apply.

What Hillpointe is looking for

  • Demonstrated ability to diagnose and repair mechanical issues in residential buildings
  • Experience with preventive maintenance and work order systems
  • EPA Type I and II or Universal certification for refrigerant recycling, or willingness to obtain it
  • Valid driver's license (required for golf cart operation on property)
  • Ability to lift up to 50 lbs regularly, climb ladders, and work outdoors in Florida's heat
  • Comfort with hand tools, power tools, and reading technical manuals or schematics
  • High school diploma or GED, plus relevant hands-on experience

Candidates who stand out bring more than technical repair skills. The ones who perform well in this type of role also communicate clearly with residents and management, stay organized across multiple open work orders, and flag safety issues before they become incidents. Hillpointe controls everything in-house from construction through asset management, which means the maintenance team interacts with a more integrated operation than you'd find at a typical third-party managed property. That structure gives good technicians real visibility into how decisions get made.

If you're building toward a lead or maintenance supervisor role, this kind of position gives you exposure to the full scope of residential property maintenance at a company that promotes from within its own operational structure.

greenhouse_6113867004.title: Maintenance Technician
greenhouse_6113867004.rewritten_description:
Maintenance in a Managed Portfolio That Tracks Every KPI

Cottonwood Residential runs a tight operation. Their communities are measured, their standards are consistent, and their maintenance teams are expected to keep units turning fast and residents satisfied. The Maintenance Technician role at Current Apartments in Murray, UT sits right at the center of that: every make-ready you complete, every work order you close, and every after-hours call you handle directly affects occupancy and NOI. This is the kind of shop where your output shows up in the numbers.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Day to day, you're moving through work orders: plumbing repairs, electrical troubleshooting, carpentry, appliance fixes, and general upkeep of units and grounds. Make-readies are a consistent part of the workload. When a unit turns, the punch list needs to get done accurately and quickly so leasing can get it back online. Slow turns cost occupancy. You know that, and so does Cottonwood.

The role carries an on-call component with after-hours emergency coverage. You'll have the support of a Service Manager when those calls come in, but the expectation is that you can triage and resolve issues independently. The physical demands are real: lifting up to 50 lbs., extended time on your feet, working at elevation, and accessing tight spaces are all part of the job.

Qualifications the team is looking for include:

  • Hands-on experience with plumbing, electrical, and general carpentry repairs
  • A valid driver's license
  • Strong English communication skills, both written and verbal
  • Availability for evenings, weekends, and on-call rotation
  • EPA Type II or Universal certification (a genuine plus, not just a checkbox)
  • HVAC troubleshooting experience (the more depth, the better)
  • CPO certification (a plus for properties with pool amenities)

HVAC competency is worth calling out specifically. Technicians who can diagnose and repair HVAC systems without always escalating to a vendor keep maintenance costs down and response times short. That skill set matters to any operator watching their capex and service budgets closely.

The Company and Where This Role Can Lead

Cottonwood Residential has a track record of promoting from within. A Maintenance Technician who builds strong diagnostic skills, keeps a clean work order close rate, and communicates well with the property team is the natural pipeline for a Lead Technician or Service Manager role. Those positions carry more responsibility over the make-ready schedule, vendor coordination, and team oversight, so the ceiling here is real if you want to grow.

Cottonwood also offers a solid benefits package: full medical, vision, dental, life, and disability coverage available within the first 30 days, a 401k and HSA with company match, three weeks of PTO in year one, and 10.5 paid holidays. For maintenance professionals who've worked at smaller operations without those benefits, this is a meaningful step up in total compensation.

Cottonwood is hosting an in-person hiring event on Wednesday, July 15th from 12 to 4pm at Park Avenue Apartments (1240 E Stringham Ave, Salt Lake City, UT 84106). No appointment needed. Walk in and meet the hiring team directly.

greenhouse_5343466008.title: Assistant Maintenance Manager - $2,500 Sign On Bonus
greenhouse_5343466008.rewritten_description:
Maintenance work in multifamily housing pulls from a wide range of skills at once. You're diagnosing a boiler issue in the morning, coaching a tech through a plumbing repair by midday, and reviewing punch lists for upcoming turns before the day ends. This Assistant Maintenance Manager role at Bozzuto's Bethesda property sits at that intersection of hands-on technical work and team leadership. Both sides matter equally here.

The Skills This Role Draws On Most

The technical foundation is broad: HVAC, plumbing, electrical, appliance repair, basic carpentry and drywall, and familiarity with complex mechanical systems including central plant, boilers, chillers, and split systems. Certifications in HVAC or EPA aren't just preferred checkboxes. They signal that you understand the systems at a level that lets you troubleshoot rather than guess.

Equally important is your ability to read people and situations. Residents submitting service tickets aren't just reporting problems. They're trusting that someone will follow through. Strong candidates in this role treat that follow-through as a professional standard, not an afterthought. The same interpersonal skill applies to the technicians you'll work alongside and lead. You'll set the pace and the tone on the floor, and the team will take cues from how you handle pressure, detail, and accountability.

Safety fluency matters throughout. Knowledge of OSHA standards, MSDS protocols, and applicable building and county codes shapes how you run day-to-day operations, not just how you respond to incidents. The goal is an accident-free environment, and that comes from habits, not luck.

What You'll Actually Be Managing

The make-ready process is a core responsibility here. Turns need to move quickly and cleanly so units can be leased without delay. That means managing your own work and keeping others on schedule, with an eye for detail that catches what a quick walkthrough might miss.

Preventative maintenance programs preserve the asset long-term, and you'll be the one making sure those schedules get executed consistently. Grounds upkeep, snow removal, general cleanliness, and safety across the community all fall within scope. This is a role that requires weekend availability and participation in an on-call emergency rotation. Those are real commitments, and worth knowing before you apply.

  • 5 or more years in the trades, facilities, or residential building maintenance
  • HVAC, EPA, and/or NAPE certification
  • Supervisory experience, or a clear readiness to step into that responsibility
  • Comfort with technology platforms, apps, and the Microsoft Office suite
  • Physical ability to frequently lift 25 to 50 pounds, climb ladders, and work in varying weather

Doing This Role at Bozzuto

Bozzuto operates across design, development, and management, which means the people running maintenance at their communities work within a company that has a direct stake in the condition and reputation of the asset. That context tends to raise the bar on how maintenance is approached. The "know it like you built it" standard they describe isn't a slogan. It reflects a mindset they look for in candidates who take ownership seriously.

For someone with strong trade skills who's ready to grow into a leadership track, this role offers a clear path. Assistant Maintenance Managers who build supervisory credibility here are well-positioned to move into Maintenance Manager roles. Bozzuto's portfolio and internal development programs support that progression. The $2,500 sign-on bonus, salary range of $61,000 to $63,000, and benefits including medical, dental, vision, 20 days of PTO, 401k with company match, and tuition reimbursement round out the package.

greenhouse_4314173009.title: Leasing & Sales Consultant - Cortland at the Nations
greenhouse_4314173009.rewritten_description:
A prospect submits an inquiry at 9 a.m. By 10, you've called, texted, and scheduled a tour. That rhythm, repeated across a full pipeline, is what drives occupancy at Cortland at the Nations.

Cortland is a vertically integrated multifamily operator, one of the top 10 in the country by portfolio size, with in-house design, construction, and management. At the property level, that structure means you're backed by real resources. As a Leasing and Sales Consultant, your job is to convert traffic into signed leases and keep the community performing against its occupancy and revenue targets.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

You own your pipeline. That means proactive follow-up, not just responding to whoever walks in. You'll use a CRM to track every lead interaction, monitor your conversion metrics, and adjust your approach based on what the numbers tell you. Consultative selling is the standard here: you're uncovering what a prospect actually needs and building a case for why this community fits, not just reciting floor plans and pricing.

Beyond the leasing office, you'll help manage the community's marketing presence, including social media, and organize resident events that build retention. When objections come up, you handle them directly and move forward. The role also carries responsibility for maintaining accurate records and reporting on lead activity consistently.

What Cortland is Looking For

  • At least 6 months of experience in sales, customer-facing work, or a performance-tracked role
  • Comfort being measured against leasing goals and conversion targets
  • Ability to build rapport quickly and handle a high volume of prospect interactions
  • Organized follow-up habits and attention to detail in CRM usage
  • Receptiveness to coaching and willingness to adjust approach based on feedback
  • Professional presentation that matches a premium brand standard

One thing that separates strong leasing consultants from average ones in this type of role: the follow-up discipline. Most lost leases aren't lost on the tour. They're lost in the 48 hours after it, when a prospect goes quiet and no one follows up with purpose. If you treat follow-up as a system rather than an afterthought, you'll outperform peers who rely on walk-in traffic alone.

Nashville's rental market has seen significant lease-up activity over the past few years, with new supply entering submarkets across the metro. That context makes consistent traffic conversion and strong resident retention more important than ever at the property level. This role sits at the center of both.

greenhouse_7802852003.title: Lead Maintenance Technician - Sedona Ranch
greenhouse_7802852003.rewritten_description:
Sedona Ranch is a conventional apartment community in Odessa, TX, and Olympus Property is hiring a Lead Maintenance Technician to run its day-to-day maintenance operation. This is essentially a working supervisor role. You're turning units, scheduling the team, pulling service requests, coordinating vendors, and getting your hands dirty on HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and appliance calls when the situation calls for it.

What You'll Actually Do

The job covers a lot of ground. On any given week you might be reviewing the make-ready schedule to confirm vacant units will hit move-in ready status on time, walking the grounds and common areas for a punch list inspection, placing parts orders to keep the shop stocked, and meeting with an outside contractor about a structural repair. You'll also hire and develop the service team under you, which means the quality of your people directly reflects your leadership. The office staff and property manager will lean on you to keep show units presentable and turns moving without delays.

On-call rotation is part of this role. That's worth stating plainly. After-hours emergencies happen at apartment communities, and as the lead, you're the escalation point when something goes sideways at 10 PM.

  • EPA/HVAC certification required
  • Minimum 3 years in apartment maintenance, with supervisory experience preferred
  • Working knowledge of HVAC, plumbing, electrical systems, appliance repair, and carpentry
  • Comfortable using property management software to track work orders, inventory, and inspections
  • Organized enough to manage a team's daily, weekly, and monthly workloads without constant direction from above

What You Bring

The candidates who stand out in this role aren't just technically strong. They're the ones who manage their team's schedule proactively, catch deferred maintenance before it becomes an emergency, and communicate clearly with the leasing office so vacant units don't sit longer than they should. Occupancy goals depend on turns being completed on time, and the lead tech is the person who makes or breaks that timeline.

Pay runs $27 to $30 per hour depending on experience and location, with monthly and quarterly bonuses available. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401(k) with employer matching, an apartment rental allowance, tuition reimbursement, and paid time off. Olympus has earned recognition from the National Apartment Association as a top employer in 2023, 2024, and 2025, which reflects something real about how the company treats its maintenance staff, not just corporate-level employees.

Standard schedule is Monday through Friday, 9 AM to 5 PM, with some flexibility built in. If you've been the reliable technician who's ready to step fully into the lead seat, or you're already supervising and want a team that invests in your growth, this is worth a serious look.

greenhouse_8059777.title: Groundskeeper
greenhouse_8059777.rewritten_description:
Grounds work at a well-run apartment community is more operational than it looks. At a property like Bexley at Brier Creek, the groundskeeper sets the tone for first impressions every single day, and in a market like Raleigh where garden-style lease-up communities are competing hard for residents, curb appeal isn't decorative. It's a leasing tool.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Weinstein Properties has operated for over 70 years as a family-owned company, managing more than 60 apartment communities across five states. Their approach leans toward hands-on daily operations, which means the groundskeeper at Bexley at Brier Creek works as a visible, active part of the on-site team rather than a background function.

The schedule runs Monday through Friday, 8am to 5pm. Daily responsibilities include litter pickup, cleaning pet waste stations, maintaining landscaped areas through weeding and planting, and supporting the maintenance team with light tasks as needed. You'll operate equipment including backpack blowers and power washers, move around the property by golf cart, and occasionally handle trash-outs on vacant units. Light painting and housekeeping support are also part of the mix. The physical demands are real: lifting up to 50 pounds regularly, prolonged walking and standing, frequent bending and stooping, and working outdoors year-round through North Carolina's heat, humidity, and occasional cold snaps.

Repetition is built into the role. Litter and pet waste pickup happen daily. That consistency is what keeps a property looking sharp, and it takes someone who finds satisfaction in maintaining standards rather than waiting for variety to keep them engaged.

Who Fits This Role

  • Reliable and punctual. The team depends on you showing up.
  • Self-directed. Much of the day involves independent work with minimal supervision.
  • Physically capable of meeting the demands described above, with or without accommodation.
  • Comfortable with repetitive, unglamorous tasks done to a consistent standard.
  • Willing to collaborate with maintenance and leasing staff when the situation calls for it.

Compensation and Growth

Pay starts at $16 per hour with quarterly bonuses. A $1,000 stay-on bonus is currently available after 90 days in good standing. Benefits include health, dental, and vision insurance, a 401k with company match, paid holidays, birthday time off, vacation and sick time, an Employee Assistance Program, and a rent discount.

Weinstein's track record suggests genuine room to grow. Team members who show a willingness to learn and a strong work ethic have a clear path toward maintenance technician roles, which carry significantly higher earning potential and broader skill sets. For someone starting out in property maintenance, a groundskeeper position is often the most direct entry point into a long-term career in multifamily operations.

greenhouse_8631169002.title: Community Manager
greenhouse_8631169002.location: Lark Gainesville, Gainesville, Florida, United States
greenhouse_8631169002.rewritten_description:
Student housing community management sits in its own category within property management. The operational calendar runs on an academic year, not a calendar year, and that shapes everything from leasing velocity to the annual turn. At Lark Gainesville, a student living community near the University of Florida, Scion is looking for a General Manager who can handle the full scope of that cycle with real competence.

What This Role Actually Covers

This is a full-operation leadership position. You're responsible for financial performance, physical plant, staffing, and the resident experience simultaneously. On the financial side, that means owning the annual budget process, managing NOI through expense control and revenue targets, handling variance reporting, and working with regional leadership on capex approvals. You're not handing off vendor bids or budget forecasting to someone else. You own those processes and coordinate with partner departments to execute them.

Facilities accountability here includes monthly property walks with scored assessments, quarterly apartment inspections, permit compliance, and identifying capital improvement needs before they become emergencies. You'll work directly with the Facilities and Capital department on project approval and execution, and you're expected to obtain competitive bids on work that exceeds the property's pre-approved threshold.

Staffing is a hands-on responsibility as well. You'll partner with Talent Acquisition and HR through Greenhouse for hiring, coordinate training and development through Scion's Learning and Development team, and manage scheduling including after-hours on-call coverage where you serve as primary responder.

The Annual Turn Is Central to This Role

At a student housing property, the summer turn is one of the most operationally demanding periods of the year. At Lark Gainesville, that means coordinating make-ready timelines across a high unit count, managing punch lists with vendors and your facilities team, tracking progress through Turnable, and staying hands-on throughout. That last point is worth emphasizing: this role explicitly includes physical tasks during turn, moving furniture, helping with punches, managing trash volume, and cleaning units alongside the team. Candidates who expect to manage the turn from a desk will find this role a poor fit.

The University of Florida's enrollment scale and the density of purpose-built student housing in Gainesville means the competitive market moves quickly during lease-up season. Leasing velocity, gain to lease, and concession management are metrics you'll be accountable for, and the market context makes those metrics genuinely meaningful.

Experience and Tools Required

  • At least three years managing a residential community with direct oversight of a team of three or more
  • Proficiency in property management systems, with Entrata preferred
  • Comfort working across multiple platforms: Vena for budgeting, ADP for payroll and scheduling, Qualtrics for experience data, ClickUp for project management, and Lattice for performance tracking
  • Strong written and verbal communication, conflict management, and vendor management skills
  • A customer-centric approach that extends to both residents and staff

Candidates who stand out in this type of role tend to have experience managing the full turn cycle at a property with significant unit count, not just leasing or maintenance coordination in isolation. The ability to read financial reports, act on them quickly, and communicate clearly with a regional team is what separates solid candidates from strong ones here. Scion offers a defined career path with internal development resources, which makes this a reasonable next step for someone currently in an Assistant Manager role who's ready to take on full P&L ownership.

If you've spent at least a year handling maintenance requests at a residential community and can move between a leaky faucet, a tripped breaker, and a cabinet repair in the same afternoon, the technical side of this role fits your existing skill set.

Curb appeal and unit condition matter here. Part of your daily work is being an extra set of eyes on the property. That kind of ownership mindset, where you treat the property like your own, is what separates a strong maintenance tech from an average one.

You don't need to be a salesperson, but you do need to handle interactions professionally and leave residents feeling taken care of.

Berkshire owns and manages its own properties, which means you're working for the owner, not a third-party operator. That structure typically means faster decisions on repairs, clearer accountability, and a maintenance team that has real standing within the organization.

greenhouse_5343765008.title: Assistant Maintenance Manager
greenhouse_5343765008.rewritten_description:
Bozzuto builds and manages properties with a reputation for quality that's visible at the unit level, and this role sits right at the center of protecting that reputation. As an Assistant Maintenance Manager at their Alexandria community, you're the person who keeps asset value intact, turns make-readies efficiently, and builds the kind of maintenance culture where residents actually notice the difference.

What You'll Actually Do

The make-ready process will be a significant part of your rhythm. You'll manage apartment turns from punch list to final walk, keeping units moving through the pipeline so leasing can do its job. Beyond turns, you'll handle HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and appliance repairs directly while also coaching the team around you. Preventative maintenance programs are yours to execute consistently, not just schedule. You'll also take responsibility for the building's mechanical systems, which at a Bozzuto property may include central plant equipment, split systems, boilers, and chillers. Grounds upkeep, snow removal, and code compliance round out the scope. Weekend availability and participation in an on-call emergency rotation are part of the role year-round.

What You Bring

  • At least five years working in the trades, facilities, or residential building maintenance
  • Hands-on proficiency in HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and appliance repair
  • HVAC, EPA, or NAPE certification
  • Familiarity with OSHA standards, MSDS, and risk management principles
  • Basic carpentry, drywall, and painting skills
  • Some supervisory or leadership experience, even informal
  • Comfort with Microsoft Office and property management technology platforms
  • Physical ability to lift 25 to 50 pounds frequently and work in variable weather conditions

Where This Role Leads

The Assistant Maintenance Manager title is a real stepping stone in this industry. People who do this job well tend to move into Building Maintenance Manager or Portfolio Maintenance Manager positions within a few years. The skills that compound fastest here are the leadership ones: learning to delegate repairs you could do yourself, building accountability into a team's daily habits, and communicating maintenance status clearly to property management. Those skills transfer directly into senior operations roles where you're less hands-on-tools and more hands-on-systems.

What separates strong candidates from average ones at this level is the ability to think about asset preservation proactively rather than reactively. Anyone can respond to a work order. The people who advance are the ones who catch the HVAC inefficiency before it becomes a capital expense, or who keep a turn on schedule when a vendor falls through. If that mindset already describes how you work, this position is a natural fit.

greenhouse_5186379007.title: Property Manager
greenhouse_5186379007.rewritten_description:
This role puts three skill sets to work every day: financial analysis, tenant relationship management, and team leadership. If any one of those is weak, the job gets hard fast. Lincoln Property Company is looking for a Property Manager in Los Angeles to run commercial assets, which may include office, retail, and industrial properties, and to do it at a level that serves both the client and the tenants well.

The Skills This Role Leans On Most

Financial fluency sits at the center of this position. You'll own the monthly reporting cycle, build annual operating and capital budgets, and track CAM and OpX recovery charges with enough precision to hold up under client scrutiny. Variance analysis and ROI recommendations are part of the regular workflow, not occasional asks. Intermediate to advanced Excel is a baseline requirement. Yardi or MRI experience will save you significant ramp time.

Tenant management is the other constant. You'll handle move-ins, move-outs, space walk-throughs, and ongoing tenant care with the goal of keeping retention high. That means being responsive, communicating clearly under pressure, and running a proactive AR process before delinquency becomes a client-level issue. Your ability to read a lease and translate its financial implications matters here because you'll also be coordinating lease administration and flagging expiration risk to ownership.

On the leadership side, you'll direct a team, manage vendor relationships and procurement, run the bid process, and hold contractors accountable to contract terms. You'll recruit, coach, and conduct performance reviews. The expectation is that you're the subject matter expert your team turns to, and the owner representative your clients rely on.

Qualifications Worth Noting

  • 3 to 5 years of commercial property management experience, ideally across office, retail, or industrial assets
  • Bachelor's degree preferred; relevant experience considered
  • California Real Estate License required
  • CPM or RPA designation, or active candidacy, preferred
  • Strong Excel skills; Yardi, MRI, and Kardin familiarity are a plus
  • Ability to be on-site at assigned properties regularly and available after hours when situations demand it

What Sets Strong Candidates Apart

Commercial PM in Los Angeles means managing properties where tenant expectations run high and lease structures can be complex. The managers who perform well here track covenant and encumbrance details proactively rather than reactively, and they build tenant relationships that reduce turnover before it shows up in the numbers. If you've delivered insightful variance reports that actually changed a client's capital decision, that experience translates directly to this role. Lincoln Property Company operates at institutional scale, so comfort working within structured processes while still driving results independently is a real differentiator.
greenhouse_5186379007.description_text: The Property Manager leads all aspects of a single asset or portfolio of commercial, industrial, and/or retail properties and coordinates all marketing, operations, and financial activities per client and/or company requirements. Essential Duties and Responsibilities: Ensure that services are provided consistent with policies, procedures, and regulations as well as contractual obligations and standards. Coordinate and lead daily and long-term activities of the team; establish work schedules, assign tasks, and cross-train staff; establish and track deadlines to meet client and company objectives; elevate team performance through subject matter expertise and suggestions to improve systems, processes, and procedures; provide formal coaching, mentoring, supervision, and guidance; recruit and hire new team members; monitor training and development of staff; develop and deliver performance reviews. Direct, review, and approve vendor invoice payments and other accounting related activities following the terms of the management agreement, LPC policies, and property management approval authorization limits. Direct and control preparation, and delivery, of timely, accurate, and insightful monthly reports as well as annual operating and capital budgets; prepare and submit tenant rent and Common Area Maintenance (CAM) or Escalation (OpX) recovery charges to client. Maintain oversight of contracted terms that impact the financial performance of the asset/company; report on expirations, covenants, restrictions, and other encumbrances that drive decision making and asset value. Coordinate all lease administration activities with lease administrator and accounting; review all lease set ups, lease changes, reporting, etc. and provide final approval.
