greenhouse_8636941002.rewritten_description:
It's move-out week at a 500-bed student property, and you're simultaneously processing a damage dispute, coordinating a vendor walk with facilities, and fielding a resident question about their final utility bill. That's a Tuesday in student housing. If that kind of overlap sounds manageable rather than overwhelming, this role is worth a close look.

The Role at Northpoint Crossing

The Scion Group is hiring an Assistant Community Manager (titled internally as Assistant General Manager) at Northpoint Crossing in College Station, Texas. This is a broad operational role that sits right alongside the General Manager and works in close coordination with the Customer and Sales Experience Manager. You're not narrowly focused on one function. Leasing performance, resident accounts, facilities coordination, team development, and the annual turn all fall within your scope.

On the administrative side, you'll manage resident accounts and utility billing, handle accounts receivable reconciliation, keep delinquency below 2% by month-end, and prepare month-end reports. You'll deliver legal notices, process evictions when required, and post damage charges from quarterly inspections. These are real financial and legal responsibilities, and they require both precision and composure.

Facilities work is part of the job too. You'll conduct monthly property walks, coordinate work orders with staff and vendors, and make sure curb appeal and common areas hold up to the Scion Standard. During annual turn, expect hands-on involvement: move-out inspections, vendor service walks, punch list assistance, and yes, physically helping move furniture and organize resident trash during high-volume turnover periods. Student housing turn is a full team effort, and this role is in the middle of it.

On the customer experience side, you'll help monitor reputation platforms like Google and Yelp, support engagement initiatives, and use KPIs to track leasing velocity, concessions, and market rates alongside the broader sales strategy. Escalated resident concerns come to you, and you're expected to close the loop quickly and identify patterns that point to systemic fixes.

You'll also share in staff development: helping recruit, onboard, and coach team members, contributing to scheduling (including on-call coverage), and stepping in as General Manager when they're out.

What Fits and What Doesn't

The systems list here is worth noting: Entrata, Turnable, ClickUp, Qualtrics, Lattice, and Greenhouse. Familiarity with Entrata in particular will reduce your ramp-up time considerably. If you've used it for lease management, billing, and resident communications, you'll feel at home faster.

What separates strong candidates in a role like this is the ability to context-switch without dropping details. Student housing at a large community runs on tight academic-year timelines, and the margin for error during turn is genuinely small. The people who thrive here tend to be organized without being rigid, direct with residents without being dismissive, and willing to do physical work during crunch periods without treating it as beneath the role.

  • At least 1 year of experience in property management or residential living communities
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Comfort with property management systems, Entrata preferred
  • Ability to maintain confidentiality across resident and employee matters
  • Eligibility to work in the United States (visa sponsorship is not available)

Benefits include health, dental, and vision insurance, 401k matching, paid parental leave, paid time off, floating holidays, a discretionary annual bonus, and learning reimbursement. This is a salaried, exempt position based on-site at Northpoint Crossing.

greenhouse_4320900009.title: Maintenance Area Lead (Fremont Region)
greenhouse_4320900009.rewritten_description:
Skills at the Center of This Role

This position runs on a specific combination of hands-on trades knowledge and operational coordination. You need to be comfortable pulling a toilet, troubleshooting an irrigation timer, and walking a unit punch list, but you also need to think like a scheduler and a trainer. The Maintenance Area Lead role at MidPen Housing covers multiple affordable housing communities across the Fremont region, so the job shifts constantly between sites, tasks, and people. Single-site maintenance techs who've never had to triage competing priorities across properties will find this adjustment real.

Multi-site work demands strong time management above almost everything else. On any given day, you might be covering a property whose maintenance tech called out sick, coordinating a vendor walkthrough at a second site, and closing out deferred work orders before an upcoming TCAC or REAC inspection. Familiarity with affordable housing regulatory inspections isn't a nice-to-have here. It's central to the job.

What You'll Be Managing Day to Day

MidPen is looking for someone who can support site teams without creating dependency. That means coaching on-site staff toward better documentation habits, better preventive maintenance follow-through, and cleaner common areas, while also jumping in physically when coverage gaps appear. This is a working lead position. You'll be doing make-readies, painting, plumbing repairs, appliance servicing, and grounds work alongside the teams you're supporting.

  • Coordinate and assist with unit inspections, safety inspections, and pre-agency inspections across the region
  • Prepare vacated units for re-occupancy: cleaning, painting, appliance servicing, and finish repairs
  • Direct contractors and service providers, and contribute input toward preventive maintenance program improvements and long-term capital planning
  • Cover maintenance operations at sites during staff absences
  • Maintain inventory control of tools, equipment, and supplies across properties
  • Ensure work orders are accurately completed, closed, and documented; assist with utility routing and shutoff documentation
  • Serve as a resource to site staff on fire and life safety items, training, and special projects

Emergency response comes with the territory. Evening and weekend calls are part of this role, and you'll need a valid California driver's license, reliable transportation, and current auto insurance to travel between properties regularly.

What Makes a Strong Candidate Here

MidPen's portfolio spans more than 130 properties across Northern California, housing working families, seniors, and residents with special needs. Affordable housing maintenance carries compliance layers that market-rate portfolios don't. Candidates who've worked in regulated affordable housing and have direct experience with REAC, TCAC, or MOR inspections will be several steps ahead. Three years of supervisory experience overseeing crews and managing turnovers at multiple sites is required, not preferred.

The stronger candidates we've seen in roles like this bring a coaching mindset. You're not just fixing things. You're also raising the baseline quality of the teams around you, which takes patience and genuine communication skills. MidPen's mission focus is real, and residents here often have fewer options and more vulnerabilities than the typical renter. That context shapes how maintenance work gets done.

Pay ranges from $34.62 to $38.94 per hour depending on experience, with benefits including health, dental, vision, a 403(b) retirement plan, paid parental leave, and an employee education reimbursement program.

Where Leasing Skill Meets Community Leadership

Most leasing roles ask you to close traffic and hand off the relationship. This one asks you to own it. Prometheus Real Estate Group, a vertically integrated owner-operator with over 13,000 apartments across the Bay Area, Portland, and Seattle, runs its communities under a resident-experience model that treats occupancy as a byproduct of genuine connection, not just conversion. The Leasing and Experience Manager role at their Carson and Raleigh communities in Portland sits at the center of that philosophy, combining sales production, team supervision, and hands-on community programming in a single position.

The title matters here. Where other operators use "Assistant Property Manager" or "Assistant Business Manager," Prometheus has built a distinct role that blends leasing performance with resident relations and team development. You'll close leases and coach others to close them. You'll manage delinquency and concessions alongside planning resident events and following up on service concerns. You'll contribute to occupancy reporting and pricing strategy while also being the person residents trust when something goes wrong. That breadth is the point.

What This Role Requires and What It Builds

To step into this position well, you need at least two years of leasing experience and a genuine comfort with sales. You should already know how to read traffic, handle objections, and move a prospect through a showing to a signed lease. Strong written and verbal communication is assumed. So is reliability on weekends, which is when Portland apartment communities see their highest foot traffic and when your presence on-site is most valuable.

What the role builds is different. Managing a leasing team, even a small one, develops supervisory instincts that carry into Community Manager and Regional roles. Setting goals, running training, and celebrating milestones are skills that compound over time. The exposure to pricing, concessions, and occupancy reporting gives you a working vocabulary in operational metrics that most leasing-only positions never offer. Candidates who move from this role into property management leadership typically point to exactly this kind of dual exposure as the reason they were ready.

A few things that separate strong candidates from average ones in a role like this: the ability to shift register quickly, from a sales conversation with a prospect to a difficult follow-up with a current resident to a coaching moment with a junior leasing ambassador, all in the same afternoon. Prometheus operates with a defined resident experience standard, and maintaining that standard under the pressure of a busy weekend requires composure, not just enthusiasm.

  • Minimum two years of leasing experience required
  • High school diploma or GED required; bachelor's degree preferred
  • Weekend availability is a consistent schedule requirement
  • Experience in customer service, sales, or marketing is valued
  • Supervisory or team lead experience is a plus, though not stated as required

Compensation runs $29.75 to $31.75 per hour, with a $200 per-lease incentive, weekend shift premium pay, and a discretionary semi-annual bonus. Benefits include fully company-paid medical, vision, and dental coverage for eligible employees and dependents, 401(k) with employer matching, tenure-based housing discounts, and tuition reimbursement, among others.

greenhouse_4318411009.title: Assistant Community Manager
greenhouse_4318411009.location: The Park at North Ridge - 7100 Claxton Cir - Raleigh, NC - 27615
greenhouse_4318411009.rewritten_description:
A resident calls at 9 a.m. with a billing question. By 10, you're posting rent payments and flagging a delinquent account for follow-up. By noon, you've toured two prospects and handed off a lease application to process. That's a normal Tuesday in this role.

The Position

Hawthorne Residential Partners is hiring an Assistant Community Manager at The Park at North Ridge, a community in North Raleigh off Claxton Circle. Hawthorne ranks among the top 50 multifamily management companies nationally, with a Southeast-focused portfolio and a reputation for promoting from within.

This role sits at the intersection of leasing, resident relations, and financial administration. You'll support the Community Manager on daily operations and step into a lead role when they're out. The work is varied: one hour you're conducting a leasing tour, the next you're reconciling a ledger or making delinquency follow-up calls.

Core responsibilities include:

  • Conducting tours, responding to leads, and guiding prospects through the full leasing process
  • Processing lease applications, renewals, and related documents accurately and on time
  • Posting rent payments, scanning checks, and monitoring delinquency with weekly follow-up
  • Reviewing resident ledgers to verify billing accuracy and payment application
  • Assisting with financial reporting for the Community Manager and regional leadership
  • Managing the community's social media presence, including resident events and engagement content
  • Maintaining the office, amenities, and common areas to a clean, presentable standard
  • Handling resident concerns professionally and following through to resolution

The office is open Monday through Friday, 9 a.m. to 6 p.m., and Saturdays, 10 a.m. to 4 p.m. One weekday off is provided weekly to maintain a 40-hour schedule. Some evening and weekend availability may be needed for resident events.

What You Bring

Hawthorne prefers candidates with at least two years of property management experience. Prior time in an assistant manager role (six months or more) is a plus. A valid driver's license is required. A CALP designation is a nice-to-have but not a dealbreaker.

The candidates who do well here aren't just strong with people. They can read a ledger, spot a billing error, and have a direct conversation with a resident about a past-due balance without it becoming a conflict. Financial literacy and interpersonal confidence carry equal weight in this role.

Compensation includes hourly pay plus monthly leasing and renewal commissions and quarterly performance bonuses. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, 401(k) with match, paid time off (including your birthday), paid parental and adoption leave, pet insurance, telehealth access, and company-paid life insurance.

Hawthorne also runs a formal Career Path Program. Assistant Community Manager to Community Manager is a common progression here, and the company's Learning and Development team actively supports that track.

greenhouse_5355642008.rewritten_description:
Bozzuto manages properties with a level of attention that shows up in the details: the follow-up call that actually happens, the tour that feels personal rather than scripted, the resident who renews because the experience was worth it. That standard starts at the leasing level, which is where this role sits.

As a Leasing Consultant at Bozzuto's Raleigh community, your core job is converting interest into signed leases. That means working every lead in the pipeline, following up with prospects before they go cold, and conducting tours that feel like a genuine introduction to a home rather than a sales pitch. Occupancy doesn't move itself. Traffic matters, but what you do with that traffic matters more. A strong leasing consultant knows the difference between a prospect who needs one more touchpoint and one who's ready to sign today.

Beyond the one-on-one interactions, you'll carry some responsibility for the community's social media presence. Instagram and Facebook aren't an afterthought here. They're part of how prospects first encounter the property, and the expectation is that you can create content that's worth stopping for. Authenticity converts better than polish in that space.

The schedule includes three weekends per month, which is standard for leasing roles and reflects a simple reality: that's when most people are actually out looking. You'll get two days off during the week in exchange. If you've worked leasing before, this isn't a surprise. If you haven't, it's worth knowing upfront.

A real estate license is required or needs to be obtained within 90 days of hire where applicable. The salary range for this role is $46,000 to $48,000 annually, with additional bonus opportunities available.

What separates a good leasing consultant from a great one at a company like Bozzuto is follow-through. Traffic-to-lease ratios are a real metric, and the consultants who move that number are the ones who treat every lead as active until it closes or goes cold, not just the ones who walked in for a tour. Raleigh's rental market has stayed competitive, which means prospects have options. The consultant who communicates clearly, responds fast, and makes the tour feel specific to what the prospect actually needs will outperform one who relies on the product alone to close.

greenhouse_6119001004.title: Affordable Housing Compliance Specialist
greenhouse_6119001004.rewritten_description:
Affordable housing compliance work sits at the intersection of regulatory precision and resident impact. Get a file wrong, and a qualified applicant gets denied or a property risks its tax credit status. This role at Asset Living, one of the larger third-party management firms in the country, keeps that from happening.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

The core of this job is file review. You'll receive Affordable Housing applications and resident files and work through them against current regulatory requirements, with a 24-hour turnaround expectation. That pace matters. LIHTC compliance doesn't wait, and neither do applicants.

Beyond the daily file queue, you'll track changes in LIHTC regulations and update internal processes when requirements shift. You'll participate in tax credit reviews conducted by outside entities and attend TDHCA trainings annually. The position also requires HCCP certification within your first two years if you don't already hold it, including a passing exam score.

One practical note: this role involves significant travel, estimated at roughly 50% of your time. That includes property visits, conferences, and training sessions. If you're used to a desk-only compliance role, the cadence here is different.

What You'll Need

  • Solid working knowledge of LIHTC regulations and file compliance requirements
  • Experience with RealPage OneSite Tax Credit software (required)
  • HCCP designation, or the commitment to earn it within two years
  • Strong organizational habits and genuine attention to detail at volume
  • Clear written and verbal communication skills
  • Familiarity with HUD programs is a plus

Where This Role Fits

Asset Living manages properties across multiple housing categories, including a sizable affordable housing portfolio. A compliance specialist here isn't supporting one property or one region. You're working across a national book of business, which means exposure to varied regulatory environments and file types that most single-site or regional compliance roles won't give you.

Specialists who build depth in LIHTC compliance often move into compliance manager or director roles, or transition into ownership and development-side positions focused on tax credit structuring. The HCCP designation this role requires is a recognized credential that travels with you regardless of where your career goes next.

greenhouse_8638247002.rewritten_description:
It's a Saturday afternoon in September, move-in weekend is barely behind you, and a prospective resident's parent is standing at the leasing desk asking about availability for next fall. That's the job in miniature: traffic doesn't pause because the turn just finished.

View on 10th is a student housing community in Waco, managed by The Scion Group, one of the larger operators in the student living sector. The role here carries the internal title of Experience Team Member, though leasing consultant is the more familiar label. It covers the full front-of-house operation: touring prospects, executing sales and engagement initiatives, supporting local marketing efforts, and keeping the office and amenity spaces running cleanly day to day. You'll also handle package logging, maintenance request coordination, and after-hours lockout coverage on a rotating basis.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Student housing runs on a leasing calendar that the conventional multifamily world doesn't quite match. Renewal season starts before most residents have finished their first semester, and the summer turn compresses what feels like a year's worth of make-ready work into a few weeks. The ETM role sits at the intersection of all of it. You're giving tours and closing leases during the academic year, running or supporting resident engagement events, and then shifting into operational support mode when turn arrives. Availability during summer and holidays is a real requirement here, not a footnote.

The social media and community marketing piece is worth noting. Scion puts genuine emphasis on local outreach and resident-facing communication, so comfort with those channels matters. If you've spent time managing an Instagram account or coordinating campus-adjacent partnerships, that background translates directly.

What Scion Is Looking For

  • A customer-first mindset that holds up under high traffic and repetitive questions
  • Strong verbal and written communication across a diverse resident and parent population
  • Flexibility to work business hours plus an after-hours on-call rotation
  • Reliability during peak periods, specifically summer and turn
  • Comfort working in an environment where priorities shift quickly

Candidates who tend to stand out in student housing leasing are the ones who can read a room quickly. A nervous incoming freshman touring with two parents requires a different approach than a returning resident who already knows the floor plan. That instinct for adjusting your pitch and tone is harder to teach than leasing software.

Benefits include health, dental, and vision coverage, 401k matching, paid time off, paid parental and maternal leave, a discretionary annual bonus, and learning reimbursement. This is a non-exempt, full-time position located on-site at View on 10th. Work authorization in the United States is required; visa sponsorship is not available.

Maintenance Supervisor at The Orchards at Cherry Creek Park

A Maintenance Supervisor at a well-run apartment community carries the full weight of physical asset performance. Turns need to hit their deadlines so leasing can move units. Service tickets need to close fast enough that residents don't start shopping. And the team needs someone who can actually develop technicians, not just direct them. At Cottonwood Residential's Orchards at Cherry Creek Park in Centennial, CO, that's the job.

What the Work Looks Like Day to Day

The make-ready process is where a lot of Maintenance Supervisors either win or lose. A slow turn cycle kills occupancy momentum and pushes concessions. You'll own that process here: coordinating punch lists, tracking unit readiness, and keeping turns moving so leasing has product to show. Beyond turns, you'll carry the standard scope of HVAC troubleshooting, electrical, plumbing, and appliance repair, and you'll be expected to resolve those issues with enough speed and quality that service ticket completion rates stay high and resident satisfaction holds.

Team development is a real part of this role, not an afterthought. You'll hire, schedule, and train techs and community care associates, including both on-the-job coaching and classroom education. Staffing the on-call rotation for 24/7 emergency coverage is your responsibility too. Grounds upkeep, safety code compliance, and keeping the property operating at peak efficiency round out the operational picture.

  • EPA Type II or Universal certification required
  • Significant HVAC troubleshooting experience expected
  • CPO certification is a plus
  • Valid driver's license required

What Sets Strong Candidates Apart

The technical skills are table stakes. What separates a good Maintenance Supervisor from a great one at a property like this is the ability to manage a turn calendar the way a leasing manager watches traffic: with urgency, precision, and awareness of how each delayed unit affects the broader occupancy picture. If you've worked at a property where the maintenance team and leasing team actually communicated well, you know how much smoother operations run. That coordination mindset matters here.

Cottonwood Residential offers competitive pay with a bonus structure, full health, vision, dental, life, and disability benefits starting within 30 days, a generous 401k and HSA company match, three weeks of paid time off in the first year, and 10.5 paid holidays.

greenhouse_8639135002.title: Maintenance Technician
greenhouse_8639135002.rewritten_description:
Waypoint Management Services operates a high-end luxury community in Vero Beach, and they're looking for a Maintenance Technician who takes genuine pride in the physical environment residents come home to every day. This isn't a role where you clock in, knock out tickets, and disappear. The expectation is that you're present, responsive, and connected to the overall experience of the community.

Day to day, you're diagnosing and resolving service requests, completing make-readies so units are truly move-in ready (not just technically checked off), and running preventive maintenance on HVAC systems and other community equipment before small issues become expensive ones. Priority work orders get a 24-hour turnaround. You'll also coordinate with contractors on make-ready conditions, handle plumbing and carpentry repairs, and keep the pool chemistry and trash compactor in proper working order. Grounds maintenance and gate and security equipment checks are part of the rotation too. On-call availability comes with the role, which is worth knowing upfront.

What makes someone genuinely strong in this position, beyond technical competence, is the ability to read a situation with residents. A frustrated resident waiting on a repair responds very differently to someone who communicates clearly and follows through than to someone who's technically capable but hard to reach. The soft skills matter here as much as the hard ones.

Vero Beach's coastal climate adds a layer of context worth noting. Salt air accelerates corrosion on HVAC components and exterior fixtures, and the heat and humidity mean HVAC preventive maintenance isn't just a best practice, it's essential. Technicians who've worked in similar coastal Florida markets tend to hit the ground running faster here.

What you'll need to bring

  • High school diploma or equivalent, with relevant maintenance experience or training
  • EPA Section 608 certification (Types I and II), required at hire
  • CPO certification is a plus
  • Working knowledge of OSHA standards and safe practices
  • Experience across plumbing, carpentry, HVAC, and general building repairs
  • Availability for on-call rotation
  • A service mindset and the kind of attitude that makes residents feel heard

Waypoint offers medical, dental, and vision coverage starting on day one, a 401(k) with matching, an onsite housing discount, and bonus opportunities. They also have referral and recognition programs, which signals that they're paying attention to how people contribute, not just whether they show up.

If you want to work for a company that's growing and values the people keeping its communities running well, this is worth a serious look.

greenhouse_5363091008.title: Maintenance Technician - Wye Junction
greenhouse_5363091008.rewritten_description:
Wye Junction is a Bozzuto-managed community in Durham, NC, and this Maintenance Technician role sits at the center of daily property operations. Technicians at this level handle the full range of residential maintenance work, from routine service tickets to after-hours emergencies, and the position rewards people who bring real trade instincts and a genuine interest in developing them further.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

On any given day, you might close out three service tickets before noon, covering a tripped breaker, a running toilet, and an HVAC filter swap, then spend the afternoon pushing a vacant unit through turn-over repairs so it's ready for move-in on schedule. Grounds upkeep, snow removal, and general building cleanliness are part of the rotation too. You'll work weekends and evenings on a rotating basis, and you'll carry on-call responsibility for after-hours emergencies. That's a real part of this job, and it's worth knowing upfront.

The core technical areas are HVAC, electrical, plumbing, and appliance repair. Bozzuto is looking for beginner to intermediate proficiency across those systems, meaning you don't need to be a master in every discipline, but you need enough foundational knowledge to diagnose and resolve common issues independently. Make-ready work, specifically preparing vacant apartments for new residents, will be a consistent part of your workload.

Skills This Role Requires vs. Skills It Builds

Coming in, you'll need:

  • Hands-on experience in building maintenance or a trades education
  • Beginner to intermediate proficiency in HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and appliance repair
  • Reliable personal transportation for daily commuting and on-call response
  • Basic comfort with software and mobile apps used for work order tracking
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, and a professional presentation
  • The physical ability to exert 25 to 50 pounds of force frequently

What the role builds is worth noting. After your 12-month anniversary, Bozzuto will cover the cost of your EPA 608 Universal Refrigerant Certification. That credential matters in residential property maintenance because it's required to legally handle refrigerants in HVAC systems. Earning it on the company's dime, while accumulating hands-on HVAC experience in the field, positions you well for a Senior Technician or Lead Maintenance role down the line.

Compensation and Support

The salary range for this position is $46,000 to $48,500 annually, with additional bonus eligibility. Bozzuto's benefits package includes medical, dental, and vision coverage, 20 days of paid time off plus holidays, a 401(k) with company match, and tuition reimbursement for team members pursuing further education or certifications.

For someone who takes the trades seriously and wants a structured environment to sharpen their skills, this role offers both the daily variety to build competence across systems and a clear path toward professional credentialing.

greenhouse_4321564009.title: Leasing & Sales Consultant
greenhouse_4321564009.rewritten_description:
Leasing consultant roles at large operators like Cortland tend to function more like structured sales positions than traditional apartment leasing gigs. That distinction matters if you're thinking about where this role can take you.

What You'll Actually Do

Your core job is filling apartments and keeping them filled. That means working a genuine sales pipeline: generating leads, following up inside a CRM, tracking conversion metrics, and closing leases against occupancy and revenue targets. Cortland measures performance against KPIs, so you'll know exactly where you stand at any given point in the month. Beyond the numbers, you're running a consultative process with each prospect, uncovering what they actually need and matching them to the right unit and lease terms. You'll also carry some community-facing responsibilities, including managing social media presence and organizing resident events that support retention and referrals. This is a full-cycle role that touches traffic generation, prospect nurturing, close, and resident experience all at once.

What You Bring

  • At least six months of sales, customer-facing, or performance-measured experience
  • Comfort being held to goals and measured against targets on a consistent basis
  • CRM fluency or a quick ability to pick it up and maintain accurate records
  • Strong follow-up discipline and time management, particularly during high-traffic periods
  • Coachability. Cortland's scale means standardized processes and active coaching. People who resist feedback don't thrive here.
  • A polished, approachable presentation that fits a Class A brand

Where This Role Leads

Leasing consultant experience at a vertically integrated operator like Cortland compounds quickly. You're learning pipeline management, objection handling, and performance accountability in an environment that tracks outcomes seriously. Those skills translate directly into a leasing manager or assistant manager role, where you're responsible for the team's conversion numbers rather than just your own. From there, the path to property manager opens up, and the CRM habits and KPI fluency you build now become foundational to running a full asset.

One honest note: this role involves weekend availability and consistent follow-up, which means some elasticity in your schedule. That's standard in leasing, and it's worth factoring in if you're coming from a Monday-through-Friday background. The upside is that strong performers in goal-driven environments tend to move up faster at operators this size than they would at smaller fee management shops where growth tracks slowly.

This position is based in Houston, TX, a market with strong multifamily demand and a competitive leasing environment where consultative selling skills genuinely separate top performers from average ones.

greenhouse_8073276.title: Housekeeper - Part Time
greenhouse_8073276.rewritten_description:
Multifamily communities run on first impressions, and the housekeeper is one of the people most responsible for making those impressions land. When a prospective resident tours the clubhouse or steps into a model unit, the condition of that space does real work. Weinstein Properties, a family-owned company with more than 70 years in the business and over 60 communities across the Southeast and Mid-Atlantic, takes that seriously at their Bexley at Left Bank community in Fort Worth.

This is a part-time, permanent role at 20 hours per week. Two schedule options give you some flexibility: Monday through Friday from 12 to 5pm, or two full days and one half day within standard business hours. Either way, it's a consistent, ongoing position with a stable employer.

What the Day Actually Looks Like

You'll move through the property with a clear sense of what needs doing. Common areas, the clubhouse, offices, and amenity spaces need daily attention. Model units and vacant ready homes get cleaned and refreshed so they're always show-ready. The coffee station gets stocked and cleaned. When a unit turns, you may be part of getting it prepped. The work is physical, it repeats, and some of it is genuinely unglamorous. That's not a surprise to people who do this well; it's just the honest shape of the role.

You'll work closely with the maintenance and leasing teams, which means communication matters. You might notice a maintenance issue while cleaning an amenity, or a leasing agent might need a model freshen before a last-minute tour. Being the kind of person who flags those things and helps without being asked is what makes someone genuinely useful on a property team.

Who Tends to Do Well Here

  • Reliable and punctual. This is a small team and your absence is felt.
  • Self-directed. You'll have a routine, but you won't always have someone checking behind you.
  • Detail-oriented in a practical sense. Noticing what's off before someone else does.
  • Physically up for the work. Prolonged standing and walking are part of every shift.
  • Comfortable with repetition. The same tasks recur because clean doesn't stay clean on its own.

Weinstein's approach has always leaned toward developing people rather than just filling slots. The $16.50 starting hourly rate, a quarterly bonus structure, and a $500 stay-on bonus after 90 days reflect that. This is the kind of employer where showing up consistently and doing good work actually gets noticed.

greenhouse_8639358002.title: Leasing Consultant
greenhouse_8639358002.location: The Republic at Lubbock, Lubbock, Texas, United States
greenhouse_8639358002.rewritten_description:
A prospective resident stops by on a Saturday afternoon, full of questions about floor plans, roommate matching, and what move-in looks like in August. You're the first impression, the tour guide, and the problem-solver, all in the same conversation.

The Republic at Lubbock serves the Texas Tech student population, which means this role runs on an academic calendar with real peaks and real pressure. Lubbock's student housing market is competitive, and Texas Tech's enrollment consistently drives strong demand for off-campus living near campus. The Experience Team Member (ETM) position at Scion sits at the center of that activity. This combines sales, marketing, community engagement, and day-to-day property administration into a single role that rarely looks the same from one week to the next.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

A significant part of this role is relationship-driven. You'll conduct community and amenity tours, handle inbound traffic from prospective residents, and follow through on customer interactions across multiple channels, including social media. Scion expects ETMs to surface real feedback on sales barriers and objections so the management team can respond with better tools and messaging. You'll also contribute ideas on local marketing that fit the Texas Tech audience.

On the administrative side, the job covers package management, office organization, maintenance request coordination, and helping keep common areas and amenities presentation-ready. After-hours lockout coverage is part of the rotation, so flexibility with your schedule matters.

Turn season is the most demanding stretch of the year in student housing. When hundreds of residents cycle out and new ones move in over a compressed window in late July and August, every team member's availability and reliability becomes critical. If you've never worked a student housing turn before, expect a steep but genuinely educational few weeks.

What Scion Is Looking For

  • A customer-first mindset that holds up under high traffic and repetitive questions
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills across a diverse resident population
  • Comfort with a schedule that includes evenings, weekends, and on-call rotation
  • Availability during summer and Turn periods, not just standard business hours
  • Self-discipline and reliability without constant supervision
  • Familiarity with social media platforms used for community engagement

Candidates who tend to stand out in ETM roles at student properties are the ones who can shift tone quickly: professional with a parent on the phone, approachable with a resident at the desk, and persuasive with a prospect on a tour. That range matters more here than a polished resume.

Scion offers health, dental, and vision coverage, 401(k) matching, paid time off, paid maternal and parental leave, a discretionary annual bonus, and learning reimbursement. Work authorization in the United States is required. Visa sponsorship is not available.

greenhouse_4320886009.title: Maintenance Technician (Brightwell West)
greenhouse_4320886009.rewritten_description:
Affordable housing maintenance work carries a weight that market-rate properties don't. The residents at Brightwell West aren't calling the front office to complain about aesthetics. They're counting on their home being functional, safe, and maintained by someone who takes that seriously. MidPen Housing has been doing this since 1970 across Northern California, and their maintenance teams are the people who make the mission tangible.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

This is a full-scope technician role, not a groundskeeper position with a wrench. You'll handle skilled repairs across electrical, plumbing, and carpentry systems, and you'll be expected to carry the technical weight when something complex comes up. Turns fall on you too: getting vacant units rent-ready within MidPen's established timeframes means painting, flooring, fixtures, and appliances, all done to a standard that holds up through inspections.

  • Electrical work covering appliances, fixtures, switches, and circuits
  • Plumbing repairs to water and sewage systems
  • Rough and finish carpentry, structural and cosmetic
  • Landscaping and irrigation system maintenance
  • Preventive maintenance scheduling and work order documentation
  • Contractor coordination: bidding, scheduling, and monitoring completion
  • Move-in, move-out, and annual inspection support for the Community Manager
  • Coaching and oversight of Maintenance Groundskeeper staff

The on-call rotation is real and worth knowing upfront. You'll cover 24/7 emergency maintenance for seven consecutive days on a rotating basis, including evenings, weekends, and holidays. That's a genuine commitment, and candidates who haven't done residential on-call before sometimes underestimate what it asks of you.

What MidPen Is Looking For

Three years of maintenance experience is the baseline, with property management experience preferred. Plumbing knowledge needs to be solid, not surface-level. Carpentry should cover both rough and finish work. You'll need a valid California driver's license, reliable transportation, and current auto insurance, since you may be moving between properties or picking up supplies. Basic OSHA familiarity and the physical ability to work in all conditions round out the requirements.

The coaching component is worth highlighting. Strong candidates here aren't just technically capable. They can explain what they're doing, show a groundskeeper the right way to handle something, and build a team that doesn't fall apart when they're off-rotation. That skill tends to travel well in this industry, and technicians who develop it often move into lead or facilities supervisor roles over time.

The Role in Context

Pay runs $25.00 to $28.13 per hour based on experience, with a benefits package that includes health, dental, vision, life and disability insurance, a 403(b) retirement plan, paid parental leave, education reimbursement, FSA options, and an EAP program, among others. MidPen has been certified as a Great Place to Work in 2025, which in our industry carries more signal than most certifications. Organizations that maintain that designation in affordable housing tend to run operationally tighter and treat maintenance staff as professionals rather than afterthoughts.

greenhouse_4323458009.title: Community Manager
greenhouse_4323458009.location: Hawthorne at Lily Flagg - 8309 Whitesburg Way SE - Huntsville, AL - 35802
greenhouse_4323458009.rewritten_description:
Community Manager roles at Southeast multifamily operators tend to blur the line between asset management and people leadership. At Hawthorne Residential Partners, that's exactly the expectation. You're running a full P&L, coaching a team, and keeping occupancy and NOI on track at Hawthorne at Lily Flagg, a Huntsville community managed by one of the top 50 largest multifamily companies in the country.

What You're Actually Responsible For

The financial side of this role is real. You'll own budget management, rent collection, delinquency tracking, and deposit accounting. You'll interpret financial reports and translate them into operational decisions. Yardi is your system of record; Knock handles lead and traffic management. Accurate records and compliance aren't optional here, they're the baseline.

On the leasing side, you're not just overseeing the team's numbers. You'll conduct tours, respond to leads, guide renewals, and manage pricing strategy to hit occupancy targets. Strong traffic-to-lease conversion and retention are both on your scorecard. You'll also manage the community's social media presence and keep the physical environment, office, amenities, and common areas, in top condition to support the leasing experience.

The operational layer includes regular property inspections, curb appeal standards, vendor oversight, and coordinating with maintenance on work orders and preventative care. When things go sideways with a resident, you handle it. Escalated concerns, online reputation management, and resident events all fall under your umbrella.

Team leadership is central. You'll hire, train, and coach both office and maintenance staff, run weekly team meetings, and build a culture of accountability without losing the human element. Hawthorne calls this their "Live It" culture. In practice, it means servant leadership is expected, not just listed as a bullet point.

Who Fits This Role

  • At least two years of property management experience, with time in both leasing and assistant manager roles
  • Six months of community manager experience in multifamily, strongly preferred
  • Working knowledge of Yardi and Knock
  • Comfort reading financial reports and making budget-aware decisions
  • Valid driver's license; CAM, CAPS, or a real estate license adds weight to your application
  • High school diploma or GED required

What separates strong candidates here is financial literacy paired with genuine team development skills. A lot of managers can hit occupancy. Fewer can read a T-12, identify where NOI is leaking, and then coach a leasing consultant through the same conversation with a prospect. If you can do both, this role fits.

Schedule, Compensation, and Growth

The leasing office runs Monday through Friday, 9 AM to 6 PM, and Saturdays 10 AM to 4 PM. You'll work 40 hours weekly with one weekday off. Resident events and community needs may occasionally require evening or weekend availability.

Compensation includes base salary plus monthly leasing and renewal commissions and quarterly performance bonuses. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401k match, paid time off (including your birthday), pet insurance, paid parental and adoption leave, telehealth access, and company-paid life insurance.

Hawthorne's Career Path Program is a real mechanism, not a talking point. Community Manager to Regional Manager is a documented trajectory here, supported by an internal learning and development team. If you're looking to grow into a portfolio-level role, the infrastructure to get there exists within this company.

greenhouse_4323116009.rewritten_description:
Leasing is one of the few property management roles where sales skill and hospitality instinct have to work together in real time. A prospect walking a tour isn't just evaluating square footage; they're deciding whether they trust the person showing it to them. The Sales and Resident Experience Consultant role at Berkshire Creekside in New Braunfels, TX is built around that dynamic.

What This Role Actually Demands

Berkshire sets a minimum 20% closing ratio as a baseline expectation, which means you're not just greeting traffic and handing out brochures. You need to qualify prospects quickly, match them to the right unit, and guide a conversation toward a decision. That's a sales skill, and it requires practice, self-awareness, and a genuine interest in people's needs rather than just a script.

Beyond closing, you'll carry responsibility for the physical presentation of the leasing office, tour routes, and model units. Think of this as your own punch list, maintained daily. First impressions are fragile, and a single detail out of place on a tour can shift a prospect's confidence. You'll also track local market conditions and bring ideas to the property manager on marketing and resident satisfaction, so there's a real contribution expected here beyond the leasing desk.

Resident communication sits inside this role too. That means written and verbal correspondence that stays professional and warm across the full resident lifecycle, from inquiry through move-in and beyond.

What You'll Build Here

Candidates coming from hospitality, retail, or other customer-facing work often find this role a natural bridge into property management. The two years of transferable customer service experience Berkshire asks for matters less as a checkbox and more as evidence that you already know how to handle a difficult conversation, a busy Saturday, and a prospect who isn't sure yet.

What the role builds on top of that foundation is market awareness. Over time, you'll develop a working understanding of how New Braunfels compares to surrounding submarkets, how concessions affect traffic, and what drives a prospect to sign or walk. That knowledge is what separates a strong leasing consultant from an average one, and it's the foundation for moving into an Assistant Manager or Leasing Manager position down the line.

  • At least two years of customer service or sales experience in any industry
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Comfort with and adaptability to new technology platforms
  • Attention to detail in administrative tasks and property presentation
  • A genuine interest in working with a wide range of people

Berkshire owns and manages its own properties, which means the team you're joining has direct skin in the asset's performance. That's a different environment than third-party management, and it tends to create more accountability and more cohesion at the site level. Benefits include three weeks of vacation, a 25% rent discount, personal development plans, and health insurance coverage.

workable_5971099.title: Full and Part time Leasing Agent Boone North Carolina Rivers Edge
workable_5971099.rewritten_description:
Student housing leasing runs on a tighter calendar than most property types. At a university market like Boone, the pre-lease window for the following academic year opens in the fall and closes fast. Hitting occupancy before competitors do matters. River's Edge, serving the Appalachian State University community, has two open positions on its leasing team: one full-time and one part-time.

What the Full-Time Role Actually Involves

At $16 to $19 per hour plus leasing commissions and renewal bonuses, the full-time position is a 40-hour-per-week role that reports to the Property Manager or Leasing Manager. The core of the job is converting traffic into signed leases. That means touring prospective residents and their parents, fielding inquiries across every channel (phone, text, email, walk-ins), processing applications and lease documents, and following up on leads consistently enough to move conversion numbers week over week.

Beyond the leasing funnel, you'll support renewal campaigns, assist with campus marketing and housing fairs, help plan resident events, and keep model units and common areas tour-ready. During turn season in July and August, the role shifts toward supporting move-in and move-out operations. Accurate data entry in platforms like Entrata or RealPage is part of the daily rhythm. Saturdays are part of the schedule, with extended hours during peak leasing season (September through March).

The full-time role includes health, dental, and vision insurance, paid time off and holidays, a 401(k) with company match, a housing discount where applicable, and a clear advancement path toward Assistant Manager or Property Manager.

What the Part-Time Role Looks Like

The part-time position runs 15 to 25 hours per week at $15 to $17 per hour, plus per-lease commissions on every signed lease you generate. Karya builds schedules around class commitments, which makes this a genuine option for current App State students. Responsibilities overlap with the full-time role on the leasing and tour side, with additional front-desk and administrative support. At least one weekend shift per week is required.

Campus involvement actually carries weight here. Someone already embedded in student organizations or Greek life comes with a referral network that converts. Social media or content creation skills are a plus for campus marketing support.

What Separates Strong Candidates

Student housing leasing has a specific dynamic: you're often selling to a parent writing the check while simultaneously convincing the student it's the right fit. The ability to read that room, address guarantor concerns about lease terms and liability, and still make the tour feel welcoming to the prospective resident separates average leasing consultants from strong ones. Prior experience in leasing, sales, hospitality, or retail helps. Familiarity with the Boone market or App State's housing cycles is a genuine advantage. Bilingual English/Spanish candidates are encouraged to apply.

  • High school diploma or equivalent required for both roles
  • Reliable weekend and occasional evening availability
  • Physical ability to walk the property and climb stairs during tours
  • Basic computer proficiency; experience with property management software preferred
  • Valid driver's license preferred for the full-time role

Both roles offer paid training. For the right candidate, the part-time position can evolve into a full-time opportunity after graduation, and the full-time role carries a direct path toward management. In student housing, leasing consultants who learn to read traffic patterns, track lead-to-lease conversion, and support a disciplined renewal campaign tend to move up quickly.

greenhouse_5315852008.title: Leasing Consultant - Lease Up
greenhouse_5315852008.rewritten_description:
Lease-up is one of the highest-pressure phases in multifamily. A new community needs to hit occupancy targets fast, often while the building is still finishing punch list work and residents are moving into units that haven't fully settled. The traffic is real, the competition is paying concessions, and every tour counts. Bozzuto is hiring a Leasing Consultant in Atlanta to carry that responsibility at a community in the 30309 corridor.

What the Role Actually Involves

Your core metric is conversion. Traffic coming through the door or filling out online forms needs to turn into signed leases, and that starts before anyone sets foot on property. You'll work every lead in the pipeline, following up with prospects and giving them enough context about the community and the neighborhood to keep momentum alive between first contact and tour. Atlanta's Midtown market is competitive, so knowing how to frame value against comparable product matters.

Tours are where the role gets personal. Bozzuto expects these to be tailored, not scripted. A prospect looking for proximity to MARTA has different priorities than someone relocating from out of state who wants walkability and green space. Reading that quickly and adjusting your pitch is what separates consultants who hit their lease-up targets from those who post a lot of traffic with thin close rates.

Social media is part of the job description, not an afterthought. You'll generate content on platforms like Instagram and Facebook to build awareness during the lease-up phase, when brand recognition for a new community is essentially zero.

The schedule runs three weekends per month, with two weekdays off. That's standard for leasing roles and reflects when most prospects are actually out shopping.

What Bozzuto Is Looking For

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Comfort with social media content creation, specifically Instagram and Facebook
  • Sales instincts and a professional presentation
  • Proficiency with software and property management apps
  • A real estate license, or the ability to obtain one within 90 days of hire where required

The base salary is $48,000, with bonus opportunities on top of that. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, 20 days of paid time off plus holidays, a 401k with company match, and tuition reimbursement.

Where This Role Can Lead

Lease-up experience is genuinely valuable on a multifamily resume. Consultants who can prove they drove a new community from 0% to stabilized occupancy have demonstrated something that steady-state leasing roles don't require. That track record opens doors to Assistant Manager positions and, for those who develop their financial fluency alongside their sales skills, to Property Manager roles where you're accountable for NOI, delinquency, and the full operating picture. Starting in lease-up compresses the learning curve significantly.
greenhouse_5315852008.description_text: At Bozzuto, every team member shares a deep commitment to doing good for those around us . We live this each day by designing, building, managing and maintaining one-of-a-kind residences. greenhouse_4323649009.title: Maintenance Technician - Cortland Ten Mile
greenhouse_4323649009.rewritten_description:
What You'll Actually Do

This role covers the full range of day-to-day maintenance at Cortland Ten Mile, a multifamily community in Meridian. Work orders come in steady: electrical issues, plumbing repairs, HVAC troubleshooting, appliance fixes, flooring, railings, and general building systems. You diagnose what's wrong, fix it correctly, and document it. That last part matters more than people expect. Recurring issues that don't get reported stay recurring issues.

Preventative maintenance is part of the job too, not an afterthought. You'll schedule and perform PM work on HVAC units and building equipment, which keeps downtime low and extends the life of assets the property depends on. You'll also keep an eye on building and security systems, flagging anything that needs attention before it becomes a liability. Hazards like broken lighting, damaged gates, or open holes get corrected fast.

On-call rotation is real. You'll respond to after-hours emergencies when it's your turn, and some of those calls will come at inconvenient times. That's part of the job at any well-run multifamily community, and Cortland structures their teams to share that load, but it's worth knowing upfront.

What You Bring

  • EPA certification (Type I, II, or Universal) required before starting
  • 1 to 3 or more years in maintenance, facilities, or multifamily housing
  • Solid hands-on skills across electrical, plumbing, HVAC, and appliance repair
  • Ability to manage multiple open work orders and prioritize without losing track of details
  • Comfort working outdoors in Idaho's weather range, climbing ladders, and lifting as needed
  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • Willingness to participate in on-call schedules and respond when emergencies come up

A Few Things Worth Knowing

Cortland is a large, vertically integrated owner-operator with in-house design, construction, and operations. For a maintenance technician, that structure means you're working within a company that takes asset preservation seriously at the ownership level, not just the management level. There's generally more consistency in how properties are maintained and resourced compared to smaller fee-management operations.

Strong candidates in this type of role tend to be self-directed once they learn a property. You're not going to have someone looking over your shoulder on every work order. The technicians who do well here know how to prioritize their own queue, communicate clearly when something's outside their scope, and treat resident interactions as part of the job rather than an interruption to it. Meridian is a growing market, and a well-maintained community with low delinquency and high occupancy starts with the people keeping the building functional.

greenhouse_7809577003.title: Assistant Manager - Cadia Crossing
greenhouse_7809577003.rewritten_description:
The morning starts with a stack of rent receipts to reconcile before the bank deadline, a maintenance call forwarded from a resident who moved out last week, and a leasing consultant flagging a prospective renter waiting in the lobby. That's a normal Tuesday at Cadia Crossing, and it's exactly the kind of morning this role is built for.

What This Role Actually Covers

As Assistant Manager at this Olympus Property community in Gilbert, AZ, you'll sit at the intersection of operations, finance, and resident relations. You'll keep financial records accurate, ensure all rent collected hits the bank before close each day, and manage move-out account statements with the kind of precision that protects the property from disputes down the line. Delinquency monitoring and rental collections fall in your lane, and you'll need to be comfortable working through those conversations with residents directly.

On the leasing side, you'll step in to show apartments when volume demands it and inspect make-ready units before move-in to make sure they meet standard. Resident retention, community events, and day-to-day service issues are also part of the job. When the Property Manager is out, you step into that seat and keep operations moving without a gap.

Staying current on the submarket matters here too. Gilbert is a growing East Valley market with active new construction, which means knowing what competitors are offering and how nearby retail and hiring trends affect traffic and occupancy is part of how you add value beyond the office.

What Strong Candidates Bring

  • Prior onsite experience as an Assistant Manager or a cross-trained Leasing Consultant
  • Familiarity with RealPage, Knock, or Onesite (strongly preferred)
  • Comfort handling financial records, deposits, and collections with accuracy and discretion
  • Availability Monday through Friday, 9 AM to 6 PM, with flexibility for resident events and the first weekend of each month
  • A systematic approach to detail without losing sight of the resident experience

Pay runs $22.00 to $24.00 per hour depending on experience, with monthly renewal incentives and quarterly bonuses on top of base. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401(k) with employer matching, tuition reimbursement, pet insurance, an apartment rental allowance, and a sabbatical program. Olympus has earned recognition as a top employer from the National Apartment Association three consecutive years running.

From a career standpoint, the Assistant Manager role is one of the most instructive positions in residential property management. You're building fluency in collections, financial reporting, leasing, and team coordination simultaneously. That combination is exactly what prepares someone to move into a Property Manager role. Candidates who treat this position as a training ground for full-site ownership tend to advance quickly, and Olympus has a stated commitment to internal career pathing.

MG Properties has been acquiring, rehabbing, and operating apartment communities across the Western U.S. for over 30 years. That track record matters when you're evaluating who you work for. Skye Apartments in Vista, CA is their current opening for a Maintenance Supervisor, and it's a real hands-on role at a community of meaningful scale.

Vista sits in North San Diego County, a market with strong rental demand and a resident base that tends to expect a well-maintained product. At the community level, that means your punch list discipline, preventive maintenance tracking, and turn quality are visible in the NOI. A sloppy make-ready process or deferred work orders show up fast in renewal rates and delinquency conversations. The Maintenance Supervisor here carries real operational weight.

Day to day, you'll diagnose maintenance issues, perform work yourself where it makes sense, and delegate to your team where it doesn't. You'll manage the service request workflow, coordinate scheduling with the property manager, run safety meetings, and keep records on preventive maintenance and expenditures. Multi-trade competency is expected. This is a working supervisor position, not a desk job with occasional walkthroughs.

What separates strong candidates in this role from adequate ones usually comes down to two things: systems discipline and crew accountability. Anyone can fix an HVAC unit or a leaking supply line. The supervisors who actually move the needle are the ones who keep the PM schedule current without being reminded, close work orders with documentation that holds up to an audit, and manage techs in a way that raises the whole team's output rather than just covering for gaps.

Minimum qualifications include:
  • At least 2 years of experience in a Maintenance Supervisor capacity
  • Prior experience at a property of 150 units or more
  • Working knowledge across all major trades
  • Valid driver's license and reliable transportation

Compensation lands at $35 to $36 per hour depending on experience, with monthly bonuses and company profit sharing on top of that. greenhouse_8640596002.title: Director of Resident Well-Being
greenhouse_8640596002.rewritten_description:
Student housing sits at an unusual intersection: it's a real estate operation, but the residents are 18-to-22-year-olds living away from home for the first time, often under academic and social pressure that property management teams aren't trained to handle. Scion built a national portfolio of off-campus student communities, and this role exists because the gap between "property concern" and "mental health concern" is narrower than most operators acknowledge. The Director of Resident Well-Being is the person who closes that gap at scale.

What This Role Actually Does

This is a strategy and infrastructure role, not a clinical one. The posting is explicit about that boundary, and it matters. You won't be counseling residents, diagnosing anything, or stepping in as a crisis responder. What you will do is build the systems, training, and partnerships that make sure a General Manager at a Scion property in any market knows what to do at 11pm when a resident's roommate calls the front desk worried. That's the real deliverable: confident, protocol-equipped teams who can recognize a concern, document it correctly, and connect a resident to the right resource without overstepping.

The external partnership work is substantial. You'll maintain relationships with university counseling centers, Dean of Students offices, Behavioral Intervention Teams, campus police, disability services, and community crisis-response agencies. Each university market has its own referral pathways and escalation contacts, and keeping those maps current and usable for field teams is ongoing work. On the internal side, you'll partner with Learning and Development to build role-specific training for GMs, regional leaders, and security personnel, and you'll sit alongside Legal, Risk Management, Operations, and HR when a significant incident requires coordinated response.

The resident-facing programming side covers a real range: transition to college, belonging, academic pressure, financial wellbeing, roommate conflict, substance misuse awareness, and crisis-resource literacy. You'll also develop peer-connection strategies, including resident ambassador and wellness champion programs, with careful attention to keeping peer leaders in a connection role rather than a counseling one.

Who Fits This Role

  • At least 10 years of progressive leadership in student affairs, student success, wellness administration, public health, higher education, or behavioral health administration
  • A bachelor's degree in a relevant discipline (psychology, higher education administration, social work, public health, organizational development); an advanced degree is preferred
  • Demonstrated experience building enterprise-wide programs and training frameworks, not just individual initiatives
  • Real familiarity with college-age populations, student development theory, FERPA and privacy considerations, and the professional boundaries around non-clinical wellness roles
  • Background in student housing, residential life, or counseling-services administration is a meaningful advantage
  • Licensed clinical credentials aren't required and won't substitute for the leadership and program-building experience this role demands

The candidates who will stand out aren't necessarily the ones with the most clinical depth. They're the ones who've built programs that actually got adopted at scale, who know how to train non-clinical staff to respond appropriately without overreaching, and who've managed the politics of university partnerships where Scion is a private operator sitting adjacent to a campus bureaucracy. That relationship management skill is harder to teach than wellness content knowledge.

This role is based in Chicago and covers Scion's national portfolio. The work will involve real-time guidance during incidents, which means occasional after-hours coordination when something significant happens at a property. That's worth knowing going in.

greenhouse_4322789009.location: Hawthorne at the Station - 531 Old Maccumber Station Rd - Wilmington, NC - 28405
greenhouse_4322789009.rewritten_description:
HVAC certification gets you in the door. What keeps a technician valuable at this level is the full package: a working knowledge of plumbing, electrical, appliance repair, and the judgment to sequence a make-ready efficiently when three units are turning at the same time. That's the skillset this role draws on daily.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Hawthorne at the Station is a garden-style community in Wilmington, NC, and this Maintenance Technician II position covers the range you'd expect: completing service requests independently, contributing to preventative maintenance schedules, and getting vacant units to make-ready status on time. Pool maintenance and common area upkeep are part of the rotation too, not afterthoughts. You'll also carry a share of the on-call rotation for after-hours emergencies. That's standard in this industry, and worth knowing going in.

Day-to-day, you're moving between work orders, coordinating with the rest of the maintenance team, and keeping the shop organized well enough that supply inventory is readable at a glance. The residents notice the work when it's done poorly. They rarely notice when it's done well. That's just the job.

Qualifications Worth Having

  • Two years of apartment maintenance experience (preferred, not negotiable in practice)
  • EPA/HVAC certification (required)
  • Valid driver's license
  • CPO certification (a genuine plus at a property with a pool)
  • High school diploma or GED

The technicians who move up quickly in this type of role are the ones who can diagnose before they repair. Anyone can swap a part. Fewer people can walk into a unit, ask the right questions, and identify root cause before ordering anything. That diagnostic habit is what separates a solid tech from a great one.

At Hawthorne Specifically

Hawthorne Residential Partners operates with a defined career path structure, and the Technician II classification sits in the middle of it intentionally. The Learning and Development program is built to move people toward Technician III, and they back that with education reimbursement for maintenance-related coursework. The bonus structure here is more layered than most: monthly renewal bonuses, quarterly performance bonuses, and quarterly resident satisfaction bonuses on top of hourly pay. The benefits package includes free dental, medical and vision options, 401k match, and paid parental leave.

Wilmington's rental market has stayed active, and properties along the Station corridor have seen steady occupancy. Hawthorne's portfolio leans into community culture, so resident satisfaction scores carry real weight internally. greenhouse_5362730008.title: Apartment Maintenance Manager
greenhouse_5362730008.rewritten_description:
Maintenance leadership at an affordable housing company carries a different weight than at a typical market-rate property. The residents depend on the physical environment in ways that go beyond preference. When something breaks, it matters. That's the context for this Service Manager role with Fairstead in Jonesboro, Georgia.

What This Role Actually Involves

Fairstead operates an integrated platform that brings development, construction, and property management together under one roof. With more than 30,000 units across 28 states, they run at real scale, and they expect their site-level maintenance leadership to match that. As Service Manager, you'll oversee the day-to-day repair and maintenance of buildings on your property, supervise other maintenance team members, and take point on special projects as they arise. Keeping mechanical systems and electrical equipment running, managing inspections, and holding the property to Fairstead's cleanliness and safety standards are core to the position.

This role isn't purely hands-off supervision. You'll work independently on routine tasks and step in on more complex projects with support when needed. Overtime comes with the territory during emergencies or larger initiatives, and that's worth knowing upfront. The ability to implement and improve procedures matters here, not just follow them.

Who Fits This Role Well

  • At least three years of property maintenance experience, with genuine depth in at least one skilled trade
  • Solid working knowledge of building systems, mechanical trades, and the tools and terminology that go with them
  • Strong safety awareness and the habit of leading others toward it, not just practicing it yourself
  • Organizational skills that hold up when multiple tasks and people need direction at the same time
  • Comfort with Microsoft Office Suite; experience with Yardi or RealPage is a plus

The strongest candidates tend to be people who've already supervised others in a maintenance context and understand that leading a team means setting the standard, not just assigning tasks. If you've worked in affordable housing before, you'll likely appreciate how that experience shapes the way you approach resident interactions and communicate urgency up the chain.

The Broader Picture

Fairstead describes itself as tech-forward and data-driven for an affordable housing operator, which means you'll likely encounter software tools and digital workflows more than you might at a smaller management company. That's worth factoring in if you're used to a more paper-based environment. It also creates a clearer path for maintenance leaders who want to grow: operators like Fairstead tend to promote from within when regional or facilities-level roles open up, and a Service Manager who's demonstrated operational discipline and team development is well-positioned for that next step.

The benefits package includes medical coverage through Meritain Health with a generous employer contribution, employer-paid vision and life insurance, a 401(k) with company match, 15 days of PTO, 7 sick days, and 12 or more paid holidays, among other perks.

workable_5973969.title: Property Manager
workable_5973969.rewritten_description:
Property management at the community level is where all the disciplines converge: leasing, financials, maintenance coordination, staff development, and resident relations all land on one desk. CommonPlace is hiring a Property Manager for their Raleigh-area community, and this role carries the full weight of that responsibility. You're running the site, leading the team, and owning the resident experience from first tour through renewal.

What This Role Covers

Day-to-day, you're overseeing leasing activity and guiding prospective residents through the full cycle: tours, applications, screenings, deposits, lease execution, and move-in. You're also managing the financial side, building and tracking budgets, monitoring variances, handling accounts payable and receivable, and completing month-end and year-end reporting. That financial fluency matters here. CommonPlace expects accurate, timely reporting, not just operational instincts.

On the maintenance side, you'll conduct regular property inspections and coordinate with your team to keep units move-in-ready and common areas clean and safe. Retention programs, resident concerns, vendor relationships, and marketing campaigns all fall within your scope as well. You're also the hiring manager, trainer, scheduler, and performance evaluator for your on-site staff, which means your leadership style directly shapes how the team operates.

  • 3 to 5 years of property management experience in a leadership capacity
  • Fair Housing knowledge with certification required
  • Demonstrated experience managing budgets and producing financial reports
  • Strong communication and conflict resolution skills across residents, staff, and vendors
  • OneSite and AppFolio experience preferred
  • Valid driver's license and current auto insurance
  • On-site presence five days per week

Where This Role Builds Skills

The craft of property management compounds in a full-cycle role like this one. You already need to arrive with budget fluency, leasing fundamentals, and the confidence to lead a team through conflict and change. What you'll develop further is the judgment that comes from owning outcomes completely. When occupancy dips, you're diagnosing the cause and adjusting marketing strategy. When delinquency creeps up, you're making the call on how to address it. When a make-ready falls behind, you're working the punch list alongside your maintenance team. That kind of decision-making, practiced consistently, is what prepares a property manager to step into a regional or multi-site role.

CommonPlace grounds its work in a community-first philosophy, which shows up in how they expect their managers to handle resident relationships: with professionalism, approachability, and genuine follow-through. The company offers a base salary of $65,000 with performance-based incentives, along with medical, dental, vision, life insurance, disability coverage, 401k, and paid vacation, sick, and volunteer time.
