greenhouse_4335856009.title: Maintenance & Construction Apprentice ($1,000 hiring bonus)
greenhouse_4335856009.rewritten_description:
What You'll Actually Do

This is a structured apprenticeship inside a property management company that owns and operates luxury apartment communities across the Carmel, IN area. You'll work alongside experienced tradespeople on renovation and maintenance projects, moving between properties as the work demands. Travel is a constant here, up to 40% of the time, so your "office" changes depending on what's on the schedule.

Day to day, the work spans the full cycle of a unit turn. That means demo and material removal, drywall patching, interior painting, installing LVP flooring and light fixtures, setting cabinets, and closing out the punch list details that separate a finished luxury unit from one that just looks finished. You'll also rotate through exterior work: power washing, seasonal repairs, landscaping, and building upkeep. Physical demands are real. You'll lift 75-plus pounds, work from ladders, and stay outdoors through whatever the Indiana weather brings.

BAM provides the tools and the training. The $1,000 hiring bonus and the $19 to $21 hourly starting pay reflect that this is a compensated apprenticeship, not an unpaid credential program. You build trade skills while earning, without the debt load that formal trade school typically carries.

What You Bring

  • A valid driver's license and reliable transportation for local property travel
  • Comfort working at heights and on ladders (safety training is provided, but comfort with heights is required on day one)
  • Basic hand tool familiarity: tape measure, hammer, screwdriver
  • Zero to two years of experience in construction, landscaping, or general labor (preferred, not required)
  • High school diploma or GED (preferred)
  • Your own tools are a plus, but the company will supply what you need

The right attitude carries more weight here than a resume. Reliability, attention to detail on finish work, and the ability to take direction from experienced tradespeople will determine how quickly you advance.

Skills This Role Builds and Where They Lead

Most people who start as maintenance apprentices in multifamily either move into a lead maintenance technician role or specialize in a specific trade area like HVAC, plumbing, or electrical. The punch list and make-ready experience you accumulate here is directly transferable to any Class A or B property, and companies pay well for technicians who can manage a full unit turn with minimal supervision. The renovation side of this role adds capex project exposure that most standard maintenance positions don't offer early on, which makes your skill set broader and more marketable faster.

The compensation package includes a significant rent discount at one of BAM's luxury communities plus free utilities, 15.5 paid holidays from the start, 88 hours of PTO at 90 days, and 120 additional PTO hours at the one-year mark. Low-cost medical, dental, vision, disability, and pet insurance round out the benefits.

We provide the training, the tools, the team, and even a steep discount on a luxury apartment with free utilities. You bring the hustle and willingness to learn. The Reality Check This is not a desk job. It is hands-on and fast-paced work. You will lift 75+ lbs, climb ladders, and work outdoors in all weather conditions. greenhouse_4332639009.title: Cleaner - Full-Time
greenhouse_4332639009.rewritten_description:
Student housing communities run on turn cycles, occupancy pressure, and the kind of daily visible cleanliness that directly affects leasing traffic and resident retention. The person keeping hallways, common areas, and grounds in shape isn't background staff. They're the first thing a prospective resident notices on a tour.

Redstone Residential operates over 38,000 beds across 20 states, making them one of the larger third-party student housing operators in the country. This full-time Cleaner role is based at their Eugene, Oregon community and pays $23.00 per hour.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

The core of this job is keeping a student housing community clean and presentable, indoors and out. That means regular cleaning of hallways, common areas, the clubhouse, office, model unit, and parking garages. It means grounds work: picking up trash and debris, clearing animal waste, watering landscaping, and maintaining curb appeal day to day. In winter, keeping walkways clear of snow and ice is part of the job.

One piece that's specific to student housing: you'll conduct scheduled cleaning checks inside residents' apartments to confirm units are being maintained to the property's standards. That's a regular duty here, and it requires someone who can handle that interaction with residents professionally and without making it adversarial. Student housing populations cycle quickly and aren't always tidy. That's just the reality of the asset class.

You'll also assist with basic repairs and general maintenance tasks as needed. This isn't a deep technical role, but being willing to help where the team needs it matters.

Who Fits This Role

  • Prior janitorial or cleaning experience, ideally in a residential or commercial property setting
  • Comfortable working independently and managing a daily task list without close supervision
  • Physically able to lift 50+ pounds and stand for four to six hour shifts
  • A genuinely friendly, approachable demeanor, especially when conducting apartment checks

The candidate who does well here tends to take ownership of their section of the property rather than waiting to be directed. In student housing, conditions can change fast between Monday morning and Friday afternoon. Staying ahead of that requires a certain kind of self-motivation.

Benefits include health, vision, and dental insurance, 15 days of PTO, 10 paid holidays, paid parental leave, three paid service days, a 401(k) with up to 6% match, short-term disability, and a continued education program.

greenhouse_5372507008.title: Apartment Maintenance Technician
greenhouse_5372507008.rewritten_description:
It's 9 PM on a Tuesday and a resident's heat is out. That call comes to you. That's the job, honestly, and knowing that upfront is more useful than a list of perks.

Fairstead is a vertically integrated affordable housing owner and operator with more than 30,000 units across 28 states. They develop, build, and manage their own properties, which means maintenance staff work within a single unified system rather than bouncing between ownership and a third-party management company. This Euclid, Ohio position carries a $2,000 signing bonus and sits at the core of keeping a residential property functional and safe for the people who live there.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Day to day, you're handling make-ready turns on vacated units, running preventative maintenance rounds, checking safety systems monthly, and working through resident work orders as they come in. Electrical diagnostics, HVAC checks, appliance repairs, and general building upkeep are all part of the rotation. You'll maintain a working inventory of supplies and tools, and you'll help enforce maintenance standards that protect the property's physical assets from misuse or premature wear. On-call rotation is part of the position, which means after-hours emergency calls are real and expected. The paperwork and communication side matters too. You'll need to document work clearly and coordinate effectively with property staff.

Fairstead operates with a tech-forward approach for an affordable housing company, including data-driven systems and digital tools. That doesn't eliminate the physical demands of the role, but it does mean you'll likely use software to log and track work orders rather than relying on paper-based processes.

What You Bring

  • Prior experience as a maintenance or service technician in a residential or commercial setting
  • Working knowledge of electrical systems sufficient to diagnose issues and complete minor repairs
  • General mechanical aptitude across plumbing, HVAC, appliances, and building systems
  • HVAC certification, CMRP, or equivalent credential (preferred, not required)
  • Ability to lift up to 70 pounds unassisted and stand for extended periods
  • Clear written and verbal communication skills
  • Attention to detail, especially on punch list items and unit inspections

The candidates who do well in roles like this one tend to be self-starters who can triage a work order list without constant direction. In affordable housing specifically, the resident population often depends on quick, reliable service in ways that are more immediate than in market-rate communities. That's not pressure meant to discourage anyone. It's just context for why responsiveness and follow-through matter here more than in some other settings.

Fairstead offers medical coverage through Meritain Health with a generous employer contribution, employer-paid vision and life insurance, a 401(k) with company match, 15 days of PTO, 7 sick days, 12 or more paid holidays, and a flexible spending account among other benefits.

greenhouse_5372196008.title: Activities Director - Orchard Mesa
greenhouse_5372196008.rewritten_description:
Multifamily operators increasingly recognize that amenities alone don't retain residents. Programming does. The Activities Director role exists because a well-run events calendar directly supports occupancy: residents who feel connected to their community renew leases, refer friends, and generate the kind of organic reputation that no ad spend can replicate. CloudTen Residential, a Nevada-based company with a portfolio spanning hotel-to-residential conversions, high-rise lease-ups, and value-add repositioning across the West, is hiring for this position at Orchard Mesa in Mesa, AZ.

What This Role Actually Involves

Working under the Community Manager, you'll own the full activities program: building a monthly calendar, writing and distributing a resident newsletter, coordinating vendors and entertainers, managing the activities budget, and supervising an Activities Assistant through event setup, execution, and breakdown. You'll design promotional materials and push programming through social media and digital communication channels. Beyond the creative side, there's real operational accountability here. You'll track income, control expenses, and handle petty cash in line with company accounting policies. Safety compliance and Fair Housing adherence are non-negotiable parts of the job, not afterthoughts.

You'll also work alongside the leasing and maintenance teams on community-wide initiatives, which means your events calendar has to fit into the broader operational rhythm of the property. When a lease-up push is underway or a capital project is disrupting amenity spaces, you adapt. That cross-functional coordination is where a lot of activities directors either grow or stall.

Pay runs $26.00 to $29.00 per hour depending on experience. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, an FSA, company-paid life insurance, and paid vacation, sick leave, and holidays.

What Strong Candidates Bring

  • A high school diploma at minimum; an associate or bachelor's degree in recreation, hospitality, or communications is preferred
  • At least two years of event or activities planning, ideally in residential or healthcare settings
  • Comfort with Microsoft Office, property management software, and basic reporting tools
  • The ability to engage genuinely with a diverse resident population and build inclusive programming
  • Strong organizational instincts and the discipline to manage multiple projects without losing detail on any single one

The candidates who tend to stand out in this role are the ones who treat resident feedback as data. Gathering post-event input, tracking participation trends, and adjusting the calendar based on what actually draws people out (versus what looks good on paper) separates a strong activities director from someone who just executes a template. If you've worked in senior living or student housing, those instincts transfer directly here.

From a career trajectory standpoint, this role builds a skill set that compounds well. Resident retention strategy, budget management, vendor relationships, cross-team collaboration, and digital communication are all transferable to community management, regional support roles, or even marketing-focused positions within a multifamily platform. CloudTen's expanding portfolio means internal movement is a realistic path for people who perform.

greenhouse_5372204008.title: Maintenance Supervisor - Multi-site - Elan Luxo II, Elan Beach Lofts, Elan Bay Lofts, Elan Pacific Lofts, Elan Coronado Bella Mer
greenhouse_5372204008.location: Elan - Baylofts ; Elan - Beachlofts ; Elan - Bella Mer Coronado ; Elan - Luxo II ; Elan - Pacific Lofts
greenhouse_5372204008.rewritten_description:
Sunrise Management runs five Elan-branded communities across San Diego, and this role sits at the center of all of them. Elan Luxo II, Beach Lofts, Bay Lofts, Pacific Lofts, and Coronado Bella Mer each have their own rhythm, their own residents, and their own maintenance needs. Your job is to hold it all together.

This is a multi-site supervisor position, which means your mornings aren't predictable. One day you're coordinating turns at Bay Lofts, the next you're troubleshooting an HVAC issue at Bella Mer while your tech handles service requests across town. A valid driver's license is required, and you'll genuinely use it. The role pays $27 to $33 per hour depending on experience.

The core of the work is what you'd expect from any maintenance supervisor: make-ready units within three to five days of move-out, preventive maintenance logs, pool and spa upkeep, appliance and HVAC repairs, curb appeal, common area cleanliness, and 24-hour service request completion. You'll also handle on-call emergency coverage when it comes up, which it will. That's the honest reality of this kind of role.

What's different here is the supervisory load across multiple sites. You're not just a skilled tech who happens to carry a radio. You're the person who sets work schedules, runs monthly safety meetings, keeps MSDS records current, trains your team on PPE protocols, and stays in close communication with multiple property managers. You'll also weigh in on hiring and performance reviews for the maintenance staff under you, and you'll surface capital improvement recommendations when you see them.

Sunrise describes their culture around resident hospitality, and that filters into maintenance too. Service requests handled within 24 hours, residents kept in the loop when parts need to be ordered, consistent community inspections. The expectation is that residents feel the attention, not just the repair.

Multi-site supervisors who do this well tend to develop a strong operational picture that translates directly into Maintenance Director roles or regional facilities positions. The exposure to multiple property types, management relationships, and vendor negotiations at this scale is hard to replicate in a single-site role.

What you'll bring

  • At least one year of hands-on property maintenance experience
  • Prior supervisory experience (required)
  • Working knowledge of HVAC, plumbing, electrical, appliances, and pool systems
  • Familiarity with Fair Housing laws and safety compliance requirements
  • Strong communication habits with both residents and management
  • Valid driver's license in good standing
  • Organized enough to track inventory, time sheets, and maintenance logs across sites

If you're the kind of person who notices the burned-out light before anyone reports it and already has a replacement in the truck, you'll fit the pace here.

greenhouse_4700174006.rewritten_description:
What You'll Actually Do

This is a field-based maintenance role covering scattered-site properties across the Lehigh Valley. You'll drive between single-family homes, commercial assets, and vacation properties owned or managed by Dream Live Prosper Communities, handling work orders across the full range of trades: plumbing, electrical, HVAC, appliance repair, painting, and general upkeep.

The standard is clear: resolve assigned service requests within 48 hours with no callbacks. You'll manage your own work order queue in property management software, keep the queue moving, and execute make-readies on vacated homes so they're rent-ready on schedule. Grounds and common area upkeep are part of the job too, not an afterthought.

On-call rotation is real here. You'll respond to after-hours emergencies as part of the team's shared rotation. If that kind of flexibility doesn't fit your life right now, this role isn't the right fit.

You'll need a reliable vehicle with room for tools and supplies. The company provides the properties; you bring the transportation and your own basic hand tools.

What You Bring

  • Hands-on experience across basic plumbing, electrical, HVAC, painting, and general repairs
  • Ability to troubleshoot and close out repairs independently, without waiting to be directed
  • Comfort with mobile work order systems and property management software
  • Physical ability to lift up to 50 lbs and work outdoors in all weather
  • Valid driver's license, clean driving record, and a vehicle capable of hauling tools and equipment
  • CPO certification is a plus, not a requirement
  • Availability for on-call rotation, including weekends

Context Worth Knowing

Scattered-site maintenance work runs differently than a traditional apartment community. There's no leasing office to anchor your day. You're planning your own route, managing your own time, and keeping several property types in good shape simultaneously. Strong candidates in this kind of role tend to be the ones who treat their work order queue like a personal commitment, not a list someone else is tracking. The 48-hour, no-callback standard exists because resident satisfaction on scattered sites depends almost entirely on the technician, since there's no front desk or community team to absorb the friction when something goes wrong.

Pay starts at $20 to $25 per hour depending on experience and certifications. Benefits include health, dental, vision, and life insurance, 401(k) matching, and PTO.

workable_5993773.title: Leasing Manager
workable_5993773.rewritten_description:
Student housing leasing management operates on a different calendar than conventional multifamily. You're selling beds a year out, managing a lease-up cycle tied to academic schedules, and working with a resident demographic that expects a social experience alongside a place to sleep. PeakMade Real Estate specializes in exactly this space, managing off-campus student communities across the country from their Atlanta headquarters. This Leasing Manager role sits onsite in Ithaca, New York, which puts you in a college market with real seasonal intensity.

What the Role Actually Covers

This is a dual-track position: half leasing leadership, half marketing execution. You'll hire, train, and manage a leasing staff while also owning the property's social media presence, digital content, and community programming. That combination is specific to student housing. Conventional multifamily rarely asks a leasing manager to shoot and edit content in Canva, manage online reputation across platforms like Reputation.com and JTurner, and still hit closing ratios. Here, that's the full job description.

On the leasing side, you'll conduct tours, sign leases (beds and apartments), support move-in and move-out events, and keep prospect traffic data current. Renewal programming falls under your scope as well, including lease renewal events and resident retention campaigns. On the marketing side, you'll develop and execute the annual marketing plan within budget, using social platforms, creative tools, and campus-specific outreach to drive traffic and conversions.

What PeakMade Is Looking For

  • 2 or more years of leasing experience specifically in off-campus student housing
  • Prior leadership experience, formal or informal
  • Hands-on comfort with Instagram, Facebook, Canva, Lightroom, VSCO, and property management software
  • Strong communication skills across in-person, phone, and online leasing channels
  • Flexibility for some evenings and weekends, especially during peak leasing season
  • High school diploma or equivalent required

The pay range runs $52,000 to $57,000 annually, with monthly, quarterly, and annual commission layered on top. PeakMade also offers a housing discount, 401(k) match, 15 days of PTO plus two additional wellbeing days, up to 12 weeks of paid parental leave, and a mentorship program.

A Note on What Separates Strong Candidates

In student housing, the leasing cycle is unforgiving. Pre-leasing for the following academic year typically starts in the fall, which means you're selling apartments to people who won't move in for another nine to twelve months. Candidates who've managed that timeline, kept traffic moving in the off-peak months, and still hit occupancy targets before the summer rush tend to do well in roles like this. If your background is conventional multifamily without student housing exposure, the calendar alone will be an adjustment. Two-plus years in the student space is a real requirement here, not a preference dressed up as one.

workable_5993943.title: Regional Property Manager Manufactured Housing Communities
workable_5993943.rewritten_description:
Manufactured housing communities operate differently from conventional apartments, and not every regional manager makes that transition cleanly. The resident base tends to be longer-term, the maintenance issues are more varied (you're dealing with homes, not just units), and the communities often span multiple small markets rather than clustering in one metro. Investment Property Group owns and operates a portfolio that spans manufactured home, multifamily, and RV communities across the country. This Oregon regional role sits squarely in the manufactured housing side of that portfolio.

The Portfolio and the Work

This position covers communities spread across the Willamette Valley and surrounding areas: Springfield, Eugene, Albany, Aumsville, Monmouth, Salem. The geography matters. You're not commuting between properties that are twenty minutes apart. Expect to be on the road three or more days per week, and plan your week accordingly. A company car is provided, which helps, but this is genuinely a travel-heavy role. If you prefer to manage from a desk, this isn't the right fit.

The portfolio sits at 1,000-plus units across multiple sites. Your direct reports are property managers and on-site teams at each location. Your job is to keep them focused, equipped, and accountable. That means regular site visits, budget reviews, hiring decisions, and stepping in when a community has a performance problem that the on-site team can't resolve independently. You'll report out to senior leadership with analysis and action plans, not just status updates.

On the financial side, you'll own the monthly review process: pulling apart the numbers, flagging anomalies, and building corrective plans when a property is drifting off target. You'll also manage budgets and work with the compliance and maintenance teams to keep operations consistent across the region.

What This Role Actually Requires

  • At least three years of senior-level multi-site management experience, area manager or regional level
  • Multi-site portfolio experience at 1,000 or more units
  • Comfort with Yardi, Rent Cafe, Blue Moon, and related platforms
  • Strong grasp of local housing market conditions across the Oregon markets listed
  • Valid driver's license and willingness to travel 30 to 70 percent of the time within the state
  • Must be Oregon-based or willing to relocate

The compensation is $120,000 to $130,000 base, with a 20 percent annual discretionary bonus and a company vehicle. Benefits include medical, dental, vision, life insurance, HSA, employee assistance program, and a 401k with company match.

One honest note: manufactured housing communities carry a specific resident relations dynamic. Residents are often long-term, sometimes multi-generational, and disputes over community rules or maintenance responsibilities can run deep. The candidates who do well in this kind of regional role aren't just financially sharp. They know how to de-escalate, they take community standards seriously, and they treat residents with consistency regardless of the situation. That combination, financial fluency plus people judgment, is what separates a strong regional manager from one who burns out or loses the trust of their on-site teams.

smartrecruiters_744000140282139.rewritten_description:
What You'll Actually Do

Mountain Gate and Trails is an AIR Communities property in Las Vegas, and this role puts you in charge of keeping it running. You'll lead a maintenance team, own the full scope of service operations, and report capital and maintenance needs up the chain. That means vendor management, preventive maintenance scheduling, apartment turns, and resident service requests all land on your desk. AIR runs a tech-forward maintenance operation, so you'll work with digital tools that are meant to increase the volume of work your team can handle each day without sacrificing quality.

Budget accountability is real here. You're expected to manage spend efficiently while holding quality steady, which is the perpetual tension of this job. You'll also carry compliance responsibility across AIR's operating procedures and Environmental Health and Safety requirements. Las Vegas is a market that doesn't slow down seasonally the way other regions do, so on-call rotations and flexible scheduling are part of the deal year-round.

Compensation runs $75,000 to $77,000 base, with a 15% target bonus opportunity plus quarterly customer satisfaction bonuses of up to $250 per month for managers who consistently deliver strong resident experiences. An on-site apartment discount is also available.

What You Bring

  • At least three years of hands-on technical maintenance and facilities experience in property management
  • One to three years leading a team in a customer service and asset maintenance environment
  • Mechanical aptitude and comfort with physical work, including moving heavy equipment
  • Ability to work evenings, weekends, and on-call shifts as needed
  • Organized, solution-focused, and detail-oriented without needing to be told twice
  • Reliable transportation

A Word on What Separates Strong Candidates

We've seen maintenance managers who are excellent technicians but struggle to develop their team, and others who are great with people but let the preventive maintenance schedule slip until small problems become capex surprises. The candidates who do well in roles like this one hold both. They run tight punch lists, stay ahead of turns, and still make time to train the person behind them. AIR invests in certifications and tuition reimbursement up to 100% for job-related credentials, which tells you something about how they view developing talent from within. greenhouse_7819672003.title: Assistant Manager - Avenue 25
greenhouse_7819672003.rewritten_description:
It's 8:55 AM and there's a bank deposit to finalize, two make-ready inspections before noon, and a resident in the leasing office waiting to talk about a charge on their account. That's a typical Tuesday at Avenue 25, and it's exactly the kind of controlled chaos this role is built for.

What the Role Actually Involves

Olympus Property is hiring an Assistant Manager for Avenue 25 in Phoenix, a full-time onsite position that sits at the intersection of financial accountability and resident relations. You'll handle daily rent collection and ensure all deposits hit before bank close, maintain accurate resident and financial records, and step into the Business Manager seat when they're out. Delinquency doesn't wait, and neither does this role.

You'll also carry leasing responsibilities when the team needs coverage. That means showing units, supporting retention efforts, and participating in community events, some of which fall after standard hours or on the first weekend of the month. Inspecting make-ready apartments before move-in is part of your regular cadence, and you'll process final account statements when residents move out, including assessing unit conditions and coordinating disposition paperwork.

Staying current on the Phoenix submarket matters here. New construction, nearby retail shifts, and hiring trends in the area all feed into occupancy decisions, and Olympus expects their onsite teams to bring that awareness into daily operations.

What Olympus is Looking For

  • Prior onsite experience as an Assistant Manager or a cross-trained Leasing Consultant at an apartment community
  • Familiarity with RealPage, Knock, or Onesite (strongly preferred)
  • Availability Monday through Friday, 9 AM to 6 PM, with flexibility for after-hours events and first-weekend coverage
  • Comfort handling both financial recordkeeping and face-to-face resident interactions on the same shift
  • Detail orientation around deposits, compliance, and file integrity

Pay runs $22 to $24 per hour depending on experience, with monthly renewal incentives and quarterly bonuses on top of base. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401(k) with employer matching, educational assistance, an apartment rental allowance, and a sabbatical program. Olympus has earned a spot on the National Apartment Association's Top Employer list three consecutive years, 2023 through 2025.

One thing that separates strong Assistant Manager candidates from average ones in a Phoenix lease-up or stabilized asset: the ability to protect NOI from two directions at once. That means keeping collections tight while also keeping renewal traffic warm. Operators who treat those as separate jobs tend to let one slip. The best Assistant Managers run them in parallel, and Olympus structures its bonus incentives to reinforce exactly that habit.

greenhouse_8088484.title: Assistant Property Manager
greenhouse_8088484.rewritten_description:
Weinstein Properties has operated apartment communities for over 70 years under continuous family ownership, and that longevity shows in how they run properties: closely, consistently, and with direct involvement from corporate. This Assistant Property Manager role at Bexley Chamblee sits inside that structure, which means you'll have real operational support rather than being left to figure things out on your own.

Chamblee's multifamily market has tightened considerably as the city has absorbed spillover demand from Buckhead and Midtown, and Class A communities there compete on service quality as much as amenities. The expectation at this property reflects that reality: residents notice when operations slip, and Weinstein's hands-on model is built to prevent that.

What the Role Actually Involves

Day-to-day, you're functioning as the operational anchor of the community. That means handling escalated resident concerns before they become bigger problems, keeping leasing activity moving, monitoring key performance metrics, and partnering with the Maintenance Supervisor to manage projects and keep the property in top condition. You'll also serve as a communication bridge between on-site staff and corporate, which at Weinstein means regular contact rather than occasional check-ins.

The corporate team is described as genuinely hands-on, providing process guidance and direct support rather than leaving property teams to self-direct. If you've worked at a company where "corporate support" meant receiving a policy manual and not much else, this will feel different.

What Strong Candidates Bring

  • Prior property management experience, with Class A multifamily exposure preferred
  • Comfort working within defined processes and a structured operating environment
  • Strong communication habits and a genuine sense of urgency when issues arise
  • Experience leading or mentoring on-site team members
  • Ability to manage high volumes of resident and corporate requests without losing attention to detail

Candidates who do well here tend to be people who find structure clarifying rather than constraining. Weinstein's model rewards accountability and consistency. If you prefer to set your own systems from scratch at every property, the fit may not be there. But if you want to operate inside a proven framework with leadership that's genuinely accessible, that's exactly what this role offers.

Compensation is competitive and experience-based, with both quarterly and annual bonus opportunities included.

greenhouse_5197987007.title: Maintenance Techician- Sonoran Apartments
greenhouse_5197987007.rewritten_description:
Maintenance technician roles at mid-size regional operators tend to reward generalists. The person who can clear a service request queue in the morning, run a make-ready punch list in the afternoon, and field an after-hours emergency call that evening is the one who grows fastest in this environment. That's the kind of technician MG Properties is looking for at Sonoran Apartments in Phoenix.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

MG Properties has spent over 30 years acquiring, developing, and managing apartment communities across the Western U.S., and their maintenance teams reflect that depth. At Sonoran, you'll be handling the full scope of day-to-day upkeep: completing resident service requests, performing appliance repairs, painting, grounds and common area cleaning, and turning units between residents. Turns, in particular, require you to move fast without cutting corners. A tight make-ready timeline keeps occupancy healthy, and a sloppy punch list creates callbacks that cost everyone time.

You'll also carry on-call rotation responsibility. That means some evenings and weekends, you're the person a resident reaches when something goes wrong. Reliable transportation isn't listed as a preference here. It's a firm requirement.

What This Role Requires

  • At least two years of apartment maintenance experience, ideally on a property of 200 units or more
  • Working knowledge across trades: plumbing, electrical, HVAC, and general repairs
  • A genuine customer service orientation. Residents interact with maintenance more directly than almost any other staff, and how you handle those moments shapes the community's reputation
  • Flexibility and the ability to work within a team, including on-call rotation
  • Reliable personal transportation

What This Role Builds

Technicians who come in with solid trade skills but limited exposure to apartment-specific operations will develop real fluency here. Managing a service request load across a 200-plus unit property teaches prioritization in a way that single-family or commercial work rarely does. You'll also build familiarity with turn workflow and the pace expectations that come with it, which is foundational if you're working toward a lead tech or maintenance supervisor role down the line.

MG Properties offers monthly bonuses, company profit sharing, a 401(k) with employer match, and a full benefits package including medical, dental, and vision. Employees also receive rental discounts and paid time off including holidays and personal days.

Phoenix's apartment market has seen sustained construction and population growth, which means properties here deal with high traffic, competitive lease-up pressure, and resident expectations that reflect newer product in the market. Maintenance teams that run tight, responsive operations are a direct competitive advantage. That's the context you'd be stepping into at Sonoran.

What You'll Actually Do

This full-time housekeeper role at Redpoint College Station puts you at the center of the resident experience every single day. The property's common areas, including the pool and spa, clubroom, public restrooms, and laundry rooms, stay clean and presentable because of the work you do. That means sweeping, mopping, dusting, and polishing on a regular schedule, clearing debris from parking areas, walkways, and stairways, and keeping the curbs clean. You'll also step in to support general maintenance needs and assist with cleaning and moving tasks as the property requires. When something looks damaged, broken, or off, you flag it to your supervisor rather than wait for it to become a bigger problem.

The on-call component is real. Outside of approved PTO, you're expected to be available for after-hours and weekend situations. Student housing runs on a tight schedule around move-ins, move-outs, and events, and the property needs to look sharp when it matters most. A valid driver's license is required, and the physical demands are genuine: standing for a full shift and lifting up to 100 lbs. are part of the job.

What You Bring

  • Ability to read instructions and document labor and materials accurately
  • Reliable attendance and schedule flexibility, including availability for after-hours emergencies
  • Valid driver's license
  • Physical ability to stand for extended periods and lift up to 100 lbs.
  • Comfort working within OSHA and safety guidelines, and following property-specific procedures

Where This Role Fits in a Property Career

Housekeeping and porter work in student housing is often where people build their first real foundation in property operations. You learn how a community functions from the ground up: what common areas drive resident satisfaction, how make-ready turns flow, and how maintenance teams coordinate. People who take this work seriously and develop a reputation for dependability often move into maintenance technician roles or lead porter positions. The skills you build here, specifically attention to asset condition, communication with supervisors, and safety awareness, carry directly into any property operations role you pursue later.

Scion offers health, dental, and vision insurance, 401k matching, paid parental and maternal leave, paid time off, a discretionary annual bonus, and learning reimbursement. For a non-exempt, full-time position in student housing operations, that's a solid package worth noting.

greenhouse_4719197005.title: Maintenance Technician
greenhouse_4719197005.rewritten_description:
Most apartment communities run on the visible work of leasing staff, but the physical product residents actually pay for depends entirely on what happens in the maintenance shop. At a stabilized residential community like Westwood Village in Westland, a skilled technician isn't just fixing things. They're protecting NOI, preserving curb appeal, and directly shaping whether residents renew. That's the context this role sits inside.

Paragon Properties is hiring a Maintenance Technician at Westwood Village Apartments, a full-time position paying up to $26/hr based on experience and certifications. The schedule is a guaranteed 40-hour week, with after-hours on-call rotation that includes weekends and holidays. Paragon provides an on-call bonus and a quarterly team bonus, which reflects a comp structure that actually rewards the extra burden of emergency availability rather than just expecting it.

What the Work Looks Like Day to Day

Your workload will split between resident service requests and make-ready work. On the make-ready side, you'll prep vacant units for occupancy, handling basic drywall patching, painting, and rough carpentry as part of the turn process. On the service side, you'll troubleshoot and repair plumbing, electrical systems, major appliances, pool and spa equipment, and HVAC. HVAC certification (Type II or Universal) is strongly preferred, and given how much of a technician's time goes toward heating and cooling calls, that credential carries real weight here.

Curb appeal and physical integrity of the property are also part of the job. You'll flag potential liabilities and propose improvements when you spot them, which means this role requires some situational awareness beyond just closing out work orders.

What the Role Builds Toward

Technicians who develop a strong combination of HVAC competency, appliance repair, and turn experience tend to move into lead tech or maintenance supervisor roles within two to four years. At a company like Paragon that offers internal certification programs and advancement pathways, the skills you build here compound quickly. Universal EPA certification alone opens doors to higher-comp positions across Class A, B, and C communities throughout any market. If you eventually want to move into a maintenance director or regional facilities role, the foundation starts with being the person who can diagnose a condensate line issue and also spot a trip hazard in the parking lot on the same afternoon.

What Paragon Offers

  • Up to $26/hr depending on experience and certifications
  • Paid time off plus 9 company-paid holidays
  • Rent discount at Paragon communities
  • 401(k) with employer contribution
  • After-hours on-call bonus and quarterly team bonus
  • Medical, dental, and vision insurance with a short enrollment waiting period
  • Company-paid life and disability insurance
  • Tool kit provided after 30-day new hire training period
  • Uniform program and employee recognition program

What the Role Requires

  • At least one year of maintenance experience, whether technical, vocational, or hands-on
  • HVAC Type II or Universal certification, strongly preferred
  • Valid driver's license and reliable transportation
  • High school diploma required; trade school or college-level coursework strongly preferred
  • Ability to work outdoors year-round in Michigan weather
  • Pre-employment background check, drug screening, and physical required

The candidate who stands out in this role combines technical range with genuine follow-through on customer service. Residents remember how a technician communicated during a repair almost as much as whether the repair held. That combination of craft and communication is what tends to get noticed at the company level and lead to the next step.

greenhouse_5373931008.rewritten_description:
Skills This Role Puts to Work Every Day

Community Manager work at Ackermann Group sits at the intersection of financial oversight, team leadership, and resident experience. You'll draw on your ability to read occupancy trends, manage delinquency, and evaluate NOI performance through property management software. Yardi Voyager experience is particularly useful here, as is comfort with reporting tools that surface T-12 and T-3 data quickly. On the leasing side, you'll need a sharp eye for traffic patterns and the judgment to adjust concessions or marketing strategies when numbers shift. This is a role where financial fluency and people skills work together constantly.

The maintenance side of the job demands a different but equally important skill set. You'll coordinate with your Maintenance Supervisor on unit turns, make-ready timelines, preventative maintenance schedules, and service request completion rates. Capex project management also falls under your scope, which means tracking budgets, communicating with leadership, and keeping projects on schedule without losing sight of day-to-day operations. The ability to hold both the strategic and the tactical at the same time is what separates a strong Community Manager from an average one.

Skills This Role Builds

If your background is primarily in leasing or assistant management, this role accelerates your development in two areas that matter most for senior property management positions: full P&L accountability and cross-functional team leadership. You'll build experience recruiting and interviewing your own staff in collaboration with HR and your Regional Manager. You'll set performance goals, run site-level meetings, and coach a leasing and maintenance team through the full operating cycle. Those experiences translate directly to Regional Manager and Director of Operations roles down the line.

Working with tools like EliseAI and AIRM also gives you exposure to AI-assisted leasing and revenue management platforms that are reshaping how multifamily operators handle prospect communication and pricing. Getting hands-on experience with these systems now puts you ahead of peers who haven't worked in environments where that technology is already embedded in daily operations.

What Ackermann Group Brings to the Role

Ackermann Group has been developing and managing properties in the Midwest since 1938. That kind of tenure in one market means the operational infrastructure is mature and the institutional knowledge runs deep. Columbus is a strong multifamily market with consistent demand driven by a large university presence, a growing tech sector, and steady in-migration. Working for a company with deep local roots means your Regional Manager understands the market dynamics you're operating in, which makes the collaboration on marketing strategy and budget planning more grounded than it often is at national operators.

What You'll Actually Do

At The Rey in San Diego, the Maintenance Technician role touches nearly every corner of daily community life. You're the person residents call when something goes wrong, and you're also the one quietly keeping things from going wrong in the first place. That balance between reactive repairs and proactive upkeep is really what defines this position.

Day to day, you'll handle the full range of general maintenance needs: plumbing fixes, electrical troubleshooting, appliance repairs, carpentry work, and general building upkeep. You'll help manage the shop, keep inventory organized, and make sure equipment and keys are properly secured. Curb appeal matters here. If something looks off walking through the property, you notice it and you address it. Management leans on you to uphold community standards, and that means being thorough on make-readies and punch list items so units are genuinely ready for new residents, not just technically turned.

You'll interact with residents regularly, which means your communication style matters as much as your technical skills. A friendly, calm presence when someone's frustrated about a maintenance issue goes a long way toward resident retention. That's not a soft skill, it's a real part of the job.

What You Bring

  • At least one year of hands-on maintenance experience in a residential community setting
  • Working knowledge across appliances, plumbing, electrical, carpentry, and general building systems
  • Comfortable with computers and basic software for work order management or communication
  • Strong written and spoken English communication skills
  • A detail-oriented approach to property inspections and safety compliance

The Fit and the Context

Berkshire Residential owns and manages its own properties, which means decisions get made closer to the ground than at a typical third-party management shop. Maintenance staff here tend to have a real voice in how things run at the property level. That's worth something if you're someone who takes ownership of your work and wants to be heard when you flag a recurring issue.

The pay range for this role in California runs from $24 to $28 per hour, depending on experience, with benefits that include health coverage, retirement, paid time off, and a meaningful rent discount for employees who live on-site or at a Berkshire community.

One thing that separates strong candidates in this type of role: the ability to prioritize well under pressure. On a busy day you might have a handful of open work orders, a unit turn in progress, and a resident standing at the office with an urgent request. The technicians who thrive here are the ones who can triage calmly, communicate honestly about timelines, and follow through without needing to be chased. That combination of technical competence and personal accountability is what makes the difference between a good hire and a great one.

smartrecruiters_744000140512309.title: Apartment Leasing Sales Consultant - Winthrop West
smartrecruiters_744000140512309.rewritten_description:
AIR Communities runs a large portfolio of apartment communities across major U.S. markets, and this onsite leasing role at their Tampa property is built for someone who treats leasing as a sales function, not a hospitality one. You're following prospects through a defined process: prompt follow-up, scheduled tours, closing. The expectation is hitting monthly leasing goals consistently, not occasionally.

The commission structure rewards more than just volume. Leasing a higher-rent unit, securing an 18-month or longer lease term, or exceeding your monthly goal each trigger separate commission tiers. That layered structure gives strong performers real upside on individual transactions, not just a flat per-lease bonus.

One benefit worth understanding: AIR offers a 25% rent discount at any of their communities. If you lease onsite, you can eliminate your commute entirely. That's a meaningful compensation component depending on Tampa rental rates at the time you're hired.

The role also includes a potential extended winter break after peak leasing season. This is unpaid time, but benefits and the rent discount stay active. It's an unusual arrangement. If you prefer year-round full-time hours, clarify that expectation before accepting. If you'd use the time well, it's a genuine perk.

What the role requires

  • At least one year of sales or customer service experience with measurable goals, in property management, hospitality, retail, or a similar environment
  • Comfort following a structured sales process and tracking your own performance against it
  • Weekend availability and schedule flexibility based on community hours and season
  • Reliable transportation
  • Strong written and verbal English communication skills
  • Working knowledge of Fair Housing laws and regulations

What separates the better candidates here is prior experience in a role where hitting a number was the actual measure of success. Leasing consultants who come from retail or restaurant backgrounds often adapt well because they're used to a traffic-driven environment where every interaction counts. People who haven't worked against a quota before tend to struggle with the pace AIR expects.

Tampa's rental market has seen consistent demand pressure over the past few years, which keeps occupancy goals achievable but also raises resident expectations. You'll be selling into a competitive submarket where prospects have options, so knowing how to communicate the specific value of your community matters more than generic enthusiasm.

greenhouse_5374437008.title: Assistant Maintenance Manager - $3,500 Sign- On Bonus
greenhouse_5374437008.rewritten_description:
Bozzuto is hiring an Assistant Maintenance Manager for one of its residential communities in Cambridge, MA, and the role comes with a $3,500 sign-on bonus. The base salary is $70,000. Cambridge is a dense, high-demand submarket with a mix of older mechanicals and newer construction, so whoever takes this seat needs to be comfortable across a range of building systems, not just the basics.

The day-to-day is what you'd expect from a senior maintenance role at a well-run company: service ticket completion, turns, preventative maintenance, grounds upkeep, and keeping the building's mechanical systems running at peak. Where this role goes beyond wrench-turning is the supervisory component. You're expected to lead a team, set the tone for quality and professionalism, and own the make-ready process end to end. Sloppy turns cost the community days of vacancy and frustrated new move-ins. That's the kind of detail this role is accountable for.

On the technical side, Bozzuto wants someone who knows HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and appliance repair at a working level, with certifications to back it up (EPA and HVAC certs are listed). Exposure to complex mechanical systems like chillers, boilers, and central plant equipment is a plus, which tells you something about the property. Basic carpentry, drywall, and paint round out the punch list skill set. If you've only ever worked in simpler garden-style product, this may be a stretch.

The on-call rotation is real. Weekend availability is required. That's not a small print item at a company like Bozzuto where resident experience expectations are high. The candidates who tend to thrive in these roles are the ones who treat emergency response as part of the job, not an imposition on it.

What You'll Need

  • 5 or more years in the trades, facilities, or residential building maintenance
  • HVAC, EPA, and/or NAPE certification
  • Working knowledge of HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and appliance repair
  • Supervisory or team lead experience preferred
  • Familiarity with OSHA standards and risk management practices
  • Comfort with property management technology platforms and basic Microsoft Office
  • Ability to lift 25 to 50 pounds frequently and work in varying weather conditions

Bozzuto offers medical, dental, and vision coverage, 20 days of PTO plus holidays, a 401k with company match, and tuition reimbursement. For someone with solid technical chops who's ready to step into a supervisory role at a company that takes building quality seriously, this is a reasonable place to do it.

greenhouse_4338172009.title: Leasing & Sales Consultant, Bilingual
greenhouse_4338172009.rewritten_description:
Leasing at a large multifamily operator is a sales job with a hospitality wrapper. You're measured on conversion rates and occupancy, but you earn trust through the quality of every interaction along the way. Cortland, one of the ten largest multifamily owners and operators in the country, is hiring a bilingual leasing and sales consultant to fill that role at one of its communities.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Most of your day centers on prospects: incoming leads, scheduled tours, follow-up calls, and CRM entries. You'll work a pipeline the way a sales role demands, tracking where each prospect stands and moving them toward a signed lease. Consultative selling matters here. That means listening for what someone actually needs before pitching an apartment, then connecting what the community offers to those specific priorities.

The bilingual requirement is a real part of the job. You'll serve residents and prospects who prefer to communicate in a language other than English, and your ability to do that fluently affects both conversion and resident experience.

Beyond the leasing side, you'll help maintain the community's social media presence, plan resident events, and handle the relationship-building that keeps renewals strong. Resident experience and occupancy are connected. Communities with engaged residents generate more referrals and fewer unexpected vacancies.

What Cortland Expects From You

  • At least six months of experience in a sales, customer-facing, or performance-driven role
  • Bilingual fluency (English plus one additional language)
  • Comfort being held to leasing goals, conversion targets, and KPIs
  • Organized follow-up habits and strong time management
  • Experience with or willingness to learn CRM platforms
  • A polished, professional presentation that fits a premium brand
  • Coachability. Cortland tracks performance closely, and feedback comes regularly.

One honest note: leasing roles at Class A operators carry real pressure. Traffic slows on weekends when you're still working, prospects ghost after tours, and monthly close-rate targets don't move. If you're wired for that kind of accountability, the environment suits you. If consistent goal-tracking feels like friction rather than motivation, this particular role probably won't.

For candidates who perform well, the leasing consultant path inside a vertically integrated company like Cortland has clear upward steps: assistant manager, then property manager, and from there into regional or corporate-facing roles. The internal structure is deep enough that lateral moves into training, marketing, or operations are also realistic over time.

greenhouse_5199551007.title: General Manager
greenhouse_5199551007.rewritten_description:
Commercial property management at the General Manager level is fundamentally an ownership proxy role. The GM doesn't just run operations; they represent the client's interests across every decision that touches asset value, from lease administration and CAM reconciliations to capital planning and vendor procurement. Lincoln Property Company is hiring for that role in Clayton, MO, one of the St. Louis metro's most established commercial submarkets, anchored by Class A office and mixed-use assets that attract institutional ownership and demand institutional-grade management.

The Scope of the Role

This position carries full operational and financial accountability for a large or complex commercial asset, or a portfolio of assets, with property managers or senior property managers reporting directly to you. The day-to-day involves a wide range of concurrent responsibilities: tenant relationship management from initial onboarding through move-out, monthly financial reporting with variance analysis, annual operating and capital budget preparation, CAM and OpX recovery billing, and lease administration coordination with the accounting team. You'll approve vendor invoices within the management agreement's authorization limits, run competitive bid processes with written analysis and client recommendations, and maintain proactive AR collection with documented recommendations on delinquency.

Construction oversight is part of the job, whether that's tenant improvement coordination or capital projects. Emergency preparedness planning, monthly property inspections, and keeping vacant spaces tour-ready round out the operational side. On the financial side, you're expected to produce insightful reports, not just accurate ones. Clients at this level expect variance explanations tied to lease events, market conditions, or operational decisions, not just numbers on a page.

You'll also function as a people manager with real depth: recruiting, hiring, scheduling, cross-training, coaching, and delivering performance reviews for your team. Lincoln's structure involves collaboration across accounting, leasing, and construction support teams, and the GM is the one holding those threads together for the client.

What This Role Requires

  • 5 to 8 years of commercial property management experience, with office, retail, or industrial asset background required
  • Bachelor's degree preferred; a strong combination of education and hands-on experience is considered
  • Active real estate license where required by Missouri regulation; CPM or RPA designation (or active candidacy) preferred
  • Intermediate to advanced Excel proficiency; familiarity with MRI and Kardin is a plus
  • Working knowledge of leases, contracts, financial instruments, tax implications, and construction processes
  • Demonstrated ability to prepare budgets with long-term capital plans, forecast outcomes, and deliver ROI and cost/benefit analysis
  • Strong written communication skills, including business correspondence and procedure documentation
  • Availability for after-hours response, weekend coverage, and emergency situations as the role demands

What separates strong candidates from solid ones at this level is the ability to hold the financial narrative. greenhouse_8093315.title: Groundskeeper - Apartment Community
greenhouse_8093315.rewritten_description:
It's 8 a.m. on a Monday and the parking lot already has weekend debris scattered across it. You grab the blower and start from the far end, working your way toward the leasing office before residents head to their cars for work. That's often how the day begins at Bexley SoCo.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Weinstein Properties has owned and managed apartment communities for over 70 years, and they're still family-operated out of Richmond, Virginia. Their portfolio spans more than 60 communities across five states. This groundskeeper role sits at their Bexley SoCo property in South Austin, and the schedule is straightforward: Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.

The day-to-day is honest, physical work. You'll pick up litter and pet waste daily, clean and restock pet waste stations, trash out vacant apartments as they turn, pressure wash, blow common areas, and do light planting and weeding. When the maintenance or leasing teams need an extra hand, you pitch in. Some days bring light painting or housekeeping-style tasks inside common spaces. The work is repetitive by nature, and that's worth knowing before you apply. If you need variety to stay engaged, this one might wear on you. If you're someone who takes genuine satisfaction in a clean, well-kept property, you'll find a rhythm here quickly.

You'll operate a backpack blower, power washer, and golf cart with trailer. The role requires lifting up to 50 pounds regularly, prolonged standing and walking, bending and stooping, and working outdoors year-round through Austin summers and the occasional cold snap. Heat in particular is real here. South Austin in July is not mild.

Who Fits This Role

  • Reliable and punctual. This is the single most important trait. The property doesn't look after itself while you figure out your morning.
  • Self-directed. A manager won't follow you around. You'll know your task list and you'll work through it.
  • Detail-oriented. Noticing a spill near the mailboxes or a broken bag dispenser before a resident complains is part of the job.
  • Physically capable of meeting all demands of the role, with or without accommodation.
  • Open to learning. Weinstein promotes from within, and groundskeeper is a legitimate starting point toward a maintenance tech role for the right person.

Pay starts at $18 per hour with quarterly bonuses, and there's currently a $1,000 stay-on bonus available after 90 days in good standing. Benefits include health, dental, and vision insurance, PTO, paid holidays, birthday time off, a 401k, an Employee Assistance Program, and a rent discount. The recruiter can walk you through the stay-on bonus specifics.

Weinstein describes their approach as hands-on, and that extends to how they develop staff. If you show up, work hard, and keep a decent attitude, there's a real path here beyond the groundskeeper title.

greenhouse_8654348002.title: Maintenance Technician
greenhouse_8654348002.rewritten_description:
Single-family rental at scale changes what a maintenance tech's day actually looks like. You're not the on-site guy at one apartment complex. You're the person keeping a distributed portfolio of homes running, which means your judgment matters more than it would in a traditional setting. No supervisor two doors down. No leasing office to loop in. You make the call, you document it, and you move on to the next address.

What the Work Looks Like Day to Day

Roofstock operates in the single-family rental space, and this Columbus-based role reflects that model directly. Your day is built around travel between properties: routine repairs, make-readies on vacant homes, move-in and move-out inspections, and onboarding audits when new properties come into the portfolio. HVAC, plumbing, and electrical work are all in scope. You'll also audit vendor work, which means you need a real eye for quality because if a contractor cut corners, you're the one who catches it before it becomes a bigger problem.

Work orders and communication run through mobile apps, so comfort with a smartphone isn't optional. A company vehicle and gas card are provided, which removes the wear-and-tear concern that comes with field-heavy roles.

The schedule is full-time with no on-call rotation and no weekend requirement. That's genuinely uncommon at this pay range in property maintenance, and it reflects a deliberate staffing model rather than an afterthought.

Who Fits This Role Well

The requirements here are straightforward:

  • HVAC Type II Certification (required); Universal Certification is preferred
  • Valid driver's license with a clean enough record to operate a company vehicle
  • Ability to work independently across multiple sites without daily supervision
  • Comfort using mobile tools for work orders, updates, and field communication
  • Physical capability for the role: lifting up to 50 lbs, bending, climbing, outdoor conditions
  • High school diploma or GED
  • Authorization to work in the U.S. (no visa sponsorship available)

Strong candidates tend to be people who can triage on the spot. In a scattered-site model, you'll sometimes arrive at a property and find something that wasn't on the work order. The technicians who do well here are the ones who troubleshoot accurately, document clearly, and don't need to be managed closely to stay productive. Self-direction isn't a soft skill in this context. It's the core of how the job functions.

Pay runs $25 to $30 per hour depending on experience, certifications, and location factors. Benefits include health, dental, and vision coverage, a 401k, generous PTO plus 12 paid holidays, paid parental leave, volunteer time off, and monthly subsidies for wellness and home office or cell phone expenses.

greenhouse_7821010003.title: Leasing Consultant (Benton)
greenhouse_7821010003.rewritten_description:
Prometheus has been holding apartments in the Bay Area since 1965, which means they've seen more market cycles than most operators care to count. As the largest privately held apartment owner in the region, with a portfolio pushing 13,000 units across Silicon Valley, Portland, and Seattle, they're not a startup figuring things out. The infrastructure is there. So is the expectation that you'll use it.

The Benton community in Santa Clara is looking for a Leasing Consultant, though Prometheus calls the role a Neighbor Ambassador internally. The title shift reflects something real about how they operate. This isn't a straight traffic-to-application conversion job. You're handling the full customer-facing experience: touring future residents, walking them through the leasing process, and staying involved after move-in to make sure people actually feel settled. On the admin side, you're preparing rental agreements, pulling market surveys, posting availability, and producing the kind of property-level reporting that keeps operations honest.

Weekend availability is required, full stop. The schedule runs with regular weekdays off, and Prometheus pays a weekend shift premium on top of the base hourly rate of $25.00 to $26.25. Add a $200 per-lease incentive, a discretionary semi-annual bonus, and additional bonuses tied to lease-up performance, referrals, and training coaching, and the compensation picture is more layered than most leasing roles at this level. Benefits include 100% company-paid medical, dental, and vision for employees and eligible dependents, 401(k) with employer matching, and tenure-based housing discounts that become more meaningful the longer you stay.

On the candidate side, Prometheus is open about hiring across industries. Prior leasing experience isn't listed as a requirement. What they're actually screening for is harder to fake: comfort in a sales and service environment, genuine follow-through with people, and the kind of self-direction that doesn't need a manager standing nearby to stay productive.

One thing worth knowing about leasing roles at well-capitalized, vertically integrated owners like Prometheus: the exposure is broader than at a fee-management shop. Because acquisitions, development, value-add renovations, and operations all sit under one roof, leasing staff at the property level tend to see more of how the full business works. For someone early in a property management career, that context compounds quickly. Leasing consultants who absorb the operational side of the role, not just the customer-facing piece, tend to move into assistant manager and then manager positions faster than those who treat it as a pure sales job.

What You Bring

  • Experience in customer service, sales, or a client-facing environment (industry doesn't have to be property management)
  • Comfort managing competing tasks across leasing, admin, and resident communication
  • Availability on weekends as a standard part of your schedule
  • Clear written and verbal communication skills
  • A track record of following through, not just initiating

greenhouse_4338115009.location: Hawthorne at Stillwater - 131 Stillwater Landing Way - Sneads Ferry, NC - 28460
greenhouse_4338115009.rewritten_description:
Skills This Role Runs On

This position pulls on three skill sets simultaneously: leasing, financial administration, and people management. You're converting prospects into residents, tracking delinquency and posting payments, and stepping into the Community Manager's seat when they're out. All three happen in the same week, often the same day.

Strong candidates already know how to read a ledger, handle a collections call without escalating tension, and close a tour. The financial side here is real work: ledger audits, payment posting, delinquency follow-up, and supporting reporting for regional leadership. If numbers aren't your thing, this role will feel harder than it should.

What You'll Be Doing at Hawthorne at Stillwater

Day to day, you're supporting leasing activity at this garden-style community in Sneads Ferry. That means responding to leads, conducting tours, processing applications, and keeping renewals moving on schedule. Occupancy is a shared goal, and your leasing activity directly affects it.

On the financial side, you'll oversee rent collection, post payments, scan checks, and run weekly delinquency follow-ups. You'll also conduct regular ledger reviews to catch billing errors and verify account accuracy before they become bigger problems.

You'll manage the community's social media presence, keep common areas and the leasing office presentable, and handle resident concerns with composure. When the Community Manager is unavailable, you run point.

  • Two years of property management experience preferred
  • Six months of prior assistant community manager experience preferred
  • High school diploma or GED required
  • Valid driver's license required
  • CALP designation is a plus
  • Availability for some Saturdays (10 AM to 4 PM) and occasional evenings for resident events

What's Distinctive Here

Hawthorne ranks among the top 50 multifamily management companies nationally, with deep roots in the Southeast. For this role specifically, they offer a structured career path program with real intent behind it: Assistant Community Manager to Community Manager is a stated trajectory, backed by a Learning and Development team. That's worth noting if upward mobility matters to you.

Compensation includes an hourly base plus monthly leasing and renewal commissions and quarterly performance bonuses. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401k match, paid time off (including your birthday), pet insurance, and paid parental leave options.

The Sneads Ferry market sits near Camp Lejeune, which creates a steady, military-affiliated renter base. That population tends toward shorter lease terms and higher turnover, so MTM management and renewal retention skills get real exercise here.

greenhouse_4339313009.rewritten_description:
This part-time role at Dexter Street Commons in Pawtucket covers the full range of day-to-day physical plant work that keeps a residential property running and looking well-maintained. At 20 hours per week, the schedule is flexible, but the work itself is varied and hands-on.

What You'll Actually Do

Most of your time goes toward completing maintenance requests as they come in: repairing doors, locks, tiles, and handrails, swapping out light fixtures, installing smoke detectors, and handling appliance repairs. Cosmetic work is a real part of this position too. Painting units, replacing window screens, and similar make-ready tasks are regular responsibilities, not occasional add-ons. You'll also need to stay sharp on documentation, keeping paperwork and invoices organized for the work you complete.

The role requires availability for emergency situations, including flood response and back-to-back move-ins. Even at part-time hours, those moments call for someone who stays composed and moves quickly. You'll coordinate with outside contractors and vendors, which means you need to know enough about the trades to hold a productive conversation with specialists and verify that work meets the property's standards.

What You Bring

  • At least six months of hands-on trade or building maintenance experience
  • Working familiarity with electrical and mechanical systems at a repair level
  • Comfort identifying safety concerns and acting on them without waiting to be told
  • Specialized trade background in plumbing, electrical, HVAC, or roofing is a meaningful advantage
  • Reliability and the ability to manage your own work order flow with minimal supervision

Context Worth Knowing

John M. Corcoran and Company has operated in New England since 1951, and the culture reflects that longevity: long tenure on staff, institutional knowledge that gets passed down, and a genuine emphasis on quality over speed. That context matters for a maintenance role because it shapes expectations. Properties managed by firms with that kind of history tend to hold high standards for presentation and resident experience, which means cosmetic attention and follow-through on punch list items carry real weight, not just the mechanical repairs.

For someone building a maintenance career, part-time work at a well-run property is genuinely useful experience. The breadth of work here, from appliance repairs to contractor coordination to emergency response, covers skills that transfer directly to a full-time maintenance technician or lead tech role. If you're looking to develop a well-rounded maintenance background while working a flexible schedule, this position builds exactly the kind of varied, documented experience that makes future employers pay attention.

greenhouse_6130097004.title: Maintenance Technician
greenhouse_6130097004.rewritten_description:
Maintenance work at a residential apartment community covers a wide range of trades, and the technician who thrives here is someone who can shift from a plumbing call in the morning to an electrical issue in the afternoon without losing focus. Cottonwood Residential is adding a Maintenance Technician at Stratford at Hillcrest Apartments in Winston-Salem, and this is a role that draws on what you already know while steadily expanding what you can do.

On the technical side, you'll handle repairs across plumbing, electrical, and general carpentry, both inside units and across the property grounds. The role operates within standard community hours, and it includes on-call responsibility for after-hours emergencies. That after-hours piece is worth being clear-eyed about: it's part of the job, and it's where your ability to diagnose and resolve problems under pressure gets sharpened most. You won't be doing it alone. The Service Manager provides support, and you'll work within established company standards on every call.

Physically, the role demands real stamina. You'll be on your feet most of the day, climbing stairs and ladders, working in tight spaces, and lifting up to 50 pounds regularly. A valid driver's license is required. EPA Type II or Universal certification, HVAC troubleshooting experience, and CPO certification each strengthen your candidacy, though they aren't listed as hard requirements.

What the role requires vs. what it builds

Coming in, you need working knowledge of residential repairs across at least a couple of trades, solid physical capability, and the communication skills to work through work orders and interact with residents clearly. What the role builds is something different: diagnostic instincts. Apartment maintenance is repetitive enough that patterns emerge quickly. Over time, you develop a mental model of how systems fail in a garden-style residential setting, which makes you faster and more accurate on every turn and make-ready you touch.

Technicians who grow fastest in roles like this are the ones who treat the on-call rotation as a learning accelerator rather than just an obligation. Emergency calls, by definition, involve conditions you haven't seen before, and the problem-solving you do at 10 PM on a Saturday builds judgment that routine daytime work can't replicate.

  • Valid driver's license (required)
  • Ability to lift up to 50 lbs and work on your feet for extended periods
  • Availability for on-call after-hours emergency coverage
  • Ability to work evenings and weekends as part of standard scheduling
  • EPA Type II or Universal certification (a plus)
  • HVAC troubleshooting experience (a plus)
  • CPO certification (a plus)

Cottonwood Residential offers health, vision, dental, life, and disability coverage with a quick eligibility window, a 401k with company match, HSA matching, three weeks of paid time off in the first year, and over ten paid holidays annually.

This role covers five apartment communities across two Pittsburgh-area submarkets: four properties totaling 198 units in Greensburg and one 97-unit community in New Kensington. Multi-site portfolios at this scale demand someone who can move fluidly between hands-on skilled trades work and the logistical side of managing people, vendors, and budgets. Birgo is looking for a maintenance supervisor who does both well.

The day-to-day splits roughly into two modes. Some of it is field work: plumbing, electrical, HVAC, drywall, turns, punch lists, and groundskeeping across properties that aren't all in the same zip code. The rest is coordination: leading a two-person tech team, sourcing and managing contractors when the scope exceeds what the crew can handle, tracking expenditures against budget, and serving as the operational link between maintenance and property management. AppFolio handles work orders in a paperless workflow, so comfort with mobile tools matters here.

The Greensburg and New Kensington markets sit in the older housing stock belt east and northeast of Pittsburgh. Properties in these corridors tend to be garden-style or low-rise buildings with aging mechanical systems, which means HVAC and plumbing calls come with some frequency. A supervisor who can personally handle high-skill repairs keeps vendor costs down and reduces unit downtime on turns. That's a real budget lever at this portfolio size.

Birgo emphasizes servant leadership internally, and that framing is worth taking seriously in the context of this role. Managing two techs means coaching and developing them, not just directing work. Strong candidates will have experience building a team's technical capability over time, not just assigning jobs and checking completions. Emotional intelligence in conflict resolution, which comes up in any maintenance team eventually, matters as much as trade credentials here.

What Birgo is Looking For

  • Hands-on expertise across plumbing, electrical, HVAC, and drywall
  • Experience managing a multi-site portfolio
