What You'll Actually Do

Maintenance technicians at The Reserve handle the full range of day-to-day upkeep: HVAC service and repairs, plumbing, electrical work, and structural fixes across the property's interior and exterior. You're also responsible for preventative maintenance, which means staying ahead of issues before they turn into emergency calls. Speaking of which, after-hours emergencies are part of this role. When a resident loses heat in January or has a water leak at midnight, someone has to respond. That's you sometimes.

On a typical day, you'll work through a queue of resident service requests, document what you find, complete the work, and move on to the next one. Keeping accurate records matters here, both for accountability and for spotting recurring problems on the property. The job keeps you moving physically, so expect time on your feet, climbing, bending, and lifting throughout your shift.

What You Bring

  • 2 to 3 years of maintenance experience in a residential or comparable setting
  • Working knowledge of HVAC, plumbing, and electrical systems
  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • Valid driver's license
  • EPA Type 2 or Universal certification (preferred but not required)
  • Ability to communicate clearly with residents and teammates, even when the situation is frustrating

The EPA certification is worth mentioning separately. If you have it, you're more useful on HVAC work from day one. If you don't, it's a credential worth pursuing early and one that adds real value to your skill set across any property you work on in the future.

The Role in Context

BAM Companies has been operating since 2010 and manages properties across multiple markets. The Reserve in Evansville is part of that portfolio. Pay for this position ranges from $17 to $19 per hour depending on experience and qualifications. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage with BAM covering a significant share of the cost, paid life insurance, rent discounts at BAM properties, and a PTO structure that gives you 88 hours after 90 days and 120 hours after your first year, plus 14.5 paid holidays.

One honest note for anyone weighing this against other maintenance roles: the difference between a solid technician and an exceptional one at a property like this usually comes down to how they handle resident interactions, not just the technical work. You can fix a unit perfectly, but if you leave a resident feeling dismissed or uninformed, the job isn't really done. The technical skills get you hired. The communication habits are what build a reputation on site.

greenhouse_4336782009.rewritten_description:
Leasing skills sit at the center of this role, and they show up in concrete, measurable ways. At Redstone Residential's Rexburg community, a Leasing Manager's effectiveness gets measured in occupancy trends, renewal rates, and the quality of every prospect interaction from the first phone call to the signed lease. This is a hands-on leasing position with real operational responsibility layered in.

Skills This Role Puts to Work Daily

Sales and customer service aren't background skills here. They drive the core function of the job. You'll conduct prospect tours, manage phone and email pipelines, and run renewal campaigns designed to hold occupancy. Redstone uses Entrata as its leasing platform, so comfort with structured software workflows matters. You'll also work within their online and social marketing systems, which means basic SEO awareness and digital communication skills translate directly into leasing performance.

On the administrative side, you'll maintain resident ledgers and keep balances accurate. That requires attention to detail and a working comfort with cloud-based tools like Google Drive and Dropbox. Mistakes in ledger management create downstream problems for collections and delinquency tracking, so accuracy carries real weight.

The Operational Layer

Beyond leasing, this role supports the Community Manager across broader operations. That includes budget performance awareness, rent collections, and some staff administration. You're not just filling units. You're helping keep the property running day to day, which gives you visibility into how leasing activity connects to NOI and overall community health.

Rexburg is a student-market town built largely around BYU-Idaho's enrollment calendar. That means leasing cycles here follow a rhythm that differs from conventional multifamily. Traffic peaks and lease-up pressure align with academic timelines, and renewal campaigns need to account for the transient nature of a student population. Experience in or awareness of student housing dynamics is a genuine advantage in this market.

What Separates Strong Candidates

  • Demonstrated ability to hit leasing goals without waiting to be directed, especially during peak traffic periods
  • Comfort using Entrata or a comparable leasing CRM, not just basic office software
  • A communication style that works equally well with prospects, current residents, and teammates
  • Enough composure to handle a high-volume leasing season without letting service quality slip

Redstone operates at scale, managing over 38,000 beds across 20 states as a third-party manager. That structure means their systems, reporting standards, and leasing processes are well-developed. For someone early in a property management career, working inside that kind of operational framework builds transferable skills quickly. The Leasing Manager role is a natural stepping stone toward a Community Manager position, particularly for candidates who develop both the leasing and administrative sides of the job.

greenhouse_5373457008.title: Assistant Community Manager
greenhouse_5373457008.rewritten_description:
What You'll Actually Do

This role sits at the center of daily operations at a Fairstead affordable housing property in Dallas. You'll work alongside the Property Manager to keep the property compliant, occupied, and financially sound. A good portion of your time goes toward HUD compliance: executing the 4350.3 Handbook requirements, coordinating annual and interim recertification reviews, and helping prepare the property for REAC inspections, Management and Occupancy Reviews, LIHTC reviews, and investor site visits. When EHS violations surface, you help get them cleared.

On the financial side, you'll track arrears daily, ensure rents are collected, posted, and deposited, and create purchase orders in Yardi. You'll work with the in-house legal team to monitor rent payment status and coordinate evictions when lease violations escalate past intervention. On the resident-facing side, you're responding to calls, emails, and complaints within a few hours, alerting staff to move-ins and move-outs, and making sure the maintenance team closes out service requests. You also manage the lease renewal program to protect retention.

What You Bring

  • At least two years of experience in affordable housing leasing or property management (required)
  • Working knowledge of EIV, Yardi, and RealPage
  • Familiarity with HUD 4350.3 compliance requirements and LIHTC recertification processes
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, specifically for resident relations and documentation
  • Knowledge of the Dallas residential market

What This Role Builds

Affordable housing compliance is a distinct discipline within property management, and this position develops real depth in it. Candidates who come from conventional multifamily often underestimate how different the regulatory cadence is. You'll sharpen your ability to read and apply HUD guidance, manage recertification timelines, and prepare a property for formal review cycles. Those skills transfer directly into Community Manager roles at affordable properties, compliance specialist positions, or regional roles within affordable housing portfolios. Fairstead operates across 28 states with more than 30,000 units, so internal advancement for people who prove themselves operationally is a realistic path.

The candidates who thrive here combine genuine attention to detail on the compliance and financial side with the interpersonal steadiness that resident-facing work requires. greenhouse_5374485008.rewritten_description:
You're wrapping up a site visit at The Hixon, then driving across Bend to check in with the team at Terava before the afternoon leasing rush. That's the rhythm of this role: two communities, one manager, constant context-switching.

The Role

CloudTen Residential is hiring a Multi-Site Community Manager to oversee day-to-day operations at two Bend, Oregon apartment communities: The Hixon and Terava. You'll report to a Regional Manager and carry full operational accountability across both sites. That means staffing, leasing, financials, maintenance oversight, compliance, and resident relations. A valid driver's license is required.

On the financial side, you'll manage rent collection, work delinquent accounts within Oregon landlord-tenant law, handle daily deposits, monitor expenses, and contribute to budget preparation. You're expected to flag inefficiencies and recommend cost-effective improvements, not just report numbers up the chain.

Leasing and marketing are part of the job too. You'll oversee unit advertising, conduct showings, keep lease records clean, and analyze local market data to guide pricing decisions. Renewal outreach and retention efforts fall under your scope as well.

People management is a core part of this position. You'll hire, train, and evaluate on-site staff across both properties. That includes building a team culture that reflects CloudTen's standards and giving people what they need to do their jobs well.

What You Need

  • At least two years of property management experience; multi-site experience is a plus
  • Solid working knowledge of Oregon landlord-tenant law and Fair Housing regulations
  • Comfort with property management software and Microsoft Office (Word and Excel in particular)
  • Strong organizational skills, since you'll be managing schedules, records, and priorities across two locations simultaneously
  • High school diploma required; college coursework or a degree in a related field is preferred
  • Valid driver's license

Compensation is set at $85,000 annually. CloudTen offers medical, dental, and vision insurance, company-paid life insurance, FSA options, paid vacation, sick leave, and holidays.

One thing worth knowing about this specific setup: managing two separate communities means your authority is real, but your time is divided. Strong candidates for multi-site roles tend to be people who build systems rather than rely on memory. If you've managed a single property well by staying on top of every detail personally, that approach gets harder to sustain when you're splitting time between two sites. Managers who document processes, delegate effectively, and trust their on-site teams tend to do better in this structure than those who prefer to control everything directly.

Multifamily maintenance operations run on the Service Manager. Leasing fills units; the Service Manager keeps residents in them. The property requires lease-up experience. That's a specific ask. During a lease-up, vacant units hit the schedule in waves, turn timelines compress, and the make-ready process has to run without much margin for error. If you've managed a maintenance team through a lease-up before, you understand the pace this role operates at from the start.

Day to day, you're directing your team's work order assignments, targeting 24-hour completion on service requests and 5-day turns on vacancies. workable_6001657.rewritten_description:
Student housing maintenance runs at a different tempo than conventional multifamily. Turns happen in concentrated windows, pool logs need to be airtight, and a broken HVAC unit in a Tempe summer is a genuine emergency. PeakMade Real Estate manages off-campus student communities across the country, and this Maintenance Technician role in Tempe sits at the center of keeping one of those assets performing at its physical best.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Day to day, you're moving through service requests, preventative maintenance tasks, and curb appeal walkthroughs. In Tempe, that means pool chemistry logs are not optional paperwork. With summer temperatures routinely pushing past 110 degrees, the pool is a heavily used amenity and the chemical records need to be accurate and current. HVAC is similarly non-negotiable. The ability to troubleshoot and repair HVAC systems independently matters here more than it would in a moderate climate.

Turn season is where student housing separates from conventional apartments. Units flip in a compressed cycle, and you'll be working with the maintenance team to schedule and execute make-ready work at volume. A clean punch list process and solid communication with the Maintenance Supervisor keeps that from becoming chaos. The rest of the year involves preventative maintenance schedules, equipment upkeep per manufacturer specs, and keeping grounds, breezeways, and common areas in good shape.

You'll also participate in on-call rotation. That's the honest part of the job that doesn't always get front-billed. For the right candidate, it's manageable. For someone who hasn't done rotating emergency coverage before, it's worth knowing upfront.

What PeakMade Is Looking For

  • At least one year of maintenance experience, apartment industry preferred
  • Ability to troubleshoot and repair HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and appliances
  • EPA Type I and II certification preferred
  • Must live within 30 miles of the property and have reliable transportation
  • Availability for a varied schedule including weekends, holidays, and on-call rotation
  • Ability to lift up to 50 pounds, work at heights on ladders, and perform physical tasks outdoors in extreme temperatures
  • Candidates should bring their own hand tools
  • Additional certifications as required by local, state, or federal law

PeakMade offers technical training and the opportunity to earn HVAC and CPO certifications through the company, which is a real differentiator for technicians looking to build credentials. A tech who comes in with strong hands-on skills and adds those certifications has a clear path toward a Maintenance Supervisor role. The company also offers paid parental leave, PTO plus two additional wellbeing days, 401(k) match, and monthly renewal bonuses.

Strong candidates for this specific role will already be comfortable working with pool systems and have some HVAC diagnostic experience. Given the Tempe climate and the student housing turn cycle, those two skill areas will get tested quickly and often.

workable_6001565.rewritten_description:
What You'll Actually Do

Channel Island Apartments is a 152-unit affordable housing community in Oxnard, and this role sits at the intersection of compliance and leasing. The Occupancy Specialist owns the full application cycle: screening income-eligible households against HUD and LIHTC regulatory requirements, processing move-ins, and completing annual and interim recertifications on time and in full. A missed recertification or a documentation gap on a tax credit file isn't a minor inconvenience here. It's a compliance event. So the person in this seat needs to be organized, detail-oriented, and comfortable working within the specific rules that govern affordable housing occupancy.

Beyond the file work, you're also the frontline leasing presence. That means conducting property tours, following up on leads, monitoring local market conditions, and contributing to marketing strategies that keep occupancy where it needs to be. You'll coordinate with the property manager and maintenance team on move-in readiness and unit inspections, and you'll handle resident concerns with the kind of professionalism that keeps a community stable. Delinquency management is part of the picture too, including rent collection and follow-up consistent with company procedures.

IPG is a national operator with a portfolio of over 40 multifamily communities and 111 mobile home locations across 13 states, so there's real infrastructure behind this role. Proficiency in Yardi or comparable property management software is expected from day one.

What You Bring

  • At least one year of leasing or occupancy experience in property management
  • Bilingual fluency in English and Spanish (this is a hard requirement, not a preference)
  • Familiarity with LIHTC and Section 8 program requirements, or a demonstrated ability to get up to speed quickly
  • Experience with delinquency tracking and rent collection processes
  • Comfort with property management platforms such as Yardi, Rent Cafe, or Blue Moon
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to interact clearly with regulatory agencies and housing authorities
  • Solid time management and the discipline to keep recertification timelines on track across a 152-unit community

Context Worth Knowing

Affordable housing occupancy roles carry a compliance burden that market-rate leasing positions don't. LIHTC files require income verification, asset documentation, and student status review at every certification. HUD programs add their own audit trail requirements. Candidates who've only worked conventional leasing will need to invest real time learning the regulatory side. Those who already understand tax credit compliance will be productive much faster and will likely find this role a strong foundation for a compliance coordinator or property manager position within an affordable housing portfolio. The $24 to $28 hourly range reflects the specialized nature of the work, and the Monday through Friday, 8 to 5 schedule is a genuine quality-of-life advantage compared to many leasing roles.

Capri North and South is an AIR Communities property in Las Vegas, and this leasing consultant role is fundamentally a sales position with a customer service backbone. Your job is to drive occupancy by converting traffic into signed leases. That means working AIR's sales process start to finish: responding promptly to inquiries, scheduling and conducting tours, and closing. Follow-up discipline matters here. Prospects who don't hear back quickly move on, and every missed connection is a missed lease.

Commission structure has multiple tiers, so your earnings aren't flat. Higher-rent units, longer lease terms (18 months or more beats the standard 12), and exceeding monthly goals each unlock additional commission percentages on top of the $20/hour base. If you're consistently closing, those layers add up fast. If you're just hitting quota, you're leaving money on the table.

Beyond your home property, you'll provide leasing support across AIR's portfolio as needed. That means your performance metrics don't live in a vacuum. You're part of a broader operation where occupancy, traffic-to-lease conversion, and delinquency prevention all connect. You'll also contribute to community marketing efforts and operate within Fair Housing guidelines at every step.

What You Bring

  • At least one year of sales or customer service experience with measurable goal achievement. Property management background is a plus, but hospitality, retail, and restaurant experience translate well.
  • A track record of following a defined sales process, not just winging it.
  • Schedule flexibility, including weekends. Leasing offices don't close on Saturdays.
  • Reliable transportation and strong English communication skills, written and verbal.
  • Genuine ability to read a prospect and adapt your pitch to what they actually need in a home.

The Bigger Picture

Las Vegas is a high-velocity rental market. Renter mobility is above average, which means traffic can be strong but conversion windows are short. The candidates who perform best in this type of environment treat every tour as a one-shot opportunity. They know their floor plans cold, they understand what makes each unit worth its rent premium, and they close without being pushy. Average leasing consultants wait for prospects to decide. Strong ones guide the decision.

AIR offers a 25% rent discount at any AIR community, which means you could live onsite and eliminate your commute entirely. The company also offers a potential winter break after peak season with benefits intact, a 401(k) with up to 6% employer match, and up to 16 weeks of paid parental leave. Career-wise, strong leasing consultants at companies like AIR typically move into assistant manager and property manager roles. The skills you build here, closing under pressure, managing resident relationships, and tracking your own performance metrics, carry directly into those next steps.

greenhouse_4341027009.title: Front Door Waste Technician-Cortland Sunbury Ridge
greenhouse_4341027009.rewritten_description:
Valet trash is one of those amenity services that residents notice immediately when it goes wrong and barely think about when it goes right. The Front Door Waste Technician at Cortland's Sunbury Ridge community in Columbus is the person who keeps it invisible in the best possible way: routes completed consistently, common areas clean, and residents who never have to wonder whether their bag got picked up.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Each shift, you'll walk the property collecting waste bags from resident doorsteps, transferring them into leak-proof carts and then into the designated vehicle for disposal at onsite compactors or containers. The route covers the full community, including stairwells, and you'll also clear trash from dog waste stations, pool areas, mail kiosks, parking lots, and other shared spaces. When there's a spill or debris near a compactor, you're the one who handles it before it becomes a bigger problem.

Prohibited or improperly disposed waste gets flagged and addressed according to company protocol, and you'll document your work through a mobile app, logging start and end times and capturing photos as needed. Cortland operates with clear productivity standards, so completing routes efficiently and on schedule matters.

You'll interact with residents, leasing staff, and management throughout your shifts. That contact is brief but meaningful. A friendly, professional presence on the property reinforces the resident experience that Cortland builds its reputation around.

What You Bring to the Role

  • At least one year of experience in waste services or a customer-facing role
  • Working knowledge of EPA and OSHA regulations related to waste handling
  • Physical ability to climb stairs, walk extended distances, and lift up to 50 lbs
  • Comfort working outdoors in variable weather and tolerating strong odors
  • A valid Class E driver's license and ability to drive locally as needed
  • A personal smartphone (Android 2.2+ or iPhone iOS 4.3+) with an active data plan for app-based reporting
  • A high school diploma or equivalent is preferred
  • Bilingual ability is a plus

The Bigger Picture

Cortland is a vertically integrated owner and operator ranked among the top ten multifamily firms in the country. That structure means decisions about how a property looks and functions are made internally, and the people doing the daily work are genuinely part of how the company delivers on its resident-centric model. Sunbury Ridge is one community in a national portfolio, but how it's maintained day to day reflects directly on what Cortland promises residents.

Candidates who stand out in this kind of role tend to be self-directed on route and don't need supervision to stay on pace. They also understand that regular contact with residents, even quick exchanges at the door, is part of the job. The combination of physical reliability and consistent professionalism is what makes the difference between someone who fills the role and someone who owns it.

greenhouse_5196987007.title: Assistant Property Manager
greenhouse_5196987007.rewritten_description:
Lincoln Property Company runs a substantial commercial portfolio, and this Assistant Property Manager role sits at the intersection of tenant relations, financial reporting, and day-to-day operations. The skills that get used hardest here are financial literacy, lease administration, and vendor management. If you're comfortable reading a management agreement, understanding CAM reconciliation methodology, and tracking invoice approvals against authorization limits, this role will feel like natural territory.

The Financial and Lease Side

A meaningful portion of this role lives in the numbers. You'll support monthly reporting packages and budget deliverables, which means you need to understand what you're looking at: operating expenses, variance explanations, and the kind of basic financial analysis that turns raw data into a coherent picture for a client. CAM and OpEx reconciliations require close coordination with the accounting team, and the accuracy of that work has direct implications for tenant billing and client trust. Lease administration runs parallel to this: setup, amendments, move-in and move-out documentation, and keeping the applicable systems current. Commercial leases carry real financial weight, and keeping lease data clean is not a back-office afterthought.

Operations and Tenant Management

On the operational side, you'll coordinate tenant needs with building staff and vendors, making sure response times and outcomes stay within the bounds of policy and lease obligations. Vendor invoice review, procurement support, and participation in bidding processes round out the daily workload. You'll also participate in property inspections and walk-throughs alongside the Property Manager and tenant improvement teams, so comfort on a commercial property floor plate is part of the job. Emergency response planning and drill participation are also in scope.

This is an in-office, Dallas-based role with regular travel to assigned properties. Remote work isn't available.

What Strong Candidates Bring

  • A bachelor's degree or equivalent combination of experience and coursework
  • One to two years of related experience, ideally in commercial office, retail, or industrial property
  • Intermediate to advanced Microsoft Office skills; familiarity with AP and CMMS platforms is a real advantage
  • Comfort with financial terms and intermediate calculations, including percentages and basic variance analysis
  • Clear written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to keep difficult conversations constructive
  • Organizational discipline to manage multiple deliverables across a property or small portfolio

The candidates who stand out in commercial APM roles typically know how to read a lease abstract and connect what it says to what gets billed. CAM rec season separates people who understand cost pools and gross-up provisions from those who are just entering data. Coming in with that baseline puts you ahead of the curve on Lincoln's reporting cycle.

Lincoln Property Company offers a benefits package covering medical, dental, and vision coverage, life and AD&D insurance, a 401(k) plan, flexible time off, paid sick leave, and company-paid holidays. Additional voluntary benefits may vary by location.

greenhouse_6130333004.title: Business Manager, Property Operations
greenhouse_6130333004.rewritten_description:
The delinquency report lands in your inbox at 8 a.m., two properties are flagging collections issues, and a regional portfolio manager needs updated capex tracking before the afternoon call. That's a Tuesday.

Asset Living, one of the NMHC top 50 management firms and an IREM Accredited Management Organization, is hiring a Business Manager, Property Operations to support a regional portfolio out of Reno, Nevada. Founded in 1986, Asset Living operates across multifamily, affordable housing, build-to-rent, student housing, and single-family rental divisions. This is a third-party management environment, which means client expectations, jurisdictional compliance, and operational consistency across multiple sites are all live concerns every week.

What the Role Covers

Occupancy management is a core part of the work. You'll support retention strategies and renewal workflows, handle resident escalations, and oversee tenant-based voucher administration and its associated compliance requirements. On the maintenance side, you'll monitor service quality, track work order completion, and partner with site teams on preventive maintenance schedules to keep resident satisfaction from eroding.

The financial piece carries real weight here. You'll own delinquency oversight and rent recovery workflows, ensure move-out charges and timelines meet jurisdictional requirements, track capex against approved budgets, and manage the full invoice cycle from PO matching through vendor payment coordination with Accounts Payable. Compliance runs through every function: federal, state, and local regulations, internal Asset Living standards, lease enforcement, evictions, and coordination with outside counsel when disputes escalate.

You'll work closely with Regional Portfolio Managers, Community Managers, and leasing teams to drive KPIs across the assigned portfolio. That means pulling operational and financial data, identifying trends before they become problems, and keeping execution consistent across properties that may differ in asset class or regulatory environment.

What You Bring

  • Minimum three years of multifamily property management, operations, or asset management experience
  • Proficiency in Yardi, RealPage, MRI, or a comparable property management platform
  • Working knowledge of Microsoft Office and Google Workspace
  • Demonstrated understanding of leasing operations, financial controls, and regulatory compliance
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills; bilingual Spanish/English preferred
  • High school diploma required; bachelor's degree in business, real estate, or a related field preferred
  • Must reside in Reno, Nevada; approximately 10% travel for property visits and internal meetings

The candidates who stand out in roles like this one tend to be operationally fluent across both the numbers and the compliance side. Knowing how to read a T-12 matters, but so does understanding what happens when a jurisdictional notice deadline gets missed. This role sits at that intersection, and comfort in both areas separates strong performers from candidates who lean only one direction.

What You'll Actually Do

The Assistant Manager at Olympus at Memorial sits at the intersection of financial accountability and daily operations. On any given morning, you're verifying that all rent receipts from the prior day cleared properly, reviewing delinquency to flag anything that needs a notice or a call, and cross-checking move-out account statements before they go out. Accuracy here matters. A misposted payment or a late deposit doesn't just create a bookkeeping headache. It affects the property's cash position and your T-12 picture.

Beyond the ledger, you're the operational backbone when the Property Manager is out. That means handling resident complaints before they escalate, inspecting make-ready units ahead of move-ins, and jumping into leasing traffic when the floor needs coverage. Olympus at Memorial expects you to know the submarket too. New construction in the Memorial corridor, hiring trends from nearby employers, concession activity at competing communities. That market awareness directly informs how you position the property on any given week.

Resident retention is part of the job description here, not an afterthought. You'll participate in community events and contribute to renewal efforts, which means the role touches occupancy and renewal rates in a real, measurable way. The base pay runs $22 to $23 per hour, with monthly renewal incentives and quarterly bonuses layered on top.

What You Bring

  • Prior onsite experience as an Assistant Manager or a cross-trained Leasing Consultant
  • Comfort with RealPage, Knock, or Onesite (strongly preferred)
  • Solid grasp of rent collection procedures, including daily deposit requirements
  • Ability to assess move-out conditions and produce accurate final account statements
  • Availability Monday through Friday, 9 AM to 6 PM, with flexibility for the first weekend of each month and occasional after-hours events

greenhouse_8097200.title: Leasing Consultant
greenhouse_8097200.rewritten_description:
Weinstein Properties has been family-owned and operated for over 70 years, managing more than 60 apartment communities across Virginia, North Carolina, Texas, Tennessee, and Georgia. Their Bexley Summerhill community in Atlanta's Summerhill neighborhood is looking for a Leasing Consultant, and the way they've written this posting tells you something useful: they're not screening for a resume, they're screening for a person.

That's worth taking seriously. Weinstein trains from the ground up, and a meaningful number of their current leaders started exactly where this role begins. The company's hands-on ownership model means decisions happen closer to the property level than at most large institutional operators, and that tends to create more visible career paths for people who perform well on-site.

The role itself covers the full breadth of leasing work. You'll be the first contact for prospects, walking them through the community, handling follow-up, and working toward move-in goals that come with monthly bonuses on top of your base hourly rate and quarterly bonuses. But it doesn't stop at sales. You'll handle resident concerns, help maintain the property's appearance, and pitch in on administrative tasks. On a given day, you might greet a walk-in, respond to a maintenance-related complaint, prep a unit for a showing, and close out paperwork before end of shift. The role rewards people who can shift gears without losing momentum.

The schedule runs weekdays 9 to 6, with Saturdays 9 to 5 shared on a team rotation. Sundays are off. You should expect occasional evening or weekend commitments around resident events or weather-related needs. That's part of on-site life and worth knowing upfront.

What separates strong candidates here is less about prior leasing knowledge and more about how they handle the parts of the job that aren't glamorous. Anyone can be warm and engaging when a tour is going well. The people who advance are the ones who stay organized under interruption, follow through on small tasks without being reminded, and genuinely enjoy solving problems for residents who are frustrated. Summerhill is a growing neighborhood, which means traffic will likely include a mix of first-time renters and people relocating to Atlanta, so comfort with varied audiences matters.

What Weinstein is looking for

  • Strong verbal and written communication skills
  • A customer-first approach, especially when situations are difficult
  • Comfort with a role that blends sales, service, and administrative work
  • Reliability and a collaborative attitude on a small on-site team
  • Goal orientation and the drive to meet leasing targets
  • Prior leasing experience is welcome but not required

Starting pay is $20 per hour, increasing with experience, plus the bonus structure noted above. Weinstein is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

greenhouse_5200011007.rewritten_description:
A prospect walks in on a Saturday afternoon, having driven by the community twice before finally stopping. Within the first few minutes of that conversation, you'll qualify their interest, match them to an available floor plan, and start building the kind of trust that turns a tour into a signed lease. That's the core of this role.

What This Role Covers

MG Properties is hiring a Leasing Consultant for Santa Rosa Apartments in Wildomar, CA. With more than 30 years operating apartment communities across the Western U.S., MG Properties manages properties with a clear emphasis on resident experience and internal growth. This position sits at the front line of both.

Day to day, you'll greet and qualify prospective residents, guide them through tours, prepare leases, and oversee signings. You'll coordinate with the maintenance team to make sure new residents move in without friction, and you'll keep rental files accurate and current. When residents have questions, complaints, or maintenance concerns, you handle those interactions professionally and see them through to resolution. Monthly administrative tasks and data entry into the property management system are part of the rhythm as well.

Occupancy is the measurable outcome of this work. Every leasing interaction, follow-up call, and move-in coordination either supports or erodes it. You'll be expected to understand that connection and treat it as a professional standard, not just a company metric.

What You Bring and What You'll Build

This role requires strong sales instincts paired with genuine customer service ability. You need to be comfortable qualifying applicants thoroughly, managing paperwork accurately, and communicating clearly with both prospects and current residents. At least one year of property management experience is preferred, and professional etiquette is non-negotiable given the volume and variety of resident interactions.

What the role builds is equally worth noting. Leasing Consultants at companies that promote from within (MG Properties explicitly does) tend to move into Assistant Manager roles once they've demonstrated lease-up competency, administrative accuracy, and the ability to handle resident relations without escalation. The combination of sales performance data and file management discipline you develop here translates directly into the skills property management companies look for when hiring for their next tier.

greenhouse_8654361002.title: Maintenance Technician
greenhouse_8654361002.rewritten_description:
Single-family rental management operates differently from traditional multifamily. There's no central leasing office, no on-site team to call, and properties are spread across neighborhoods rather than clustered in one building. That model works well for investors, but it puts real demand on the maintenance technicians who keep those homes in good shape. This role at Roofstock sits squarely in that world.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Most days, you're moving between properties across the Tampa area, working from a company vehicle with a gas card. Your schedule is structured around service orders, make-readies, and property inspections rather than a fixed site. You'll handle HVAC, plumbing, and electrical repairs across the portfolio, and you'll also prepare vacant homes for incoming residents, which means completing turns efficiently and to a consistent standard.

Inspections are a regular part of the job too. Move-in and move-out walkthroughs, onboarding audits for newly acquired properties, and quality checks on work completed by outside vendors. That last piece matters more than it sounds. When a third-party contractor finishes a job, you're the one verifying it was done right before the company signs off. That requires both technical knowledge and the judgment to push back when something doesn't meet the mark.

Work orders come through a mobile app, and you'll use it throughout the day to log progress, communicate updates, and post legal notices as needed. If you're the type who prefers pen and paper and a single fixed location, this setup will feel uncomfortable. If you're organized, self-directed, and comfortable with digital tools, it fits naturally.

Who Tends to Succeed Here

The schedule is genuinely different from most maintenance roles: full-time hours, no on-call rotation, no weekends. That's a real quality-of-life difference, and it attracts technicians who've burned out on the traditional emergency-response model. What the role trades in return is independence. You're not working alongside a maintenance supervisor or a team. You're the one making judgment calls in the field.

  • HVAC Type II Certification is required; Universal Certification is preferred and worth having
  • Valid driver's license, since the vehicle and travel are central to the role
  • Comfort troubleshooting across trades, not just one specialty
  • High school diploma or GED
  • Ability to lift up to 50 lbs, climb, bend, and work in both indoor and outdoor conditions
  • U.S. work authorization (no visa sponsorship available)

Pay runs $25 to $30 per hour depending on experience, licensure, and location. Strong candidates bring a track record across multiple trade types, not just HVAC, because a scattered residential portfolio generates a wide variety of repair needs on any given day. The technicians who thrive here are the ones who can close out five different work orders in five different neighborhoods and still do each one carefully.

What the Role Actually Covers

You'll conduct community and amenity tours, field prospect and resident inquiries, and assist with social media and local marketing outreach. On the administrative side, expect package logging, office and amenity upkeep, maintenance request coordination, and after-hours lockout coverage on rotation. Availability during summer and Turn is a real requirement here, not a formality. Turn at a student property is controlled chaos at best. greenhouse_4339727009.title: Assistant Community Manager of Permanent Supportive Housing (Immanuel Sobrato)
greenhouse_4339727009.rewritten_description:
Affordable housing management carries compliance weight that market-rate property work typically doesn't. At a property like Immanuel Sobrato, a permanent supportive housing community in San Jose, that means layering HUD, Tax Credit, and welfare exemption requirements on top of standard daily operations. MidPen Housing has been doing exactly this work since 1970, and this assistant-level role sits directly inside that operational reality.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

The Assistant Community Manager here supports the full operating cycle of a permanent supportive housing property. On any given day, that means scheduling income verification appointments, processing lease agreements, managing the waitlist, and helping residents understand emergency preparedness procedures. Turnover work involves scheduling vacancies, preparing and monitoring turn forms, and coordinating with facilities staff to keep work orders moving. Rent collection, security deposit processing, petty cash logs, and bank deposit prep also fall within this role's scope.

Compliance is a meaningful part of the job. You'll assist with annual recertifications, welfare exemption documentation, and preparation for Management and Occupancy Reviews (MOR) and TCAC audits. File integrity matters here in a way that goes beyond the ordinary: resident files contain sensitive information, and maintaining confidentiality under audit conditions is a baseline expectation, not an occasional task.

The role also requires real relationship management. MidPen's property teams work closely with onsite Resident Services staff, local law enforcement, and community partners. At a permanent supportive housing property, those relationships carry more operational weight than at a standard affordable or market-rate community.

What MidPen Is Looking For

  • High school diploma or GED with at least one year of residential property management, customer service, or administrative experience (or an equivalent combination)
  • Proficiency in MS Office; RealPage experience is a plus
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with genuine attention to detail
  • Ability to work independently and stay organized across multiple compliance and operational tracks
  • Alignment with MidPen's mission around affordable housing and resident stability

Candidates who tend to stand out in roles like this have some prior exposure to income-restricted housing, even at the administrative level. Understanding the difference between a TCAC review and a standard lease audit, or knowing why recertification timelines matter, shortens the learning curve considerably. That said, MidPen explicitly considers equivalent experience, so strong administrative or customer service backgrounds from adjacent fields are worth presenting clearly.

The pay range is $23.27 to $26.18 per hour, based on experience. MidPen offers health, dental, vision, life, and disability insurance, a 403(b) retirement plan, paid parental leave, tuition reimbursement, FSA options, and an EAP program, among other benefits.

greenhouse_7822181003.title: Groundskeeper (Lease Up)
greenhouse_7822181003.rewritten_description:
The morning starts before most residents have poured their first cup of coffee. You're doing a walkthrough of the grounds, checking that the property looks exactly the way it should when the first person steps outside. On a lease-up community, that standard matters even more: every prospective resident who tours the property is forming a first impression, and curb appeal either supports or undercuts everything the leasing team says.

The Work Itself

This is a Groundskeeper role supporting a lease-up community for Prometheus Real Estate Group in Los Altos, California. The core of the job is maintaining the physical condition and cleanliness of the property: common areas, exteriors, landscaping details, trash, and anything that affects how the community looks and feels to the people who live there and those considering it. You'll work with some independence, managing your own daily tasks without needing step-by-step supervision, while staying responsive to resident needs and the expectations of a team that takes curb appeal seriously.

Customer service is genuinely part of this job. Residents notice the person maintaining their community, and how you engage with them shapes how they feel about where they live. On a lease-up property, that sense of pride in the community is still being built, and everyone on the maintenance and grounds team contributes to it.

The physical demands are real. The role requires regular lifting (up to 50 lbs occasionally), extended time on your feet, climbing, and repetitive physical tasks. Prior custodial or apartment experience is helpful but not required to be considered.

Compensation and Benefits

The pay range for this position runs from $21.75 to $23.25 per hour, and Prometheus layers in additional earning opportunities including a discretionary semi-annual bonus, standby and on-call premium pay, a lease-up bonus, and referral and training bonuses where applicable. The benefits package is notably strong for a grounds-level role:

greenhouse_4332782009.title: Assistant Community Manager
greenhouse_4332782009.location: Oasis at Southpark - 5355 Southpark Drive - Lake Charles, LA - 70607
greenhouse_4332782009.rewritten_description:
What You'll Actually Do

This role splits its time across two pretty different kinds of work, and you need to be comfortable with both. On the leasing side, you're fielding leads, running tours, walking prospects through applications, and working to hit occupancy goals. You're also managing renewals and thinking about resident retention, because a lease that doesn't renew is a turn that costs money and time.

On the financial side, you're handling rent collection, payment posting, ledger reviews, and delinquency follow-up. That means weekly calls to residents behind on rent, coordinating with the Community Manager on eviction procedures when it gets to that point, and making sure account records are clean before they go up the chain. If you're not comfortable with that side of the work, this role will be harder than it looks.

You'll also step into the lead role when the Community Manager is out. That's not a ceremonial title. It means the team looks to you, residents escalate to you, and you're the one keeping operations on track until they're back.

The schedule runs Monday through Friday, 9 to 6, with Saturdays from 10 to 4. One weekday off per week keeps it at 40 hours, but resident events and community needs can pull you in on evenings or weekends. That's the nature of on-site work.

What You Bring

  • At least two years of property management experience, with some time in an assistant manager role preferred
  • Comfort reading financial reports, catching billing errors, and making decisions with budget awareness
  • Leasing instincts: you know how to read a prospect, show a home, and close without being pushy
  • A valid driver's license
  • CALP accreditation is a plus, not a requirement
  • High school diploma or GED

Context Worth Knowing

Hawthorne Residential Partners manages communities across the Southeast and ranks among the top 50 largest multifamily operators in the country. The Oasis at Southpark sits in Lake Charles, Louisiana. This is a fee-managed portfolio where regional visibility matters, so your financial reporting and documentation need to be accurate and timely, not just close enough.

The career path here is real. Assistant Community Manager is a direct stepping stone to Community Manager, and Hawthorne has a formal development program to move people along that track. If you want that progression, the skill set you build here, reading a T-12, managing delinquency, running a team under pressure, carries directly into the next role.

Compensation includes hourly pay plus monthly leasing and renewal commissions and quarterly performance bonuses. Benefits include medical, dental, vision, 401k with match, paid time off including your birthday, pet insurance, and paid parental and adoption leave.

greenhouse_4339601009.title: Concierge- Luxury Highrise (M-F 4pm-12am)
greenhouse_4339601009.rewritten_description:
This role runs on interpersonal skill and situational awareness. You're reading a lobby full of residents, guests, and prospects all at once, deciding who needs a warm greeting, who needs a quick answer, and who needs to be politely redirected. At a luxury high-rise in Reston, that judgment call happens dozens of times per shift.

What This Role Actually Requires

Customer service is the core skill here, but the specific application matters. Luxury residential concierge work sits somewhere between hospitality and security. You're coordinating amenity reservations, managing loading dock and elevator bookings, fielding calls, and keeping the front desk area clean and organized. You're also doing daily building walks to catch maintenance items before residents notice them. The shift runs 4pm to midnight, Monday through Friday, which means you're covering the high-traffic evening hours when residents come home, guests arrive, and deliveries need to be managed.

Strong problem-solving matters more than most postings let on. Evening shifts don't have a full management team behind you. When something comes up, you handle it or you escalate it correctly. Either way, the decision is yours in the moment.

Qualifications Worth Noting

  • High school diploma or GED required
  • At least one year of concierge or high-end customer service experience preferred
  • Comfort with Microsoft Office, especially Outlook, Word, and Excel
  • Ability to work holidays and pick up additional shifts when needed
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Ability to work independently with minimal supervision

Working at Comstock

Comstock manages a growing residential portfolio, which means there's real room to move into leasing or property management roles over time. Concierge positions at Class A properties are a common entry point for people who want to build a career in residential property management. You're learning how a luxury building operates from the front lines, which is useful context if you move toward leasing, assistant management, or community management later.

The benefits package includes medical, dental, vision, 401k match, life insurance, parental leave, commuter benefits, free parking with EV charging, and a housing discount. Comstock also provides annual professional development funds. Pay for this position ranges from $18 to $22 per hour, depending on experience.

greenhouse_4340582009.title: Maintenance Technician - Part-Time
greenhouse_4340582009.rewritten_description:
It's 7:45 a.m. and a new resident moves in at noon. The apartment needs a final walk, a light bulb swapped, and the grounds outside the building need a quick pass before the leasing team starts showing the property. That's where this role lives.

The Work

Redstone Residential manages more than 38,000 beds across 20 states, operating as one of the country's largest third-party student housing managers while also growing a conventional multifamily portfolio. This part-time Maintenance Technician position sits at their Orem, Utah property and pays $15.00 per hour.

Day-to-day, the role centers on two things: curb appeal and turns. You'll keep common areas, hallways, the clubhouse, and building exteriors clean and presentable. You'll manage apartment turnovers, making sure each unit is in move-in-ready condition before a new resident takes the keys. Basic repairs, grounds maintenance, landscaping, pool upkeep, and trash removal all fall within scope. When something exceeds your bandwidth, you flag it to the Maintenance Supervisor or Property Manager so nothing slips.

Emergency response is part of the job. Redstone has defined policies and procedures for after-hours situations, and you're expected to follow them. Customer service matters here too. Resident interactions happen constantly, and how you handle them affects satisfaction scores and retention.

What the Role Requires

  • At least one year of relevant experience; property management background is a plus
  • Working knowledge of pool service and maintenance
  • Strong attention to detail and solid basic maintenance skills
  • Ability to lift a minimum of 75 lbs. and work 8 to 10 hour shifts on your feet
  • Genuine customer service instincts

Redstone offers a 401(k) plan with up to 6% matching, which is a real benefit for a part-time hourly position.

One practical note for candidates: student housing properties run on tighter turn cycles than conventional multifamily. At a Redstone community, the make-ready window between a student lease-end and the next move-in can be compressed to days rather than weeks. If you've worked turns under that kind of time pressure before, that experience will translate directly here and set you apart from candidates who haven't.

greenhouse_5376336008.title: Maintenance Technician - Brockford Place
greenhouse_5376336008.rewritten_description:
Multifamily maintenance is where technical skill and resident experience intersect most directly. A leaking faucet at 11pm, a unit that needs to be rent-ready in three days, a pool that has to pass inspection by Friday: the maintenance technician is the person the whole operation depends on to keep those things from becoming bigger problems. Sunrise Management is hiring for that role at Brockford Place in Sacramento, and the position suits someone who takes real ownership of a property rather than just working through a ticket queue.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

The core of the role covers the full range of hands-on maintenance: plumbing, basic electrical, HVAC, appliance repair, carpentry, painting, and pool upkeep. You'll keep common areas clean and presentable, manage curb appeal, and handle the make-ready process for vacant units with a target of three to five days from vacancy to rent-ready. Service requests need resolution within 24 hours, which means you'll need to prioritize quickly and communicate clearly when parts or scheduling push a timeline out.

Beyond reactive repairs, you'll work through monthly preventive maintenance checks covering lighting, fire safety, pool and spa systems, and life-safety hazards. You'll know where every shutoff lives on the property. You'll track tool and supply inventory, document vacant unit status, and assist with move-in and move-out inspections. On-call emergency coverage is part of the schedule, so flexibility on evenings and weekends is a real requirement, not a footnote.

What You Bring and Where This Can Lead

Sunrise is looking for one to two years of hands-on experience across the core trades, plus solid computer and mobile device skills since work orders and documentation run through software. Strong communication matters here: you're the face of the property for residents when something goes wrong, and how you handle a frustrated tenant during a repair visit shapes retention as much as the fix itself does.

  • 1 to 2 years of experience in plumbing, electrical, HVAC, carpentry, or painting
  • Comfortable using a mobile device for work order management
  • Able to work a flexible schedule including on-call emergency response
  • Familiarity with MSDS documentation and safety compliance practices
  • Strong communication skills and the ability to work independently with minimal supervision

Technicians who build depth across trades and develop strong documentation habits tend to move into lead tech or maintenance supervisor roles within two to three years. From there, the path to a regional maintenance director position or facilities management role opens up, especially at a company with a growing portfolio. The skills you compound here, specifically preventive maintenance planning, resident communication, and compliance documentation, are exactly what separates candidates for those senior roles. The pay range is $22 to $24 per hour depending on experience, with medical, dental, and vision coverage, FSA, company-paid life insurance, and paid time off.

workable_5961835.title: Part-Time Leasing Consultant
workable_5961835.rewritten_description:
Leasing is a sales job. The consultants who outperform their peers on traffic-to-lease ratios don't do it by accident. They qualify fast, follow up relentlessly, and close with urgency. PeakMade Real Estate is hiring a part-time Leasing Consultant for their East Lansing community, and the skill set they're prioritizing is exactly what you'd expect from a company that tracks conversion metrics closely.

The Skills This Role Runs On

Multi-touch outreach is the engine here. Calls, emails, texts, timed right and personalized. A prospect who tours on Saturday and hears nothing by Monday morning is a lost lease. Strong candidates will have a documented history of follow-up discipline, not just a general sense that they're good with people. CRM fluency matters too. PeakMade works within platforms like Yardi, Entrata, or RealPage, and clean prospect data is how you track pipeline and identify where leads are stalling. If you've ever looked at your conversion funnel and asked why a stage is leaking, you'll fit the mindset here.

The tour itself is a sales conversation, not a walkthrough. Identifying what a prospect actually needs, creating urgency around availability, and handling objections before they harden into hesitation. These are teachable skills, but PeakMade wants at least one year of demonstrated leasing or sales experience before day one.

What You'll Own

  • Converting inbound and outbound leads across phone, digital, and in-person channels
  • Delivering tours that move prospects toward a decision
  • Maintaining current knowledge of pricing, unit availability, and competing properties
  • Accurate lease paperwork, deposit collection, and CRM data entry
  • Supporting move-in and move-out events and contributing to the annual turn process
  • Assisting with market surveys to keep competitive positioning sharp

This is a commission-eligible position, which means your earning potential tracks directly to your close rate. Occupancy targets are real, and the expectation is that you hit them and push past them.

The East Lansing Context

East Lansing is a student-housing market with a pronounced leasing cycle tied to Michigan State's academic calendar. Traffic spikes early, and the consultants who build their pipeline in the fall and winter are the ones celebrating strong occupancy numbers by spring. Understanding that seasonal urgency, and knowing how to communicate it honestly to prospects, is a real competitive edge in this market. Availability windows are tight, and hesitant prospects need accurate information quickly, not pressure tactics.

PeakMade pairs this role with housing discounts (which vary by community), a 401(k) match, and internal development opportunities for those who want to grow toward a full-time or senior leasing position. The part-time schedule includes weekends and peak leasing hours, which is standard in student housing and worth factoring into your decision. Availability during high-traffic periods is when this role has the most impact.

Who You Are: Our highest-performing Leasing Consultants don’t just meet goals. At our core, how we work matters just as much as what we achieve. In this role, success means living our standards every day: Build trust fast through consistent follow-up and clear communication Create standout experiences that turn tours into leases Take ownership of every lead, every follow-up, and every result Execute the basics flawlessly—speed, accuracy, and preparation Continuously improve and refine your sales approach What You’ll Do: Sales & Leasing Convert leads into leases through phone, online, and in-person interactions Deliver high-impact tours that identify needs, create urgency, and close Proactively follow up and nurture leads to maximize conversion Maintain strong knowledge of pricing, availability, and competitors Achieve and exceed community leasing goals and occupancy targets Execute strategies that drive traffic, increase qualified leads, and maximize revenue Respond to leads quickly with a sales first mindset Resident Experience Provide excellent customer service and serve as an example to your team as a representative of Peak & your community Build rapport quickly and tailor the experience to each prospect Support resident satisfaction to drive renewals and referrals Community Operations Support Complete lease paperwork accurately and collect deposits Maintain CRM accuracy and prospect data Support office presentation and model readiness Assist in performance of annual turn process Maintain thorough product knowledge of the property and competition Assist with market serveys as needed Perform various administrative tasks Assist with all move out and move in events as well as collect deposits and/or fees associated with move in. workable_6001938.title: Floating Leasing Consultant
workable_6001938.rewritten_description:
It's 10 a.m. on a Saturday and you're pulling into a property you've only been to twice before. The model needs a quick check, there's a tour in 45 minutes, and the leasing office at your home site just texted asking for a renewal packet. That's a floating consultant's morning.

The Role

CommonPlace is hiring a Floating Leasing Consultant to cover multiple communities across Charlotte. This isn't a single-site position where you get comfortable with one floor plan and one comp set. You're moving between properties, stepping into different leasing offices, and expected to perform at the same level regardless of which site you're standing in. The pay runs $24 to $25 per hour plus commission, and benefits include medical, dental, vision, life insurance, short and long-term disability, and a 401k, along with paid vacation, sick time, and volunteer time.

The core of the job is traffic and conversion. You'll greet prospects, conduct tours, walk people through applications and screenings, collect deposits, execute lease agreements, and get residents to the move-in finish line with their files clean and their renter's insurance confirmed. Renewals are part of the job too: preparing documents, sitting down with residents, and keeping occupancy from bleeding out the back door.

Beyond the leasing cycle itself, you'll monitor curb appeal and make-ready readiness in coordination with maintenance, stay current on the local comp set, and keep digital lead sources active through social media, listing platforms, and property websites. Response time on leads matters here. Speed and follow-through are what separate a good leasing consultant from one who just shows units.

What CommonPlace Is Looking For

  • Prior leasing experience preferred; customer service or sales background considered
  • Comfortable with Microsoft Office; OneSite or AppFolio experience is a plus
  • Strong written and verbal communication
  • Weekend availability is required
  • Valid driver's license, current insurance, and reliable transportation (you will be driving between sites regularly)
  • Ability to stand, walk, and move through properties for extended periods

The floating format is genuinely useful for consultants who want to build toward an assistant manager or property manager role. Exposure to multiple sites, multiple rent rolls, and different lease-up or stabilized scenarios gives you a broader read on operations than a single-site role typically allows. If you're early in your PM career and want to accelerate, this kind of multi-property visibility is hard to replicate otherwise.

Background check and E-Verify required. CommonPlace is an equal opportunity employer.

greenhouse_5375406008.title: Assistant Maintenance Manager - Navy Yard - $2,500 Sign-On Bonus
greenhouse_5375406008.rewritten_description:
Asset Preservation at a Bozzuto Community in Navy Yard

Bozzuto runs some of the more prominent Class A communities in the Mid-Atlantic, and their Navy Yard property sits in one of DC's most active residential corridors. An Assistant Maintenance Manager role here means you're not just fixing things. You're running a program: turns, preventative maintenance schedules, emergency response, and vendor oversight, all while keeping the building's systems and finishes at the standard a Bozzuto lease commands.

The $2,500 sign-on bonus reflects real competition for credentialed trades talent in this market. DC proper has a thin bench of candidates who can competently handle complex mechanical systems alongside the resident-facing side of the job. If you've got the certs and the supervisory experience, that's a combination worth paying for.

What the Role Actually Covers

Day to day, you're managing service ticket completion with the kind of follow-through residents notice, and the kind that protects renewal rates. Make-readies need to move on schedule so units can be leased without delay. Beyond turns, you're running the preventative maintenance program that keeps the building's systems from becoming expensive emergencies. Bozzuto places real emphasis on "preserve and protect," which in practice means you're thinking about asset value every time you walk the property.

On the technical side, the role requires hands-on proficiency across HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and appliance repair. Familiarity with more complex mechanical systems, central plant, boilers, chillers, split systems, is a meaningful differentiator for candidates. Basic carpentry, drywall, and paint round out the punch list work. You'll also manage grounds upkeep, snow removal, and general common area cleanliness, code and OSHA compliance, and you'll carry a rotation on the emergency on-call schedule.

What Strong Candidates Bring

  • 5 or more years in trades, facilities, or residential building maintenance
  • HVAC, EPA, and/or NAPE certification (required, not preferred)
  • Supervisory experience and the ability to hold a team accountable without micromanaging
  • Working knowledge of OSHA, MSDS, and risk management practices
  • Comfort with technology platforms and basic Microsoft Office proficiency
  • Physical capability to lift 25 to 50 pounds regularly and work in varying outdoor conditions

The candidates who thrive in this kind of role at a Bozzuto property tend to be the ones who take the building personally. They know every mechanical room, they track their PM schedule without being reminded, and they communicate with residents like adults. The supervisory piece matters too: you're a player-coach here, and the team will follow your lead on standards and professionalism.

Compensation runs $66,560 to $69,160 annually, plus bonus eligibility and a benefits package that includes medical, dental, and vision coverage, 20 days of paid time off, a 401k with company match, and tuition reimbursement.

At Olympus Las Colinas, the Assistant Manager sits at the intersection of resident experience and property financials. On any given day, that means posting rent, reconciling deposits before bank close, and reviewing move-out condition reports to get final account statements out accurately and on time. Delinquency doesn't wait, and neither does this role.

You'll keep resident files current, handle confidential records with care, and make sure every dollar collected hits the operations system correctly. When the Property Manager is out, you run the show. That includes fielding resident complaints, coordinating with the leasing team, walking make-ready units before move-in to catch punch list items, and keeping an eye on what's happening in the Las Colinas submarket: new lease-up activity nearby, competing concessions, hiring trends that drive renter demand in the area.

You'll also step into a leasing support role when traffic picks up. Showing units, supporting retention efforts, and participating in community events are part of the job, not exceptions to it. greenhouse_8653897002.title: Communications Associate
greenhouse_8653897002.rewritten_description:
What You'll Actually Do

Scion operates student housing communities across the country, and this role sits at the intersection of resident relations, reputation management, and cross-functional communication at the corporate level. As a Communications Associate based out of Scion's Chicago headquarters, you'll handle inbound contacts from residents and guarantors across phone, email, chat, and social channels. That includes everything from routine questions to sensitive, high-stakes complaints that require coordination with legal or operations leadership before you respond.

A significant portion of the work involves managing online review responses across multiple platforms, which means you're not just answering residents directly. You're shaping how Scion's communities appear publicly to prospective residents and their families. You'll also work alongside on-site teams to build their capacity in reputation management, review strategy, and proactive resident engagement, including tools like Review Harvest and Entrata. When incidents or operational disruptions hit a community, you'll help coordinate resident communications so that messaging stays consistent and on-brand under pressure.

Beyond individual interactions, you'll track feedback patterns, flag recurring themes, and contribute to the internal resources that keep communication consistent: templates, FAQs, and response guidelines. The documentation side of this role is real. You'll maintain records in a reputation tracker and help inform the broader strategy based on what you're hearing from residents day to day.

What You Bring

  • A bachelor's degree in Communications, Marketing, Hospitality, or a related field, or comparable professional experience
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to write clearly under pressure and across different tones and audiences
  • Genuine comfort handling difficult conversations without becoming reactive or dismissive
  • Organizational discipline to manage multiple open cases, follow-up threads, and documentation tasks simultaneously
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office; familiarity with ClickUp or Entrata is a plus
  • The ability to work independently and coordinate across teams without needing heavy oversight

Context Worth Knowing

Student housing operates on a cycle that's distinct from conventional multifamily. Guarantors (typically parents) are often as engaged as the residents themselves, and that dual audience shapes how communications need to be framed. Lease-up seasons, move-in windows, and academic calendars create predictable spikes in volume and urgency. Someone who can anticipate those pressure points and help communities prepare for them will add real value in this role beyond just answering tickets.

The $58,000 to $60,000 salary range reflects a corporate associate-level position with a clear path toward senior communications, reputation strategy, or operations support roles as Scion's portfolio continues to grow. Hours are primarily standard business hours, though some evening and weekend coverage is expected to meet resident needs. The role is fully in-office at Scion's Chicago headquarters.

greenhouse_4333307009.title: Groundskeeper
greenhouse_4333307009.rewritten_description:
Curb appeal drives leasing traffic. Residents notice a well-kept community before they notice the unit finishes, the amenity package, or the rent. That's why the groundskeeper role carries more weight than its entry-level label suggests. At Hawthorne Residential Partners, this position in Jamestown, NC keeps the exterior of an apartment community looking like people actually care about it, because someone does.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Most of your day happens outside, and that's by design. You'll move through the property consistently, picking up debris, clearing sidewalks and breezeways, keeping parking lots clean, and making sure pet stations and compactor areas don't become eyesores. Pool decks, courtyards, grilling stations, and outdoor seating areas all fall within your scope. Light landscaping tasks like raking, weeding, and trimming come up regularly, directed by the maintenance team.

You'll also handle smaller but visible details: replacing burned-out exterior bulbs, doing touch-up painting on curbs and signposts, and keeping the maintenance shop and storage areas organized. When a unit turns, you may assist with light cleaning or debris removal to help the team move through make-readies faster. During seasonal shifts, you'll support storm prep and cleanup. And from time to time, you'll distribute resident communications door to door, which puts you in direct contact with the people who live there.

The schedule is Monday through Friday, 8 AM to 5 PM, with participation in an on-call rotation for after-hours needs.

Who Fits Well Here

A high school diploma or GED is required. A valid driver's license is required. Some background in yardwork or general facility upkeep is expected. Prior maintenance or repair experience is a plus, but Hawthorne has built a formal career path program specifically to develop people who don't yet have a full technical skill set.

What actually separates people who thrive in this role from those who don't isn't experience level. It's consistency. Showing up, completing the full walk of the property, not letting small things slide, and treating residents and coworkers with basic respect. A groundskeeper who does those things well tends to get noticed by maintenance leadership, and Hawthorne's internal career path formally supports movement from this role toward Maintenance Technician I and beyond.

  • High school diploma or GED required
  • Valid driver's license required
  • Some yardwork or facility maintenance experience expected

greenhouse_6132377004.title: Maintenance Technician
greenhouse_6132377004.rewritten_description:
Skills That Drive This Role

Maintenance work at a residential community runs on a specific combination of hands-on trade knowledge and people skills. At Stonebriar of Frisco Apartments, a Cottonwood Residential community in Frisco, TX, you'll use both every day. The technical side covers plumbing repairs, electrical troubleshooting, general carpentry, and HVAC diagnostics. The human side means showing up to a resident's door, explaining what you're doing, and leaving the unit better than you found it. If you hold EPA Type II or Universal certification, or a CPO cert, those credentials give you a head start. HVAC troubleshooting experience is genuinely useful here, not just a checkbox.

This is an entry-level position, which means Cottonwood isn't expecting a seasoned maintenance supervisor. They're looking for someone who learns quickly, communicates clearly in English (written and verbal), and can handle the physical demands of the job: lifting up to 50 lbs., working on ladders and scaffolding, and spending most of the day on your feet. A valid driver's license is required.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

A typical day moves between work orders and whatever comes up unexpectedly. You might start the morning running a make-ready punch list on a vacated unit, then shift to a plumbing call in the afternoon, then help with a grounds issue before the end of your shift. Evenings and weekends are part of the schedule, and on-call rotation means you'll occasionally respond to after-hours emergencies. You won't be handling those calls alone. The Service Manager provides backup and guidance, especially while you're still learning the property and the company's standards.

That on-call piece is worth being honest about. It's a real commitment, and it affects your schedule in ways that a standard 9-to-5 doesn't. For the right person, it's also where you build trust with residents fast. Showing up reliably during a leak or a lockout leaves a stronger impression than a dozen routine work orders.

What Makes Cottonwood a Particular Fit

Cottonwood Residential has positioned itself as a company that moves early on technology adoption. Their rollout of Self-Guided Tours is one example of how they approach the resident experience differently. For a maintenance tech, that context matters because it signals a company culture that values service delivery as a differentiator, not just a checkbox. Your work directly supports the experience residents have, from the condition of their units to how quickly problems get resolved.

The benefits package is worth noting for an entry-level role. Health, vision, dental, life, and disability coverage becomes available within the first 30 days. The company also offers a 401(k) with a match, an HSA match, 120 hours of paid time off in year one, and 10.5 paid holidays. That's a meaningful package at this level of the career path.

For technicians looking at where this role leads: strong performers in entry-level maintenance positions typically move into lead tech or Service Manager roles as they build certifications and property-specific experience. EPA Universal and CPO certifications, in particular, open doors across the industry and increase your value on any property, regardless of where your career takes you.
