greenhouse_5378381008.title: Leasing Consultant - Reserve at Hamburg
greenhouse_5378381008.rewritten_description:
Leasing is a volume game with a relationship core. At a 318-unit community like the Reserve at Hamburg, that tension is constant: you're expected to convert traffic into signed leases, but the way you get there is by actually listening to what a prospective resident needs and matching them to the right unit. Ackermann Group has been doing real estate development and property management in the Midwest since 1938, and they're hiring a full-time Leasing Consultant to join the on-site team in Lexington, KY.

What the Day Actually Looks Like

Most of your time splits between guest interactions and the administrative work that surrounds them. You'll greet prospects in person and over the phone, schedule and lead tours, and handle the full leasing paperwork trail: guest cards, applications, lease prep, and move-in documentation. Yardi Voyager and Rent Café are the preferred platforms here, so comfort with property management software matters.

Beyond the leasing desk, you'll do regular walk-throughs of units and common areas to confirm they're market-ready. That means picking up trash, tidying a unit before a showing, and flagging anything that needs maintenance attention. You're the first point of contact for resident service requests too, which means logging the need and routing it to the right person, quickly.

Rotating Saturdays are part of the schedule (9am to 4pm), and occasional after-hours resident events come with the role. That's worth knowing upfront. It's not constant, but it's real.

The commission structure ties to both new leases and renewals, so your earning potential has a direct connection to how well you convert traffic and retain residents. Understanding local market conditions well enough to position Hamburg against competing communities is part of how strong consultants earn that commission consistently.

What Ackermann Is Looking For

  • Prior customer service experience (required); leasing or sales background strongly preferred
  • Comfort with property management software, specifically Yardi Voyager, Rent Café, and CRM tools
  • Solid written and verbal communication, with the ability to build rapport quickly
  • Working knowledge of fair housing requirements and lease documentation standards
  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • Ability to work Monday through Friday, 9am to 6pm, plus rotating Saturdays

Ackermann offers medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401(k) with company match, paid time off including your birthday, an employee rent discount at any Ackermann community, and career development support.

One thing that separates a strong leasing consultant from an average one at a property this size: the ability to stay organized under traffic pressure without letting follow-up slip. Prospects who don't hear back within 24 hours often sign somewhere else. The consultants who track their pipeline carefully and follow through consistently are the ones whose close rates hold up month after month.
greenhouse_5378381008.description_text: About Ackermann Group: Since 1938, the Ackermann Group has a long history in real estate development and property management that has continued to grow and thrive in the Midwest region. Our guiding principles of collaboration, commitment to a personal approach, and delivering above expectations are paramount to who we are as an organization. greenhouse_8673946002.title: Maintenance Supervisor
greenhouse_8673946002.rewritten_description:
It's 7:15 a.m. and a resident just called about a leak that started overnight. Before the office opens, you've already pulled the work order, assessed the source, and have a plan in motion. That's the pace this role runs at, and it suits some people well.

The Work

Waypoint Management Services is hiring a Maintenance Supervisor for a high-end luxury community in St. Augustine, FL. This is a hands-on leadership position. You'll carry real accountability for the physical condition of the property, from daily work order completion to preventive maintenance on HVAC systems, pool chemical readings, grounds upkeep, and make-ready turns. Units need to be genuinely move-in ready, which means reviewing make-ready status with contractors regularly and holding that standard without exception.

Budget awareness is part of the job. You'll manage maintenance costs with efficiency in mind, track tool and equipment inventory, and operate within OSHA standards. When service emergencies come up, and they will, you're expected to coordinate corrective action fast. The 24-hour work order response standard applies even when it's inconvenient. On-call availability is required, so that's worth being honest with yourself about before applying.

You'll also keep gated entrances and security equipment operational, oversee trash compactor service, and handle plumbing, carpentry, and general repairs alongside your team. The Community Manager is your primary partner on the leadership side, so clear and consistent communication there matters.

What Waypoint Needs From You

  • Prior supervisory experience leading maintenance staff and managing vendors or contractors
  • EPA Section 608 certification (Types I and II) required at time of hire
  • CPO certification required, or must obtain within 90 days of start
  • CAMT certification preferred
  • High school diploma or GED plus at least two years of general maintenance experience
  • Bilingual in Spanish and English strongly preferred
  • Comfortable working an on-call rotation

Compensation runs $32 to $35 per hour. Benefits including medical, dental, and vision coverage start on day one. The company also offers a 401(k) with matching, an employee referral program, and an onsite housing discount for eligible employees.

One thing worth noting for candidates coming from Class B or C communities: luxury assets carry higher expectations around curb appeal, resident communication, and finish quality on turns. The punch list standards at a property like this tend to be more detailed, and residents notice. Strong candidates for this role bring not just technical skill but a genuine ownership mentality toward the physical product.

They're the first real conversation a prospective resident has with a property, and in a market like Los Angeles County, where competition for qualified tenants is constant, the quality of that conversation determines occupancy. Marketing is part of the job too: PMA expects you to support vacancy promotion through online platforms and social media, not just wait for leads to arrive. Compensation runs $19.50 to $23.00 per hour for 40 hours per week, with a leasing bonus structure on top: $100 per new lease signed and $50 per renewal. Full-time employees receive medical, dental, vision, and life insurance with an employer contribution, a 401(k) with discretionary company match after one year, short and long-term disability, and a PTO package covering vacation, holidays, and sick time.

greenhouse_5378706008.rewritten_description:
This role covers multiple properties across the Portland metro area, which means your week probably won't look the same twice. One day you're running a team standup at one site, the next you're reviewing a punch list at another, then handling a delinquency situation or sitting in on a lease signing somewhere else entirely. A valid driver's license isn't a formality here. You'll use it.

CloudTen Residential operates a genuinely varied portfolio: hotel-to-residential conversions, high-rise lease-ups, value-add repositioning. That range matters for this role because each property type carries its own operational personality. A lease-up runs differently than a stabilized garden-style community, and a conversion brings its own quirks around resident expectations and maintenance history. The multi-site Community Manager here needs to shift gears between those contexts without losing focus on the details that matter at each one.

Day-to-day, the work spans the full scope of site management. You'll oversee rent collection and delinquency, monitor expenses, prepare budgets, and keep accounting procedures clean. You'll hire and train on-site staff, conduct inspections, enforce move-in and move-out protocols, and make sure service requests get resolved within 24 to 48 hours. On the leasing side, you'll track market trends, adjust pricing as conditions shift, and support retention through timely renewals. Fair Housing compliance runs through all of it.

The honest part: multi-site work is demanding in ways a single-property role isn't. You're responsible for multiple teams who each need clear direction, and you're doing it across locations. Resident concerns and staff issues don't wait for you to arrive at that property. Strong organizational discipline and the ability to manage competing priorities without dropping the details are what separate candidates who thrive in this setup from those who find it overwhelming.

What CloudTen is looking for

  • At least two years of property management experience, with demonstrated comfort in a leadership capacity
  • Solid working knowledge of Oregon landlord-tenant law and Fair Housing regulations
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office and at least one property management software platform
  • Comfort with basic accounting: budgets, deposits, expense tracking, delinquency management
  • A valid driver's license and the ability to move between sites regularly
  • High school diploma required; college coursework or a degree is preferred

Pay runs between $30.00 and $32.00 per hour. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, FSA options, company-paid life insurance, and paid time off. CloudTen is an equal opportunity employer and maintains a drug-free workplace.

workable_6008322.title: Temporary Turn Associate - Office
workable_6008322.rewritten_description:
Student housing turn season is one of the most compressed, high-volume periods in property management. Leases expire in bulk, residents move out within days of each other, and new residents start arriving almost immediately. During that window, office teams need extra hands to keep the move-in process from buckling under the volume.

PeakMade Real Estate is bringing on a temporary office associate at their student housing community in Allendale, Michigan to cover exactly that period. This is a short-term, high-activity role that supports the leasing office through turnover.

What the Work Looks Like

Most of your time will be spent at the front end of the resident experience during move-in and move-out. That means fielding questions from incoming and outgoing residents, helping the office team stay organized, and making sure administrative tasks don't fall through the cracks when traffic at the front desk spikes. You'll handle general office support as directed and treat every interaction with residents, vendors, and teammates professionally.

This isn't a role that requires prior property management experience. What it does require is the ability to stay composed when things get busy, pay attention to detail, and show up reliably. Hours run 32 to 40 per week, and weekend availability is expected during peak turn activity. Evening and weekend schedules can also be considered depending on your availability.

What PeakMade Is Looking For

  • High school diploma or equivalent preferred (no degree requirement)
  • Reliable transportation to get to the property consistently
  • Flexibility to work weekends and varied hours during the turn period
  • Strong attention to detail and a calm, professional manner with residents
  • Ability to take direction and shift priorities quickly as needs change

PeakMade specializes in off-campus student housing, multifamily, and build-to-rent communities across the U.S. and is headquartered in Atlanta.

One practical note for candidates new to property management: turn season office work is a useful entry point. You'll see how a leasing office actually operates under pressure, get exposure to move-in documentation and resident communication, and build a reference in a specialized housing sector. For anyone considering a longer-term path in property management, this kind of temporary role often leads to consideration for permanent leasing or administrative positions when they open up.

workable_6007806.title: Providence at McDowell Assistant Community Manager
workable_6007806.rewritten_description:
It's 9 a.m. on the first of the month at Providence at McDowell, and your morning is already shaped by the ledger. Which residents posted overnight, who still owes, and which accounts are moving toward a late notice. That rhythm, financial accountability layered underneath everything else you do, defines what this role actually is.

What This Role Covers

Karya Property Management is hiring an Assistant Community Manager for Providence at McDowell, a full-time, hourly, on-site position in Phoenix. The role sits at the intersection of collections, leasing, and community operations, and you'll carry real ownership across all three.

On the financial side, you'll post payments, process deposits, and maintain resident ledgers daily. Delinquency management is yours end to end: late notices, statutory notices under the Arizona Residential Landlord and Tenant Act, payment plan negotiations, and coordination with legal counsel when matters escalate to eviction. You'll also handle move-in and move-out accounting, security deposit dispositions within Arizona's statutory window, and contribute to weekly and monthly reporting on occupancy, budget variance, and collections.

Leasing is a real part of the job, not secondary to the admin work. You'll carry an individual leasing and renewal goal, conduct tours, work leads through to close, and manage the full application pipeline from screening through lease execution. Renewal campaigns, rent increases, and resident retention outreach are also part of your workload, alongside competitor surveys and occasional social media support.

When the Community Manager is off-site, you're running the property. That includes resident escalations, vendor coordination, unit turns, punch walks, and whatever the day brings. You'll also participate in the on-call rotation for after-hours emergencies.

What You'll Need and What You'll Build

This role requires at least one year in a customer-facing field, strong comfort with numbers and spreadsheet-level detail, and the communication skills to handle a frustrated resident and a vendor call in the same hour without losing composure. A high school diploma or equivalent is required. Weekend availability and flexibility during peak leasing and turn seasons are both expected.

Prior multifamily experience, especially collections and evictions, gives candidates a real advantage. Familiarity with Yardi, Entrata, or RealPage is preferred, as is working knowledge of Arizona landlord-tenant law, Fair Housing requirements, and bilingual ability in English and Spanish.

What the role builds is worth naming directly. Candidates who come from leasing or hospitality will develop serious financial fluency here: delinquency management, ledger accuracy, and budget-variance thinking are skills that carry directly into Community Manager roles. Candidates who come from an admin or accounting background will develop the leasing confidence and resident-relations judgment that rounds out a full property management skill set. Either path leads somewhere.

One honest note: Phoenix summers are real, and this role includes outdoor property walks during turns and outreach events. Physical stamina during peak season is part of the job description, not a footnote.

Compensation includes an hourly rate, leasing commissions, renewal bonuses, quarterly and annual performance bonuses tied to occupancy and delinquency targets, medical, dental, and vision insurance, a 401(k) with company match, paid time off, and a potential housing discount.

workable_6008474.title: Maintenance Technician
workable_6008474.rewritten_description:
FLATS operates urban apartment communities in Chicago with a design-forward identity and a tech-integrated approach to property operations. This Maintenance Technician role sits at the center of the day-to-day physical plant: work orders, make-readies, grounds, life safety systems, and everything in between.

What You'll Actually Do

Your day starts with the work order queue. You'll triage, prioritize, and close out resident service requests, keeping response times tight. Make-ready work is a regular part of the job: prepping vacant units to company standards before a new resident takes possession. Beyond turns, you'll handle common area cleaning, exterior grounds upkeep, and seasonal duties including pool maintenance. Property walk-throughs are part of your routine, and when something's off, you document it and move toward a fix.

Annual inspections don't manage themselves. Fire extinguishers, life safety systems, elevators, and any other city or state-mandated checks fall within your scope. When outside contractors are needed for larger projects, you'll help coordinate that under the direction of the Maintenance Engineer or Property Manager. Inspection prep is part of the job too.

What You Bring

  • At least one year of residential maintenance experience
  • HVAC experience is required; certification is a plus
  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • Comfortable with Microsoft Office for basic documentation and communication
  • Strong time management and the ability to shift priorities without losing track of open items
  • Good resident-facing communication skills, which matter more than people expect in this role
  • Physical readiness: this job involves lifting up to 100 pounds, working in varying weather, and spending most of the day on your feet, crawling, climbing, or crouching
  • Safety-conscious habits around electrical, mechanical, and airborne hazard exposure

A Few Honest Notes

Urban mid-rise maintenance in Chicago carries its own rhythm. Winters push HVAC and exterior work hard, and the life safety inspection calendar in the city is thorough. If you've worked a Chicago property before, you already know the pace. If you haven't, expect to learn it quickly. The coordination side of this role, managing contractors and inspection schedules, tends to separate the technicians who stay and grow from the ones who burn out. Good documentation habits and a methodical approach to work order management go further here than raw technical speed.

FLATS offers medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401(k) with employer match, paid time off, sick leave, and paid holidays.

smartrecruiters_744000141545787.title: Regional Property Manager - Northern Colorado
smartrecruiters_744000141545787.rewritten_description:
It's a Tuesday morning and you're standing in the leasing office of a new-build community in Thornton, walking through traffic numbers with a Community Manager before heading north to check on a stabilized asset in Fort Collins. By noon, you'll be reviewing a punch list with a maintenance lead. That's the rhythm of this role.

The Scope

AIR Communities operates apartment communities across major U.S. markets, and this position covers a Northern Colorado portfolio that spans both lease-up assets and mature, stabilized properties. The two types demand different thinking. A new-build community needs aggressive leasing strategy, concession discipline, and close attention to early occupancy trends. A stabilized asset needs operational consistency, retention focus, and tight expense management to protect NOI. You'll be doing both, often in the same week.

This is a field-based role by design. Four to five days per week, you're at properties, not working remotely. You'll lead Community Managers and their onsite teams, which means coaching on sales process and leasing metrics, addressing delinquency, managing budgets, and keeping resident satisfaction scores where they need to be. You'll also partner closely with maintenance to make sure make-ready timelines stay on track and community standards hold up across the portfolio.

Financial accountability is real here. You're responsible for budget oversight, revenue growth, and expense management across multiple assets. A general understanding of property financials isn't enough; you need to be comfortable reading a T-12, identifying where performance is slipping, and adjusting strategy accordingly.

What AIR Is Looking For

  • At least five years leading multifamily teams across multiple communities, with measurable results in occupancy, leasing performance, and resident retention
  • Experience managing a portfolio that includes lease-up or new construction alongside stabilized assets
  • Strong financial acumen: budgets, expense control, and revenue growth strategies
  • Hands-on, present leadership style. This role doesn't work for someone who manages from a distance
  • Familiarity with property management platforms such as OneSite, SmartRent, or Salesforce
  • A background in competitive, metrics-driven sales environments, whether in multifamily, hospitality, or similar fields

Compensation is $120,000 to $140,000 annually, plus an annual target bonus. AIR also offers medical, dental, vision, and life insurance, HSA/FSA options, company-paid short and long-term disability, a 401(k) with up to 6% employer contribution, paid parental leave up to 16 weeks, tuition assistance, and a 25% rent discount at any AIR community. The application deadline is August 3, 2026, though AIR will continue reviewing submissions on a rolling basis after that date.

Northern Colorado's multifamily market has added significant supply over the past few years, particularly in the Greeley and Fort Collins corridors. That means the leasing environment is more competitive than it was even three years ago, and concession strategy matters more at the community level. Candidates who have managed through a lease-up in a supply-heavy submarket will have a real advantage here.

greenhouse_5379171008.title: Assistant Maintenance Manager
greenhouse_5379171008.rewritten_description:
It's 6:45 a.m. on a Monday and your phone already has two work orders from overnight: a unit reported no heat, and a common area light fixture is out near the entrance. Before the leasing office opens, you want both resolved.

That's the pace of this role. Bozzuto is hiring an Assistant Maintenance Manager for a residential property in Jersey City, NJ. The position sits between hands-on trade work and team leadership. You're still in the tools regularly, but you're also responsible for making sure others are doing the work correctly and on time.

What the Work Actually Involves

The make-ready process is central to this job. Turns need to move quickly and cleanly so apartments are ready to lease without delays. You'll own the punch list mentality: thorough walkthroughs, no shortcuts, units handed off in move-in condition. Beyond turns, you'll handle HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and appliance repairs across the property, respond to resident service tickets with genuine follow-through, and keep preventative maintenance programs running on schedule rather than reacting to failures after the fact.

The building itself demands attention. Grounds upkeep, snow removal, common area cleanliness, and safety compliance all fall within your scope. Bozzuto places real weight on asset preservation, which means this role isn't just about fixing things when they break. It's about protecting the long-term condition of the property. You'll also be expected to work weekends and participate in the emergency on-call rotation. That part of the job is real, and it's worth knowing upfront.

What You Need to Bring

  • At least 5 years of experience in the trades, facilities, or residential building maintenance
  • HVAC, EPA, or NAPE certification
  • Working knowledge of HVAC systems, plumbing, electrical, and appliance repair
  • Basic carpentry, drywall, and painting skills
  • Familiarity with OSHA, MSDS, and risk management standards
  • Exposure to complex mechanical systems such as boilers, chillers, central plant, or split systems is a plus
  • Prior supervisory experience, even informal, is preferred
  • Comfort with technology platforms and basic Microsoft Office proficiency
  • Physical ability to lift 25 to 50 pounds regularly, climb ladders, and work in variable weather

The candidates who tend to stand out here combine technical depth with real communication skills. You can diagnose a failing boiler and also explain the timeline to a frustrated resident without getting defensive. That combination is rarer than most people assume, and it's exactly what separates a strong assistant maintenance manager from a good technician.

Compensation for this role falls between $70,000 and $72,000 annually, with additional bonus opportunities. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, 20 days of paid time off plus holidays, a 401k with company match, and tuition reimbursement.

greenhouse_7826681003.title: Groundskeeper / Maintenance Technician - Montair at Somerset Hill
greenhouse_7826681003.rewritten_description:
Grounds and maintenance roles at apartment communities tend to get underestimated. They're actually the first impression a property makes, every single day, before a single leasing conversation happens. At Montair at Somerset Hill in Tumwater, WA, Olympus Property is hiring a Groundskeeper/Maintenance Technician to own that first impression.

What the Role Involves

Your primary focus is curb appeal and cleanliness across the community. That means daily trash and debris pickup through common areas, parking lots, breezeways, hallways, laundry rooms, and other shared spaces. You'll also handle light cleaning and minor repairs as part of the make-ready process before new residents move in, keep an accurate inventory of cleaning supplies and equipment, and assist the office team periodically with door notices. The schedule is full-time, Monday through Friday, 9 AM to 6 PM.

Prior experience in landscaping, grounds maintenance, facilities work, or janitorial services is required. You'll be working outdoors regularly, in all kinds of Pacific Northwest weather, so comfort with variable conditions is part of the job, not an occasional inconvenience. Physical requirements include the ability to lift 25 pounds and operate light equipment.

Skills This Role Builds

If you're early in a property management career, a grounds role teaches you things that are hard to learn any other way. You develop an eye for what makes a property look and feel well-maintained, a skill that translates directly if you move into maintenance technician, lead tech, or facilities supervisor positions down the road. You also learn how a community operates from the outside in: traffic patterns, resident habits, the relationship between curb appeal and occupancy. Those observations matter more than most people realize.

The technicians and groundskeepers who grow quickly in this industry are the ones who treat the property like it's theirs. They notice the thing that needs attention before anyone asks. They communicate with the office team clearly. They show up with consistency. That's the baseline Olympus is looking for here.

The Company Behind the Role

Olympus Property has been recognized by the National Apartment Association as a top employer three years running (2023, 2024, and 2025). The benefits package here is genuinely comprehensive:

  • Medical, dental, and vision coverage
  • 401(k) with employer matching
  • Educational assistance and tuition reimbursement
  • Apartment rental allowance
  • Pet insurance
  • Short-term and long-term disability
  • Life and AD&D insurance
  • Paid time off and sabbatical
  • Monthly performance bonuses for eligible team members

The starting pay range is $23.00 to $25.00 per hour, depending on experience and location. For a grounds role with a defined schedule, a real benefits package, and a company that has a documented track record of promoting from within, this is a strong entry point into property management.

greenhouse_8109374.title: Leasing Consultant
greenhouse_8109374.rewritten_description:
Leasing is where occupancy gets won or lost. A community can have great amenities and a solid location, but if the person greeting prospects at the door can't convert traffic into signed leases, none of that matters. Weinstein Properties understands this, which is why they invest heavily in training the people who hold this role, even when those people have never worked a day in property management.

Weinstein is a family-owned operator headquartered in Richmond, Virginia, with more than 70 years in the business and over 60 apartment communities across Virginia, North Carolina, Texas, Tennessee, and Georgia. The Bexley Westshore community in Cumming, GA is hiring a Leasing Consultant. Starting pay is $20/hour and scales with experience. Quarterly bonuses are part of the package, and this specific opening includes an alternate schedule bonus of $80 per pay period for working Saturdays and taking a weekday off instead.

The Schedule and Compensation Structure

This is an alternate-schedule position. You'll work five days per week including Saturdays (9am to 5pm), with Sundays and one weekday off each week. Weekday hours run 9am to 6pm. The schedule stays consistent week to week, which makes it easier to plan your life around. In addition to base pay and the alternate schedule bonus, you'll earn quarterly bonuses tied to performance. Benefits include a rent discount, health, dental and vision insurance, 401k with company match, paid holidays, birthday time off, vacation, and sick time.

What the Role Actually Involves

Leasing Consultants at Weinstein are the first point of contact for prospective residents and a daily resource for current ones. You'll handle tours, follow up on leads, process applications, and support the administrative side of the leasing office. Property walks, unit inspections, and helping maintain the overall appearance of the community are part of the job too. Resident events and occasional weather-related situations may pull you outside standard hours from time to time.

Weinstein is explicit that prior leasing experience is not required. Their training program is built to bring motivated people up to speed from the ground. What they screen for is attitude, communication, and the ability to stay organized when priorities shift mid-day, which happens constantly in a leasing office.

  • Strong verbal and written communication skills
  • Comfort engaging with people in person, by phone, and via email
  • Organized, goal-oriented, and able to manage competing tasks
  • Team-oriented with a willingness to pitch in beyond a defined job description
  • Flexible availability, including Saturdays

One thing worth knowing about this career path: leasing consultant roles at well-run operators like Weinstein are genuine entry points into property management. Strong performers typically move into Assistant Manager roles where they own the financial reporting side, including rent collections, delinquency tracking, and NOI contribution at the property level. Weinstein notes that many of their current leaders started exactly where this role begins.

Cumming sits in Forsyth County, one of the fastest-growing counties in Georgia, which means lease-up pressure and steady traffic are real factors at communities in this market. For a leasing consultant, that translates to a high-volume environment with genuine opportunity to build conversion skills quickly.

greenhouse_5203844007.title: Community Manager - Bear Valley
greenhouse_5203844007.rewritten_description:
MG Properties has been acquiring, developing, and managing apartment communities across the Western U.S. for over three decades. Bear Valley Apartments in Denver is one of those communities, and they're looking for a Community Manager who can run the full operation: team development, leasing performance, budget oversight, and day-to-day property management.

Denver's multifamily market rewards operators who can balance occupancy with NOI discipline. The city has absorbed significant new supply in recent years, which means community managers at stabilized properties have to work harder on retention and traffic conversion than they did five years ago. Concessions are part of the conversation in certain submarkets, and budget management matters more when rent growth is measured rather than assumed. Bear Valley sits in the southwest part of the city, a more established residential area compared to the high-rise corridors downtown, which typically means a different resident profile and a different leasing rhythm.

This role carries real authority. You'll hire and develop your on-site team, set the operational tone, manage the property's budget, and own the marketing strategy. MG Properties wants someone who has already done this, not someone building toward it. Yardi experience is a plus, and a valid driver's license is required.

What strong candidates bring

  • Recent, hands-on experience managing a residential apartment community (not just assistant-level work)
  • Proven ability to build and lead an on-site team through hiring, training, and performance management
  • Demonstrated budget management skills, including variance analysis and expense control
  • Marketing and leasing acumen, with an understanding of how to drive traffic and improve conversion
  • Yardi proficiency (preferred)
  • Valid driver's license and proof of insurance

The compensation range is $79,000 to $81,000 annually, with monthly and performance-based incentive bonuses on top of that. MG Properties also offers company profit sharing, a 401(k) with employer match, medical, dental, and vision coverage, paid holidays, paid sick time, and rental discounts. This position is expected to be filled by September 2026.

greenhouse_4355921009.title: Assistant Community Manager
greenhouse_4355921009.location: Evolve Palm Coast - 23 Evolve Parkway - Palm Coast, FL - 32137
greenhouse_4355921009.rewritten_description:
Most assistant manager roles in multifamily sit at the crossroads of leasing and collections, and that's exactly where this one lives. At Evolve Palm Coast, a Hawthorne Residential Partners community in Palm Coast, FL, the Assistant Community Manager keeps daily operations moving while the Community Manager handles the bigger picture. It's a real dual-track role: you're closing leases in the morning and reviewing delinquency reports in the afternoon.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

On the leasing side, you'll handle tours, respond to incoming leads, process applications, and push renewals through on time. Occupancy is a shared responsibility here, and you'll feel the weight of that number. You'll also manage the community's social media presence, which means creating content that actually reflects what's happening on the property, not just stock graphics.

The financial piece is where this role separates itself from a pure leasing position. You'll oversee rent collection and payment posting, run weekly delinquency follow-up calls, and coordinate eviction procedures when it gets to that point. Ledger reviews are part of the routine, checking that billing and payment applications are accurate before they become problems. You'll also pull together financial documentation for the Community Manager and regional leadership. If numbers make you uncomfortable, this role will push you past that quickly.

When the Community Manager is out, you step up. That means keeping the team focused, handling resident concerns, and making sure nothing falls through. Hawthorne calls it their "Live It" culture, but practically speaking, it means you're expected to de-escalate difficult conversations with professionalism and actually follow through, not just smooth things over.

The schedule runs Monday through Friday, 9 AM to 6 PM, with Saturdays from 10 AM to 4 PM. You'll get one weekday off to keep things at 40 hours. Resident events and community needs can pull you into evenings occasionally, so flexibility matters.

What Hawthorne Is Looking For

  • High school diploma or GED equivalent
  • Two years of property management experience preferred
  • At least six months in an assistant community manager role preferred
  • Valid driver's license required
  • CALP certification is a plus

Compensation includes an hourly base plus monthly leasing and renewal commissions and quarterly performance bonuses. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, 401(k) with company match, paid time off (including your birthday), paid parental and adoption leave, pet insurance, telehealth access, and company-paid life insurance. Hawthorne also runs a Career Path Program specifically designed to move Assistant Community Managers into Community Manager roles, and their Learning and Development team actively supports that progression.

The candidates who do well here tend to be comfortable with financial reports, direct with residents when situations require it, and organized enough to juggle leasing traffic and back-office tasks in the same shift. The ones who struggle are usually strong in one area but not the other. This role demands both.

greenhouse_5374173008.title: Community Manager
greenhouse_5374173008.rewritten_description:
Workforce housing is one of the most active development segments across the Sun Belt right now, and Hillpointe sits near the center of it. As a fully integrated developer and builder, they control the full cycle from land acquisition through construction and into operations. That integration means the Community Manager here works inside a company that has genuine visibility into how each decision at the property level connects to asset performance and long-term value.

This role at their Four Corners, FL community carries the full weight of on-site leadership. You'll own daily operations, occupancy, financial performance, resident experience, and vendor coordination. Hillpointe expects its Community Managers to think like operators, not administrators.

What the Day-to-Day Actually Looks Like

Your mornings might start with a property walk, checking that amenities are in like-new condition and flagging anything that needs attention before residents head out for the day. From there, you're likely shifting between reviewing accounts payable, checking leasing traffic, and talking through a maintenance request with the facilities team. You're the connective tissue between what residents experience and what the regional manager sees on a report.

You'll work closely with your Regional Manager to hit and hold budgeted occupancy and rent levels, which means staying on top of lease activity, monitoring concessions, and identifying additional revenue opportunities when they appear. Entrata proficiency will help you move quickly here. Budget oversight, vendor management, and lease administration all run through this role. The expectation is availability outside standard hours except during approved time off, which is worth knowing before you apply.

Who Fits Well Here

  • Property management experience, particularly in a lease-up or active Class A or B community
  • Comfort working in Entrata or comparable property management software
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to work through legal documents and explain lease terms clearly to residents
  • Basic financial literacy: calculating percentages, reading budget reports, managing fiscal records
  • Valid driver's license (required for golf cart use on property and routine local travel)
  • High school diploma or equivalent; some property management background preferred
  • Physical ability to access all areas of the property and handle up to 20 pounds independently

The candidates who tend to thrive in roles like this one aren't just organized. They read the community's energy accurately. They notice when resident satisfaction is drifting before it shows up in renewal numbers, and they build enough trust with the maintenance team that problems get solved before they become complaints. That kind of situational awareness is harder to teach than software skills, and Hillpointe's model gives Community Managers real room to act on it.

greenhouse_4342363009.title: Limpiador de Plaza Exterior - Springfield
greenhouse_4342363009.rewritten_description:
Office environments in commercial real estate depend on consistent, visible upkeep to signal professionalism to tenants and their clients. The porter role exists because that standard doesn't maintain itself. It requires someone on-site, on schedule, and paying close attention to the details that tenants and visitors notice immediately.

Comstock's ParkX division is hiring an exterior porter based in Springfield, VA. The work centers on keeping shared office spaces clean and presentable across floors, restrooms, kitchens, meeting rooms, and common areas. You'll follow daily cleaning schedules and checklists, empty trash and recycling, maintain janitorial storage areas, and assist the Senior Operations Manager with special cleaning requests as they come up. End-of-shift documentation and proper handoff to the next shift are part of the routine. So is monitoring supply inventory and flagging any maintenance issues, equipment damage, or safety concerns to management before they become bigger problems.

What This Role Requires Coming In

  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • Valid driver's license with a clean record
  • Ability to lift up to 50 pounds and sustain physical activity throughout a shift, including standing, bending, kneeling, and climbing stairs
  • Comfort working in variable conditions, including exposure to cleaning chemicals, dust, and outdoor environments
  • Availability for weekend and after-hours coverage during events or peak periods
  • Reliability, punctuality, and the ability to work independently with minimal supervision

What the Role Builds

Porters who take this kind of work seriously develop skills that transfer directly into facilities coordination and property operations roles. Working across a commercial portfolio, you'll build familiarity with preventive equipment care, safety compliance, and the communication rhythms between janitorial staff and property management. You'll also get experience interacting with tenants and visitors in a professional setting, which is a foundation for anyone who wants to grow toward a facilities supervisor or property operations coordinator position.

Comstock offers a 401(k) match, career development pathways within their expanding portfolio, free parking, and EV charging. The compensation range for this position in Virginia is $14 to $15 per hour, with final offers based on experience and the specific needs of the role.

Strong candidates for this type of role tend to be self-directed and detail-oriented in equal measure. Following a checklist is only part of it. The best porters notice what's not on the checklist and address it anyway, then communicate what they found.

greenhouse_4355301009.rewritten_description:
What You'll Actually Do

Estancia Townhomes sits in the Dallas market, where Class B and C garden-style and townhome communities have been competing hard on concessions as new Class A supply has pressured lease-up timelines across the metro. Running a sub-300-unit property here means you're close enough to the numbers to feel every shift in occupancy and delinquency, but you're also the face of the community in ways that larger mid-rise operations don't require of their managers. This is a hands-on role.

Your mornings will likely involve reviewing T-3 and T-12 financials, tracking NOI performance against budget, and working through delinquency reports with your team. Afternoons can look completely different. Berkshire's culture is intentionally informal in spots, and resident engagement is taken seriously alongside the ledger work. You'll collaborate with your Regional Manager on annual budgets, monthly and quarterly forecasts, capital plans, and staffing plans. When something operational shifts, you're expected to understand how it flows through the financial statements, not just flag it for someone else to interpret.

Team development is a real part of this job. You'll recruit, hire, train, and assess your on-site staff, and Berkshire places genuine weight on how managers grow their people. Resident communications, service request follow-up, and community marketing (including social content) also fall within your scope.

What You Bring

  • At least five years of multifamily property management experience
  • Comfort reading and interpreting financial statements and operational reports
  • Demonstrated experience managing and developing a site team
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills for both resident-facing and internal reporting
  • Proficiency with property management software for financial and operational problem-solving
  • A leadership style that shows up in how you work, not just how you describe yourself

The Role in Context

Berkshire owns and manages its own properties rather than operating as a third-party fee manager. That distinction matters: decisions at the site level carry real weight because the company has direct financial exposure to the asset. A property manager here isn't executing someone else's strategy at arm's length. You're close to the investment itself.

Strong candidates at this level typically separate themselves through financial fluency. Plenty of experienced managers can handle leasing traffic and maintenance coordination. Fewer can look at a monthly variance report, identify whether a NOI miss came from controllable expenses or market-driven revenue pressure, and adjust their operational plan accordingly. If that kind of analysis is already part of how you think, this role fits.

Berkshire offers unlimited PTO for salaried staff (with approval), a 25% rent discount, insurance, and personal development planning. The company emphasizes an ownership culture with room for individual growth across its portfolio.

greenhouse_4354955009.title: Cleaner - Part-Time
greenhouse_4354955009.rewritten_description:
Redstone Residential operates more than 38,000 beds across 20 states, with a heavy focus on student housing and a growing conventional multifamily portfolio. This part-time Cleaner role is based at one of their Provo communities and keeps the property looking sharp day in and day out.

What You'll Actually Do

The bulk of this job is straightforward: keep common areas clean and presentable. That means hallways, the clubhouse, leasing office, model unit, and parking areas on a consistent schedule. Outdoor work includes picking up trash and debris, clearing animal waste, and keeping the grounds and landscaping maintained. In winter, that extends to snow and ice removal in walkways and common spaces.

You'll also run scheduled cleaning checks inside resident apartments to confirm units meet the property's cleanliness standards. That's a meaningful part of the role, and it requires a professional, respectful approach when entering occupied homes. On top of that, you'll handle minor repairs and light general maintenance tasks as needed.

Shifts run four to six hours, and you'll be on your feet the entire time. You need to be able to lift 50-plus pounds.

What You Bring

  • Prior janitorial or cleaning experience, professional or otherwise
  • Ability to manage your task list independently without needing constant direction
  • A genuinely friendly, courteous approach to residents and coworkers
  • Physical stamina for standing shifts and occasional heavy lifting

Context Worth Knowing

Student housing communities run on tight turn schedules. Between lease cycles, properties need to flip dozens or hundreds of units quickly, and the cleaning team is central to that process. Getting familiar with make-ready standards now builds real, transferable skill for anyone who wants to grow into a maintenance or facilities coordination role down the line. This position pays $13.00 per hour and includes access to Redstone's 401(k) plan with up to 6% employer matching, which is a solid benefit for a part-time role.

greenhouse_5380116008.title: Apartment Maintenance Technician
greenhouse_5380116008.rewritten_description:
Fairstead operates a portfolio of more than 30,000 apartments across 28 states, and the work that keeps those units occupied and those residents housed happens at the property level, one work order at a time. This Maintenance Technician role in Newark is a direct contributor to that mission. Fairstead builds and manages affordable housing, and the physical condition of each unit directly affects occupancy, resident retention, and NOI. A well-run maintenance program keeps turns tight, punch lists short, and emergency calls manageable. That's the operational reality this role lives in every day.

Day to day, you're moving between scheduled preventative maintenance, unit inspections, and responding to resident service requests. Make-readies are a core part of the rhythm: cleaning and prepping vacated units so the next resident can move in without delay. Deferred turns cost money and drag down occupancy. You'll also check electrical systems for code compliance, test safety devices monthly, and keep a working inventory of tools and supplies so nothing slows you down mid-job.

On-call rotation is part of the role. After-hours emergencies happen in multifamily, and Fairstead expects a prompt response when they do. That's a real commitment worth acknowledging upfront.

Strong candidates come in with hands-on experience across general maintenance trades, a working knowledge of electrical systems, and an HVAC certification or equivalent. The ability to lift 70 pounds and stay on your feet for extended periods is a physical requirement of the work, not a formality. What separates a good technician from a great one at a property like this is attention to detail during inspections and the discipline to follow preventative maintenance schedules before problems compound into capex issues.

What Fairstead is looking for

  • Prior experience as a maintenance technician or in a comparable service role
  • Mechanical aptitude for minor repairs across plumbing, electrical, and general fixtures
  • HVAC, CMRP, or equivalent certification (preferred)
  • Clear written and verbal communication skills
  • Physical ability to lift up to 70 pounds and stand for extended periods
  • Availability for on-call rotation and after-hours emergency response

Compensation runs $24 to $26 per hour depending on experience and qualifications. Benefits include medical coverage through Meritain Health with a generous employer contribution, employer-paid vision and life insurance, a 401(k) with company match (100% on the first 3%, 50% on the next 2%), 15 days of PTO, 7 sick days, and 12 or more paid holidays. greenhouse_5380874008.title: Maintenance Supervisor - Multi site
greenhouse_5380874008.location: 445 W. University; Melrose Canyon Apartments; Park Diplomat
greenhouse_5380874008.rewritten_description:
It's 7 a.m. and you're already mapping out which of the three San Diego properties needs you first: a vacated unit at Melrose Canyon that has to be market-ready by end of week, a pool chemical check at Park Diplomat, and a work order backlog at 445 West University. That's the rhythm of this role.

What This Job Covers

Sunrise Management is hiring a multi-site Maintenance Supervisor to oversee physical operations across three residential properties in San Diego. You'll rotate between locations based on project needs, so a valid driver's license is a hard requirement, not a formality.

The core of the job is keeping units turning and common areas clean and functional. Make-ready timelines here run three to five days after vacancy. You'll handle the painting, coordinate carpet cleaning, run through punch list items, and make sure each unit passes inspection before it goes back on the market. On top of turns, you'll manage the full preventive maintenance calendar: HVAC, water heaters, pool and spa systems, lighting, fire safety checks, and life-safety walkthroughs.

Day-to-day work orders need to close within 24 hours. When parts delays push that window, you communicate directly with site management and keep residents informed. You'll also be on call for after-hours emergencies, which is standard for a supervisor role at this level.

This is a team leadership position. You'll supervise maintenance staff across sites, assign schedules, run monthly safety meetings, maintain MSDS records, and make sure PPE protocols are followed. You'll also have a hand in interviewing and training new maintenance hires, and you'll submit timesheets for your team.

Budget awareness matters here. You control supply purchases, get manager approval on expenditures, and flag capital improvement needs or repair recommendations up the chain. Sunrise wants someone who can identify a problem before it becomes expensive.

What You Bring

  • At least 2 years of hands-on property maintenance experience
  • Prior supervisory experience, managing a team and holding people accountable
  • Working knowledge of HVAC, plumbing, electrical, appliances, carpentry, and pool systems
  • Familiarity with Entrata or AppFolio is a plus
  • Valid driver's license with reliable transportation between sites
  • Understanding of Fair Housing laws
  • Comfort with PPE requirements and adherence to safety and hazardous materials policies

Pay runs $27 to $32 per hour depending on experience. Candidates who stand out tend to bring pool certifications, HVAC experience, and a track record of keeping turns tight without cutting corners on quality. Multi-site experience is a genuine advantage here because managing your time across three addresses with competing priorities is a skill in itself.

greenhouse_4702710006.title: Service Technician
greenhouse_4702710006.rewritten_description:
Affordable housing maintenance operates on tighter margins and higher expectations than most people assume. At a community like Harbor House on Saratoga in Corpus Christi, a Service Technician isn't just fixing things. They're directly protecting the quality of homes for working families who depend on the property running well. Dream Live Prosper Communities, a subsidiary of DLP Capital, is staffing this full-time role at their Corpus Christi location.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

The job centers on two rhythms: reactive and planned. On the reactive side, you're responding to resident service requests within 24 hours, handling the full range of plumbing, electrical, HVAC, appliance, and drywall work that comes up in any occupied community. On the planned side, you're running apartment turns, with a five-day target from vacancy to move-in ready. That turnaround window is tight, and hitting it consistently requires you to walk a unit, build a punch list quickly, sequence the work, and execute without a lot of hand-holding.

HVAC certification is required here, not preferred. That signals how central mechanical systems are to this community's operations. Beyond the technical work, this role includes some team coordination: assigning service requests, mentoring other technicians, managing the on-call schedule, and keeping the maintenance shop stocked without overspending. If you've only ever worked as a solo tech, the team leadership piece is worth taking seriously as part of the job description.

The role also involves grounds maintenance, emergency on-call rotation, and working in South Texas weather conditions year-round. After-hours calls are real, and consistent availability matters.

Where This Role Leads

A Service Technician position at a growing affordable housing operator is one of the cleaner paths into a Maintenance Supervisor or Maintenance Director role in property management. The skills that compound fastest here are turn management and vendor coordination. Techs who understand how a five-day turn affects occupancy, and who can manage cost-per-unit on make-readies, become genuinely valuable to regional operations teams. Add HVAC certification, some capex project exposure, and a track record of low delinquency-related damage disputes (through solid move-out documentation), and you've built a profile that carries weight across the industry.

What separates strong candidates in this specific role is the combination of technical range and communication. The job requires talking to residents professionally, coordinating with vendors, and reporting up to property management. Technicians who treat resident interaction as secondary to the wrenches tend to struggle here. The ones who move up treat both as equally important parts of the job.

  • HVAC certification required
  • Proficiency in electrical, plumbing, appliance repair, painting, and drywall
  • Ability to complete apartment turns within five days
  • Experience with turnovers in both newer and older building stock
  • Valid driver's license with a clean driving record and reliable transportation
  • Ability to lift up to 50 lbs and work in varied physical conditions including roofs, crawl spaces, and attics
  • Availability for after-hours emergencies and on-call rotation
  • Your own basic tools
  • Familiarity with property management operations and basic budgeting (preferred)

This is a full-time position with a schedule that includes weekends. Benefits include PTO, health, dental, vision, and life insurance, 401(k) matching, and learning and educational incentives.

workable_6010919.rewritten_description:
It's 11 PM and a resident calls because the heat stopped working. You're on rotation. You go.

That's part of the job at Aspen Riverpark Apartments, a 261-unit affordable community in Newark, New Jersey managed by Investment Property Group. IPG is a private firm headquartered in Park City, Utah, operating 150 properties across 13 states in multifamily, manufactured homes, and RV communities. They're looking for a Maintenance Technician who can handle the full range of day-to-day upkeep and emergency response at a mid-size property.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Most of your week runs Monday through Friday, 8am to 5pm. You'll work through assigned work orders, follow a preventative maintenance schedule, and do daily walkthroughs of common areas and building systems to catch problems before residents notice them. Plumbing, HVAC, appliances (refrigerators, stoves, washers, dryers) make up a big chunk of the technical work. You'll pull materials from the maintenance shop, track what you use, and flag reorder needs to your supervisor. The job doesn't require constant hand-holding, but you're expected to operate within established procedures and safety standards.

The after-hours on-call rotation is real and required. Overtime pay applies when you're called in, but you should go into this knowing that some nights and weekends won't be entirely yours. That's the honest reality of maintenance at a 261-unit property. Emergencies don't schedule themselves.

Resident interaction is a consistent part of the role. You're often the person a resident sees when something in their home is broken. How you handle that interaction matters as much as whether you fix the problem correctly.

Qualifications

  • At least one year of maintenance experience at a multifamily community of 100 or more units
  • Working knowledge of plumbing, HVAC, and appliance repair
  • Basic electrical and plumbing repair experience is a plus
  • Comfortable using and maintaining hand tools and power tools (you'll need to supply your own hand tools)
  • Valid driver's license
  • Able to participate in after-hours on-call rotation and respond to emergencies
  • Strong communication and customer service skills

Pay runs $24.00 to $28.00 per hour depending on experience and qualifications. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, life insurance, an HSA, an employee assistance program, 401k with company match, and four weeks of accrued PTO.

One thing that separates strong candidates in this role: comfort working independently on a property this size. At 261 units, the work order volume can stack up. Technicians who triage well, communicate clearly with residents when a repair needs a follow-up visit, and keep the maintenance supervisor informed tend to thrive. Those who need close supervision for every task tend to struggle.

smartrecruiters_744000141585539.title: Leasing Sales Consultant - Verdant
smartrecruiters_744000141585539.rewritten_description:
Leasing is a skill set, and this role uses several of them at once. You're reading people quickly, adjusting your pitch mid-tour, following up without being annoying, and closing without being pushy. At Verdant in Boulder, CO, AIR Communities is looking for a Leasing Consultant who brings that combination to work every day.

The Skills This Role Draws On Most

Sales instinct sits at the center of this position, but it's paired with genuine customer service ability. You're not just filling units. You're helping people make a significant life decision, sometimes on a tight timeline, and they'll remember how the process felt. The consultants who do well here tend to be comfortable with structure (AIR uses a defined sales process with follow-up cadences and tour frameworks) while still making interactions feel personal rather than scripted.

Adaptability matters too. Leasing volume shifts with the season, priorities change, and you may provide coverage at other communities in the AIR portfolio when needed. The ability to read a situation and recalibrate without losing momentum is genuinely useful here.

What You'll Be Doing Day to Day

Your core responsibilities break down like this:

  • Managing active prospects through prompt follow-up and scheduled tours
  • Conducting tours that highlight the specific value of Verdant, not just a generic apartment pitch
  • Consistently meeting or exceeding monthly leasing goals
  • Supporting resident experience through strong customer service at every touchpoint
  • Contributing to community marketing efforts
  • Following Fair Housing laws and regulations without exception

The typical schedule runs Tuesday through Saturday, 10:00am to 6:30pm, though hours can shift based on community needs and season. Reliable transportation is required.

Compensation and What Makes This Offer Distinct

The base rate starts at $21.00 per hour, and commission is structured to reward several leasing behaviors beyond just volume. You can earn more per lease by closing on longer lease terms (18 months or more), leasing higher-rent units, or hitting tiered monthly goals. That structure gives you multiple levers to pull rather than a single metric to chase.

AIR also offers a 25% rent discount at any AIR community, including the option to live on-site at Verdant. There's a paid Winter Break after peak season ends. You keep benefits during that unpaid time off, which is an unusual perk worth noting if work-life rhythm matters to you. Full benefits include medical, dental, vision, 401(k) with up to 6% employer match, paid parental leave up to 16 weeks, and tuition assistance.

One thing that separates strong candidates here: experience in a role where hitting a number wasn't optional. Hospitality, retail, and restaurant backgrounds translate well because those environments build the same muscle this role requires. You've been told "no" before, you've recovered, and you've still ended the month where you needed to be. That track record matters more than industry-specific knowledge at the start.

Boulder's rental market draws a mix of students, young professionals, and people relocating for work in the tech and outdoor industry sectors. Prospects tend to be informed and have options. The ability to have a real conversation about why Verdant fits their life specifically, rather than defaulting to a features rundown, will serve you well here.

greenhouse_5380284008.title: Assistant Maintenance Manager
greenhouse_5380284008.rewritten_description:
What You'll Actually Do

This role sits between hands-on trades work and team leadership, and you'll feel that tension every day. You're not managing from a distance. You're diagnosing HVAC problems, pulling service tickets, walking the make-ready units, and checking punch lists alongside your team. When something breaks at 11pm, you're in the on-call rotation. That's the job, and it's worth saying plainly before you apply.

Day to day, you'll handle maintenance requests across HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and appliance repair while keeping the turn process moving so vacant units hit leasing-ready status on time. Preventative maintenance programs are yours to execute consistently, not just when things slow down. You'll also stay on top of grounds, common areas, and building systems, making sure everything from lighting to mechanical rooms reflects the standard the property is held to. Code compliance and safety practices aren't paperwork exercises here. They're part of how the operation runs.

The leadership piece matters. You'll set the tone for how your team approaches the work. If you cut corners on a punch list, they will too. Bozzuto's properties attract residents with high expectations, and the maintenance team is a direct factor in retention.

What You Bring

  • At least 5 years working in the trades, facilities, or residential building maintenance
  • HVAC, EPA, and/or NAPE certification
  • Solid working knowledge of plumbing, electrical, and appliance repair, plus basic carpentry, drywall, and painting
  • Familiarity with complex mechanical systems including central plant, split systems, boilers, or chillers is a plus
  • Supervisory experience or a demonstrated ability to lead and motivate a small team
  • Working knowledge of OSHA standards, risk management practices, and MSDS requirements
  • Comfort with technology platforms, work order systems, and basic Microsoft Office tools
  • Physical ability to lift 25 to 50 pounds frequently, climb ladders, and work in outdoor conditions year-round
  • Availability for weekend coverage and emergency on-call rotation

Context Worth Knowing

The Edgewater/Wynwood corridor in Miami has seen significant Class A development over the past several years, and resident expectations in that market reflect it. Residents in these communities expect fast response times and a well-kept property. Deferred maintenance gets noticed quickly, and so does a maintenance team that actually follows through. If your background is in hospitality facilities or high-end residential, that attention to presentation will translate well here.

The salary range for this position is $63,000 to $67,000, with bonus eligibility on top of that. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, 20 days of paid time off plus holidays, a 401k with company match, and tuition reimbursement. For someone who wants to grow into a Maintenance Manager role, this position builds exactly the combination of technical depth and supervisory experience that makes that move possible.

greenhouse_4356008009.title: Cortland at the Village Maintenance Hiring Event - 8/14/2026
greenhouse_4356008009.rewritten_description:
It's 8:47 a.m. on a Monday and there's already a work order for a down HVAC unit, a leak under a kitchen sink, and a resident locked out of her unit. That's maintenance in multifamily. Cortland knows it, and they're looking for people who can handle that before lunch without losing their composure.

Cortland is hosting a facilities open house at Cortland at the Village in Smyrna, GA on Friday, August 14th from 10:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m. The address is 2085 Lake Park Dr SE, Smyrna, GA 30080. They're hiring across three levels of maintenance, and they'll be meeting candidates in person that day.

Who They're Hiring

Three roles are on the table, each with distinct experience expectations:

  • Maintenance Technician: Two to five years of hands-on experience required. An active EPA certification is required for this level.
  • Service Technician: At least one year of experience. EPA certification is not required at this level, which makes this a reasonable entry point for candidates still building credentials.
  • Service Manager: Three to five years of experience, plus both an active EPA and an active CPO. This is the senior track, so bring the paperwork.

When you show up, bring an updated resume, your driver's license, and copies of any relevant certifications. If your EPA or CPO is sitting in a filing cabinet somewhere, dig it out the night before.

About Cortland

Founded in 2005 and headquartered in Atlanta, Cortland is a vertically integrated owner-operator ranked among the top 10 multifamily firms in the country. They handle design, construction, and operations in-house, which means their maintenance teams work within a more coordinated structure than you'd find at a typical third-party management shop. Work orders, capital projects, and make-ready standards tend to be more systematized at that scale, which is a plus if you like clarity and a challenge if you prefer doing things your own way.

For maintenance professionals in the Atlanta metro, Cortland's portfolio depth matters. Getting in at a property like Cortland at the Village can open doors to other assets in the portfolio, and the company's size means there's a real path upward for Service Technicians who earn their EPA and develop their diagnostic skills. We've seen plenty of techs move from wrench-turning to supervising a team within a few years at operators this size. The infrastructure to grow is there if you use it.

Cortland is an equal opportunity employer and participates in E-Verify. The company maintains a drug-free workplace policy.

greenhouse_5205971007.title: Assistant Property Manager
greenhouse_5205971007.rewritten_description:
It's 9 a.m. on the first of the month, and the CAM reconciliation package is due to a client by noon. Three vendor invoices hit the AP queue overnight, a tenant submitted a maintenance escalation, and the Property Manager needs the monthly report drafted before a 10 o'clock ownership call. That's a normal Tuesday in this role.

The Work

Lincoln Property Company is hiring an Assistant Property Manager to support day-to-day operations across a commercial portfolio in Burlington, MA. The portfolio spans office, industrial, and retail assets, so exposure here is broad. You'll work directly alongside the Property Manager on financial reporting, lease administration, and tenant relations, with enough ownership over specific workstreams to build real operational depth.

On the financial side, you'll help prepare monthly reports and budget packages for institutional clients, manage operating expense reconciliation data (CAM/OpX), and review vendor invoices for accuracy and compliance with the management agreement and authorization limits. These aren't rubber-stamp tasks. Clients expect clean numbers delivered on time, and you'll be accountable for the inputs that make that happen.

Lease administration runs through this role as well: setting up new leases in applicable systems, processing changes, and coordinating tenant move-ins and move-outs, including walk-throughs with tenants and tenant improvement teams. You'll also support procurement and vendor bidding activities, help maintain emergency response plans, and provide direction to any direct reports on your team.

What Lincoln Is Looking For

  • A bachelor's degree (BA/BS) preferred, or equivalent combination of education and relevant experience
  • 1 to 2 years of experience in commercial property management or a closely related field
  • Intermediate to advanced proficiency with Microsoft Office, particularly Excel
  • Familiarity with AP and CMMS platforms is a plus
  • Ability to calculate percentages, discounts, and basic financial figures with accuracy
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to work through tenant and vendor issues while keeping relationships intact
  • Solid organizational habits and a track record of hitting deadlines under real workload pressure

This position is fully in-office in Burlington. No remote or hybrid option is available. Monthly property inspections and travel to assigned sites are part of the schedule.

Candidates who tend to separate themselves in this type of role are the ones who can hold the financial detail and the people side simultaneously. CAM reconciliation accuracy matters, but so does how you handle a frustrated tenant at 8:45 a.m. before the inbox is even clear. Lincoln operates a 720-million-square-foot portfolio nationally, which means the systems, reporting standards, and client expectations here are institutional-grade. If you're early in your commercial PM career and want exposure to that level of operation, this role delivers it.

greenhouse_6135808004.title: Business Manager, Property Operations
greenhouse_6135808004.rewritten_description:
What This Role Does

Asset Living is a third-party management firm with a national portfolio spanning multifamily, affordable housing, build-to-rent, student housing, and single-family rentals. This Business Manager position sits between regional leadership and site teams, keeping operations tight across a portfolio rather than running a single property. The work is operational and financial in equal measure.

Day to day, you're tracking delinquency, overseeing collections, and making sure move-out charges and timelines hold up under jurisdictional rules. You're monitoring work order completion rates and maintenance follow-through. You're reviewing capex spend against approved budgets and keeping vendor invoices moving through AP without bottlenecks. When legal matters come up, including evictions and lease enforcement, you coordinate with attorneys and keep the process on track.

Occupancy management is also in scope. That means supporting renewal workflows, handling resident escalations, and administering tenant-based voucher programs where applicable. You'll work alongside Regional Portfolio Managers, Community Managers, and leasing staff to hit portfolio KPIs, and you'll analyze operational and financial data to flag trends before they become problems.

What the Role Requires

  • At least three years in multifamily property management, operations, or asset management
  • Hands-on experience with Yardi, RealPage, MRI, or a comparable platform
  • Working knowledge of Microsoft Office and Google Workspace
  • Solid grasp of leasing operations, financial controls, and regulatory compliance
  • Strong written and verbal communication; bilingual Spanish/English preferred
  • High school diploma required; bachelor's degree in Business, Real Estate, or a related field preferred

The posting lists Portland and Seattle as locations, but candidates must reside in Reno, Nevada. Confirm that detail before applying. The Washington pay range is listed at $80,000 to $85,000.

What Sets Strong Candidates Apart

Candidates who do well in roles like this tend to have experience managing compliance across multiple jurisdictions, not just one market. Affordable housing background helps here too, particularly if you've touched tenant-based voucher administration. The volume of financial detail in this role, delinquency tracking, capex reporting, PO-to-invoice matching, rewards people who stay organized under load rather than those who do well in calm conditions. Third-party management adds another layer: you're accountable to both Asset Living's internal standards and individual client expectations, and those don't always align without active effort.

You'll also handle light cleaning and prep work ahead of resident move-ins, track cleaning supply inventory, and occasionally assist the office team with door notices. Olympus has been recognized as a National Apartment Association Top Employer three consecutive years (2023, 2024, 2025), and the benefits package reflects that. The candidates who stand out show up with a systems mindset, keeping a mental map of what needs attention when, and they communicate proactively with maintenance and leasing teams when something looks off.
