workable_6018531.title: Maintenance Supervisor
workable_6018531.rewritten_description:
Maintenance Supervisors at PeakMade Real Estate spend the majority of their time with tools in hand. That 60 to 70 percent hands-on split is a real number, and it shapes everything about who succeeds in this role. Strong diagnostic skills across HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and appliances carry more weight here than administrative polish. The supervisory piece matters too, but it's built on a foundation of credibility earned by actually knowing how to fix things.

What This Role Draws On

The core technical skills this position requires include HVAC diagnosis and repair (EPA Type II certification is required before you start), intermediate plumbing and electrical work, appliance troubleshooting, general carpentry, sheetrock, painting, and pool care where applicable. Beyond repairs, you'll need enough working knowledge of local and state codes to stay compliant on permitting, pool regulations, and safety standards. OSHA familiarity is expected, and you'll be responsible for keeping the maintenance shop organized, stocked, and hazard-communication compliant.

The organizational side of the role involves prioritizing and assigning service requests, tracking daily completion, following up on anything outstanding, and coordinating vendor and contractor activity throughout the turn process. Make-ready supervision is a real part of this job. You'll direct the team in getting vacant units prepped for marketing, manage key control per company policy, and participate in monthly unit inspections. When capital improvements come up, you'll work directly with the National Facilities Director to gather bids.

The Profile That Fits

  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • At least 2 years of maintenance supervisory experience, multifamily background strongly preferred
  • EPA Type II certification required; CPO preferred
  • Valid driver's license, current auto insurance, and a reliable personal vehicle (required for the role)
  • Must live within 30 miles of the assigned property
  • Ability to lift up to 50 pounds, work at height on ladders, and work outdoors in extreme temperatures
  • Personal hand tools required (not supplied by the community)

What separates a good candidate from a strong one here is the combination of technical range and resident-facing composure. Maintenance Supervisors at PeakMade interact directly with residents through the move-in and move-out process and handle concerns as they surface. The ability to resolve issues professionally without escalating friction matters as much as any certification.

The PeakMade Context

PeakMade is an Atlanta-based company that manages student housing, multifamily, and build-to-rent communities across the country. Student housing communities run on tight turn timelines, typically concentrated in summer, which means the turn coordination skills this role requires get tested at real volume. If you've managed turns at a student property before, that experience translates directly. If your background is conventional multifamily, the fundamentals carry over, but the pace and seasonality of student housing turns is worth understanding before you step in.

PeakMade offers technical certifications (HVAC and CPO), a facilities leadership program, and monthly renewal bonuses alongside standard benefits including PTO, 401(k) match, and paid parental leave. For a Maintenance Supervisor with strong diagnostic skills and an interest in growing into facilities management, the path here is reasonably clear.

workable_6021710.title: Part Time Community Manager Manufactured Housing Community PLUS HOUSING
workable_6021710.rewritten_description:
Managing a manufactured housing community for seniors takes a different kind of patience than a conventional multifamily site. Residents at a 55+ community tend to be long-term, invested in their neighborhood, and vocal when something isn't right. That's not a complaint. It's just the reality of the demographic, and it shapes everything from how you handle a maintenance concern to how you run a lease enforcement conversation.

The Role at Woodburn Estates

Investment Property Group operates Woodburn Estates, an 82-home senior manufactured housing community in Woodburn, Oregon. This is a part-time position, 28 hours per week, Monday through Friday from 10am to 4:30pm, and on-site housing is part of the compensation package. The position comes with a 2-bedroom, 2-bathroom manufactured home including a carport and storage shed. Living on site is a requirement of the role, not optional.

Day to day, you're running the full operation of the community. That means overseeing rent collection, reviewing delinquent accounts, managing the move-in application process, and making sure your team is following through on resident requests and complaints. You'll also handle hiring, training, and performance management for on-site staff, and you'll serve as the point of contact for local agencies and law enforcement when needed. Fair Housing compliance, lease enforcement, and regulatory reporting are all part of the job. The pay range is $24 to $28 per hour depending on experience and qualifications.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

A typical morning might start with a stack of resident correspondence, a call from a vendor, and two residents waiting outside the office before you've had a chance to open your inbox. The schedule is contained, but the work inside those hours is dense. Residents at a 55+ community often have more time to stop by in person, and many prefer it. Being genuinely approachable matters here, not just professionally cordial.

The delinquency side of the role deserves honest mention. Rent collection in manufactured housing communities follows specific legal frameworks that differ from conventional multifamily, and Oregon has its own landlord-tenant rules for MHCs. If you haven't worked in manufactured housing before, there's a learning curve on the regulatory side. IPG does want at least one year of experience managing a manufactured housing or multifamily community of 100 or more units, so some of this groundwork should already be familiar.

What Strong Candidates Bring

  • Genuine comfort working with older adults, including the patience to repeat information and handle emotional conversations calmly
  • Working knowledge of delinquency management and rent collection workflows
  • Experience with property management software and basic accounting systems
  • Conflict resolution skills that don't escalate situations unnecessarily
  • A valid driver's license
  • Ability to identify operational inefficiencies and bring practical suggestions forward

IPG is a privately held firm headquartered in Park City, Utah, with a portfolio spanning 150 properties across 13 states. For someone who performs well here, the company's scale means internal advancement opportunities do come up. Community manager experience in manufactured housing, especially at a senior community, translates well to regional or district-level roles as the portfolio grows.

workable_6021813.title: Regional Property Manager - West Coast Portfolio (Chicago)
workable_6021813.rewritten_description:
Regional property management has always required financial discipline and operational range, but the expansion of multifamily portfolios across multiple states has raised the bar considerably. When a company is simultaneously stabilizing existing assets and opening ground-up developments in new markets, the regional manager role becomes one of the most consequential positions in the organization. That's exactly the situation at FLATS, and it shapes everything about what this role demands.

FLATS operates multifamily communities across California, Nevada, and Washington, with additional ground-up development underway in Southern California. The Regional Property Manager hired into this position will carry full accountability for the operational and financial performance of that portfolio while also supporting new lease-ups as communities come online. This is a hybrid role based in the Chicago area, and travel throughout the portfolio is a consistent part of the job.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

On the financial side, you'll own annual budget development, monthly variance analysis, and NOI performance across the portfolio. That means digging into T-12s, identifying where delinquency is trending in the wrong direction, reviewing operating expenses against service quality, and presenting clear performance narratives to ownership groups and investors. You'll also weigh in on capex recommendations and oversee projects that affect both asset value and resident experience.

Operationally, you'll conduct regular site inspections, partner with facilities and maintenance teams on preventative maintenance execution, and hold onsite teams accountable to FLATS' brand and compliance standards. Fair Housing, ADA, and OSHA compliance fall within your scope, as do vendor relationships and emergency response protocols. When a new development transitions out of construction and into lease-up, you're one of the key people making sure that process goes smoothly.

The people side of this role is equally demanding. You'll recruit, coach, and develop Property Managers across geographically dispersed markets, which means doing meaningful leadership work without the luxury of being in the same building every day. Building a culture of accountability across sites in San Diego, Las Vegas, and Portland requires more than good intentions. It takes consistent communication, regular presence, and the kind of credibility that comes from knowing the numbers as well as the operations.

What Strong Candidates Bring

  • An active real estate license
  • At least 3 to 5 years of multifamily experience, including regional or multi-site oversight
  • Genuine financial fluency: budget management, forecasting, and a track record of driving NOI
  • Experience supporting lease-ups or new development transitions, not just stabilized assets
  • Comfort operating independently across markets without waiting for direction
  • Strong instincts for owner and investor communication, including the ability to present performance data with confidence

The candidates who tend to thrive in roles like this are the ones who treat the financial reports and the site visits as equally important. Operators who only show up for the numbers miss what's happening on the ground. Operators who are great with people but vague on variance analysis struggle when it's time to defend a budget to an ownership group. The combination matters here more than usual because this portfolio is actively growing, and growth amplifies both strengths and gaps.

From a career trajectory standpoint, this role builds the full stack of regional leadership skills: multi-market financial oversight, lease-up experience, team development across dispersed sites, and direct ownership relations. Those are exactly the competencies that lead to VP of Operations, Director of Asset Management, or senior leadership roles at larger ownership groups and third-party management firms. Regional experience at a company actively expanding its footprint tends to compress that timeline, because the problems are real and the stakes are visible.

greenhouse_5385820008.title: Assistant Maintenance Manager
greenhouse_5385820008.rewritten_description:
Multifamily properties in Boston's urban core run complex mechanical systems, tight turn schedules, and demanding residents. Bozzuto's Cambridge community needs an Assistant Maintenance Manager who can handle all three without losing composure.

This is a working leadership role. You'll carry a wrench and a clipboard. You'll pull service tickets, troubleshoot HVAC and plumbing issues, and also coach the technicians around you. The make-ready process is a real priority here: apartment turns need to be tight and on schedule so units can lease and new residents can move in without delays. Preventative maintenance gets the same attention as reactive work.

Day-to-Day Scope

Most of your week splits between resident service requests and building systems. You're diagnosing and resolving issues across HVAC, electrical, plumbing, and appliance repair. You're walking the property for general upkeep, grounds maintenance, and safety compliance. In winter, that includes snow removal. You'll also manage punch list completion on turns, support preventative maintenance scheduling, and keep the operation running inside applicable building and safety codes.

Weekend availability is required, and you'll participate in the emergency on-call rotation. That's a real commitment. Properties like this don't go quiet after business hours.

What the Role Requires

  • 5 or more years in the trades, facilities, or residential building maintenance
  • Hands-on proficiency with HVAC, plumbing, electrical systems, and appliance repair
  • HVAC, EPA, or NAPE certification
  • Familiarity with complex mechanical systems: central plant, boilers, chillers, split systems
  • Basic carpentry, drywall, and painting skills
  • Knowledge of OSHA standards, risk management practices, and MSDS
  • Supervisory experience or demonstrated leadership in a team setting
  • Comfort with technology platforms and basic Microsoft Office proficiency
  • Physical ability to lift 25 to 50 pounds frequently and work in varying weather conditions

Strong candidates for this role tend to think like building owners. They notice the things residents haven't reported yet, track patterns in recurring failures, and don't let punch lists linger. If you've managed turns at a Class A mid-rise or high-rise and kept delinquency in your maintenance queue close to zero, that experience translates directly here.

The salary range is $62,000 to $72,000, with additional bonus eligibility. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, 20 days of paid time off plus holidays, a 401k with company match, and tuition reimbursement.

greenhouse_4362002009.title: Bilingual Screening & Applications Specialist - Sandy Springs, GA
greenhouse_4362002009.rewritten_description:
A prospective resident calls in frustrated. Their application has been pending for two days, they're trying to move in before their lease ends across town, and they're not sure their documents uploaded correctly. Your job, in that moment, is to be the calm, competent voice that turns that anxiety into a clear next step.

Cortland, one of the largest multifamily owners and operators in the country, runs a centralized Contact Center that handles application processing and resident screening across its portfolio. This bilingual Screening and Applications Specialist role sits inside that operation, serving as the main point of contact for applicants from the moment they submit an application through move-in. The work is phone-heavy, documentation-intensive, and requires genuine patience alongside real organizational discipline.

What the Day Actually Looks Like

You'll be reviewing and processing rental applications, verifying documentation, and keeping applicants informed at each stage of the process. Calls, emails, and chat inquiries come in simultaneously, and you'll be managing multiple applicants at different points in the pipeline at any given time. When something stalls, whether a missing document or a compliance question, you're the one who figures out the path forward and communicates it clearly. De-escalating tense conversations is part of the job, and Fair Housing compliance is non-negotiable throughout.

Cortland uses platforms like RealPage, OneSite, and Funnel, so comfort with property management software matters. You'll also be working inside CRM tools and adapting to system updates as they roll out. The environment moves quickly and the volume is real.

Bilingual fluency is central to this role. Applicants who speak Spanish (or another language, depending on the market) deserve the same quality of communication as anyone else, and your ability to bridge that gap directly affects their experience and Cortland's conversion rates.

Who Fits Well Here

  • 2 or more years of customer service experience, preferably in a high-volume contact center or multifamily leasing environment
  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • Bilingual proficiency (English plus at least one additional language)
  • Demonstrated ability to handle confidential applicant information with care and discretion
  • Strong attention to detail when reviewing applications and verifying documents under volume pressure
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office and comfort with property management platforms
  • Flexibility to work weekends and extended hours when the business needs it

The candidates who tend to thrive in centralized leasing operations like this one aren't just organized. They're also good at reading the emotional temperature of a conversation and adjusting accordingly. Applicants are often stressed. They're making a significant financial and personal decision. The specialists who stand out treat that seriously without letting it slow down their throughput.

This role can serve as a strong foundation for moving into leasing management, compliance coordination, or operations roles within a large vertically integrated portfolio. Cortland handles design, construction, and property operations in-house, which means there's genuine internal mobility for people who perform well and want to grow.

greenhouse_5208797007.rewritten_description:
MG Properties runs apartment communities across the Western U.S. and has been doing it for over 30 years. Their portfolio spans acquisition, development, rehab, and day-to-day management. The Housekeeper role at Texcoco in San Diego is a ground-level position that directly affects how residents experience the property every single day.

What You'll Actually Do

This job covers the full footprint of a residential community. Common areas, hallways, laundry rooms, waste disposal areas, the leasing office, clubhouse, restrooms, and model units all fall under your scope. You'll also prep vacant apartments for incoming residents, which means cleaning and staging them to move-in-ready condition and keeping them that way until occupied.

Daily sanitizing of the leasing office and clubhouse is part of the routine. You'll also track cleaning supplies and flag shortages to management before they become a problem. Safety concerns you spot during your rounds get reported, not ignored.

What You Bring

  • Solid knowledge of cleaning chemicals and equipment, including safe handling and application
  • Strong attention to detail and consistent follow-through on cleanliness standards
  • Ability to work independently and manage your time without close supervision
  • Reliable transportation (required, no exceptions)
  • Punctuality and dependability as baseline work habits
  • A cooperative attitude when working alongside maintenance and leasing teams

Compensation and Context

Pay runs $21 to $23 per hour depending on experience. The role includes monthly bonuses, company profit sharing, a 401(k) with employer match, and full medical, dental, and vision coverage. PTO, paid holidays, personal days, and paid sick time are included. MG Properties also offers rental discounts, which matters if you're looking to live closer to where you work.

One thing worth knowing: make-ready cleaning on vacant units is where attention to detail gets tested most. A unit that looks clean on the surface but has grime in corners, residue in appliances, or smudged windows will get flagged during inspection. The strongest housekeepers in multifamily work treat every vacant unit like it's the one a prospective resident will walk through that afternoon, because sometimes it is.

greenhouse_8693453002.title: Maintenance Technician
greenhouse_8693453002.rewritten_description:
Maintenance work in single-family rental requires a specific kind of independence. You're not working alongside a team at one property. You're moving between houses across a market, diagnosing problems without a second opinion nearby, and closing out work orders through your phone. That's the core skill set this role runs on: self-directed troubleshooting, mobile-first field operations, and the hands-on range to handle HVAC, plumbing, and electrical without calling a specialist for every ticket.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Roofstock manages single-family rental homes, which shapes the day significantly. There's no leasing office to check into, no on-site team. You'll drive a company vehicle (gas card included) between properties across the Charlotte area, handling a mix of routine repairs, make-readies, and move-in and move-out inspections. When a unit turns, you're the one walking it, building the punch list, and getting it rent-ready. You'll also audit vendor work, which means you need to know what a completed job actually looks like, not just what was invoiced.

Work orders and communication run through mobile apps, so comfort with that workflow matters. Posting legal notices is part of the job too. Physical demands are real: expect lifting up to 50 pounds, climbing, bending, and working in both indoor and outdoor conditions depending on the day.

One thing worth noting directly: this role has no on-call requirement and no weekend schedule. In single-family rental, that's genuinely uncommon. Most technician roles in this space carry after-hours exposure. This one doesn't.

What Roofstock Needs From You

  • HVAC Type II Certification (required); Universal Certification preferred
  • Valid driver's license with a clean enough record to operate a company vehicle
  • Comfort working independently and managing your own daily schedule in the field
  • Strong diagnostic instincts across trades, especially when you're the only one on site
  • Ease with mobile apps for work order management and field communication
  • High school diploma or GED; U.S. work authorization required

What Makes This Role at Roofstock Distinctive

Single-family rental at scale is a relatively young model, and companies like Roofstock are still building out how field operations work efficiently across dispersed assets. That means technicians here tend to develop a broader operational view than those working traditional multifamily. You're not just fixing things. You're functioning as the eyes on properties that don't have on-site staff. Technicians who perform well in this environment often move into lead or regional field roles as portfolios grow, because the institutional SFR sector is still expanding and field-level experience is genuinely hard to find.

Pay runs $25 to $30 per hour based on experience, licensure, and location. The company provides a vehicle and gas card, a generous PTO policy with 12 paid holidays, 401k, parental leave, volunteer time off, and monthly subsidies for wellness and home office or cell phone costs. Health, dental, and vision coverage round out the package.

greenhouse_4362606009.title: Community Manager (Summer Oaks)
greenhouse_4362606009.rewritten_description:
A resident stops by the office with questions about their re-certification paperwork. Your maintenance tech radios in about a plumbing issue in building two. You've got a unit turn to track and a compliance deadline on Friday. That's a normal Tuesday at Summer Oaks.

MidPen Housing has operated affordable housing communities across Northern California since 1970, with a portfolio covering more than 142 properties and roughly 22,800 residents. Summer Oaks is one of those communities, and the Community Manager role here sits at the center of everything: compliance, facilities, resident relations, fiscal oversight, and staff development.

What This Role Covers

You'll report to the Property Manager and lead a small on-site team. Day-to-day, that means rent collection, delinquency management, bank deposits, and income verification. It also means keeping certifications current, processing applications and re-certifications, and maintaining accurate waitlists and resident files. Regulatory compliance is a constant: Fair Housing, HUD, TCAC, and local requirements all apply, and documentation needs to be tight.

On the facilities side, you'll set preventative maintenance schedules, conduct property inspections, and coordinate repairs. Curb appeal and unit turns are part of your scorecard. When a unit comes available, you're responsible for making sure it's ready and re-leased within established timeframes.

You'll also build relationships outside the property. That includes local community organizations, government contacts, and public safety partners. MidPen's Resident Services team works closely with site staff, so expect real collaboration there too.

What Qualifies You

  • Associate degree plus at least three years of multi-family residential management experience, with a minimum of two years in affordable housing (or an equivalent combination)
  • At least one year of supervisory experience
  • Tax Credit Specialist (TCS) or Certified Occupancy Specialist (COS) certification, or the ability to obtain one within six months (MidPen covers the cost)
  • Working knowledge of Fair Housing laws; ability to pass the FHA test within the first 60 days
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office and RealPage property management software
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including comfort interpreting regulatory documents

Pay runs $25.62 to $28.81 per hour based on experience. Company-provided on-site housing is available. Benefits include health, dental, vision, life and disability insurance, a 403(b) retirement plan, paid parental leave, education reimbursement, FSA options, an EAP, pet insurance, and paid time off including wellness days and company holidays.

The candidates who do well in this role tend to have two things in common: they understand the compliance side of affordable housing well enough to catch errors before they become audit findings, and they're steady under the kind of daily operational pressure that comes with managing a community where residents are dealing with real challenges. If you've worked in tax credit or HUD-regulated housing and you've led a team, this role is a direct fit.

greenhouse_4363024009.rewritten_description:
Evolve Soundside sits in Hampstead, NC, a coastal Pender County market that's grown steadily as buyers and renters migrate away from Wilmington's higher price points. Managing a community here means working with a resident base that often values the quieter, small-town feel while still expecting the amenities and service quality of a well-run Class A or B property. That context shapes what this Community Manager role actually looks like day to day.

Hawthorne Residential Partners, ranked among the top 50 multifamily management companies nationally and rooted in the Southeast, is hiring a Community Manager for this community. The scope is full-cycle: financial oversight, leasing performance, team development, vendor relationships, and resident experience all report through this position. You're the operator on the ground, which means the NOI story, the occupancy numbers, the delinquency report, and the culture of the leasing office are all yours to own.

Financially, you'll manage budgets, oversee rent collection, handle deposit accounting, and track delinquency with accuracy. Yardi and Knock are the primary platforms, so comfort with both is a real advantage coming in. On the leasing side, you'll drive renewals, set pricing strategy, support traffic conversion, and keep occupancy on target. You'll also conduct tours and guide prospects through the leasing process directly when the situation calls for it.

Team leadership is central here. You'll hire, train, and coach both office and maintenance staff, run weekly team meetings, and build a culture where accountability and support coexist. Resident escalations land with you, and you'll also oversee the community's online reputation and social media presence.

What separates strong candidates in this role is the ability to read a financial report and connect it to an operational decision the same day. Community managers who excel at Hawthorne aren't just people-first leaders; they understand how resident retention affects NOI, why delinquency trends matter before they become a month-end problem, and how to coach a leasing consultant on conversion without micromanaging every interaction. The financial fluency and the human fluency have to work together.

The schedule runs Monday through Friday with one weekday off to keep the week at 40 hours, plus Saturdays from 10 to 4. Some evening and weekend availability comes with the territory for resident events or community needs.

What Hawthorne Looks For

  • Two years of property management experience, including time as a Leasing Consultant and Assistant Community Manager
  • Six months of direct Community Manager experience in multifamily, strongly preferred
  • Working knowledge of Yardi, Knock, and Microsoft Office
  • High school diploma or GED required; CAM, CAPS, or a real estate license is a plus
  • Valid driver's license

Hawthorne's career path program is a real differentiator worth noting. Community Manager to Regional Manager is a documented trajectory, and the company's learning and development investment is structured around it. If you're stepping into this role with an eye on regional operations, the framework to get there exists here.

Compensation includes base salary plus monthly leasing and renewal commissions and quarterly performance bonuses. Benefits cover medical, dental, vision, 401k match, paid parental leave, pet insurance, and paid time off including your birthday.

greenhouse_4723135005.rewritten_description:
A Role Built on Sales Skill and Market Awareness

Leasing at a mixed portfolio site takes more than a friendly tour. At Prentiss Pointe Apartments and The Reserve, a new construction single-family homes community in Harrison Township, you're working two distinct product types simultaneously. That means reading prospects quickly, matching them to the right option, and closing consistently. Paragon Properties is looking for a Leasing Manager who brings real closing discipline, a 40 to 50 percent closing ratio is the expectation, not an aspiration, along with the analytical habits to track traffic patterns, monitor renewal pipelines, and run competitive market surveys monthly.

The Macomb County rental market sits in an interesting spot. Harrison Township draws renters who often compare it against options further up the lakeshore corridor or back toward Eastpointe and Roseville. Knowing your comp set cold, running monthly phone shops and quarterly in-person shops, matters here because prospects in this submarket do their homework. The Leasing Manager owns that competitive intelligence function directly.

Day-to-Day Responsibilities

The core of this role covers the full leasing cycle: touring market-ready units and models, reviewing and processing applications, managing the CRM queue, coordinating move-in orientations, and verifying renters insurance compliance at move-in. Beyond individual leasing, you'll manage lease expiration timelines, prepare weekly occupancy reports for operations and the Regional Manager, and actively work the renewal process alongside the property manager.

Marketing ownership is a real part of this position. You'll plan and execute site-level advertising, manage Facebook and Instagram presence, send weekly eblasts, and conduct outreach to local businesses and employers. Resident event planning also falls here. On the operational side, you'll enter service requests into Yardi, assist with market-ready unit inspections, and flag deficiencies before they become liabilities.

You'll also lead the leasing staff directly: running marketing meetings, coaching closing ratios, and modeling the professional standards Paragon expects across prospect and resident interactions.

What Strong Candidates Bring

  • At least one year of on-site leasing or assistant manager experience, with demonstrated sales performance
  • Yardi proficiency or comfort picking it up quickly
  • Solid working knowledge of Fair Housing guidelines at the federal, state, and local level
  • Strong written communication for CRM follow-up, eblasts, and social content
  • Experience running comp shops and translating that data into pricing or marketing adjustments
  • High school diploma required; college-level coursework strongly preferred

Candidates who stand out at this level typically combine consistent closing performance with genuine comfort in a coaching role. If you've only ever been an individual contributor in leasing, the shift to managing and motivating a team while still carrying your own closing expectations is the adjustment that trips most people up. Coming in with some experience leading peers, even informally, puts you ahead.

Compensation runs up to $24 per hour depending on experience, with monthly move-in bonuses, quarterly renewal bonuses, and a benefits package that includes medical, dental, and optical coverage with a short waiting period, company-paid life and disability insurance, a 401(k) with employer contribution, paid holidays, and a rent discount.

greenhouse_6139942004.title: Groundskeeper
greenhouse_6139942004.rewritten_description:
Grounds work at a multifamily property is more physical and more visible than most maintenance roles. Residents form their first impression of a community before they ever walk through a leasing office door, and the groundskeeper is the person who controls that impression every single day.

What the Work Looks Like

At The Westerly Apartments in Millcreek, the groundskeeper role covers the full range of exterior upkeep: trash and litter removal from common areas and pathways, sweeping and pressure washing building surfaces and walkways, basic gardening and weeding, cleaning windows and common area furniture, and handling general maintenance tasks tied to grounds and building repairs. This is active, on-your-feet work across the entire property. You'll climb stairs, use ladders, navigate uneven terrain, and regularly lift items up to 50 pounds. The ability to communicate clearly in English matters here too, both for processing work documentation and for interacting professionally with residents when your paths cross.

On-call availability for nights, weekends, and company events is part of the job. That's worth knowing upfront. Grounds conditions don't follow business hours, and a property that looks sharp Monday morning often required someone showing up on a Saturday.

Skills This Role Requires vs. Skills It Builds

What you bring to this role: physical stamina, attention to detail at a property-wide scale, and the self-direction to work through a task list without constant supervision. Grounds work rewards people who notice what others walk past, a piece of litter near the entry, a weed breaking through a seam, a scuff on a common area window.

What the role builds: a working understanding of how a multifamily property operates as a physical asset. Groundskeepers who pay attention learn how curb appeal connects to traffic and occupancy, how deferred exterior maintenance creates larger capex problems later, and how resident satisfaction ties directly to what the property looks like on the walk from the parking lot to the front door. For someone interested in growing into a porter, make-ready tech, or maintenance technician role, this is a legitimate starting point.

The Team and the Employer

Cottonwood Residential has a track record as an early adopter in multifamily operations, including self-guided tour technology that changes how prospects experience a community before they ever speak to a leasing agent. That culture of trying new approaches extends to how they support their on-site teams. Benefits here are available within the first 30 days and include full medical, vision, dental, life, and disability coverage, a 401k and HSA with company match, 10.5 paid holidays, and three weeks of paid time off available in the first year.

  • Full health, vision, dental, life, and disability insurance (available within 1 to 30 days)
  • 401k and HSA with company match
  • 120 hours (3 weeks) PTO eligible in year one
  • 10.5 paid holidays annually

If you take pride in how a property looks and want to build a foundation in multifamily operations, this role gives you both the daily craft and the team to grow with.

greenhouse_4362152009.title: Maintenance Supervisor (Nantucket Cove)
greenhouse_4362152009.rewritten_description:
Maintenance operations at a multifamily property don't fail because of one catastrophic event. They fail from accumulated deferred work, skipped PMs, and a team without clear direction. BAM Companies is hiring a Maintenance Supervisor at Nantucket Cove in Champaign, IL to make sure that doesn't happen on their watch.

This is a multisite role, which means your day isn't contained to one property. You're moving between communities, triaging work orders, checking on your team's output, and making sure preventative maintenance schedules are actually being followed rather than just documented. The mechanical side covers the full range: HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and general building systems. The leadership side is just as real. You're training technicians, giving feedback, and building a team that can execute without needing you to stand over every task.

What the Role Covers

  • Lead and train maintenance staff across properties in HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and general upkeep
  • Oversee preventative maintenance scheduling and ensure inspections happen on a consistent cycle
  • Manage supply purchasing and keep maintenance operations within budget
  • Hold properties to BAM's brand standards for curb appeal, common areas, and overall condition
  • Coach your team with hands-on support, structured feedback, and ongoing development

Qualifications BAM Is Looking For

  • 2 to 3 years of property maintenance experience; supervisory background is a plus
  • EPA Type 2 or Universal Certification required
  • Valid driver's license and reliable vehicle (multisite coverage makes this non-negotiable)
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills

Pay ranges from $26 to $29 per hour depending on experience, education, and other factors. BAM offers medical, dental, vision, and life insurance, plus 14.5 paid holidays and PTO that kicks in after 90 days. Rent discounts at BAM properties are also part of the package.

One thing worth noting for candidates considering this role: the multisite structure means your effectiveness shows up in aggregate metrics across properties. Turn times, PM completion rates, and work order close-out speed are all visible at the portfolio level. Supervisors who thrive here tend to be planners first and firefighters second. They build systems that reduce the number of emergencies, rather than simply responding well when one hits.

BAM was founded in 2010 and operates with a strong internal culture, referring to their team as the "BAMFAM." That's worth taking at face value if culture and team cohesion matter to you in a maintenance leadership role.

greenhouse_4362436009.title: Maintenance Technician
greenhouse_4362436009.rewritten_description:
Maintenance technicians at residential communities carry more of the resident experience than most people realize. The work is visible: a slow drain, a tripped breaker, a door that won't close right. When it gets fixed quickly and correctly, residents notice. When it doesn't, they remember. At Berkshire Residential Investments, the maintenance role at Tribeca Apartments sits at the center of that experience.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Day to day, you're keeping the property in shape: completing service requests, supporting the make-ready process on turns, doing your part to keep curb appeal where it needs to be. You'll work closely with property management to uphold community standards and make sure safety protocols stay in place. Inventory control, equipment maintenance, and key security all fall within your scope. None of it is glamorous, but all of it matters.

The role calls for a working knowledge across appliances, plumbing, electrical, carpentry, and general building maintenance. You don't need to be a licensed contractor in every trade, but you do need to be genuinely capable across them. The "jack of all trades" description gets used a lot in this field. Here it's accurate.

Who Fits Well Here

  • At least one year of hands-on maintenance experience in a residential community setting
  • Comfort with basic computer systems and work order platforms
  • Strong written and verbal communication in English
  • A service orientation that holds up on a hard day, not just an easy one

What separates strong candidates from average ones in this role is often attitude under pressure. Residents don't always present issues calmly. Requests stack up. Priorities shift. The technicians who thrive here take quality seriously without taking friction personally. They keep moving, stay organized, and treat every interaction with a resident as part of the job, not a distraction from it.

The Team and the Trajectory

Berkshire owns and manages its own properties, which means decisions get made closer to the ground level than at companies where management is third-party. That context matters for someone in maintenance: you're working within a structure that has a real stake in how the property performs, not just a management fee to protect.

The company offers three weeks of vacation, a 25% rent discount, personal development plans, and solid insurance coverage. Those are real benefits, and they reflect a team that's thought about retention. For someone looking to grow, a maintenance technician role at a company like this often leads toward lead tech or maintenance supervisor positions as you build a track record. Berkshire's emphasis on individual development plans suggests they're interested in that kind of growth conversation.

If you take pride in a well-kept property and want to work somewhere that takes its people seriously, this is worth a closer look.

greenhouse_4021810009.title: Maintenance Porter - Part-Time
greenhouse_4021810009.rewritten_description:
Curb appeal drives traffic. Traffic drives leases. And leases drive NOI. It's a chain that starts at the ground level, literally, which is why a property's porter role carries more operational weight than it might appear on an org chart.

Redstone Residential operates more than 38,000 beds across 20 states, making them one of the largest third-party student housing managers in the country. Their conventional multifamily portfolio is growing alongside that student housing base. At that scale, consistent community presentation isn't cosmetic, it's a performance metric.

What the Role Covers

This is a part-time porter position focused on the cleanliness, safety, and presentation of a Redstone community. The core of the job is keeping common areas, hallways, parking structures, and outdoor grounds in clean, safe, orderly condition. That includes clearing snow and ice, managing debris and animal waste, maintaining landscaping and flower beds, and keeping shared spaces like the clubhouse, leasing office, and model unit looking sharp at all times.

Beyond grounds and common area maintenance, you'll assist with basic repairs and general maintenance tasks as needed. The expectation is that you manage your daily responsibilities with minimal supervision and bring a genuinely friendly approach to every resident and team interaction you have on site.

Shifts run four to six hours, and the role requires the ability to lift 50-plus pounds and stay on your feet throughout. This is physical, hands-on work.

What Redstone Looks For

  • Prior janitorial or cleaning experience in a residential or commercial setting
  • A track record of completing daily tasks independently, without needing constant direction
  • A friendly, professional demeanor with residents and coworkers
  • Physical capability to lift 50-plus pounds and work full standing shifts
  • Willingness to participate in Redstone's required training programs

The candidates who stand out in porter roles at larger operators like Redstone tend to be the ones who treat curb appeal as a personal standard, not a checklist. A clean property signals to prospective residents that the management team is attentive, and that perception influences leasing decisions more than most people credit. Redstone offers a 401(k) plan with up to 6% matching for eligible employees.

greenhouse_5385162008.title: Apartment Maintenance Technician

What You'll Actually Do

This role puts you at the center of daily property operations at a Fairstead affordable housing community in Virginia Beach. Your week will include scheduled preventative maintenance on building systems, responding to resident work orders, and handling the turns between move-out and move-in. Make-readies are a real part of the job: cleaning and prepping vacated units so they're genuinely ready for incoming residents, not just surface-clean. You'll inspect electrical systems for code compliance, test safety devices monthly, maintain a working inventory of tools and supplies, and participate in the on-call rotation for after-hours emergencies. That last part is worth taking seriously. On-call is a real responsibility here, and the role rewards technicians who stay calm and organized when the phone rings at 10pm.

Fairstead operates as an integrated owner, operator, and developer across more than 30,000 units in 28 states, which means the maintenance function connects directly to a larger platform. Work orders, inspections, and inventory aren't just local tasks; they feed into data systems that help the organization track asset performance at scale. Technicians who document carefully and communicate clearly make a measurable difference in how well that system works.

What You Bring

  • Hands-on experience in a service technician or general maintenance role
  • Working knowledge of electrical systems: diagnosis and minor repairs
  • Mechanical aptitude across plumbing, appliances, and building fixtures
  • Physical capability to stand for extended periods and lift up to 70 pounds unassisted
  • Clear written and verbal communication, because work order notes and handoff logs matter
  • HVAC certification (EPA 608, CMRP, or equivalent) is preferred and will strengthen your candidacy
  • Attention to detail, especially on punch list items during make-readies and safety inspections

Skills This Role Builds

If you're early in your maintenance career, this position develops real breadth. Affordable housing properties typically run leaner than Class A market-rate communities, which means technicians here handle a wider range of work rather than specializing narrowly. You'll build competency across electrical, plumbing, HVAC, and unit turns. That breadth is exactly what companies look for when promoting to Lead Technician or Maintenance Supervisor. Technicians who combine strong trade skills with solid documentation habits, and who treat resident communication as part of the job rather than an interruption, tend to move up quickly in organizations like Fairstead that operate at scale. If you want to grow into a supervisory role, the exposure you get here is genuinely useful.

greenhouse_5385206008.title: Leasing Consultant
greenhouse_5385206008.rewritten_description:
What You'll Actually Do

This is a front-line leasing role at a Griffis Residential community in Shoreline, Washington. You'll handle the full prospect-to-resident cycle: fielding inquiries by phone, email, and walk-in, conducting tours, qualifying applicants, and getting leases signed. You'll also support renewals, coordinate move-in and move-out paperwork, and stay in contact with maintenance to make sure resident concerns get resolved without dragging.

Marketing support is part of the job too. That means helping the team promote the community and contributing to the reputation scores that factor directly into your quarterly bonus.

Speaking of which: the bonus structure here is tied to occupancy, online reputation, and retention. Bonuses start at $175 per lease and go up to $2,000 per year on the quarterly side. The base pay runs $23 to $25 per hour. You'll also get a 50% rental discount if you live onsite.

What You Bring

  • At least one year of onsite leasing experience in multifamily, hospitality, or a comparable sales environment
  • Solid communication skills across in-person, phone, and written channels
  • Familiarity with Fair Housing regulations (or a genuine willingness to get up to speed fast)
  • Comfort working weekends and occasional evenings
  • A high school diploma at minimum; a bachelor's degree or NALP certification is preferred
  • Detail orientation that holds up when you're juggling multiple prospects and lease files at once

A Few Things Worth Knowing

Shoreline sits just north of Seattle and has seen steady multifamily demand tied to light rail expansion along the 1 Line. Communities in this corridor tend to see consistent traffic, which means a leasing consultant here stays busy. Strong candidates will know how to prioritize warm leads without letting cold ones go cold entirely.

The benefits package is thorough: 11 paid holidays, three weeks of PTO accruing from day one, 401(k) with up to 4% company match, full medical/dental/vision, tuition reimbursement up to $5,250 per year, and paid parental leave. The wellness reimbursement and student loan PTO exchange program are less common in this segment and worth noting if those matter to you.

For someone early in a property management career, this role builds the core skills that feed into a leasing manager or assistant property manager position down the line. Griffis operates a national portfolio, so internal movement is a realistic path for strong performers.

workable_6022580.title: Maintenance Supervisor
workable_6022580.rewritten_description:
Maintenance supervisors in multifamily carry a split job. Part of the day is hands-on work. The other part is managing people, vendors, and schedules. PeakMade puts that split in writing: 60 to 70 percent of this role is direct repair and maintenance work, and the rest is supervision and coordination. If you want a pure desk job, this isn't it. If you want to stay in the field while building leadership experience, the structure fits.

What the Work Looks Like

This position covers a conventional apartment community in Olathe, Kansas. You'll own the service request queue: prioritizing, assigning, tracking completion, and stepping in to finish work when the team needs it. Daily property walks keep curb appeal and liability concerns in check. You'll also run the preventative maintenance program, manage shop inventory inside budget, and keep the maintenance space organized and OSHA-compliant.

Turn coordination is a real part of the job. You'll schedule and direct the team through make-ready cycles, supervise vendors and contractors during turns, and ensure vacant units are restored and ready for marketing. Unit inspections happen monthly. You'll also work with the Property Manager on budget performance and connect with the National Facilities Director when capital improvement bids are needed.

Technical scope includes HVAC, intermediate plumbing, intermediate electrical, appliances, carpentry, sheetrock, roofing, gutters, painting, irrigation, and landscaping. Pool care and small engine maintenance may apply depending on the community. EPA Type II certification is required before you start. CPO is preferred.

What PeakMade Needs From You

  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • At least 2 years of maintenance supervisory experience, multifamily preferred
  • EPA Type II certification required; CPO preferred
  • Valid driver's license, current auto insurance, and your own reliable vehicle
  • Must live within 30 miles of the property
  • Basic hand tools supplied by you, not the community
  • Ability to lift up to 50 pounds, work at heights, and perform physical tasks in outdoor temperatures above 90 or below 32 degrees

PeakMade operates student housing, multifamily, and build-to-rent communities across the country. This role sits in their multifamily portfolio. Candidates who do well in this type of position tend to be strong diagnosticians who can also communicate clearly with residents and hold contractors accountable during turns. The leadership piece matters as much as the technical piece once you're in the supervisor seat.

Benefits include PTO, wellbeing days, 401(k) match, paid parental leave, technical certification support for HVAC and CPO, monthly renewal bonuses, and a facilities leadership development program for those who want to move up.

workable_5901643.title: Leasing Consultant - Portland Oregon
workable_5901643.rewritten_description:
The leasing consultant role sits at the front edge of a property's revenue. Every lease signed, every prospect converted, every renewal retained flows through this position first. At Karya Property Management's Portland-area community, that responsibility belongs to you.

What You'll Actually Do

Your day centers on converting traffic into signed leases. That means greeting prospects, walking them through the property, and presenting the community's features in a way that connects to what they're actually looking for in a home. You'll explain lease terms clearly, including the TAA Lease Contract, so future residents understand exactly what they're signing before move-in day arrives.

Beyond the initial sale, you'll coordinate move-in packets, prepare units, and manage the day-of experience for incoming residents. You'll also do at least one full property walk daily to assess curb appeal and flag anything that needs attention before a prospect sees it. Resident events and marketing coordination fall into this role as well, so there's a creative side alongside the sales work.

Weekend and evening availability on a rotating schedule is part of the job. Leasing traffic doesn't follow a Monday-through-Friday pattern, and the strongest consultants treat weekend shifts as opportunities rather than inconveniences.

What You Bring

  • High school diploma or equivalent required; a college degree is preferred
  • Clear, confident verbal and written communication skills
  • Strong customer service instincts with residents, prospects, and vendors
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office, Word, and Outlook
  • A sense of urgency and the ability to manage competing deadlines
  • Physical ability to walk the property daily, climb stairs, and lift up to 15 pounds

Skills This Role Builds

A leasing consultant role is where most property management careers start, and for good reason. You'll develop a working command of lease administration, fair housing compliance, and the full prospect-to-resident lifecycle. The objection-handling and closing skills you build here translate directly into assistant manager and property manager roles, where leasing performance becomes one of several metrics you're responsible for rather than your primary focus. Consultants who learn to read traffic patterns, track their own closing ratios, and take ownership of curb appeal tend to move up faster because they're already thinking like operators.

What separates a strong candidate here is the ability to hold a genuine conversation with a prospect while staying accurate on lease terms and community details. The sales piece matters, but residents who feel well-informed at move-in create fewer headaches down the line and renew at higher rates. If you bring that combination of warmth and precision, this is a solid place to build the foundation of a property management career.

smartrecruiters_744000142925441.title: Apartment Maintenance Technician - Verdant Peachtree Creek
smartrecruiters_744000142925441.rewritten_description:
Maintenance work in multifamily housing covers a wide range of skill levels, and this role at AIR Communities' Verdant Peachtree Creek community in Atlanta sits squarely in the hands-on technical tier. You'll carry out resident service requests, complete turns to get units ready for incoming residents, and handle routine upkeep across plumbing, electrical, HVAC, appliances, and carpentry. The expectation is that you're already proficient in at least two of those trades and can move through work orders independently with general direction rather than constant supervision.

What this role builds on top of that foundation is real breadth. Because community needs shift by season and by what mechanical systems are in play, you won't spend every week doing the same two tasks. One stretch might be weighted toward HVAC as summer leasing ramps up; another might call for more appliance work and punch list completion during a turn cycle. Technicians who stay curious about the trades they're weaker in tend to develop faster here than those who stay in their lane.

AIR uses technology to manage task flow and prioritization, which means you'll work with digital tools to track and close out work orders rather than relying on paper logs or verbal handoffs. That's worth knowing if you're coming from a smaller operation where systems were informal. The upside is that organized shops and stocked supplies are part of the model, so you spend less time hunting for parts and more time actually fixing things.

The role pays $23.00 to $26.00 per hour depending on your experience and trade skill level, and there's a quarterly customer service bonus structure that can add up to $250 per month for technicians who consistently earn strong resident satisfaction scores. A 50% rent discount at any AIR community is also available, which matters if you want to eliminate your commute by living onsite.

What you'll need coming in

  • At least two years of maintenance experience in a facilities or building environment
  • Proficiency in two or more trades: plumbing, electrical, HVAC, appliance repair, carpentry
  • Willingness to work flexible hours including evenings, weekends, and on-call shifts (roughly one week per month)
  • Reliable transportation for after-hours emergency response
  • Physical ability to move heavy equipment and machinery as needed

One thing worth understanding about on-call in multifamily: it's not decorative. Residents call when something fails, and that includes nights and weekends. If you've done on-call before, you already know how to triage what's urgent versus what can wait until morning. If you haven't, that judgment develops quickly and it's one of the more transferable skills this role gives you, applicable at any property type or ownership structure you work for later in your career.

AIR's internal development program, Ascend, is designed to map a path forward based on where you want to go, whether that's a lead technician role, a service manager position, or something more specialized. The company has a stated preference for internal promotion, so the ceiling here is higher than the job title suggests.

greenhouse_7856003003.title: Maintenance Technician - Cielo
greenhouse_7856003003.rewritten_description:
A resident submits a work order at 8 AM: no hot water. By 9, you've diagnosed a faulty heating element, swapped it out, and updated the ticket in the system before the office team even opens their email. That rhythm, moving from diagnosis to resolution without a lot of hand-holding, is what this role runs on.

The Work at Cielo

Cielo is an Olympus Property community in Charlotte, and this full-time Maintenance Technician position runs Monday through Friday, 9 AM to 6 PM, with emergency availability when needed. You'll work alongside the Lead Maintenance Technician and the broader service team, handling the full scope of day-to-day repairs: HVAC maintenance and filter changes, plumbing repairs and fixture replacements, appliance work across refrigerators, washers, dryers, ovens, and stoves, electrical switches and fixtures, and lock changes or door repairs. Preventative maintenance on HVAC units, including coil cleaning, is a regular part of the calendar. You'll also help maintain grounds, common areas, and pool areas, and keep the maintenance shop organized and properly stocked. Work orders get tracked through property management software, so staying current on documentation matters as much as the wrench work.

The pay range starts at $24 to $25 per hour, with monthly and quarterly bonuses on top of base pay. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401(k) with employer matching, short and long-term disability, life insurance, paid time off, an apartment rental allowance, educational assistance, and pet insurance.

What Olympus Looks For

  • At least two years of maintenance experience in residential, apartment, or commercial settings
  • Working knowledge of HVAC systems; an EPA 608 certification or HVAC license is a plus
  • Hands-on comfort with plumbing, electrical, carpentry, painting, and appliance repair
  • Ability to operate hand tools and power tools safely and independently
  • Willingness to be available for emergency calls outside regular hours

Olympus has earned a spot on the National Apartment Association's Top Employer list for 2023, 2024, and 2025. That kind of recognition tends to reflect how a company treats people day to day, and the benefit package and bonus structure here back it up.

From a career standpoint, a role like this builds the kind of documented, multi-trade experience that moves technicians toward Lead Technician and eventually Service Manager positions. Technicians who develop strong HVAC diagnostic skills in particular tend to have real leverage in the market, since that competency is consistently hard for operators to find. Two or three years of solid work order history, good resident interaction habits, and a growing EPA certification puts you in a strong position for the next step up in portfolio management.

greenhouse_8120450.title: Leasing Consultant - Part Time
greenhouse_8120450.rewritten_description:
It's Saturday morning, a prospect walks in five minutes before their tour, and two current residents are waiting at the desk with questions. That's a pretty average Saturday in leasing. If that scenario sounds manageable rather than overwhelming, keep reading.

The Role at Bexley Village at Concord Mills

Weinstein Properties has been family-owned and operated for over 70 years, with a portfolio of more than 60 apartment communities across Virginia, North Carolina, Texas, Tennessee, and Georgia. That longevity isn't accidental. The company runs a hands-on operation and has built a reputation for developing people from within. This part-time Leasing Consultant position at their Concord Mills location reflects that philosophy directly.

The schedule runs approximately 20 hours per week. Saturdays are part of the rotation, and weekday hours fall in the 9am to 6pm window with some flexibility on which days you work. Pay starts at $18 per hour and increases based on experience, with quarterly bonuses added on top.

Day to day, you'll handle prospect traffic, conduct tours, follow up on leads, and convert interest into signed leases. That's the sales side. You'll also handle administrative tasks, address resident concerns, assist with property appearance, and occasionally support resident events. In leasing, everyone does a little of everything, and Weinstein is straightforward about that expectation.

What They're Looking For

Weinstein is genuinely open to candidates without prior leasing experience. The training program is real, not a disclaimer. That said, a few qualities tend to separate people who thrive in this role from those who struggle:

  • Clear, warm communication, both in person and in writing
  • A customer-first instinct, especially when a situation gets uncomfortable
  • Comfort with shifting priorities mid-day without losing composure
  • Willingness to pitch in on tasks outside your immediate lane
  • Goal orientation and basic organizational discipline

The people who do well here tend to be the ones who treat a prospect walking through the door with the same energy at 5pm as they did at 9am. Consistency matters more than flash in leasing.

One honest note worth mentioning: this is a physically active role. You'll be on your feet, walking units, inspecting make-readies, and engaging with people throughout your shift. It's not a desk job, and Weinstein is clear about that upfront.

For someone looking to build a career in property management, leasing is the standard entry point, and for good reason. You learn traffic patterns, closing techniques, resident relations, and the operational rhythms of a property all at once. Many regional managers and corporate roles in this industry trace back to a leasing desk. Weinstein's internal promotion history reflects that path.

Weinstein Properties is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

greenhouse_8700296002.title: Assistant Community Manager
greenhouse_8700296002.location: Central House Columbia, 3200 South Rock Quarry Road, Columbia, MO 65201
greenhouse_8700296002.rewritten_description:
Skills This Role Runs On

Student housing puts a specific set of demands on an Assistant Community Manager that conventional multifamily doesn't. You'll use your financial acumen daily: posting damage charges from quarterly inspections, reconciling accounts receivable at month end, keeping delinquency under 2%, and managing utility billing with the kind of consistency that makes audits uneventful. Alongside that, you'll work the sales side, conducting weekly market surveys, tracking KPIs, managing concessions within budget, and directing leasing activity to hit occupancy and revenue targets. The operational and financial threads run in parallel here, and the ability to hold both at once is what separates a strong ACM from one who's perpetually behind.

Entrata proficiency matters at this property. Scion lists it as preferred, and in student housing that preference is usually a soft requirement once you're in the seat. Move-in assignments, room transfers, move-outs, and resident account management all flow through the system. If you've worked in Entrata, you'll recognize the workflow. If you haven't, plan to get comfortable with it fast.

What the Role Actually Covers

This is a full-scope ACM position at Central House Columbia, a student community on South Rock Quarry Road. The General Manager owns the asset's overall performance, and you support that directly while running your own lane across operations, leasing, resident relations, and staff development.

  • Coach and hold accountable onsite staff, including coverage for after-hours on-call rotation
  • Own resident account management: AR reconciliation, NSF and late fee enforcement, move-out billing and deposit disposition
  • Lead and execute annual turn alongside the GM, which in student housing is a compressed, high-volume process requiring precise coordination
  • Inspect vacant units monthly and walk grounds and common areas regularly to maintain curb appeal and code compliance
  • Coordinate work orders with maintenance staff and vendors
  • Handle escalated resident concerns and manage eviction filings in accordance with local ordinances and company policy
  • Manage promotional materials, marketing messaging, and local outreach to drive traffic during lease-up cycles
  • Step into the GM role during absences, which means you need to understand the full picture, not just your own tasks

A word on the turn: at a student property, the annual turn is its own season. Hundreds of move-outs and move-ins compressed into a short window, punch lists running simultaneously across the building, damage assessments, billing, key exchanges. If you've done it before, you know. If you haven't, expect the first one to be a steep and instructive week.

What's Distinctive About This Role at Scion

Scion operates at scale in the student housing sector, which means the systems, training infrastructure, and operational playbooks are more developed than you'd find at a smaller regional operator. There's genuine room to grow here. ACMs at student properties who handle the financial side well tend to move into GM roles faster than their conventional multifamily counterparts, partly because the operational complexity of student housing translates cleanly to larger assets.

Scion also offers learning reimbursement, which is worth noting if you're considering credentials or continuing education in property management. The benefit structure includes health, dental, vision, 401k matching, and paid parental leave, along with a discretionary annual bonus.

You need at least one year of experience in property management or a residential community setting. Strong written and verbal communication is non-negotiable in a role that involves resident notices, staff coaching, and direct leasing conversations. The detail orientation required here is real: this isn't the kind of position where close enough works on account reconciliation or Fair Housing compliance.

greenhouse_7859955003.title: Maintenance Technician I (Crystal Springs Terrace)
greenhouse_7859955003.rewritten_description:
It's 7:45 a.m. and you've already got three service requests queued, a unit turning Friday, and a resident at the office door with a leaky faucet. That's a normal Tuesday at a Prometheus property.

Prometheus Real Estate Group is hiring a Maintenance Technician I at Crystal Springs Terrace in San Bruno, California. This is a general maintenance role covering the full scope of day-to-day upkeep: service requests, apartment turns, and the ongoing repairs that keep a residential community running. The pay range sits at $27.75 to $28.75 per hour, with standby and on-call premium pay on top of that.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Turns are a significant part of this role. You'll move through punch lists, handle make-ready prep, and coordinate repairs across appliances, plumbing, carpentry, electrical, and paint. Beyond turns, you're fielding resident service requests and troubleshooting mechanical systems, both major and minor. Prometheus calls their residents "Neighbors," and that framing reflects something real about how they expect their maintenance team to operate: with care and responsiveness, not just technical competency. Residents notice the difference between a tech who fixes the problem and one who also treats the interaction like it matters.

On-call availability is required. If that's new to you, budget some mental energy for it. It's a real part of the job, not a footnote.

What Prometheus Is Looking For

  • At least two years of apartment maintenance experience
  • Working knowledge of appliances, plumbing, basic electrical, carpentry, and paint
  • High school diploma or GED
  • Basic computer proficiency
  • Ability to lift up to 50 lbs. occasionally; comfortable working outdoors in moderate temperatures
  • Clear written and verbal communication in English

The benefits package here is genuinely strong by industry standards. Prometheus covers 100% of medical, vision, and dental premiums, including eligible dependents, with buy-up options available. There's a 401(k) with employer matching, a behavioral health program accessible around the clock, paid volunteer time, and tenure-based housing discounts that become more meaningful the longer you stay. They also offer a semi-annual discretionary bonus and several bonus categories tied to specific performance milestones, including renovation and lease-up bonuses that can apply depending on property needs at a given time.

For technicians who want a clear path upward, this kind of role builds the foundation. Strong performers in Technician I positions typically move toward lead tech or maintenance supervisor roles as they accumulate experience across more complex systems and demonstrate reliability on call rotation. The San Bruno Bay Area market means properties generally run at high occupancy with demanding resident expectations. That pressure sharpens your skills faster than a slower-moving market would.

greenhouse_5387325008.title: Maintenance Supervisor
greenhouse_5387325008.rewritten_description:
Hillpointe builds and operates market-rate workforce housing across the Sun Belt, and they do it vertically integrated: land acquisition, construction, procurement, and asset management all run in-house. That means the maintenance team isn't just servicing a stabilized asset. They're also expected to support lease-up communities as they come online and get to occupancy.

What the Role Actually Covers

As Maintenance Supervisor, you own the full physical operation of the community. Service requests, preventative maintenance, make-ready turns, grounds and amenity appearance, vendor oversight, and inventory management all fall under your scope. On the make-ready side, you're managing inspections and repairs on vacant units to keep them rent-ready and minimize days off-market. Every day a unit sits unready is a day of lost rent, so turn speed and punch list quality matter directly to NOI.

You'll also conduct safety meetings, maintain OSHA compliance, and inspect work completed by contractors and your own team. Hillpointe's development pipeline means you may periodically assist with the setup and stabilization of new communities as they open, which gives this role exposure beyond typical property maintenance work.

On-call rotation is real here. Evenings, weekends, and early mornings are part of the schedule, and after-hours emergency response is expected. That's standard for this level in multifamily, but worth knowing going in.

Certifications and Qualifications

  • EPA Type I and II or Universal refrigerant certification (required)
  • CPO certification preferred, or willingness to obtain it
  • All state and local certifications as required by jurisdiction
  • Valid driver's license
  • Proficiency with hand tools, mechanical equipment, and basic office software
  • High school diploma, GED, or equivalent hands-on experience
  • Physical ability to lift up to 50 lbs regularly, climb ladders, and work in variable outdoor conditions

What Sets Strong Candidates Apart

The supervisory piece matters as much as the technical skills here. Hillpointe is a top-ranked NMHC builder and developer with multiple communities in various stages across the Sun Belt. A candidate who can train and onboard new maintenance staff, hold vendors accountable on quality and timeline, and keep a punch list moving without hand-holding will outperform someone who's only strong on the wrench side. Jacksonville's heat and humidity also mean HVAC and pool systems take real abuse in summer, so hands-on mechanical troubleshooting in those areas is a genuine day-to-day advantage. The candidates who grow fastest in roles like this tend to move into Regional Maintenance Director positions as a company scales its portfolio.

Built on its long and proven track record of real estate development, the firm’s investment approach is centered around its in-house general contracting expertise, enabling direct control of cost and delivery timeframe. For each project, Hillpointe directly controls land acquisition, land development, construction, procurement of building materials, asset management, and capital markets. CPO certification is preferred (be willing to obtain) Must have all certifications as required by State and Local jurisdictions. Must have a valid driver’s license. PHYCIAL REQUIREMENTS: Ability to lift, push, pull and carry up to 50lbsregularly and occasionally heavier loads. Frequent standing, walking, bending, stooping, kneeling, and crouching. greenhouse_4363986009.title: Business Manager 1500-2500 - Remote, Washington
greenhouse_4363986009.rewritten_description:
Remote accounting roles in multifamily tend to get underestimated. The title says "Business Manager," but the actual work sits at the intersection of collections strategy, resident relations, and operational compliance across a significant portfolio. At Berkshire Residential Investments, this role covers communities in the 1,500 to 2,500 unit range, which means the decisions you make on delinquency and account management carry real NOI weight.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Your day centers on resident accounts and the financial health of multiple communities. You'll pursue recovery of delinquent balances, coordinate with attorneys when accounts reach eviction action, and ensure that process stays compliant with state and local law. You'll process security deposit dispositions, manage former resident accounts through collections, and handle FAS processing. Beyond the collections cycle, you're also reviewing rental applications and approving or flagging prospects, which means you're touching the front end of occupancy as well as the back end of delinquency.

The role is remote, but it's not independent. You'll work closely with on-site property management teams to keep resident ledgers accurate and to coordinate eviction and abandoned unit timelines. The flexible 40-hour schedule adjusts to the time zone needs of the properties you support, so your day may shift depending on where your communities are located.

  • Three or more years in property management, with multifamily experience preferred
  • At least two years in accounts receivable or payable
  • Two or more years in customer service or sales
  • Yardi experience strongly preferred
  • Strong communication skills across both property teams and residents
  • Comfort working independently in a remote environment with multiple properties

Skills That Compound From Here

This role builds a specific and transferable skill set. Managing delinquency across 1,500 to 2,500 units at once trains you to think at portfolio scale, not just property level. That's the kind of exposure that typically positions people for regional accounting roles, compliance-focused positions, or transitions into asset management support. The application review component adds leasing and risk assessment judgment to your profile, which makes you more rounded than a pure collections specialist. If you're three to five years into multifamily and want to build depth on the financial operations side, this is a logical next step.

Berkshire owns and manages its own properties, which means you're working within a vertically integrated structure. That matters because your counterparts on-site have real authority and real accountability, and so do you. The collaboration here isn't just coordination; it directly affects occupancy outcomes and community financial performance.
