greenhouse_8719845002.rewritten_description:
Pacific City sits in a stretch of the Oregon Coast that draws vacation traffic year-round, not just in summer. The combination of beach access, state park proximity, and short driving distance from Portland means short-term rental turnover here is real and recurring. Keeping those homes guest-ready between stays requires someone who can move quickly, spot problems before guests do, and take ownership of the physical condition of each property.

Roofstock, which expanded into short-term rental management through its 2025 stake in Casago, is hiring a Hospitality Coordinator to serve as the field-level operator for a portfolio of STR homes in this market. The pay is $22.50 per hour, and the company provides a $135 monthly car allowance plus $100 monthly for tools and equipment. The schedule is full-time with two days off per week, but availability for weekends, holidays, early mornings, and evenings is a genuine requirement, not a formality.

The work centers on keeping homes functional, clean, and stocked for every arrival. That means pre- and post-stay inspections, restocking consumables, handling light maintenance tasks like bulb replacements or TV resets, resetting decor, making beds, removing trash, and leaving welcome touches for incoming guests. When something goes wrong mid-stay, you're the person dispatched to handle it on the ground. You'll document issues through task management tools, flag supply irregularities, and coordinate with a maintenance team when a problem goes beyond your scope. You'll also support Hospitality Managers with dispatching during off-peak hours and cover other zones in the market when volume requires it.

This role reports to a Team Lead within Hospitality Ops. Performance is measured against guest review scores (the portfolio target is a 4.8 average or higher), inspection completion rates, task accuracy, and how consistently homes meet brand standards between stays.

What Roofstock is looking for

  • At least one year of experience in hospitality, vacation rental care, property maintenance, or a closely related field
  • Reliable, detail-oriented, and able to follow brand checklists consistently across multiple properties
  • Physically capable of lifting up to 50 lbs and moving through properties on foot throughout a shift
  • Comfortable with mobile apps and task tracking software
  • Valid driver's license and a reliable personal vehicle
  • Available to work weekends, holidays, and on-call rotations

The candidates who do well in this type of role tend to be self-managing in the field. A team lead isn't walking properties with you. You're reading a checklist, making judgment calls about what needs to be flagged versus fixed on the spot, and moving on to the next home on time. Guest review scores in the STR space respond quickly to small oversights, so the attention-to-detail requirement here is tied directly to measurable outcomes, not just a hiring preference.

greenhouse_8722782002.title: Assistant Community Manager
greenhouse_8722782002.rewritten_description:
The Scion Group operates student housing at scale, and 44 North in Minneapolis reflects that model: a community where occupancy pressure, lease-up timing, and resident satisfaction all hit at once, usually during the same week. The Assistant Community Manager title here carries real operational weight. Scion calls the role Resident Services Manager internally, and the scope matches: this person owns the resident experience from move-in to move-out while keeping leasing workflows, delinquency follow-up, and compliance processes moving in parallel.

Day to day, you're watching the Entrata dashboard the way a revenue manager watches a hotel's booking curve. Delinquency notices go out on schedule. Lease documents get generated, reviewed, and countersigned under the General Manager's direction. Move-in inspections get coordinated. When a resident dispute escalates, you're the one mediating it before it becomes a negative review or a legal matter. Reputation management across review platforms is an explicit part of the job, which means your resident interactions have a measurable downstream effect on traffic and lease conversion.

The leasing support component is real. You're not running the leasing team, but you provide backup on lead follow-up, sales calls, and lease execution when volume demands it. During peak move-in periods, which in student housing often means a compressed August window where hundreds of residents arrive in days, evening and weekend availability is expected. The role also calls for occasional support at other properties in the Scion portfolio, so comfort operating outside your home community matters.

Student housing creates a specific operational challenge worth naming: residents are often first-time renters, which means the volume of service requests, questions, and complaints runs higher than at a conventional multifamily property. Strong candidates come in with conflict resolution instincts already developed, not just customer service polish. The ability to handle a crisis call, a delinquency escalation, and a resident event all in the same day without losing composure is the real differentiator here.

  • Organized enough to track renewals, notices, insurance compliance, and leasing metrics concurrently

Community Manager at Encore at Heritage, Wake Forest, NC

Community Manager roles at mid-size multifamily operators tend to split your time three ways: keeping the financials on track, keeping the team focused, and keeping residents happy enough to renew. At Hawthorne Residential Partners, a Southeast-rooted company that ranks among the top 50 multifamily management companies nationally, this position at Encore at Heritage in Wake Forest carries all three responsibilities with real authority behind them.

What the Job Actually Covers

You run the community. That means owning the budget, managing delinquency, overseeing deposit accounting, and reading financial reports well enough to make decisions from them. Yardi and Knock are the primary tools here, so familiarity with both saves you a significant ramp-up period.

On the leasing side, you're not just supervising. You'll conduct tours, respond to leads, and guide prospects through the process yourself when needed. Renewals, occupancy goals, and pricing strategy all sit on your plate. You'll also manage the community's social media presence, which increasingly drives traffic at the property level.

Team leadership is a core part of the role. You hire, train, and coach both office and maintenance staff. Weekly team meetings, performance accountability, and day-to-day support are expected, not optional. You'll also handle escalated resident concerns and plan resident events, which requires some flexibility on evenings and Saturdays.

The schedule runs Monday through Friday, 9 AM to 6 PM, with Saturdays from 10 AM to 4 PM. One weekday off per week keeps the total at 40 hours, though community needs can occasionally shift that.

What Hawthorne Is Looking For

  • High school diploma or GED; two years of property management experience covering both leasing consultant and assistant manager work
  • Six months of experience as a community manager in multifamily, highly preferred
  • Yardi, Knock, and Microsoft Office proficiency, highly preferred
  • Valid driver's license required; CAM, CAPS, or a real estate or property management license preferred

The candidates who perform best in this type of role can read a financial report and act on it, defuse a difficult resident situation without escalating it further, and hold their team accountable while still being someone people want to work for. Those two things, financial clarity and people judgment, tend to separate strong community managers from average ones more than any credential does.

Compensation and Growth

Salary is supplemented by monthly leasing and renewal commissions plus quarterly performance bonuses. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401k match, paid time off (including your birthday), pet insurance, paid parental and adoption leave, telehealth access, and company-paid life insurance.

Hawthorne runs a formal career path program, and the internal trajectory from Community Manager to Regional Manager is a stated priority, not just recruiting language. The Learning and Development team is structured to support that progression.

greenhouse_6145251004.title: Maintenance Supervisor at Raveneaux Apartments
greenhouse_6145251004.rewritten_description:
Raveneaux Apartments is a multifamily community in Houston managed by Cottonwood Residential, a fully integrated real estate company with a national portfolio. The Maintenance Supervisor role here carries real weight. You're the person residents think of when something goes wrong, the person your techs look to when priorities shift mid-morning, and the person ownership counts on to keep costs in line without letting the property slip. That's a lot of relationships to manage well, and it's worth being honest about that from the start.

Day to day, you're running maintenance operations end to end. That means owning the make-ready process, keeping the preventative maintenance schedule from becoming a wishlist, and making sure work orders don't age out in the system. You'll also be hands-on when the situation calls for it, working across HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and general repairs alongside your team rather than just delegating from a distance. Vendor coordination is a meaningful part of this job too. Scheduling, supervising scope, holding people accountable to timelines. Houston's vendor market is active and competitive, so knowing how to build productive working relationships with reliable contractors matters more than it might in smaller markets.

The leadership piece is where this role gets nuanced. You'll hire, onboard, train, and coach your service team, which means you're responsible for both their output and their development. That's not always easy. Techs come in with different skill levels, different work styles, and sometimes different ideas about urgency. The supervisors who do well in this kind of role tend to be direct communicators who set clear expectations without micromanaging, and who understand that retention on the maintenance side often comes down to whether people feel respected and supported on the job.

Cottonwood also expects you to stay close to the numbers. You'll manage maintenance-related expenses against the property budget, support purchase order processes, and keep documentation accurate, including SDS logs and vendor records. Resident communication runs through this role as well. When a service request sits too long or something gets missed, it's usually the maintenance supervisor who fields the follow-up, whether that's from the resident directly or from the leasing office.

What You'll Need

  • High school diploma or GED
  • Valid driver's license and reliable transportation
  • At least 2 years of multifamily maintenance experience
  • At least 2 years supervising or leading a maintenance team
  • EPA Type II or Universal certification (required)
  • CPO certification (preferred)
  • CAMT certification (preferred)
  • Solid working knowledge of HVAC, plumbing, and electrical systems
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office; experience with Entrata is a plus
  • Availability for evenings, weekends, and on-call rotation
  • Ability to lift up to 75 lbs. regularly, with assistance for heavier loads

Candidates who stand out tend to have a track record of low delinquency on their work order queues and can speak specifically to how they've developed junior techs. If you've overseen a lease-up or brought a neglected property back to standard, that experience translates directly here. Cottonwood is growing nationally, and supervisors who demonstrate operational discipline and people leadership tend to find real advancement opportunities within the portfolio.

Skills This Role Puts to Work Every Day

The Assistant Community Manager position at Waypoint Management Services in Davenport, FL sits at a useful intersection: part financial analyst, part leasing coach, part operations generalist. You'll spend meaningful time on delinquency tracking, rent collection, and reporting, which means your ability to read a rent roll and connect financial performance to operational decisions gets a real workout. At the same time, you're supporting the leasing team's training and day-to-day performance, so your communication and coaching instincts matter just as much as your spreadsheet fluency.

Yardi experience carries real weight here. If you've already worked in Yardi, you'll move faster through lease records, make-ready schedules, occupancy reports, and renewal tracking. If you haven't, it's learnable, but the preference signals that Waypoint runs a data-forward operation where accuracy in the system isn't optional.

What the Work Actually Involves

Day to day, you're partnering with the Community Manager to keep operations running across leasing, financial management, and resident relations. That includes:

  • Supporting leasing team performance and helping execute sales and marketing strategies
  • Conducting and interpreting market surveys to inform pricing and occupancy recommendations
  • Managing rent collection, tracking delinquencies, and supporting eviction processes when necessary
  • Maintaining accurate lease files, rent rolls, and resident records
  • Monitoring make-ready schedules and renewal pipelines
  • Staying current on competitor activity and local market conditions
  • Supporting compliance with federal, state, and local regulations

Weekend availability is part of the rotation. Multifamily communities don't pause on Saturdays, and the Assistant Community Manager role reflects that reality.

Where This Role Tends to Lead

The ACM position is one of the most reliable proving grounds in multifamily. You're close enough to the financial reporting to understand NOI drivers, close enough to leasing to develop traffic and conversion instincts, and close enough to operations to learn what makes a make-ready schedule actually hold. Professionals who do this role well and build fluency across all three areas typically move into Community Manager positions within one to three years, and the ones who distinguish themselves are usually the ones who treat the financial side as seriously as the resident-facing side.

Waypoint's benefits package includes monthly leasing and renewal bonuses, medical, dental, and vision coverage starting on day one, a 401k with company match, 120 hours of PTO in year one, and an employee housing discount program. The professional development training is worth noting if you're thinking about this role as a step rather than a destination.

Two years of leasing, sales, or hospitality experience is the baseline. A high school diploma or equivalent is required, and you'll need a valid driver's license. Strong Microsoft Office skills and comfort with social media round out the profile Waypoint is looking for.

greenhouse_4372008009.title: Maintenance Technician (Nantucket Cove)
greenhouse_4372008009.rewritten_description:
Maintenance technicians at apartment communities wear a lot of hats, and the role at Nantucket Cove in Champaign is no different. BAM Companies has been managing residential properties since 2010, and this position sits at the center of daily community operations, from routine work orders to after-hours calls that keep residents feeling taken care of.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Most of your days will move between scheduled work orders and preventative maintenance tasks. You might start the morning turning an apartment unit, running through a punch list to get it make-ready before a new resident moves in. By afternoon, you could be troubleshooting an HVAC system, clearing a plumbing clog, or handling a minor electrical repair. The work is genuinely varied, and that's part of what keeps it engaging. You'll also be expected to document maintenance needs proactively, catching small issues before they become expensive problems.

After-hours support is part of this role. Emergencies don't follow a schedule, and residents rely on the maintenance team when something goes wrong at night or on weekends. If that's a dealbreaker, it's worth knowing upfront. If you're the type who takes pride in being the person who shows up and gets it handled, it's one of the more satisfying parts of the job.

What BAM Is Looking For

  • Two to three years of hands-on maintenance experience, ideally in a residential or multifamily setting
  • Comfort working across HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and general building systems
  • A valid driver's license
  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • EPA Type 2 or Universal certification is a plus, not a hard requirement
  • Clear, respectful communication with residents and teammates alike

The candidate who tends to thrive in a role like this is someone who self-manages well. Maintenance techs often work without a supervisor looking over their shoulder. You're trusted to prioritize, communicate what you find, and close out work orders completely. That ownership mindset matters more than any single technical skill.

Team Culture and Compensation

BAM refers to its team as BAMFAM, which is a bit of a brand thing, but the underlying point is real. Smaller regional property management companies often have tighter team dynamics than large institutional operators, and that tends to show up in how people treat each other day to day. If you've worked at a large REIT-managed property where you felt anonymous, this environment is likely a different experience.

Pay runs between $17 and $19 per hour depending on experience and qualifications. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage with BAM covering a significant share of the premium, paid life insurance, and a PTO structure that starts with 88 hours after 90 days and grows from there. Rent discounts at BAM properties are also available, which can be meaningful if you're considering living on-site or nearby.

For technicians thinking longer term, this kind of role builds the cross-trade experience that positions you well for a lead maintenance or service manager role down the road. Strong techs who also communicate well with residents and owners are exactly the profile that gets considered for those next steps.

greenhouse_4370441009.title: Leasing Consultant (Floating)
greenhouse_4370441009.rewritten_description:
Berkshire Residential Investments is looking for a Floating Leasing Consultant to cover communities across New Jersey as staffing needs shift. The base salary runs $43,500 to $50,000, depending on experience.

This is a travel-heavy role. You won't be anchored to one property. Berkshire will move you between communities based on where the leasing team needs coverage, so adaptability isn't optional. You need to walk into an unfamiliar office, get oriented quickly, and start contributing the same day.

The core of the job is leasing. You're working leads, conducting tours, following up, and closing. Berkshire sets a minimum 20% closing ratio as a baseline expectation, so this isn't a role where showing people around counts as success. You're converting traffic into signed leases. Beyond that, you're keeping the leasing office and tour routes in good shape, staying current on local market conditions, and communicating professionally with both prospects and current residents.

The administrative side matters here too. Floating consultants often step into communities mid-process, which means picking up where someone else left off. Clean notes, accurate records, and attention to detail keep things from falling apart during transitions.

What separates a strong floating consultant from an average one is the ability to read a community fast. Every property has its own rhythm: different resident demographics, different competitive pressures, different objections in the leasing office. The consultants who do well in this structure don't need weeks to get comfortable. They ask the right questions on day one and adjust.

What you'll bring

  • At least two years of customer service experience, ideally in leasing or a sales environment
  • Comfort with technology and the ability to pick up new platforms quickly
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Reliable transportation and willingness to travel across New Jersey communities

Berkshire owns and manages its own portfolio, so you're working within a single organization rather than a third-party management structure. That tends to mean more consistency in systems and standards across properties, which helps when you're moving between sites regularly.

greenhouse_4373068009.rewritten_description:
What You'll Actually Do

This role puts you at the center of daily community life at a Redstone Residential property in Logan, Utah. Your days will include responding to resident maintenance requests, keeping common areas clean and presentable, and making sure every unit looks its best before a new resident moves in. Apartment turns are a real part of this work. You'll walk units, identify what needs attention, and see it through so the next resident gets a home worth being proud of.

Curb appeal is taken seriously here. That means grounds, landscaping, trash removal, and the general condition of hallways, the clubhouse, and shared spaces all fall within your scope. When something's beyond your reach or needs escalation, you'll communicate it clearly to your Maintenance Supervisor or Property Manager. Emergency response is also part of the job, and Redstone has policies in place to guide you through those situations.

What You Bring

  • At least one year of relevant experience, property management maintenance experience is a plus
  • Solid basic maintenance skills and working knowledge of common repair tasks
  • Genuine customer service instincts. Residents notice how you show up, not just what you fix
  • Strong attention to detail, especially during make-ready prep and turns
  • Physical readiness to lift up to 75 lbs. and work 8 to 10 hour shifts on your feet

Compensation is $20.00 per hour. Benefits include health, vision, and dental insurance, 15 days of PTO, 10 paid holidays, paid parental leave, a 401K with up to 6% company match, short-term disability, and access to continued education and professional development programs.

The Dynamics Worth Knowing

Redstone manages over 38,000 beds across 20 states, with a portfolio that spans student housing and conventional multifamily. Logan is a college town, which means the resident base skews younger and the pace around turn season can be intense. If you've worked student housing before, you already know what that looks like. If you haven't, it's worth understanding that the expectations around unit readiness and curb appeal run higher than you might expect at a comparable conventional property.

The team dynamic matters here. Maintenance techs at Redstone work closely with property managers and supervisors, and the communication piece is real. The strongest candidates in this type of role aren't just technically capable. They're the ones residents actually trust, the person who follows up, who shows up on time, and who takes the condition of the property personally. That quality is hard to train and easy to spot in an interview.

greenhouse_5390709008.title: Senior Community Manager - Affordable Housing
greenhouse_5390709008.rewritten_description:
What You'll Actually Do

This role sits at the intersection of compliance, operations, and resident services on an affordable housing property in Saint Paul. The day-to-day is dense. You're tracking delinquency, managing recertifications, coordinating with the compliance department on regulatory responses, and keeping your maintenance program tight enough to pass a REAC inspection without scrambling. When a Management and Occupancy Review lands on the calendar, you're the one who owns the preparation.

Compliance is a core function here, not a side task. HUD 4350.3 is your operating manual. You'll handle annual and interim recertifications, monitor EIV activity, and stay current on LIHTC requirements through TCS. When residents fall out of compliance with lease or program requirements, you're coordinating intervention strategies with your Regional Manager rather than waiting for a problem to escalate into litigation.

On the financial side, you're attending monthly budget meetings, watching bad-debt write-offs, and pursuing delinquencies through legal channels when necessary. You're also the point person for vendor coordination, unit inspections, and bi-annual walk-throughs with the Building Superintendent. Construction updates, violation avoidance, and resident access during renovation cycles all run through you.

What You Bring

  • At least three years of management experience that includes direct team supervision (property management experience in affordable housing is the target profile)
  • COS or CPO certification, active and current
  • TCS certification for tax credit compliance
  • Hands-on EIV experience and comfort in Yardi
  • Working knowledge of HUD regulations, Fair Housing, ADA, and FCRA
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office and the ability to manage multiple compliance deadlines simultaneously
  • Bachelor's degree preferred but not required

The Operational Reality

Affordable housing management at this level requires a specific kind of attention. Recertification errors, missed MOR prep, or delinquency that goes unmanaged long enough to hit bad-debt don't just affect NOI, they affect residents and regulatory standing. The candidates who perform well in roles like this tend to be comfortable owning compliance outcomes end-to-end, not just flagging issues upward. If you've managed a HUD or LIHTC property through a REAC cycle or an MOR and came out clean, that experience translates directly here.

Fairstead operates as an integrated platform across development, construction, and property management, which means a Senior Community Manager here has more visibility into capital projects and construction coordination than you'd typically find in a third-party management environment. The salary range for this position is $68,000 to $70,000, with a benefits package that includes employer-contributed medical and dental through United Healthcare, a company-matched 401(k), and 15 days of PTO plus 12 paid holidays.

Skills This Role Runs On

This Community Manager position at Griffis Residential in West Palm Beach centers on three core skill sets: financial oversight, team development, and operational execution. You'll read budgets, track delinquency, manage capex projects, and keep occupancy where it needs to be. At the same time, you're coaching leasing staff, running inspections, and staying current on the local competitive market. The role requires someone who can shift between a budget spreadsheet and a resident conversation without losing a beat.

Strong lease comprehension matters here. You'll handle collections, interpret legal documents, and make calls on rent-related situations that have real financial consequences. Griffis uses iPad-based leasing and marketing tools, so comfort with technology is part of the daily workflow, not an occasional task.

What You'll Actually Be Doing

Day-to-day, you're running the property. That means leading and delegating to your team, reviewing community conditions through regular inspections, responding to resident service needs, and keeping vendors accountable to scope and budget. You'll oversee capital improvement projects from progress monitoring through payment approval.

On the leasing side, you're coaching associates on conversion and customer service standards, not just watching the numbers come in. Griffis has defined leasing and marketing expectations, and part of your job is making sure your team meets them consistently.

You'll also track market conditions and competitors, which feeds your recommendations on concessions, pricing, and strategy. This isn't a passive reporting function. Griffis expects Community Managers to bring informed opinions to the table.

  • Three or more years in multi-family or hospitality management
  • Solid grasp of community financials, collections, and lease documentation
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Outlook, Excel, Word)
  • High school diploma required; bachelor's degree or CAM/ARM certification preferred
  • Demonstrated ability to build and coach a team

What Makes This Role Worth a Closer Look

The compensation range sits between $87,000 and $100,000, plus a $2,500 sign-on bonus. The bonus structure is layered: a quarterly bonus of up to 25% of annual salary, a retention bonus, and an occupancy bonus starting at $175 per lease. That's meaningful upside if you perform.

The benefits package is substantial. Griffis offers a 50% rental discount, 401(k) with up to 4% company match, 11 paid holidays, a minimum of three weeks PTO accruing from day one, paid parental leave, and tuition reimbursement up to $5,250 annually. The PTO exchange for student loan repayment is a less common perk worth noting if that's relevant to you.

One thing that separates strong candidates in this role: the ability to hold a team accountable while still developing them. Managers who focus only on results without investing in their staff tend to see turnover that hurts occupancy and morale. Griffis has built out coaching and cross-training expectations into the role itself, which signals they take team development seriously at the operational level.

lever_9083bf68-5dff-46ae-ba9a-513f19fd65.title: Experienced Field Maintenance Technician (3+ Years Required)
lever_9083bf68-5dff-46ae-ba9a-513f19fd65.rewritten_description:
What You'll Actually Do

This role puts you in the field across a portfolio of residential and commercial properties in the Lawrenceville area, working through work orders that you own from start to finish. That means diagnosing the problem, executing the repair, managing the budget for the job, and closing it out correctly. Lessen operates at scale, completing millions of work orders annually through a network of vetted vendors and in-house technicians, so the expectation is that you bring enough experience to work independently. At least three years of verifiable, hands-on maintenance or trade experience is a genuine floor here, not a soft suggestion.

The day-to-day covers a broad scope of general property maintenance. You'll manage your schedule, prioritize your queue, and make judgment calls on what needs immediate attention versus what can be planned. The company's stated priority is quality over volume, which matters in practice: you're not being pushed to close ten tickets by noon. You're expected to close the right tickets correctly.

A few things worth noting about the structure of this position: there's no on-call rotation and the schedule runs weekdays. For experienced techs who've spent years fielding Saturday night calls, that's a meaningful shift. The company provides a fleet vehicle, fuel card, a tool and equipment allowance, and a cell phone stipend. A $1,500 sign-on bonus is included, along with eligibility for a quarterly discretionary bonus of up to 5% of quarterly earnings.

What You Bring

  • Minimum 3 years of verifiable hands-on experience in property maintenance or a skilled trade
  • Ability to diagnose and resolve a wide range of maintenance issues without supervision
  • Comfort managing work order budgets and tracking costs per job
  • Solution-oriented approach: you're expected to problem-solve in the field, not escalate everything
  • Reliable, organized, and able to manage your own schedule across multiple properties

Where This Role Can Lead

Lessen is expanding nationally and has explicitly built a growth path into this position. Strong field technicians here have a clear trajectory toward Lead Technician and Field Maintenance Manager roles. That path is worth thinking about seriously. The skills you build in a portfolio-level maintenance role, specifically budget management, multi-property coordination, and vendor-quality judgment, translate directly into operations management in property management. Technicians who understand how work orders connect to NOI and asset performance become candidates for roles most maintenance techs never reach. If you're three to five years into a maintenance career and thinking about what comes next, a position that gives you ownership over your work and exposes you to large-scale property operations is a genuine step up the ladder.

A prospective resident walks in off Park Boulevard with questions about availability. What This Role Covers

Logan Property Management is hiring a Leasing Consultant to support daily operations at Trolley Court. The role centers on leasing activities, resident services, and working alongside the on-site team to keep the property running smoothly. You'll guide prospective residents through the leasing process, handle inquiries, and follow up on traffic to maintain occupancy. You'll also assist with resident concerns and help coordinate between team members to make sure nothing falls through the cracks.

SRO properties serve a specific resident population. Many residents rely on this housing as a primary or long-term home, so the ability to communicate clearly, handle sensitive situations with professionalism, and stay consistent under pressure matters more here than in a conventional apartment setting. Resident satisfaction is a real metric, not a talking point.

What You Bring

  • Prior leasing experience, ideally in a residential property management setting
  • Strong communication skills, both written and in person
  • Comfort working with a diverse resident base and handling difficult conversations calmly
  • Ability to support team coordination and stay organized across multiple tasks

smartrecruiters_744000144111939.rewritten_description:
Collections work sits at the intersection of financial accountability and human sensitivity. The best people in this role carry two skills in equal measure: the ability to hold a firm line on payment expectations and the ability to treat a resident who's two months behind like a person, not a number. That balance is genuinely hard to find, and it's exactly what AIR Communities is looking for in this Shared Service Center role based at their Denver Tech Center corporate office.

The Skills That Drive This Role

Communication and negotiation do the heavy lifting here. On any given day, you might be drafting a late notice, working through a payment plan with a resident who's hit a rough patch, processing a legal filing, or reviewing a warrant of restitution. The thread connecting all of it is your ability to stay composed and clear-headed when conversations get uncomfortable. Delinquency conversations can go sideways fast if the person on the other end of the phone feels cornered. The skill is in redirecting that tension toward a workable resolution rather than an escalation.

You'll also need to be comfortable moving between systems and documentation tasks. Tracking collection activities, following up on payment arrangements, and recommending charge-offs when accounts are unrecoverable all require attention to detail and consistent record-keeping. This is corporate-side work, not on-site property management, so your output feeds into decisions made across a large portfolio.

What the Day-to-Day Actually Looks Like

You're operating within a Shared Service Center, which means you support properties across multiple markets rather than working at a single community. That structure keeps the work varied. One afternoon might involve processing eviction-related filings; the next morning might be a series of outbound calls to residents on existing payment plans, checking in and documenting progress. The pace is steady and the caseload is real.

The commission component tied to collections performance is worth taking seriously. Base pay lands between $21 and $23 per hour, but your earning potential grows with results. That structure rewards people who are organized enough to follow through consistently, not just those who are good at the initial conversation.

One honest note: this kind of work carries cumulative stress. You're regularly engaging with people in financial distress, and some interactions won't resolve neatly. Strong candidates in collections roles tend to have genuine stress management habits, not just the ability to say they do.

Why AIR Specifically

AIR Communities is one of the larger apartment ownership and operating platforms in the country, with a focus on higher-quality assets in major markets. Working on their collections team means you're part of a centralized operation with real infrastructure behind it. You're not figuring out processes alone. The role is in-office five days a week, which reflects the company's view that collaboration in this kind of shared services environment benefits from physical presence.

For someone early in a property management finance or admin career, collections experience at this scale transfers well. Delinquency management, legal filing processes, and negotiation skills are directly applicable to property management roles, regional accounting positions, or compliance-adjacent work further down the road. It's a substantive starting point in the industry.

  • Strong verbal and written communication, especially in difficult conversations
  • Negotiation skills and the ability to structure workable payment arrangements
  • Comfort with documentation, follow-up, and system-based record-keeping
  • Patience and composure under sustained pressure
  • Ability to work independently within a defined process framework

greenhouse_5215384007.rewritten_description:
This role runs on a specific combination of skills: financial literacy, tenant relationship management, and operational follow-through. At Lincoln Property Company's Austin operation, you'll use all three daily, often at the same time.

What This Role Actually Requires

The financial side is real here. You'll be working through operating expense reconciliations, CAM and OpEx, coordinating with accounting rather than just handing things off. You'll review vendor invoices against management agreement terms and authorization limits, and you'll help build out monthly reporting packages that go directly to institutional clients. If you're not comfortable with intermediate financial analysis and the math behind it, this role will feel harder than it should.

On the operational side, you're coordinating tenant move-ins and move-outs, managing lease administration across systems, participating in property walk-throughs, and making sure building technical staff are actually resolving issues within the timeframes the leases require. Lincoln manages a commercial portfolio that spans office, retail, and industrial, so the tenant mix and the lease structures you'll encounter aren't uniform. Flexibility matters.

Procurement support is also part of the job. That includes bidding activities and vendor sourcing, which means you need to understand what you're buying before you can evaluate whether the price is right.

The Skills That Separate Strong Candidates

We've seen a lot of people move through assistant PM roles at commercial firms. The ones who advance quickly share a few traits: they can write a clear, professional communication to a tenant without it turning into a problem, they understand that the management agreement defines the boundaries of what you can approve, and they don't wait to be told twice when a punch list item is overdue.

Proficiency with AP and CMMS systems is listed as preferred, and it genuinely matters. If you've touched Yardi, MRI, or a comparable platform in a commercial context, that's a real advantage. Microsoft Office at an intermediate-to-advanced level is a baseline expectation, not a differentiator.

Working at Lincoln

Lincoln is one of the larger private real estate firms operating in the U.S., with a commercial portfolio well north of 700 million square feet under management. Austin is an active market for them. The firm has a reputation for promoting from within its PM track, and an assistant PM role at a firm this size typically leads toward property manager responsibilities within a few years, particularly for candidates who can demonstrate client-facing competency early.

This is a fully in-office position in Austin. Standard business hours, on-site presence required. Monthly property inspections and travel to assigned properties are part of the routine. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, 401(k), and flexible time off, with eligibility governed by plan documents.

  • Bachelor's degree preferred; relevant experience considered in combination with education
  • 1 to 2 years of related commercial property management experience
  • Experience with office, retail, or industrial properties preferred
  • AP and CMMS system proficiency preferred
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills required
  • Must be authorized to work in the U.S. without visa sponsorship

greenhouse_8141438.title: Leasing Consultant
greenhouse_8141438.rewritten_description:
Leasing Consultant roles at family-owned operators tend to look different than those at institutional REITs. Weinstein Properties has run apartment communities for over 70 years under the same family ownership, and that hands-on culture shows up in how they hire and train. At Bexley Village at Concord Mills, this position sits at the front line of occupancy: every tour, every follow-up call, every lease signed moves the needle directly.

The Work Itself

Your days will mix sales, service, and light administrative work in roughly equal measure. You'll greet prospects, guide them through tours, and work to convert traffic into signed leases. Between tours, you'll handle resident concerns, help keep the property presentable, and process the paperwork that keeps the office moving. Saturdays rotate among the team, and the occasional resident event or weather-related situation may pull you outside normal hours. The schedule is weekdays 9 to 6 and Saturdays 9 to 5, with Sundays off.

Pay starts at $18/hour and increases with experience. Quarterly bonuses are part of the compensation structure, which means your leasing performance has a direct line to your paycheck. Benefits include health, dental, and vision coverage, a 401k, PTO, paid holidays, a birthday day off, an Employee Assistance Program, and a rent discount.

What Weinstein Is Actually Looking For

Prior leasing experience is genuinely optional here. Weinstein has a documented track record of building strong consultants from scratch, so the hiring criteria centers on character over credentials. The traits that matter:

  • Clear, warm communication in person and in writing
  • Genuine interest in helping people solve problems
  • Comfort with shifting priorities and an active, on-your-feet workday
  • A team-first attitude. Everyone pitches in on tasks that fall outside the strict job description
  • Goal orientation and the self-motivation to follow up consistently

What separates strong candidates from average ones in a role like this is follow-through after the tour. Plenty of people can give a pleasant showing. The consultants who move occupancy are the ones who follow up on time, remember details from the conversation, and close without being pushy. That skill is part instinct, part habit, and Weinstein's training is built to develop both.

Where This Role Can Go

Weinstein operates more than 60 communities across Virginia, North Carolina, Texas, Tennessee, and Georgia. Leasing Consultant is the standard entry point into property management careers at operators this size, and the path forward is real. Many of their current site managers and corporate staff started in leasing roles. If you perform, the progression to Assistant Manager and eventually Property Manager is a documented pattern at this company, not just a line in a job posting.

What You'll Actually Do

This is an operations-heavy role at Redpoint Gainesville, a student housing community managed by The Scion Group. You'll work directly under the General Manager and step in to run the property when they're out. That means owning the day-to-day across leasing support, resident accounts, facilities coordination, and staff development simultaneously.

A typical week pulls you in several directions. You might start Monday reviewing delinquency and chasing down outstanding balances to keep the property under 2% by month-end. By midweek, you're walking units with the facilities team to punch through a make-ready list, then fielding an escalated resident concern that came in through Entrata. Friday could mean auditing utility billing records or responding to a Google review before the weekend on-call rotation kicks in.

The annual turn is where this role gets intense. Student housing turns fast, and at a property like Redpoint, you're coordinating vendors, tracking unit readiness through Turnable, assessing move-out damage, processing final billing, and physically helping move furniture when the team needs hands on deck. It's not a desk job during turn season.

On the financial side, you'll assist with month-end reporting, manage accounts receivable reconciliation, and use KPIs to track leasing velocity, concessions, and gain-to-lease trends. You'll also work alongside the Customer and Sales Experience Manager on resident engagement and reputation management across Google, Yelp, and internal survey platforms.

What You Bring

  • At least one year of experience in property management or residential community operations
  • Familiarity with a property management system, Entrata experience preferred
  • Strong written communication skills, you'll be drafting resident notices and review responses regularly
  • Comfort with financial basics: accounts receivable, late fees, NSF policies, and delinquency tracking
  • Ability to handle confidential information and resident account matters with discretion
  • Organizational discipline to manage competing priorities during high-volume periods like turn

Context Worth Knowing

Student housing runs on a lease-up cycle tied to the academic calendar, which creates predictable pressure points: fall move-in, spring renewals, and the summer turn window. Candidates who've only worked conventional multifamily sometimes underestimate how compressed and physical the turn process is in this sector. If you've managed turns before, that experience translates directly here. If you haven't, expect a steep but manageable learning curve during your first summer.

Scion uses a tech stack that includes Entrata, ClickUp, Turnable, Lattice, and Qualtrics. You don't need to know all of them on day one, but comfort picking up new platforms quickly will matter. This role is eligible for an annual discretionary bonus and includes standard benefits: health, dental, vision, 401k matching, paid parental leave, and learning reimbursement.

Weekend availability is a firm requirement. Leasing traffic peaks on Saturdays and Sundays, so your regular days off will fall during the week. This schedule suits some people well and frustrates others. Know which category you fall into before you apply.

Qualifications and Compensation

Prometheus hires across industries and doesn't require prior property management experience. What they're looking for is genuine customer orientation, comfort in a sales environment, and the kind of self-direction that makes someone effective without constant supervision. Strong written communication matters too, since much of the administrative work involves drafting-facing content and reports.

Compensation for this role includes:

  • Hourly pay range of $25.00 to $26.25, plus a weekend shift premium
  • $200 per lease incentive
  • Discretionary semi-annual bonus
  • Additional bonuses tied to referrals, training, renovation projects, and lease-up assignments
  • 100% company-paid medical, vision, and dental coverage including eligible dependents
  • 401(k) with employer matching
  • Tenure-based housing discounts
  • Educational assistance and tuition reimbursement
  • Paid volunteer time and 12 paid holidays, including your birthday

One thing worth noting for career-minded candidates: leasing consultant roles at well-structured companies like this one tend to feed directly into assistant manager and property manager tracks. The combination of sales performance, resident relations, and administrative exposure you get here covers the core competencies that most promotion decisions in property management are based on. If you treat this as a training ground rather than just a job, the path forward is clear.

greenhouse_4374447009.title: Assistant Community Manager
greenhouse_4374447009.location: Enclave at Deep River - 4203 River Birch Loop - Greensboro, NC - 27409
greenhouse_4374447009.rewritten_description:
What You'll Actually Do

This role splits your week between leasing and ledgers, and you need to be comfortable with both. Some days you're walking prospects through available homes at Enclave at Deep River, building rapport, and closing leases. Other days you're deep in accounts receivable: posting payments, reviewing ledgers for billing errors, making delinquency follow-up calls, and coordinating with the Community Manager when an eviction procedure needs to move forward. Neither side of the job is optional.

You'll also step in as the acting lead when the Community Manager is out. That means keeping the team on task, fielding resident concerns, and making judgment calls without someone to escalate to. It's a real test of whether you can hold the operation together under pressure, and Hawthorne's structure treats it as preparation for the next step, not just gap coverage.

The schedule runs Monday through Friday, 9 to 6, and Saturdays 10 to 4, with one weekday off each week to hit 40 hours. Resident events or community-specific needs can pull you into evenings occasionally. That's the honest reality of the schedule.

What You Bring

  • At least two years of property management experience, with preference for candidates who've already held an assistant community manager title
  • Comfort reading a rent roll, catching ledger discrepancies, and having direct conversations with delinquent residents
  • Leasing instincts: identifying what a prospect actually needs, matching them to the right home, and moving the paperwork through cleanly
  • High School diploma or GED required; a CALP credential is a plus
  • Valid driver's license
  • Ability to de-escalate resident conflicts without losing your composure or your paper trail

Context Worth Knowing

Hawthorne Residential Partners manages communities across the Southeast and ranks among the 50 largest multifamily operators in the country. For candidates thinking about career trajectory, this role is a direct pipeline to Community Manager. Hawthorne runs a formal Career Path Program with internal learning and development support, so the path isn't just implied, it's structured.

What separates a strong candidate here from an average one is financial fluency. Plenty of people can run a tour. Fewer can catch a misapplied payment, hold a firm but fair delinquency conversation, and still retain the resident at renewal. If you've done both sides of the job consistently, this role fits your experience well.

Compensation includes hourly pay plus monthly leasing and renewal commissions and quarterly performance bonuses. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401k match, paid time off (including your birthday), paid parental and adoption leave, pet insurance, company-paid life insurance, and 24/7 telehealth access.

greenhouse_4375596009.title: Leasing Consultant
greenhouse_4375596009.rewritten_description:
Leasing consultant roles vary a lot by company. At John M. Corcoran & Company, a firm that has operated in New England since 1951, the work is hands-on from day one: you're showing units, processing applications, and helping new residents settle in, all at Beverly Commons in Beverly, MA.

What the Job Involves

The core of this role is converting traffic into signed leases. You'll walk prospective residents through available apartments, explain pricing and lease terms clearly, and move applications through to approval. From there, you'll build lease packages and coordinate move-ins to make sure the process runs cleanly.

Marketing is part of the job too. You'll set leasing goals and work toward them through online advertising, social media, and networking. Maintaining curb appeal through regular property inspections is also on your plate. Once residents are in, you stay in contact with them throughout their tenancy.

  • Show apartments and explain pricing, concessions, and lease terms to prospects
  • Process rental applications and prepare lease packages
  • Coordinate move-ins and deliver consistent customer service through the process
  • Support marketing efforts through social media, websites, and local outreach
  • Conduct property inspections and flag curb appeal issues
  • Maintain ongoing communication with current residents

What They're Looking For

A high school diploma or equivalent is the baseline. Beyond that, JMC wants someone who communicates well in person and in writing, stays organized under pressure, and brings a consistent, positive energy to resident interactions. Strong computer skills matter here because lease administration, marketing platforms, and resident communication all run through software.

The Tuesday through Saturday schedule (9 a.m. to 5 p.m. most days, 10 a.m. to 6 p.m. on Wednesdays) is worth noting before you apply. Weekend availability is a standard expectation in leasing, and this schedule reflects that.

Compensation and Where This Role Can Lead

Pay runs $23 to $27.50 per hour, with a $2,500 sign-on bonus. Benefits include medical, dental, vision, and life insurance, paid time off plus holidays, and a 401(k) with company match.

What separates strong leasing consultants from average ones at a company like JMC is follow-through. Prospects who don't lease on the first visit often do convert later, but only if someone follows up consistently and knows the property well enough to answer questions on the spot. Leasing roles also tend to be a natural entry point into assistant manager or property manager tracks, particularly at firms that promote from within. JMC's tenure history suggests they do.

greenhouse_8139629.title: Floating Maintenance Technician (Fayetteville)
greenhouse_8139629.rewritten_description:
Fayetteville's rental market carries a particular rhythm shaped by Fort Liberty. High resident turnover, frequent PCS moves, and a consistent demand cycle mean properties here stay busy year-round. Van Metre operates four communities across the city, and this floating technician role sits at the center of keeping all of them running.

The position covers The Villagio, Hunter's Ridge, Stone Gate, and Village on the Lake. Rather than being anchored to a single property, you'll move between sites based on need, which means your day can shift from completing turns at one community to knocking out service requests at another. Occasional travel to Van Metre properties in Greensboro and Burlington is possible, though Fayetteville is the primary focus. The role reports to the Director of Facilities and works closely with Service Managers on the ground at each site.

The core work covers the full range of a technician's responsibilities: service requests, make-ready turns, preventative maintenance, exterior and grounds upkeep, and daily property walks for curb appeal and safety. You'll also carry on-call responsibility as part of the team's 24/7 coverage rotation, so after-hours calls are part of the job and worth factoring in before you apply.

Candidates need to come in ready to work. This means holding an EPA 608 certification, CFC credentials, and a current CPO. Solid working knowledge of appliance repair, plumbing, electrical, and basic HVAC is expected. You'll also need to supply your own basic tools and hold a valid driver's license for travel between sites.

Qualifications

  • 1 to 2 years of hands-on maintenance experience, or equivalent formal training
  • EPA 608 and CFC certifications (required, not preferred)
  • CPO certification current and active
  • Working knowledge of appliance, electrical, and plumbing repair
  • Basic understanding of HVAC systems and electrical circuitry
  • Familiarity with OSHA and current building safety standards
  • Own basic tools and ability to use them safely
  • Valid driver's license
  • Availability for weekend work and after-hours emergency calls

Pay runs from $23 to $26 per hour depending on experience and credentials, with an annual bonus of up to $5,000 paid quarterly. Van Metre's benefits package includes a strong PTO structure, company-matched 401(k), tuition reimbursement, company-paid certifications, and a wellness reimbursement of up to $900 per year. Employees also receive rental discounts across Van Metre communities.

One thing worth noting for technicians considering the floating structure: the variety accelerates your familiarity with different property layouts and maintenance histories faster than a single-site role typically does. If you're aiming toward a Service Manager position down the road, cross-site exposure gives you a broader operational picture and makes that transition easier to argue for.

greenhouse_4374655009.title: $1,500 Sign-On Bonus - Multisite Maintenance Supervisor
greenhouse_4374655009.rewritten_description:
A resident puts in a work order at 7 a.m. By 8, you've already triaged it, assigned it to the right tech, and moved on to a scheduled HVAC inspection at the second property across town. That's the rhythm of this role.

BAM Companies, a Indianapolis-based property management firm founded in 2010, is hiring a Multisite Maintenance Supervisor to lead maintenance operations across multiple residential properties. The pay range runs $25 to $30 per hour, and the position comes with a $1,500 sign-on bonus plus a housing discount at a BAM property.

What the Job Covers

You'll oversee a team of maintenance technicians and take direct responsibility for keeping mechanical systems, common areas, and grounds in good working order across properties. Day-to-day, that means scheduling and tracking preventative maintenance, managing supply purchasing, and making sure work orders get completed to standard. You'll also carry a training and coaching function: this is a supervisory role, so developing your team is part of the job, not a side task.

  • Lead and train maintenance staff across HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and general upkeep
  • Build and manage a preventative maintenance calendar to catch problems before they become costly
  • Hold the team to consistent property standards across all sites
  • Manage supply budgets and keep operations cost-efficient
  • Maintain curb appeal and common areas alongside mechanical systems

What BAM Needs from You

Two to three years of hands-on property maintenance experience is the baseline. Supervisory experience is a plus, but BAM is open to candidates who have the technical depth and are ready to step into a leadership role. You'll need an EPA Type 2 or Universal certification, a valid driver's license, and a reliable vehicle since you're moving between sites regularly.

Strong written and verbal communication matters here. You're coordinating between residents, your team, and property management, so the ability to communicate clearly across all three keeps things from falling through the cracks.

Benefits include medical, dental, vision, and life insurance, plus 14.5 paid holidays and PTO that kicks in after 90 days.

One thing worth knowing about multisite maintenance roles: the split-focus nature of the job means you need strong organizational habits. Techs at one property may need direction while you're physically at another. Supervisors who succeed in this setup tend to build reliable checklists and communication routines early so the team can operate with some autonomy between your visits. If you've worked a single-site role and want more scope, this is a natural next step.

greenhouse_4374925009.title: Community Manager
greenhouse_4374925009.rewritten_description:
Redstone Residential runs over 38,000 beds across 20 states, making them one of the largest third-party student housing operators in the country. Their Rexburg, Idaho property needs a Community Manager who can own every metric on the dashboard: occupancy, delinquency, NOI, leasing velocity, and resident retention. This is the top site-level role, and the person in it is accountable for all of it.

Day to day, that means tracking Redstone's KPIs closely, managing the property to an approved operating budget, and driving the leasing and renewal strategy with enough consistency to hit occupancy targets cycle after cycle. Student housing in a college market like Rexburg runs on tight pre-lease timelines. Missing a leasing window by a few weeks can cost you a full year of occupancy, so the manager here needs to stay ahead of traffic numbers and conversion rates, not just react to them. Rent collection and delinquency management are equally non-negotiable, and you'll submit weekly and monthly reports directly to your Regional Manager.

Beyond the numbers, this role carries real people management responsibility. You're setting the tone for customer service standards, training staff, running performance evaluations, and keeping a team aligned in what Redstone describes as a highly entrepreneurial environment. You'll also interface with campus and community contacts, which in a student housing context matters more than it might elsewhere. Relationships with university housing offices and local community organizations can directly affect referral traffic and reputation.

Project scope here is broader than leasing alone. Expect to manage marketing initiatives and coordinate construction or capital projects as they come up, which means staying organized across multiple moving pieces simultaneously.

What separates a strong candidate from a capable one in this role is P&L ownership experience. Redstone lists budget management and profit-and-loss accountability as required, not preferred. Candidates who can read a T-12, spot where NOI is leaking, and make operational decisions that reflect that understanding will move faster here than those who treat the financial side as someone else's job.

Qualifications

  • At least one year of property management experience, with student housing or multifamily background
  • Demonstrated experience managing a budget and owning P&L outcomes
  • Client-ready professional presence with prior client-facing experience
  • Ability to manage multiple projects and priorities under pressure
  • Comfort with technology platforms; Entrata experience is a plus but not required
  • Proficiency with Google Apps and Microsoft Office
  • Strong team leadership and communication skills

Compensation runs $16 to $20 per hour depending on experience, with a performance bonus opportunity of up to 20% of salary. Benefits include health, vision, and dental insurance, 15 days of PTO, 10 paid holidays, paid parental leave, and a 401(k) with up to 6% company match. Redstone also offers continued education and professional development programs, which reflects the growth trajectory available to site-level managers who perform well.
greenhouse_4374925009.description_text: Redstone Residential is a national student and multi-family housing operator, managing more than 38,000 beds across 20 states. We are one of the largest third-party student housing management companies in the U.S. - and we're just getting started. greenhouse_5394490008.title: Community Assistant Manager - Multi site - Wedekind, Patton, and Linden
greenhouse_5394490008.rewritten_description:
CloudTen Residential is a Nevada-based operator with a portfolio that covers a fair amount of ground, from hotel-to-residential conversions to high-rise lease-ups to value-add repositioning plays. This role sits across three of their Reno communities: Wedekind, Patton, and Linden. If you've done multi-site work before, you already know the drill. If you haven't, this is your orientation.

The title is Assistant Manager, but the scope is wider than a single-property AM position. You're rotating across three locations, which means you're filling gaps, maintaining consistency, and keeping things moving when the Community Manager is pulled elsewhere or out entirely. You'll handle rent collections, daily deposits, delinquency follow-up, and the paperwork side of move-ins and move-outs. You'll also lease. Traffic logging, apartment showings, lease execution review, renewal support , it's the full leasing cycle, not just answering phones.

The financial side is straightforward but requires discipline. Delinquency management, distributing non-payment notices, following through on eviction proceedings when it comes to that, and staying current on Nevada's landlord-tenant statutes. Weekly and monthly reporting runs through you as well. CloudTen uses Entrata, so familiarity there is a real advantage.

A valid driver's license is required. You're moving between properties regularly, so that's not a minor detail.

What separates the candidates who thrive in multi-site AM roles from those who struggle is usually self-management. When you're splitting time across three communities, no single manager is watching your daily schedule. You have to prioritize independently, communicate proactively with each site team, and not let things fall through the cracks just because you were somewhere else that day. The candidates who do well here tend to be organized to the point of mild obsession and genuinely comfortable operating without constant direction.

What You'll Bring

  • 2 to 5 years of property management experience, with leasing and administrative responsibilities
  • Comfort with Entrata, Excel, and standard MS Office tools
  • Working knowledge of Fair Housing laws
  • Experience managing delinquency and collections processes
  • A valid driver's license
  • Strong written and verbal communication across resident, team, and vendor interactions
  • The organizational habits to manage multiple properties without losing detail

Pay runs $22 to $24 per hour depending on experience. This is a solid entry point for someone who wants to build toward a Community Manager role. Multi-site AM experience translates well when you're ready to step up, because you've already operated with less hand-holding than a single-property AM typically gets.

workable_6039645.title: Maintenance Technician
workable_6039645.rewritten_description:
The Role at a Glance

PeakMade Real Estate manages off-campus student housing across the country, and this Maintenance Technician position sits at one of their San Marcos communities. Student housing runs on a different clock than conventional multifamily. Turn season is compressed, service request volume spikes around move-in, and residents expect fast responses. If you've worked in apartment maintenance before, you already know the pace. If that pace suits you, read on.

What the Job Actually Involves

Your day-to-day centers on completing service requests thoroughly and on time, keeping the property looking sharp, and supporting the Maintenance Supervisor across a range of tasks. That includes HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and appliance repairs, plus preventative maintenance on equipment following manufacturer schedules. You'll handle pool maintenance and keep accurate chemical logs. Grounds, breezeways, and common areas need regular attention. During turn events, you'll help coordinate and execute make-ready work so units are rent-ready on schedule.

You'll also participate in the on-call rotation for after-hours emergencies. That's a real part of this job, not a footnote. Nights and weekends come with the territory, particularly around move-in and move-out periods.

Key qualifications PeakMade is looking for:

  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • At least one year of maintenance experience, preferably in apartment communities
  • EPA Type I and II certification preferred
  • Ability to troubleshoot and repair HVAC, plumbing, electrical systems, and appliances
  • Reliable transportation and willingness to work a rotating on-call schedule
  • Must live within 30 miles of the property
  • Ability to lift up to 50 pounds, work at heights, and perform physical tasks outdoors in extreme temperatures
  • Personal hand tools required

Growth and What Sets Strong Candidates Apart

PeakMade offers HVAC and CPO certifications, a facilities leadership program, and additional technical training. For a technician looking to move toward a Maintenance Supervisor role, this is a real path. The company also provides monthly renewal bonuses and a recognition program that includes a 10-year anniversary trip, which signals they're thinking about retention, not just filling a seat.

What separates a strong candidate here: comfort with the student housing environment. High turnover of residents, a compressed summer turn, and a younger demographic mean communication skills matter as much as technical ones. Technicians who can explain a repair clearly to a first-time renter and keep their cool during a busy move-in weekend tend to stand out from those who are technically solid but struggle with resident interaction.

workable_6041663.title: Part Time Maintenance Technician Manufactured Housing Community
workable_6041663.rewritten_description:
Castle Park is a 74-home manufactured housing community in Castle Rock, Colorado. It's a smaller property, which means the work here is varied and visible. When something's off, residents notice quickly, and so does management. That's the nature of this size of community, and it suits technicians who like ownership over their patch rather than being one of a dozen faces on a large team.

Investment Property Group, headquartered in Park City, Utah, owns and operates around 150 properties across 13 states, including multifamily, manufactured home, and RV communities. This role sits within that broader portfolio but the day-to-day is very much local and hands-on.

The schedule is Monday through Friday, 10am to 2pm, at $22 to $26 per hour depending on experience. That's 20 hours a week, which works well as a secondary income or a structured part-time arrangement. The honest caveat: the role does include after-hours emergency coverage and on-call rotation, so it's not a clean 20-hours-and-done situation every week. That's worth knowing upfront.

Day to day, you're completing work orders, walking the property each morning to catch problems before residents report them, keeping up with a preventative maintenance schedule, and managing inventory for supplies and tools. Irrigation, water lines, and sewer repairs come up regularly in manufactured housing communities, so comfort with those systems matters. Basic plumbing skills are a genuine plus here, not just a checkbox.

Because Castle Park is a smaller community, there's less buffer between you and the residents. You'll interact with them often, and how you handle those interactions shapes the living experience as much as how quickly you close a work order. Fair, consistent treatment of residents is listed as a responsibility, and that's accurate. It's part of the job, not a soft add-on.

What the role calls for

  • At least one year of maintenance experience at a manufactured or multifamily community of 100 or more units
  • Knowledge of irrigation systems, water lines, and sewer repairs
  • Safe use and upkeep of power tools and mechanical equipment
  • Ability to respond to after-hours emergencies and participate in on-call rotation
  • Strong time management and the ability to work with minimal supervision
  • Professional communication with residents, staff, and visitors

Benefits include a 401k with company match, PTO accrual at one hour per 30 hours worked, critical illness and accident coverage, an employee assistance program, and an employee referral program.

For someone with manufactured housing experience specifically, this role is a reasonable fit. The community size keeps things manageable, the schedule has structure, and IPG's portfolio size means there's room to move into full-time or larger-property roles if that's the direction you want to go.

smartrecruiters_744000144357049.title: Apartment Accounts Receivable Assistant
smartrecruiters_744000144357049.rewritten_description:
Skills This Role Puts to Work Every Day

Delinquency management sits at the intersection of financial operations and resident relations, and the skills it demands are specific. You'll need steady communication instincts, the ability to hold a firm position without escalating tension, and enough organizational discipline to track dozens of accounts simultaneously across different stages of the collections cycle. This role at AIR Communities draws on all of that, daily.

AIR is one of the largest apartment owners in the country, operating high-quality properties across major U.S. markets. Their Shared Services Center in the Denver Tech Center handles centralized collections across that portfolio, which means the volume and variety of accounts you'll work is meaningful from day one. This is a five-day-in-office position at their corporate headquarters, which spans the top two floors of a DTC tower.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

The core of this job is outbound contact with delinquent residents: phone calls, written notices, and follow-up on payment arrangements. You'll process late notices, handle legal filings, review warrants of restitution, and coordinate evictions when accounts reach that point. Setting up alternative payment plans is part of the toolkit, as is documenting every interaction and activity accurately for audit and legal purposes. You may also recommend charge-offs on accounts that have exhausted recovery options.

The negotiation piece is real. Conversations with residents who owe back rent are rarely easy, and maintaining professionalism under that kind of pressure is a skill this role will test and develop. Composure matters as much as process knowledge here.

On the technical side, you'll work across multiple systems and office tools. AIR uses software common in large-scale multifamily operations, and comfort picking up new platforms quickly is expected.

What Separates Strong Candidates

The candidates who perform best in centralized collections roles like this one tend to combine two things that don't always travel together: genuine patience in difficult conversations and a consistent follow-through habit on documentation. Missing either one creates problems. If you've worked in collections, property management, or any high-volume customer-facing role where you had to hold people accountable to financial commitments, that experience transfers directly.

The commission structure tied to collections performance also means your earning potential has a real ceiling determined by how effective you are, not just by the base pay range of $21 to $23 per hour.

  • Strong verbal and written communication across a range of resident situations
  • Negotiation skills with the ability to reach workable resolutions
  • Ability to manage stress and stay composed during difficult account conversations
  • Computer literacy and comfort learning new property management or collections software
  • Attention to detail in documenting collection activity accurately

AIR's benefits package includes medical, dental, vision, and life insurance, HSA and FSA options, short and long-term disability covered by the company, a 401(k) with up to 6% employer match, paid parental leave up to 16 weeks, tuition assistance, and a 25% rent discount at any AIR community. For someone building a career in multifamily finance or operations, the exposure this role provides to large-scale delinquency workflows across a national portfolio is genuinely useful experience.

greenhouse_5394533008.title: Assistant Property Manager
greenhouse_5394533008.rewritten_description:
Bozzuto operates across design, construction, management, and maintenance, which means the people running their communities carry real operational weight. This Assistant Property Manager role in Foster City sits inside that broader ecosystem, and the day-to-day reflects it: you're part leasing engine, part financial steward, part team leader, all at once.

Rent collection and delinquency management are central to the financial side of this role. You'll work against occupancy and NOI targets, which means tracking who's paid, who hasn't, and what the exposure looks like week to week. That P&L awareness extends to budget management, so candidates who've only touched leasing without ever looking at a financial summary will feel the gap quickly. Exposure to revenue and budget cycles matters here.

On the leasing side, you'll conduct tours and convert traffic into signed leases. Bozzuto communities tend to hold themselves to a high standard on curb appeal and resident experience, so the quality of those interactions carries real weight in renewal rates and brand reputation. Social media is part of the toolkit too, specifically Facebook and Instagram, and the expectation is that you can create content that actually connects, not just repost.

When the Property Manager is out, you run the property. That's a real leadership expectation, and it's worth taking seriously. The strongest candidates for this kind of role tend to be people who already think in terms of what the property needs, not just what their job description says. If you're waiting to be told what to do, the transition to covering for a PM will feel hard. If you're already scanning for gaps and solving before being asked, it'll feel natural.

Weekend availability is part of the schedule, typically one to two weekends per month, with weekday days off in exchange. Foster City's rental market draws a professional renter base, and Saturday and Sunday are when a meaningful share of traffic comes through.

What You Bring

  • A four-year degree or equivalent experience in property management, hospitality, or retail
  • At least two years in a relevant industry role with exposure to P&L and budget management
  • Proficiency in Yardi or comparable property management software
  • Demonstrated sales ability and strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Comfort creating and managing social media content

The salary range for this position runs from $65,000 to $75,000, with additional bonus opportunities. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, 20 days of paid time off plus holidays, a 401k with company match, and tuition reimbursement.
