greenhouse_4376190009.title: Bilingual Leasing Hub Specialist - Sandy Springs, GA
greenhouse_4376190009.rewritten_description:
Cortland's Leasing Hub Specialist role is built around two skills that most leasing consultants develop slowly over time: high-volume outbound sales and the ability to translate a brand's value proposition into a genuine conversation. Here, you'll use both from day one.

The Skills This Role Runs On

This is a centralized leasing position, not a community-based one. You won't be walking prospects through model units or managing a single property's traffic. Instead, you'll work from a hub, handling inbound leads and making outbound contact across Cortland's portfolio of communities. Expect to manage 40 to 50 leads per day through calls, emails, and texts, fielding inquiries routed through RealPage's OneSite platform and converting that interest into scheduled appointments at specific communities.

The skills this requires are distinct from traditional leasing. You need genuine telephone sales instincts, the kind that come from prior customer-facing or sales experience. You need to communicate clearly and warmly under volume pressure, and you need to shift tone and detail depending on which Cortland community you're representing in any given conversation. Bilingual fluency in English and Spanish is part of the job, not a bonus. The role is specifically designed to serve prospects across markets and demographics, and that language skill is load-bearing.

What You'll Build Here

The skills this role develops are worth naming directly. Working a centralized hub gives you portfolio-wide exposure that a single-property leasing role rarely offers. You'll build a detailed understanding of how multiple communities are positioned against each other and against the broader market, which sharpens your ability to match a prospect's stated needs to the right product. That cross-community knowledge transfers directly into roles like regional leasing support, training coordinator, or leasing manager for a lease-up property.

Cortland also invests in structured training and site visits to deepen your community knowledge over time. This is relevant because your credibility with prospects depends on knowing the specifics: amenities, pricing tiers, concessions, community culture. Fluency in those details is something you'll develop systematically, not by accident.

What Makes a Strong Candidate Here

  • At least two years of customer service or sales experience, with real comfort making outbound contact
  • Demonstrated bilingual fluency in English and Spanish
  • Strong written and verbal communication, including the ability to keep a text exchange or email thread moving toward a scheduled appointment
  • Proficiency in OneSite (RealPage); familiarity with L2L is a plus
  • Typing speed and computer comfort that can keep pace with high lead volume

The candidates who perform well in hub-based leasing roles tend to be genuinely energized by the sales cycle itself, not just the face-to-face side of leasing. If you find satisfaction in moving a cold lead to a warm appointment through good communication, this structure suits you. If you prefer the slower rhythm of community-based relationship building, a different leasing role would be a better fit.

Cortland is a top-10 multifamily owner and operator in the US, with in-house design, construction, and management under one structure. The hub model reflects that integrated approach. You're part of a centralized system that feeds a large, active portfolio, and the performance expectations reflect that scale.

greenhouse_7916913003.title: Business Manager - Olympus Pinegrove
greenhouse_7916913003.rewritten_description:
The regional VP is asking for budget variance explanations by Friday, a vendor just called about a disputed invoice, and two of your leasing agents need coaching on closing. It's 10 AM on a Tuesday. Welcome to the Business Manager role at Olympus Pinegrove in La Plata, Maryland.

Olympus Property is looking for a seasoned operator to run day-to-day and long-term operations at this community. The title says Business Manager, but the scope is full property management: financials, team development, physical asset condition, and resident experience all land on your desk. This is a hands-on leadership position, not a coordinator role with a fancy title.

What You'll Own

Financial performance is the backbone of this role. You'll manage rents, occupancy, and expenditures, build out annual business plans and budget forecasts, and hold regular strategy conversations with Regional leadership around monthly performance and projections. You're expected to understand a T-12, explain variances, and have an opinion on where the asset is headed. Delinquency, NOI, and concession strategy are part of your regular vocabulary.

On the people side, you'll lead both office and maintenance staff, which means hiring, training, counseling, and motivating a team that has to perform consistently. You'll direct leasing and renewal programs to keep occupancy strong, coach your team on sales and marketing execution, and make sure the property presents well enough to compete in its submarket. Regular inspections, make-ready oversight, and amenity space condition fall under your watch. You'll also bid and negotiate vendor contracts, manage one-time projects, and keep everything running within safe workplace standards.

What Olympus Wants to See

  • At least two years of multifamily property manager experience at the helm of a community, not just in a supporting role
  • Class A or luxury experience is strongly preferred, given the product type
  • Familiarity with RealPage, Knock, and Onesite will move your application forward
  • Availability Monday through Friday with schedule flexibility for resident events and the occasional after-hours situation

Starting pay is $87,550 annually, with monthly commissions and quarterly and annual bonus eligibility layered on top. Olympus also offers a benefits package that includes medical, dental, and vision coverage, 401(k) with employer matching, an apartment rental allowance, tuition reimbursement, and a sabbatical program. Olympus has earned recognition as a top employer from the National Apartment Association three consecutive years running, which in this industry is worth noting.

One thing that separates strong candidates in this type of role: the ability to hold financial accountability and team culture simultaneously without letting one erode the other. Properties run by managers who focus only on the numbers tend to see turnover spike. Those who focus only on culture tend to miss budget. The candidates who last in Business Manager seats know how to do both, and they know which one needs attention on any given week.

greenhouse_8142345.title: Leasing Consultant
greenhouse_8142345.rewritten_description:
Skills That Drive This Role

Leasing is fundamentally a people skill. The ability to read a room, listen past the surface question, and make someone feel genuinely welcomed matters far more here than knowing what an NOI is on day one. At Bexley Steelecroft in Charlotte's Steele Creek area, Weinstein Properties is looking for a Leasing Consultant who leads with warmth and follows through with organization. If you've worked in hospitality, retail, customer service, or any role where you had to earn someone's trust quickly, you already have the foundation this job builds on.

Strong written communication matters too. You'll respond to inquiries, follow up with prospects, and handle resident correspondence regularly. Clear, friendly writing that doesn't feel robotic is a real differentiator in leasing, and it's something Weinstein trains for if you're still developing it.

What You'll Actually Be Doing

Day to day, you're the first face prospects see and often the first call a current resident makes when something needs attention. You'll guide people through tours, field questions about availability and pricing, and help move them from interested to signed. But the role extends well beyond that transaction. Inspecting homes, supporting the property's overall appearance, handling administrative work, and addressing resident concerns are all part of the regular rhythm. Saturdays rotate among the team, so the schedule is manageable, and Sundays are off entirely.

Weinstein is direct about expectations: this is a high-energy, on-your-feet position. Some days you'll shift gears a dozen times before lunch. The people who do well here aren't thrown by that. They actually prefer it.

Compensation starts at $18 per hour and increases with experience, plus quarterly bonuses. Benefits include a rent discount, health, dental, and vision coverage, PTO, paid holidays, birthday time off, and a 401k.

What Makes Weinstein Worth Considering

Weinstein Properties has been family-owned for over 70 years, with more than 60 communities across Virginia, North Carolina, Texas, Tennessee, and Georgia. That kind of longevity in property management doesn't happen without genuine investment in the people running the properties. They're candid that many of their current leaders started in leasing roles exactly like this one. The career path is real: strong leasing consultants move into assistant manager roles, then property management, and sometimes into regional or corporate positions. The training program is hands-on and structured, which matters if you're newer to the industry.

One thing worth knowing: leasing roles at family-operated companies tend to carry a different accountability than at large institutional operators. There's less anonymity. Your contributions are noticed, and so are gaps. That's a genuine advantage if you're motivated and want recognition to feel personal rather than procedural. It also means the culture is collaborative in a practical sense. Everyone pitches in, and that expectation is consistent across the team.

  • Prior leasing experience is not required
  • Strong interpersonal and written communication skills are essential
  • Comfort with a varied, active daily schedule is important
  • Goal orientation and follow-through matter more than a polished resume

greenhouse_6146917004.title: Customer Experience Specialist at Antero Apartments
greenhouse_6146917004.rewritten_description:
A prospective resident walks in on a Saturday afternoon, slightly frazzled after touring three other communities that morning. Within five minutes, you know their move-in timeline, their must-haves, and which available floor plan fits both. That's the core of what this role asks of you every day at Antero Apartments in Colorado Springs.

What the Role Actually Covers

Cottonwood Residential is hiring a full-time Customer Experience Specialist at Antero Apartments. The schedule includes evenings and weekends, which is standard for leasing-side work at any occupied community with consistent traffic. You'll greet prospects, residents, and vendors in person, respond to inquiries across phone, email, and text, and keep detailed records of every interaction. Knowing current availability, pricing, and unit details cold is a baseline expectation, not a stretch goal.

Beyond the leasing desk, the position has a real operational component. You'll walk the tour path, vacant homes, amenities, and common areas regularly to confirm everything meets Cottonwood's presentation standards. Make-ready readiness before a prospect tour or a resident move-in falls partly on you. You'll also organize the package room daily, support community event planning, assist with social media content, and help maintain vendor communication. It's a broad scope for an entry-level role, and that's intentional: Cottonwood structures this position as a genuine on-ramp toward property management.

Cottonwood was an early adopter of Self-Guided Tours, so you'll be working within a leasing model that expects technology comfort alongside interpersonal skill. Prospects who come in after a self-guided tour often arrive more informed and with sharper questions. Being able to meet them at that level matters.

What Cottonwood Is Looking For

  • Strong verbal and written communication across in-person, phone, and digital channels
  • A track record of staying organized under competing priorities
  • Comfort with a rotating schedule that includes weekend availability
  • A genuinely warm, professional presence when greeting anyone who walks through the door
  • Curiosity and a willingness to learn systems, pricing tools, and community-specific details quickly

Colorado Springs has seen meaningful apartment supply growth over the past several years, with several lease-up communities competing for the same renter pool. At a property like Antero, the leasing experience itself becomes part of the competitive advantage. Prospects have options, and the quality of that first interaction often determines whether they come back or sign elsewhere. Strong candidates in this role tend to understand that instinctively, without needing it explained.

Compensation includes a competitive base pay plus a quarterly bonus structure. Benefits, including full health, vision, dental, life, and disability coverage, become available within the first 30 days. The company also offers a 401k with match, HSA match, three weeks of paid time off in the first year, and 10.5 paid holidays.

greenhouse_4376007009.title: Maintenance Technician - Dallas, TX
greenhouse_4376007009.rewritten_description:
What You'll Actually Do

This is a hands-on maintenance technician role at Berkshire's Medical District property in Dallas. Day to day, you're handling service requests across the full range: appliances, plumbing, electrical, carpentry, and general building upkeep. You're also keeping an eye on curb appeal, managing inventory in the shop, tracking keys, and making sure safety standards stay where they should be. Make-readies and punch list work are part of the rhythm here, not the exception.

Berkshire owns and manages its own portfolio, which means you're working for the owner, not a third-party fee manager. That tends to translate into more consistent capital support and less of the "we have to get approval from ownership" runaround when something genuinely needs fixing.

The Medical District location puts you in a dense, high-traffic Dallas submarket. Expect a mix of healthcare professionals and young renters who keep odd hours and have real expectations for service turnaround. Quick, clean response times matter here.

What You Bring

  • At least one year of residential maintenance experience in a multifamily or similar setting
  • Working knowledge of plumbing, electrical, appliances, and carpentry
  • Comfort with computers and related maintenance or work order applications
  • Strong written and verbal communication in English
  • Genuine attention to curb appeal and property presentation

A Few Honest Notes

Maintenance tech roles at multifamily properties involve after-hours on-call rotations. The posting doesn't detail the schedule, but plan for it. The candidates who thrive in this kind of role aren't just technically capable. They communicate well with residents, close out work orders cleanly, and don't leave management guessing about what got done and what didn't. That last part matters more than most postings let on.

Berkshire offers three weeks of vacation, a 25% rent discount, and personal development plans, which is a reasonable package for this level. For a tech looking to grow, time with a vertically integrated owner like Berkshire can build toward a lead tech or maintenance supervisor path, since you're seeing the full operational picture rather than a narrow slice of it.

greenhouse_5396380008.rewritten_description:
Community management at a San Diego property draws on a wide range of skills simultaneously. You're reading delinquency reports in the morning, walking units for make-ready punch lists by midday, and handling a resident concern before the afternoon's done. If that kind of operational range suits you, this role at Parkview Terrace is worth a close look.

The Skills This Role Leans On

Sunrise Management is looking for a Community Manager who can hold the financial side and the people side of operations in equal focus. On the financial front, that means owning rent collections, managing delinquent accounts within the requirements of California landlord-tenant law, maintaining bank deposits, and contributing to budget preparation and expense monitoring. The NOI doesn't manage itself, and in California's regulatory environment, every collection action has to be done by the book.

On the leasing and marketing side, you'll be tracking traffic, adjusting pricing based on market conditions, and keeping occupancy healthy through both new leasing activity and retention efforts. Renewals are part of this job, not an afterthought. Fair Housing compliance runs through everything from how you advertise to how you handle a renewal conversation.

Leadership is the third leg of the stool. You'll hire, train, and evaluate on-site staff, which means you need to be comfortable giving direct feedback and resolving operational issues without waiting for someone above you to step in. Inspections of common areas, units, and grounds are your responsibility, and so are move-in and move-out protocols executed with consistency.

What the Day Actually Looks Like

California community managers carry a heavier compliance load than most. Fair Housing, ADA, and state-specific landlord-tenant law aren't background knowledge here. They're active daily considerations. Resident service requests are expected to close within 24 to 48 hours, which means your maintenance coordination has to be tight. Payroll submissions, accurate record-keeping, and accounting procedures all land on your desk too. Property management software proficiency is a baseline requirement, not a bonus.

One honest note: this is a role where the workload doesn't always stay neatly within business hours. Resident concerns, unit issues, and staffing gaps have a way of surfacing at inconvenient times. That's the job. Candidates who've managed a California property before will recognize the rhythm.

What Separates Strong Candidates Here

  • Proven experience managing collections and delinquency in California, where the legal process is specific and unforgiving of shortcuts
  • Comfort reading the market and making pricing recommendations, not just executing what's handed down
  • A track record of building and retaining an on-site team, not just supervising one
  • Familiarity with property management software and enough spreadsheet competency to support budget work
  • One to two years of property management experience at minimum, with community management experience preferred

Sunrise Management operates with a resident hospitality orientation, so candidates who treat resident relations as a core operational function rather than a distraction from "real" work tend to fit better here. The pay range runs $26 to $28 per hour depending on experience, with medical, dental, vision, FSA, company-paid life insurance, and paid time off rounding out the package.

workable_6044379.title: Full-Time Leasing Consultant
workable_6044379.rewritten_description:
A prospect submits an inquiry at 9 a.m. By 9:15, you've called, sent a follow-up email, and booked a tour for Thursday. That kind of speed is the baseline here, not the exception.

PeakMade Real Estate is hiring a full-time Leasing Consultant for a community in New Brunswick, New Jersey. This is a front-line sales role. You'll own the leasing pipeline from first contact to signed lease, and you'll be expected to hit occupancy targets consistently.

What the Job Covers

Most of your day runs through lead conversion. You'll field inquiries by phone, email, and online platforms, then guide prospects through tours tailored to what they actually need. The goal is to create urgency and close. You'll track every lead in the CRM, execute multi-touch follow-up, and monitor pricing, availability, and competitor positioning so your conversations stay sharp.

Beyond leasing, you'll handle lease paperwork accurately, collect deposits, and support move-in and move-out events. You'll also pitch in on the annual turn process, help keep the model and office presentation ready, and assist with market surveys when needed. Weekends and peak leasing hours are part of the schedule.

What You Need to Bring

  • At least one year of sales or leasing experience with measurable conversion results
  • Comfort working in Yardi, Entrata, RealPage, or a comparable CRM
  • Documented follow-up discipline: calls, emails, texts across multiple touchpoints
  • Ability to work weekends and adjust to peak leasing demand

The pay range is $20 to $24 per hour, and the role is commission-eligible. Benefits include PTO, wellbeing days, a 401(k) match, wellness programs, and housing discounts that vary by community.

One thing that separates strong candidates in student and young professional markets like New Brunswick: the ability to read a prospect quickly and adjust your pitch on the spot. Generic tour scripts don't close here. Consultants who ask good questions, listen, and connect the apartment to what the prospect actually said they need will convert at a higher rate than those who rely on memorized talking points alone.

workable_6042436.title: Floating Maintenance Technician
workable_6042436.rewritten_description:
The Role at a Glance

Floating maintenance positions cover multiple properties instead of one fixed site. That means more variety day to day, but also more coordination. You need to read a new property quickly, assess what's behind, and get to work. CommonPlace by Collective Residential operates garden-style communities in the Raleigh-Durham area and is hiring a Floating Maintenance Supervisor to keep those properties safe, clean, and ready for residents.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

A good portion of your time goes toward unit turns. You'll complete make-readies, run punch lists, and confirm units are genuinely move-in ready before keys hand over. You'll also schedule and perform preventive maintenance, handle service requests per company guidelines, and oversee vendor work on-site to make sure quality and compliance standards are met.

On the supervisory side, you're responsible for training the maintenance team, managing schedules, and holding work to CommonPlace's standards. You'll track inventory, submit supply orders, maintain MSDS sheets and replacement logs, and keep tools and equipment organized. Lock changes after evictions, snow removal, and on-call emergency response are also part of the job.

You'll report unusual conditions directly to the Property Manager. Staying ahead of problems before they become resident complaints is a core part of performing well in this role.

Key qualifications CommonPlace is looking for:

  • 3 to 5 years of hands-on maintenance experience in property management
  • 1 to 3 years of supervisory experience
  • Solid working knowledge of plumbing, electrical, HVAC, appliances, and general construction
  • Comfortable with hand tools, power tools, and motorized equipment
  • Ability to lift and carry up to 50 lbs independently
  • Valid driver's license and personal auto liability insurance (required for traveling between properties)
  • Availability for an on-call rotation

What Sets Strong Candidates Apart

The floating nature of this role is the real differentiator. Technicians who do well in fixed-site roles sometimes struggle when the property, the team, and the punch list change week to week. The candidates who stand out here are the ones who can walk a property they've never seen, identify what needs attention without being told, and get a team moving quickly. HVAC competency in particular goes a long way in Raleigh's climate, where summer calls spike and residents feel every delay. If you've worked lease-up or heavy turn seasons before, that experience translates directly.

Pay runs $31.00 to $34.00 per hour. Benefits include medical, dental, vision, and a 401k with employer match, plus paid vacation, sick time, and volunteer time.

workable_6042499.title: Maintenance Supervisor
workable_6042499.rewritten_description:
Apartment maintenance is unglamorous work much of the time. You're unclogging drains, patching drywall, replacing appliances in vacant units, and picking up trash before residents notice it piled up. Then your phone rings at 11 p.m. because a water heater went out. That's the job, and FLATS LLC in Las Vegas wants someone who already knows this and shows up anyway.

FLATS LLC, part of the ProperXPM family, is hiring a Maintenance Supervisor for one of their Las Vegas residential communities. The scope covers what you'd expect from a full-service maintenance role: completing work orders, handling turns on vacant units, keeping common areas clean and functional, and running preventive maintenance on building systems. Pool maintenance and seasonal amenity upkeep are part of the rotation too. Minor plumbing, electrical, drywall, painting, light carpentry , you need to be competent across all of it, because this isn't a role where you wait on a specialized sub for every small fix.

After-hours on-call is on a rotating schedule, so it won't be every night, but it will come around. That's worth knowing before you apply.

What you bring

  • Proven apartment or building maintenance experience, or a strong background in a related trade
  • Working knowledge of electrical, plumbing, HVAC, and appliance repair
  • Comfortable with hand and power tools, physical tasks, and lifting up to 50 lbs
  • Valid driver's license and reliable transportation
  • High school diploma or equivalent preferred

The candidates who do well in roles like this tend to be self-directing. A property manager can't follow you from unit to unit. You'll get a list of work orders, a punch list of make-ready tasks, and the expectation that you'll work through them without constant check-ins. If you need a lot of hand-holding to prioritize your day, this will be frustrating for everyone. If you're the type who finishes a turn and immediately checks what's next, you'll fit the rhythm of this operation.

Las Vegas heat puts real stress on HVAC systems and pool equipment, which means preventive maintenance here isn't just a checkbox. Catching a failing condenser before peak summer is the difference between a manageable repair and a building full of unhappy residents. Technicians with experience in desert climates know this already.

Benefits include health, dental, and vision insurance, a 401(k), paid time off, and a referral program. This is a full-time, on-site position.

smartrecruiters_744000144548318.title: Apartment Maintenance Technician - City Center on 7th
smartrecruiters_744000144548318.rewritten_description:
City Center on 7th is a 700-plus-unit community in Pembroke Pines, and a property that size generates serious maintenance volume. This technician role sits at the center of that daily operation, handling everything from resident repair requests to apartment turns between tenancies.

The Day-to-Day

A typical day here moves fast. You might start with a punch list item from a recent turn, shift to a plumbing call, and end the afternoon troubleshooting an HVAC unit before the Florida heat makes it someone's emergency. AIR uses technology to route and prioritize work orders, which keeps things organized, but it also means the pace is visible. You'll see exactly where you stand in the queue, and so will your supervisor.

Make-readies are a real part of this job. Getting an apartment to move-in condition requires attention to detail and the ability to spot what others miss. At a community this size, turns happen regularly, and the quality of that work directly affects the resident's first impression.

Repairs fall across plumbing, electrical, HVAC, and appliances. You need solid working knowledge in at least two of those trades. You don't need to be a licensed contractor, but you do need to be the person who fixes it right the first time without needing someone to hold your hand through it.

What This Job Actually Requires

  • At least two years of maintenance experience in a facilities or residential building environment
  • Proficiency in two or more trades: plumbing, electrical, HVAC, appliance repair, or carpentry
  • Flexibility to work evenings, weekends, and on-call shifts at least one week per month
  • Reliable personal transportation for after-hours emergency response
  • Physical ability to move heavy equipment and machinery as part of regular duties
  • Ability to read, write, and speak English

On-call is worth addressing plainly. You will get calls after hours. That's the job at a property this size. If that's a dealbreaker, this one probably isn't the right fit. If you can handle it, the compensation reflects that expectation: the hourly rate runs $20 to $24 depending on your skills, and technicians who consistently earn strong resident satisfaction scores can pick up up to $1,500 in quarterly bonuses.

Compensation and Career Path

The 50% rent discount at any AIR community is a real benefit, especially in South Florida where housing costs are significant. Living on-site at City Center or nearby eliminates commute time and puts you close when on-call responses happen.

AIR's Ascend program is built around individual development rather than a one-size track. If you want to move toward lead technician or maintenance supervisor, the structure is there. Large communities like this one are actually good training ground because the volume of work exposes you to more situations faster than a smaller property would. Technicians who build a record of quality turns, low callbacks, and strong resident feedback tend to get noticed.

Additional benefits include a 401(k) with up to 6% employer match, medical, dental, and vision coverage, 14 paid holidays, up to 16 weeks of paid parental leave, and tuition reimbursement for job-related certifications and licenses.

greenhouse_6150995004.title: Regional Manager
greenhouse_6150995004.rewritten_description:
What You'll Actually Do

This is a portfolio-level operations role with Asset Living, one of the largest third-party management firms in the country. You'll oversee a group of communities in the Salt Lake City market, working offsite but staying close enough to each property that nothing slips through. Your week will pull you between financial reviews, site visits, staffing conversations, and ownership reporting. The leasing environment in the Wasatch Front has been active, and occupancy pressures shift quickly as new supply continues to come online along the I-15 corridor. Knowing how to read that kind of market and translate it into a sharp marketing plan matters here.

On the financial side, you'll own NOI performance across your portfolio. That means developing annual operating budgets, reviewing monthly variance reports on income and expense line items, and flagging capex needs before they become emergencies. You'll monitor rent collections, reconcile deposits, approve vendor invoices, and make sure ownership financial reports close accurately and on time. When a property's T-12 starts showing a pattern, you're expected to catch it and recommend an adjustment, not wait for someone upstream to notice.

Personnel management takes up a significant share of your attention. You'll screen and hire community managers, coach them consistently, and hold them accountable using documented processes. Salary recommendations, timesheets, performance counseling, and terminations all run through you. Asset Living operates across multifamily, build-to-rent, affordable housing, and student housing segments, so your portfolio may not be uniform. The ability to lead site teams through different compliance environments and operational rhythms is genuinely useful here.

You'll also be responsible for leasing strategy at each property. That includes developing yearly marketing plans, evaluating staff leasing techniques, and building resident retention programs that keep renewals strong. When traffic slows or concessions creep up, you'll be expected to diagnose why and respond with a real plan.

What You Bring

  • Demonstrated experience managing a portfolio of multifamily communities as a regional or district manager
  • Solid grasp of property financials: budgeting, NOI analysis, variance reporting, and capex planning
  • Hands-on experience hiring, training, and managing on-site property management teams
  • Working knowledge of fair housing regulations and safety compliance requirements
  • Familiarity with leasing performance metrics and marketing strategy for multifamily assets
  • Strong communication skills with ownership groups and internal leadership
  • Experience with property management software and reporting systems

Context Worth Knowing

Asset Living operates as a fee management company, which means your communities have owners who expect accurate reporting and responsive communication. Regional managers in third-party management carry a different kind of accountability than those at owner-operators. You're representing the firm's reputation on every property, every quarter. Candidates who do well in this kind of role tend to be disciplined about documentation, comfortable having direct conversations with both site staff and ownership, and consistent in how they apply company standards across a mixed portfolio. The Salt Lake City market rewards managers who stay ahead of the leasing calendar rather than reacting to vacancy after it appears.

greenhouse_7943690003.title: Lead Maintenance Technician - Olympus Latitude
greenhouse_7943690003.rewritten_description:
Olympus Property has earned the National Apartment Association's Top Employer designation three years running (2023, 2024, 2025), which tells you something about how the company treats the people doing the actual work. The Lead Maintenance Technician role at Olympus Latitude in Albuquerque sits at the center of that operation. This is a maintenance supervisor position in all but title, and the scope reflects that.

Day to day, you're running the service operation for the community. That means scheduling your team's daily, weekly, and monthly workloads, coordinating turns so vacant units are make-ready on time, and managing both in-house technicians and outside contractors. You'll handle preventative maintenance, oversee grounds and irrigation, coordinate repairs across structural, mechanical, electrical, and HVAC systems, and keep the shop organized and properly stocked. Monthly, quarterly, and yearly property inspections fall to you as well. You'll work closely with the on-site office team and the Business Manager to keep show units and upcoming move-ins clean and ready.

EPA/HVAC certification is required, along with at least three years of residential or apartment maintenance experience in a technician or supervisor capacity. The schedule runs Monday through Friday, 9 AM to 5 PM, with weekend availability and on-call rotation built in.

What This Role Builds

Lead tech roles are often where strong maintenance careers take a meaningful turn. You stop being purely reactive and start developing skills that compound: team development, vendor management, budget awareness through inventory control, and the kind of cross-functional communication that property managers rely on when things go sideways. People who do this role well often move into Regional Maintenance Supervisor positions or transition into property operations roles where that technical fluency becomes a real asset. The software systems Olympus uses to track service requests and inventory are the same types of platforms you'd encounter across any institutional owner's portfolio, so what you learn here travels.

What separates strong candidates from average ones at this level isn't just technical range. It's the ability to prioritize competing demands without losing track of unit turns, keep a team motivated through busy seasons, and build contractor relationships that actually hold up when you need someone on-site fast. Albuquerque's climate puts real demands on HVAC systems and irrigation, so comfort with both is genuinely useful here.

  • Minimum 3 years residential or apartment maintenance experience
  • EPA/HVAC certification required
  • Full-time availability, Monday through Friday, with weekend and on-call coverage
  • Experience managing or coordinating a maintenance team preferred

Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, 401(k) with employer matching, tuition reimbursement, pet insurance, short and long-term disability, life and AD&D insurance, paid time off, an apartment rental allowance, and a sabbatical program. Monthly and quarterly bonuses are part of the compensation structure for eligible team members.

greenhouse_4379741009.title: Community Manager
greenhouse_4379741009.location: West End Station - 206 N. Green St - Winston-Salem, NC - 27101
greenhouse_4379741009.rewritten_description:
West End Station is a property that calls for a community manager who can run a full operation, not just put out fires. Hawthorne Residential Partners, one of the larger Southeast-based multifamily operators in the country, is hiring for this Winston-Salem location and looking for someone who's ready to own the outcome.

What This Role Actually Covers

This is the full seat. You're accountable for financial performance, occupancy, team development, resident satisfaction, and the physical condition of the asset. On any given week, that means reviewing delinquency reports and following up on collections, walking the property for curb appeal and punch list items, coordinating with maintenance on work order backlog, and making sure your leasing team is converting traffic. It also means sitting in on a tough conversation with a resident and then turning around to coach a new leasing consultant on objection handling. The scope is real.

On the leasing side, you'll set pricing strategy and renewal targets alongside whatever guidance comes from regional. You'll support your team on tours when volume demands it, and you'll monitor occupancy closely enough to adjust concessions or marketing spend before a problem becomes a headline. Yardi and Knock are the core platforms here, so comfort with both matters from day one.

Vendor management, compliance, deposit accounting, move-out processing, online reputation, social media, resident events. It's all on your plate. That's the job.

Who Fits This Role

  • At least two years in multifamily, including time as a leasing consultant and assistant manager
  • Six months of direct community manager experience, strongly preferred
  • Working knowledge of Yardi, Knock, and Microsoft Office
  • High school diploma or GED; CAM, CAPS, or a real estate license is a plus
  • Valid driver's license

The candidates who tend to succeed here aren't necessarily the ones with the flashiest resumes. They're the ones who understand how financial performance and team morale connect. A manager who can read a T-12, spot where NOI is leaking, and then walk back to the leasing office and genuinely motivate their team is a different skill set than most people think. If you've only ever done one or the other, this role will stretch you.

Growth and Compensation

Hawthorne structures a career path from community manager to regional manager and backs it with a formal learning and development program. That's worth taking seriously if you're looking at your next two to three years in multifamily. The compensation package includes a base salary plus monthly leasing and renewal commissions and quarterly performance bonuses. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401k match, paid time off (including your birthday, which is a small thing that's actually a nice touch), pet insurance, paid parental and adoption leave, and company-paid life insurance.

The leasing office runs Monday through Friday, 9 to 6, with Saturday hours from 10 to 4. One weekday off per week keeps it at a 40-hour schedule, though resident events and community needs can pull you outside those hours on occasion. That's property management.

greenhouse_6150824004.title: Temporary Project Access Assistant at Alpha Mill Apartments
greenhouse_6150824004.rewritten_description:
A vendor crew arrives at 8:30 AM ready to pull cable through a unit, and it's your job to make sure they get in, stay on track, and don't create surprises for residents or management. That's the core of this role, and it's more coordination-intensive than it sounds.

What the Work Actually Involves

Cottonwood Residential is running a network infrastructure installation at Alpha Mill Apartments in Charlotte, and they need someone on-site to manage the day-to-day flow of that project. The assignment is temporary, estimated between one and seven weeks depending on how the installation progresses.

Each day, you'll coordinate vendor access to individual apartment homes and shared community spaces. That means walking units and common areas repeatedly throughout the day, not just doing a single morning walkthrough. You'll watch that the work is being done correctly, flag anything that looks off or behind schedule, and keep the IT Manager informed with timely updates. At the end of each shift, you'll produce a written daily recap covering progress, issues, and any resident interactions worth noting.

You'll also serve as the face of Cottonwood on-site. Residents may have questions or concerns when vendors are moving through their building. Handling those interactions professionally matters here, because a network installation can feel disruptive to residents even when it's going smoothly.

Skills This Role Requires and Skills It Builds

On the required side, you'll need strong organizational habits and real attention to detail. You're essentially keeping a live record of a construction-adjacent project, and gaps in documentation tend to surface as problems later. Clear written communication is non-negotiable since your daily recaps are the IT Manager's primary visibility into site conditions. You'll also need to be genuinely comfortable on your feet: stairs, hallways, and outdoor areas are part of the daily circuit.

What this role builds is equally worth noting. Vendor coordination and on-site project oversight are skills that transfer directly into property management, facilities management, and construction administration roles. Learning to track work against a scope, document deviations, and communicate up the chain under time pressure is exactly the kind of experience that distinguishes a strong coordinator candidate later. For someone early in a property management or real estate operations career, this short-term assignment produces a concrete, citable example of site management work.

  • Strong organizational skills with attention to detail
  • Ability to walk units, stairs, and community grounds repeatedly throughout the day
  • Clear written and verbal communication skills
  • Professional customer service approach with residents, staff, and vendors
  • Basic computer proficiency for documentation
  • Dependable, punctual, and capable of working independently
  • Bilingual English and Spanish is a plus

The position pays $15 to $17 per hour depending on experience, runs Monday through Friday from 8:30 AM to 5:00 PM, and targets a September 14th, 2026 start date. The role reports to the IT Manager.

workable_6048143.title: Multifamily maintenance tech
workable_6048143.rewritten_description:
Maintenance tech roles at multifamily properties are pretty straightforward on paper. In practice, your day shifts between planned preventive work and whatever residents decided needed attention overnight. At Karya Property Management in Phoenix, this position covers the full range of day-to-day upkeep across residential apartment communities.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

You'll handle repairs across the standard trades: plumbing, electrical, HVAC, carpentry, and painting. Some days that means working through a ticket queue of resident requests. Other days it means responding to something urgent before the morning's half over. You'll also carry a share of the turn and make-ready workload, which in Phoenix's market means moving efficiently through punch lists during peak leasing periods without cutting corners on quality. Preventive maintenance rounds, tool upkeep, and inventory management round out the routine.

The role requires flexibility on hours, including evenings, weekends, and on-call availability. That's not a buried footnote. It's a real part of the job and something worth factoring in before you apply.

What Karya Is Looking For

  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • One to three years of hands-on multifamily maintenance experience, or comparable work in a related field
  • Working knowledge of HVAC systems, plumbing, electrical, and general carpentry
  • Ability to troubleshoot and complete repairs independently without waiting for someone to walk you through it
  • Valid driver's license and reliable transportation
  • Solid communication skills and enough organizational sense to manage your own ticket flow

HVAC knowledge carries real weight in Phoenix. The Valley runs air conditioning hard for a long stretch of the year, and a tech who can diagnose and address HVAC issues without escalating every call keeps residents satisfied and keeps the maintenance team running smoothly. If that's a strength you've built, lead with it.

Where This Role Can Take You

Technician roles at well-run multifamily companies are a legitimate path into lead maintenance and eventually maintenance supervisor positions. The techs who move up tend to be the ones who treat preventive maintenance as seriously as emergency response, who communicate clearly with the office team, and who bring a consistent standard to make-readies regardless of how tight the turn schedule gets. Karya offers health and wellness benefits, strong PTO, and parental leave, which signals a company that's thinking about retention rather than just filling a seat.

workable_6049758.title: Paint & resurface tech
workable_6049758.rewritten_description:
The make-ready cycle is where resident impressions get set, and a sloppy paint job or a bubbling countertop resurface will undermine everything else the team did right on that turn. Karya Property Management is building out the maintenance side of their residential portfolio in Phoenix and adding a dedicated Paint and Resurface Technician to keep that work consistent and in-house.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Most of your time will split between unit turns and ongoing property upkeep. On a turn, you're prepping surfaces, patching holes and cracks, sanding, priming, and laying down finish coats on interior walls and trim. You'll also handle countertop and cabinet resurfacing, which is the kind of work that significantly changes how a unit photographs and how it feels to a prospective resident walking in. Exterior surfaces come into the rotation too, so you're not confined to unit interiors.

Beyond the turn work, you'll coordinate with the broader maintenance and property management teams to schedule jobs and move efficiently across properties. That scheduling piece matters more than it sounds. A tech who can sequence prep, cure times, and resurfacing work without holding up a unit goes-live date is genuinely valuable. Phoenix heat affects dry times and material behavior, so knowing how to adjust application technique in high temperatures is a real skill here.

What Karya Is Looking For

  • Prior experience in painting and surface resurfacing, residential preferred
  • Familiarity with different finishes, application techniques, and appropriate materials for various surfaces
  • Detail orientation and consistent workmanship quality
  • Ability to manage your own schedule and work independently across sites
  • Valid driver's license and reliable transportation
  • Clear communication with maintenance coordinators and property teams

Karya offers health and wellness benefits, PTO, and maternity and paternity leave. The role includes the standard safety protocol expectations that come with any maintenance position.

One honest note: techs who do this work well tend to become indispensable on any maintenance team, because consistent, quality paint and resurface output is hard to find and easy to notice when it's missing. It's a role with a clear path toward senior maintenance or facilities coordination for someone who wants to grow.

smartrecruiters_744000145319979.title: Apartment Community Manager - The Rosery
smartrecruiters_744000145319979.rewritten_description:
A resident stops by the office at 10:15 on a Tuesday morning, frustrated about a maintenance follow-up that slipped through the cracks. By 11:00, you've pulled the work order history, coached your maintenance lead on the communication gap, and turned that resident into someone who renews their lease three months later. That's the daily reality of running The Rosery.

The Role

AIR Communities is hiring a Community Manager for The Rosery, their apartment community in Largo, FL. This is a full P&L leadership position. You'll own the property budget, drive NOI, and carry responsibility for occupancy, revenue growth, and resident satisfaction. Leasing activity, maintenance coordination, delinquency management, and adherence to legal and company standards all fall under your oversight.

Your direct team will include at least two reports spanning leasing and maintenance functions. A significant part of the job is developing those people: coaching performance, setting expectations, and building a team that can execute consistently without needing you in every room. AIR positions its Community Managers as operators first, and that expectation starts on day one.

The typical schedule runs Tuesday through Saturday, 10:00am to 6:30pm, though hours can shift with the season and community needs. Reliable transportation is required.

What You'll Bring

  • At least 4 years of experience in sales, customer service, and asset management, ideally in property management or a comparable service industry
  • At least 2 years in a property management leadership role, with a track record of coaching and developing a team
  • Comfort working with property financials, budgets, and performance metrics to identify problems and act on them
  • Familiarity with platforms like Entrata, OneSite, SmartRent, or Salesforce
  • A Florida Real Estate License, or a genuine commitment to obtaining one within six months of hire
  • Affordable housing experience is a plus

The compensation range sits between $75,000 and $80,000 base, with a 15% target bonus, commissions on new leases and renewals, and a full benefits package that includes medical, dental, vision, 401(k) with up to 6% employer match, paid parental leave up to 16 weeks, tuition assistance, and 14 paid holidays. An on-site apartment discount is also available.

Pinellas County's rental market has stayed competitive, with Largo and the broader Clearwater corridor drawing steady renter demand from both relocators and long-term locals. Managers who understand how to balance concessions discipline with strong renewal conversion tend to outperform here, because traffic alone doesn't protect occupancy when the surrounding submarkets are offering aggressive move-in incentives. If you've managed through a lease-up or a competitive turn season in a similar Florida coastal market, that experience will translate directly.

greenhouse_4379834009.title: Front Door Waste Technician-Cortland Lake Ridge Ridge
greenhouse_4379834009.rewritten_description:
It's 6:30 p.m. on a Tuesday. Residents are getting home from work, dogs need walking, and the valet trash window is open. Your route needs to run clean and on time, because in multifamily, the details residents notice most are the ones that happen right outside their front door.

What the Role Actually Involves

Cortland is hiring a Front Door Waste Technician at their Lake Ridge community in Hilliard, OH. This is a valet trash position, which means you're running a nightly collection route through the property, picking up resident waste bags set outside unit doors, loading them into leak-proof carts, and transporting everything to the onsite compactors or waste containers. You'll also clear trash from dog waste stations, pool areas, mail kiosks, parking lots, and common areas throughout the property.

The job has a real physical component. You're climbing stairs, covering ground on foot, and lifting up to 50 pounds through the full shift. Outdoor work in all weather is part of it, and so is the occasional strong odor. That's just the reality of the role. If you've worked in waste services or a service-focused job before, you already know what you're signing up for.

Cortland tracks route completion through a mobile app. You'll log start and end times, document your work with photos, and flag any improper or prohibited waste you encounter. Staying visible on property and communicating clearly with residents and staff is a daily expectation, not an afterthought. This is a resident-facing position, and how you carry yourself matters.

What Cortland Is Looking For

  • High school diploma or equivalent, preferred
  • At least one year of experience in waste services or a customer-facing role
  • Working knowledge of EPA and OSHA regulations for waste handling
  • Strong communication skills; bilingual ability is a plus
  • Ability to operate basic equipment, including compactors
  • Valid driver's license for local driving as needed
  • Personal smartphone (Android 2.2+ or iPhone iOS 4.3+) with an active data plan for app-based reporting
  • Physical ability to climb stairs, walk long distances, and lift up to 50 lbs throughout a shift

What separates the candidates who stick around in this role from those who don't is consistency. Routes run five or more nights a week. Residents notice immediately when service slips, and property managers notice too. Reliability, a professional attitude with residents, and attention to site cleanliness are the things that actually matter here day to day.

Cortland is a large, vertically integrated multifamily operator, founded in 2005 and ranked among the top ten multifamily owners in the country. They run their own design, construction, and operations, which means their properties tend to be actively managed with clear standards. For the right person, this kind of environment offers stability and a defined set of expectations, which can be easier to succeed in than a loosely run smaller operation.

greenhouse_8152830.title: Assistant Property Manager
greenhouse_8152830.rewritten_description:
Weinstein Properties has been family-owned and operated for over 70 years, with more than 60 apartment communities across Virginia, North Carolina, Texas, Tennessee, and Georgia. That kind of longevity doesn't happen by accident. It reflects a consistent commitment to how people are treated, both residents and employees. This Assistant Property Manager role in Henrico's West End sits at the center of that philosophy.

What the Day-to-Day Actually Looks Like

This role touches nearly every part of community life. In the morning, you might be responding to internet leads and scheduling tours. By midday, you're walking a make-ready unit with maintenance to confirm it's truly move-in ready. The afternoon could bring a lease renewal conversation, a security deposit disposition, or helping a resident work through an account question. No two days stack up the same way.

Specific responsibilities include:

  • Working with prospective residents from first contact through lease signing, including phone and internet inquiries, tours, applications, and paperwork
  • Providing ongoing resident support: renewals, notices to vacate, transfers, pet addendums, work order follow-ups, and general account questions
  • Posting rent, tracking balances, and following up on amounts owed
  • Coordinating with maintenance on unit readiness and property upkeep
  • Processing move-outs and handling security deposit dispositions
  • Planning and hosting resident events
  • Supporting the Property Manager and helping train and lead the on-site team

Saturday hours are part of the schedule, worked on a rotating basis with the team. Occasionally, resident events or weather situations will ask something extra of you. That's the nature of on-site property management, and Weinstein is straightforward about it.

Who Tends to Succeed Here

Prior property management experience is a plus, but Weinstein genuinely recruits from hospitality, sales, and customer service backgrounds. If you've managed people or handled difficult customer situations with composure, the leasing and operations knowledge can be taught. What's harder to teach is the ability to hold a conversation with a frustrated resident, de-escalate without getting defensive, and then pivot to showing a prospective resident the community with genuine warmth. That's the real skill set this role demands.

Strong candidates tend to be organized without being rigid. They keep the punch list moving on a make-ready while also catching an incoming call and not making either person feel like they're second priority. Attention to detail matters here because mistakes on lease paperwork or security deposit dispositions create real problems downstream. Leadership experience is required because this role carries real responsibility for team outcomes, not just individual tasks.

Growth and Company Culture

Weinstein has a track record of promoting from within. Many of their current leaders started in leasing or assistant roles. The training program here is structured and intentional, so if you're newer to property management, you won't be left to figure things out on your own. The company wants this to be a career you grow into over time, which shows up in how they invest in coaching and professional development at the site level.

Compensation starts at $21 per hour, increases with experience, and includes quarterly bonuses. Benefits include health, dental, and vision coverage, a 401k with company match, paid holidays, birthday time off, an employee assistance program, and a rent discount.

greenhouse_4378873009.title: Desk Clerk (Ira D. Hall Square)
greenhouse_4378873009.rewritten_description:
Desk Clerk roles at affordable housing communities carry more weight than a typical front-desk job. You're often the first person a resident sees in a crisis, the last line of building security at night, and the connective tissue between management and the people who actually live there. At MidPen Housing's Ira D. Hall Square in Sunnyvale, that context matters.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

This is a part-time evening position, Monday through Friday, 6PM to 10PM. During those hours, you're the point of contact for everyone entering and leaving the building. You'll greet and screen visitors, maintain the front desk log, monitor the camera system, answer phones, and write incident reports when something happens. Administrative tasks round out the shift: filing, distributing notices, completing work orders, and keeping the lobby and entrance area tidy and professional.

You'll report to the Community Manager and work within MidPen's Fair Housing and community policy guidelines. The expectation is that you apply those policies consistently and communicate clearly with residents, guests, and staff.

What You Bring

  • A high school diploma or GED and at least one year of receptionist or administrative experience
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Comfort with basic computer tasks, including Microsoft Word and Excel
  • Flexibility to handle varied tasks as they come up during a shift
  • Genuine alignment with the mission of providing stable, dignified housing to people who need it

Where This Role Can Lead

Evening desk roles at mission-driven housing organizations are a real entry point into property management. The skills you build here, specifically incident documentation, resident relations, and policy enforcement, are the same ones that Community Managers look for in Leasing Consultants and Resident Services Coordinators. MidPen manages over 142 properties across Northern California, which means internal mobility is a realistic path for people who prove themselves reliable and mission-aligned.

Affordable housing also gives you exposure to a population mix and a compliance environment that builds genuine fluency fast. If you eventually want to move into site management or resident services coordination, time spent in a desk role at an affordable community teaches you things a Class A lease-up position simply won't.

The pay range for this position is $17.69 to $19.90 per hour, based on experience. MidPen offers a benefits package that includes health, dental, vision, retirement, and paid time off, even for part-time staff, which is not the norm in this industry.

greenhouse_4378196009.title: Assistant Community Manager
greenhouse_4378196009.location: Yester Oaks - 100 Yester Oaks Way East - Greensboro, NC - 27455
greenhouse_4378196009.rewritten_description:
The assistant community manager role exists because running an apartment community is genuinely too much for one person. The CM sets direction and handles ownership-level accountability. The ACM keeps the daily operation from slipping: delinquency follow-up, ledger accuracy, leasing traffic, and the dozen small fires that don't wait for a convenient moment. At Hawthorne Residential Partners, a Southeast-based management company that ranks among the top 50 multifamily operators nationally, this position sits at Yester Oaks in Greensboro, NC.

The Day-to-Day Reality

This is a split-focus role, which is both its challenge and its appeal. Part of your week runs through the leasing office: working leads, conducting tours, moving applications through to executed leases, and handling renewals. The other part is administrative and financial. You're posting payments, scanning checks, monitoring delinquency, making collection calls, and reviewing ledgers for billing accuracy. When the Community Manager is out, you run the site. That's not a once-a-year thing. Plan for it.

Hawthorne also expects this role to contribute to social media content and to keep the leasing office and common areas presentation-ready. Neither is glamorous, but both affect how prospects experience the community on tour days.

The schedule runs Monday through Friday, 9 to 6, with Saturdays from 10 to 4. One weekday off keeps the week at 40 hours. Resident events and community-specific needs may pull you in on evenings or weekends periodically.

What Hawthorne Is Looking For

  • Two years of property management experience preferred
  • Six months in an assistant community manager or similar capacity preferred
  • Comfort reading financial reports and working within budget constraints
  • Confidence handling resident conflict without escalating it
  • High School diploma or GED required; CALP designation is a plus
  • Valid driver's license required

Candidates who perform well here already know how to read a delinquency report and act on it without being told twice. The leasing side is learnable; the financial discipline is harder to train. If you've worked a site where you owned collections and ledger review, you'll feel the difference immediately.

Compensation includes an hourly base plus monthly leasing and renewal commissions and quarterly performance bonuses. Hawthorne runs an internal career path program, and the ACM-to-CM track is a real one, not a talking point. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, 401k with match, paid time off (including your birthday), paid parental and adoption leave, pet insurance, company-paid life insurance, and 24/7 telehealth access.

greenhouse_4373561009.title: Leasing Consultant (Part-Time)
greenhouse_4373561009.rewritten_description:
A prospective resident walks in on a Saturday afternoon, having toured three other communities that week. They're tired, they're skeptical, and they haven't signed anywhere. What happens in the next thirty minutes depends entirely on you.

That's the central skill this part-time leasing consultant role at Berkshire Residential Investments builds, day after day: reading people quickly, earning trust, and converting genuine interest into a signed lease. Berkshire owns and manages its own properties, which means the team you join has real stake in outcomes. This isn't third-party management where directives come from a distant asset manager. The people above you in the org chart care about occupancy and resident satisfaction for the same reasons you will.

What the Work Actually Involves

Your primary job is guiding prospective residents from curiosity to commitment. Berkshire holds consultants to a closing ratio of at least 20%, which is a real benchmark that keeps you honest about your sales technique. Beyond the close, you'll maintain tour routes and model units so they consistently make the right first impression, track local market conditions so your pitches stay grounded in reality, and handle resident communications with enough professionalism that people feel heard rather than processed. Administrative accuracy matters here, because leasing paperwork done sloppily creates downstream problems for the whole team.

You'll also contribute ideas on marketing and resident satisfaction to the property manager. That collaboration matters more than it sounds. Consultants who pay attention to what objections come up repeatedly, or which concessions actually move traffic, bring real operational value beyond their closing numbers.

What You're Building Toward

Part-time leasing roles are often where strong property management careers start, and for good reason. The skills compound fast. You develop fluency in lease terms and fair housing compliance, you learn how occupancy decisions ripple into NOI, and you build the resident relationship skills that become essential if you move toward assistant manager or leasing director roles. Consultants who take the market-awareness piece seriously, not just memorizing comps but understanding why rents move, tend to make the jump to management-track positions more quickly.

Berkshire looks for at least two years of transferable customer service experience, comfort with technology, and strong written and verbal communication skills. Prior leasing experience isn't listed as a requirement, which means this can be a genuine entry point into residential property management for someone coming from retail, hospitality, or another client-facing field.

  • Minimum 20% closing ratio expectation
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • At least two years of customer service or related experience
  • Comfort adapting to leasing software and emerging technology
  • Attention to detail in administrative tasks

Anticipated base salary ranges from $21,750 to $25,000 annually, with placement determined by experience and qualifications. The position is part-time and based at Ellington Metro West.

greenhouse_5385174008.title: Leasing Manager
greenhouse_5385174008.location: New York, New York, United States
greenhouse_5385174008.rewritten_description:
Affordable housing leasing in New York City operates under a distinct set of pressures. HUD regulations, NYC Rent Stabilization rules, waiting list management, and income eligibility requirements stack on top of one another in ways that have little parallel in conventional market-rate leasing. Fairstead, which owns and manages more than 30,000 units across 28 states, is hiring a Leasing Manager to oversee leasing operations at its New York properties and lead a team of leasing specialists through exactly that complexity.

What the Role Actually Covers

This is a supervisory leasing position with hands-on responsibility for occupancy performance. You'll manage the full leasing cycle: qualifying prospective residents against program eligibility criteria, showing units, processing applications, preparing leases and addendums, and reviewing move-in files for completeness and accuracy. Beyond your own activity, you're accountable for the accuracy of data entered by your leasing team in Yardi, and you'll monitor weekly occupancy and traffic reports to spot gaps before they become problems.

Waiting list management is a meaningful part of the job at affordable properties. Keeping those records current, processing applicants in compliance with HUD and agency guidelines, and ensuring all correspondence reflects program requirements takes consistent attention. NYC Rent Regulation laws add another layer, so familiarity with Rent Stabilization procedures matters here in a practical, day-to-day sense.

You'll also stay involved after move-in. Resident retention support, ongoing customer service, and work order coordination are part of the scope, which reflects Fairstead's integrated owner-operator model where leasing and operations stay connected rather than siloed.

What Strong Candidates Bring

  • Three or more years of on-site leasing or sales experience, ideally with exposure to affordable or subsidized housing programs
  • Working knowledge of HUD regulations and NYC Rent Stabilization requirements
  • Proficiency in Yardi and Blue Moon, both of which are used actively in this role
  • Experience supervising or coaching leasing staff, with a track record of improving team performance
  • Comfort managing applicant eligibility reviews under specific program guidelines, not just standard credit and income screening
  • Bachelor's degree
  • Fair housing knowledge and strict adherence to compliance standards

The candidates who stand out in affordable leasing management typically combine genuine compliance fluency with the ability to coach their team through nuanced eligibility conversations. Getting an application wrong at an affordable property isn't just a leasing miss; it can trigger regulatory exposure. The managers who do this well understand that distinction and build habits in their teams accordingly.

Compensation for this role ranges from $90,000 to $100,000 annually, with a benefits package that includes employer-contributed medical coverage, employer-paid vision and life insurance, a 401(k) with company match, and 15 days of PTO plus 7 sick days and 12 or more paid holidays.

workable_6050530.title: Part-Time Leasing Consultant
workable_6050530.rewritten_description:
Student housing and conventional multifamily both need leasing consultants who can close, but student-oriented operators like PeakMade put extra pressure on the leasing cycle. Traffic peaks hard in late winter and spring, renewal decisions happen months before move-out, and a prospect who doesn't hear back within hours often signs somewhere else. This part-time role at a PeakMade community in Akron is built around that reality.

What the Role Actually Involves

Your primary job is converting leads into signed leases across phone, email, in-person tours, and online inquiries. That means responding fast, running tours that uncover what a prospect actually needs, creating urgency without being pushy, and following through on every lead until you get a yes or a definitive no. You'll track all of it in a CRM (Yardi, Entrata, or RealPage, depending on the property), and you'll be expected to keep that data accurate, not just current.

Beyond the front-end sales work, you'll handle lease paperwork, collect deposits, support move-in and move-out events, and help keep the model unit and office presentation in shape. During turn season, you'll assist with the process of getting units ready for the next wave of residents. You'll also stay sharp on competitor pricing and run market surveys as needed. The role touches enough of the operation that you'll learn how a community actually functions, not just how its leasing office looks from the lobby.

  • 1 or more years in sales or leasing, with a track record of hitting conversion targets
  • Comfort with CRM platforms and disciplined multi-touch follow-up habits
  • Availability on weekends and during peak leasing hours
  • Strong communication and the ability to read what a prospect needs quickly

Where This Role Can Take You

Part-time leasing is one of the more underrated entry points in property management. You build closing skills and CRM fluency, but you also get exposure to operations, lease administration, and resident retention. Consultants who demonstrate strong conversion rates and a clean pipeline often move into full-time leasing roles, then into Leasing Manager or Assistant Manager positions where they're coaching others on the same skills they developed here. The commission structure means your earnings grow with your performance, which also means your results are visible in a way that accelerates recognition.

What separates strong candidates from average ones here is follow-up discipline. Most leasing consultants are reasonably good on the tour itself. The ones who consistently hit occupancy targets are the ones running multi-touch outreach sequences without being reminded, personalizing each follow-up, and keeping their CRM data clean enough that nothing falls through. If you've built that habit somewhere else, whether in apartment leasing, retail sales, or another high-volume sales environment, you'll have a head start.

workable_6050522.rewritten_description:
Investment Property Group runs a genuinely large portfolio for a private firm: 150 properties across 13 states, spanning multifamily, manufactured home communities, and RV parks. Their Pacific Northwest presence includes several Grants Pass communities, and this part-time assistant manager role sits right in that mix. You'd be splitting your time between two 55+ manufactured housing communities, Rogue Lea (215 homes) and Westlake Village (93 homes), both in Grants Pass. That's a combined 308 homes, which is a real operational footprint for a part-time position.

The schedule runs Monday through Friday at 27.5 hours per week, with some flexibility built in for occasional evening marketing events or weekend open houses. The pay range is $24 to $28 per hour depending on your background.

Day to day, you'll work closely with the Community Manager on the full range of operations: rent collection, delinquency follow-up, maintenance coordination, vendor communications, and administrative reporting. You'll also carry genuine sales responsibility, touring prospective buyers through available homes, running open houses when needed, and staying on top of local market conditions. In manufactured housing communities, that sales piece often gets underestimated by candidates coming from conventional multifamily. Homes are sold, not just leased, and building relationships with prospective buyers takes a different rhythm than traditional apartment leasing.

The resident demographic matters here. Both communities are age-restricted (55+), which shapes nearly every interaction. Residents tend to be long-term, engaged with their community, and attentive to how concerns are handled. Strong conflict resolution skills and genuine patience go a long way. Someone who enjoys those relationships will find this work rewarding; someone who treats resident interaction as a box to check will struggle.

What makes a strong candidate here

  • At least one year of experience in a manufactured housing or multifamily community of 100+ units
  • Hands-on experience with rent collection and delinquency management
  • Comfort with property management software (Manage America, Rent Cafe, Blue Moon, or similar)
  • Sales or leasing experience, with the ability to conduct tours and close
  • Strong written and verbal communication, especially for resident-facing situations
  • Valid driver's license
  • Organizational discipline to manage two separate communities without things slipping

Candidates who do well in roles like this tend to be self-directed. With a part-time schedule spread across two properties, you won't always have someone looking over your shoulder to sequence your day. The ability to triage competing priorities, a maintenance request at one community while a prospective buyer needs a tour at the other, is exactly the kind of thing that separates a good fit from a great one.

IPG offers a 401k with company match, accrued PTO (one hour per 30 hours worked), critical illness and accident coverage, an employee assistance program, and an employee referral program. For a part-time role, that's a meaningful benefits package worth factoring in.
