smartrecruiters_744000145382489.title: Apartment Community Manager - Verdant Peachtree Creek
smartrecruiters_744000145382489.rewritten_description:
It's a Tuesday morning and occupancy is sitting at 94%. You've got a lease expiring Friday, a maintenance ticket that aged past 24 hours, and your leasing associate just flagged a prospect who toured twice but hasn't signed. You handle all three before noon. That's the rhythm of this role.

What This Role Actually Involves

AIR Communities is hiring a Community Manager for Verdant Peachtree Creek, an apartment community in Atlanta. This is a full P&L leadership position. You'll own the property budget, drive revenue growth, and keep operations aligned with both company policy and local legal requirements. That means tracking NOI, managing delinquency, and making decisions that affect the financial performance of the asset month over month.

You'll lead a team of at least two direct reports across leasing and maintenance, which requires you to coach toward sales outcomes while maintaining resident satisfaction and service quality. Facilitating leasing activity is part of the job, and commissions for new leases and renewals are built into the compensation structure, so your team's close rate has a direct effect on your earnings. The expected base salary range is $75,000 to $85,000 with a 15% target bonus opportunity.

The standard schedule runs Tuesday through Saturday, 10:00am to 6:30pm, though hours can shift by season or community need. An on-site apartment discount benefit is available if you want to live at the property you manage.

Skills This Role Requires vs. Skills It Builds

You need to arrive with a few things already in place. At least four years of experience in sales, customer service, and asset management, with at least two of those years in a property management leadership role. Familiarity with platforms like Entrata, OneSite, SmartRent, or Salesforce matters here because AIR operates at a scale where system fluency saves time daily. You also need a working command of property financials: reading a budget, understanding variances, and knowing when occupancy trends require a leasing response.

What the role develops is different. Managing to metrics across a team sharpens your ability to coach rather than just direct. Overseeing both leasing and maintenance functions at once builds a cross-functional instinct that transfers directly to regional or multi-site roles later. Community managers at this level who demonstrate consistent NOI improvement and team retention tend to move into area manager or regional positions, and AIR supports that trajectory with paid training, leadership development, and tuition assistance up to 100% for job-related certifications.

  • 4+ years in sales, customer service, or asset management (property management preferred, hospitality and retail considered)
  • 2+ years leading a team in a competitive, service-focused environment
  • Demonstrated ability to use sales processes and performance metrics to drive results
  • Working knowledge of property management software platforms
  • General fluency with budgets and financial reporting
  • Reliable transportation and schedule flexibility

Strong candidates in this role tend to be the ones who treat the leasing funnel and the maintenance log with equal attention. Occupancy and resident experience aren't separate concerns at the community manager level. The managers who advance fastest understand that resident retention is a financial strategy, not just a hospitality habit.

greenhouse_5397620008.title: Assistant Property Manager
greenhouse_5397620008.rewritten_description:
Some roles in property management are primarily operational. This one runs on relationship skills first, and everything else follows from there. The Assistant Property Manager at Bozzuto's Mountlake Terrace community spends a meaningful portion of each day reading people: prospective residents deciding where to live, current residents working through a concern, vendors needing direction, and teammates who look to you when the Property Manager is out.

The Skills This Role Draws On Most

Sales instinct matters here, but it's not the transactional kind. Bozzuto tours are meant to be personalized conversations, not scripted walkthroughs. You'll need to listen well enough to connect what you're showing someone to what they've told you they care about. That ability, to genuinely hear people and respond to what's actually being said, is the same skill that makes delinquency conversations go better, that keeps residents loyal when something goes wrong, and that makes coaching a leasing consultant feel like support rather than criticism.

On the financial side, you'll own rent collection and delinquency management, and you'll work with P&L exposure and budget awareness. Comfort with numbers matters, but so does the judgment to know when to push and when to problem-solve with a resident. Yardi proficiency (or a willingness to get there quickly) will help you stay on top of the operational picture day to day.

You'll also be active on social media, creating content that reflects both the community and the broader Bozzuto brand. This isn't a posting-for-the-sake-of-it expectation. The content has to feel genuine to the community and the people who live there.

What the Week Actually Looks Like

One or two weekends per month, you'll be on-site when prospective residents are actively searching. Those days often carry the most traffic and the most energy. In exchange, you get two weekdays off. It's a rhythm that works for some people and not for others, so it's worth being honest with yourself about that before you apply.

When the Property Manager is away, you step into the lead role. That means decisions don't wait. The team looks to you, vendors need answers, and residents still have needs. Experience in hospitality or retail translates well here because those industries train people to handle ambiguity in front of others without it showing.

What Makes This Role at Bozzuto Distinctive

Bozzuto operates across the full property lifecycle (development, construction, management, and maintenance), which gives their on-site teams a broader organizational context than you'd find at a pure fee management shop. For an APM with genuine ambition, that matters. The jump from Assistant Property Manager to Property Manager is the natural next step, and at a company with a portfolio of this size, those openings exist.

The candidates who tend to stand out aren't necessarily the ones with the longest resume. They're the ones who've demonstrated they can hold a team together during a difficult stretch, who've handled a tough delinquency situation without burning a resident relationship, and who bring the same energy to a Tuesday afternoon as they do to a Saturday tour.

  • 4-year degree or equivalent experience in a relevant field
  • 2 or more years in property management, hospitality, or retail
  • Familiarity with P&L basics and budget management
  • Strong written and verbal communication
  • Yardi or comparable property management software experience preferred
  • Comfort creating and managing social media content

Compensation ranges from $30.31 to $34.00 per hour, with bonus eligibility. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, 20 days of paid time off plus holidays, a 401k with company match, and tuition reimbursement.

greenhouse_6151761004.title: Regional Manager
greenhouse_6151761004.rewritten_description:
You're on a call at 8 a.m. reviewing last month's T-12 for a property that missed NOI targets, and by noon you're walking a site with a community manager who needs coaching on leasing follow-up. That's a Regional Manager's day at Asset Living. The role covers the full range, and it moves fast.

What This Role Covers

Asset Living is a third-party management firm, and this Regional Manager position oversees a portfolio of multifamily communities in the Atlanta market. You're the offsite leader accountable for operations, personnel, financial performance, leasing strategy, and compliance across every property in your book.

On the personnel side, you screen, hire, coach, and develop on-site staff. You handle counseling documentation, performance management, and terminations when necessary. You approve timesheets and salary requests, and you work directly with HR and senior leadership when situations escalate.

Financially, you build and own the yearly operating budgets. You track income and expense variances monthly, write evaluations when line items drift off-budget, and flag capex needs before they become emergencies. You also oversee vendor contracts, invoice coding, and deposit reconciliation to keep each property's financials clean at closeout.

Leasing strategy falls to you as well. You develop annual marketing plans, sharpen site-level leasing techniques, and monitor conversion and follow-up across your portfolio. Resident retention programs, including events and outreach, are part of the mix. So is handling escalated resident complaints when on-site staff can't resolve them.

On the administrative and maintenance side, you conduct regular property inspections, monitor service request turnaround, and make sure punch list items get closed. You coordinate emergency response procedures and ensure your teams follow company guidelines when something goes wrong on-site.

What Strong Candidates Bring

  • Demonstrated experience managing a multifamily portfolio as a regional or multi-site leader
  • Comfort reading and presenting financial statements, including budget-to-actual variance analysis
  • Experience developing site-level staff, including performance documentation and HR coordination
  • Solid working knowledge of fair housing regulations and risk management practices
  • Ability to manage multiple community managers and keep each site accountable without micromanaging

Because Asset Living operates as a third-party management company, regional managers here often oversee properties with different ownership groups, asset classes, and reporting expectations simultaneously. Candidates who have worked in fee management environments adapt faster than those who've only managed in-house portfolios. That context matters when you're presenting ownership reports and fielding client calls alongside your day-to-day operations work.

greenhouse_7963332003.title: Maintenance Technician - Avion
greenhouse_7963332003.rewritten_description:
The work order queue fills up fast on a Monday morning in Bozeman. By 9 AM, you might be diagnosing a refrigerator that stopped cooling over the weekend, then pivoting to a plumbing call before lunch. That rhythm, steady and varied, is what a Maintenance Technician role at Olympus Property's Avion community actually looks like day to day.

What the Work Covers

This is a full-scope maintenance position, not a single-trade role. You'll work through a range of service requests that pull from multiple disciplines: HVAC filter replacements and coil cleaning, minor to moderate plumbing repairs, electrical fixture and switch replacements, appliance repairs across refrigerators, stoves, washers, dryers, and ovens, and lock changes or door hardware replacements. Preventative maintenance on HVAC systems is a consistent part of the schedule, so familiarity with those systems matters from day one.

Beyond in-unit work, you'll help maintain grounds, common areas, and pool facilities. The maintenance shop needs to stay organized and stocked, and you'll track all completed work through the property's software system. Daily and weekly priorities run through the Lead Maintenance Technician, so you're working as part of a coordinated service team, not independently. Emergency availability is required when situations arise outside standard hours.

Standard schedule is Monday through Friday, 9 AM to 6 PM, though hours can shift slightly based on property needs.

What You'll Bring and What You'll Build

The role requires a minimum of two years of maintenance experience in a residential, apartment, or commercial setting. You should arrive with hands-on knowledge across plumbing, carpentry, painting, and appliance repair. HVAC experience is expected, and an EPA or HVAC certification is valued. Comfort with hand tools and power tools is assumed from the start.

What this role builds is efficiency under real operational pressure. Technicians who develop a clean, consistent punch list process, who close work orders with accurate notes and minimal callbacks, become candidates for Lead Technician roles over time. The breadth of trade knowledge you'll use here makes you genuinely more versatile across any property type you might work on in the future.

Pay runs between $25.00 and $28.00 per hour depending on experience and location, with monthly and quarterly bonus eligibility. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401(k) with employer matching, tuition reimbursement, short and long-term disability, life insurance, pet insurance, an apartment rental allowance, and a sabbatical program. Olympus Property has earned recognition as a top employer by the National Apartment Association in 2023, 2024, and 2025.

  • Minimum 2 years of residential, apartment, or commercial maintenance experience
  • Working knowledge of HVAC systems; EPA or HVAC license preferred
  • Competency across plumbing, electrical, carpentry, painting, and appliance repair
  • Proficiency with hand tools and power tools
  • Ability to respond to emergency maintenance situations as needed
  • Full-time availability, Monday through Friday

greenhouse_8743478002.location: Redpoint Tuscaloosa, Tuscaloosa, Alabama, United States
greenhouse_8743478002.rewritten_description:
Student housing operates on a rhythm that most multifamily professionals never experience. The lease-up timeline compresses into a single academic calendar, traffic spikes in waves tied to housing fairs and move-in weekends, and the resident population turns over almost entirely once a year. If you want to understand leasing fundamentals under real pressure, this is a strong place to start.

What You'll Actually Do

Scion's Experience Team Member role at Redpoint Tuscaloosa sits at the intersection of leasing, marketing, and customer service. Day to day, you're giving property tours, fielding prospect questions, and handling the back-and-forth communication that moves someone from curious to signed. You'll also support social media content, help plan and run resident engagement events, and flag what's working (and what isn't) in terms of sales conversations and objections. On the administrative side, expect package management, office upkeep, maintenance request coordination, and rotating after-hours on-call coverage including lockouts. Turn periods at student properties are dense, fast, and require everyone on the team to show up ready to execute.

What You Bring

  • A genuine comfort with talking to people from different backgrounds, in person and online
  • Reliability and self-discipline, especially during high-volume periods like summer and Turn
  • Flexibility to work evenings, holidays, and rotating on-call shifts as the schedule demands
  • Strong organizational habits that hold up when the office gets busy
  • Eligibility to work in the United States (visa sponsorship is not available)

Where This Role Takes You

The skills you build here transfer directly into roles like leasing manager, assistant community manager, or marketing coordinator at conventional multifamily properties. Student housing teaches you to close under urgency, communicate across a wide demographic, and manage operations during one of the most logistically demanding events in property management: a full community turn. Operators in Class A garden-style and mid-rise communities actively recruit people with student housing backgrounds because of that experience. The ETM position at Scion is a legitimate entry point into a career track, not just a leasing job. Candidates who advance quickly tend to be the ones who treat every resident interaction as a data point, actively report what's slowing down conversions, and take the on-call rotation seriously rather than treating it as an inconvenience.

greenhouse_5399815008.title: Maintenance Technician
greenhouse_5399815008.rewritten_description:
Hillpointe builds and manages market-rate workforce housing across the Sun Belt, and they do it with an unusually tight vertical structure: land acquisition, construction, procurement, and asset management all run in-house. That means a maintenance technician at one of their communities isn't working for a third-party manager with a slim ops budget. They're working inside an owner-operator that controls its own capital and cares about long-term asset performance.

What the Work Looks Like Day to Day

This role covers the full range of residential maintenance at a garden-style community in Cartersville, GA. You'll run work orders for resident repair requests, perform preventive maintenance on building systems, and turn vacant units through the make-ready process so they're move-in ready on schedule. Grounds upkeep, common area inspections, and supply inventory management round out the routine. Documentation matters here: tracking materials used, logging work orders accurately, and keeping records clean are part of how the property stays operationally sound.

You'll also participate in a rotating on-call schedule, which means evening, weekend, and morning availability come with the position. That's standard at most residential communities, and worth knowing before you apply.

What Hillpointe Is Looking For

  • Hands-on mechanical troubleshooting ability across building systems and common areas
  • Comfort with pre-move-out inspections and punch list work during unit turns
  • EPA Type I and II or Universal certification for refrigerant handling, or willingness to obtain it
  • Experience coordinating with vendors and contractors, including scheduling and materials tracking
  • Valid driver's license for on-site equipment operation
  • High school diploma or GED, plus relevant hands-on experience
  • Ability to lift up to 50 lbs regularly, work at heights, and handle tools in varying outdoor conditions
  • Familiarity with OSHA standards and willingness to follow safety protocols consistently

Where This Role Can Go

Technicians who build strong diagnostic skills and learn to manage turns efficiently tend to advance into lead tech or maintenance supervisor roles as their portfolio of properties grows. At a company developing multiple communities across the Sun Belt at once, internal mobility is a realistic path, especially for someone who takes ownership of their unit and communicates well with the property management team. The combination of preventive maintenance discipline and solid vendor coordination is what separates candidates who grow quickly from those who plateau at the technician level.

greenhouse_6161240004.title: Maintenance Supervisor at Cottonwood Clermont
greenhouse_6161240004.rewritten_description:
Maintenance Supervisor roles at apartment communities demand a specific kind of person: someone who can swap a motor, coach a junior tech through their first HVAC call, and still make time to follow up with the resident in 4B who's been waiting on a work order. At Cottonwood Clermont, that full picture is exactly what this position covers.

What the Day Actually Looks Like

Your mornings will likely start with a review of open service tickets and a check-in with your team before the day gets going. From there, the work is genuinely varied. You'll troubleshoot HVAC, electrical, plumbing, and appliance issues yourself when needed, but a big part of your value here is knowing when to step in and when to let a tech work through a problem on their own. The make-ready process will take real attention: units need to be turned on time so leasing can keep pace, and that punch list mentality matters. Grounds, common areas, pool compliance (CPO certification is a plus here), and building systems all fall under your watch too.

You'll own the on-call schedule, making sure 24/7 emergency coverage is covered without burning out your team. Scheduling is one of those quiet leadership tasks that either builds trust or erodes it fast. Getting it right matters.

Who You're Working With

You'll interact daily with residents who just want things fixed promptly and communicated clearly. That follow-through on service tickets isn't just a performance metric. It's a real piece of how residents decide whether they want to renew. You'll also coordinate with vendors, work alongside the property management team, and take the lead on developing your technicians through both hands-on training and any available classroom education opportunities. Cottonwood supports that development, which means you're expected to take it seriously.

The people dynamics here are real. Not every tech will come in at the same skill level. Some days, you're a plumber; some days, you're a coach; some days, you're the person who has to have a hard conversation about standards. All of that is part of the job.

What the Role Requires

  • EPA Type II or Universal certification (required)
  • Substantial hands-on HVAC troubleshooting experience
  • Valid Driver's License
  • CPO certification (preferred)
  • Experience leading or mentoring a maintenance team
  • Comfort working within building, county, and safety codes

Candidates who tend to stand out in roles like this aren't just technically sharp. They document well, communicate with residents in a way that feels human rather than transactional, and bring a consistency to how they run the team that doesn't depend on who's watching. If you've supervised a maintenance team at a garden-style or mid-rise community before, that experience translates directly here.

Cottonwood Residential has positioned itself as an operator that invests in both tech and people, including early adoption of self-guided tour tools that put more of the leasing process in the resident's hands. That broader mindset tends to carry into how they support maintenance operations too. For a supervisor who wants room to develop a team and build real systems around preventive maintenance and turn efficiency, that context is worth noting.

greenhouse_8155136.rewritten_description:
Apartment communities run on first impressions. A prospective resident walking into a leasing office or model home decides fast. The housekeeper is the person who makes sure that moment lands right. At Bexley Westshore in Cumming, GA, Weinstein Properties is hiring for exactly that role.

Weinstein Properties is family-owned and has been managing apartment communities for over 70 years. They own and operate more than 60 communities across five states. That scale matters here because it means real infrastructure: training, benefits, and a defined path if you want to grow.

What the Job Actually Looks Like

This is a Monday through Friday, 8 AM to 5 PM position. No nights, no weekends. Your day runs across the community: cleaning and resetting leasing offices, clubhouses, fitness centers, and other amenity spaces. You'll also clean and prep vacant apartments and model homes, restock coffee stations, and do touch-up work on move-in ready units.

A straight-up preview: the work is physical and repetitive. You'll spend most of the day on your feet, walking the property, bending, lifting, and cleaning. Some tasks are less glamorous than others. That's the honest version of the role.

What separates the people who thrive here from those who don't is attention to detail and self-direction. Nobody follows you around. You need to spot what needs attention, handle it, and keep moving through your list without being told twice.

Compensation and Qualifications

Starting pay is $17/hour, with higher starting rates available depending on experience. On top of base pay:

  • Quarterly performance bonuses

  • Apartment rent discount

  • Medical, dental, and vision insurance

Weinstein hires for potential. A number of their current leasing consultants, maintenance technicians, and property managers came up through entry-level roles. No specific prior experience is listed as required. Reliability, work ethic, and genuine care about clean, well-kept spaces matter more than a resume.

greenhouse_8747655002.title: Leasing Consultant

greenhouse_8747655002.rewritten_description:
Student housing leasing moves at a different rhythm than conventional multifamily. The academic calendar drives everything: your busiest periods cluster around fall move-in, spring renewals, and summer turn, and the residents you're working with often have parents involved in the decision, roommate dynamics to sort out, and zero prior renting experience. Scion operates Copper Beech Harrisonburg on Virginia's James Madison University corridor, and this Experience Team Member role sits at the center of that resident relationship from first tour to ongoing community life.

What the Day-to-Day Actually Looks Like

A good chunk of your week involves direct resident and prospect interaction: touring the community, answering questions about floor plans and amenities, and following up with people who haven't committed yet. You'll also help management understand where deals are getting stuck, so your observations on objections and pricing friction genuinely matter here. Beyond leasing, you'll assist with resident engagement programming, contribute to social media content, and handle operational tasks like package logging, office upkeep, and coordinating maintenance request follow-through. There's an on-call rotation that includes after-hours lockout assistance, so flexibility isn't optional.

Summer and turn periods deserve a specific mention. Student housing communities can see most of their resident population turn over in a matter of weeks. During those windows, the pace is compressed and the coordination required is real. If you've worked retail or hospitality during a holiday rush, you have some frame of reference, though the physical and logistical scale of a turn is its own thing.

Who Fits This Role Well

  • Someone who genuinely enjoys talking to people across a wide range of backgrounds, including both students and their families
  • Strong communicators who can shift tone depending on whether they're texting a prospect, posting on Instagram, or explaining a lease policy to a concerned parent
  • People who stay organized under variable workloads, because quiet weeks and chaotic weeks can follow each other quickly
  • Candidates available for weekend hours and key seasonal periods including turn

Growth and Team Fit

Experience Team Members who develop a feel for both the sales and operational sides of this role often move into assistant manager or leasing manager positions as they build tenure. Student housing is a distinct specialty, and people who understand the academic-calendar-driven leasing cycle carry that knowledge into any future multifamily role. Scion offers learning reimbursement, which signals that internal development is something the company actually invests in rather than just lists on a job posting. This position is full-time, non-exempt, and based on-site at Copper Beech Harrisonburg.

greenhouse_4376606009.rewritten_description:
Savannah's rental market keeps growing, and 8000 Waters is a community that needs someone who can run the full operation, not just hold the title. Hawthorne Residential Partners is hiring a Community Manager for this Savannah property, and the scope of the role is genuinely broad: financial oversight, leasing performance, team development, resident experience, and vendor coordination all fall under your watch.

On any given day, you might pull delinquency reports in Yardi, walk the property for a punch list, coach a leasing consultant through a tough objection, respond to an escalated resident complaint, and still find time to review renewal pricing before the office closes. That's the realistic picture. The job rewards people who can shift gears without losing track of what actually moves NOI: occupancy, renewals, and expense control.

Hawthorne expects this person to be genuinely present in team leadership. Weekly meetings, one-on-ones, hiring decisions, performance conversations , these aren't checkbox activities here. The maintenance side requires real coordination too. Work orders, preventative care, vendor accountability, and curb appeal inspections are part of your operational rhythm, not someone else's problem.

The schedule runs Monday through Friday with Saturday hours, and the office observes one weekday off to keep the week at 40 hours. Resident events and community needs can pull you outside normal hours occasionally. That's the honest reality of site-level management, and it's worth knowing going in.

Hawthorne's career path structure is worth noting for anyone thinking about trajectory. Community Manager to Regional Manager is a defined progression the company actively supports through a Learning and Development program. If you're managing your first site and want a path forward, the infrastructure exists to move up. Compensation includes base salary, monthly leasing and renewal commissions, and quarterly performance bonuses.

What Hawthorne Is Looking For

  • At least two years of property management experience, including time as a Leasing Consultant and Assistant Community Manager
  • Six months of Community Manager experience in multifamily, strongly preferred
  • Familiarity with Yardi and Knock, strongly preferred
  • Comfort interpreting financial reports and making budget-conscious decisions
  • A valid driver's license; CAM, CAPS, or a real estate license is a plus but not required
  • High school diploma or GED equivalent

The candidates who tend to thrive in site manager roles are the ones who don't treat leasing and operations as separate departments. When occupancy dips, they look at traffic sources, concessions, and renewal conversion simultaneously. They also know how to hold a team accountable without burning through goodwill. If that's how you operate, this role is worth a serious look.

greenhouse_4707912006.title: Leasing Consultant - Lake View
greenhouse_4707912006.rewritten_description:
A prospect walks into the leasing office at Lake View on a Tuesday afternoon, having already toured two other buildings that morning. What you say, how you show the space, and how quickly you follow up afterward will determine whether Reside Living gets that lease or not. That's the core of this role.

The Work Itself

Reside Living manages roughly 3,000 apartments across Chicago, with this position focused on properties in East Lake View and Gold Coast. Both are high-demand neighborhoods where occupancy expectations are real and traffic needs to convert. You'll handle the full leasing cycle: responding to inquiries by phone, text, and email; scheduling and conducting tours; recording every touchpoint in the CRM; and closing applications in compliance with fair housing law, the Fair Credit Reporting Act, and all applicable state and federal regulations.

Beyond the direct leasing work, you'll physically inspect vacant units and common areas, flag anything that needs attention from maintenance, and help coordinate resident events. You'll also run monthly audits of the property's online presence, looking for gaps in how the building shows up in search, on ILS platforms, and in reviews. Findings go directly to the Property Manager, and Reside Living expects consultants to bring ideas, not just observations.

Daily and weekly reporting is part of the job. You'll track your own numbers closely, because the path to earning commission and quarterly bonuses runs through your ability to hit and hold occupancy targets.

What This Role Requires vs. What It Builds

You need to bring at least one year of leasing or sales experience, strong written and verbal communication, and a working knowledge of Microsoft Office and a property management platform like Yardi. Attention to detail and follow-through aren't optional here: a missed callback or a sloppy CRM entry can cost a lease.

What the role builds is more interesting. Leasing consultants at Reside Living have a stated path into property management and leadership. You'll start developing the NOI awareness and occupancy management instincts that property managers use every day. Strong performers here learn to read their own traffic trends, adjust marketing strategy in real time, and build the kind of resident relationships that reduce turnover. Those skills transfer directly upward.

Candidates who stand out tend to already understand that leasing is a sales role with a service component baked in permanently. The follow-up after the tour matters as much as the tour itself. The best consultants treat every prospect touchpoint as part of a longer conversion process, not a one-time pitch.

  • High school diploma or GED required
  • Minimum one year of leasing or sales experience
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite
  • Experience with Yardi or comparable CRM platform preferred
  • Personal smartphone required (iPhone or Android); $50/month stipend provided

Compensation includes a base salary plus commission and quarterly bonuses. Benefits include medical, dental, and life insurance, paid time off, 401(k) matching, a commuter benefit, a 25% monthly apartment discount, and $100 per month in student loan assistance.

greenhouse_6163520004.title: Maintenance Supervisor at Antero Apartments
greenhouse_6163520004.rewritten_description:
A Maintenance Supervisor role at a residential apartment community carries real weight. You're responsible for the physical condition of the asset, the experience of every resident who submits a work order, and the development of the technicians who work alongside you. At Antero Apartments in Colorado Springs, Cottonwood Residential is looking for someone who can hold all three of those responsibilities at once without letting any of them slip.

The Work Itself

The technical foundation here is non-negotiable. You'll troubleshoot and resolve HVAC, electrical, plumbing, and appliance issues, and you'll need EPA Type II or Universal certification coming in. CPO certification is a plus. A valid driver's license is required. What you'll build on top of that foundation is systems thinking: managing the make-ready and turn process so units move through the punch list quickly, keeping occupancy gaps tight and new residents moving in on schedule. You'll also oversee grounds maintenance, general upkeep, and ensure the property stays compliant with applicable building and safety codes. Emergency coverage doesn't stop at 5pm, and you'll be the one setting the staffing schedule that ensures 24/7 response capacity.

On the people side, you'll hire, train, and develop your maintenance techs and community care associates. That means formal classroom instruction and hands-on coaching, not just assigning work orders and walking away. The standard you set for response time, attention to detail, and resident communication becomes the team's standard.

What You Bring vs. What You'll Build

The skills this role requires on day one include:

  • Considerable HVAC troubleshooting experience
  • EPA Type II or Universal certification
  • Working knowledge of electrical, plumbing, and appliance systems
  • Experience managing a make-ready or turn process
  • Ability to lead a team and hold performance standards

What the role develops is harder to list but worth naming. Running a team that handles emergency calls, coordinates turns, and keeps a community clean and code-compliant sharpens your operational judgment in ways that transfer directly to multi-site maintenance roles or regional facilities management. Supervisors who demonstrate strong unit economics in their turn cycle, specifically low vacancy days and controlled make-ready costs, tend to move into those broader roles faster than those who stay purely technical.

The Company Context

Cottonwood Residential positions itself around the resident experience, and that shows up in how they approach maintenance. Timely service ticket follow-up and genuine care for how residents feel about their home are treated as part of the job, not extras. They've also invested in technology like Self-Guided Tours, which signals an organization open to operational change. Compensation includes competitive pay, a bonus structure, full health benefits available within the first 30 days, 401k and HSA company match, three weeks of PTO in the first year, and 10.5 paid holidays.

If you take pride in the physical quality of a community and know how to build that pride in the people who work with you, this role has real room to grow.

greenhouse_5405946008.title: Maintenance Supervisor
greenhouse_5405946008.rewritten_description:
What This Role Actually Demands

This position runs on two core skill sets: trade expertise and operational discipline. You need real plumbing knowledge, the kind that keeps repair calls from turning into vendor invoices. And you need to manage work orders, budgets, schedules, and people with the same attention you'd bring to a tough repair. Birgo operates a paperless maintenance operation across nine multifamily properties in the Buffalo area, so comfort with mobile apps and digital workflows isn't optional. AppFolio is the platform. You'll live in it daily.

The territory covers Tonawanda, Buffalo, and Hamburg. That means you're moving between sites, not anchored to one building. Multi-site experience matters here because the coordination load is real: turns across multiple properties, vendor scheduling, contractor oversight, and an on-call rotation all happen simultaneously. The schedule is Monday through Friday, 8:00 AM to 4:30 PM, with on-call coverage shared across the team.

Day-to-Day Responsibilities

  • Lead apartment turnovers and make-readies across all nine properties, including punch list completion and quality checks
  • Complete high-skilled trade work, particularly plumbing, but also electrical, HVAC, drywall, and general repairs, to reduce outside vendor costs
  • Manage and develop a two-person maintenance tech team: hiring, training, performance, conflict resolution
  • Process work orders and maintain records through AppFolio on a mobile device
  • Track expenses, control costs, and report against budget
  • Source and coordinate vendors and contractors when outside help is required
  • Support preventative maintenance programs and capital improvement projects as needed
  • Set and enforce safety standards for the team
  • Serve as the operational link between property management and the maintenance crew

What Separates Strong Candidates Here

Five or more years in multifamily maintenance and three or more years supervising are the baselines. What pushes a candidate from qualified to exceptional in this role is the combination of hands-on trade skill and administrative follow-through. A lot of experienced technicians don't want to manage paperwork. A lot of supervisors have drifted away from the tools. Birgo needs both in one person, and they're paying $32 to $34 per hour to find it.

The technology fluency piece is worth taking seriously. Birgo runs a fully paperless operation, which keeps the team efficient but requires genuine buy-in. If you've spent years resisting software and prefer paper work orders, this environment will be a grind. If you've already worked in a digital-first maintenance operation, you'll get up to speed quickly and spend more time on the work that actually matters.

Birgo offers a profit-sharing program, mileage and boots reimbursement, professional development support, and a full benefits package including medical, dental, vision, and a 401(k) with employer match. The company manages its own properties rather than operating as a third-party firm, which tends to mean more operational consistency and clearer accountability at the site level.

greenhouse_8742436002.title: Maintenance Supervisor
greenhouse_8742436002.rewritten_description:
Waypoint Management Services runs a high-end luxury community in Daytona Beach, and they need a Maintenance Supervisor who can keep a property performing at that level day in and day out. This isn't a tool-belt-only position. You're leading people, managing a budget, coordinating with contractors, and staying close enough to the Community Manager that nothing slips between the cracks.

The work itself spans the full range of residential property maintenance: HVAC preventive maintenance, plumbing repairs, make-ready turns, pool chemical readings, CPO-level pool oversight, grounds coordination, and emergency response. Work orders turn within 24 hours. Units are move-in ready before a resident ever sets foot inside. You review make-ready punch lists with contractors regularly, and when something breaks on a Saturday night, you're the one coordinating the corrective action.

Daytona Beach's coastal humidity is hard on building systems. HVAC units cycle hard through the summer, and pool chemistry can shift quickly in the heat. A supervisor who treats preventive maintenance as optional tends to spend the back half of the year catching up. The candidates who thrive in markets like this build their PM schedule early, stick to it, and train their team to flag small issues before they become capex problems.

Waypoint is actively growing, which means a Maintenance Supervisor who performs well here has a real path toward Maintenance Director or regional oversight responsibilities as the portfolio expands. That growth also means the systems and processes you help build now may become the standard across future properties.

Bilingual ability in Spanish and English is strongly preferred, which reflects both the team environment and the resident population many Florida communities serve.

What you'll need to bring

  • High school diploma or GED with at least 2 years of hands-on maintenance experience
  • EPA Section 608 certification, Types I and II (required at hire)
  • CPO certification, or willingness to complete it within 90 days of start
  • CAMT certification (preferred)
  • Prior supervisory experience managing both employees and outside vendors
  • Comfort with on-call availability as needed
  • Bilingual Spanish and English (strongly preferred)
  • Working knowledge of OSHA standards and safe operating practices

Benefits start on day one and include medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401k with matching, an employee referral program, and an onsite housing discount. Incentive and bonus opportunities are also part of the package.

greenhouse_4383370009.title: FT Exterior Porter (Mon-Fri, 3PM-10PM)
greenhouse_4383370009.rewritten_description:
Exterior porter work at a mixed-use property like Comstock's Reston portfolio is a skilled trade in its own right. This full-time position with ParkX runs Monday through Friday, 3PM to 10PM, which means you're covering the busiest part of the day for foot traffic, tenant movement, and common area wear. The hours demand someone who can assess what needs attention quickly and prioritize without being told twice.

Skills This Role Uses Every Day

The core of this position is sensory and physical: you read a space and know when it falls short of standard before anyone else notices. Pressure washing, window cleaning, trash removal, and routine janitorial tasks are the daily foundation. You'll also support event setup and breakdown when the schedule calls for it, which requires flexibility and an ability to shift from a steady cleaning rhythm to short-burst, deadline-driven work.

Chemical handling, equipment maintenance, and supply inventory management are real responsibilities here. Knowing how to use cleaning agents safely, keep a janitorial closet orderly, and flag equipment issues before they become failures is part of the craft. End-of-shift documentation and handoff procedures mean your work doesn't disappear when you clock out; it gets recorded and transferred properly.

Customer interaction matters more in this role than people expect. You're visible to tenants, guests, and property staff throughout your shift. A professional demeanor, a courteous acknowledgment of the people around you, and the ability to respond to cleanliness concerns without being prompted are all things the team will notice and rely on.

Skills This Role Builds

Porters who pay attention here develop a strong operational eye. You'll start to recognize patterns: which areas generate the most foot traffic, which surfaces need more frequent attention, and how event activity changes the maintenance load. That kind of pattern recognition is directly transferable to facilities coordination, operations support, and maintenance roles within property management.

Working within a structured reporting chain, communicating hazards to management, and following standardized checklists are habits that translate well into any service-side property role. If your goal is to grow into a lead porter, facilities coordinator, or operations manager position, the documentation and communication habits you form here are the foundation.

What Comstock Offers and What They Expect

Comstock brings a portfolio scope that gives this role real variety. The ParkX operation covers multiple sites in the Reston area, so familiarity with different property types and common area configurations is part of what you'll gain. Benefits include medical, dental, vision, 401(k) match, life insurance, free parking with EV charging, and an annual professional development fund. The company invests in advancement from within, which matters for anyone treating this as a career entry point rather than a placeholder.

The role requires a valid driver's license, a high school diploma or equivalent, and the physical capacity to lift up to 50 pounds and work in variable outdoor conditions. Availability for occasional weekend and after-hours event coverage is part of the position. The posted compensation is $17.80 per hour.

The candidates who stand out in this kind of role are the ones who don't need a supervisor to identify a problem. They see a sidewalk that needs attention at 4PM and handle it before the complaint comes in. That self-direction, paired with consistent reliability, is what separates a good porter from one who gets promoted.

greenhouse_5209959007.title: Property Manager
greenhouse_5209959007.rewritten_description:
Onsite property manager roles in Southern California often spread candidates thin across a single large community. This one works differently: you'll oversee three separate properties totaling 87 units in Pasadena, which means daily variety and a real ownership mentality over a small portfolio rather than one building.

What the Day-to-Day Looks Like

Property Management Associates needs someone who can run the full cycle. That means morning walk-throughs across the properties, tracking preventative maintenance items, coordinating with your maintenance staff and outside vendors, and handling unit and property inspections. You'll also carry the leasing side: showing units, running competitive rent analyses, and keeping occupancy where it needs to be. Delinquency follow-up, notices, and the operational paperwork that keeps everything moving are all part of the job.

You'll live on-site in a provided one-bedroom apartment. One weekend day per week is required, and on-call availability comes with the territory. A valid driver's license and auto insurance are required. PMA provides a $300 monthly auto allowance to cover the multi-site driving.

What You Need

  • At least three years of conventional multifamily property management experience
  • Working knowledge of Yardi for property accounting
  • Ability to supervise maintenance staff and schedule vendors
  • Demonstrated leasing skills, including market analysis
  • Strong written and verbal communication; solid command of Microsoft Office
  • Valid driver's license and current auto insurance

Background check, DMV check, and pre-employment physical are required before hire.

Compensation and Benefits

Pay runs $23 to $25 per hour, plus the on-site apartment and auto allowance. Full-time employees receive medical, dental, vision, and life insurance with an employer contribution, a 401(k) with discretionary company match after one year, short- and long-term disability, supplemental plans, and a generous PTO package covering vacation, holidays, and sick time.

One thing worth noting for candidates considering this role: managing three separate addresses rather than one sharpens your operational instincts fast. You'll build skills in portfolio-level thinking, multi-site vendor coordination, and independent decision-making that translate well into regional or area manager positions down the line. PMA has been in business over 30 years and promotes from within, so the growth path is real for someone who performs.

greenhouse_5407077008.title: Administrative Assistant
greenhouse_5407077008.rewritten_description:
Administrative roles at Bozzuto-managed communities sit at the intersection of resident experience and property operations. This position supports the leasing and management office at a residential community in Centreville, VA, handling the clerical and organizational work that keeps daily operations running cleanly.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

You'll spend your time between the business office and the concierge desk, which means your day shifts regularly between documentation tasks and direct resident interaction. On the documentation side, you'll type up leases, build out resident files, and compile property data for reporting purposes. On the front-facing side, you're a point of contact for residents, which requires clear communication and a genuine interest in delivering good service. Both sides of this role demand accuracy and professionalism in equal measure.

Microsoft Office proficiency is a baseline requirement here. Outlook, Word, and Excel come up constantly in lease preparation, file management, and report compilation. Intermediate math skills matter too, especially when pulling together property data. Strong written communication is not optional; leases and resident correspondence carry legal weight, and errors have real consequences.

Skills This Role Builds

If you're early in a property management career, this kind of role is genuinely useful for developing craft. You'll learn how lease files are structured and maintained, how property reporting flows from raw data to something management can use, and how a leasing office runs operationally day to day. The concierge desk experience, specifically, builds the resident-relations instincts that become more valuable as you move into leasing or assistant manager roles over time.

What separates strong candidates in an admin role like this is the ability to switch contexts without dropping the ball. You might be mid-way through compiling a report when a resident approaches the desk with a question that needs a real answer, not a brush-off. The people who do this work well are organized enough to track multiple open tasks and communicable enough to handle the interruptions gracefully.

The Bozzuto Context

Bozzuto operates across development, construction, and property management, and their managed communities tend to skew toward higher-quality residential product. That means the expectation for professionalism at the community level, including in the admin role, reflects the brand they maintain with residents and clients. The reported salary range for this position is $65,000 to $69,132, with bonus eligibility, health and dental and vision coverage, 20 days of paid time off plus holidays, a 401(k) with company match, and tuition reimbursement.

  • Microsoft Office Suite proficiency (Outlook, Word, Excel)
  • Intermediate written and mathematical skills
  • Strong verbal communication and customer service orientation
  • Comfort working in both a leasing office and concierge desk environment

greenhouse_4384195009.title: Bilingual Leasing Hub Specialist - Sandy Springs, GA
greenhouse_4384195009.rewritten_description:
Centralized leasing hubs exist because following up on 40 to 50 leads a day across multiple communities is a full-time job that on-site teams rarely have the bandwidth to handle well. Cortland built a dedicated hub so that prospect communication actually gets done, and done consistently. This role sits inside that operation.

You won't be stationed at a single community. You'll work from a centralized position in Sandy Springs, fielding inbound calls, emails, and texts from prospective residents across Cortland's portfolio, and making outbound contact to keep leads warm. Your job is to qualify interest, match prospects to the right community based on their needs, and hand off appointment-ready leads to on-site leasing teams. It's a volume role with a sales rhythm. If you've worked in a call center or high-traffic leasing office and liked the pace, this structure will feel familiar.

What the Day Actually Looks Like

Leads come in through RealPage. You work them. That means returning inquiries quickly, asking the right questions to understand what someone actually needs (unit size, location, budget, timeline), and building enough genuine rapport that they want to take the next step. You're representing Cortland's brand in every interaction, so community knowledge matters. You'll do site visits and complete training to stay current on what each property offers, pricing, concessions, and amenities so your recommendations land with confidence rather than guesswork.

Bilingual fluency is listed as a qualification because a portion of Cortland's prospect pool communicates primarily in Spanish. If that's you, this hub needs that capability.

What You Bring

  • At least two years in customer service, ideally with a direct sales component
  • Fluency in English, with bilingual Spanish fluency preferred
  • Strong written and verbal communication across phone, email, and text
  • Comfort with property management software, specifically OneSite. Familiarity with L2L is a plus
  • Typing speed and computer skills that can keep up with a multi-channel lead environment

The candidates who do well here tend to be organized under pressure and genuinely comfortable on the phone. Managing 40 to 50 lead touches a day is repetitive by design. That's not a warning, it's just the reality of the role. People who thrive in it find satisfaction in the conversion, not just the conversation.

For someone looking to grow in multifamily, a centralized leasing hub gives you broad exposure to how a large portfolio operates across different communities, price points, and resident profiles. That cross-community knowledge is a real asset if you eventually move into on-site leasing management or a regional role.

greenhouse_7979826003.title: Maintenance Technician (HVAC Required)- Olympus Fenwick
greenhouse_7979826003.rewritten_description:
Olympus Fenwick in Savannah, GA is adding a Maintenance Technician to the service team. This is a full-time, site-based role covering the standard Monday through Friday schedule with emergency on-call availability folded in. The pay range runs $24 to $25 per hour, with monthly and quarterly bonus eligibility on top of that.

What You'll Actually Do

The bulk of your day will look familiar if you've worked residential maintenance before: working through the service request queue, completing turns, handling preventative maintenance on HVAC units, and fielding the occasional after-hours emergency. HVAC is the non-negotiable here. Coil cleaning, filter changes, and full diagnostic work on units are expected skills, not things you'll learn on the property's dime.

Beyond HVAC, the role covers a wide scope of general maintenance: plumbing repairs and fixture replacement (sinks, showers, toilets), appliance troubleshooting and replacement across the standard kitchen and laundry lineup, electrical fixture and switch work, lock changes and door hardware, and basic carpentry and painting. You'll also support grounds and common area upkeep, including pools, and keep the maintenance shop organized and properly inventoried. Service requests are tracked in software, so comfort with basic digital tools is part of the job.

You'll work directly with the Lead Maintenance Technician on daily and weekly priorities, which keeps the workload structured rather than reactive. That said, emergencies don't schedule themselves, and weekend availability is part of the agreement.

What You Bring

  • Minimum two years of maintenance experience in residential, apartment, or commercial settings
  • EPA/HVAC certification (preferred, and genuinely expected given the role's focus)
  • Working knowledge across plumbing, electrical, appliances, carpentry, and painting
  • Availability for the Monday through Friday schedule and emergency call coverage

The Broader Picture

Savannah's rental market has seen consistent demand, which means properties need service teams that can hold occupancy through responsive maintenance. Resident retention has a direct relationship with how quickly and cleanly work orders get closed. A technician who can handle HVAC competently, keep the shop tight, and communicate well with the office team will have more impact on the property's performance than the role title might suggest.

Olympus Property has earned recognition as a top employer from the National Apartment Association three consecutive years. The benefits package is genuinely competitive for the industry: medical, dental, vision, 401(k) with employer matching, tuition reimbursement, pet insurance, an apartment rental allowance, and sabbatical eligibility among others. For a technician looking to build a long-term career rather than just fill a slot, there's real infrastructure here for growth.

greenhouse_8163291.title: Field Support Supervisor - Multifamily Regional Maintenance
greenhouse_8163291.rewritten_description:
Weinstein Properties has been family-owned and operating for over 70 years, which matters more than it might sound. Self-managed, vertically integrated ownership means decisions don't run through a five-layer approval chain, and the people doing the work are accountable to the same company that cuts the checks. They own and operate apartment communities across Virginia, North Carolina, Texas, Tennessee, and Georgia. This role sits within their Asset Management and Support team and covers the Dallas-Fort Worth portfolio.

The Field Support Supervisor title is accurate to what the job actually is: field-heavy, regional, and technical. You're out on properties regularly, not reviewing reports from a home office. The work involves assessing maintenance operations across multiple communities, helping site teams prioritize and scope projects, evaluating vendors, and managing capex work from bid to completion. You'll also help bridge the gap when the Construction Group hands a project off to the property team, which is one of the more genuinely useful things a regional support person can do. That transition is where documentation falls apart and institutional knowledge gets lost. Doing it well requires someone who can read a set of blueprints and also explain what's on them to a maintenance tech who's never seen a set before.

The technical depth here is real. Weinstein is specifically looking for experience with exterior building repairs, water intrusion, erosion issues, and the ability to write coherent work requirements. Vendor management is a meaningful part of the job. You're not just approving invoices. You're evaluating scope, pushing back on cost reasonableness, and actively recruiting quality contractors to bid projects, which in a competitive DFW market takes more effort than it used to.

The strongest candidates in this kind of role are the ones who've been the person on-site long enough to know what maintenance teams actually need versus what they say they need, and who've also spent enough time on the regional side to translate that into project scope and vendor accountability. EPA Universal certification (or at minimum Type I and II) is required, along with a valid driver's license and five or more years of hands-on multifamily maintenance experience, at least three of which in a regional or multi-site support capacity.

What separates a good regional maintenance supervisor from a great one is usually vendor relationships and credibility with site staff. If technicians and service managers don't trust your read on a problem, the support role breaks down fast. This position requires both.

Qualifications

  • 5+ years of multifamily maintenance experience, with 3+ years in a regional or multi-site support role
  • EPA certification, Type I and II or Universal
  • Hands-on experience with capital projects: exterior repairs, water intrusion, erosion, blueprint reading, and writing work scopes
  • Working knowledge of job site safety requirements
  • Valid driver's license

Weinstein offers competitive compensation, benefits, and a 401k. Given the structure of the organization, this role also carries real visibility with asset management leadership, which tends to matter for people who want to grow into broader operational or construction oversight responsibilities over time.

greenhouse_5222056007.title: Maintenance Supervisor- Westview Heights
greenhouse_5222056007.rewritten_description:
Maintenance supervisors at established multifamily operators don't just fix things. They build systems. At MG Properties, a Western U.S. operator with three decades of apartment acquisition, development, and management behind them, this role at Westview Heights in Portland puts you in charge of how maintenance actually runs, not just whether it gets done.

The day-to-day scope is broad by design. You'll diagnose issues and either handle them directly or assign them to your team based on skill level and priority. You'll inspect completed work, manage the incoming flow of resident service requests, and coordinate scheduling so the right people are in the right place. Preventive maintenance records, expenditure tracking, and equipment upkeep all fall under your watch. Safety meetings are yours to run on a regular cadence. The property manager relies on you to keep the maintenance side of operations organized and accountable.

What this role builds is worth naming clearly. Supervisors who come up through general maintenance often develop strong diagnostic instincts, but the organizational habits that make a maintenance department actually function, scheduling logic, documentation discipline, team performance management, come from leading at this level. You'll sharpen all of it here.

What the role requires going in is equally specific. MG Properties is looking for someone with at least two years of supervisory experience and a background managing maintenance across a minimum of 150 units. Multi-trade competency is expected across plumbing, electrical, HVAC, and general repair. You'll need a valid driver's license and reliable transportation. Beyond technical skill, the work is resident-facing enough that your customer service instincts matter as much as your tool knowledge.

Qualifications

  • Minimum two years of experience as a Maintenance Supervisor, preferably in multifamily
  • Hands-on experience at a property of 150 units or more
  • Proficiency across multiple trades (plumbing, electrical, HVAC, general repair)
  • Strong communication and team coordination skills
  • Valid driver's license and reliable transportation
  • Customer-focused approach to resident interactions

Portland's multifamily market runs a mix of garden-style and mid-rise product, and experienced supervisors who can manage aging mechanical systems alongside modern unit interiors are consistently in demand. MG Properties offers monthly bonuses, profit sharing, a 401(k) with employer match, and a full benefits package including medical, dental, and vision. Rental discounts and paid time off round out the compensation picture.

For maintenance professionals thinking about career trajectory, the Maintenance Supervisor role is often the clearest path toward regional facilities management or Director of Maintenance positions at larger operators. The documentation habits and team leadership skills you refine here translate directly to overseeing multiple properties or training junior staff across a portfolio.

greenhouse_8755504002.title: Assistant Community Manager
greenhouse_8755504002.location: Lark San Antonio, 15655 Market Hl, San Antonio, TX 78256
greenhouse_8755504002.rewritten_description:
Student housing runs on a different clock than conventional multifamily, and Lark San Antonio makes that clear fast. Annual turnover here means something specific: hundreds of students cycling out within a compressed window, every unit on a punch list, vendors coordinated against hard move-in dates. The Assistant General Manager role at this Class A student community sits at the center of all of it.

Scion operates purpose-built student housing at scale, and this position functions as the operational backbone of the property when the General Manager is present and the decision-maker when they're not. That's a real expectation, not a distant possibility. You'll touch every functional area: leasing and sales performance, delinquency management, the annual turn, facilities coordination, team development, and resident experience metrics. Each one feeds the others, and this role is responsible for making sure none of them drift.

On the financial side, you'll help keep delinquency below 2% at month end, manage accounts receivable, process damage charges from quarterly inspections, and assist with month-end reporting and reconciliation. Utility billing and RUBS-adjacent account management are part of the picture. You'll also run weekly market surveys, manage concessions within budget, and partner with a centralized sales team to hit occupancy and revenue targets. Traffic generation and conversion don't just belong to leasing agents here , this role owns the strategy behind them.

The annual turn is where student housing separates from conventional PM. Scion uses Turnable to track progress against an electronic turnover board, and this role is expected to be hands-on: inspecting units, processing move-out damage assessments, coordinating vendor walks, and providing direct labor support where needed, including moving furniture and helping with punches. If you've only managed turns from a desk, expect an adjustment.

The tech stack runs through Entrata (preferred), ClickUp, Lattice, Qualtrics, and Greenhouse. Comfort with these platforms matters for both daily operations and keeping up with Scion's internal reporting and performance systems.

What the role requires

  • At least one year of experience in property management or residential living communities
  • Proficiency in Entrata or a comparable property management system
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, especially for escalated resident issues and review platform responses
  • Detail orientation across financial records, compliance, and inspection documentation
  • Availability for on-call shifts and non-traditional hours, particularly during turn season
  • Eligibility to work in the United States (visa sponsorship is not available)

For candidates thinking about where this leads: the Assistant GM track in student housing is one of the more direct paths to a General Manager role in PM. The exposure here spans leasing, operations, financial reporting, HR basics, and facilities, which is breadth that many conventional multifamily assistant manager roles don't provide. Candidates who perform well in the turn and demonstrate comfort with the financial metrics tend to move up quickly within Scion's structure.

Benefits include health, dental, and vision coverage, 401k with matching, paid parental leave, a discretionary annual bonus, PTO, floating holidays, and learning reimbursement. This is an exempt, salaried position based on-site at Lark San Antonio.

greenhouse_7979899003.title: Leasing Consultant (Cupertino Park Center & Cupertino City Center)
greenhouse_7979899003.rewritten_description:
What You'll Actually Do

This is a leasing role at two Prometheus communities in Cupertino: Cupertino Park Center and Cupertino City Center. Day to day, you're the first point of contact for prospective residents. You'll show apartments, follow up on leads, walk people through applications, and close leases. Prometheus calls this role a "Neighbor Ambassador," and the title reflects something real: the job extends past getting a signature on a lease agreement.

You'll also handle the administrative side of leasing operations. That means preparing rental agreements, running market surveys, keeping occupancy reports current, and managing apartment listings. The customer service piece doesn't stop at move-in. You're helping current residents feel settled and heard, not just converting traffic into signed leases.

Weekend availability is required. That's when foot traffic peaks, and Prometheus schedules accordingly. Your regular days off will fall during the week.

Pay runs $25.00 to $26.25 per hour, plus a $200 per-lease incentive, a semi-annual discretionary bonus, and weekend shift premium pay. Additional bonuses apply for referrals, lease-up periods, and occupancy contests. Medical, dental, and vision are 100% company-paid, including for eligible dependents. A 401(k) with employer matching, tuition reimbursement, and tenure-based housing discounts round out the package.

What You Bring

  • Comfort in a customer-facing, sales-oriented environment
  • Strong written and verbal communication
  • Ability to work independently and manage multiple tasks without being prompted
  • Weekend availability built into your regular schedule
  • A track record in customer service, sales, or hospitality (prior leasing experience is not required)

Why This Role Is Worth a Closer Look

Prometheus is the largest privately held apartment owner in the Bay Area, with over 13,000 units across Silicon Valley, Portland, and Seattle. They're vertically integrated, handling acquisitions, development, renovations, and operations in-house. For someone starting out in property management, that structure matters: you're not working for a third-party management company hired to run someone else's asset. You're working for the owner, which tends to mean more stability, longer investment horizons, and less pressure from fee compression.

Cupertino is a high-barrier, high-demand submarket. The residents you'll be working with are often tech professionals with specific expectations around service quality. Candidates who do well here typically combine genuine warmth with organizational follow-through. Charm gets people in the door; attention to detail closes the lease and keeps renewals on track. If you build a strong leasing foundation at a company this size, paths into assistant management and property management open up faster than at smaller operators.

greenhouse_4385691009.location: Hawthorne Palmetto - 9001 Blue Flag Dr - Simpsonville, SC - 29681
greenhouse_4385691009.rewritten_description:
Hawthorne Residential Partners runs nearly 50,000 apartment homes across the Southeast, and the Assistant Community Manager role at Hawthorne Palmetto in Simpsonville, SC is where you'll feel the full weight of that operation at the property level. This is a working role. You'll be in the leasing office handling traffic, following up on delinquency, reviewing ledgers, and covering for the Community Manager when she's out. The job has real range, and that's both the appeal and the honest challenge of it.

On any given day you might run a leasing tour in the morning, spend part of the afternoon on payment posting and ledger audits, then de-escalate a resident complaint before the office closes. The financial side is real work: rent collection, check scanning, delinquency tracking with weekly follow-up calls, and supporting eviction procedures when it gets to that point. It won't always get to that point, but you need to be comfortable with it when it does. Renewals, lease document accuracy, and occupancy goals are yours to own alongside the Community Manager.

Hawthorne leans into internal growth. Their Career Path Program is a real part of how they develop staff, and the ACM seat is explicitly positioned as the step before Community Manager. If you want to get to the CM chair, this role builds the habits that get you there: financial literacy at the property level, confident conflict resolution, and the ability to hold a team together when leadership is absent.

What the role calls for

  • High school diploma or GED
  • Two years of property management experience preferred
  • At least six months in an assistant community manager capacity preferred
  • Valid driver's license required
  • CALP designation is a plus, not a requirement

The schedule runs Monday through Friday, 9 to 6, with Saturdays from 10 to 4. One weekday off keeps it to 40 hours, but resident events and community needs can shift things occasionally. That's standard for this work and worth knowing upfront.

Compensation includes an hourly base plus monthly leasing and renewal commissions and quarterly performance bonuses. Benefits cover medical, dental, vision, a 401k match, paid time off including your birthday, pet insurance, paid parental and adoption leave, and company-paid life insurance. Telehealth access is included as well.

Strong candidates here tend to be people who already understand the rhythm of a multifamily office, know how to read a resident ledger without needing a tutorial, and don't freeze when a situation gets tense. The leasing piece matters, but the financial and administrative side is what separates a capable ACM from one who's still figuring it out six months in.

greenhouse_8160367.title: Assistant Property Manager (Piedmont Raleigh)
greenhouse_8160367.rewritten_description:
The Role at a Glance

Assistant Property Managers at residential communities tend to wear two hats at once: they're part of the leasing team generating traffic and closing rentals, and they're part of the operations team keeping resident accounts in order and the day-to-day running smoothly. At The Piedmont Raleigh, a Van Metre residential property in Raleigh, NC, this position sits right at that intersection. You'll report to the Property Manager and work across leasing, collections, resident relations, and general property support.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

A typical week here moves between several different kinds of tasks. You might start a morning greeting prospective residents, walking them through available units and amenities, and executing leases with those who qualify. By midday, you could be working through a delinquency report, contacting residents about overdue balances, or reconciling deposit accounting. Afternoons might involve inspecting vacant units to confirm they're make-ready, following up on maintenance requests, or preparing a market survey for the Property Manager. Weekend availability is required, which is worth knowing upfront since weekends often bring the heaviest leasing traffic.

Community outreach is part of the job too. Van Metre expects their team to actively network locally and generate qualified traffic, not just respond to inbound leads. On the resident retention side, you'll help plan and facilitate resident events, respond to complaints with genuine care and professionalism, and work to make sure residents feel known rather than just processed.

When collections efforts don't resolve a delinquency, you'll handle the administrative steps involved in processing evictions. That part of the role requires both accuracy and composure.

Who Tends to Succeed Here

  • At least 2 years of residential property management experience
  • Demonstrated sales and customer service background
  • Comfortable with Yardi or comparable property management software, plus Microsoft Office
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills across different audiences
  • Prior supervisory experience is a plus
  • Bilingual ability is preferred but not required
  • Genuinely detail-oriented, especially around financial records and resident ledgers

The candidates who do well in this kind of role aren't just good with people. They're organized enough to hold multiple moving pieces at once without things slipping. Leasing a unit, chasing a past-due balance, coordinating a maintenance follow-up, and prepping for a resident event can all land in the same day. Composure and attention to detail matter as much as personality here.

Van Metre's compensation package for this position includes a base hourly rate of $23 to $26, an annual bonus of up to $5,000 paid quarterly, plus additional bonus potential tied to delinquency and collections performance. Leasing and renewal commissions are also part of the picture. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, a company-matched 401(k), tuition reimbursement, and a wellness reimbursement of up to $900 annually. PTO includes 11 holidays, 10 vacation days, 10 sick days, plus personal days, volunteer days, a birthday day off, and a day off for an annual physical. Van Metre also offers rental discounts and development support through mentoring, certifications, and defined growth paths. For someone looking to grow toward a Property Manager role, this kind of full-scope position builds exactly the right foundation.
