lever_02b289b0-9af2-4bdf-833c-2538e704ef.rewritten_description:
The Skills That Drive This Role

Field maintenance at scale is a different animal than site-based apartment maintenance. At Lessen, you're not assigned to one property where you learn every quirk of the HVAC over time. You're moving across a portfolio, reading work orders cold, diagnosing fast, and executing without a lot of hand-holding. That demands a specific skill set: strong diagnostic instincts across multiple trade areas, solid time management, and the ability to own a job from intake to close without constant oversight.

Lessen operates a tech-enabled platform that routes work orders across a network serving over one million properties nationally. In the Frisco market, that means you'll work across a range of residential property types. The DFW suburb corridor has seen significant build-out over the past decade, and the portfolio demand reflects that: newer construction with its own maintenance profile, alongside older stock that needs more hands-on intervention. Technicians who've worked both ends of that spectrum tend to hit the ground running here.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Your day centers on assigned work orders. You'll manage your own schedule, track against budgets tied to each job, and handle the full scope of general property maintenance across residential units. Lessen's model emphasizes quality over volume, which means you're expected to close work correctly the first time rather than rush through a punch list and leave callbacks behind.

Core competencies the role draws on daily:

  • Plumbing repairs and fixture work
  • Electrical troubleshooting within scope (outlets, switches, fixtures)
  • HVAC filter maintenance and basic mechanical diagnostics
  • Appliance repair and replacement
  • Carpentry, drywall, and interior finish work
  • General exterior and common area upkeep

You'll document your work through Lessen's platform and coordinate with the operations team as needed. The company provides a fleet vehicle with a fuel card, so you're not putting miles on your own truck. A $50 monthly tool allowance and $50 cell phone allowance round out the field support.

What Makes This Position Worth Considering

The structure here is genuinely different from most property maintenance roles. There's no on-call rotation and the schedule runs weekdays. For experienced techs who've spent years on rotating emergency lines, that's a meaningful quality-of-life change. The $1,500 sign-on bonus and a quarterly discretionary bonus of up to 5% of quarterly earnings add upside beyond the base hourly rate, which starts at $23 and goes to $27 depending on verified experience and skill level.

Lessen is a venture-backed company expanding nationally, and they're explicit about internal growth paths into Lead Technician and Field Maintenance Manager roles. Technicians who document well, close work orders cleanly, and demonstrate sound judgment on-site tend to move into those tracks. OSHA training is provided, which matters for techs who haven't had a corporate employer cover that credential before.

The minimum bar is real: three or more years of verifiable, hands-on experience in property maintenance or a related trade. If you've built that foundation, the role offers a structure that rewards self-direction and consistent execution.

workable_6065264.title: Community Manager Manufactured Housing Community
workable_6065264.rewritten_description:
Managing a manufactured housing community for residents 55 and older is a distinct specialty within property management. The pace and priorities differ from conventional multifamily: residents tend to stay longer, relationships run deeper, and the community manager often becomes a genuinely central figure in daily life on-site. Investment Property Group, a private firm headquartered in Park City, Utah, operates over 150 properties across 13 states and is looking for a Community Manager at Meadowcrest Farm Estates, a 71-home senior MHC in Portland.

What You'll Be Managing

This is a full-scope site management role. You'll oversee daily operations, supervise on-site staff, and take ownership of financial performance against budget. That means reviewing delinquency, managing collections, completing bi-monthly deposits, and staying on top of resident receivables and accounting reports. You'll also handle the application and move-in process for new residents, enforce lease terms and community rules, and serve as the point of contact for resident concerns and grievance requests.

The compliance side of this role carries real weight. Manufactured housing communities in Oregon operate under specific state regulations, and you'll be expected to prepare and submit reports to partner agencies, liaise with local community development offices and law enforcement when needed, and keep the property operating in line with Fair Housing requirements. You'll also have some outdoor responsibilities, including meter readings and home site inspections.

  • 1 or more years managing a manufactured housing or multifamily community of 100 or more homes or units
  • Demonstrated experience with rent collection and delinquency management
  • Comfort with property management software and basic accounting systems
  • Strong conflict resolution skills, particularly with an older adult demographic
  • Marketing and leasing ability to maintain strong occupancy on vacant lots or homes
  • Clear written and verbal communication skills for working with residents, vendors, and local agencies

What Makes This Role Work Well for the Right Person

Portland's rental market has historically leaned toward conventional multifamily, but manufactured housing communities serve a distinct and often underserved segment of the housing stock. At a 71-home 55+ community, you're managing a close-knit population where reputation travels fast and consistency matters enormously. Residents notice when management is present, responsive, and fair. The managers who do well here tend to be people who genuinely enjoy being accessible, can hold a boundary when needed, and bring the same approach to a frustrated resident as they do to a routine conversation. Strong organizational habits matter as much as interpersonal skill, because the administrative load (compliance reporting, collections, site inspections) is real and ongoing.

IPG describes a Monday through Friday, 8 to 5 schedule, which offers more predictability than many on-site roles. Compensation is listed at $28.00 to $32.00 per hour depending on experience and qualifications. The company offers medical, dental, and vision coverage, life insurance, an HSA, an employee assistance program, a 401k with company match, and four weeks of accrued PTO.

For someone building a career in manufactured housing management, a well-run senior community is solid footing. The operational complexity (compliance, collections, resident services, staff supervision) maps directly onto larger MHC portfolios or regional management tracks. IPG operates at scale across multiple states, which means internal advancement is a realistic path for managers who perform.

workable_6064247.title: Property Manager
workable_6064247.rewritten_description:
The leasing office opens at nine, but your morning starts earlier. You're walking units with the construction punch list in one hand and a leasing report in the other, figuring out which homes close out by end of week and which ones need another pass before they're ready to show. That's the rhythm of a new-construction lease-up, and it defines this role from day one.

FLATS is a lifestyle-focused multifamily operator with a distinct brand identity centered on design-forward urban living. The company is building out operations at a newly constructed community in Las Vegas and needs an experienced Property Manager to carry it from delivery through stabilization and beyond. This is a full-cycle leadership role covering leasing performance, team management, financial oversight, and regulatory compliance under Nevada law.

What This Role Covers

On the leasing side, you'll own the lease-up strategy: setting pricing, managing concessions, tracking traffic and conversion, and pushing occupancy toward stabilization targets. You'll approve applications, manage renewals, enforce leases, and keep a close eye on collections and delinquency. Monthly financial reporting, budget management, and expense controls fall within your scope as well, along with vendor invoice approvals and coordination with accounting and ownership on performance updates.

You'll supervise onsite staff, which means recruiting, training, and managing performance in alignment with company standards. Coordinating with maintenance and construction teams to keep make-readies moving, punch lists closing, and service requests resolved on time will take real attention during the lease-up phase. Regular property and unit inspections, curb appeal standards, and compliance with Fair Housing, ADA, FCRA, and NRS 118A round out the operational side of the job.

What FLATS Is Looking For

  • Prior experience managing or supporting a multifamily lease-up or new-construction community
  • Working knowledge of Nevada landlord-tenant law (NRS 118A) and Fair Housing requirements
  • Proficiency with property management software such as Yardi Voyager or comparable CRM platforms
  • Ability to analyze leasing, occupancy, and financial data and act on what you find
  • Strong leadership skills with demonstrated ability to train and develop onsite teams
  • Intermediate Microsoft Office skills across Outlook, Word, Excel, and PowerPoint
  • Valid driver's license, clean driving record, and current auto insurance
  • Nevada Real Estate License is preferred but not required
  • Bilingual in Spanish is a plus

Las Vegas is worth understanding in context here. The metro has seen significant multifamily delivery over the past few years, and lease-up timelines have extended in some submarkets as new supply competes for the same renter pool. A manager who can read concession strategy carefully, hold rate discipline where possible, and build genuine resident retention from the start will have a real advantage. FLATS positions itself on brand and experience, so the manager sets the tone for how that brand lands with residents from their first tour through renewal.

Strong candidates will bring more than operational competence. smartrecruiters_744000146239202.title: Service Manager - Flamingo
smartrecruiters_744000146239202.rewritten_description:
The Flamingo is one of Miami Beach's most recognizable addresses, and the team running its day-to-day maintenance operation needs someone who can hold a high standard without being held up by every small problem. AIR Communities is hiring a Service Manager for this community, and the role carries real weight: a direct team of ten or more people, a broad maintenance scope, and a resident base that expects a lot.

This is a leadership role first. The technical side matters, and you'll need genuine hands-on maintenance and facilities experience to earn credibility with your crew. But what separates a strong Service Manager from a capable technician is the ability to develop people, set expectations clearly, and keep quality consistent even when the day doesn't go as planned. Turn quality, response times on service requests, and resident satisfaction scores all reflect on you and your team together.

On any given day, you might be reviewing a punch list from yesterday's turns, working through a vendor conversation about an upcoming capex project, and fielding a time-sensitive service request before noon. You'll communicate maintenance and capital needs up to leadership, manage your budget with an eye toward protecting NOI without cutting corners on quality, and make sure the property stays in step with AIR's operating procedures and environmental health and safety requirements. The community's appearance is a direct outcome of how well this team operates.

The schedule is honest about its demands. Evenings, weekends, on-call rotations, and stretches of seven-day coverage are part of the job depending on community needs and the time of year. Miami Beach isn't a slow market, and a property of this profile keeps a steady pace. That's worth knowing going in.

AIR is offering a base salary between $105,000 and $115,000, a 15% target bonus, and quarterly customer satisfaction bonuses of up to $250 per month for Service Managers who consistently deliver strong resident experiences. An on-site apartment discount option is also available.

What you'll bring

  • At least three years of technical maintenance and facilities experience in property management
  • One to three years leading a team in a customer service and asset maintenance environment
  • Mechanical aptitude and comfort with physical work, including moving heavy equipment
  • Flexibility for evenings, weekends, and on-call coverage (minimum one week per month)
  • Strong organizational skills and attention to detail
  • Reliable transportation
  • Proficiency in English (read, write, speak)

If you've built a team that takes pride in their work and can point to tangible improvements in resident satisfaction or operational efficiency, that experience translates directly here. AIR invests in ongoing development, certification reimbursement, and leadership training, so this role can grow with you if you're looking to move toward a regional or portfolio-level position over time.

greenhouse_4387571009.rewritten_description:
What You'll Actually Do

Palo Alto Gardens is an affordable housing community managed by MidPen Housing, a non-profit with over 50 years of experience and one of the larger affordable portfolios in Northern California. This Assistant Community Manager role sits squarely in the operational center of the property. You'll handle income verifications, lease prep, waitlist maintenance, and rent collection. You'll process turns, monitor turnover forms, and coordinate with facilities staff to keep work orders moving. Compliance work is a real part of this job: re-certifications, MOR prep, TCAC reviews, welfare exemption documents. If you've worked affordable housing before, you know that compliance is not a once-a-year event. It's a steady drumbeat.

Resident relations are woven through all of it. You'll issue notices, communicate emergency procedures, and coordinate logistics for resident meetings. You'll also maintain resident and property files with appropriate confidentiality and support relationships with local law enforcement and emergency agencies when needed. The reporting line is directly to the Community Manager.

One genuine advantage of the affordable housing side of our industry: the compliance framework gives new managers a structured way to build their skills. Tax credit and HUD requirements teach you documentation discipline that transfers well to any property type later. It's not glamorous, but it builds real competency.

What You Bring

  • High school diploma or GED with at least one year of residential property management, customer service, or administrative experience (or an equivalent combination)
  • Proficiency in MS Office; familiarity with RealPage is a plus
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with genuine follow-through
  • Ability to work independently and stay organized without someone checking over your shoulder
  • Comfort with the compliance demands of affordable housing, specifically tax credit and HUD regulatory environments
  • Multilingual skills in Mandarin, Russian, or Spanish are preferred and likely useful given the resident community
  • Alignment with MidPen's mission around affordable housing and community stability

Context Worth Knowing

The pay range is $21.15 to $23.80 hourly, based on experience. Benefits include health, dental, vision, life and disability insurance, a 403(b) retirement plan, paid parental leave, FSA options for childcare, medical, and commuter expenses, an employee education reimbursement program, an EAP, pet insurance, paid time off, company holidays, and wellness days. This is a non-profit employer, so the 403(b) structure is standard here rather than a 401(k).

Candidates who do well in affordable housing operations tend to have genuine patience for process and a resident-centered orientation that isn't performative. The compliance side of this work rewards people who find satisfaction in getting details right the first time. If you're coming from conventional market-rate housing and haven't worked with TCAC or HUD regulatory frameworks before, expect a learning curve on the compliance piece. It's manageable, but it's real.

greenhouse_4382112009.rewritten_description:
Affordable housing communities run on precision. Compliance requirements, income certifications, and delinquency tracking demand a different level of attention than conventional market-rate leasing, and that's exactly the environment this role sits inside. John M. Corcoran & Company, a New England real estate operator with roots going back to 1951, is hiring an Assistant Property Manager for Townhouse Apartments in Whitman, MA. The schedule runs Tuesday through Saturday, 9 to 5, which is worth knowing upfront since it shapes your week.

What the Job Actually Covers

This is a full operational support role, not a pure leasing seat. You'll handle leasing activity from traffic through application approval, but you'll also own rent collection, delinquency follow-up, move-in and move-out coordination, inspections, and resident account management. Accurate resident files and timely reporting are part of the daily rhythm. Affordable housing compliance sits at the center of this position, so a working knowledge of Fair Housing regulations and program requirements isn't optional. The property runs on Yardi, and comfort with Microsoft Office is expected from day one.

Resident relations is a meaningful part of the load. You'll field questions, address concerns, and coordinate community activities. That resident-facing work directly affects retention, and retention directly affects occupancy. On a stabilized affordable asset, keeping occupancy tight and delinquency low is how the property performs. You'll be helping manage both.

What Strong Candidates Bring

  • At least three years of property management experience, with direct exposure to affordable housing programs and compliance processes
  • Demonstrated ability to manage leasing activity and rental applications with accuracy
  • Solid delinquency follow-up habits, including early outreach before balances compound
  • Comfort with Yardi for resident ledgers, reporting, and file maintenance
  • A high school diploma or equivalent; relevant experience carries real weight here

The candidates who stand out in affordable housing APM roles tend to be detail-oriented under administrative pressure and consistent communicators with residents who may be navigating difficult circumstances. The compliance piece rewards people who treat paperwork as a discipline rather than a burden. A missed certification or a documentation gap creates real exposure on an affordable asset, so thoroughness matters as much as leasing energy.

JMC offers a $2,500 sign-on bonus, a pay range of $25.50 to $36.00 per hour, medical, dental, vision, and life insurance, paid time off and holidays, and a 401(k) with company match. The company has built a reputation for internal mobility, with many team members growing their careers there over the long term. For someone coming from a leasing or resident services background who wants to step into a role with real operational responsibility on an affordable community, this is a solid next move.

greenhouse_4385735009.title: Full Time Limpiador de Oficinas (Mon-Fri, 7AM-3:30PM)
greenhouse_4385735009.rewritten_description:
Comstock's ParkX Porter team keeps mixed-use and commercial properties in Reston running the way tenants and visitors expect: common areas clean, lobbies presentable, and problems flagged before they become complaints. This position works Monday through Friday, 7AM to 3:30PM, which means a consistent daytime schedule with visibility across the full property day.

Skills This Role Puts to Work Daily

Attention to detail carries more weight here than raw speed. A porter who notices a spill at a lobby entrance, a cluttered janitorial closet, or a pressure-washing area that was missed on the checklist is more valuable than one who moves fast but leaves gaps. The role also calls for genuine professionalism with people. Tenants, visitors, and property staff all cross paths with this position throughout the shift, and how you handle those interactions reflects directly on the property's service standard.

Time management matters too. You'll follow structured cleaning schedules and checklists assigned by the Senior Operations Manager, which means self-direction is part of the job. You won't have someone standing over you confirming each task. You track your own progress, document what's been done at shift end, and hand off cleanly to the next shift.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

  • Maintaining cleanliness across common areas including lobbies, restrooms, sidewalks, and public spaces throughout the shift
  • Pressure washing assigned exterior areas as directed by management
  • Supporting event setup and breakdown, including preparation and cleanup before and after meetings or public gatherings
  • Monitoring cleaning supply inventory and using chemicals safely and correctly
  • Reporting safety hazards, maintenance issues, or equipment damage to management promptly
  • Completing required end-of-shift documentation and ensuring accurate shift handoffs
  • Covering for teammates during absences when needed, including occasional weekend or off-hours availability during high-traffic events
  • Keeping the janitorial room and storage areas organized and hazard-free at all times

The physical demands are real: extended time on your feet, lifting up to 50 pounds, working in variable outdoor and indoor conditions, and exposure to cleaning chemicals and biological hazards are all part of the job. Candidates should be comfortable with that reality before applying.

What Makes This Role Worth Your Time at Comstock

Comstock operates a growing portfolio, and ParkX specifically manages parking and property services across multiple sites. For someone who performs consistently, that scale creates real room to move up. Porter roles that demonstrate reliability and an eye for property condition often lead to senior porter or facilities coordinator positions as a company expands its footprint.

The benefits package includes medical, dental, and vision coverage, 401(k) matching, life insurance, parental leave, and annual professional development funding. Free parking and EV charging access are also included. The Monday-through-Friday daytime schedule is a genuine advantage for candidates who want stability over irregular shift work.

Qualifications required include a high school diploma or equivalent and a valid driver's license with no major violations. Bilingual candidates comfortable working within a Spanish-speaking team environment will find this role fits naturally.

greenhouse_4386073009.title: Cleaner - Part-Time
greenhouse_4386073009.rewritten_description:
Redstone Residential runs one of the larger third-party student housing platforms in the country, with over 38,000 beds spread across 20 states. Their Rexburg property sits squarely in student housing territory, which means the cleaning and groundskeeping work here has a rhythm that's distinct from conventional multifamily. Turns happen fast, common areas take real abuse, and curb appeal matters to prospects who are often visiting for the first time with their parents in tow.

This is a part-time, non-exempt role paying $12.00 per hour. The shift length runs four to six hours, and you'll spend most of that time on your feet. The work covers the full scope of property cleanliness: common areas, hallways, parking structures, grounds, and scheduled cleaning checks inside residents' apartments. That last piece is worth noting. Resident cleaning checks aren't standard at every property, but in student housing they're common, and doing them well requires a combination of consistency, documentation, and the ability to interact professionally with residents even when the feedback isn't what they want to hear.

Day to day, you're making sure the property looks sharp before prospects walk in, picking up debris and animal waste from the grounds, keeping the clubhouse and leasing office presentable, handling basic landscaping upkeep, and clearing snow and ice when Rexburg winters demand it. Some light maintenance assistance comes with the role as well. Nothing here requires a trades background, but the ability to work through a task list independently is genuinely important. This isn't a role with a supervisor walking alongside you every hour.

In student housing, curb appeal and common area condition directly affect traffic and leasing velocity. A clean, well-maintained property photographs better, tours better, and retains residents better. Porters and cleaners quietly support occupancy in ways that don't always get acknowledged.

Redstone offers 401(k) with up to 6% matching, which is a real benefit for a part-time hourly position.

What they're looking for

  • Some janitorial or cleaning experience, even informal
  • Ability to work through daily tasks without needing constant direction
  • Physical capability to lift 50+ pounds and stand for a full shift
  • A genuinely friendly approach with residents and team members

Candidates who tend to stand out in roles like this are the ones who take ownership of their section of the property without being asked twice. In student housing, that self-direction matters more than in some other environments. If you're looking to get a foot in the door with a growing national operator, this is a legitimate way to do it.

greenhouse_5405929008.title: Leasing Manager
greenhouse_5405929008.rewritten_description:
It's 10 a.m. on a Saturday and three tours are queued back to back. By noon, you'll need to have followed up by phone on yesterday's walk-ins, posted to the property's Facebook page, and confirmed the outreach packet drop you scheduled with a local employer for Tuesday. That's the rhythm of a Leasing Manager at Bozzuto's Annapolis community.

The Role

This position sits at the intersection of sales production and team leadership. You're responsible for hitting monthly lease quotas while also coaching a Sales and Marketing Associate team to do the same. The performance expectations here are specific: a lead-to-appointment conversion ratio of at least 8%, a closing ratio of 30%, and a structured follow-up cadence that includes a phone call within 24 hours of every tour and an email within 48 hours. Outreach marketing is also part of the job. You'll generate at least one outreach event per week and build ongoing relationships with local employers to drive qualified traffic. Competitive shopping happens quarterly across your immediate competitive set, with a weekly survey to keep your market knowledge current between formal shops.

Resident retention is the other half of the equation. You'll attend community social events, respond to and close out work orders where applicable, and be the calm, professional presence when a frustrated resident walks through the door. Lease paperwork accuracy is on you. Weekend availability is expected: three weekends per month, offset by two weekdays off.

What You Bring

  • A four-year degree or equivalent experience in a relevant field
  • Previous leasing experience in multifamily property management
  • 1 to 3 years of direct B2C sales experience, ideally in property management, retail, or hospitality
  • 1 to 3 years of phone sales experience with a track record of consistent conversion
  • Comfort with both the metrics and the human side of the role: traffic reports in the morning, a difficult conversation with a resident in the afternoon

The candidates who stand out at this level already understand that closing ratios don't improve through charm alone. They build repeatable habits: disciplined follow-up, honest product articulation, and consistent outreach that keeps the top of the funnel healthy even when walk-in traffic softens. Bozzuto's marketing team handles broader brand strategy, but you'll need to execute at the property level with real consistency.

Compensation falls in the range of $52,530 to $61,532, with additional bonus opportunities tied to performance. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, 20 days of paid time off plus holidays, a 401(k) with company match, and tuition reimbursement.

greenhouse_4385460009.title: Community Manager
greenhouse_4385460009.rewritten_description:
Community Manager roles at large, vertically integrated operators like Cortland carry more weight than the title suggests. You're not just keeping the lights on and resolving noise complaints. You're running a multimillion-dollar asset, managing a team, and hitting NOI targets that matter to investors. If that's the scope you want, this is worth reading.

What the Job Actually Covers

Cortland is hiring a Community Manager for their Cary, NC property. The role spans the full operational picture: leasing performance, financial oversight, team development, resident satisfaction, and vendor management. You'll own the budget, monitor KPIs, and work directly with corporate partners and centralized support teams to keep the community performing.

On the leasing side, you're setting goals, coaching your team on conversion, and working with marketing on campaigns and social presence. On the financial side, you're managing expenses, reading community metrics, and making decisions that protect and grow NOI. Day-to-day, you're also handling property inspections, vendor relationships, contract negotiations, and escalated resident concerns when your team needs backup.

Cortland operates with in-house design, construction, and property management under one roof, which means onsite managers tend to have more corporate support than you'd find at a third-party fee management shop. That's a real structural difference. It also means there are more stakeholders to align with, and the expectation for disciplined execution is high.

What They're Looking For

  • At least two years leading a sales-driven team in a high-velocity environment (multifamily, hospitality, luxury retail, or similar)
  • A real track record on occupancy, revenue, and NOI, with numbers to back it up
  • Experience with property management software, CRM tools, and Microsoft Office
  • Strong financial acumen: budgeting, forecasting, expense control
  • Ability to coach and develop a team, not just manage tasks
  • Comfort analyzing data and using it to make decisions, not just report on it
  • High school diploma required; bachelor's degree preferred

A Few Honest Notes

Community Manager positions at Class A properties like Cortland's come with real pressure. Occupancy targets don't pause for staffing gaps or difficult residents. Escalated situations land on your desk because your team couldn't resolve them. Budget reviews happen whether the month went well or not. None of that is unique to Cortland, but it's the reality of the role, and candidates who've managed a property before already know it.

What separates strong candidates here is financial fluency paired with genuine coaching instincts. Plenty of managers can read a T-12 or run a leasing report. Fewer can pull a struggling leasing consultant through a tough stretch and come out the other side with a better performer. Cortland's model relies on onsite leaders who can do both, because the corporate infrastructure exists to support good operators, not to carry weak ones.

For the right person, this role is a clear path toward multi-site or regional oversight. Cortland's scale means those opportunities exist internally, and Community Managers who consistently hit their numbers tend to move up.

greenhouse_6167346004.location: Fairfield, CA; San Francisco, CA; Vacaville, CA; Walnut Creek, CA
greenhouse_6167346004.rewritten_description:
Regional management at Asset Living pulls on a specific mix of skills that few property management roles demand simultaneously: financial analysis, personnel development, leasing strategy, and physical asset oversight, all applied across a multi-property portfolio rather than a single community. This position covers sites across Fairfield, Vacaville, Walnut Creek, and San Francisco, a geography that spans Class B garden-style suburban submarkets and the denser Bay Area and East Bay corridors. The operational and market conditions can shift significantly from one city to the next, so portfolio thinking matters here as much as site-level execution.

What This Role Actually Requires Day to Day

The financial side of this position is substantive. You'll develop annual operating budgets, review T-12 performance, monitor NOI trends across your portfolio, and write monthly variance explanations on income and expense line items that fall outside plan. When capex projects come up, you're evaluating bids, tracking work in progress, and confirming ownership reports close accurately. That kind of financial accountability means you need to read a P&L comfortably and understand what's driving delinquency or occupancy shifts before you see them in the numbers.

On the personnel side, you're hiring and coaching community managers and their teams, handling performance documentation, approving timesheets, and managing the full cycle from onboarding to, when necessary, termination. Asset Living operates as a third-party management firm, so consistency with company policy and client reporting standards is non-negotiable. Your site staff represent both Asset and the property owner, and it's your job to ensure those standards hold across every property in your region.

Leasing oversight means reviewing traffic conversion, evaluating whether concessions are warranted, assessing make-ready timelines, and building annual marketing plans that reflect local demand. If a property is running high MTM exposure or struggling with lease-up velocity, you're the one developing the strategy to correct it, not just flagging the problem.

Skills That Carry Weight Here

  • Demonstrated ability to manage NOI at the portfolio level, including budget development and monthly financial reporting
  • Experience supervising onsite teams across multiple properties, with a track record of effective coaching and performance management
  • Familiarity with fair housing compliance and risk management in an offsite leadership capacity
  • Competency with leasing strategy, including occupancy management, concession analysis, and resident retention programs
  • Experience reviewing vendor contracts, monitoring construction or rehab work, and coordinating maintenance standards across sites

Working Within Asset Living's Structure

Asset Living is one of the larger third-party management operators in the country, ranked in the NMHC top 50, and holds Accredited Management Organization status through IREM. That structure gives regional managers real institutional support, including HR, training benchmarks, and reporting systems, but it also means you're accountable to both company standards and individual ownership groups simultaneously. Strong regional managers in this kind of environment tend to be people who can hold the line on policy while still building genuine relationships with onsite staff and ownership stakeholders.

The Bay Area and East Bay markets where this portfolio operates have seen meaningful rent moderation in some submarkets over the past few years, which puts a premium on retention and operational efficiency rather than riding market tailwinds. That context makes the NOI discipline and resident retention programming parts of this role genuinely important, not just boxes to check.

Skills That Drive This Role

This Assistant Community Manager position at Hillside San Marcos runs on two distinct skill sets working at the same time: financial discipline and people management. On any given day, you might be chasing down a delinquent account, coaching a leasing associate through a difficult resident interaction, walking a vacant unit for a punch list, and then sitting down to reconcile accounts receivable before the month closes. Student housing doesn't slow down, and neither does this role.

The financial side is real and consequential. You'll own delinquency tracking with a hard target of under 2% at month end, which means consistent follow-through on late fees, NSF charges, and collection procedures. Move-out billing, damage assessments, and utility billing coordination all run through you. Scion uses Entrata, so comfort with a property management system isn't optional; it's the baseline expectation from day one.

On the people side, you're coaching staff, backing up the General Manager, and stepping in to run the property when they're out. That's a meaningful level of responsibility for an assistant-level title. It requires someone who can handle escalated resident concerns without losing composure and who understands that the team's output reflects directly on their own performance.

The Work Itself

Student housing has its own rhythm. The annual turn is the defining operational event, and you'll help plan and execute it. Hundreds of move-outs and move-ins compressed into a short window, room assignments, transfers, inspections, and make-readies all happening in parallel. If you've managed a turn before, you already know what that pressure feels like. If you haven't, expect to learn quickly.

Outside of turn season, the work includes:

  • Weekly market surveys to stay current on local comps and pricing
  • Monthly walks of vacant apartments and bed spaces
  • Regular inspections of grounds, common areas, and amenities
  • Coordinating work orders with maintenance staff or outside vendors
  • Managing promotional materials and concession budgets within set parameters
  • Delivering resident notices and handling eviction filings per local ordinance
  • After-hours on-call coverage as part of the standard schedule rotation

Fair Housing compliance training and enforcement applies to all onsite staff, and you're responsible for making sure your team stays current.

What Sets Strong Candidates Apart Here

Student housing attracts a specific kind of operator. The resident population is younger, more transient, and often dealing with living independently for the first time. That means a higher volume of customer service interactions, more escalations, and residents who sometimes need guidance rather than just a policy citation. The candidates who do well here combine genuine patience with clear boundaries. They don't let difficult situations fester, but they also don't treat every noise complaint as a confrontation.

Experience in student housing or lease-up environments is a real advantage. The bed-space model, the roommate dynamics, the parent calls during move-in week: these aren't things you want to encounter for the first time in a senior-adjacent role. One or more years in property management is required, but relevant context matters as much as tenure.

This role sits one level below General Manager. For someone building toward that title, the AGM position at a larger student housing operation gives you exposure to both the operational and financial sides of asset performance, which is exactly the experience that prepares you for a GM seat.

Groundskeeping at a Class A urban property like Tinsley on the Park requires a specific skill set: sharp attention to detail, physical stamina, and the ability to represent a community well in front of residents every single day. This role centers on those three things.

What This Work Requires

The core skill here is observation. A good groundskeeper doesn't wait for problems to get reported. They catch litter, debris, and damage during routine property walks before residents notice. Curb appeal drives first impressions for prospective residents and sets the tone for existing ones, so the eye for detail matters constantly, not just at scheduled intervals.

Physical fitness is a genuine requirement, not a checkbox. This work involves regular movement, lifting, bending, and outdoor exposure across the property grounds and common areas. Prior experience in cleaning, construction, or facilities maintenance helps you hit the ground running, but the mindset of ownership over your space matters more than credentials.

Basic computer literacy and clear written and spoken English are needed for logging work orders and communicating with the maintenance team. You'll also assist maintenance staff when they need an extra set of hands, so some comfort working alongside technicians on general tasks is useful.

Day-to-Day Responsibilities

  • Walk property grounds and common areas regularly to collect litter and debris
  • Maintain curb appeal standards across the exterior, amenities, and shared spaces
  • Support maintenance staff with tasks as directed
  • Interact professionally with residents and guests during daily operations

Working at Berkshire

Berkshire Residential Investments owns and manages its own portfolio, which means decisions about properties happen in-house. For groundskeeping staff, that typically translates to more consistent standards and direct support from the management team rather than split accountability across a third-party structure. Berkshire offers three weeks of vacation, a 25% rent discount, insurance coverage, and personal development plans.

The strongest candidates in this type of role take genuine ownership of their section of the property. The difference between a good porter and a great one usually comes down to whether they treat the grounds as their own or just a task list to complete. At a community like Tinsley on the Park, that distinction shows.

greenhouse_4387034009.title: Cleaner - Part-Time
greenhouse_4387034009.rewritten_description:
Student housing operations run on tight turns and high curb appeal standards, especially in college markets where prospective residents and their parents form opinions fast. The cleaner role exists because a property can have great amenities and strong leasing numbers, but if the hallways smell like last weekend or the parking garage is a mess, it shows up in renewals and traffic quality.

Redstone Residential operates over 38,000 beds across 20 states and carries one of the larger third-party student housing portfolios in the country. This part-time position is based at their Rexburg, Idaho community and pays $15.00 per hour. There's a 401(k) with up to 6% matching, which is worth noting for a part-time hourly role.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

The core of the job is keeping common areas, hallways, parking garages, and outdoor grounds clean and presentable on a regular schedule. That includes snow and ice removal, trash and debris pickup, animal waste, landscaping upkeep, and watering. You'll also be responsible for cleaning and maintaining the clubhouse, leasing office, model unit, and other interior common spaces. Shifts run four to six hours and require being on your feet the whole time. You'll need to lift 50-plus pounds.

One piece that's specific to student housing: resident cleaning checks. You'll conduct scheduled inspections of residents' apartments to verify they're meeting the property's cleanliness standards. In student communities, this is a standard practice that most conventional multifamily operators don't bother with. It requires a balance of consistency and a decent bedside manner. You're going in to verify compliance, but you're also a face of the property to the residents you encounter.

There's also light assist work on basic repairs and general maintenance tasks as needed.

Who Fits This Role

  • Some janitorial or cleaning background, professional or otherwise
  • Comfortable working independently without daily hand-holding
  • Physically able to handle a standing shift and heavier lifting
  • Genuinely decent with people, especially in resident-facing interactions

The candidate who does well here is someone who takes pride in the physical state of a property and doesn't need someone checking behind them to stay on task. Student housing tends to cycle through this role with people who treat it as temporary, so candidates who show up consistently and work with some initiative tend to stand out quickly. That kind of reliability in a part-time cleaner often opens doors to full-time consideration or crossover into maintenance or porter work as properties grow. Redstone's conventional portfolio is expanding, which means there's at least some reasonable upward path for people who perform.

greenhouse_5408806008.title: Resident Manager - Lanai Village
greenhouse_5408806008.rewritten_description:
Resident management at the property level is one of the most skill-intensive roles in this industry. You're doing leasing, collections, maintenance coordination, compliance, and resident relations simultaneously, often before 9 a.m. on a Tuesday. The Resident Manager position at Lanai Village in Spring Valley leans on all of it.

The Skills This Role Runs On

California landlord-tenant law shapes almost every decision a site manager makes here. Security deposit procedures at move-out, proper notice requirements, Fair Housing compliance during leasing, Cal/OSHA awareness on property. Candidates who've operated in other states often underestimate how much California-specific knowledge this work requires. That's not a knock on anyone; it's just the reality of this market.

Beyond compliance, the role demands a specific combination of financial discipline and interpersonal range. You're collecting rent, monitoring delinquency, issuing receipts, and making bank deposits on one hand. On the other, you're the face of the community, handling resident concerns, conducting tours, and keeping retention from slipping. Bilingual ability in English and Spanish is a real operational advantage here, not just a checkbox, given the demographics of the Spring Valley area.

Day-to-Day Responsibilities

  • Conduct unit, amenity, and common area inspections to stay ahead of maintenance and safety issues
  • Manage work orders and push toward 24-48 hour completion windows
  • Oversee move-in and move-out inspections in compliance with California security deposit law
  • Handle leasing from inquiry through executed lease, maintaining accurate applicant records
  • Collect rents and deposits, track delinquency, and coordinate with supervisors before any legal action
  • Verify that contractors and vendors carry proper licensing and insurance
  • Support budgeting and expense tracking alongside regional leadership

This position is on-site and live-in, so if you haven't done resident management before, understand what that means practically. The property is also your address. The line between work and personal time softens. Experienced site managers adjust; people new to the format often don't anticipate how that dynamic feels until they're in it.

What Makes the Difference Here

Sunrise Management operates with a hospitality-forward philosophy, which in practice means resident experience is taken seriously as an operational metric, not just a cultural talking point. Strong candidates for this role tend to have sound judgment on when to handle something themselves and when to escalate. The ones who struggle typically either over-escalate minor resident issues or sit on problems too long before looping in regional. Neither extreme works well in a lean on-site structure like this one.

Two or more years of property management experience is the baseline expectation. Comfort with property management software and Microsoft Office rounds out the technical side. The compensation range is $16.90 to $20.00 per hour, with a medical, dental, and vision package, FSA, company-paid life insurance, and paid time off.

greenhouse_4385374009.rewritten_description:
Running a 269-Unit Community in Denver's University Hills Corridor

Colorado Station Apartments sits at 3725 E Buchtel Blvd, a 269-unit mid-rise community in a high-demand Denver submarket. RedPeak, a Denver-native owner-operator with 24 years focused exclusively on the Front Range, is hiring a Community Manager to run this asset. This is a full P&L role: you own occupancy, NOI, delinquency, team performance, and the resident experience from lease-up to renewal.

RedPeak operates as an in-house platform, meaning you're not reporting to a third-party management company. Decisions move faster, accountability is direct, and the support structure is built around people who actually know Denver neighborhoods. The company's stated culture puts residents in the neighbor category, which shows up operationally in how service calls and lease renewals get handled.

What the Day-to-Day Looks Like

Monday through Friday, 9 to 6. You're the senior operator on site. That means owning the budget, reviewing actuals against the T-12, and understanding where variances are coming from. Delinquency management, lease expirations, concession strategy, traffic-to-lease conversion rates , these are your numbers to track and move. You're also coordinating maintenance, which at a single-building 269-unit property means staying close to your make-ready pipeline and punch lists without getting buried in them.

On the team side, you're guiding and motivating the onsite staff. Leasing, service, communications , you set the standard. The role comes with bonus potential tied to results, and there's a monthly maintenance bonus component built into the comp structure.

  • Market-rate property management experience, with demonstrated financial and operational results
  • Comfort running budgets, reporting financials, and interpreting performance data
  • Strong resident-facing instincts , you know how to de-escalate, retain, and build community
  • Tech fluency across leasing platforms, communications tools, and maintenance coordination software
  • Leadership presence: your team takes cues from you on pace, professionalism, and follow-through

Compensation, Benefits, and Career Context

The base range is $65,000 to $85,000 annually, plus bonus. Benefits include full medical, dental, and vision coverage, employer-paid short-term disability, a 401(k) with company match that vests on day one, 16 PTO days, 10 paid holidays, and a 20% rent discount. RedPeak also offers a student debt repayment program, a scholarship fund administered by the Denver Foundation, and up to $75 monthly toward a health club membership.

RedPeak describes this as well-suited for an entry-to-mid-level Community Manager looking to grow. That's meaningful context: if you're coming off a successful run as an Assistant Manager and ready to own a full asset, this is a legitimate path in. A single building at 269 units is a manageable scope for a first full Community Manager role, and RedPeak's in-house model means you'll have direct visibility into how ownership-level decisions get made, which accelerates development faster than most fee-management shops.

Strong candidates will bring a track record of occupancy performance they can speak to with actual numbers, not just general experience descriptions. Knowing your T-12, being able to explain a delinquency trend, and having a point of view on concessions strategy will separate you in the interview process.

greenhouse_6173943004.title: Senior Regional Manager, Affordable Housing
greenhouse_6173943004.rewritten_description:
The quarterly LIHTC file review is done, the regulatory agency follow-up is logged, and it's not yet 10 a.m. That's the pace of a Senior Regional Manager in affordable housing at Asset Living, where compliance deadlines and NOI targets move in parallel, not in sequence.

The Role

Asset Living is a third-party management firm ranked in the NMHC top 50, with a portfolio spanning multifamily, affordable housing, build-to-rent, student housing, and single-family rentals. This Senior Regional Manager position sits within their affordable housing division, based in Miami, and carries full operational accountability across a portfolio of communities. That means personnel, leasing, financial performance, maintenance oversight, administration, and risk management all fall under your watch.

On the compliance side, this role demands daily fluency in LIHTC and Section 8 requirements. You'll monitor LIHTC application pipelines and annual recertification cycles, conduct file reviews, perform semi-annual physical inspections, and maintain active working relationships with regulatory agencies. Equal Housing Opportunity and Affirmative Fair Housing adherence is non-negotiable, and you'll be the person ensuring your sites hold the line.

Financial management at this level means developing annual operating budgets, producing monthly written variance analysis for income and expense line items running over budget, and making capex recommendations that hold up under ownership scrutiny. The expectation is that you identify NOI trends early and bring a strategy with you, not just the problem.

Responsibilities and Qualifications

On the people side, you'll screen, hire, train, and develop on-site staff using Asset's established training benchmarks. Performance documentation, salary increase requests, timesheet approvals, and HR escalations are all yours to manage. The job requires consistency, especially when performance problems surface and corrective action is needed.

Leasing and marketing responsibilities include building annual marketing plans, evaluating your team's leasing technique, monitoring traffic and closure rates, and maintaining accurate reporting systems. Resident retention programs, complaint resolution, and move-in coordination round out the leasing scope. You'll also support emergency response protocols at the property level.

  • Demonstrated experience managing LIHTC and/or Section 8 affordable housing portfolios
  • Proven ability to oversee multi-site operations as an off-site supervisor
  • Competency in budget development, financial reporting, and NOI management
  • Working knowledge of Fair Housing law and regulatory compliance requirements
  • Track record of hiring, coaching, and developing on-site property management teams
  • Strong documentation habits for personnel matters and ownership reporting

One thing that separates strong candidates in this specific role: the ability to hold both compliance precision and financial performance in the same hand without letting one slip. Affordable housing regional oversight carries a heavier regulatory load than conventional multifamily. File deficiencies, missed recertification deadlines, or inspection failures can trigger agency findings that ripple far beyond a single property. Candidates who've managed through a regulatory audit or agency correspondence already know what that pressure looks like. That experience matters here more than portfolio size alone.

Miami's affordable housing market adds another layer. South Florida carries significant demand pressure, strict regulatory oversight, and a complex funding environment. Regional managers working this market deal with high occupancy alongside tight income qualification windows, which puts recertification accuracy at a premium.

greenhouse_8165224.title: Maintenance Assistant Supervisor
greenhouse_8165224.rewritten_description:
Weinstein Properties has been family-owned for over 70 years, and that tenure shows in how they operate. With more than 60 apartment communities across five states, including Virginia, North Carolina, Texas, Tennessee, and Georgia, they run a hands-on shop where the maintenance team directly shapes occupancy outcomes and resident retention. The Assistant Maintenance Supervisor role at Bexley at Triangle Park in Cary sits at the center of that equation.

This is a working lead position, which means you're not stepping back from the tools. You're diagnosing HVAC systems, handling electrical and plumbing repairs, managing turns, and supervising both in-house technicians and outside vendors. On any given day, you might be reviewing open work orders in the morning, coordinating a make-ready punch list at midday, and fielding a resident call about a failing A/C unit in the afternoon. The role pairs genuine trade skill with the organizational responsibility of scheduling, quality control, and team oversight.

What separates candidates who thrive in this role from those who struggle is the ability to shift registers quickly. You have to be technically credible enough that your team follows your lead on a repair call, and people-oriented enough that residents feel heard when something goes wrong in their home. Both matter. Neither alone is enough.

What the role requires

  • At least 4 years of trade experience, with a minimum of 2 years in apartment maintenance supervision
  • Hands-on HVAC repair experience and EPA/CFC certification (Type I and II or Universal)
  • Working knowledge across plumbing, electrical, carpentry, appliances, and exterior systems
  • Comfort with business software for work order management, turn scheduling, and supply ordering
  • Valid driver's license, personal transportation, and your own tools
  • Willingness to share on-call rotation with the team

Compensation starts at $25 per hour based on experience. On-call pay is structured as a $150 weekly bonus regardless of call volume, plus an additional $150 for holiday on-call coverage. There's also a quarterly performance bonus with up to $1,110 in potential earnings tied to property and team metrics. Benefits include vacation and sick time, holiday pay, health insurance, a rent discount, and a 401(k) with company match.

From a career trajectory standpoint, this role builds exactly the resume a Maintenance Supervisor position demands. You're getting reps on scheduling and vendor coordination, learning to manage through people rather than just alongside them, and tying your technical output to measurable property performance. Weinstein's stated commitment to promoting from within means the path to lead supervisor isn't abstract. The skills you build here, especially the blend of trade depth and team leadership, carry cleanly into senior maintenance roles, facilities management, or regional service director tracks at larger operators.

greenhouse_8761327002.location: Hillside San Marcos, San Marcos, Texas, United States
greenhouse_8761327002.rewritten_description:
The Scion Group has built a real niche in student housing, operating communities near major universities across the country. Their Hillside San Marcos property sits in a market shaped almost entirely by Texas State University, where enrollment consistently pushes above 38,000 students. That context matters for this role. You're not leasing to a general renter pool. You're talking to 19-year-olds, their parents, transfer students, and grad students, often all in the same afternoon, and each conversation requires a different register.

The Experience Team Member title is intentional. Scion treats the leasing function as customer experience work, and the ETM role reflects that. Yes, you'll tour prospects and close leases. You'll also handle package logging, help coordinate maintenance follow-ups, assist with social media content, and pull after-hours lockout duty on a rotating basis. The scope is genuinely broad, and the ability to shift gears quickly is a real requirement, not a throwaway line in the job description.

Student housing has its own operational rhythm that separates it from conventional multifamily. The turn period, typically concentrated in a tight window before the fall semester, is the most demanding stretch of the year. A successful ETM knows that summer availability and turn-period reliability aren't optional, they're central to how student housing actually operates. If you've worked a conventional lease-up or a garden-style community and want to understand how student housing works, this role teaches you that fast.

What Scion Is Looking For

  • A customer-first instinct with genuine follow-through, not just a friendly demeanor
  • Strong communication across a diverse resident population, including international students and families
  • Comfort with flexible scheduling, including evenings, weekends, holidays, and the turn season rush
  • Self-discipline and reliability without needing close supervision
  • Familiarity with social media platforms as marketing and engagement tools

This position is full-time, hourly, and based on-site at Hillside San Marcos. Benefits include health, dental, and vision coverage, 401k matching, paid maternal and parental leave, paid time off, a discretionary annual bonus, and learning reimbursement. Work authorization in the U.S. is required. Visa sponsorship is not available.

For candidates thinking about where this leads: ETMs at student housing operators often move into assistant manager roles with leasing oversight, and student housing experience transfers well into conventional lease-up work, where traffic management and closing under pressure are equally valued skills.

greenhouse_7980973003.rewritten_description:
Maintenance at a Company That Invests Long-Term

Prometheus Real Estate Group has been holding and operating apartments in the Bay Area since 1965, and their approach shows it. They don't flip properties or chase short-term yield. That means the maintenance team is expected to care for communities the way a long-term owner would, not just patch things up until the next sale. For a technician, that distinction matters day to day.

This Maintenance Technician II role sits at the Ironworks community in Sunnyvale, a market where residents have high expectations and operational standards follow suit. You'd be part of the team keeping the physical experience of living there consistent and reliable.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

A significant part of this role is turns. When a resident moves out, you're running the make-ready process from start to finish: completing the punch list, troubleshooting whatever the previous occupant left behind, and getting the unit back to a condition that earns the next resident's confidence. The work spans appliance repair and installation, plumbing, carpentry, electrical, and painting. No single discipline dominates, which means you need real breadth rather than deep specialization in one area.

Service requests fill the rest of your schedule. Prometheus calls their residents "Neighbors," and the expectation is that you treat the relationship that way. When someone submits a work order, they're trusting that you'll show up prepared, communicate clearly, and actually fix the problem. The customer service component here isn't a soft add-on to the job description. It's central.

On-call availability is required, so this role does carry after-hours responsibility. That's honest. It also comes with standby pay and on-call premium pay, which reflects that Prometheus has thought about how to compensate people fairly for that commitment.

  • Minimum two years of apartment maintenance experience
  • Working knowledge of plumbing, electrical, appliances, carpentry, and painting
  • Comfortable using basic computer tools (work order systems, email)
  • Able to lift up to 50 lbs. occasionally; most work is performed outdoors in moderate temperatures
  • High school diploma or GED required
  • Strong English communication skills for resident interaction and workplace safety

The Team and the Upside

Prometheus is a vertically integrated company with over 500 employees and a portfolio of more than 13,000 apartments across Silicon Valley, Portland, and Seattle. That scale creates real internal mobility. Technicians who develop strong diagnostic skills and build trust with their site teams often grow into lead tech or maintenance supervisor roles over time. The company also offers a Training Coach Bonus and educational assistance, which signals that they'll invest in developing people who want to grow.

Pay runs $31.00 to $32.25 per hour, with a semi-annual discretionary bonus and additional incentive programs including referral and renovation bonuses. The benefits package covers medical, vision, and dental at 100% for employees and eligible dependents, along with 401(k) matching, tenure-based housing discounts, and twelve paid holidays including your birthday.

If you care about the physical quality of the place where people live and you want to work for an owner who does too, the fit here is worth taking seriously.

greenhouse_4387275009.title: Community Manager
greenhouse_4387275009.rewritten_description:
It's a Tuesday morning, and before the leasing office opens you're already pulling the prior day's traffic numbers in Knock, reviewing a delinquency report in Yardi, and checking in with your maintenance supervisor about two pending make-readies. That's the rhythm of a Community Manager role at Hawthorne Residential Partners in Greer, SC, and it suits people who want ownership over real outcomes, not just tasks.

What This Role Actually Covers

Hawthorne is one of the larger Southeast-rooted multifamily operators in the country, and this position puts you at the center of a full community operation. You'll carry responsibility for the financial performance of the property, including budget management, rent collection, deposit accounting, and delinquency tracking. Occupancy goals, renewal strategy, and pricing decisions live on your plate. So does the resident experience, from handling escalated concerns to organizing community events that actually move the needle on satisfaction scores and online reputation.

On the leasing side, you stay hands-on. Conducting tours, responding to leads, and guiding prospects through the process are part of the job even at the manager level. You'll also manage vendor relationships, oversee work order flow alongside your maintenance team, and keep common areas and amenities in strong condition. Social media management for the community falls under this role as well.

Team leadership is the other half of the work. You'll hire, train, and coach both office and maintenance staff, run weekly team meetings, and serve as the primary culture driver on site. Hawthorne's internal career path program is built around this kind of development work, and Community Manager is explicitly positioned as a stepping stone toward Regional Manager.

Qualifications and What Sets Strong Candidates Apart

  • High school diploma or GED required
  • At least two years of multifamily property management experience, including time as a Leasing Consultant and Assistant Community Manager
  • Six months of Community Manager experience strongly preferred
  • Yardi, Knock, and Microsoft Office experience preferred
  • Valid driver's license required; CAM, CAPS, or a real estate license is a plus

The candidates who tend to perform well here aren't just operationally strong. They can read a T-12, connect a budget variance to a leasing trend, and explain both to ownership groups clearly. Greer sits in the growing Greenville-Spartanburg corridor, a market that has seen consistent population and employment growth, which keeps occupancy pressure real and renewal strategy important. A manager who treats renewals as a revenue tool rather than an afterthought will find traction here.

Schedule is Monday through Friday, 9 AM to 6 PM, with Saturdays from 10 AM to 4 PM. One weekday off is built in each week to keep the schedule at 40 hours. Occasional evenings may come up around resident events. Compensation includes base salary plus monthly leasing and renewal commissions and quarterly performance bonuses.
greenhouse_4387275009.description_text: At Hawthorne Residential Partners , we’re looking for passionate, hardworking , and caring individuals who are ready to make a meaningful impact at our award-winning apartment communities each day. As one of the top 50 largest multifamily management companies in the country- proudly rooted in the Southeast—we lead with heart and operate with purpose. It's 9:15 a.m. and your leasing board already shows three appointments before noon, a vendor callback on a pending HVAC contract, and a delinquency report that needs your attention before end of week. That's a typical Tuesday at The Overlook at Daytona.

Cortland is one of the top 10 multifamily owners and operators in the country, and this community manager role sits at the center of everything that makes a property perform. You'll carry full P&L responsibility for a multimillion-dollar apartment community in Daytona Beach, with accountability spanning NOI, occupancy, leasing velocity, expense control, and the resident experience from first tour to renewal.

What This Role Actually Requires

The financial side is non-negotiable. You'll own the budget, track performance against your T-12, and make spend decisions that protect NOI without letting the asset drift. That means reading your numbers with genuine fluency, not just reporting them upward. When occupancy softens or concessions creep up, you'll need to diagnose the cause and respond with a plan, not a status update.

On the leasing side, you'll set team goals, monitor traffic-to-lease conversion, and coach your team through the full sales cycle. Cortland operates at a premium, so the expectation isn't just closing leases. It's creating the kind of prospect experience where the decision feels easy. You'll work alongside corporate marketing partners on campaigns and maintain the community's social presence, but the on-the-ground execution is yours.

Operations at this level means regular property inspections, vendor management, contract negotiation, and strict adherence to Fair Housing and OSHA standards. You'll field escalated resident concerns personally and set the tone for how your team handles the ones that don't reach your desk.

Who Fits This Role

  • At least 2 years of sales leadership in a high-velocity environment: multifamily, hospitality, luxury retail, or a comparable short-cycle sales setting
  • Demonstrated results on occupancy, revenue, and NOI targets (not just familiarity with the concepts)
  • Experience building and coaching a team, with a track record of accountability and development
  • Strong financial acumen: budgeting, forecasting, and expense management at the community level
  • Comfort with property management software, CRM platforms, and data-driven decision making
  • High school diploma required; bachelor's degree preferred

The candidates who stand out here combine two things that don't always travel together: the ability to read a financial report and the ability to energize a leasing team on a slow Monday. If you're stronger at one than the other, this role will expose that gap quickly. Cortland's vertically integrated structure means you have real resources behind you, but it also means performance expectations are well-defined and tracked closely.

Daytona Beach's rental market sees consistent demand tied to its tourism economy and year-round population base, which creates steady traffic but also requires clear brand differentiation at the premium end of the market. Understanding how to position a Class A community in that context matters here more than in a single-demand-driver market.

greenhouse_6163700004.title: Regional Manager
greenhouse_6163700004.rewritten_description:
Third-party management at scale creates a specific kind of regional role. Asset Living oversees portfolios that cut across multifamily, build-to-rent, affordable housing, and student housing, which means their regional managers don't just monitor one asset class. They manage across property types, ownership structures, and reporting relationships simultaneously. This Raleigh-based Regional Manager position sits inside that complexity.

Raleigh's rental market has remained competitive through recent years of sustained in-migration and new supply coming online. That combination puts real pressure on NOI: concessions are a live conversation at many properties, and occupancy targets require active marketing strategies rather than passive lease renewal cycles. A regional manager here needs to read T-3 and T-12 trends together, because short-term dips in a supply-heavy submarket can obscure fundamentals that are actually sound.

What This Role Covers

This is a full portfolio operations role. You'll carry responsibility for personnel, leasing performance, financial outcomes, maintenance standards, and compliance across all sites you oversee. On any given week that means reviewing budget variances and writing explanations for line items that have drifted significantly over projection, approving timesheets, conducting property inspections, and working with on-site Community Managers on staffing decisions including hiring, coaching, and when necessary, termination. The personnel management piece here is real work, not oversight from a distance. You'll screen candidates, document performance issues properly, coordinate with HR, and sign off on salary requests before they move up the chain.

Financially, you'll build yearly operating budgets, track income and expense performance monthly, and flag capital improvement needs before they become deferred maintenance problems. You'll also review vendor proposals and monitor work in progress on larger projects. On the leasing side, you'll develop annual marketing plans, assess staff closing techniques, and build resident retention programs that reduce turnover costs at the property level.

What Strong Candidates Bring

  • Demonstrated experience managing multiple properties simultaneously, with measurable NOI results
  • Comfort reading financial reports at the ownership level, not just the property level
  • Direct experience with personnel decisions: coaching plans, written evaluations, and terminations handled correctly
  • Familiarity with fair housing compliance as an operational habit, not an occasional training topic
  • Ability to develop a marketing strategy that responds to actual local traffic data, not generic templates

The candidates who struggle in regional roles at third-party management firms are usually strong at one function but thin in another. Operators who are excellent with financials but passive about staff development find that site performance erodes quietly. The reverse is equally common. Asset Living's portfolio breadth means the regional manager who performs well here typically develops a cross-property type fluency that opens paths into senior vice president roles or asset management functions over time.

greenhouse_7982363003.rewritten_description:
Most Class A lease-ups eventually settle into a stabilized rhythm, and that's exactly where a property's financial discipline gets tested. The Business Manager role at Station 250 in Mundelein exists to own that rhythm, keeping occupancy strong, budgets grounded in reality, and a team performing at the level a luxury asset demands.

Olympus Property has held a spot on the National Apartment Association's Top Employer list three consecutive years (2023, 2024, 2025), which is worth noting for candidates weighing company culture alongside the role itself. For a Business Manager, culture isn't abstract. It shapes how onsite teams respond to difficult residents, how maintenance approaches make-readies, and how front-office staff treats a prospect walking in on a Wednesday afternoon.

What the Role Actually Covers

This is a full-scope property management position. You'll own the financial performance of the asset, which means building and tracking budgets, reviewing monthly financials, projecting NOI, and presenting strategy to Regional Leadership. On the operational side, you'll oversee both office and maintenance staff, manage vendor contracts (bidding, negotiating, and holding vendors accountable to scope), and make sure units, common areas, and amenity spaces stay market-ready. Leasing and retention programs fall under your direction as well. Keeping occupancy up at a luxury address means the renewal program has to be sharp and the traffic conversion has to be consistent.

RealPage/Knock/Onesite experience is strongly preferred. At a Class A property, those platforms touch everything from prospect communication to lease execution to delinquency tracking, so a candidate who already works fluently in that stack will ramp up faster.

What Strong Candidates Bring

  • At least two years of multifamily property management experience, with preference for luxury or Class A assets
  • Comfort reading and presenting financial reports, not just generating them
  • Experience managing a mixed team of leasing and maintenance staff
  • Familiarity with vendor contract negotiation and project oversight
  • Availability Monday through Friday with flexibility for after-hours resident events and occasional emergencies

The candidates who stand out at this level tend to be the ones who've already managed a stabilized asset through at least one full budget cycle. Understanding how to build an annual business plan, defend line items with a Regional VP, and adjust mid-year when actuals drift from projections separates a solid leasing manager from a property manager who can genuinely run a building.

Compensation is $80,000 to $90,000 annually, with monthly commissions and quarterly and annual bonus eligibility on top of base pay. Benefits include medical, dental and vision coverage, 401(k) with employer matching, tuition reimbursement, an apartment rental allowance, and a sabbatical program, among others. Olympus also offers structured career pathing and leadership development, which matters if you're thinking about where this role goes next.
