greenhouse_8166819.title: Groundskeeper
greenhouse_8166819.rewritten_description:
Groundskeeping builds a specific set of skills that transfer well into broader property maintenance careers, and Weinstein Properties structures this role with that path in mind. The work itself is physical and repetitive by design. What it develops is equally real: an eye for property condition, the habit of proactive problem-spotting, and the kind of reliability that maintenance supervisors actively recruit from when a tech position opens up.

What This Role Actually Requires

The Bexley at Whitestone community in Cedar Park, TX needs a groundskeeper who operates largely independently and keeps the exterior spaces clean, welcoming, and well-maintained on a daily basis. That means trash and pet waste pickup every morning, operating equipment like backpack blowers and power washers, maintaining planted areas through weeding and seasonal upkeep, and supporting the maintenance team with light painting and turnover tasks when needed.

This is outdoor work, year-round, in Central Texas heat and occasional cold snaps. Lifting up to 50 pounds, prolonged walking and bending, and operating golf carts and trailers are routine parts of the day. The honest version of this role is that a significant portion of the work is recurring and unglamorous. The people who do it well are the ones who take genuine ownership of what a property looks like rather than just completing a checklist.

Skills That Compound Over Time

Groundskeepers who move into maintenance tech roles often credit their time on the grounds team for building one thing that's hard to teach otherwise: the ability to scan a property and see what's off before a resident reports it. That observational habit, developed through daily walkthroughs, carries directly into punch list work, make-ready inspections, and eventually work order prioritization. It's a foundational skill in multifamily operations.

Weinstein Properties, a family-owned company managing over 60 communities across five states for more than 70 years, has a stated emphasis on developing people from entry-level roles upward. That's a meaningful distinction in an industry where groundskeeping positions are often treated as isolated labor. Here, the role has an explicit growth track toward maintenance tech and beyond.

What Strong Candidates Bring

  • Consistent reliability, including showing up on schedule without supervision required
  • Comfort with physical, repetitive outdoor work across all weather conditions
  • A proactive approach to noticing and reporting property issues
  • Willingness to cross into adjacent tasks like light maintenance support or unit trash-outs
  • A growth mindset toward learning equipment operation and basic maintenance skills

The schedule is Monday through Friday, 8am to 5pm, with competitive hourly pay starting at $18/hour, quarterly bonuses, and a retention bonus available after 90 days. Benefits include a rent discount, health, dental, and vision coverage, a 401k with company match, paid holidays, and birthday time off.

Apartment maintenance at a 200-plus unit property is a volume game. Service requests stack up, turns come in waves, and the on-call rotation means a leaking water heater doesn't care what time it is. MG Properties is hiring a Maintenance Technician for Axcess15 Apartments in Portland, and the posting is straightforward about what the work actually involves.

What the Work Looks Like Day to Day

The bulk of your time will split between completing resident service requests and keeping the property's common areas, grounds, and offices clean and functional. When units turn, you're doing the make-ready work: painting, appliance repairs, punch list items, and whatever else it takes to get the unit rent-ready. Trades coverage is broad here. Plumbing, electrical, HVAC, and general repairs all fall within scope, so this isn't a role where you can be strong in one area and shrug at everything else. MG Properties specifically wants someone with at least two years of apartment maintenance experience at a property of comparable size. That background matters because the pace and the variety of problems at a 200-unit community are different from smaller sites.

The on-call rotation is real. Emergency calls happen after hours, and reliable transportation is a firm requirement, not a preference. If that part of the job is a dealbreaker, it's worth knowing upfront rather than finding out during orientation.

  • Monthly bonuses and company profit sharing
  • 10 days PTO accrued per year, plus 10 paid holidays and 2 personal days
  • 40 hours paid sick time
  • 401(k) with employer match
  • Medical, dental, and vision coverage, plus an Employee Assistance Program
  • Life insurance, FSA, and dependent care spending account
  • Rental discounts

MG Properties has been operating across the Western U.S. for over 30 years, with a portfolio that spans acquisition, development, rehabilitation, and ongoing management. That scale means internal mobility is a real possibility for technicians who perform well. The step from technician to lead tech or maintenance supervisor is a common trajectory at regional operators of this size, and those roles come with meaningful pay differences and responsibility over a team rather than just a work order queue.

Strong candidates will bring multi-trade competence and a customer service orientation that holds up when a resident is frustrated about a slow repair. The combination of technical skill and communication is what separates technicians who stay and grow from those who burn out. If you can work a full turn efficiently, handle an emergency call calmly, and follow up with residents in a way that leaves them feeling heard, you'll do well here.

greenhouse_8766222002.title: Assistant Community Manager
greenhouse_8766222002.location: The Parlor, San Marcos, Texas, United States
greenhouse_8766222002.rewritten_description:
It's the first week of August at The Parlor, and every bed on the property needs to turn in roughly 72 hours. Your punch list isn't a list anymore. It's a war room. That's the heartbeat of student housing, and this role sits right at the center of it.

The Role

The Scion Group is hiring an Assistant Community Manager (titled internally as Assistant General Manager) for The Parlor, their student housing community in San Marcos, Texas. This is a full-scope operations role. You'll work alongside the General Manager on financial performance, resident accounts, leasing activity, and facilities. When the GM is out, you're running the asset.

On the financial side, your benchmark is clear: delinquency below 2% at month end. You'll manage accounts receivable, post damage charges from quarterly inspections, process final billing at move-out, and assist with month-end reporting and account reconciliation. You'll also enforce late fee and NSF policies consistently, which matters more than most candidates realize. A student housing property with loose collections practices can see delinquency creep up fast given the transactional nature of the resident base.

Leasing and revenue are part of the job too. You'll manage sales interactions directly and coach your team through them, run weekly market surveys, oversee concessions and promotional materials within budget, and use KPIs to spot trends before they become problems. Traffic-to-lease ratios, occupancy targets, renewal velocity. You'll be expected to know these numbers and act on them.

Facilities and curb appeal fall under your watch as well. That means regular inspections of vacant bed spaces and common areas, coordinating work orders, and keeping the property in a condition that supports both leasing and resident retention. In student housing, the physical condition of a community is a direct sales tool.

Annual turn planning is one of the most operationally demanding stretches in this business. You'll help lead the team through that process, which in student housing means managing hundreds of move-outs and move-ins in a compressed window, all while keeping service quality intact.

What Strong Candidates Bring

  • At least one year of experience in property management or residential community operations
  • Proficiency in a property management system, with Entrata experience preferred
  • Demonstrated ability to handle resident escalations, collections enforcement, and compliance with Fair Housing requirements
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Comfort working non-traditional hours during peak leasing periods and on-call rotations

Candidates who stand out in student housing ACM roles typically come in with a solid handle on collections discipline and a genuine interest in the leasing side. The properties that hit their occupancy and NOI targets usually have an ACM who treats delinquency as a daily metric, not a month-end cleanup task. Familiarity with the San Marcos market and the Texas State University enrollment cycle is a real advantage here, though not a stated requirement.

San Marcos is a competitive student housing market given its enrollment growth trajectory. Knowing how to read concession trends and time lease-up decisions around academic calendars separates good operators from average ones at properties like this.

Benefits include health, dental, and vision insurance, 401k matching, paid time off, paid parental and maternal leave, learning reimbursement, and a discretionary annual bonus.

What You'll Actually Do

The leasing consultant role at Hawthorne Residential Partners' Integra Landings community in Orange City, Florida puts you at the front of the resident experience from first contact to move-in. On a typical day, you're fielding inquiries by phone, email, and online portals, converting that traffic into tours, and walking prospects through apartments in a way that connects the floorplan to their actual lifestyle. That last part takes more skill than it sounds. Closing a lease requires listening well enough to understand what someone actually needs, then showing them how this community meets it.

Beyond leasing, you'll work on occupancy and renewal goals alongside the broader site team, help coordinate resident events, and keep the leasing office and common areas presentable. Hawthorne also expects you to track competitor properties and stay current on local market conditions, which sharpens your ability to position the community accurately against alternatives a prospect might be considering.

What You Bring

  • At least one year of customer service, sales, or apartment leasing experience (preferred, not required)
  • Comfort communicating across channels: in person, phone, and written correspondence
  • A genuine ability to read people and move a conversation toward a decision without being pushy
  • Accuracy when handling leasing applications, verifications, and move-in paperwork
  • High school diploma or GED equivalent
  • Valid driver's license; CALP accreditation is a plus
  • Availability for the standard schedule: Monday through Friday 9 AM to 6 PM, Saturdays 10 AM to 4 PM, with one weekday off each week

Skills This Role Builds and Where It Goes

Leasing is one of the best entry points into property management because it gives you hands-on exposure to the full resident lifecycle: lead generation, qualifying prospects, the application and approval process, move-in coordination, and retention through renewals. The skills you develop here, specifically objection handling, occupancy awareness, and relationship-building with residents, transfer directly into an assistant community manager role, which Hawthorne explicitly supports through a structured Career Path Program.

Strong candidates come in knowing how to sell without pressure and leave having learned how to read occupancy trends, respond to delinquency early through renewal efforts, and contribute meaningfully to a site's NOI through consistent lease conversions. The difference between a leasing consultant who stays in the role and one who advances quickly usually comes down to how well they understand the numbers behind the community, not just the people in front of them. Hawthorne's compensation structure, which includes monthly leasing and renewal commissions on top of an hourly base, gives you a financial incentive to develop that understanding early.

greenhouse_4384218009.rewritten_description:
The work order queue shows six open requests, a unit turn needs a punch list walk before Friday's move-in, and the boiler room log is overdue for its weekly entry. That's a typical Tuesday morning for a Maintenance Manager at JMC's 3200 Washington property in Jamaica Plain.

What the Role Demands

John M. Corcoran & Company has operated across New England since 1951, and the maintenance function at their Jamaica Plain community reflects that institutional seriousness about property condition. This role carries real operational ownership. You'll oversee daily work orders from assignment through completion, run a preventive maintenance program, and keep the property's electrical, mechanical, and building systems functioning and documented. Unit turns fall under your coordination as well: tracking make-ready status, confirming punch list items are closed, and making sure units are genuinely move-in ready before keys change hands.

You'll supervise maintenance technicians, janitorial staff, and grounds crew, which means your organizational and communication skills get tested daily. Vendor coordination and supply management require you to work within budget guidelines, so cost awareness matters here. JMC expects accurate records: maintenance logs, purchase orders, and reports kept current and accessible. On-call rotation is part of the position, and after-hours emergencies will come up.

Minimum qualifications for this role include:

  • High school diploma or equivalent education or experience
  • At least three years of trade or general building maintenance experience
  • Working knowledge of electrical, mechanical, and building systems
  • Strong organizational, communication, and leadership skills
  • Ability to follow safety procedures and company policies consistently

What the Role Builds

Candidates who step into this position with solid trade knowledge but limited supervisory experience will develop real crew management skills here. Managing a mixed team of maintenance, janitorial, and grounds staff across a residential property teaches you how to prioritize competing demands, communicate expectations clearly, and hold a team accountable without friction. Those are transferable skills that open doors to multi-site maintenance director roles or regional facilities management positions.

Strong candidates will arrive knowing the difference between a reactive shop and a preventive one. If your current instinct is to run a PM schedule before things break rather than after, and you can coach that discipline into a team, you'll fit the culture JMC describes. The managers who struggle here tend to treat paperwork as secondary. At a company with this much operational history, accurate records are part of the craft, not a burden on top of it.

The position runs Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., with on-call rotation. Compensation ranges from $33 to $39 per hour, with a $2,500 sign-on bonus. Benefits include medical, dental, vision, and life insurance, paid time off plus holidays, and a 401(k) with company match.

Residential maintenance at a multi-family property isn't a single trade. It's a rotation through plumbing calls, appliance failures, electrical diagnostics, HVAC concerns, carpentry patches, and pool chemistry, often in the same week. The Maintenance Technician 3 designation at Ackermann Group reflects that breadth. This is a journeyman-level role that expects cross-trade competency on arrival and builds sharper independent judgment through hands-on ownership of a full property's maintenance cycle.

Ackermann Group has operated in Midwest real estate development and property management since 1938, with a portfolio and culture built around long-term thinking and community investment. The Florence, KY position is a full-time, Monday through Friday role with an after-hours emergency on-call rotation.

What This Role Demands

The core of the job is intermediate-to-advanced troubleshooting across the maintenance trades: plumbing, electrical, carpentry, appliance repair, HVAC, and painting. You'll carry out resident service requests, participate in move-in and move-out inspections, and coordinate unit turn scheduling with approved contractors. Managing parts inventory and turn-related supplies falls to you as well, so organizational discipline matters as much as technical skill.

Beyond reactive work, you'll contribute to the property's preventative maintenance plan and handle exterior and interior building and grounds upkeep including light janitorial. Pool water management is part of the role where applicable, and seasonal responsibilities include snow event preparation and removal. All of this gets documented through Ackermann's internal technology and software platforms.

  • EPA Type I and II certification required
  • CPO and CAMT certifications preferred
  • Aquatherm system experience preferred
  • Valid driver's license with proof of insurance
  • One or more years of broad general maintenance experience
  • High school diploma or equivalent

What This Role Builds

Technicians who come in with solid trade fundamentals and grow through a role like this tend to develop something that's harder to teach: the ability to manage contractor relationships, work within a maintenance budget, and prioritize across competing demands with minimal supervision. Those are exactly the skills that move a strong technician toward a Maintenance Supervisor position. The financial and organizational acumen the role expects on day one sharpens considerably when you're the person accountable for inventory and contractor coordination on every turn cycle.

What separates strong candidates from average ones here is the combination of technical range and communication. Resident-facing service work requires you to explain what you found, what you fixed, and what the next steps are, clearly and professionally. Technicians who treat communication as part of the job, rather than an interruption to it, tend to advance faster and carry more trust from the management team.

greenhouse_8764826002.rewritten_description:
What This Role Actually Builds

The Assistant Community Manager role at a multifamily property is one of the most skill-dense positions in residential property management. You're touching leasing performance, financial operations, compliance, and team development at the same time. At Waypoint Management Services in Vero Beach, that means working alongside the Community Manager to keep a premier multifamily community running well across all of those dimensions simultaneously.

The financial side gets real here. You'll work through delinquency, support rent collection, track the rent roll, and flag reporting issues before they compound. If you've only done leasing up to this point, this is the role where you start reading numbers, not just running traffic. That shift from leasing consultant to ACM is one of the most important career transitions in multifamily, and the financial exposure you build here is exactly what separates future Community Managers from people who plateau in leasing.

Day-to-Day Responsibilities

The week-to-week workload covers a lot of ground:

  • Supporting the leasing team through coaching, training, and operational accountability
  • Tracking make-ready schedules and occupancy reports to keep turns on schedule
  • Monitoring renewals and helping execute pricing recommendations based on market surveys and occupancy goals
  • Executing sales and marketing strategies to bring in qualified prospects and retain current residents
  • Keeping lease files, resident records, and administrative reporting accurate and current
  • Maintaining compliance with applicable federal, state, and local regulations
  • Assisting with evictions when delinquency reaches that point

Weekend availability is required, which is standard at stabilized multifamily properties. If that's new information, factor it into your decision. If it's familiar, you already know the tradeoff: weekday flexibility often compensates for it.

What Sets Strong Candidates Apart

Waypoint prefers Yardi experience, and that preference matters. Candidates who already know how to pull reports, process charges, and manage lease data inside a property management platform can contribute from week one instead of spending the first month learning the software while also learning the property. Microsoft Office proficiency and comfort with social media round out the tech expectations, but Yardi fluency is the real differentiator at the application stage.

Beyond software, the ACMs who move up quickly tend to be the ones who treat the financial reports as seriously as the leasing board. greenhouse_4390516009.title: Leasing Consultant (Westgate on Third)
greenhouse_4390516009.rewritten_description:
Leasing is a conversion game. Traffic comes in, your job is to turn it into signed leases, and every interaction between a prospect's first call and their move-in date runs through you. At Westgate on Third in Bloomington, BAM Companies is looking for a Leasing Consultant who can work that full cycle well: fast follow-up, confident tours, clean paperwork, and residents who feel taken care of before they ever get their keys.

What the Day-to-Day Looks Like

You're the first point of contact for prospective residents reaching out by phone, email, or walk-in. The expectation is quick response times and genuine conversation, not a scripted pitch. You'll tour units, explain pricing and features, and walk prospects through the application and deposit process all the way to lease execution. Between tours, you're maintaining show units and the leasing office so everything stays sharp, logging activity in the CRM, and supporting the property manager on marketing pushes, outreach events, and community programming.

Weekends are part of the schedule here. Bloomington is a university market, and leasing activity doesn't pause for a Monday-Friday workweek. A reliable vehicle is required since outreach and off-site activity come with the role.

What BAM Is Looking For

  • High school diploma or equivalent; some college experience is a plus
  • Background in leasing, retail, hospitality, or any sales-adjacent role
  • Strong follow-up habits and genuine comfort talking to people through a major decision
  • Basic CRM and computer proficiency
  • Organized, reliable, and able to juggle multiple prospects at different stages of the funnel
  • NALP credentials, bilingual skills, or prior real estate interest are preferred but not required

Compensation and Benefits

Base pay runs $17 to $19 per hour depending on experience, location, and overall fit. On top of that, leasing commissions add performance-based income tied directly to signed leases. BAM also offers 15.5 paid holidays starting on day one, PTO that builds after 90 days and grows again at your one-year mark, and a full insurance package covering medical, dental, vision, life, disability, and pet coverage. Housing discounts at BAM properties are available if you want to live where you work.

Bloomington's rental market is heavily driven by Indiana University's enrollment cycle, which means leasing activity hits predictable peaks around application and renewal season. Consultants who learn to read that rhythm, stay on top of their follow-up queue during high-traffic windows, and close cleanly under volume pressure tend to build a strong performance record quickly. That track record is what typically opens doors to Assistant Manager and Property Manager roles within a company like BAM.

greenhouse_4388621009.rewritten_description:
What This Role Is Really About

At a well-run multifamily property, curb appeal is a direct line to occupancy. A prospect pulling into the parking lot forms an impression before they ever meet a leasing agent, and that impression affects traffic-to-lease conversion. The Groundskeeper/Porter at Ames Lofts in Los Angeles owns that first impression. Berkshire Residential Investments operates a vertically integrated platform, meaning they own and manage their own communities, so the standards here reflect a real investment stake in the asset, not just a third-party contract obligation.

Berkshire is offering $18.50 to $22.00 per hour for this position, depending on experience, with a benefits package that includes health coverage, retirement, paid time off, and a 25% rent discount.

Day-to-Day Responsibilities

This is a physically active, outdoor-forward role. You'll walk the grounds and common areas on a regular cycle to keep the property clear of litter and debris. Curb appeal isn't a buzzword here: it's a measurable standard that shows up in how the property photographs, how it reads during a prospect tour, and how current residents feel about renewing. Beyond grounds maintenance, you'll assist the maintenance team when needed, which can include helping with turns and make-ready prep work between residents. Strong customer service matters too. You'll interact with residents and prospective renters on the property daily.

  • Routine grounds and common area walkthroughs to remove debris and maintain appearance
  • Support maintenance staff with tasks as directed
  • Uphold service standards when interacting with residents and prospects
  • Attention to physical detail across the entire exterior of the property

What Strong Candidates Bring

Prior experience in cleaning, construction, or general maintenance gives you a practical foundation, though Berkshire lists this as preferred rather than required. What matters more is that you're genuinely comfortable with physical work, you take pride in how a property looks, and you stay consistent even when no one is watching. In a market like Los Angeles, where Class A lease-ups compete hard on presentation and resident experience, a Groundskeeper who treats the property like it's their own asset is a real operational advantage.

Basic computer proficiency and strong English communication skills round out what Berkshire is looking for. This role carries more visibility than many people expect. A well-kept property retains residents, supports renewals, and keeps delinquency issues from compounding due to dissatisfied tenants looking for reasons to leave. The Groundskeeper is part of that retention equation.

greenhouse_4387608009.title: Community Manager
greenhouse_4387608009.rewritten_description:
It's 8:45 on a Tuesday morning. A resident is at your door about a maintenance issue that was supposed to be closed out last week, your leasing consultant just flagged a delinquency report that needs attention before noon, and you have a call with your Regional Manager at ten. That's a normal morning in this role.

Redstone Residential operates more than 38,000 beds across 20 states, with a portfolio that spans student housing and a growing conventional multifamily side. The Community Manager position in Rexburg, Idaho is the top site-level role, meaning the property's operational and financial outcomes run through you. You report to the Regional Manager, but day-to-day, you're the decision-maker on the ground.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

You'll own the lease-up strategy and occupancy goals, track KPIs through Redstone's systems, and manage the property to an approved operating budget with P&L accountability. Delinquency collections, renewal outreach, and marketing coordination are all part of your scope. You'll also submit weekly and monthly performance reports and may oversee projects that range from marketing campaigns to construction-adjacent capex work.

Because this is a student housing market, the leasing calendar is compressed and cyclical. Renewal season arrives fast, traffic spikes come in waves, and concessions strategy matters more than it does at a typical conventional lease-up. Rexburg is a college town built around BYU-Idaho, which means your resident base is transient, your turnover is predictable but high-volume, and community relationships with campus contacts carry real weight for referral traffic.

You'll also be the person setting the tone for customer service on your team. That means training staff, running performance evaluations, and being honest when someone needs to improve.

What Redstone Is Looking For

  • At least one year of property management experience, with direct experience in student housing or multifamily
  • Demonstrated budget management and P&L ownership
  • Professional presentation and prior experience in client-facing situations
  • Ability to juggle multiple processes simultaneously under real pressure
  • Comfort with property management software (Entrata experience is a plus, but not required)
  • Proficiency with Google Workspace and Microsoft Office
  • A team-oriented approach, including the ability to give constructive feedback and hold people accountable

The compensation for this role is $16.00 per hour (non-exempt, full-time), with the ability to earn up to an additional 20% through performance bonuses. Benefits include health, vision, and dental insurance, a 401(k) with up to 6% employer matching, short-term disability, an employee assistance program, and continued education and professional development support.

The candidates who tend to thrive here aren't necessarily the ones with the longest resume. They're the ones who can hold a leasing conversation and read a budget in the same afternoon without losing focus on either. Student housing rewards people who stay organized under volume, communicate directly with residents and staff, and treat occupancy targets like real commitments rather than suggestions.

greenhouse_5411111008.title: Apartment Maintenance Technician
greenhouse_5411111008.rewritten_description:
Maintenance work at an apartment community is physical, repetitive, sometimes inconvenient, and genuinely important. At Fairstead's Scottsville, Kentucky property, a Maintenance Technician keeps housing functional for residents who depend on affordable, well-managed homes. The role draws on a specific combination of skills every single day: mechanical aptitude, electrical knowledge, systems thinking, and the kind of attention to detail that catches a problem before it becomes an emergency.

The Skills This Role Runs On

Electrical diagnostics are a real part of this job. You'll check wiring for compliance, identify problems, and handle minor repairs correctly. That requires comfort with basic electrical systems, not just a willingness to try. Mechanical skills come into play across HVAC, plumbing, appliances, and general fixtures. Preventative maintenance is a core discipline here, not an afterthought. You're running scheduled inspections on buildings and equipment, checking safety systems monthly, and managing an inventory of supplies and tools so nothing falls through the cracks when a repair comes up.

Make-ready work is part of the rotation too. When a unit turns, you're cleaning and preparing it so the next resident moves into a home that's actually ready. That work is unglamorous and physically demanding, and it matters a great deal to occupancy.

The on-call rotation is honest about what this job asks of you. Emergency maintenance problems don't wait for business hours. If you've worked apartment maintenance before, you already know this. If you're coming from a similar service technician background, it's worth being clear-eyed about: after-hours calls happen, and they're part of this role.

Qualifications Worth Knowing

  • Prior experience as a maintenance or service technician in a residential or commercial setting
  • Working knowledge of electrical systems and the ability to diagnose and repair minor issues
  • General mechanical skills across plumbing, HVAC, appliances, and fixtures
  • HVAC certification, CMRP, or equivalent credential preferred
  • Ability to lift up to 70 pounds without assistance and stand for extended periods
  • Written and verbal communication skills sufficient to document work and communicate with residents and staff

Working Within Fairstead's Operation

Fairstead owns and manages over 30,000 units across 28 states, with development, construction, and property management handled under one platform. That integration matters at the property level because decisions about capital work, vendor relationships, and maintenance standards move through a company that actually understands operations from the inside. For a technician, that typically means clearer systems, better tools access, and management that knows what maintenance work involves.

The company also takes a data-driven approach to operations, including maintenance tracking. That won't eliminate the physical side of the work, but technicians who document well and communicate clearly tend to have a longer runway at organizations like this. Strong candidates in this role combine trade skill with the discipline to keep records accurate and communicate problems before they escalate. That combination is what separates a good technician from one who just fixes things when asked.

greenhouse_5411716008.title: Community Manager - Delaware Pines
greenhouse_5411716008.rewritten_description:
Community managers at conventional properties carry a deceptively broad mandate. You're running a small business: hiring, collections, leasing, maintenance coordination, vendor oversight, and resident relations, all inside a single job title. At a property like Delaware Pines in Huntington Beach, that breadth is exactly what this role demands.

This is a part-time position, which is worth saying plainly. The pay range runs $24 to $25 per hour depending on experience, and the role does not include benefits eligibility. For someone building their PM resume or returning to the industry, it can be a solid fit. For someone who needs full-time income and benefits, that's a practical mismatch to weigh before applying.

The Scope of the Work

Reporting to a Regional Manager, you'd carry full operational responsibility for the property. That means staffing: hiring, training, and evaluating on-site personnel, not just supervising them once they're settled. It means financial oversight, including rent collection, delinquency management, and daily bank deposits under California landlord-tenant law. Budget prep and expense monitoring fall here too.

On the leasing side, you'd manage available units through approved advertising, conduct showings, keep leasing records clean, and support renewals to protect occupancy. Market awareness matters here. Huntington Beach carries a competitive coastal submarket, and pricing decisions need to stay calibrated to what's actually happening in the comp set, not just what the budget assumed six months ago.

Resident relations includes the full range: service request follow-through within 24 to 48 hours when possible, fair housing compliance at every touchpoint, and the general work of keeping people satisfied enough to renew. Regular inspections of units, common areas, and grounds round out the day-to-day.

What Strong Candidates Bring

  • One to two years of direct property management experience, meaning you've actually run leasing activity and collections, not just assisted
  • Working knowledge of California landlord-tenant law and Fair Housing, applied in practice rather than just on paper
  • Comfort in property management software alongside Microsoft Office
  • Genuine organizational discipline, because a community manager without a system for tracking delinquency, open work orders, and lease expirations will feel it quickly
  • A college degree or relevant coursework, preferred but not hard-required

What separates a solid applicant from a great one here is usually the delinquency piece. Managers who treat collections as a monthly scramble tend to struggle under California's procedural requirements. The ones who run clean ledgers and communicate early with residents before accounts age are the ones who actually keep NOI stable. That discipline shows up in interviews if you know what to look for.

Sunrise Management describes its operating philosophy around what they call resident hospitality, a practical orientation toward retention and service quality rather than just occupancy targets. If that framing resonates with how you've approached resident relations in past roles, that's a reasonable culture signal worth taking seriously.

greenhouse_4710134006.title: Maintenance Technician
greenhouse_4710134006.rewritten_description:
Maintenance work at an affordable housing property asks more of you than just knowing which wrench to grab. You're reading a building, tracking what's wearing out before it fails, and keeping a tight turn schedule so a vacant unit doesn't sit past five days. At Harbor House in Corpus Christi, Dream Live Prosper Communities is hiring a full-time Maintenance Technician to do exactly that kind of work across their affordable rental portfolio.

The Skills This Role Runs On

HVAC certification is required from the start. Beyond that, the daily work pulls from a wide toolkit: electrical troubleshooting, plumbing repairs, appliance work, drywall patching, painting, and lock hardware. You'll handle resident service requests within 24 hours and complete make-readies within five days, which is a real constraint that demands both technical competence and good scheduling instincts. You'll need your own basic hand tools and a valid driver's license with a clean record, since assignments move across the property and on-call rotation takes you off-site when emergencies come in.

The physical demands are real and worth acknowledging plainly. Climbing ladders, accessing crawl spaces and attics, working outdoors in South Texas heat, and lifting up to 50 pounds are regular parts of this job. After-hours emergency calls are part of the rotation. If that's a dealbreaker, this posting isn't the right fit.

What You're Actually Managing Day to Day

Resident service requests, unit turns, grounds upkeep, and shop inventory all live on your plate simultaneously. You'll also carry some team-level responsibility: coordinating the service team's hours, mentoring other technicians, managing security deposit dispositions related to maintenance, and keeping purchasing disciplined without leaving the shop understocked. That last piece matters more than it sounds. Overspending on supplies is easy; keeping costs lean while staying stocked takes real attention.

Experience with turnovers in both newer and older buildings is specifically called out in the qualifications. Older affordable housing stock tends to have mixed systems, aging fixtures, and surprises behind walls. Technicians who've only worked Class A new construction sometimes struggle with that variability. If you've worked on properties where the bones are older, that experience translates directly here.

What Separates Strong Candidates Here

The five-day turn target is where good technicians prove themselves at affordable properties. It requires you to walk a unit, write your own punch list, sequence the work correctly, and execute without a lot of hand-holding. Technicians who wait for direction on every task slow the whole operation down. The ones who thrive here can assess a vacant unit independently, prioritize what has to happen before move-in, and close it out on time.

Dream Live Prosper Communities operates as a subsidiary of DLP Capital, which has an affordable housing focus and a track record of growth. The mission around attainable housing is genuine in how they describe the work, and the resident population at a property like Harbor House reflects that. Clear, professional communication with residents matters here, not because it's a corporate talking point, but because the people you're serving are working families who depend on their homes functioning.

  • HVAC certification required

greenhouse_5411486008.title: Housekeeper
greenhouse_5411486008.rewritten_description:
It's 8 a.m. and the fitness center needs to be spotless before the morning rush of residents finishes their workouts. That's your first stop, and the pace from there stays steady through amenity spaces, the clubhouse, the leasing office, and vacant apartments getting prepped for incoming residents.

What This Role Actually Involves

Griffis Residential manages a portfolio of luxury apartment communities, and the Centennial property runs to that same standard. The housekeeping role here isn't limited to common areas. You'll move between shared amenity spaces and individual apartment homes, following make-ready cleaning checklists to get vacant units resident-ready on schedule. If a unit has been sitting on the ready list for more than a week, you'll do touch-up cleaning to keep it fresh. Findings that cross into maintenance territory get communicated to the Service Manager so nothing falls through the cracks.

Daily task lists come from the Community and Service Managers. You'll follow established product safety and procedure guidelines, which means paying attention to cleaning product labels and handling materials correctly in occupied and unoccupied spaces alike. Residents, prospective residents, and team members will cross your path throughout the day, so how you carry yourself in those moments matters to the community's overall feel.

Who Fits Well Here

  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • At least one year of cleaning experience in multifamily housing, hospitality, or a comparable setting
  • Genuine attention to detail, especially across varied spaces with different cleaning standards
  • Strong communication skills, both for resident interactions and for flagging issues to management
  • English proficiency required; bilingual Spanish is a plus

The candidates who do well in this role tend to be self-directed once they know the standard. Make-ready cleaning has a checklist, but hitting that checklist well requires judgment, not just box-checking. Spotting what a unit needs before it becomes a resident complaint is the kind of instinct that separates a solid housekeeper from a great one.

Pay ranges from $20.75 to $23.00 per hour. Griffis offers a strong benefits package for full-time associates, including a 50% rental discount, 401(k) with up to 4% company match, medical, dental, and vision coverage, a minimum of three weeks of PTO accruing from day one, 11 paid holidays, tuition reimbursement up to $5,250 per year, paid parental leave, and performance-based bonuses tied to occupancy and community reputation metrics.

workable_6068685.title: Resident Director
workable_6068685.rewritten_description:
Renewal leasing is a discipline of its own, and this role at PeakMade Real Estate in Springfield, Missouri leans on it hard. The Resident Director position lives at the intersection of sales technique, relationship management, and operational coordination. If your leasing background has sharpened your instincts around retention strategy and renewal timing, this is where those skills get a real workout.

The Skill Set This Role Runs On

Renewal ratio improvement doesn't happen through enthusiasm alone. PeakMade is looking for someone who can read leasing data, identify where momentum is slipping, and adjust the approach before occupancy takes a hit. You'll work directly with the Property Manager and Regional Manager to set renewal goals and build the plans to hit them. That means you need to be comfortable pulling accurate reports in Entrata, spotting the gaps, and communicating what you're seeing to leadership. Verbal skill matters here too. You'll be the one building relationships with university contacts, running guarantor events, and mentoring leasing staff through the full leasing cycle from prospect call to signed renewal.

Student housing has its own rhythm. The academic calendar compresses your leasing season, and renewals often need to close while current residents are still settling into their lease year. Strong candidates in this space don't wait for renewal conversations to come to them.

Day-to-Day Responsibilities

  • Lead the property's renewal leasing program and track progress against budgeted occupancy targets
  • Coordinate with the Property Manager to monitor leasing activity and support areas showing weakness
  • Oversee internet lead response, prospect calls, and property tours conducted by the leasing team
  • Assist residents and guarantors through renewal paperwork, move-in, move-out, and lease takeover processes
  • Plan and execute renewal parties, guarantor events, and team competitions to drive retention
  • Audit lease and renewal files alongside the Leasing Manager for compliance and bonus submission accuracy
  • Conduct weekly team meetings, deliver training sessions, and manage staff scheduling
  • Participate in property inspections and contribute to upkeep of office and common areas
  • Build and maintain relationships with local universities and community organizations

What Makes This Role Specific to PeakMade

PeakMade operates across off-campus student housing, conventional multifamily, and build-to-rent communities nationwide, with its home office in Atlanta. The Springfield property fits within a portfolio managed with an emphasis on branding consistency and structured programs, so the Resident Director here isn't reinventing the playbook. You're executing it well and finding the local angles that improve retention on your specific asset.

Compensation includes potential monthly commission and a housing discount, plus a benefits package with paid parental leave and a 401(k) match. One to two years of multifamily or student housing leasing experience is the baseline ask, with preference for candidates who've sat in a Leasing Manager seat and know what it takes to run a team through a full lease-up cycle.

workable_6075093.title: Community Manager Manufactured Housing Community PLUS HOUSING
workable_6075093.rewritten_description:
Skills That Drive This Role

This position runs on a specific combination of abilities: financial oversight, resident relations, team leadership, and regulatory compliance. At Alpine Vista Village, a 123-home manufactured housing community in Loveland, Colorado, those skills get exercised every day across a property where you're the senior decision-maker on site. If you've managed occupancy, chased delinquency, handled eviction workflows, and coached a small staff, you already speak the language this role requires.

Manufactured housing communities operate under a distinct set of rules compared to conventional multifamily. Lot lease agreements, state-specific MHC regulations, and relationships with community development agencies all create compliance demands that go beyond what a typical apartment manager handles. Comfort with that regulatory environment, or the ability to get up to speed quickly, matters here.

What You'll Be Responsible For

The core of the job is operational management: rent collection, delinquency review, bi-monthly deposits, lease enforcement, and making sure community rules are upheld consistently. You'll oversee new resident applications, manage the on-site team through hiring, training, and performance reviews, and serve as the primary contact when residents bring concerns or grievances to the office.

The financial side of the role includes reviewing receivables, monitoring performance against budget, and identifying where efficiency or profitability can improve. On the compliance side, you'll coordinate with local agencies and law enforcement as needed, prepare required regulatory reports, and maintain Fair Housing standards across all operations.

  • 1 or more years managing a manufactured housing or multifamily community of 100-plus units
  • Demonstrated experience with rent collection and delinquency management
  • Comfort with property management software and basic accounting systems
  • Strong conflict resolution skills and a customer service mindset suited to this community demographic
  • Marketing and leasing experience to support occupancy and lot/home availability
  • Valid driver's license required
  • Ability to live on site (a 2-bedroom, 2-bathroom manufactured home with a fenced backyard and storage shed is provided)

What Makes This Role Distinctive at IPG

Investment Property Group manages over 150 properties across 13 states, with a portfolio that spans multifamily, manufactured housing, and RV communities. That breadth matters for your career: managers who perform well at the community level have access to a real growth path within a company that's actively expanding its footprint.

On-site housing is included as part of the compensation package, which means your cost of living calculation looks different here than it would at a conventional apartment management role. The pay range of $26 to $30 per hour, combined with provided housing, positions this competitively for the Loveland market. The schedule is Monday through Friday, 8am to 5pm, which is a meaningful quality-of-life detail in a sector where weekend and after-hours demands are common.

What separates strong candidates from average ones in this role is the ability to stay even-keeled when the day breaks differently than planned. Manufactured housing residents often have longer tenancy histories and stronger community ties than typical apartment residents. Managing those relationships well, while still enforcing lease terms and maintaining financial performance, is where experienced community managers earn their standing.

workable_6072873.title: Resident Manager
workable_6072873.rewritten_description:
What You'll Actually Do

This role sits at the center of resident life at a Flats community in Chicago. You're the main point of contact from the moment a prospect walks in the door through the day they hand back their keys. That means leasing, renewals, move-ins, move-outs, and everything in between. You'll report to the Property Manager and supervise leasing consultants on site.

On the leasing side, you'll manage the full pipeline: tours, follow-up, lease execution, and conversion tracking. You'll stay current on pricing, availability, and any concessions in play, and you'll monitor traffic and lead sources closely enough to adjust strategy when numbers slip. Marketing support is part of the job too, including social media presence and responding to online reviews in a way that actually reflects well on the community.

On the resident side, you'll own the experience after move-in. That includes a 48-hour move-in follow-up, handling questions and amenity reservations, coordinating resident events, and running renewal outreach before leases go month-to-month. When residents give notice, you'll process it in Yardi, schedule the walkthrough, and coordinate with maintenance to keep turns on track and vacancy loss low. Make-ready timelines matter here. A slow punch list costs real money.

An active Illinois Leasing License is required for this role.

What You Bring

  • Active Leasing License (Illinois)
  • Experience in property management, hospitality, or a customer-facing service role
  • Working knowledge of Yardi or comparable property management software
  • Strong follow-through on leasing pipeline and renewal tracking
  • Clear, professional communication with residents, prospects, and internal teams
  • Ability to manage competing priorities without dropping the ball on documentation

A Few Things Worth Knowing

Flats positions itself as a tech-forward, experience-driven operator. That means residents arrive with high expectations. They've seen the brand, read the reviews, and expect someone responsive on the other end when something goes wrong. The 48-hour move-in follow-up isn't just a checkbox. It tends to be where early friction either gets resolved or turns into a bad review two weeks later.

This is a fully on-site role. No hybrid option exists. If you've come from a management style that relies on flexibility around hours and location, that's worth factoring in. Resident-facing work runs on the community's schedule, not yours.

For candidates thinking about where this goes: the Resident Manager role at a company with Flats' structure is a direct path toward a Property Manager position. You're already doing most of the operational work. The next step is full P&L ownership and broader team leadership. Candidates who pay close attention to NOI drivers, not just occupancy, tend to move faster into that seat.

smartrecruiters_744000147061919.title: Regional Property Manager - Atlanta Market
smartrecruiters_744000147061919.rewritten_description:
Where Financial Acumen and People Leadership Meet

Regional property management is one of those roles where the skills you sharpen don't stay siloed. Reading a T-12, coaching a Community Manager through a tough delinquency month, and pushing occupancy in a competitive market all pull from the same core: pattern recognition, influence, and accountability. This role with AIR Communities in Atlanta asks you to do all of that across a portfolio of apartment communities, and to do it consistently enough that it compounds into something real.

AIR Communities operates in major markets with a reputation for running high-quality assets. The Atlanta Regional Property Manager position means you're responsible for the financial and operational performance of multiple communities. You're setting direction on budgets, revenue growth, and NOI while also staying close enough to leasing activity and resident satisfaction to catch problems before they show up in the numbers. The portfolio has Community Managers in place, and developing those managers is central to the job. The expectation is that you build the team's capacity, not just respond to gaps.

The Skills This Role Sharpens Most

Multi-site leadership accelerates certain skills faster than almost any other role in property management. You'll develop fluency in reading operational data across properties simultaneously, spotting which site needs a pricing adjustment versus which one has a maintenance backlog dragging satisfaction scores. A few specific capabilities this role will deepen:

  • Budget oversight across multiple assets, with direct accountability for revenue targets and expense control
  • Sales process coaching, helping leasing teams use metrics and traffic data to close more effectively
  • Platform proficiency across tools like OneSite, SmartRent, and Salesforce in a real operational context
  • Leading diverse teams through performance conversations, coaching cycles, and high-turnover stretches
  • Compliance and legal standard adherence across a multi-property footprint

Candidates who succeed here typically arrive with at least five years in property management or a high-performance service environment, and at least five years leading sizable teams through competitive, results-measured work. Hospitality and retail backgrounds translate well if the fundamentals are sharp, but the financial layer of this role requires genuine comfort with budgets, not just familiarity with the vocabulary.

What's Distinctive About This Position

AIR's model leans toward institutional discipline. They own and operate, which means Regional Managers work within a structure that has real capital behind it and clear performance expectations. For a Regional with ambitions beyond Atlanta, that context matters: you're building a track record at a company where operational results are visible and career development is explicitly supported through training programs, tuition reimbursement, and certification funding.

The Atlanta multifamily market has enough submarkets and Class A supply pressure to make this a genuinely demanding portfolio to run. Strong candidates will read that as interesting rather than intimidating. The compensation range of $120,000 to $130,000 base plus bonus reflects the level of accountability involved, and the full benefits package includes a 401(k) with a 6% employer contribution and paid parental leave of up to 16 weeks.

From a career arc standpoint, Regional Manager roles at well-capitalized operators like AIR tend to position people well for VP of Operations, Director-level roles, or ownership-side asset management. The skills you'll sharpen here: multi-site P&L accountability, talent development, and performance culture creation, transfer cleanly into any senior leadership path in multifamily.

greenhouse_5411491008.title: Assistant Maintenance Manager
greenhouse_5411491008.rewritten_description:
Assistant Maintenance Manager roles at Bozzuto properties carry real weight. You're not just turning wrenches. You're helping set the standard for how the building runs, how the team performs, and how residents experience the place they call home. At a company that manages Class A communities across multiple markets, that standard is consistently high.

What This Role Actually Involves

The core of this job is hands-on technical work combined with team leadership. On any given day, that might mean diagnosing an HVAC issue in one unit, walking a make-ready punch list in another, and following up with a resident whose service ticket has been open too long. The work spans HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and appliance repair, with additional exposure to complex mechanical systems like central plant equipment, chillers, and boilers. Preventative maintenance scheduling, grounds upkeep, and maintaining code compliance are all part of the routine.

The supervisory side matters just as much. You'll be expected to motivate others, hold the team to Bozzuto's maintenance standards, and model the kind of professionalism that keeps a property running smoothly. This isn't a role where technical skill alone carries you. You have to communicate clearly, document thoroughly, and earn the trust of both the people above you and the technicians around you.

Spanish and English bilingual ability is preferred, which reflects the Miami market. Being able to communicate directly with residents in their preferred language speeds up service and builds real rapport.

What the Job Actually Asks of You

  • 5 or more years in the trades, residential maintenance, or facilities management
  • HVAC, EPA, and/or NAPE certification
  • Working knowledge of OSHA standards and risk management practices
  • Comfort with Microsoft Office and property management technology platforms
  • Physical ability to lift 25 to 50 pounds frequently and work in varying outdoor conditions
  • Availability for an emergency on-call rotation, including weekends

The on-call rotation deserves a straightforward mention. After-hours calls come with this role. Emergencies don't wait for Monday morning, and part of being in a leadership position at a residential property means you're reachable when something goes wrong at 11 PM. That's the honest reality of this level of maintenance management, and it's worth factoring into your decision.

Where This Can Take You

The Assistant Maintenance Manager role is a recognized stepping stone in residential property management. Technicians who develop both their trade depth and their leadership skills at this level routinely move into Maintenance Manager and Chief Engineer positions, particularly at larger or more complex assets. Bozzuto's scale as a company means internal mobility is a real option, not just something listed in a job posting.

The compensation for this position starts at $57,000, with additional bonus opportunities. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, 20 days of paid time off plus holidays, a 401k with company match, and tuition reimbursement for continued development.

greenhouse_4355221009.title: Centralized Painter, IFM - Orlando, FL
greenhouse_4355221009.rewritten_description:
Cortland runs a centralized painting operation across its multifamily portfolio in Orlando, and this role sits inside that IFM (Integrated Facilities Management) structure. You're not assigned to a single community. You move between properties, covering unit turns, touch-ups, and surface repairs wherever the workload demands it.

What You'll Actually Do

The daily expectation is straightforward: complete one full-unit repaint or two touch-up units per day, depending on the turn schedule. That means prep, prime, and finish, not just rolling walls. You'll also handle drywall patching, sanding, and texture matching as part of the make-ready process. Spray equipment is part of the job, and you're expected to maintain it, not just use it.

Between units, you're responsible for keeping your paint shop organized, stocked, and safe. OSHA protocols and MSDS compliance aren't optional extras here. Cortland tracks work through a CMMS, so logging completed tasks and material usage is part of your daily close-out.

You'll coordinate with Service Managers on scheduling and priorities. When something affects your timeline, whether it's a material shortage or an access issue, you raise it early. Reliability and independent judgment matter in this role because there often isn't a supervisor on-site with you.

What You Bring

  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • 2 or more years of interior residential painting experience; custom home background is a plus
  • Solid skills with brush, roller, and spray application, including proper spray prep
  • Ability to perform small drywall repairs and texture matching; comfort with larger repairs is a bonus
  • Valid driver's license with required vehicle insurance, you'll travel between properties regularly
  • Working knowledge of spray equipment maintenance, OSHA regulations, and elevated-work safety
  • Comfort working at heights using ladders, lifts, or scaffolding
  • Familiarity with CMMS software, or willingness to learn quickly
  • Availability for all shifts, including weekends when the turn schedule calls for it

A Note on This Type of Role

Centralized painting positions within large multifamily operators like Cortland tend to offer more consistent volume than property-level maintenance roles. Because you're covering a portfolio, the work stays steady rather than peaking and dropping with a single community's lease-up or renovation cycle. For painters who want predictable workload and don't mind windshield time between sites, that's a meaningful difference from a traditional on-site maintenance position. It also gives you exposure to a wide range of unit conditions and property types, which sharpens diagnostic and texture-matching skills faster than staying on one asset.

greenhouse_5228891007.title: Assistant Property Manager
greenhouse_5228891007.rewritten_description:
It's Tuesday morning, and a tenant on the third floor is flagging a maintenance issue while an operating expense reconciliation sits half-finished on your screen and a vendor invoice is waiting for your review before it can go to the property manager for approval. That's not a bad day. That's the job.

What This Role Actually Covers

Lincoln Property Company is looking for an Assistant Property Manager in Dallas to support day-to-day operations across commercial, industrial, or retail assets. This is a broad, hands-on role inside one of the largest private real estate firms in the country, managing more than 720 million square feet across its combined portfolio. You'll work closely with the property manager and engage directly with tenants, vendors, and internal accounting teams on a regular basis.

Core responsibilities include:

  • Responding to tenant needs and coordinating with building and administrative staff to resolve issues in line with lease obligations and company policy
  • Reviewing and recommending vendor invoice approvals within the parameters of the management agreement and authorization limits
  • Supporting monthly report and budget package preparation to meet client deadlines and accuracy standards
  • Collecting data and drafting CAM and operating expense reconciliations in coordination with accounting
  • Handling lease administration tasks including setup, amendments, and system updates
  • Coordinating and documenting tenant move-ins and move-outs, including walk-throughs with tenants and tenant improvement teams
  • Assisting with vendor sourcing, bid coordination, and procurement support
  • Contributing to emergency response planning and participating in required drills
  • Providing work direction and performance feedback to direct reports where applicable

This is a fully in-office position based in Dallas. Property inspections are part of the routine, so expect to be on your feet and at the asset, not just behind a desk.

What You Bring and What You'll Build

The role requires a working knowledge of financial terms and concepts, including the ability to run basic financial analysis and calculate figures like percentages accurately. Intermediate to advanced proficiency with Microsoft Office is expected. Familiarity with AP systems and CMMS platforms is a plus, as is prior exposure to commercial office, retail, or industrial properties. Strong written and verbal communication skills matter here, because you'll be the face of the management team in a lot of tenant interactions. A bachelor's degree is preferred, though relevant experience combined with education is also considered. One to two years of related experience is the baseline.

What this role builds is equally worth naming. CAM reconciliation work is a skill set that carries real weight in commercial property management and opens doors to senior PM and portfolio roles. Strong candidates coming out of this position tend to move into full property manager responsibilities, particularly those who develop fluency across lease administration, financial reporting, and vendor management at the same time. The professionals who distinguish themselves here are the ones who own the administrative details with the same attention they bring to tenant relationships. Both sides of that equation matter at Lincoln.

Lincoln supports career development through mentorship, training programs, and a culture that encourages initiative within a structured platform. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, 401(k) options (traditional and Roth), flexible time off, and company-paid life insurance and long-term disability, among other offerings.

greenhouse_6177734004.title: Regional Manager, Affordable Housing
greenhouse_6177734004.rewritten_description:
What You'll Actually Do

This role sits above the property level, which means your days look different from a site manager's but the accountability doesn't shrink. You're overseeing a portfolio of affordable housing communities across the Los Angeles area, which means your week will move between file reviews, physical inspections, budget variance conversations, and one-on-ones with Community Managers who need guidance on everything from delinquency to recertification timelines.

The affordable housing piece carries real regulatory weight. LIHTC compliance isn't something you hand off. You're monitoring application and annual recertification processes, ensuring proper Section 8 procedures are followed, and interfacing directly with regulatory agencies when needed. File reviews happen regularly, and semi-annual physical inspections are part of the job. If a LIHTC file is out of order or a unit fails inspection, the fallout lands on your portfolio.

On the financial side, you're developing yearly operating budgets, reviewing monthly income and expense variances, and pushing toward the highest possible NOI through cost control and revenue management. You'll also weigh in on capex recommendations and monitor large vendor contracts and work in progress at your sites. Ownership financial reports need to be accurate and delivered on time. That's a standard you enforce, not just track.

Personnel management takes up more of your bandwidth than some Regional roles. You screen, hire, coach, and when necessary, terminate site staff. You approve timesheets, sign off on salary requests for Community Managers, and make sure counseling statements and written evaluations are properly documented and routed to HR. Affordable housing communities often carry leaner staffing than conventional Class A properties, so when a site is short-handed, you feel it.

What You Bring

  • Direct experience with LIHTC compliance, including recertification processes and regulatory reporting
  • Working knowledge of Section 8 / HUD program requirements
  • Demonstrated ability to manage multi-site portfolios as an off-site leader
  • Experience developing and managing operating budgets, with the ability to explain variances in writing
  • Strong personnel management background, including hiring, performance documentation, and terminations
  • Familiarity with fair housing law, EHO requirements, and affirmative fair housing obligations
  • Ability to manage emergency response situations and coordinate with on-site staff and ownership

What to Expect Going In

Asset Living is a large third-party management firm, which means you're operating within established systems and reporting upward to a Senior Vice President. The structure is there, but affordable housing regional work in Los Angeles carries its own challenges. The regulatory environment in California is dense, agencies scrutinize compliance closely, and the resident base has real needs that don't pause for business hours. Emergency situations pull you in regardless of the calendar.

What separates strong candidates here is the combination of LIHTC fluency and genuine management instinct. Plenty of people understand the compliance piece. Fewer can also hold a Community Manager accountable for leasing performance, push back on a vendor invoice, and write a clear monthly budget narrative for ownership. The candidate who lasts in this role handles all three without treating any of them as secondary.

greenhouse_7983406003.rewritten_description:
Olympus Property has earned a reputation as one of the better operators to work for in multifamily, and their Business Manager role at Auburn Lakes in Spring, TX reflects what that actually looks like day to day. This is a full property management position where you own the financials, the team, and the resident experience at a luxury Class A community.

Spring sits in the northwest Houston corridor, a submarket that's seen consistent population growth tied to the energy sector and corporate relocations along the Grand Parkway. Class A communities in this pocket compete hard on amenity quality and service reputation, which means occupancy and renewal performance here depends less on price concessions and more on execution. A Business Manager who understands that dynamic will approach resident retention and leasing programs differently than someone coming from a value-add or Class B background.

On the financial side, you'll carry real accountability. That means building annual business plans, managing to budget, and analyzing monthly performance alongside your Regional Manager and Regional VP. You'll review T-12 trends, track NOI, and know why delinquency is moving in either direction before leadership asks. This isn't a support role that reports upward. You're expected to bring analysis and solutions together.

Day to day, you're moving between office staff and maintenance, making sure the leasing team is sharp on sales and marketing execution while the maintenance team is keeping units market-ready and common areas in condition that reflects the property's positioning. You'll bid and negotiate vendor contracts, conduct property inspections, and step in for resident events or emergencies when the schedule calls for it. The hours are generally Monday through Friday with flexibility built in, which is typical for this level of role at a well-staffed community.

What separates strong candidates here is the ability to coach a team without micromanaging it. At a luxury property with competitive occupancy goals, your leasing staff needs to be sharp and motivated, not supervised at every step. Business Managers who thrive in this environment build accountability into their team culture rather than carrying the whole operation themselves.

What Olympus is looking for

  • At least two years of direct multifamily property management experience, with luxury or Class A background preferred
  • Comfort with RealPage, Knock, or Onesite software
  • Demonstrated ability to manage budgets, read financials, and contribute to asset-level planning
  • Experience leading and developing both office and maintenance teams
  • Availability for a full-time Monday through Friday schedule with flexibility for events and emergencies

The base pay range sits at $75,000 to $78,000 annually, with monthly commissions and quarterly and annual bonuses layered on top. Olympus also offers a benefits package that includes medical, dental and vision coverage, 401(k) with employer matching, tuition reimbursement, an apartment rental allowance, and sabbatical eligibility, among other options.

greenhouse_8170973.title: Groundskeeper
greenhouse_8170973.rewritten_description:
Weinstein Properties has been family-owned for over 70 years, operating more than 60 apartment communities across Virginia, North Carolina, Texas, Tennessee, and Georgia. The Addison at Swift Creek community in Midlothian is looking for a Groundskeeper to join the on-site team. This is a Monday through Friday, 8am to 5pm position, which is genuinely one of the better schedules in residential property management for an hourly role.

The work is physical and repetitive, and Weinstein says so plainly before you ever apply. You'll pick up trash and pet waste daily. You'll trash out vacant units. You'll use backpack blowers, power washers, and a golf cart or trailer to move around the property. Some days you'll do light painting or housekeeping tasks. You'll be outside year-round, which in central Virginia means hot, humid summers and cold, wet winters. Lifting up to 50 pounds regularly is part of the routine, not the exception. If that's the kind of work you find satisfying, this role has real merit. If you're hoping it's mostly mowing and mulching in pleasant weather, it isn't.

What makes groundskeeper roles at communities like this one worth considering is the path forward. Weinstein has stated openly that they train people into Maintenance Technician roles. That's a meaningful step up in pay, skill set, and long-term career options. The groundskeeper position is where a lot of solid maintenance techs get their start because they spend time learning the property, building relationships with the maintenance team, and developing habits around proactive care. If you come in with a good attitude and stick around, that trajectory is real.

Pay starts at $16.50 per hour with quarterly bonuses. There's also a $1,000 stay-on bonus available after 90 days in good standing. Benefits include health, dental, and vision insurance, a 401k, PTO, paid holidays, birthday time off, an Employee Assistance Program, and a rent discount if you live at a Weinstein community.

Strong candidates for this role:

  • Show up on time, consistently, without needing to be followed up on
  • Take initiative when they see something that needs attention, without waiting to be told
  • Handle repetitive, unglamorous tasks without cutting corners
  • Communicate well with the maintenance and leasing teams and pitch in when needed
  • Are genuinely open to learning maintenance skills over time

No specific experience is required. What Weinstein is selecting for is reliability and work ethic. If you've got those, the rest can be taught.

A prospective resident walks in on a Saturday morning, unannounced, with a list of questions and a tight move-in timeline. How you handle that next thirty minutes determines whether they sign or keep shopping. That's the core of this role.

What the Job Actually Involves

Hawthorne Residential Partners is hiring a Leasing Consultant (internally called a Leasing and Live It Specialist) for their community at 10 Perimeter Drive in Atlanta. The job sits at the front line of leasing operations: greeting prospects, conducting tours, fielding inquiries by phone, email, and web, and moving leads through the funnel to a signed lease. You'll handle applications, verification paperwork, and move-in documentation with accuracy.

Beyond the leasing cycle, this role carries a resident-facing component. You'll help coordinate and attend community events, respond to resident concerns, and keep the leasing office and common areas presentable. You'll also assist with social media and local outreach to support property marketing, and you'll stay current on competitor properties and local market conditions.

The office runs Monday through Friday, 9 AM to 6 PM, and Saturdays from 10 AM to 4 PM. You'll get one weekday off each week to keep the schedule at 40 hours. Some evenings and weekends may come up around resident events.

  • High school diploma or GED
  • Valid driver's license
  • CALP certification is a plus
  • Comfortable communicating in person, on the phone, and in writing
  • Able to handle objections and follow up consistently without being pushy
  • Open to coaching and learning company-specific processes

Compensation includes an hourly base plus monthly leasing and renewal commissions, and leasing incentive programs. Benefits include medical, vision, and dental coverage, a 401k match, paid time off (including your birthday), paid parental and adoption leave, pet insurance, telehealth access, and company-paid life insurance.

Hawthorne runs a formal career path program. Leasing Consultant is a real entry point into multifamily management, and the internal track to Assistant Community Manager is well-defined. If you want to move into property operations and eventually take on a site leadership role, this is a practical first step with a company that has the scale to promote from within.
