greenhouse_4730651005.rewritten_description:
Leasing is a high-contact, high-turnover function at most apartment communities. The consultant role exists because occupancy doesn't manage itself. Someone has to answer the phone, run the tour, close the application, and follow up after move-in. At Lakeside Village Apartments in Clinton Township, Paragon Properties is filling that seat.

What the Job Actually Involves

This is a full-cycle leasing position. You're handling traffic from first contact through signed lease, which means phone and email inquiries, in-person tours, application processing, and move-in paperwork. You'll also stay involved after the lease is signed: work order follow-up, renewal conversations, and resident retention are all part of the scope. Community inspections, model apartments, and vacant units need to meet standards before prospects ever walk through the door, and keeping that in order falls to you too.

Beyond the leasing desk, you'll support site marketing and outreach to local businesses and employers, and help plan and attend resident events. It's a broad role for a single title.

The schedule is guaranteed full-time at 40 hours per week. Starting pay is $18.50 per hour, negotiable based on prior leasing experience. The company offers move-in bonuses, a rent discount, 401(k) with employer contribution, medical/dental/vision with a short waiting period, and paid life and disability insurance. Nine paid holidays and PTO are included.

Who Fits This Role

  • At least one year in a customer service or sales role; six-plus months of on-site leasing experience preferred
  • High school diploma required; some college coursework preferred
  • Comfortable with MS Office (Word, Excel, Outlook); Yardi experience is a plus
  • Working knowledge of Fair Housing regulations preferred
  • Strong attention to detail and the ability to manage multiple tasks during busy traffic periods

Pre-employment background check, drug screening, and physical are required before start.

The candidates who do well in this kind of role tend to be the ones who treat the phone lead with the same energy as the walk-in. Plenty of consultants are good in person and let their phone and email conversion slip. Consistent follow-through across every touchpoint is what separates average occupancy numbers from strong ones. If you've got the sales instinct and the follow-up habit, there's real room to grow here into a senior leasing or assistant manager track.

greenhouse_5414015008.rewritten_description:
Hillpointe builds and operates market-rate workforce housing across the Sun Belt, and they do it vertically integrated from land acquisition through asset management. That context matters for this role. When a new community opens, this team is involved in stabilization. The Maintenance Supervisor here isn't inheriting a 10-year-old property with established systems. There's a real chance you're helping get a community dialed in from the start.

What You'll Actually Do

Day to day, you're running the maintenance operation at a Palm Coast community. Service requests, preventative maintenance, make-ready turns on vacant units, punch list inspections, grounds and amenity appearance. You'll supervise vendors and contractors and be accountable for the quality of their work, not just your own. Inventory management falls to you too, keeping supplies stocked without blowing the budget.

The on-call rotation is real. Evenings, weekends, after-hours emergencies. That's not unique to Hillpointe, that's the job. Worth saying plainly rather than burying it.

Because Hillpointe is actively developing communities, there's a secondary piece: you may be pulled in to help with new property setups and stabilization as projects come online. If you've done lease-up maintenance work before, you already know what that phase looks like. If you haven't, expect a steeper initial learning curve.

What You Bring

  • EPA Type I and II or Universal certification for refrigerant recycling (required)
  • CPO certification or willingness to obtain it
  • Valid driver's license
  • All state and local certifications required by jurisdiction
  • Competency with hand tools, power tools, and mechanical equipment
  • Comfort with basic office software for work order management
  • High school diploma, GED, or equivalent hands-on experience
  • Physical ability to lift up to 50 lbs regularly, work at heights, and perform in outdoor Florida conditions year-round

A Note on What Separates Strong Candidates

We've seen plenty of maintenance techs who are excellent with their hands but struggle with the supervision side. This role carries real oversight responsibility. You're inspecting vendor work, holding contractors accountable, and training new staff. The candidates who thrive here know how to communicate expectations clearly, document what they see, and follow through. Technical skills get you in the door. The supervisory piece is what determines whether you're effective in this seat long term. Prior lead or supervisor experience in multifamily makes a meaningful difference.

Palm Coast sits in Flagler County, a market that's grown quickly with new residential development. Workforce housing demand here is genuine, and Hillpointe's Sun Belt focus puts them squarely in that trend. For a maintenance professional who wants to be part of a growing portfolio rather than a static one, the timing is reasonable.

greenhouse_6178330004.title: Maintenance Technician at Morgan Ridge Apartments
greenhouse_6178330004.rewritten_description:
Maintenance work at an apartment community runs on a specific set of skills used daily: HVAC troubleshooting, basic plumbing and electrical repairs, carpentry, and the kind of calm problem-solving that kicks in when a resident's heat goes out at 11 PM. Morgan Ridge Apartments in Winston-Salem is hiring a Maintenance Technician who brings those skills to the job and can apply them consistently across a full residential property.

What the Work Actually Involves

The bulk of your days will be service requests: diagnosing and repairing issues in occupied units across plumbing, electrical, and general carpentry. HVAC troubleshooting will come up often, and candidates with EPA Type II or Universal certification will find that background directly applicable. CPO certification is a plus if pool maintenance is part of the property's scope.

The physical side of this role is real and worth knowing upfront. You'll be on your feet most of the day, climbing stairs and ladders, working in tight spaces, and lifting up to 50 lbs. That's routine, not occasional. You'll also carry on-call rotation responsibilities, meaning after-hours emergency calls are part of the job. The Service Manager provides support during those calls, which matters when something complicated comes up at an inconvenient hour, but you'll still need to be reachable and ready to respond.

A valid driver's license is required. Strong English communication skills are necessary for resident interactions and for accurately processing work orders and safety documentation.

Where Strong Candidates Stand Out

Most applicants can handle basic repairs. What separates a solid maintenance tech from an average one at a residential property is HVAC competency and the ability to troubleshoot before calling for outside help. A tech who can accurately diagnose a refrigerant issue, a faulty capacitor, or a drainage problem saves the property time and money, and keeps residents from waiting days for a fix. If you have hands-on HVAC experience and can back it up, that's where you'll distinguish yourself here.

Working at Cottonwood Residential

Cottonwood operates its communities with a service focus that extends to how residents first encounter the property. They were early to implement self-guided tours, which reflects an operational style that doesn't wait for industry consensus before trying something practical. For maintenance staff, that culture tends to mean clearer processes and a team that takes the resident experience seriously rather than treating it as overhead.

Benefits are available starting within 30 days of hire and include health, vision, dental, life, and disability coverage. The company offers a 401k and HSA match, three weeks of paid time off in the first year, and 10.5 paid holidays.

  • EPA Type II or Universal certification preferred
  • CPO certification a plus
  • Considerable HVAC troubleshooting experience required
  • Valid driver's license required
  • On-call availability required, with Service Manager support

greenhouse_5415634008.title: Leasing Agent
greenhouse_5415634008.rewritten_description:
It's 10 a.m. on a Saturday and your phone has already pulled in three new inquiries from the weekend push. You've got two tours lined up by noon and a move-in packet to finalize before you leave the Greensburg office. That's a normal morning here.

The Role

Birgo is hiring a leasing agent based out of their Greensburg office, covering communities in Greensburg and one property in New Kensington. Administrative work stays centralized, but this is a road-and-property role: you're out meeting prospects, conducting showings, and walking new residents through move-in. The portfolio includes both market-rate and Section 8 units, so you'll need to be comfortable with Fair Housing compliance as a baseline, not an afterthought.

Day-to-day, you're the first voice a prospective resident hears. You're converting inquiries to tours, tours to applications, and applications to completed move-ins with inspections documented and nothing left on the punch list. You'll keep listings current, monitor ad performance, and coordinate with property management and maintenance to protect occupancy. Tenant care doesn't stop at the lease signing; part of this role is building the kind of rapport that keeps renewals off the delinquency radar before they ever get there.

Compensation is structured as an $18/hour base with performance commissions on top, with on-target earnings ranging from $46,000 to $70,000 annually. The benefits package includes medical, dental, vision, pet, and life insurance with a company contribution, a 401(k) with employer match, paid time off, sick time, mental health days, mileage reimbursement, a profit-sharing program, a professional development stipend, and a healthy lifestyle reimbursement. Birgo also offers discounted rates at their own properties.

What Birgo Is Looking For

  • At least one year of leasing experience preferred; strong candidates from sales, hospitality, or customer service will be considered
  • Familiarity with Fair Housing principles and multifamily leasing basics
  • Experience with property management or leasing software is a plus
  • High school diploma required
  • Valid driver's license, insured vehicle, and willingness to travel between sites
  • Availability for some evenings and weekends
  • Comfort working on-site; limited remote flexibility

The candidates who do well here aren't the ones running a script. Birgo has stated explicitly they value genuine service over polished sales tactics, and in a mixed market-rate and Section 8 portfolio, that matters. Prospects for affordable units often have more questions, more anxiety about the process, and more to lose if something goes sideways at move-in. The leasing agents who build real occupancy in these communities are the ones who actually follow through.

One thing to know before applying: because this position involves managing rentals on Birgo's behalf, the role prohibits concurrent outside real estate sales, leasing, or property management activity.

greenhouse_4392344009.title: Residential Porter - Ashburn, VA
greenhouse_4392344009.rewritten_description:
Comstock's ParkX division keeps a portfolio of mixed-use properties in Northern Virginia looking sharp, and this porter role sits at the front line of that effort. You're the person residents, guests, and staff see every day. How the property looks and feels reflects directly on your work.

What You'll Actually Do

The core of this job is keeping common areas clean and presentable on a consistent schedule. That means lobbies, restrooms, sidewalks, and public spaces , daily cleaning rounds, pressure washing as assigned, trash removal, and restocking supplies. You'll follow checklists and cleaning schedules set by the Senior Operations Manager, and you'll document what you find: supply levels, equipment issues, safety hazards, anything that needs a management decision.

Event support is part of the job too. When the property hosts gatherings, you'll help with setup and breakdown, and you'll handle any cleanliness issues that come up before, during, or after. Weekend and after-hours availability comes with the territory, especially during busy periods.

You'll also cover for coworkers when they're out, keep your janitorial closet organized and hazard-free, and complete end-of-shift documentation so the next person knows exactly where things stand.

What You Bring

  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • Valid driver's license with no major violations
  • Ability to lift up to 50 pounds and handle physical work across variable conditions (heat, cold, outdoor/indoor, chemical exposure)
  • Availability for weekends and after-hours as needed
  • Solid time management and the ability to work independently without constant direction
  • A professional, courteous manner with residents, guests, and staff
  • Attention to detail on checklists and documentation

A Few Things Worth Knowing

Ashburn is one of the faster-growing submarkets in the DC metro area. Comstock's ParkX properties in the region are mixed-use developments with active retail and residential traffic, which means this porter role sees more variety than a standard apartment community would. You're not just cleaning a hallway; you're maintaining shared spaces that hundreds of people move through on a daily basis.

The pay range for this position runs $15 to $17 per hour, with a benefits package that includes medical, dental, vision, 401(k) match, life insurance, parental leave, and an annual professional development fund. Comstock also notes genuine advancement opportunities within a growing portfolio, so for someone who wants to build a career in property operations, there's a path here beyond the porter role.

greenhouse_5228501007.title: Property Manager
greenhouse_5228501007.rewritten_description:
Managing three properties across a combined 94 units isn't a sprawling portfolio, but it's not a lightweight assignment either. At that scale, you're close enough to the operation to know every problem before it becomes a complaint, and accountable enough that there's nowhere to hide when things slip. This role with Property Management Associates fits that profile: a hands-on, live-on-site position covering conventional multifamily in Long Beach.

What the Day Actually Looks Like

Your morning probably starts with a walk. PMA puts real weight on preventative maintenance and daily property inspections, which means you're developing a feel for each asset rather than waiting for work orders to tell you what's wrong. From there, you're juggling leasing activity, coordinating maintenance staff and vendors, managing delinquency, and staying on top of reporting in Yardi Voyager. Voyager proficiency isn't a nice-to-have here. It's the operating system for the job.

Because you're living on-site, the line between work and off-hours is softer than most PM roles. On-call status and one weekend day per week come with the territory. That's an honest trade-off, and the compensation reflects it: $23 to $25 per hour, a free one-bedroom unit, and a $300 monthly auto allowance. A valid driver's license and proof of insurance are required.

What PMA Is Looking For

  • At least three years of conventional multifamily property management experience
  • Demonstrated proficiency with Yardi Voyager
  • Proven leasing and marketing ability, including closing traffic into signed leases
  • Experience supervising maintenance staff and scheduling vendors
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Solid command of Microsoft Office and general computer fluency
  • Valid driver's license with clean DMV record (DMV check is part of the screening process)
  • Ability to pass a background check and pre-employment physical

PMA has operated in the greater LA County market for over 30 years across residential and commercial assets. At a company that size, a manager who performs well on a 94-unit portfolio tends to have a clear path toward larger or more complex assignments. The structure here rewards people who treat the role like an owner would: watching the details, communicating proactively, and keeping occupancy and collections tight without waiting to be asked.

Full-time employees receive medical, dental, vision, and life insurance with employer contribution, a 401(k) with discretionary company match after one year, short and long-term disability coverage, supplemental plans, and paid vacation, holiday, and sick time.

greenhouse_4393319009.title: Maintenance Technician
greenhouse_4393319009.rewritten_description:
Berkshire Residential Investments runs an in-house management model, which means the maintenance team here isn't contracted out or rotating through a third-party vendor arrangement. You're part of the community itself. That context matters because it shapes how residents experience your work, and how you experience the job.

The Maintenance Technician role at Berkshire Main Street sits at the center of daily property life. Residents notice when things get fixed fast and done right. They also notice when curb appeal slips, when a work order drags, or when the person who showed up seemed like they'd rather be somewhere else. This role asks for genuine engagement with both the physical plant and the people living in it. That combination of technical competence and resident-facing warmth is harder to find than most job postings acknowledge.

Day to day, you'll handle the full range of maintenance needs across the community: plumbing, electrical, appliances, carpentry, and general building upkeep. You'll support management in keeping the property aligned with community standards, help maintain the shop and equipment, manage inventory, and take key security seriously. Curb appeal is part of the job too. A property that looks cared for tells residents something about how they'll be treated, and you're one of the people making that statement.

You'll also be someone teammates rely on. Maintenance work in a residential community doesn't happen in isolation. There's coordination with leasing, communication with management, and plenty of moments where a resident is stressed about something in their home and you're the person standing in front of them. Composure and a decent attitude go a long way.

What separates a strong candidate here from someone who's technically qualified but a poor fit: the willingness to take ownership. Berkshire's in-house model means the property's condition reflects directly on the people who work there. Technicians who treat their community like their own tend to do better work, build stronger resident relationships, and move into lead or supervisor roles faster.

What you'll bring

  • At least one year of hands-on maintenance experience in a residential or similar setting
  • Working knowledge across appliances, plumbing, electrical, carpentry, and general building systems
  • Comfort with basic computer use and written communication in English
  • Reliability, attention to detail, and the ability to shift priorities without losing track of open work orders

Berkshire offers three weeks of vacation, personal development support, a 25% rent discount, and solid insurance coverage. The company's ownership of its own assets means there's real investment in the teams who keep those properties running well.

greenhouse_4393461009.title: Leasing Specialist - Part-Time
greenhouse_4393461009.rewritten_description:
Redstone Residential runs a large book of business: more than 38,000 beds across 20 states, split between student housing and conventional multi-family. They're one of the bigger third-party student housing operators in the country, and their conventional portfolio is growing. This part-time leasing role sits at their Logan, Utah community and pays $18.00 per hour with performance bonuses on top.

The day-to-day is front-desk focused. You'll greet prospects and residents, handle package intake, keep the lobby running smoothly, and answer questions as they come in. When the leasing team needs support, you step in: tours, application processing, and whatever else moves traffic through the door. The role is part-time, so the hours flex, but the expectation around reliability and consistency doesn't.

Entrata experience helps. A lot of student housing operators run on it, and Redstone is no exception. If you've used other property management software, that background transfers. If you haven't used any, be upfront about it.

Student housing leasing has a rhythm that's different from conventional. Prospects often tour with parents, leasing cycles compress into a short window, and move-in periods hit hard. If you've worked retail, hospitality, or any customer-facing role where the pace spikes without warning, that experience reads well here. The ability to stay composed when three people need something at once is genuinely useful in this setting.

Qualifications

  • 1 to 2 years of customer service or sales experience
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills
  • Basic computer proficiency: email, correspondence, data entry
  • Familiarity with Entrata or similar PM software (preferred, not required)
  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • Calm and dependable under pressure

This kind of role tends to be a starting point. Leasing specialists who learn the software, get comfortable with the sales process, and show up consistently are the ones who move into full-time leasing or assistant manager positions. Redstone has the portfolio size to make that path real rather than hypothetical.

greenhouse_4393594009.rewritten_description:
What You'll Actually Do

This role covers two adjacent affordable communities in Livermore: Chestnut Square Senior and Chestnut Square Family. That dual-site setup means your day moves. Income verification appointments, lease processing, waitlist management, recertifications, bank deposits, and turn scheduling can all land in the same week. MidPen operates under TCAC and HUD compliance frameworks, so familiarity with MOR reviews, welfare exemptions, and tax credit recertification timelines will matter here. Compliance paperwork in affordable housing doesn't forgive shortcuts.

Beyond the desk work, you'll do regular property walks to flag maintenance and security issues, coordinate work orders with facilities staff, and keep resident and property files organized without letting confidential information slip. You'll also be a point of contact for emergency preparedness communications and resident meeting logistics. MidPen's property management team works closely with their onsite Resident Services staff, which is a meaningful difference from conventional market-rate operations. You'll have support, but you're also expected to carry your weight independently.

What You Bring

  • At least one year of residential property management, administrative, or customer service experience (or an equivalent combination)
  • High school diploma or GED
  • Comfort with MS Office; RealPage experience is a plus
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, especially under pressure
  • Detail orientation that holds up during recertification season
  • Genuine alignment with affordable housing as a mission, not just a job category

Context Worth Knowing

Affordable housing compliance is a discipline of its own. Candidates who've only worked conventional market-rate properties often underestimate how different the documentation burden is. Tax credit properties run on strict income and occupancy rules, and annual TCAC reviews reward thorough file management. If you've worked affordable, you already know this. If you're making the transition from market-rate, the learning curve is real but manageable with the right attitude toward process.

The pay range for this position runs from $21.15 to $23.80 hourly, based on experience. MidPen offers a full benefits package including health, dental, vision, life and disability coverage, a 403(b) retirement plan, paid parental leave, employee education reimbursement, FSA options, an EAP, and pet insurance, among others.

For an assistant-level candidate with some affordable housing exposure, this is a solid foundation. ACMs who build strong compliance and resident relations skills here have a clear path toward Community Manager roles, particularly within a portfolio as large as MidPen's across Northern California.

greenhouse_7985617003.title: Maintenance Technician II (Freewell, Carson, Raleigh, & Saltwood)
greenhouse_7985617003.rewritten_description:
Prometheus Real Estate Group runs a portfolio of over 13,000 apartments across the Bay Area, Portland, and Seattle, and they've been at it since 1965. That kind of tenure means their properties get maintained, not deferred. This Maintenance Technician II role covers four Portland communities: Freewell, Carson, Raleigh, and Saltwood. If you've worked multi-site before, you know the rhythm. If you haven't, expect to learn it quickly.

The work is bread-and-butter apartment maintenance. Turns, service requests, appliance repairs, plumbing, electrical, carpentry, painting. You'll troubleshoot major mechanical systems and handle minor repairs independently. Prometheus calls their residents "Neighbors," which signals something about how they expect you to treat people. Residents who feel ignored or dismissed will let you know about it, and you'll need to de-escalate that while still getting through your punch list. That's the real job.

On-call is part of this position. That's not buried in the fine print here. After-hours calls happen, and if you've been in apartment maintenance for more than a few months, you already know what that means for your personal schedule. The standby pay and on-call premium are real compensation for that time, not token gestures, but the expectation is genuine availability.

Prometheus is a vertically integrated company, which matters for a tech because capital improvement projects, value-add renovations, and lease-up activity all create additional work at the property level. There are bonus opportunities tied to some of these, including renovation and lease-up bonuses, which means a busy property can translate into more take-home pay.

What this role requires

  • Minimum two years of apartment maintenance experience
  • Hands-on competency across plumbing, electrical, carpentry, appliance repair, and painting
  • Ability to lift up to 50 lbs. and perform physically demanding work outdoors in varying conditions
  • Basic computer proficiency for work order systems
  • Availability for on-call rotations
  • High school diploma or GED

Pay runs $26.00 to $27.25 per hour, and the benefits package is genuinely strong. Prometheus covers 100% of medical, vision, and dental premiums for employees and eligible dependents, which stands out. There's a 401(k) with employer matching, a semi-annual discretionary bonus, paid volunteer time, and tenure-based housing discounts. They also offer tuition reimbursement, which matters if you're thinking about an HVAC certification or electrical license down the road.

One thing worth noting for candidates who are serious about growth: multi-site technician experience at a company with in-house renovation and development capabilities tends to build a broader skill set than a single-property position would. Techs who do turns efficiently, keep delinquency in maintenance work orders low, and communicate well with property managers often move into lead tech or maintenance supervisor roles faster than they expect. The exposure across four communities accelerates that.

greenhouse_4382508009.title: Groundskeeper
greenhouse_4382508009.location: Liam at Hays Farm - 401 Haysland Rd SW - Huntsville, AL - 35802
greenhouse_4382508009.rewritten_description:
Grounds work at a multifamily community is physical, visible, and immediate. Residents notice it every single day, and the skills it builds, attention to detail, familiarity with exterior systems, and an eye for curb appeal, carry forward into every maintenance role above it. At Liam at Hays Farm in Huntsville's growing south corridor near Jones Valley, Hawthorne Residential Partners is hiring a Groundskeeper to keep this community's exterior looking the part.

What This Role Actually Demands

The core skill here is observation. A good groundskeeper walks the property and registers what's off before anyone else does: a light out in a breezeway, debris collecting near the compactor, a pet station that needs attention, a pool deck that's lost its presentation. You won't be handed a checklist at 8 AM and left alone. You'll be expected to develop an instinct for what the property needs and act on it.

Day-to-day, that means cleaning and picking up debris throughout exterior areas, maintaining sidewalks, parking lots, and green spaces, and keeping amenity areas like courtyards, grilling stations, and pool decks clean and presentable. Light landscaping tasks like raking, trimming, and weeding come with the role, as does assisting the maintenance team with exterior touch-ups, bulb replacements, and make-ready support for vacant units when needed. You'll also help distribute resident communications and pitch in on seasonal prep and cleanup.

Who Fits This Role Well

  • Comfort working outdoors in variable Alabama weather, including summer heat
  • Some background in yardwork or general facility upkeep
  • A valid driver's license
  • Reliability and a consistent presence the team and residents can count on
  • Willingness to learn from the maintenance team and take direction without friction
  • A high school diploma or GED equivalent

Prior maintenance or HVAC experience is a plus, but Hawthorne has structured this as an entry point. The work ethic matters more than the resume here.

Where This Role Can Take You at Hawthorne

Hawthorne runs a formal Career Path Program, and the Groundskeeper role is explicitly positioned as a stepping stone toward Maintenance Technician I. That's a meaningful distinction. Many companies say they promote from within; Hawthorne builds that progression into their training infrastructure. If you want to expand into HVAC, plumbing, or electrical work over time, this is a legitimate place to start building toward those credentials while earning a paycheck.

Compensation includes hourly pay plus a monthly renewal bonus program. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401k with company match, paid time off (including your birthday), paid parental and adoption leave, pet insurance, telehealth access, and company-paid life insurance.

The schedule runs Monday through Friday, 8 AM to 5 PM, with participation in an on-call rotation for after-hours emergencies and occasional support for resident events when needed.

greenhouse_8784079002.title: Leasing Consultant
greenhouse_8784079002.rewritten_description:
Miami's rental market moves fast, and leasing consultants are the ones actually closing the gap between traffic and occupancy. Waypoint Management Services is hiring a Leasing Consultant to handle the full cycle: generating interest, qualifying prospects, executing leases, and keeping residents happy enough to renew. This is a sales role with a service wrapper, and the two have to coexist.

The Work Itself

You'll manage prospect relationships across every channel, phone, email, in-person tours, and follow-up sequences that actually move people toward a decision. That means knowing your floor plans cold, having a working read on the competitive set, and responding with enough urgency that leads don't go cold while the prospect shops three other communities down Brickell or Doral. Lease preparation, applicant qualification, proration calculations, and file assembly for manager approval all fall to you. So does keeping the leasing office, model, and amenity spaces tour-ready at all times. Waypoint also wants this person contributing to renewal activity and maintaining an organized waitlist, which means your occupancy impact extends well past the initial lease-up push.

Marketing outreach and referral networking are part of the role too, not an afterthought. If you've only ever waited for leads to come in through ILS traffic, you'll need to adjust that habit here.

Fair Housing compliance isn't optional. Waypoint expects you to know the regulations and apply them consistently, not just acknowledge that they exist.

What Waypoint Is Looking For

  • At least two years in leasing, sales, or a hospitality-facing role
  • Comfort managing the full leasing process, including financial calculations and lease documents
  • Familiarity with Yardi and CRM platforms (a plus, not a hard requirement)
  • Bilingual English/Spanish preferred, which in Miami is less a bonus and more a practical daily asset
  • Weekend availability for rotation
  • Valid driver's license
  • High school diploma or equivalent required

Compensation includes a competitive base wage, monthly leasing and renewal bonuses, a leaser-of-the-month monetary award, and an employee housing discount. greenhouse_4393407009.rewritten_description:
What This Role Actually Runs On

A Maintenance Supervisor at a smaller community (under 300 units) touches almost every part of daily operations. You're diagnosing HVAC issues in the morning, reviewing work order backlogs by midday, walking make-readies in the afternoon, and coaching a technician on punch list standards before end of shift. The skills this role draws on most heavily are prioritization, hands-on technical judgment, and the ability to develop people who may be earlier in their careers than you are.

Berkshire Residential Investments owns and manages its own properties, which means decisions move faster and accountability sits closer to the team on the ground. You're not waiting on a third-party owner to approve a capex item through three layers of approval. That structure gives a Maintenance Supervisor more direct influence over how the property runs, but it also means the expectations are real and the standards are your responsibility to uphold.

The Work Itself

You'll oversee the full service team, which means your job is as much about output quality as it is about wrench-turning. Scheduling daily activities, enforcing safety compliance, managing inventory and key security, and keeping the shop organized are baseline expectations. So is making sure tour routes and model units stay sharp. A prospective resident walking a model that looks neglected is a leasing problem, and the Maintenance Supervisor owns that.

You'll work closely with the Property Manager to maintain community standards and support budget awareness. Berkshire expects familiarity with property budgets and longer-range planning, so you should be comfortable thinking beyond the current work order queue.

  • At least 2 years of maintenance experience managing a residential community's service needs
  • At least 1 year leading or supervising a maintenance team
  • Comfort with technology and basic computer applications for work order and property management systems
  • Strong verbal and written communication in English

What Sets a Strong Candidate Apart Here

The candidates who thrive in this kind of role are the ones who treat coaching as part of the job, not a distraction from it. If your instinct when a tech makes a mistake is to fix it yourself and move on, this role will frustrate you. Berkshire's emphasis on team development means the Maintenance Supervisor is expected to mentor actively, set goals with staff, and model the behavior they want to see. Technical skill gets you in the door. How you develop the people around you determines how well you do here.

This posting is listed as a future opportunity at Angeline in Columbia City, Seattle. Columbia City is a dense, walkable neighborhood with a resident base that tends to have high service expectations. Responsiveness and communication with residents matter as much as technical execution in that kind of environment.

Berkshire offers three weeks of vacation, a 25% rent discount, and personal development plans. Those details are worth noting because they reflect a company that's at least trying to retain maintenance staff, which is often the hardest retention problem in property management.

greenhouse_5414310008.title: Apartment Maintenance Technician
greenhouse_5414310008.rewritten_description:
Fairstead operates a large affordable housing portfolio across 28 states, and this Maintenance Technician role in Fayetteville is a hands-on, boots-on-the-ground position. You'll be responsible for keeping a residential property running well for the people who actually live there. That means everything from routine work orders to make-readies to emergency calls that come in after hours.

What the Work Looks Like Day to Day

A typical week involves regular building and equipment inspections, completing preventative maintenance tasks before small problems become expensive ones, and handling repairs across plumbing, electrical, and HVAC systems. When a unit turns, you're helping get it ready for the next resident: cleaning, patching, checking appliances, working through the punch list until it's move-in ready. You'll also track supplies and maintain inventory so you're not scrambling for parts in the middle of a repair.

The on-call rotation is real. Affordable housing communities tend to have residents who depend heavily on the property team, and when something breaks after hours, someone has to show up. That's part of this role, and it's worth knowing upfront.

  • Inspect buildings and equipment on a regular schedule and flag issues before they escalate
  • Perform preventative and corrective maintenance as needed across the property
  • Check electrical systems for code compliance and safety systems monthly
  • Prepare vacant units for occupancy, including cleaning and repair work
  • Respond to emergency maintenance issues outside of normal business hours as part of the on-call rotation
  • Maintain accurate inventory of tools, equipment, and supplies

What Fairstead Is Looking For

You'll need prior experience as a service or maintenance technician, solid general maintenance skills, and enough electrical knowledge to diagnose and handle minor repairs safely. HVAC certification is preferred, not just a nice-to-have on paper. Physical requirements are straightforward: you'll be on your feet most of the day and need to lift up to 70 pounds without assistance.

The candidates who tend to stand out in roles like this are the ones who communicate clearly with residents and management alike. A lot of maintenance techs can fix things. Fewer can explain what they did and why, or flag a systemic problem before it gets buried in a backlog of work orders. If you're organized, keep clean notes, and treat residents with patience even when they're frustrated, you'll fit well here.

Company and Compensation

Fairstead brings development, construction, and property management together under one platform, which means the maintenance team isn't siloed. Benefits include medical coverage through Meritain Health with a generous employer contribution, employer-paid vision and life insurance, a 401(k) with company match (100% of the first 3%, 50% of the next 2%), 15 days of PTO, 7 sick days, and 12 or more paid holidays. Compensation is based on experience and market benchmarks for this location.

greenhouse_5416790008.title: Community Manager - Multi site - Van Mall North and Arborlane Apartments

Skills That Drive This Role

Multi-site community management runs on a specific combination of skills that single-property roles don't fully develop: rapid context-switching, strong financial literacy across multiple ledgers, and the kind of leadership that holds teams accountable without daily proximity. CloudTen Residential is hiring a Community Manager to oversee Van Mall North and Arborlane Apartments (formerly Corporate Woods) in Vancouver, WA, splitting time across both properties as operational needs shift. If you've managed delinquency curves, coached leasing staff, and kept occupancy healthy at more than one asset simultaneously, this role matches that experience directly.

Vancouver's rental market sits in an interesting position relative to Portland. Renters priced out of the west side increasingly cross the river, which keeps demand reasonably steady but also means pricing decisions matter. The ability to read traffic patterns, adjust concessions thoughtfully, and keep renewal rates strong through genuine resident engagement is something CloudTen will expect you to bring to both properties from day one.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Your week will distribute across both sites depending on what each property needs. Some days that means running inspections, reviewing make-ready timelines, and walking punch lists with maintenance. Other days it means sitting with leasing records, monitoring delinquency against State landlord-tenant requirements, and preparing budget notes for your Regional Manager. The financial side of this role is real: you'll oversee rent collection, complete daily bank deposits, monitor expenses against budget, and flag cost-saving opportunities before they become problems.

On the people side, you're responsible for hiring, training, and evaluating on-site staff at your assigned properties. That means building cohesive teams across two locations that may have different cultures, different needs, and different gaps. Fair Housing compliance, move-in and move-out protocol enforcement, and resident service response windows of 24 to 48 hours all fall under your watch. A valid driver's license is required given the travel between sites.

  • Two or more years of property management experience, with multi-site exposure a genuine plus
  • Working knowledge of State landlord-tenant law and Fair Housing regulations
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office and property management software platforms
  • High school diploma required; college coursework or a degree preferred
  • Strong accounting fundamentals: budgets, deposits, expense tracking, delinquency management
  • Self-directed and organized enough to manage priorities across locations without daily direction

What Makes CloudTen a Specific Fit

CloudTen operates a deliberately varied portfolio across the West, including hotel-to-residential conversions and high-rise lease-ups, which means their managers tend to build broader operational experience than peers at single-asset companies. The Portland metro group is established, and this role sits within a regional structure with a supervising Regional Manager providing oversight. Compensation is hourly in the $33 to $34 range depending on experience, with leasing bonus eligibility at the assigned properties. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, FSA access, company-paid life insurance, and paid vacation, sick leave, and holidays.

Candidates who tend to stand out in multi-site roles have one quality above all others: they build systems rather than relying on memory. When you're splitting time between two properties, the managers who succeed are those who create consistent processes their teams can execute independently, so that site performance doesn't drop the moment the manager is at the other location.

What You'll Actually Do

The Dream Montrose community in Houston runs on the work this role produces every day. Residents depend on it. As a Maintenance Technician here, you'll carry a full slate of responsibilities that go beyond fixing leaky faucets. You'll manage service requests on a 24-hour turnaround, respond to emergency calls during on-call rotation, and keep vacant units moving through a five-day turn cycle. That last point matters: five days from move-out to move-in ready means you're coordinating repairs, painting, appliance checks, plumbing, HVAC, drywall, and lock replacements on a real schedule, not an ideal one.

You'll also mentor and direct other members of the maintenance team, which means your interpersonal skills matter as much as your trade skills. Coaching a junior tech through a repair, communicating clearly with a frustrated resident, coordinating with a vendor while keeping costs in check , these are the human dynamics that fill a normal week. You'll manage the maintenance shop inventory, handle purchasing with an eye on cost control, and track security deposit dispositions. Groundskeeping and exterior cleanliness are part of the job too, not delegated away.

Dream Live Prosper properties sit in the affordable housing space, which carries real purpose. Residents here are counting on their homes being safe and functional. When something breaks, the stakes feel personal to them. That context shapes the service expectation in this role.

What You Bring

  • HVAC certification (required)
  • Hands-on experience with plumbing, electrical, and appliance repair
  • Demonstrated ability to complete apartment turns within five days
  • Plaster, drywall, and painting proficiency
  • Experience with lock replacement and basic hardware
  • Familiarity with both older and newer building systems
  • Valid driver's license, clean driving record, and a reliable personal vehicle
  • Your own basic tools
  • Comfort with budgeting and cost-control basics
  • Clear, practical communication skills with residents, vendors, and teammates

Property management experience is a plus, but trade competence and a steady, dependable work ethic will carry significant weight in the hiring decision.

Context Worth Knowing

This role carries a flexible schedule with nights and weekend availability required. That's honest. On-call rotations are part of maintenance work at any community, and this one is no different. If you've done apartment maintenance before, you already know what that means for your personal planning. If you're newer to the property side and coming from a trade background, it's worth factoring in before you apply.

For technicians who want to grow, this kind of role , where you're already managing team hours, coaching others, and touching budgets , is solid preparation for a Maintenance Supervisor or Facilities Manager position down the road. The combination of technical breadth and team leadership exposure is exactly what separates a journeyman tech from someone who moves into a senior or oversight role.

Dream Live Prosper has built its portfolio within the affordable housing segment, which tends to attract team members who find meaning in the work itself. If that kind of environment sounds like a good fit for how you operate, this is worth a closer look.

greenhouse_5417077008.title: Maintenance Supervisor - Roving - Pine Vista, Vogue Manor, Castilian and Las Palmas

greenhouse_5417077008.rewritten_description:
Roving maintenance roles exist because multi-family portfolios rarely distribute deferred work, turnover volume, or staffing gaps evenly across sites. Sunrise Management's solution is a Maintenance Supervisor who moves across four San Diego communities , Pine Vista, Vogue Manor, Castilian, and Las Palmas , plugging in where the need is highest on any given week. The role pays $29 to $31 per hour depending on experience.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

The core accountability is keeping four communities physically healthy and market-ready at the same time. Turns are a significant part of that. Sunrise expects make-ready apartments to be painted, cleaned, and punched out within three to five days of vacancy. At multiple sites simultaneously, hitting that window consistently requires real scheduling discipline and the ability to direct a crew without micromanaging every task.

Beyond turns, the day-to-day spans a wide range of trades: HVAC, plumbing, appliance repair, electrical, pool and spa maintenance, carpentry, and custodial work. Preventive maintenance runs on a monthly directive cycle covering lighting, fire safety, life and safety hazards, pool systems, and signage. You'll maintain the logs, track inventory across sites, and flag any capital-level repairs or deferred maintenance to the property manager. Emergency on-call service is part of the job. Service requests carry a 24-hour completion target, and when parts delay a repair, the expectation is proactive communication to both management and the resident , not silence.

Because this is a supervisory position, you'll also coordinate with site management teams on scheduling, assist with hiring and performance reviews for maintenance staff, and run monthly safety meetings. MSDS recordkeeping, PPE compliance, and adherence to Sunrise's hazard materials policies are non-negotiable. Fair Housing awareness applies to maintenance staff just as it does to leasing , you're expected to understand why that matters operationally.

What Separates Strong Candidates

The multi-site structure is where this role gets interesting and where underprepared candidates struggle. You won't have the luxury of owning one property's rhythm and settling in. Priorities shift depending on which site has the highest vacancy, the most urgent work orders, or the thinnest staffing. The strongest candidates here are the ones who can triage quickly, communicate clearly across multiple managers, and maintain consistent standards at each stop.

  • 2 or more years of hands-on property maintenance experience, required
  • Prior supervisory experience, required
  • Valid driver's license, required (travel between sites is a core function)
  • Familiarity with Entrata or AppFolio, preferred
  • Broad trades competency across plumbing, HVAC, electrical, pool systems, and carpentry
  • Comfort working within preventive maintenance programs, PPE requirements, and safety compliance frameworks

Experience with portfolio-wide or roving maintenance work is a genuine differentiator here. Someone who has only ever managed one property's physical plant will find the context-switching demanding at first. Someone who's done it before will recognize the pattern and adapt quickly. Entrata experience in particular helps, since work order tracking and communication across sites runs through the platform.

workable_6078851.title: Full-Time Leasing Consultant
workable_6078851.rewritten_description:
It's a Tuesday afternoon, and there are four prospects booked for tours in the next two hours. One came in through an online lead form this morning, one's been in the CRM for nine days without a response from anyone, and two are walk-ins. That's the rhythm of leasing at a well-run student or multifamily community in Murfreesboro, and it's exactly the environment this role is built for.

What This Role Actually Requires

PeakMade Real Estate is hiring a full-time Leasing Consultant at one of their Murfreesboro communities. This is a front-line sales role with a direct line to occupancy. You're converting leads across phone, email, text, and in-person visits, and the expectation is clear: speed matters. Leads that go cold in the first hour cost occupancy points. The highest-performing consultants here run disciplined multi-touch outreach, they know the pricing and availability matrix cold, and they can pivot a tour on the fly based on what a prospect actually needs.

Day-to-day responsibilities cover the full leasing cycle: generating and nurturing leads, delivering tours that create real urgency, closing leases, processing paperwork accurately, and collecting deposits. You'll maintain CRM records in platforms like Yardi, Entrata, or RealPage, keeping prospect data clean and follow-up cadences on track. When the annual turn comes around, you'll support the make-ready process. Market surveys are part of the job too, so you'll stay sharp on what the competition is offering and how this community stacks up.

Renewals and referrals don't happen by accident. Resident satisfaction starts at the first tour, and the way you handle that initial experience has a downstream effect on retention numbers. Strong consultants here think about the full resident lifecycle, not just the signed lease.

What You'll Need to Compete

  • At least one year of sales or leasing experience with measurable conversion results
  • Demonstrated follow-up discipline across multiple outreach channels
  • Working knowledge of a CRM platform (Yardi, Entrata, RealPage, or similar)
  • Comfort working weekends and peak leasing hours
  • Strong product knowledge habits, including competitive awareness

What separates the consultants who hit commission targets from those who don't usually comes down to follow-up consistency. Multi-touch outreach isn't a preference here; it's the baseline. If your instinct is to send one email and wait, this role will be a grind. If you track your own conversion rates and adjust your approach when the numbers slip, you'll find real earning potential in the commission structure.

PeakMade offers housing discounts (community-dependent), PTO plus dedicated wellbeing days, 401(k) matching, and structured opportunities for growth into leadership. For consultants with strong closing numbers and an interest in moving into an Assistant Manager or Property Manager track, leasing roles at companies with regional portfolios like this one are a well-worn path to that next step.

workable_6079073.title: Leasing Consultant
workable_6079073.rewritten_description:
It's 10 a.m. on a Saturday and three walk-ins just showed up at the same time. You greet all three, pull up available floor plans, and start working the room. By noon, two of them have submitted applications. That's the job.

The Role

Karya Property Management is hiring a Leasing Consultant for their Dallas portfolio. This is a front-line sales and hospitality position where your output shows up directly in the occupancy number. You'll carry the property's traffic from first contact to signed lease, which means greeting walk-ins, working internet leads, conducting tours, processing applications, and staying on top of follow-up until a lead converts or goes cold. The closing ratio and the vacancy report are your scorecards.

Day-to-day, you'll match prospects to floor plans, process income and credit screenings, prepare lease documents and addenda, and keep guest cards and traffic logs current in the property management system. Before any showing, you'll confirm units are market-ready. You'll walk the property regularly and flag curb appeal or maintenance issues as you go. Move-in orientations, renewal outreach, and lease-expiration follow-up are all part of the cycle.

Beyond direct leasing, the role includes competitor market surveys (pricing, specials, concessions), contributing content for social media and listing sites, supporting outreach to local employers and referral partners, and helping staff resident events. Fair Housing compliance and general office coverage round out the responsibilities.

What Karya Needs From You

  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • At least one year in a customer-facing role: leasing, sales, hospitality, retail, or similar
  • Comfortable asking for the sale and following up persistently without crossing into pushy
  • Strong phone, email, and in-person communication
  • Basic computer proficiency; Microsoft Office or Google Workspace
  • Weekend availability and flexibility for evening hours during peak leasing season
  • Valid driver's license and reliable transportation

Prior multifamily experience, working knowledge of Yardi, Entrata, RealPage, or a comparable platform, and bilingual ability in English and Spanish are all preferred but not required to apply.

The candidates who stand out aren't necessarily the ones with the most leasing experience. They're the ones with tight follow-up habits, a genuine ability to read what a prospect actually needs in a home, and the discipline to treat every guest card as an open task until it's resolved one way or another. Leasing coordinators who come from restaurant or retail backgrounds often bring exactly that instinct, and it translates quickly in this environment.

workable_6081497.rewritten_description:
Investment Property Group operates 150 properties across 13 states, with a portfolio spanning multifamily, manufactured home communities, and RV parks. This role puts you on the ground at two of their Auburn, Washington communities: Skylark Village Estates 1, a 141-home senior community, and Skylark Village Estates 2, a 116-home all-ages community. Combined, that's 257 homes worth of resident relations, rent collection, delinquency management, and daily ops sitting in your queue.

The pay range is $24.00 to $28.00 per hour depending on your background, and the schedule runs Monday through Friday with some flexibility built in for weekend open houses and after-hours marketing events (offset by adjusted weekday hours to keep you at 40).

Day to day, this role has two distinct modes. The first is sales and leasing: conducting tours, hosting open houses, driving traffic to available homes, and knowing your local market well enough to close. The second is operations: supporting rent collection, working delinquency procedures with the Community Manager, coordinating maintenance requests, reviewing vendor activity, walking the property to catch curb appeal issues before they compound, and handling resident concerns with the patience that senior and all-ages demographics each require in different ways.

Manufactured housing operates differently from conventional multifamily in a few practical ways worth understanding. Resident relationships tend to run longer and run deeper. Turnover is lower, but when a home-site does go vacant, selling or leasing it back requires actual sales skill, not just application processing. Delinquency management in MHCs also carries its own regulatory weight, particularly in Washington State, where landlord-tenant law applies to MHCs but with specific provisions around notice periods and eviction procedures. Candidates who've worked MHC or large multifamily (100-plus units) and understand those distinctions will hit the ground faster here.

Strong candidates will know property management software. IPG specifically uses Manage America, which is built for manufactured housing and RV communities, along with Rent Cafe and Blue Moon. Comfort with that stack matters. So does the ability to keep administrative documentation clean: transaction records, inspection logs, reporting docs. The Community Manager relies on this person to own those functions without needing to be reminded.

What IPG is Looking for

  • At least one year of experience at a manufactured housing or multifamily community with 100-plus units
  • Demonstrated experience with rent collection and delinquency procedures
  • Sales and marketing skills specific to filling vacant homes and home-sites
  • Proficiency with property management software, ideally Manage America or similar platforms
  • Valid driver's license
  • Strong written and verbal communication across multiple audiences: residents, vendors, contractors, inspectors
  • Ability to handle conflict calmly and enforce community standards consistently

IPG offers medical, dental, and vision coverage, life insurance, an HSA, an employee assistance program, a 401(k) with company match, and four weeks of accrued PTO. For someone building a career in manufactured housing management, this is a realistic path toward a Community Manager title, particularly within a company actively expanding its footprint across multiple states.

smartrecruiters_744000147642369.title: Senior Project Manager
smartrecruiters_744000147642369.rewritten_description:
Skills That Drive This Role

This position runs on three things: project controls, design judgment, and vendor accountability. You'll carry capital improvement projects across AIR's multifamily portfolio from initial scoping through final closeout, which means your ability to build a realistic budget, hold a schedule, and keep contractors honest matters more here than any single credential. Design sensibility also carries real weight. You're not just tracking milestones; you're evaluating finishes, reviewing layouts, and making calls that affect how a renovated leasing office or common area actually performs for residents and staff.

Project budgets typically fall between $100K and $500K-plus. These are multi-phase efforts spanning hallway overhauls, amenity repositioning, operational space redesigns, and leasing office transformations. You'll manage several at once, across properties in different markets, which requires tight organization and proactive communication with a wide range of internal and external partners.

What You'll Own Day to Day

Expect roughly half your time to be travel. Site visits aren't optional check-ins; they're how you catch quality issues before they become budget problems and how you maintain real accountability with vendors. Between visits, you're writing scopes of work, running bid processes, negotiating contracts, and delivering status reports to leadership.

  • Lead project scoping, design development, budgeting, bidding, scheduling, and closeout
  • Source and manage contractors, architects, consultants, and vendors across the full project lifecycle
  • Run kickoff meetings, set milestones, and establish clear performance expectations with every vendor from day one
  • Identify risks early and adjust plans before delays or overruns compound
  • Coordinate with property operations, facilities, procurement, and design teams throughout execution
  • Provide regular reporting and executive-level updates on active projects

Five or more years managing capital improvement or construction projects is the baseline. If that experience comes from multifamily, commercial real estate, or hospitality, it translates directly. Strong candidates tend to bring a specific combination: they can read a set of drawings and push back on a contractor's pricing, but they're equally comfortable presenting project status to a senior leadership team without losing the room.

The Role at AIR

AIR Communities is one of the larger multifamily REITs operating in the U.S., with a portfolio concentrated in high-barrier coastal and Sun Belt markets. The east regional office is in Bethesda, and this is a five-day-in-office role. Candidates based in South Florida or Atlanta will also be considered.

The capex work at a portfolio of this scale tends to be more systematized than you'd find at smaller operators. AIR has established brand standards, internal design partners, and procurement processes, which means less time reinventing processes and more time executing. For a project manager who's been improvising everything at a smaller shop, that structure is an asset. For someone who prefers to build everything from scratch, it's worth understanding before you apply.

A bachelor's degree or equivalent experience is preferred. Proficiency with project budgeting, scheduling, and reporting tools is expected. The ability and willingness to travel approximately 50 percent is a real requirement, not a formality.

greenhouse_5415813008.title: Maintenance Manager - $5,000 Sign On Bonus
greenhouse_5415813008.rewritten_description:
Bozzuto is hiring a Maintenance Manager for a residential property in Newark, NJ, with a $5,000 sign-on bonus and a salary range of $85,000 to $100,000. This is a full supervisory role, not a lead tech position with a title bump. You're running the operation.

Day to day, that means overseeing make-ready turns, managing vendor relationships, executing preventative maintenance programs, and keeping the building's mechanical systems running at peak. The technical scope is real: HVAC, plumbing, electrical, appliance repair, and exposure to complex systems including central plant, boilers, chillers, and split systems. Carpentry, drywall, and paint are part of the picture too, though your main job is directing the work, not doing all of it yourself.

The people side of this role carries just as much weight as the wrenches. You'll hire, schedule, and develop your maintenance team, build in 24/7 emergency coverage, and stay accountable for keeping turnover timelines tight so leasing can keep pace. Residents notice slow service tickets. Bozzuto's model depends on that not happening.

You'll also own capex and special projects on the cost side, which means reading budgets, managing vendors, and making decisions that protect the building's long-term value. Annual jurisdictional inspections, OSHA compliance, and safety codes fall in your lane as well.

What the role requires

  • 7+ years in facilities or residential building maintenance
  • 3+ years in a supervisory capacity, with a track record of building and keeping strong teams
  • HVAC, EPA, and/or NAPE certification
  • Advanced skills in HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and appliance repair
  • Familiarity with central plant, boilers, chillers, and split systems
  • Working knowledge of OSHA, risk management, and MSDS standards
  • Comfort with Microsoft Office and property technology platforms
  • Availability for on-call emergency response
  • Ability to handle physical demands: lifting up to 50 lbs, ladder use, and working in varying weather

One thing worth knowing about this market: Newark properties often deal with aging mechanical infrastructure, mixed jurisdiction requirements across Essex County, and a competitive labor pool for skilled techs. The candidates who stand out at this level are the ones who can read a T-12 on the maintenance cost side, spot deferred issues before they become capex emergencies, and retain techs in a market where good ones have options. If you've managed through a major systems replacement or a significant building rehab, that experience travels well here.

Bozzuto offers medical, dental, and vision coverage, 20 days of paid time off plus holidays, a 401k with company match, and tuition reimbursement. The sign-on bonus applies in addition to the base salary range.

greenhouse_4394383009.title: Maintenance Technician
greenhouse_4394383009.rewritten_description:
Multifamily properties run on the people who keep them functional. When an HVAC unit quits in August or a plumbing issue floods a unit at midnight, the maintenance technician is the one who makes it right. Cortland, one of the larger vertically integrated multifamily operators in the country, is hiring a Maintenance Technician for their community in Herndon, VA.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

This is a full-spectrum maintenance role. Day to day, you're moving through work orders: electrical issues, plumbing repairs, appliance fixes, HVAC service, flooring, railings, and general building systems. You're also doing the less glamorous stuff, correcting hazards before they become liabilities, tracking inventory so you're not chasing parts when a resident is waiting, and documenting completed work accurately so nothing falls through the cracks.

Preventative maintenance is a real part of this job, not an afterthought. Cortland emphasizes asset preservation, so you'll be scheduling and performing PM on HVAC units and building equipment on a regular cycle. That kind of proactive work reduces emergency calls over time, but it doesn't eliminate them. On-call rotations are part of the role, and emergency response is expected. If that's a dealbreaker, this position probably isn't the right fit.

Resident interaction comes with the territory. You're often the most visible face of management for residents, especially when something's gone wrong in their unit. Professional, patient communication matters as much as technical skill in those moments.

What Cortland Is Looking For

  • EPA certification, Type I, II, or Universal (required)
  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • One to three or more years of maintenance experience, ideally in multifamily or facilities
  • Hands-on competency in electrical, plumbing, HVAC, appliances, and general building systems
  • Ability to manage multiple open work orders without losing track of priorities
  • Physical capability to lift, climb, and work in varying weather conditions
  • Willingness to participate in on-call rotations and respond to after-hours emergencies

The technicians who stand out in this kind of role aren't just good with tools. They communicate clearly with residents, flag recurring issues before they become bigger problems, and maintain their paperwork without being reminded. Cortland operates at scale, and the technicians who advance tend to be the ones who treat asset preservation as seriously as they treat individual repairs.

Herndon sits in the broader Northern Virginia market, which runs dense with Class A and B communities and residents who expect responsive, professional service. The expectations here are higher than in slower markets, and the pace reflects that.

greenhouse_5231280007.rewritten_description:
Commercial Property Management, Washington DC

Lincoln Property Company manages a substantial commercial portfolio across office, retail, and industrial asset types, and this Assistant Property Manager role sits inside that operation. The work is genuinely broad: tenant relations, financial reporting, lease administration, vendor oversight, and building operations all fall within scope. That breadth is what makes this a solid growth role, but it also means the pace is real and the detail load is constant.

What the Day-to-Day Actually Looks Like

A significant portion of this role is financial and administrative. You'll support monthly reporting packages, assist with operating expense reconciliations including CAM and OpEx, coordinate with accounting, and review vendor invoices for accuracy and compliance with the management agreement. Proficiency with AP systems matters here. Mistakes in invoice approval or reconciliation drafts have downstream consequences for client reporting and owner relationships.

On the tenant-facing side, you'll respond to needs as they come in, track that building staff or vendors resolve issues on time, and document move-ins and move-outs. Walk-throughs with tenants and tenant improvement teams are part of this, so you need to be comfortable on property and in front of people. Lease administration work includes system setup, lease changes, and reporting, which requires attention to detail and comfort in a CMMS environment.

The role is also partially supervisory. You'll provide work direction and performance guidance to direct reports, so this isn't an entry-level position where you're just learning the ropes. Some prior experience with commercial assets and a working familiarity with financial terms are expected from day one.

  • Bachelor's degree preferred, or equivalent combination of education and experience
  • 1 to 2 years of related commercial property management experience
  • Intermediate to advanced Microsoft Office skills
  • Experience with AP and CMMS systems preferred
  • Familiarity with commercial office, retail, or industrial properties preferred
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Ability to perform property inspections and travel to assigned properties
  • Must be authorized to work in the US without visa sponsorship
  • Position is fully in-office, no remote option

Where This Role Can Take You

Assistant Property Manager positions at large third-party management firms tend to serve as a proving ground for the full PM seat. Lincoln's portfolio scale means exposure to institutional clients, real reporting standards, and complex lease structures. Candidates who develop strong CAM reconciliation skills and get comfortable with owner reporting cycles tend to move into Property Manager roles faster than those who stay on the tenant relations side only. If you're building toward a career in commercial property management, the financial discipline you'll develop here transfers directly to any asset type.

One honest note: commercial property management runs on deadlines. Monthly reports, budget cycles, and lease compliance windows don't flex much. If you're organized and comfortable managing competing priorities, the structure works in your favor. If you're not, it shows quickly.

greenhouse_6183222004.rewritten_description:
What You'll Actually Do

This is a multi-site oversight role covering several affordable housing communities in the Orlando area, reporting up to a Regional Manager. Your job is to hold NOI together across a portfolio where budget discipline, compliance, and resident retention all compete for attention at once. You're building yearly operating budgets, watching cost trends, and making real-time calls on where to tighten spend and where to push revenue. Vendor contracts, large-project proposals, and invoice coding all run through you before they move further up the chain.

On the leasing side, you're not just reviewing traffic numbers. You're ensuring your site teams actually convert. That means evaluating leasing technique, monitoring follow-up procedures, keeping documentation tight, and developing marketing plans that fit the specific demands of affordable housing, where income qualifications and waitlist management add layers that market-rate doesn't carry. Resident retention programs, complaint resolution, and service request turnaround all fall within your scope as well.

Maintenance oversight is hands-on. You'll walk units, review make-ready punch lists, and hold teams accountable for work order completion timelines. Emergency response coordination is part of the job too. When something breaks at 10pm, you're the escalation point, and how that gets handled reflects directly on the ownership relationship Asset Living maintains.

Expect to travel. This role runs between 25 and 50 percent travel, spread across property visits, training, and business meetings. If you're based in Orlando but your portfolio pulls you across the region, that's the rhythm of the work.

What You Bring

  • At least three years of property management experience, with multi-site or supervisory background preferred
  • Working knowledge of Fair Housing Laws and OSHA requirements
  • Proficiency with property management software; you need to run reports, not just read them
  • CAM or ARM designation preferred, though equivalent field experience carries weight
  • Experience building and managing to an operating budget, with the ability to spot delinquency trends and act before they compound
  • Strong personnel management instincts: hiring, coaching, performance documentation, and when necessary, termination

Context Worth Knowing

Affordable housing management operates inside a tighter compliance framework than conventional multifamily. Program requirements, income certifications, and regulatory reporting create administrative pressure that doesn't exist in Class A market-rate work. The strongest candidates for this role have already worked inside that framework and understand that a missed certification or a Fair Housing misstep carries consequences well beyond a standard lease dispute. If your background is entirely in conventional management, the learning curve here is real.

Asset Living is a third-party management firm with a national affordable housing presence, which means your portfolio performs for an owner, not an owner-operator. NOI targets, ownership reporting accuracy, and financial closeout deadlines carry direct client relationship weight. Area Managers who perform well here often move into Regional Manager roles as Asset Living continues to grow its affordable book of business.

Area Manager The Area Manager is responsible for overseeing the entire operations of several multifamily housing communities under the supervision of the Regional Manager. As an Area Manager, you will manage all phases of operations, including personnel, leasing, maintenance, financial, administration & risk management. Essential Duties & Responsibilities Personnel Management Use consistent techniques & company directives to screen, hire, train, coach, and develop on-site staff Ensure effectiveness of staff through ongoing training, coaching, counseling, and guidance in compliance with Asset training benchmarks Complete weekly/daily office & maintenance staff schedules and assignments Deal effectively and consistently with performance problems; document adequately, communicate with Regional & Senior Vice President and HR and terminate appropriately when necessary Promote harmony and quality job performance of staff through support and effective leadership Ensure staff compliance and consistency with Company policies and procedures Financial Management Achieve the highest possible net operating income through the implementation of effective cost control and revenue & leasing improvement; identify trends and recommend strategies and adjustments Develop yearly operating budgets/forecasts Monitor all proposals and contracts for large projects at sites and check work in progress Monitor & maintain the timely receipt and reconciliation of deposits, rent collections, and charges to ensure submitted on a timely basis Monitor & approve the timely receipt, reconciliation, and coding of all vendor invoices Ensure property closeout is completed on time and ownership financial reports are accurate Strategic Leasing Management Develop yearly marketing plan and utilize marketing strategies & systems Ensure staff leasing techniques are effective in obtaining closure, follow up procedures met, signing/documentation of leases, and reporting systems are accurate and up to date Deal with resident complaints, concerns, and requests to ensure resident satisfaction Develop and implement resident retention programs (i.e., resident functions, special promotions, monthly newsletter, etc.) Effectively show, lease, and move in prospective residents Administrative & Maintenance Management Ensure all administrative & leasing reporting is accurate, complete, and submitted on a timely basis Assist with the emergency team for the property; ensures proper response and handling of all property emergencies with staff, residents, buildings, etc. within company guidelines to minimize liability Manage excellent customer service and monitor service request turnaround and responsiveness of maintenance staff Maintain property appearance and ensure repairs are noted and completed on a timely basis (this requires regular property inspections and tours) Plan for and utilize property resources, equipment and supplies economically (i.e., obtaining bids/pricing from vendors, suppliers, and contractors, dealing with inadequate service, etc.) Give direction to and monitor maintenance, construction, and rehabilitation activities to ensure quality and expediency (i.e., “walk” units to ensure make-ready and work orders are completed) Travel This position entails travel, estimated at 25-50% of work time annually. Travel may be required for property visits, conferences, training sessions, or other business-related activities. Education & Experience High School Diploma or Equivalent; Bachelor’s degree preferred or four years experience in the housing industry; or 3+ years related experience and/or training; or equivalent combination of education and experience Certified Apartment Manager (CAM) or Accredited Resident Manager (ARM) preferred Ability to understand and perform all on-site software functions; basic computer skills required Must have basic knowledge of Fair Housing Laws and OSHA requirements This job description should not be considered all-inclusive.
